docs.title: Creatures of this alignment have total disdain and scorn for life,
docs.text: Creatures of this alignment have total disdain and scorn for life, beauty, truth, and freedom. Their only purpose is total conquest of the world through any means necessary, most likely at the expense of others. They also believe in the total eradication of good creatures and often capture and manipulate them into being their slaves. It is extremely rare for a normal creature to become this evil without some supernatural or magical assistance.

docs.title: Creatures of this alignment hold values such as life, beauty, truth
docs.text: Creatures of this alignment hold values such as life, beauty, truth and freedom of little importance and generally scorn them. These creatures are generally out to gain power and control over others through fear, torture and any other means necessary.

docs.title: Good creatures strongly believe in beauty, kindness, truth, and freedom.
docs.text: Good creatures strongly believe in beauty, kindness, truth, and freedom. However in their pursuits for truth sometimes certain sacrifices may have to be made in the name of all that is good.

docs.title: Nasty creatures can be those that have just entered a lifestyle of evil
docs.text: Nasty creatures can be those that have just entered a lifestyle of evil pursuits. They are lacking respect for one or more of the following: life, beauty, truth, freedom. They may have also entered into this lifestyle unwittingly, but only value themselves and as much power they can get.

docs.title: Neutral creatures look upon all the other alignments as being part of the
docs.text: Neutral creatures look upon all the other alignments as being part of the natural order of things. They think that the alignments must exist in order for the natural balance of things to hold.

docs.title: Nice creatures are those that believe in things such as beauty, kindness,
docs.text: Nice creatures are those that believe in things such as beauty, kindness, truth and freedom, as they will ultimately make the world a better place by bringing maximum benefits to all.

docs.title: Saintly creatures value nothing more than the pursuit of beauty, kindness,
docs.text: Saintly creatures value nothing more than the pursuit of beauty, kindness, freedom, and truth. In order for this pursuit to succeed, all that is not good must be eliminated.

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS __INIT DESCRIPTION This function is constructed automagically by the parser at compiler, if the parser was compiled with #define INITIALISATION__INIT. This function is not intended to be defined by the lpc objects, and never to be called from lpc objects. This man page is here just for completeness. SEE ALSO initialisation(LPC)

docs.title: DEPRECATED
docs.text: DEPRECATED SYNOPSIS int add_weight(int w) DESCRIPTION In compat mode, this function is used by the efun transfer(). An object that can contain other objects and is not a room must define this function. It is called with the extra weight of the object that is moved into it. If this is ok, then it has to increment the local weight count, and return true. Otherwise, return false, and the new object can not be entered into this object. The function is also called with the negative weight in the object that the moving leaves. Note that no set_weight() is required by the parser. HISTORY Deprecated in LDMud 3.3 as transfer() has been deprecated. SEE ALSO transfer(E), query_weight(A), prevent_insert(A)

docs.title: NAME
docs.text: NAME applied DESCRIPTION This directory contains descriptions for the lfuns used by Amylaar's version of the LPC parser. These are functions that are applied by the parser to the LPC objects on various occasions. SEE ALSO efun(E), master(M), concepts(C), lpc(LPC), driver(D)

docs.title: DEPRECATED
docs.text: DEPRECATED SYNOPSIS int can_put_and_get() DESCRIPTION In compat mode, this function is used by the efun transfer(). Define this function in objects that are neither living nor rooms if you want to make it possible to put something into current object. Return true if ok, otherwise 0. That means that default is that it is not possible to put something into an object. HISTORY Deprecated in LDMud 3.3 as transfer() has been deprecated. SEE ALSO transfer(E), prevent_insert(A)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS void catch_msg(mixed *arr, object obj) DESCRIPTION When say() or tell_room() are used with an array as message, the array will be passed to catch_message() in all living objects that can hear it, instead of writing to the user resp. sending to catch_tell(). This can be used to implement communication protocols between livings. The second denotes the object that has sent the message. SEE ALSO say(E), tell_room(E), catch_tell(A)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS void catch_tell(string) DESCRIPTION When a message is sent to an non-interactive object, via say(), tell_object, tell_room() or write(), it will get to the function catch_tell(string). The idea is to enable communications between NPCs and from a user to an NPC. Messages sent to an interactive object are also passed to that object's catch_tell() lfun, _if it has one_. If the receiver (or one of its shadows) doesn't have that lfun, the text is sent to the socket directly. Only messages sent by an interactive object to itself is always written to the socket immediately. This allows to filter and process text before it is written to a player. SEE ALSO enable_commands(E), say(E), tell_object(E), tell_room(E), write(E), snoop(E), catch_msg(A)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS int <lfun> (int refcount) int <closure>(int ref, object ob) DESCRIPTION The hook H_CLEAN_UP defines a lfun or a closure used to clean up an object. In older drivers this was hardwired to the lfun clean_up(). The function is applied by the driver when an object hasn't been used for a long time, to give it a possibility to self-destruct. The refcount <ref> passed as argument will be 0 for clone objects, 1 for a simple loaded object, and greater when the object is cloned or inherited by some existing object. It is recommended not to self_destruct the object when the reference count is greater than one. By convention, a refcount < 0 is used if some other object asks the called object to clean_up. If the function is a closure, the second argument <ob> is the object to clean up. If the hook specifies a non-existing lfun, or if the call returns 0, no further attempt to clean up this object will be done. Returning a non-zero value is only recommended when the reason why the object can't self-destruct is likely to vanish without the object being touched, that is, when no local function is called in it, (and in compat mode also when the object is not being moved around). A typical mud configuration defines the time to wait for clean_up() so long that you can assert reset() has been called since the object has been touched last time. EXAMPLES A clone of /std/drink defines clean_up() to self-destruct if it is empty, not carried a living being and not touched for a long time. A room that inherits /std/room defines clean_up() to self-destruct if it is neither inherited nor used as a blueprint, is empty and was not entered for a long time. HISTORY Before 3.2.1, the function was hardwired to the lfun clean_up(). SEE ALSO reset(A), heart_beat(A), call_out(A), destruct(E), remove(A), hooks(C)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS void create() DESCRIPTION The H_CREATE_SUPER/_OB/_CLONE hooks define the function or closure to be called when the driver creates a new object. In older drivers this was hardwired to the lfun create(), and a lot of hook implementations still follow this tradition. This function will be called only once on creation of the object (this is when the object will be loaded or cloned). Inside this function all major initialization can be done. The current user and the previous object are defined but the object has no environment. EXAMPLE object cloner; void create() { cloner=this_player(); } Initialize the global variable to hold the one who created/cloned the object. For 3.2.1, the mudlib may be programmed to call other lfuns than create() on an objects creation. SEE ALSO reset(A), init(A), __INIT(A), initialisation(LPC), hooks(C), native(C)

docs.title: DEPRECATED
docs.text: DEPRECATED SYNOPSIS int drop(void) int drop(int silently) DESCRIPTION In compat mode this lfun is used by the efun transfer(). It is called to check if an object wants to be moved out of the inventory of a living object. drop() should return 1 to prevent dropping. This is the opposite of the get() function. That is because if drop() is not defined, it will always be possible to drop an object. If the object self-destructs when drop() is called, be sure to return 1, as the destructed item surely not can be dropped. Most compat mode LPC libraries to define one argument for drop. If silently is true, no messages should be written. HISTORY Deprecated in LDMud 3.3 as transfer() has been deprecated. SEE ALSO transfer(E)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS void exit(object ob) DESCRIPTION This function was used in compat mode drivers in context with moving objects. Nowadays objects are moved by means of the H_MOVE_OBJECT0/1 hooks, and use of this lfun is up to the mudlib. This function was called in the old environment everytime a living object ob leaves it. The function this_player() will return a random value, don't use it at this point. WARNING: Using this function is EXTREMELY dangerous. A single bug, and you are forever (i.e. until the next reboot occurs) caught in the room. SEE ALSO init(A)

docs.title: DEPRECATED
docs.text: DEPRECATED SYNOPSIS int get() DESRIPTION In compat mode, this function is used by the efun transfer(). If an object wants control over when it is possible to pick it up, i.e. moved into a living object, then it must define get(), and return 1 if ok to pick up. id() has been called before this to identify the object. HISTORY Deprecated in LDMud 3.3 as transfer() has been deprecated. SEE ALSO transfer(E), drop(A)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS void heart_beat() DESCRIPTION This function will be called automatically every 2 seconds. The start and stop of heart beat is controlled by the efun set_heart_beat(). Be careful not to have objects with heart beat running all the time, as it uses a lot of driver resources. If there is an error in the heart beat routine, the heart beat will be turned off for this object and the master function heart_beat_error() is called. If the call to the master function returns a non-zero value, the heart beat will be turned back on again. The function this_player() will return this object, but only if it is living. Otherwise, this_player() will return 0. The function will be called only if there is at least one interactive user in the game. Note that error messages will be given to the current user which will be the object itself or nobody. EXAMPLE object owner; void create() { ... owner=this_player(); set_heart_beat(1); } void heart_beat() { tell_object(owner, "Your heart goes: BUM BUM\n"); } We have to use tell_object() because write goes to the current user and this can only be the object itself or nobody. SEE ALSO set_heart_beat(E), call_out(E), enable_commands(E), heart_beat_error(M)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS int id(string str) DESCRIPTION Let the object identify itself. If str matches an id of the current object then return a none zero value. This lfun is applied for the efun present(). EXAMPLE int id(string str) { return "sword" == str || "sword of fire" == str; } SEE ALSO present(E)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS void init() DESCRIPTION The H_MOVE_OBJECT0/1 implement the details of moving objects. In older drivers, init() was called to handle the adding of actions, and a lot of hook implementations still follow this tradition. The main purpose of this function is to set up the add_actions() of an object. Therefore init() will always be called when an object moves near another object and one or both of them are marked as living. The way init() will be invoked is determined in the following manner: If the object O that moves is marked as living then first call init() of the destination object D with this_player() set to O. Then apply the two following rules for each object C inside D: If C is marked as living then call O->init() with this_player() set to C. If O is marked as living then call C->init() with this_player() set to O. Finally, if D is marked as living then call O->init(), with this_player() set to D. With 3.2.1, the actual move handling became part of the object library, so a given installation may implement any other scheme of calling init(). EXAMPLE (This example assumes a traditional implementation of the movement handling) Lets say we have a object structure of living (l1 and l2) and non living objects (n1 and n2) as the following: l1 n1 l2 n2 If we now move another living object l3 into l1, the call suequence of the init() functions looks like this: l1->init() first init() of the destination will be called n1->init() now iterate throw the inventory of the destination l3->init() l2->init() n2->init() l3->init() and finally call init() of the object that has been moved SEE ALSO add_action(E), set_environment(E), environment(E), move_object(E), hooks(C)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS int logon(void) DESCRIPTION When the parser accepts a new connection, it first calls connect() in the master object and then applies logon() to the object that is returned by the master. That will usually be a special login object, that is expected to clone and get going a user shell or user object. Should return 0 on failure, everything else means success. SEE ALSO connect(M), exec(E)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS int|string <name>(string cmd) DESCRIPTION After set_modify_command(mob) was called for an interactive object iob, all commands for that user will be passed to mob-><name>(), and the return will then be checked for actions. The actual name of the lfun to call is specified by the H_MODIFY_COMMAND_FNAME hook - traditionally it's 'modify_command'. If the result is a string, it is the new command to execute instead of the given one. Note that it is not possible to make several commands from one this way! If the result is a non-zero number, the given command is to be ignored. In case of the closure/lfun setting this may mean that the closure/lfun already executed it. If the result is 0, the originally given command is to be used. HISTORY In 3.2.1@109 the name of the lfun to call must be specified using the H_MODIFY_COMMAND_FNAME driver hook. SEE ALSO set_modify_command(E), hooks(C)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS string *parse_command_adjectiv_id_list(void) DESCRIPTION Return all adjectives associated with this object. Used by parse_command(). EXAMPLE string * parse_command_adjectiv_id_list() { return ({ "iffish" }); } SEE ALSO parse_command(E)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS string *parse_command_id_list(void) DESCRIPTION Return the normal singular names of this object. Used by parse_command(). SEE ALSO parse_command(E), parse_command_pural_id_list(A)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS string *parse_command_plural_id_list(void) DESCRIPTION Return the plural names of this object. If this function doesn't exist, the parser tries to pluralize the names returned by parse_command_id_list(). Used by parse_command(). SEE ALSO parse_command(E), parse_command_id_list(A)

docs.title: DEPRECATED
docs.text: DEPRECATED SYNOPSIS int prevent_insert() DESCRIPTION In compat mode, this function is used by the efun transfer(). Define this function in objects that are neither living nor rooms if you want to prevent to put something into current object. Return true if ok, otherwise 0. That means that default is that it is not possible to put something into an object. HISTORY Deprecated in LDMud 3.3 as transfer() has been deprecated. SEE ALSO transfer(E), can_put_and_get(A)

docs.title: DEPRECATED
docs.text: DEPRECATED SYNOPSIS int query_weight(void) DESCRIPTION In compat mode this lfun is used by the efun transfer(). Not that no set_weight() is required by the parser. HISTORY Deprecated in LDMud 3.3 as transfer() has been deprecated. SEE ALSO transfer(E), add_weight(A)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS int remove(void) DESCRIPTION remove() does some housekeeping to ensure consistency and then destructs the current object. This lfun is not applied by the parser, but by other objects to tell the current object to self-destruct. remove() should be supplied by the base classes of the library. Return 1 if actually self-destructed, 0 otherwise. An alternative way to ensure the housekeeping on destruction is through the use of the master apply prepare_destruct(). NOTE Your actual mudlib may name this lfun differently, "remove()" is just the traditional name. SEE ALSO destruct(E), prepare_destruct(M)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS void reset(int arg) /* compat mode */ void reset(void) /* native mode */ DESCRIPTION The H_RESET hook defines the function or closure to be called when the driver needs to reset an object. In older drivers this was hardwired to the lfun reset(), and a lot of hook implementations still follow this tradition. In compat mode, reset() was called with arg 0 after the object was compiled, and with arg != 0 every once in a while. In native mode, create() is called after compiling, and reset() is called without arguments every once in a while. So, if the argument is zero, the parser is running in compat mode, and reset() may call your create() code. If create() is called, you're on the new version and reset() is not called for object creation. You may call reset() from create() and vice versa, but make sure they do not call each other recursive on either type of driver. reset() will be called only in objects that have been used since the last call to reset(), i.e. a function in them was called (other than reset() or clean_up()), or it was moved around. This function can be used to reset the state of the object or do some checks or what ever. The game wouldn't be fun if no challenges remained. For 3.2.1, the mudlib can be programmed to call an other lfun than reset() to reset an object. SEE ALSO clean_up(A), heart_beat(A), call_out(E), create(A), __INIT(A), hooks(C), initialisation(M), native(C)

The diary contains the personal entries of the high priestess. She apparently
docs.text: The diary contains the personal entries of the high priestess. She apparently only chose to record events of great personal significance. The first entry is: Marpenoth 10: A travelling evangelist named Elgar visited our cathedral today. He is a follower of Mitra who hails from the city of Darkwind far to the south. Apparently the practices of this church failed to impress the righteous Elgar, for he delivered a scathing sermon on the evils of falling from Mitra's grace, and the perils of having an imperfect leader. I think this Elgar needs to look to his own arrogance before looking for sins in others. It seems he is at least right about one thing. I am hardly a perfect leader for this church. A true holy priestess would not have been moved by his harsh words, but, alas, I feel my anger rise at the mere memory of him. No further visitors from Darkwind will be welcome at this church.

docs.title: Nighal 14: I have finally found the secret of the stone. It allows a person
docs.text: Nighal 14: I have finally found the secret of the stone. It allows a person to enter another's dreams. I fail to see how this can help, but it is my last chance. I will sleep, sleep until someone can try it on me. I have no way to tell how long that will be, and it may be that I may die before I am saved. I locked the apparatus so that the spirits could not steal the stone. Three twists to the left and a press of the button in the middle will release the stone. The diary ends here. You take specific note of the directions to release the stone.

docs.title: Marpenoth 26: I wish that priest had never set foot in our cathedral! I am
docs.text: Marpenoth 26: I wish that priest had never set foot in our cathedral! I am becoming more and more concerned that his words may be true, that I may bring disaster on my followers because of my imperfections. Why could not have Arla, my mentor, have chosen another, more sutiable priestess? I must fight a constant battle with my temper these days, and have taken lately to sitting for long hours in sorrow instead of sleeping. And worst of all, yesterday when a party of elven hunters took refuge from a snowstorm, I actually found myself attracted to one of the leaders. I fear my purity is becoming compromised. I must cleanse myself before it is too late.

docs.title: Uktar 12: I fear my contamination is growing worse. I see symbols of Mitra's
docs.text: Uktar 12: I fear my contamination is growing worse. I see symbols of Mitra's wrath everywhere I look. I hear voices in rooms where no one else is. I can see things out of the corner of my eye that vanish when I try to look at them directly. I have drawn upon the Well of Life to sustain me, and its power is helping me deal with my problems. I don't understand why all these things are going wrong. If I was this flawed before, how could I have become a priestess, let alone be chosen to lead this church? I must be absolutely pure, as the slightest fault could bring down the doom I see suspended over me. I have sequestered myself in my quarters, for I find I can better deal with my temper and my lusts and my envy when I am not among other people.

docs.title: Uktar 17: My loss of control alarms me. When the king's envoy came to do some
docs.text: Uktar 17: My loss of control alarms me. When the king's envoy came to do some research in our library, I nearly bit the man in two. Then I found myself yelling at all the young ladies of the congregation about the evils of men. Not preaching, yelling. Was I just envious of their freedom to love, to be with a man? I just ran back to my room and collapsed. They told me later that the envoy kept the key to the library. I hardly care. I am too concerned about myself and my church. Am I slipping into madness?

docs.title: Uktar 24: The madness grows worse. The problems grow worse. The shadows haunt
docs.text: Uktar 24: The madness grows worse. The problems grow worse. The shadows haunt my dreams and seem to even appear when I am awake. I have ceased to perform my duties and turned over the bulk of them to Aria, the best and most intelligent of the priestesses here. She will not have the power of the Well, but that doesn't matter now. I can only pray for salvation.

docs.title: Uktar 29: I ventured out of my quarters to greet a traveller, Miala by name,
docs.text: Uktar 29: I ventured out of my quarters to greet a traveller, Miala by name, who came to the cathedral today. He is a mystic, and I suspect he is a remnant of the old druidic order that broke up many years ago. He seemed to look through me, and he said to me, "Your night lies close at hand, but this stone will save you from the darkness." He gave to me a large gem, about the size of my fist, that was pale blue and seemed to pulse with life. I looked into it, but I couldn't sense any magic to it. I fear that Miala may be as mad as I soon may be.

docs.title: Nighal 2: I don't know what inspired me to build the contraption in my
docs.text: Nighal 2: I don't know what inspired me to build the contraption in my quarters. It seemed to be the right way to examine the stone. Maybe the stone itself instructed me, or maybe the Well of Life inspired me. I still cannot let myself hope for rescue from the madness that grows ever thicker around me. The shadows appear to me constantly, the voices grow ever-dissonant. What hope have I for salvation now?

docs.title: Nighal 6: I am losing my ability to distinguish between hallucination and
docs.text: Nighal 6: I am losing my ability to distinguish between hallucination and reality. I could swear the shadow spirits that appear when I wander the halls have actually attacked me. That's impossible, of course. How could a hallucination harm me?

docs.title: Nighal 10: It is the power, the limitless power. That is the source. The
docs.text: Nighal 10: It is the power, the limitless power. That is the source. The spirits now wander the upper halls of cathedral, lashing out at any who crosses them. I have sent the others to the first floor and told them to stay there. The power has no direction save that I give it. When I invoked it when I was mad, I gave it madness. How long before the strain of the Life and the madness pulls me apart?

docs.title: Entry 1:
docs.text: Entry 1: Today I am setting out with the largest hunting party that I have ever been in. There are a total of 12 of us leaving the village. The queen has said that there is heightened barbarian activity, so we have to travel in larger groups now. No one is very optimistic about finding any good game with us travelling with so many people (some that aren't very good at the hunt if you ask me). I wanted to chronicle the journey so that the child that my companion is carrying might learn of the past through it some day. Entry 2: We have been in the brush for about three days and have had small success in finding game large enough to be worth tracking. Yesterday, something weird happened though. The forest became very quiet, so much that Varie, the leader of our hunting party, decided that we should stop for the entire day so that we might outwait the bad omens that she is sensing. Most are nervous and would rather be on the move then to wait and see what happens, but Varie is experienced in these matters so I will trust her in this judgement. Entry 3: After a day of waiting, we finally started moving again, but in a different direction this time. Valie said that she sensed danger was about and wanted to head south to the bluffs so that we could get a better look at what else was out there in the jungle. We fanned out through the jungle floor and moved slowly and silently southward towards the bluffs. At the end of the day we finally made it to the bluffs and discovered that Varie's insincts were right. About a half a day's journey to the east of where we had been were fires that we could only assume were from a barbarian camp. It was decided among all of us that we would find out what information we could about them and eliminate them if possible. We all hate the barbarians, though most have never seen one alive. Entry 4: After some travel we are very close to the barbarians. We are sure now that it is them because as we come closer we can better hear the ongoing pounding of their ceremonial drums. Varie has decided that we will get as close as possible to determine the size of the party that has set foot in our jungle. Our party is ready now, after several days of nervousness we feel that we are ready for conflict, if it comes to that. Entry 5: We saw the barbarians today and engaged them. After some slow moving trying to keep from being detected we came upon their line. There were about twenty of them trodding through the forest not even caring about the huge amount of noise that they were making. After trailing them for about an hour and a half Varie passed the word around to our party, we were going to attack them. We spread out in groups of two and partially surrounded the men. Kai and I were partnered together and that was comforting because we both were confident in each other's abilities. A call came from the other side of the barbarians and she and I let arrows fly into our enemies. Within a few short seconds a handful of the barbarians were felled. Kai and I took aim again and fell two more as we heard the sounds of hand to hand combat taking place to the left. We rushed in that direction to help embattled friends. We were two late though, by the time we could see them three barbarians crushed the last person in that group to the ground Kai drew her daggers and prepared herself to avenge our fallen friends. I, however let loose an arrow into the three. My aim was true and one fell to the ground. The barbarians began to rush us, and I knew that if they reached us we would have no chance under their phyiscal mass. Kai let out a scream and started running at them. I let another arrow loose, knowing that taking at least one of them out was her only chance at survival. This time my luck did not hold out as I hit him in the leg and he pressed on to destroy us. Kai and the barbarians clashed and she slit the throat of the man that I had already wounded. The other barbarian swung his club and hit her in the ribs and she crumpled to the ground. I shot again praying that I would be in time to save her from death and I caught him in the eye. Such aim I have never before had in my life, and I think that it was the mother herself that guided my hand there. I rushed to Kai's side and found that she was still breathing, though badly injured. All of the ribs on the left side of her body had been broken and her breathing was very ragged. I heard a cheer go up from the forest and knew that the day had been won. Two women, including Kai, had to be laid on stretchers to make the journey back to our village and three were dead. I consider myself to be lucky to have been part of such a glorious battle. Before we headed back, we searched out enemies belongings and found several untouched corpses of game that we took back with us. These would be more than enough to feed our village for a week. While I was searching the enemies corpses I happened upon a curious finding. A large black soulstone, larger than any I have ever seen. I kept it a secret from my amazon sisters and told only Kai, whose stretcher I hid it on for the duration of our trip. I didn't know what I would do with it, but I was sure that I could find some value for it. Entry 6: We entered the village and received a heroine's welcome. Apparently word had travelled ahead of us as to what had happened. When we entered, Kai told me of a friend of hers that would hide the stone for me in her hut without asking any questions. That afternoon I went and talked to her and she gave me an old key to a door and said that it was the only key so not even her herself would have access to it. I do not want to keep the key myself, because I fear that it will raise suspicions as to what it fits. I need to find some way to hide it and keep it secure at the same time. Entry 7: The Queen announced today that there would be a festival in honor of our hunting party's success in battle. There is even some rumor that some of us will be promoted to amazon warriors. I do hope there is some truth in that rumor as it is a great honor to be bestowed. Preparations are going on all over town to get ready for the festival. Even the children are helping. I have had our priestess in my confidence for some time now and I asked her if she would keep the key for me. She told me that she has a storeroom that she keep an eye on but that she would also give me another key so that I might have access to the room should she not be there. Now I have the dilemma of finding a place to hide that key. Entry 8: Since I mentioned her in my last entry I thought I would write a little about the priestess that our village has. I only know a little bit about her, but this story is one that actually did happen when I was younger. Not many people remember it, but I do so I want to put it on paper so it might get passed down. About ten years ago the male slaves were not treated as well as they are today. They had to eat the leftovers of the table scraps and they were worked to the bone and supposedly they had made contact somehow with a necromancer that had been working with the barbarians. They had even transported him into village, but he was detected by the priestess. Sometime late that night she snuck into the slaves quarters and confronted the necromancer. The loud noises of spells in battle came from the quarters that night and everyone in the village was woken up. I was a fearless stupid child at the time so I went to peer through the wall there. The priestess seemed twice her normal size and I will never forget that necromancer. His eyes were completely white and this weird black aura surrounded him. He stuck his finger out at the priestess and muttered some arcane words and the black energy shot out and engulfed the priestess. I was certain that we were all done for until she fought back. She uttered a prayer and appeared to feel better. She pointed her staff at the necromancer and a radial of fire shot at him. This confrontation went back and forth for the better part of an hour until she stood over the charred remains of him. She didn't say a word, she walked back to the royal hut, but I could tell that she was hurt. I think she knew that I was there and that is why our relationship stands as it is today. With that in mind I hid the key in the area of the slaves quarters. No one goes there and the slaves are not smart enough to find it, after all they are only men. After that confrontation the queen changed our treatment of the slaves. They were fed well and not overworked and they actually are very loyal to us now.

docs.title: Amber Fly Synopsis:
docs.text: Amber Fly Synopsis: This is what I like to call a newbie quest tutor. It is not designed to be difficult at all, in fact, just the opposite. It was made for players of level 4 or less that have no clue when it comes to questing -- not the slightest idea what exactly a quest is or why anyone would bother to do one. I was this type of newbie and learned how to quest the hard way, by doing them -- both by myself and with others. This learning process was painfully slow, so I felt it would be a good thing to design what I have here in order to simplify the process. Note: Newbies are not told explicitly what to do in each situation. At the beginning they are led by the hand, given quite obvious hints about what to do, but as the quest progresses, the hints tend more towards the vague side. To help out, at various stages, they are referred to a primer which tells them about some aspect of questing, which just happens to be the one which is relevant to their current situation. I tried to be as complete as possible with the primer docs without being utterly boring. Starting out, newbies will enter a building where they will acquire the primer. This primer directs them down a hall into a den where they find Ezekiel Milquetoast, the sage. Comforting him, or hugging him, as is blatantly hinted at in his description will reveal the situation: goblins have stolen his little trinket, an amber fly. He then directs the player to the courtyard. In the courtyard, the players will find a hut which houses a blacksmith. He will ask the player to fill the bucket therein with water so that he might cool what he is working on. Doing this is trivial, as there is a lake nearby, and gains the player a rope with a grappling hook attached. From there, the player can climb the willow tree in the orchard whose branches droop over the courtyard wall, follow the path around the front of a dark goblin cave to a hole in the ground, and climb down into a cavern. After bumping into the wall a few times, the player will eventually find his way into the central chamber wherein is found the goblin chieftain and his assistant the witch doctor. The latter has the fly in question, but attacking him is impossible as the chieftain jumps in the way. Now the chieftain is kind of tough for newbies so the primer has been equipped with a special function so that it can burst into a flash of bright light wounding the chieftain and making him easier to kill; this is to simulate guild powers for the newbie who will have none. After the chieftain dies, the witch doctor flees, leaving the fly behind for the player to take. Once the fly is returned to Ezekiel, he rewards the player with a protective aura (AC 20), and the quest is complete with the newbie a wiser player. I have placed all the docs for the primer in /open/wizards/lingo/nq_docs for perusal by all the builders, imps, and supers. If anyone feels something important has been omitted or misrepresented, Please let me know so that I may make the appropriate changes. --------- This doc brought to you by Lingo@Darkwind.

docs.title: You are now entering the newbie quest tutorial area.  This place was
docs.text: You are now entering the newbie quest tutorial area. This place was specially designed to teach you about quests, both the idea behind them and ways to solve them. If you are familiar with quests and MUDs in general, you'll probably find the approach taken herein to be ridiculously pedantic and entirely extraneous, but then again, this wasn't designed for you. This is for the completely clueless, those who have no idea what a quest is, let alone how to do one or even why anyone would want to do one. This place is designed for people like me (Lingo) when I started. First off, a quest is a task set forth by the builders on Darkwind to test your mettle, both the physical stuff of which your character here is made and that brain of yours. Some lean towards more of one aspect than the other, but almost all have at least some of both. You can find out which aspect is emphasized in a particular quest by going to the adventurer's guild (1 west, 1 south of where you logged in) and typing 'list' then selecting one of the quests listed and typing 'list <quest_name>'. This will yield a short description of the quest, which I will talk more about later, and the quest's Brain/Brawn ratings, in percentages. A quest with, say 90% Brawn rating and 10% Brain suggests that it is a quest full of combat, or has just a little combat which is exceptionally difficult. A quest with 10% Brawn and 90% Brain ratings, on the other hand, encourages you to find solutions other than killing in order to get things done, i.e. it requires you to use that gray matter between your ears, and I don't mean earwax. The quest that you are about to undertake is rated at 50% Brain and 50% Brawn, so it will be a nice balance between the two. Of course, the combat part will be scaled down so that you, as a newbie, can handle it, so don't let the large Brawn rating scare you off. Similarly, though, don't let a quest's small Brawn rating make you think that you can easily handle whatever combat that might come along in the process of working on it; this is not always the case, especially if you are of particularly low level. This leads us to a discussion about the rules behind questing. You should type 'help quests' at the earliest opportunity and absorb the information there. Note especially the provision again sharing 'quest info' that is anything you have learned about a quest, including but not limited to its location, the difficulty of the creatures there in combat, the workings of a particular device within the area, and anything else really that can be associated with the quest. The exception, and an important one, is when you are partying during a quest. Then, while the party is questing, the members should feel free to exchange information. In fact, the whole questing process becomes much easier if you do. After all, two heads are better than one (unless you're an ettin and both of them are unbelievably stupid -- no offense to any ettins reading this). What one person doesn't come up with another might, and the quest can be completed much faster. Once the party breaks up, however, this privilege is immediately sacrificed. Whatever you gain on your own, or with others, after that is not to be shared with your former quest-mate. You can be severely punished for any such dissemination of quest info, so please, for your own sake, don't do it, and similarly, don't prod others into disseminating quest info to you as this is just as bad if not worse. Well, enough jabber for the moment, let's proceed. If you haven't done this quest before (in this character if you once had another character which has since been wiped) please go through the northern archway so we can get you some quest points!

docs.title: OK, now we're going to start you out on this quest.  This first
docs.text: OK, now we're going to start you out on this quest. This first thing to know about a quest is its name. In fact, sometimes all you need to know about a quest is its name because it's fairly obvious what should be done, e.g. Kill Bueferd. You can get a list of all the quests anywhere by using the command 'quest list'. This will also tell you the Brawn/Brain ratings of the quest, how many quest points it is worth, and whether or not you have done it. This quest is entitled 'Amber Fly' and if you look on the list you will see that it has a 50% Brain and 50% Brawn rating, as stated before, and that it is only worth a few quest points. The number of quest points a given quest is worth is directly propotional to its difficulty, i.e. the harder a quest is to complete, the more it is worth to you. One way in which difficulty is measured is by the frequency with which a quest is completed. That is, if a quest is done often, its value tends to be lower because it is assumed that this means it is easier than something which is only completed occasionally. So, as these quest point values are constantly changing, it would be in your best interest not to share quest info as this would drive down the value of quests to you, slowing your own advancement. The next thing to note, since the title of a quest rarely gives you enough information to get started, is the quest description. This tells you a little more about the quest so you can make an attempt at solving it. Normally the only way to get such a description is by going to your guild (or the adventurer's guild) and typing 'list <quest_name>'. This will yield an output something like this: Quest Name: Amber Fly Description/Hint: Ezekiel Milquetoast, sage of Darkwind and renowned abjurer, is terribly distraught over the loss of an item. Seek him out north of the city and rectify the situation. Completed: NO Value: 11 Brawn %: 50 Brain %: 50 Now you at least have an idea what the goal of the quest is: to help out Ezekiel. You could probably also guess that this will involve finding the item he lost and returning it to him, since that is the most logical way to fix the problem he is having. The only thing you don't really know is _where_ to get started. That is one of the biggest parts of a quest -- finding the quest area. Once you do that, you've overcome one of the larger hurdles in the way of your completion of the quest. But guess what, you're already in the quest area! Now all you have to do is find Ezekiel and you'll be on your way to acquiring some real quest points! Note that, in general, it is usually a little more difficult to reach this stage, especially if the quest description gives you very little clue as to where to look. The only way you will know where to go is if you have found it before, and the only way to find it is to explore. Therefore, if you want to be good at quests, explore a lot. You'll just stumble upon places that turn out to be quest areas which you can go back to later when you are ready to tackle the quest. Now, find Ezekiel and let's get this show on the road!

docs.title: Congratulations, you found Ezekiel!  Now that wasn't so bad, was
docs.text: Congratulations, you found Ezekiel! Now that wasn't so bad, was it? Granted, it was rather straightforward, but what did you expect, a four-dimensional maze with wandering aggressive monsters? Now that you've found Ezekiel, you've got to figure out some way to get some information out of him. You'll notice that he says something every once in a while, mostly lamenting about his current situation so that is really not of much use to you. However, you should note this as one way of acquiring information during a quest. Sometimes, key pieces of information in the little blurbs that NPCs spout off. A more consistent source of useful information is in the environment itself. Providing you're not wandering around in brief mode (You're not, are you? If you are stop it right now. You'll never learn anything wandering around in brief mode, and you'll more likely wander into some nasty death trap), you see a room description every time you move. This details all the little things you have available for inspection around you. However, you can gain even more information by examining the things that you see in the description. You can do this by using the following commands, all of which are equivalent: look at, l at, examine, and exa. This will generally tell you more specific information about whatever you are looking at, sometimes useful, sometimes not. On occasion, when you examine an object, it will make reference to another object that wasn't listed in the room description, e.g. you might examine a machine and discover a lever on the back that can be pulled. Of course, you should then examine these objects, too, because they are just as important, if not more important, than those which you are told about right off the bat. Generally, you should also try to manipulate such objects that you see in the most obvious ways. If you see a lock, try to unlock it (providing you have the right key). If you see a button, consider pushing it (providing you don't think it will cause you serious harm). Quests necessarily require exploration, which I will talk about more later. One facet of it is this constant curiosity which manifests itself in the form of prodding, pulling, and general tampering. Try examining and manipulating what you find in this room, and see where it leads you.

docs.title: Now you've come to a point in the quest at which you will have
docs.text: Now you've come to a point in the quest at which you will have to engage in one of the most common activities of any quest: exploration. In order to find the goblin cave Ezekiel referred to, you're going to have to look through the area, covering quite a large portion of the place. It is always a good idea to do this while engaged in a quest and it is also a good to make a map while doing so, both so that you won't become completely lost and so that you might more easily move through the region. A very interesting consequence of exploring an area fully and making a map as you go along is that you quite often can see where secret passageways and such might be just by looking at the gaps in your map! Therefore, you should truly try to cover as much of a quest area as you can, making a simple map, so as to ease your progress through it. While you are doing so, it is also good to remember to examine what seem to be important features of every room as these often provide clues about things which pop up during the quest itself. Now judging what is an important feature and what isn't is not easy to do, and the ability to do so really only comes with experience. A safer approach is to examine all the features of every room. While this can be a bit tedious, especially if the quest area is large, it is bound to yield abundant information, especially if the quest is heavy on thinking and exploration and not so much on combat. Go looking about this area now, being sure to cover the whole place, and make a map while you do so, just for practice.

docs.title: A couple of notes about quest objects, such as the bucket you just
docs.text: A couple of notes about quest objects, such as the bucket you just acquired. First, like quest info, you are not allowed to share them except with people in your quest party. Some quests are designed so that you can't even share your items with other people in your party, an example of which might be a ring which automatically puts itself on your finger when you pick it up and cannot be removed. However, this is not a terribly common set-up and when it does occur you'll know it. My second point, and as important and practical as the first, involves the availability of quest objects. The objects in this quest have been specially designed so as to be there whenever you should happen to go through. Very often, though, this is not the case. You may have to wait for a room to reset, which it does with relative frequency, before you can acquire a given item, because someone else had already taken it. So, just becase you don't find a certain item in a certain place doesn't mean it isn't to be found there; it only means that it isn't there at the moment. You may come back later and find the item you are looking for sitting right where you expected it to be. Then again, you might not. The only way you can be sure is if you know no one has been in the area recently. If you see someone else wandering around the region, you can probably assume that he, too, is working on the quest, in which case you might consider pooling your resources and working on it together, rather than fighting over the same items.

docs.title: red herring  n. 1. A smoked herring having a reddish color.
docs.text: red herring n. 1. A smoked herring having a reddish color. 2. Something that draws attention from the matter or issue at hand. [From its use to distract hunting dogs from the trail.] Whether or not you are familiar with the concept of a red herring, it is something which you will see quite a lot of in quests, at least the well-coded ones. A red herring is something a builder throws into a quest just for giggles and which has absolutely no purpose in the end. In other words, if you know something is a red herring, don't bother doing it as it won't get you anywhere in terms of completing the quest. Unfortunately, you will only know if something was merely a distraction _after_ you complete the quest. So what's a player to do? First, as stated before, try everything. If you don't try, you won't know, and then you won't get anywhere. Second, don't get caught up on one thing. If you can't figure something out, go look around and fiddle with other things in the area. It may be that you need another item to do whatever you're trying to do, or it may be that the problem in question is just a red herring thrown in to annoy and distract you. So be patient, take it easy, and look out for fish.

docs.title: Now to explore (no pun intended) another facet of exploration, that
docs.text: Now to explore (no pun intended) another facet of exploration, that is searching. Searching an area or a feature of that area is a way of gaining even more specific information about it than examining will do, that is when there is actually something more to be seen. Quite frequently you will receive the default message when you search, namely 'You search <argument> and see nothing.' All this means is that the builder has not placed anything special to be noticed in the specific spot you are searching. There very well could be something to be seen or found in the area by means of a search, but that you have not selected the correct component of the room to give the once over lightly. For example, you might be trapped in a prison cell and when you 'search walls' you receive the default message, but when you 'search north wall' you find a secret passage out of your predicament. Thus you must be sure to be thorough in your searches of rooms. Also do not forget that you need not always provide an argument for your search command. A rather generic 'search' will sometimes reveal something about a room which the room description did not. Keep searching in mind when exploring this segment of the quest, and indeed in any quest, and you will likely be quite successful.

docs.title: First off, don't panic.  There is a way out of this.  In fact,
docs.text: First off, don't panic. There is a way out of this. In fact, you're on the right track and even almost finished! Good for you! Now would be a good time to talk about hidden exits and syntax. Hidden exits are exactly that, ones which are not listed in the room description. They are somehow concealed from you, though sometimes they are right under your nose. If you've reached this point, you've likely already encountered one hidden exit, namely the hidden path between the ferns. That type of hidden exit is used on occasion by builders to conceal part of their area but not terribly often. The reason is that anyone could use it even without knowing it was there, which can cause substantial confusion for the player who wanders into someplace he wasn't supposed to even know about. It also often results in the player finding out things that he shouldn't before he's supposed to know them with regards to the quest. For example, if the quest involved determining which of a group of people was responsible for an attack on someone and you stumbled through one of these hidden exits into a secret chamber where the prince was summoning demons, then you would already suspect the prince, something which could make your quest for truth considerably simpler. Well, builders don't want you getting away with any shortcuts, so you'll see that these types of exits are generally rare. The other type of hidden exit is much more common. That's the type of hidden exit which requires some input from you other than a simple directional command like 'north.' You have also already seen this type when you climbed the willow tree to reach this side of the courtyard wall. This sort of thing is great for builders as they can hide their secret areas to all but the most observant or even to everyone who hasn't done some other deed. For example, if you have to say 'foo' to open some door and there is no way to know this except to talk to the court jester, then you won't know to say 'foo' until you talk to the jester. This way, builders can truly control who gets into where, and quests can be constructed in a much more organized manner. Now what should you, as an inexperienced player, take from all of this? Only that you should be aware of the possibility of hidden exits. You should poke, prod, and generally turn upside down any room looking for nonstandard ways out or even clues which might grant you some other out in some other room. Sometimes you might have to struggle with the syntax a little, e.g. 'move stone' could return 'What?' while 'push stone' reveals something, but this in unavoidable. So as always, be patient, and remember that just because an exit isn't listed, doesn't mean you can't go that way.

docs.title: Well here you are, the final encounter.  This is a standby
docs.text: Well here you are, the final encounter. This is a standby for quests. Quite often, even if the quest is not combat oriented, you will be required to overcome some enemy bigger, tougher, and meaner than yourself in order to get what you need to complete the quest. This one is no different. However, because you will be in at least one guild, more than likely, to do your questing, you will usually have some guild powers at your disposal to assist you in this matter. Well since you aren't and you don't, respectively, I'm going to help you out. This primer that you're holding is capable of helping you defeat the goblin chieftain and the nasty witch doctor. I'm not going to tell you exactly what it does, but the syntax to bring it about is 'newbieblast.' So when you're ready to take them on, go for it.

docs.title: Hail thee of might and valor:
docs.text: Hail thee of might and valor: I, the Burgomaster of Barovia, send you honor -- With dispair. My adopted daughter, the fair Elisia, has been these past nights bitten by a creature calling its race 'Vampyr'. For over 400 years, he has drained this land of the lifeblood of its people. Now, my dear Elisia languishes and dies from an unholy wound caused by this vile beast. Yet I fear, too, that the creature has some more cunning plan in mind. He has become too powerful to be fought any longer. Go I say you, give us up for dead and encircle this land with the symbols of good. Let holy men call upon their power that the evil one may be contained within the walls of weeping Barovia. Leave our sorrows to our graves, and save the world from this evil fate of ours. There is much wealth entrapped in this community. Return for your reward after we are all departed for a better life. -Rolyan Indrirovich, Burgomaster

docs.title: Chapter 1: Talamh Darag, before the Darkwind.
docs.text: Chapter 1: Talamh Darag, before the Darkwind. The name "Talamh Darag" stands for "Land of oak trees" in the elder tongue. Long before the Darkwind blew, Talamh Darag was a land inhabited by three factions: the Cinneach Siochair, The ancient race and the Coingeis Gineal. The Cinneach Siochair, which in the elder tongue meant "Nation of elves, faeries and dwarves", was considered the ruling party of Talamh Darag. They served the deity Ban-righinn dùrachd which translates to "Queen of sincerity and good-will" - the same deity we now refer to as Mitra. A now presumed extinct race of demonic creatures also lived on Talamh Darag. Vile and ghastly in appearance they thrived on causing pain, death and chaos. It's probably for this reason that they served Àrd-thainistear an-dòchas, "Lord-regent of despair" nowadays better known as Set. The knowledge of their true name has been lost over the many centuries, as such they are now only known as the "ancient race". The Coingeis Gineal, which in the elder tongue is closely translated as "The independent races" encompassed a broad group of races that were not particularly aligned to some cause. If they even served a deity it was rarely Ban-righinn dùrachd or Àrd-thainistear an-dòchas serving instead Màthair anam, "Mother source of life" or the entity we call today, Gaea. Little is still known about this period of time. With the massive destruction caused by the Darkwind most knowledge of this era was forever lost.

docs.title: Chapter 2: Talamh Darag, after the Darkwind.
docs.text: Chapter 2: Talamh Darag, after the Darkwind. After the Darkwind had blown, causing massive destruction in its wake, only small groups of the numerous races that had once inhabited Talamh Darag survived. It appeared a lot of races had gone extinct, including the ancient race. With the destruction of the ancient race, the Cinneach Siochair disbanded since the races no longer shared the same mutual enemy. The surviving races all went in their own direction, finding a new place to live and rebuild their society. The dwarves dug into the ground creating an extensive underground network of tunnels to build their homes and harvest natural minerals such as gems. The elves created a new home deep in the forest that they named "Baile Gloir", "Town of glory". The faeries split off in several small colony's on the island and the independent races all went their own way. Rebuilding of the new civilization was still in progress when elf scouts chanced upon a group of adventurous duine, "Humans". They learned the duine came from a different island. Sailing huge and massive ships they had explored the fuathas sàl, "great salt water" or ocean. The elves and duine, being so much alike, soon saw each other as kindred spirits. The duine taught the elves the concept of trade and built a castle halfway between their docks and Baile Gloir. This castle functioned as a resting place and trading point for the merchants of both races, generating a trade route and making for safe travelling. As such it was dubbed Wayfare castle by the duine. It didn't take long for the elves to realize the potential in trade and they soon established trade routes with the other races. Gnomish ale, dwarven gems or silky cloth from the faeries - it didn't really matter what one needed, if it existed one could probably buy it at Baile Gloir. A glorious and wondrous era for the elves just launched, or so it seemed.

docs.title: Chapter 3: The ancient prince.
docs.text: Chapter 3: The ancient prince. One day word reached Baile Gloir that a demon dressed in black garbs walked the lands. Everywhere he went he infected innocents with tinneas beò bàs, "disease of the living dead". This disease was in the past spread by the ancient race to create slaves out of other races. The infected were called beathaich fuil, "blood feeders" nowadays referred to as vampires. The beathaich fuil were inferior creatures when compared to their full blood brethren, the ancients. Still their power was superior to that of almost any other race. The only creatures that are to some extent naturally able to resist tinneas beò bàs are the Faeries, while the infection does cause them to turn deeply evil they remain in control of their own free will. One of the faery colonies near Baile Gloir was infected and its inhabitants became an evil breed of faeries known as the Sidhe. This faery sub race will be discussed in chapter 4: The Sidhe. The elves of Baile Gloir erected city walls and prepared for a great battle. By now it was clear the demon had amassed a great army, capable of destroying almost any foe. It is at this time that a female elven paladin heroine named Enelya Ar-Feiniel went on a holy crusade to beseech Ban-righinn dùrachd for a blessing to protect her people. After a long and successful journey she returned to her home just in time, the sounds of battle were eminently clear in the forest around her as she sped her way to Baile Gloir. Hundreds of dead were scattered about the streets as numerous beathaich fuil were feeding on the corpses of men, women and children. Several other elves were still in battle, fighting for their lives. From Enelya's body a white aura extended, touching every still living elf. A holy and divine power channelled strength into each one of them, enabling the elves to drive their opponents off. Most of the surviving elves now fled to Wayfare castle, looking for a safe place to hide. Enelya and several other champions stayed behind to cover their retreat. From this point on no one truly knows what happened. It is believed Enelya and the other heroes sacrificed themselves by erecting a mystical field around the town, trapping themselves, the demon now known as the "ancient prince" and his beathaich fuil in Baile Gloir. Baile Gloir, while once representing the glory of the elves now was a town of the undead. As such its name was changed to Baile Greim-bàis, "town in a death grip". The elves started a new town near Wayfare castle and dubbed it Wayfare city. The castle is still owned by the duine, but no longer serves its original purpose - it is now a home to the duine ambassador.

docs.title: Chapter 4: The Sidhe
docs.text: Chapter 4: The Sidhe The Sidhe Fae are demonic faeries of incredible magical aptitude. Regardless of the information gathered about them in this article they remain a mysterious enigma. Even the followers of the Ancient Prince himself do not know what purpose they serve and if they are even loyal to Set or the Ancient Prince. The Sidhe have a tight Hierarchal order, much like that of a bee society. There is the queen, the Arch-magi, The warriors and the drones. The Sidhe queen is rumoured to be a humanoid female of great beauty. Unlike her fellow Sidhe she's about the same height as a regular human being. She is unarguably the most powerful of the Sidhe and has the voice of a siren. Once she starts to sing any male will stand paralyzed, listening to her voice, unable to move. The arch-magi are those individuals who have shown great aptitude as mages. Trained in the arts of magic since a very young age these are the elite troops of the Sidhe. The warriors are trained in both physical combat as well as the arts of magic. Their small frail bodies don't appear perfect for physical conquest, yet they do rank among the fiercest warriors known to us. The drones have slight mystical powers and are the working backbone of the Sidhe colony. Their daily tasks include gathering food and maintaining the Sidhe forest. The Sidhe forest is also known as the forest of no return. According to legends this forest exists in three different planes of existence. Any person walking through the forest will get shifted from plane to plane without warning. It is a deadly maze filled with aggressive Sidhe. According to folklore the Sidhe are unable to conceive children of their own. Every Sidhe baby is born mutilated and disfigured. During the night the Sidhe invade the homes of unsuspecting new mothers and replace their hideous offspring with that of the house owner. The stolen baby will be transformed into a Sidhe Fae by the Sidhe queen and raised as one of their own.

docs.title: Vampire Psychology
docs.text: Vampire Psychology Vampires are individual beings; they live alone or in small groups; they are forever hunted by the people from which they arose - including people they might have known personally. They have needs which must be satisfied; they have a body which behaves very differently from their previous life. They also have an understanding that they are different. It is not surprising that vampires often show signs of deep psychosis, experience mood swings and gross personality changes. It is for the hunter to understand these rival pressures and find consequent weaknesses that can be exposed. Being Different: From the moment of induction, the protégé knows that they are special. They will be told - if they did not already know - they have been selected for a new life, while others have been ignored, farmed, or simply exsanguinated. This will lead to an initial confusion; 'What have I lost, what will I gain? Is this immortality? Why have I feared these creatures that are just like me? What about my friends, my family?" A newly-created vampire is at its most vulnerable; it has little idea of how to survive, and is torn between escape and clinging to the familiar. It may panic; some disintegrate psychologically at this time. But the vampire who performed the induction will be close, and will have planned carefully to protect its protege. The protégé will be taught not only to survive and thrive, but to believe that it is a superior being, it is special, it is a chosen one. Religion: New beliefs will clash with deeply ingrained expectations and religious beliefs. In most cases, the pre-vampire person was brought up in a close Mitra'n world ; the vampire still possesses all that knowledge, and, subconsciously, all those beliefs. It will also be aware that vampires are feared as evil incarnate. These contradictions must be suppressed for the vampire to survive, and fully mature vampires will be emotionally cold, arrogant beings who will show little interest in their previous existence or current events in the world of men and women. At times of stress subconscious thoughts will be close to the surface, so it is not surprising that crucifixes and religious incantations can offer some protection to humans under attack - the vampire will hesitate, and may even flee. Marks made on the vampire's skin by a crucifix are not due to any religious effect, however, but the more mundane chemical effect of wood or silver on vampire metabolism.

docs.title: Vampire Pathology
docs.text: Vampire Pathology A vampire starts life as a human being; any age, size, race; there is no known immunity. Infection: A vampire bite can cause death by anaphylactic reaction; repeated bites can cause death from haemorrhagic shock, occasionally from sub-acute anaemia. A small minority of bites can lead to a metamorphosis from 'normal human being' to vampire; vampirification. One study suggests fewer than 1% of attacks lead to vampirification. There is no record - or rumour - of vampire reproduction in any other way, supporting theories of a parasitic factor; vampirification as a means of increasing the vampire population. The favoured age of victims is early twenties; almost equal numbers of male and female victims, with a marked predominance of healthy, educated and intelligent people. Indeed, one mark of a threatened and declining vampire group may be a deviation from this careful preselection of victims. Vampirification: The process of vampirification may follow a deliberate act on the part of a vampire; occasionally it may be a chance infection. It is argued that any partaking of blood by a vampire might result in vampirification, but there are problems with this thesis. Vampires have been shown to take blood from cattle, horse and sheep (among others), with no record of these creatures being affected, beyond blood loss. This may be a species immunity result, or may be evidence that accidental vampirification simply does not occur. The process of vampirification is still poorly understood; it may be a natural result of a viral infection, a sophisticated drug-induced process - or, most likely, a parasitic infection. The problem has always been a lack of hard pathological evidence; no vampire has yet co-operated with researchers, and no viable specimens have been obtained from captured vampires, as they always chose self-destruction before co-operation. The consensus in the vampire hunting community is that the process bears comparison with the metamorphosis of a caterpillar into an adult butterfly. The process of metamorphosis involves three distinct developmental stages: human, pupa and vampire. In temperate zones, the pupal stage is thought to take 3 to 4 days, much longer in colder climates. Views differ on the effects of higher temperatures; vampires are rare in hot climates, and this may be because the process cannot occur above a certain temperature. Anatomy: Though some people suggest vampires change from a human visage to a demonic appearance as they attack, few accounts support this contention. There is no obvious change in appearance after vampirification, except for a marked pallor, and an almost universal appearance of significantly below average weight. Such minor changes, however, conceal significant changes under the skin. A wealth of circumstantial evidence suggests that the pupal stage involves major changes to heart, circulation and renal systems, with consequent alterations to other systems to accommodate a very altered lifestyle. Human haemoglobin uses iron as its core; the vampire equivalent uses magnesium. This allows the vampire to dispense with an artificially maintained body temperature; it creates a highly efficient cardiac muscle allied to more flexible blood vessels and it virtually eliminates the risk of thrombosis/embolism. Deficiency of magnesium is known to lead to anxiety, irritability, anger, insomnia and mood swings; all features reported in vampires, especially when deprived of sustenance. Physiology: Respiration in the vampire does not involve the lungs at all. Pending full dissection and analysis, it is impossible to conjecture in detail on the chemical processes involved. Oxygen-based respiration would present a serious risk of spontaneous combustion, and this may explain the vampire's need for fresh blood; the oxygen held in oxyhaemoglobin can be stored by the vampire, enabling controlled and safe combination with magnesium to produce copious energy. The freedom from requiring 10+ respirations per minute would significantly facilitate inactivity and hibernation. Spared the need for maintaining mammalian temperatures, energy requirements can be reduced to near zero for extended periods. Nutrition, for all living organisms, is about meeting the needs of growth and repair, plus energy for activities of life. For the vampire, a magnesium-based physiology allows the body to function like a fuel cell; power is available for concerted activity, while prolonged rest following binge consumption allows for regeneration and repair processes. Unlike in human anatomy, the vampire kidney appears adapted to preserving magnesium with great efficiency; extraction from the liquid diet might be sufficient for the vampire lifestyle. Reproduction does not exist within vampire communities; human anatomy maintained at low temperatures, without carbon/oxygen metabolism could not function; procreation could not occur. While this means the inconvenience of 'recruiting' new blood, it also means that the energy of child rearing is not expended. Growth and Aging: Vampires are normally recruited as adults; no significant growth appears to be required, and longevity is a well documented feature; with periods of inactivity and virtual hibernation, individual vampires are known to have lived for centuries. Repair processes appear to very efficient, with activity hardly affected by multiple magical or stab wounds, and complete recovery from severe injuries within a few days.

docs.title: Vulnerabilities
docs.text: Vulnerabilities Vampires and weapons Wooden stakes have long been a weapon of choice for the vampire hunter, but it is no accident that hand-wielded, fresh cut unvarnished pine is much more likely to prove fatal than hardwood or crossbow-fired polished wooden darts. This is because it is not the wood itself that causes the reaction, but the enzymes that are found in the resin of many varieties of wood. Indeed, a fragrant pine forest can lead to an asthma-like condition that may be fatal to the vampire. Efficient vasoconstriction, coupled with powerful regenerative powers have given the vampire the reputation of being unstoppable by blade or arrow - most experienced hunters will not relax until the vampire has been burned or beheaded; injuries that would lead to almost instant death in a human being are a minor inconvenience to a healthy vampire. Vampires and Sunlight: Sunlight has long been known to be the most effective method of destroying vampires. While the use of magnesium has granted vampires great advantages, it also brings vulnerabilities. In certain circumstances, magnesium can be an explosive element; this means that no vampire will risk direct sunlight for fear of spontaneous combustion. Recent forensic evidence suggests that vampire perspiration contains magnesium-based substances which are liable to combustion in certain conditions, including high air temperature (greater than 42oC) and specific light wavelengths 560-580nm; when illumination is above 5cd/m2. In effect, this means direct sunlight around dawn and dusk or a 'bright' day, even with substantial cloud cover. Magical light sources can be used, but the correct frequency is vital, and the required brightness would be difficult to achieve other than in a fairly small enclosed space. Hunting by night, even with a bunch of light sources, would be doomed to failure, and might prove foolhardy. Sunlight has been used effectively since long before formal records have been kept, and has been shown to be the simplest, surest and safest method of vampire destruction. The risk lies in the methods used to force the vampire into daylight; attacking a vampire at rest during the day is a challenge that has attracted many novel approaches; a courageous woman, prepared to risk her life in distracting the vampire until daybreak features in many urban legends. Vampires and crucifixes A wooden crucifix could cause serious superficial burns, and, given enough time, could prove fatal. But this is a chemical effect, not a religious one. Many vampires are of devout Mitran descent, and a crucifix could well trigger severe guilt feelings; in some cases, self-loathing. But not fatality. Vampires and water A vampire really is an incendiary device waiting to be detonated (check the theory), and water, even steam, presents a real risk to the vampire.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text: Aftermath --------- Leader lay on the ground, exhausted, watching in disbelief as the Pup slowly walked up the little mound -- obviously he hadn't yet fully recovered either. "Not finished"? What did the Pup mean? What was so important about this mound? Another wolf trotted by and fell in behind the Pup. Younger Sister, apparently recovered. Leader watched as both wolves went up the little hill. Oh, but _this_ is a fine thing! thought Leader, being very careful to keep it only to himself and not let it out via the pack's telepathy. A fine thing, indeed! My two youngest pups continue on while I, their _Leader_, lie here unable to move?! I'd never hear the end of it! And he roused himself, grimacing with the effort. Elbows, hands, knees, and finally, painfully, on his feet. He retrieved his halberd from the Dancer's carcass and followed the two pups up the hill. Keeper was no longer screaming, Gaea be praised, but he still groaned loudly in his pain. _Rikard_? queried Leader. Keeper didn't answer. From Shamaness came no specific words, but a strong, general feeling of worry. _Natalia_? _Be_fine_, answered Older Sister, still a few kilometers to the rear at the original battle site. Leader promised himself that he would see to them soon. First, see this thing, whatever it was, to the end. With every step up the hillock, the Pup's anxiety increased. It was only by the sheerest force of will that he managed to put one paw in front of the other. That he must go up there was certain, he somehow knew. But he didn't know why, and most of all he didn't know why he should feel such an irrational, inexplicable _fear_ of it. Liar. You know exactly why you need to go up there and you know exactly what you will find when you do. No! I do not! Denial. You have foreseen this. And now you must see it. No. Do not falter now. Confront your worst fear. No! He was unaware that he was standing still until he felt a soft nudge on his face. He opened his eyes. They were filled with water, and so the image of his pack sister was a little blurry at first. Her wolfen features regarded him with concern and confusion. _Little_brother_? The Pup just stood there. The memory was coming back to him despite his best effort to suppress it. He noticed now that he was just below the lip of the little hill. One more step and he'd be able to see over the top. He began to tremble. _Marc_? A clawed hand rested gently on his head. The Pup looked up into Leader's crinoid face. "The dream, Pup, isn't it?" If any other humanoid being had been there, they would have heard a much- garbled version of that sentence, but another Garou understood it perfectly. Pup nodded, still trembling. Leader nodded back. "Shamaness told me. I don't understand your bond to this thing. I cannot explain to you why you feel it and the rest of us do not. We can puzzle it out later. But right now, I need you to guide us. You're not alone. I'm right here with you." _Here_too_! chimed in Younger Sister, and she licked his face. Leader smiled at her and then turned back to the Pup. "Come. Let's end this now together." Pup nodded and composed himself. And took the deliberate last step up the hill. The top of the mound turned out to be the lip of a bowl. And there, down in the center of the depression, stood The Thing. Straight out of the Hell of his dream it came. It was the "Wyrm Tree", from the dream in which his packmates died right before his eyes. Died attacking this monstrous Wyrmling. The Pup was beginning to hyperventilate. "Easy now, Pup," reassured Leader. "Eaaaaasy. Focus! Tell us what you see." The Pup closed his eyes and forced himself to relax, slow his breathing. Then he opened them again and looked at It. It was the Tree-Thing, all right. But how strange ... he saw now that it was not the same as in his dream. The Dream-Tree had been large and omnipotent. But if "tree" it was, why, then this one was only a "sapling". It had the same physical structure -- "roots" in the ground, a "trunk" for a body, and tentacled "branches" -- but it was small. _Young_, he thought. _It_is_young_. Leader nodded. "What else, Pup?" _It_is_... He narrowed his eyes with concentration. Something... _Weak_! But that wasn't all of it. More to-the-point, it was... _Dying_!
