And with that, the Pup bolted away from the others and slid down the sides of the bowl, down toward the Wyrm Sapling. After a moment's hesitation, Sister and Leader slid down after him. They ringed it, being careful to stay out of the reach of the tentacles -- "sapling", "weak", or "dying", it was still Wyrm -- and regarded it up close. _It's_hungry_,_continued_Pup_.__Starving_. "What does it want?" asked Leader. _Blood_.__Sacrifice_. "The villagers?" _Yes_.__Dying_without_. "Should we attack it? Finish it?" _No_.__Almost_gone_now_. Indeed, even Leader and Sister could now see the creature withering before their eyes. And so they waited as it deteriorated. When it no longer moved and the remains of its tentacled tree-body were a dried-out husk, it began to dissolve into dust. At which point the Pup began to dig in the ground right around it. Sister and Leader joined in. _Roots_? queried Leader. Pup nodded. And so they dug all around it. Every time they uncovered "roots", they would stop, and the roots would wither and dissolve right before their eyes. They dug until they found no more, going deep and wide. Pup: _No_sequel_. "No," agreed Leader. "The End is now." They were finished here. They ran back to check on Keeper. He lay there, unconscious. Shamaness had wrapped him as best she could in whatever bits of clothing she found on the dead. "How is he?" asked Leader. She looked at him. There were dark rings under her eyes. "He lost consciousness a few minutes ago. That's a great blessing. As far as I can tell, he's stable, but critical." She paused and drew breath. "I don't know if he's going to--" She swallowed. "We need to get him back to the Sept. Now." "You go." Shamaness shook her head. "I want to, but I cannot. That boy saved my life back there. He needs me too, and I promised him I'd return. There's nothing more I can do for Keeper, anyway. He needs wiser heads." "The Uktena." "Yes." Leader nodded. He looked at Keeper's face for the first time. It was pockmarked with angry-looking boils. Leader winced. Shamaness understood and answered the unspoken question. "Yes, the rest of him looks like that too. I -- I just don't know." Leader nodded again. "All right. Quickly, now. Let's build a litter for him." He turned to the two Pups. "Jemi. Marcus. You two will go fastest. Haul him to the Sept. Give him to the Uktena. They'll know what to do." In a few minutes, it was done. Leader and Shamaness tied Keeper to the litter and harnessed it to the two lupus Pups. Leader knelt down and spoke to them. "Be careful how you drag him. That's not a 'nice' litter he's on. But don't be too careful -- speed is important now. Understand?" Two wolfish heads nodded. "Go, my Pups!" And they were off. That finished, Leader and Shamaness quickly covered the distance back to the original battle site. Older Sister was sitting up, a crude bandage covering her forehead. She looked very tired, but otherwise in one piece. She smiled as Leader and Shamaness approached. "They made this for me," she said, pointing to her forehead. They looked around. The villagers were in a pitiful state, under shock from the traumatic events of the night. But here and there, several of them were moving amongst their neighbors, offering what help and comfort they could. One of them saw Shamaness and hurried over. He dropped to a knee and bowed. "Savior," he said. Shamaness looked distinctly uncomfortable and quickly helped him to his feet. "If anyone is to bow here, young lad, then _I_ shall do so to _you_. I owe you my life." The boy gave a small shrug and looked uncomfortable himself. Shamaness smiled. "My name is Shanti. These are my packm-- ... my friends. That's Natalia, and this big fellow is Nagha. What's your name?" The boy stood up a little straighter, looking more like a young man. "Harel, my lady. My father is -- my father was -- Horrac, Chief of the Village." Shamaness nodded. "You are the chief's son. I'm very sorry for your loss." The young man nodded. "Thank you." Shamaness leaned over until her eyes were level with his. "You're a very brave lad. What you did for me today will always leave me in your debt. But now you have even more important work to do. Do you realize this?" The young man glanced around him at the other villagers and then back at Shamaness. He nodded nervously. "They need you," continued Shamaness. "You're the Chief now." The boy swallowed, but nodded again. "My friends and I will help you. We have much to do, so let us begin." "Yes," agreed the new Chief. He turned to go, but then looked back, a puzzled expression on his face. "Shanti, what ... what were those things that attacked us this night? There were wolves. And ... things that looked like ... wolfmen, or something. What in...?" He trailed off, confused. Shamaness laid an hand on his shoulder. "No. Just a band of very evil men. Slave traders, probably. They like to wear wolfskins, and they travel with large dogs, the meanest they can find and train." "But --" Shamaness shook her head and held his gaze. "It was dark, you were asleep when they came, and your shock is severe. The mind plays tricks. You saw only what they wanted you to see, to increase your fear and confusion. It's over now. Let's go see to your people." The young Chief frowned, but then relaxed. "Yes, of course. It makes perfect sense. What else could it have been?" Then resolutely, "Yes, my people. Let us see to them now." The young man and the three strangers turned to their task as the sun came over the horizon.

docs.title: The Battle
docs.text: The Battle ---------- "Reports to the Council" are meant to be precise and factual accounts of important incidents that have relevance not just for one Pack, but the entire Sept; or even the Garou Nation. As such, they are short, to-the-point, and free of emotionalism. The side effect: sometimes they make the described event seem easy. It was anything but. And it didn't tell the whole story... On Leader's "_Now_!", the Pack howled its rage and surged forward. Keeper and Younger Sister each took the neck of a Lupus Dancer in their jaws and promptly tore them to hell. The Pup did the same with a Crinos Dancer. Leader, in crinos, embedded the left edge of his halberd into a Dancer neck, yanked it free, whipped completely around and did the same with the right edge, decapitating his victim. Older Sister sliced open her foe's chest with her crystal sword (Pup, of course, had no idea where she got such a thing), twirled with her momentum, and as she came around, drove it point-first into his heart. Shamaness' opponent was already off-balance thanks to the wind spirit she had called in upon it, and now she violently brought her hands -- pulsing with manifested eurus energy -- together, with the hapless Dancer's head between them. She dug the heel of each hand into a temple and the Dancer's eyes bulged, its tongue shot out, and it went limp. Four seconds into the battle, the odds had gone from 4-to-1 to 3-to-1. In the fifth second, the Dancers became fully aware that they were under attack and reacted. But they were spread around their prisoners, had suddenly lost a fourth of their membership, and needed a few seconds to regroup themselves. The Garou Pack exploited the confusion and attacked again. The next melee round was a little more difficult because of lost surprise, but momentum was still theirs. 13 seconds since the attack began. 12 Dancers down and six healthy Garou on the field. The Dancers, now fully recovered from their shock, howled their own rage as they came on, and the battle began in earnest. Clawing, biting, slashing. Growling, roaring, howling. Claw and fang, rage and terror. No mercy given. No mercy wanted. Wolf and Wolfbeast of Gaea and of Wyrm, locked in struggle, here and everywhere, past-present- future, war unending through the ages until Final Victory and Final Defeat. 31 seconds. 15 Wyrmlings down. Four Gaeans lightly wounded. Older Sister's crystal sword pierced a Dancer's leather armor, the abdomen underneath, and got hung up. The Dancer screamed his agony, and whacked her savagely upside the head with his stone club. Ignoring the thunderstorm in her skull, she wrenched the sword sideways with everything she had, roaring with the effort. The abdomen opened and its well-packed contents spilled onto the ground, steaming in the predawn coolness. The Dancer convulsed, eyes bulged, and its weapon fell. She gave another mighty heave on the sword, this time upwards, willing it to find the creature's hideous heart and make it stop beating. Suddenly, the light in the Dancer's bulging eyes went out and the carcass slumped forward. Older Sister fell to her knees, dropped the sword, and held her head, unable to ignore the migraine any longer, nor the warm, sticky flow of blood from her forehead. Leader had two skillful crinos to contend with and was totally defensive, keeping them at bay with wide swings of his halberd. Keeper, having finished his last opponent, lunged at one of them and bore him to the ground, his teeth finding the Dancer's neck after a brief struggle. Leader exploited the opportunity, renewed his attack on the remaining Crinos, and despatched him after a flurry of strikes and parries. Shamaness was in trouble. A big Crinos had her in a bear hug, the jaw full of crooked teeth _not_ on her neck only because her right arm was still free and her eurus-encased hand held the Dancer's head at bay. But it was a simple, brute-force battle, and in her homid form, she knew she would lose it. Even now the teeth grazed her neck. Desperately, she brought up a knee and it found the creature's groin. The Dancer convulsed and relaxed his grip enough for her to push him away, but then his fist crashed into the side of her head and she went down. The Dancer was on her immediately, pinning her on her back while both clawed hands wrapped around her neck and squeezed. Her distress call reached the other five in the next instant, but they were too involved to come in time. Still, she continued to resist, calling upon Luna for strength, even as blackness filled her vision. Suddenly, the dancer convulsed and the death grip around her neck loosened. Then a liquid >thud< and the Dancer convulsed again, eyes wide. Its tongue fell out and the lifeless body crashed on top of her. She pushed it out of the way, sat up, and beheld a strange sight. A boy. No more than 15. Holding an axe. A Dancer axe. With fresh Dancer blood on it. A prisoner who'd escaped his bonds. His whole body trembled and his eyes were wide in shock and terror. He looked down at the axe, studying it as if he didn't know how it had come into his hands. He met Shamaness' gaze, eyes still wide, mentally detached from whatever had just happened in a desperate bid to preserve sanity. His trembling increased. The axe loosened itself from his grasp and fell to the ground. The boy's legs wobbled and he went down on his arse, mumbling gibberish. Shamaness scrambled over to him. He was hyperventilating. "Easy now, son, easy!" she soothed. "Breathe deep now and--" The boy choked, turned his head to the side, and vomited. "There now," Shamaness continued, her very voice a relaxant. She had him in her arms and was rocking him like a baby. "Easy now, it's over. You did fine. Real fine! Breathe deep, now. Yes. That's it." The boy was coming around slowly. She pulled back and looked in his eyes. Still frightened, but recovering. _Pursue_! Leader's order. The battle was 55 seconds old. 19 Dancers down, the other five in retreat. All Garou wounded, but only Older Sister unable to continue the fight. Shamaness pursed her lips together. The boy needed a bit more time, but there was none. She laid a hand on his shoulder and looked in his eyes. "I'll be back," she promised. "Do what you can for the others." And she was off and running. She passed Older Sister, who'd relapsed into Homid form. "I'll be fine," she assured Shamaness, although she looked up with a face full of blood and couldn't hide a grimace of pain. Another one who needed help, but again there was no time. Shamaness nodded, muttered a prayer to Luna under her breath, and hurried after the others.

docs.title: Battle Plan
docs.text: Battle Plan ----------- The Dancers had an hour's head start, but they had prisoners. That would slow them down and allow the Pack to close on them fairly quickly despite the time lag. And as the eastern sky began to lighten, Keeper, Younger Sister, and Wolf found them. Leader never needed to say, "Get downwind of them" -- that was always a given. It required circling around a bit, but it was always worth it. While Leader, Older Sister, and Shamaness still sped to their location, the lupus wolves sent their report... 24 Dancers -- 15 crinos, nine lupus; 57 prisoners -- 22 adult females, 35 children, all human, tied together in six groups nine or 10 each. The nine lupus dancers ranged around the entire party at intervals, two crinos dancers moving each prisoner group and remaining three crinos in the lead. Dancers very much in haste, but can't move their prisoners fast enough. The two crinos closed up -- only Shamaness was still out. Leader studied the scene, quickly compared mental notes with the three lupus, and reached a decision just as Shamaness arrived. An elderly woman couldn't keep up. A crinos guard cut her loose and rebound the line to fill the gap; his companion ripped out the woman's throat. Amidst the screams of the prisoners who witnessed it, the guard yelled "faster!" although in his crinos form, he garbled the word badly. Leader: _Lower_right_open_intervals.__Shadow.__My order.__Stay_ together_mass_surprise.__Take_lupus,_crinos_. ("At certain intervals, there is a gap in the lower right of the defensive ring the nine lupus dancers provide, so we'll attack there. We shadow them until the moment is right. Wait for my order, then attack. Remain together during the attack. We compensate for their superior numbers by massing the Pack at one location and crushing them one by one, maximizing element of surprise. Take down lupus first, then crinos, but stay together and maintain mass.") Leader didn't need to ask for questions -- if the plan was unclear, someone would ask without a prompt. No one asked. Leader moved -- he was the Guide now -- and the Pack moved with him. The Dancers were still very much in a hurry and appeared to be desperately trying to move their captives along. One of the lead crinos barked an order, and five of the lupus dancers forsook the defensive screen, moved in amongst the prisoners, and with nips, bites, and snarls, attempted to speed things up. _Perfect_! That thought came from all six Pack members simultaneously. Leader: _Now_! And the early morning erupted with howls of Garou Rage.

docs.title: The Beast Within
docs.text: The Beast Within ---------------- The Elf stood before the bowl filled with the strange ointment and peered down into it. Peering back at him was your basic elf -- long blond hair, blue eyes, pointed ears, soft and somewhat fragile-looking features -- his own reflection. But he knew that couldn't be. The fluid was not clear, but creamy; it just wasn't possible that he was seeing his reflection in it. The Elf continued to stare at his reflection-that-could-not-be- there and noticed that it was changing, shimmering slightly, getting fuzzy around the edges. And then it metamorphosed -- not gradually, but all at once, from one instant to the next. From gentle and beautiful elf into... ...the Elf gasped in shock and took a step back -- a gut-level reaction to the horrific image he had just seen. He couldn't remember what it looked like, even though it was just a moment ago. Its physical appearance had surprised him, but not upset him. The upsetting part was the way the image had, at least for a moment, fused itself to his brain and touched that part of him that had nothing to do with reason, logic, sound judgment, or that which the Elf comfortably and reassuringly classified as "reality." No, the image had wanted nothing to do with "reality". It had homed in on something else within him; something deeply buried in some dark recess of his mind all his life, wild and unpredictable. Something _feral_. A part of him so well hidden that nothing could ever hope to find it; so well guarded that, even if found, nothing could ever penetrate its defenses; so deep that, even were the defenses breached, nothing could ever haul it up to the light of day. Nothing could ever accomplish that feat. Until now. Here, in a small clearing in the woods southwest of the City. An eccentric but somehow powerful Old Man. A bowl of strange ointment. And the image of a Beast therein. A Beast which came not from the ointment, the Old Man, or the forest -- but from the repressed subconscious mind of the Elf himself. The Elf realized his knees were shaking. He bent down enough so that his hands could rest on them, holding them, a steadying influence. He closed his eyes. Breathed in deeply. Forced himself to let it out slowly. Opened his eyes. His knees were no longer shaking. The Elf straightened himself and took another deep breath. In. Out. There. That was better. He glanced at the Old Man, but the Old Man seemed deep in a meditative trance. No help there, but no matter either. The Elf took a step back in the direction of the bowl of ointment and, after a moments hesitation, looked into it again. Nothing -- just some creamy fluid in a bowl in a cleearing in the woods. He could no longer discern the Image of the Beast therein. But the memory of it was strong and no longer subconscious. He was aware of it now. The Beast had risen from its secret hiding place and taken up residence in the Elf's conscious awareness. And now that the initial shock was over, the Elf gradually realized that the Beast was neither destructive nor evil. It stood now in the forefront of his mind, allowed the Elf to study it, feel it. If the Elf had felt fear before, then he was now giving himself over to excitement and anticipation. It is said that every creature has one moment in the span of its life where everything it has been and done culminates, one moment where it all comes together. And the Elf knew that his moment had come. The door was open -- he had only to walk through it. The Elf extended his hand toward the bowl.

docs.title: The Dancer
docs.text: The Dancer ---------- The five remaining Dancers, all crinos, sped northeast away from the battle, five Garou in hot pursuit. Keeper, Pup, and Younger Sister, in lupus, closed the distance first and attacked, at which point all five Dancers swung about and fought back. Six seconds later, three wolves were down, stunned, and the five Dancers were speeding away again. Leader caught up. _OK_? Keeper: _Best_last_. (They saved their best fighters for last). The three shook it off and regained their four feet. Leader: _Together_.__Shanti_? Shamaness: _On_my_way_! Leader: _Catch_best_.__Four_close_! (Catch up as best you can, Shamaness. The four of us will close on them). 1,000 meters later, they did just that. This time, four of the Dancers hung back to fight while the fifth kept going. Eight seconds later, many things happened at once. The four Dancers were no more. Leader and Younger Sister were also down, not hurt badly, but needed to regain strength and close their wounds enough to continue. The Pup was just scratched, but had needed the entire time to bring his Dancer down and was just finishing. Shamaness closed up and quickly checked the two down Garou, who assured her they would be fine. Keeper had taken his opponent down first and was bounding away, closing on the last, lone Dancer. But said Dancer was no longer running. He had stopped about 100 meters from the melee and now faced the five Defenders of Gaea. Behind him, a curious-looking mound gently rose up, about two meters high at the top and perhaps 20 meters in diameter at its base. Pup now took notice of it, and for some reason that he couldn't understand, it filled him with dread ... some nameless fear that he felt he should recognize, but couldn't quite place. The Dancer stood his ground, breathing heavily, concentrating his malevolent gaze on the lupus Garou surging toward him. Keeper was far gone with feral rage. His only thought as he raced along was how good it would feel to close his jaws like a vise around the neck of that last Dancer and hold them there until there was one less Servant of the Wyrm walking Gaea's Green Earth. But Shamaness' spirit was more in balance, and thus did she recognize what Keeper did not. And with that realization, the cold hand of pure terror closed around her spine. _No_Rikard_no_! Her thought was so strong that it penetrated even the haze of Keeper's rage -- and he saw. The Dancer's right hand. Coming up to head-level, palm toward Keeper. And in that palm, a sickly kind of green fireball, pulsating with malicious intelligence. Balefire. Keeper was 50 meters from his prey. It may as well have been 50 kilometers. He would never make it, not before... Shamaness: _Rikard_hold_! Keeper skidded to a stop, braking with all four paws, his widened eyes inexorably drawn to the green ball of flame in the Dancer's hand. Shamaness prayed desperately. _Sister_Luna_,_hear_me_now_._ _Guide_and_protect_! And she extended her hand in Keeper's direction, bending all her willpower toward him, hoping against hope that it was not too late, as tears coursed down her cheeks. The Dancer roared and hurled the ball of green flame toward Keeper. One does not "dodge" Balefire. It is the very lifeblood of the Wyrm, and as such, possesses an evil intelligence all its own. Once released, it will strike its target. One can only "resist" it. If one can. A beam of moonlight -- shining brightly in the light of the dawn of the new day -- reached down from the heavens and shone upon Keeper, forming a luminous, white glow around his head before quickly fading away. Shamaness sobbed in gratitude and collapsed from her exertion. Would it be enough? Keeper stood his ground and watched the fireball quickly fill his sight. _Oh_Mighty_Gaea_,_Earth_Mother_Eternal_,_give_me_ strength_! And he roared his defiance as the Balefire slammed into him. The impact knocked him off his paws and somersaulted him backwards. Energies of Green Fire and White Light sizzled and crackled and fought each other for control of Keeper's body as he tumbled. The Green weakened. But the White was consumed. Keeper's lupine body smacked the ground in a tangle of fur, teeth, and limbs. His roar of defiance quickly turned into an impossibly high-pitched scream of pure agony that went on and on and on, changing tone as the trauma forced his body from lupus to crinos and all the way back to homid. Leader tried to stand, but it was too early and his legs buckled underneath him. Just one more minute ... but there was no time! Even now, another green ball was forming in the Dancer's hand. Leader knew the tactical drill: two attackers running flat out toward the target -- one would take the Balefire, and the other would take the Dancer. There was no other way. Shamaness reached Keeper's side. He was still screaming and writhing. She tried to lay her hands on him to steady him, but only succeeded in burning her fingers. If only they'd been ready! thought Leader in profound frustration. But Keeper had attacked alone -- all other pack members were out of position ... Older Sister was back at the battlefield, wounded ... Shamaness was too slow in homid ... Leader and Younger Sister were hurt and recovering ... and the Pup had needed too much time to take down his Dancer -- well, he was a Pup after all, so-- Leader suddenly blinked in surprise. The Pup was no longer there. Now where in all the-- As if guided by Fate, Leader's head turned toward the Dancer. His mouth fell open. The next green fireball was almost fully formed, pulsating wickedly as the Dancer raised his hand to throw it. Another second or two was all he needed. But this was not why Leader gaped. A streak of grey. Moving so fast that one couldn't tell what it was unless one knew. And in a flash of recognition, Leader did know. The Pup. It could not be anything else. The Dancer's hand and the horrid object it held reached shoulder level. He had only to cock it back a bit and let it fly. He already had his target fixed: the grey blur barrelling toward him. And with sickening clarity, Leader knew that the Pup was going to die -- no other result was possible. Either the Balefire would take him, or this Dancer -- powerful enough to summon the Flame of the Wyrm -- would obliterate him in paw-to-paw combat. Leader scrambled to his feet, ignoring the pain, managed to stand by sheer willpower and a little help from his halberd, on which he leaned as he straightened up. Keeper continued to scream, tongues of sickly, green flame still licking at his ruined body. Shamaness managed now to touch him without getting burned, her lips moving as she invoked Rejuvenation. And just before the Dancer could bring his hand forward for the fatal throw, the Streak of Grey slammed into him. Wolf of Gaea and Wolfbeast of Wyrm tumbled and rolled over each other. The ball of green flame dropped from the beast's hand, weakened, lost consistency, and completely dissipated as it hit the ground. The Pup had his jaws on the Dancer's neck. He closed his eyes and bit down with everything he had, concentrating on nothing else except making his teeth come together. But they weren't even close. The Dancer had a hand on each jaw and held them apart. The Pup opened his eyes and met the Dancer's gaze -- a mix of pure hatred and malicious pleasure. The Dancer freed his neck and flung the Pup away. Pup hit the ground, rolled, and got his four paws under himself. But before he could do more, a great, clawed hand closed around the scruff of his neck. He felt himself lifted completely off the ground, and then he sailed through the air and smacked head-first into the side of the strange mound. Stars formed in his head, dizziness took him, and he puked. Again the hand closed on his neck, the underside this time. The Dancer lifted the Pup with one paw and held him off the ground at arm's length. Pup struggled wildly, head twisting savagely in an effort to free himself from the visegrip of that paw, four legs flailing in the air. It was hopeless. He couldn't breathe, and the world was going black. He met the Dancer's gaze again and saw his enemy's amusement. And then amazement. The Dancer's eyes were wide with it, and the grip on Pup's neck loosened. And then let go. Pup fell to the ground. The Dancer turned sideways. There was something sticking in his back. A halberd. Leader's halberd. Leader himself about five meters away, limping, but approaching quickly. He must have thrown it like a spear. The Dancer managed to reach around behind him, grasp the weapon, and pull it free -- just as Leader's fist connected with his head. The Dancer staggered backward and the halberd fell to the ground. Leader rolled, picked it up, and as the Dancer recovered and leapt at him, Leader buried the pointed, forward end of his weapon in the Dancer's chest. The Dancer convulsed, eyes wide. Leader pushed, howling with the effort. The Dancer landed on his back, the halberd still in his chest, and Leader leaning on the halberd. The Dancer's massive, clawed hands closed on the weapon's shaft, tried to pull it free. Leader howled again and twisted the weapon savagely. The Dancer's hands left the shaft, arms flailing outward, and the great maw vomited blood. Leader put his back into it, leaning on his weapon, teeth gritting with the exertion. Again the Dancer's hands grabbed the shaft. Again Leader twisted the halberd, roaring, locking eyes with his foe. And after what seemed an eternity, Leader came to understand that the eyes staring back, defiant though they be, no longer contained the spark of life. Leader relaxed, released the weapon, fell to his knees, then crashed to the ground next to his victim. _Done_, he thought, flat on his back, panting with exhaustion. _It_is_done_. _No_. Leader frowned in surprise. He turned his head toward the Pup, who was standing and gazing up at the strange mound. _Not_yet_. And the Pup began walking up the little hill.

docs.title: The Dancers
docs.text: The Dancers ----------- "Dancers" is simply the short name that the Garou give to a very peculiar -- and very dangerous -- tribe of Garou (or EX-garou, depending on how you look at it). Their full name: The Black Spiral Dancers. It is a name that no self-respecting Garou utters willingly or casually, but only when necessity dictates and then only with great loathing; or perhaps pity for what has become of their former brethren. "Former" brethren, 'tis worth noting. Over a millennium ago, before their corruption, the Dancers were part of the Garou Nation and had a different name: The White Howlers. The Howlers had a reputation as savages -- not surprising, considering their kinship with the Picts and the Fianna. Still, the Howlers were proud members of the Garou Nation, and although there was sometimes friction with the other tribes, all had a common enemy -- the Wyrm. And the White Howlers certainly did their part in the War, fighting the Wyrm with their accustomed savagery. But their enthusiasm proved their undoing, for in their zeal to destroy the Wyrm, in their blind rage, their overriding desire to end it once and for all, they attacked the Wyrm directly before they were mentally prepared for the danger. The Howlers crossed over into the Umbra -- the Spirit World -- and into Malfeas, the Wyrm's very home. And there the servants of the Wyrm tricked them into dancing the Black Spiral. The ritual utterly twisted the White Howlers and drove them insane. The Wyrm then took control of them, and ever after, they've been known as the Black Spiral Dancers -- the Wyrm's own Garou, its most potent and demoralizing weapon against the Garou Nation. Dancers live underground, in labyrinthine cave systems called "Hives", analogous to the "Caerns" of the Garou Nation. But "Caern" is too sacred a word to use to describe anything related to the Wyrm, and so the Garou call them "hives". The Dancers themselves aren't difficult to recognize. Most of them are physically ugly, independent of what form they're in. As homids, they tend to be pale, with oily, unkempt hair and unhealthy skin. Many have open sores. In lupus and crinos, their heads resemble those of the hyena, and their teeth are jagged and crooked. Their ears are pointy and hairless, like a bat's. Even normal humans can see that there is something "wrong" with a homid Dancer in their midst -- but they would go mad indeed if they had any inkling of the creature's true nature. But even more disturbing than their physical hideousness is that sound -- the mad call of the whippoorwill, their tribal totem. When the Dancers come for you, that's the last sound you hear before death -- if you're lucky; or capture -- if you're woefully _un_-lucky ... for the Black Spiral Dancers are always looking for breeding stock, toys, or things to sacrifice to the Wyrm. And that brings us back to our Pack -- three lupus, two crinos, and a homid, standing in a dewy field in the predawn hour, stock still, listening to the barely-audible, mad call of the whippoorwill somewhere in the distance, cursed with full knowledge of its implications, perhaps envious of the humans, elves, dwarves, and other non-garou races asleep in their beds, blissfully ignorant of the horrid things going bump in the night. Shamaness closed her eyes and began to sway slightly from side-to- side, signalling the onset of another Vision. Leader and Older Sister remained standing, not moving and trying to breathe as quietly as possible. Our Wolf, Younger Sister, and Keeper were also still, straining to hear any recurrence of the sound. Shamaness stopped swaying and opened her eyes. "I cannot see them," she said aloud, perhaps because the slowness of real speech allowed more time to think. "I see only the village in the distance." Leader: _Just_one_? "Yes, it is the only one, and I looked wide. It is beyond narrow." By which Shamaness meant that she could discern the distant village with "wide" vision, which found many things over a great distance, but didn't see them clearly, but it was too far away when she used "narrow" vision, which would have allowed her to see things happening in the village, were it close enough. Leader nodded. _Pup_Guide_. The Wolf glanced at Leader, thinking he had misunderstood. He'd never been tapped to be the Guide before. But Leader's steady gaze confirmed it. Swallowing nervously, the Wolf set out. His first thought was to try to home in on it by estimating the direction from which the sound came, but it was too faint to be sure, so he simply relaxed (as much as one _could_ "relax" whilst running on all fours) and felt for it with his feelings. The Pack fanned out again, but this time, since they knew what they were hunting, they stayed within 500 meters of each other, and Shamaness remained as close to Wolf as possible, closing up when Wolf halted, as she still remained in homid form. Every few hundred meters, he stopped to listen for the whippoorwill or whatever Intuition would tell him. Each time he waited for Shamaness to catch up before starting out again. On one of the stops, when the Pack was nearly 10 kilometers from the spot where Wolf had first heard the whippoorwill, Shamaness laid her hand on Wolf's head. "Wait," she said. And then she swayed again, eyes closed, frowning at whatever she was seeing in the Vision. As she opened her eyes, the rest of the Pack closed up. "I see the village now in narrow," she sighed. "There are no Dancers there. The ground is blooded and corpses litter it." Leader: _Survivors_? Shamaness shook her head. "None in the village. If there are, they have either fled or been taken." Younger Sister: _Too_late_we_are_? "To prevent this, yes." The whippoorwill sounded again. This time, Leader and Older Sister, in crinos, could just make it out, while the three lupus heard it stronger than before. Keeper: _Mayhap_not_all_too_late_. Leader: _Continue_Pup_. On the surface, further "guiding" seemed unnecessary, for Shamaness had already identified the village in narrow vision, which told the Pack exactly where it was and how far, so it would have been easy enough to just make for it directly. Even so, there could be other "signs" along the way (or even just _off_ the way) that the Pack should find. And thus did Leader order Wolf to "continue". But if there were more signs, the Pack missed them, and so they came upon the village. The scents confirmed that there had indeed been a raid, even Shamaness in homid could tell that. There was no scent of anything alive (nothing humanoid, anyway), and so the Pack entered the place and gathered info... The Dancers had left about an hour ago. They had come from the northeast and departed the same way. The tracks thus mixed with each other and any estimate of their numbers could not be exact, but it seemed there had been at least 20 but no more than 30. There had been isolated struggles, but no serious resistance from the villagers -- the hour had been that typical pre-dawn time when humans sleep so deeply that you could steal the bed out from under them. Judging by the number and sizes of the various buildings, the village's population (before the raid, of course) looked to have been at least 75 but no more than 100. Exactly 27 corpses lay on the ground, mostly adult males, some of them partially eaten. There were no tracks or scents of any kind leading anywhere but northeast; ergo, the Dancers had taken the rest with them. All this the Pack gathered with their heightened senses and then shared and cross-checked with each other via telepathy. Seven minutes after entering the village, the Pack knew it all. They rallied up on the northeast edge of the village, where the Dancers had come and gone. Leader: _Thoughts_? By this, Leader did _not_ mean, "should we or shouldn't we?" The answer to _that_ question was only too obvious -- the Garou don't allow Dancers to have the run of anyplace on Gaea's Earth as long as the Garou have life in their bodies. That the Pack would continue the Hunt was a given that no one doubted even for a moment. This Garou Pack was, by this time, a very cohesive one, and simply didn't need to be long-winded (or "long-thought") when it came to their telepathic communication. They knew each other enough to get whole thoughts from short messages. So what Leader really said (thought), translated into normal verbose speech, was something like: "Does anyone have any other relevant info or opinion to share before we set off northeast? Anything that we should consider? Anything that might influence our next action that we should be aware of _now_?" Keeper: _Dawn_less_hour_.__Remote_few_. ("We have less than an hour before dawn. However, this location is a remote wasteland with very few inhabitants.") Older Sister: _Veil_hold_yes_. ("If we must fight without cover of darkness, then I believe no non-garou will observe us and thus we will preserve the secrecy of the Garou from their unsuspecting eyes and insufficiently developed awareness.") Younger Sister: _Good_dark.__Shock_. ("Still, fighting by darkness will be to our advantage when we take on the Dancers, for the element of surprise will be easier to maintain.") Older Sister nodded her wolfish head. _Power_overwhelming_destroy_now_. Five heads of various forms turned sharply toward our Wolf. The Wolf blinked in surprise at himself. Had he really sent that thought? Yes, he had. It had come from deep within him and without his conscious will to guide it. He had no idea why. The Pack sensed his confusion. Keeper: _Dancers_? ("You mean that the Dancers are 'overwhelming'? Surely not. Dangerous yes, but not above our ability to fight.") Wolf: _More.__Know_must.__Is_. ("I cannot explain. I simply know that, whatever is ahead, it is not only about a Dancer raid and dead or captured villagers. There is something more important at work here. I know this because I must know it and I cannot tell you why I know it. It is simply so.") Leader nodded. _Find.__Best speed.__Wait_. ("Find them now with all possible speed. This means that you three in lupus will arrive first, and Shamaness last, but we must catch them now and find out what we can. When you get there, wait for the Pack to close up -- do not attack until we are all there and I give the order.") _Go_! And the six moved as one.

docs.title: The Duel
docs.text: The Duel -------- The Elf stood with his left foot in front, toes pointing forward, and his right foot behind, toes pointing to the right. His knees were bent just enough so that his legs could propel him forward or backward at a moment's notice. In his hands he held an oaken quarterstaff diagonally and in front of his body, more of a defensive posture than offensive -- he wasn't about to take any chances with his opponent until he saw what she was capable of. Apropos "opponent" ... her stance was a near mirror image of the Elf's, but she held her staff forward in a more offensive posture. Neither she nor the Elf wore any armor; the Elf had a simple tunic and pants that hung just below the knee. His opponent wore a light robe that normally reached to mid-thigh, but she had tied it at the waist in such a way that it inched a bit higher; not to mention the deep cut in front. Under normal conditions, seeing her like this might have awakened more pleasurable thoughts in the Elf's mind, but her hard eyes, locked with his, belied any image of "pleasure" -- in them, he recognized only a desire to hurt, maim, and kill. And so, under the circumstances, all the Elf could think about was survival. She leapt forward, swinging her staff as she came. There was a loud >CRACK!< as the Elf parried. He jumped left and swung his staff around on a perfect collision course with her head, but there was only a loud >WHOOSH!< as she perfectly ducked and counter-swung low. The Elf jumped high as her staff WHOOSHed beneath him. As gravity pulled him back to Earth, he swung on a vertical axis, aiming for her head, but was again frustrated when she rolled sideways and his staff harmlessly struck the ground where she had been. She regained her feet and the two repositioned themselves. Eyeing each other warily, staves raised, Elf and Girl circled each other. Then the Elf came on and attacked relentlessly, switching axes lightning fast as she successfully parried each thrust and swing, CRACK!'s and WHOOSH!'es blending with each other like some musical cadence; the two combatants repeatedly ducked, lunged, retreated, spun, jumped, their movements a dance that would have been beautiful were it not so deadly. Finally they separated again, eyeing each other, both breathing heavily now and covered in a glistening sheen of sweat. Only their hair held some semblance of order -- Elf had tied his long, blond locks into a ponytail, and the Girl had hers in a tight bun. "You're holding back," she said, still breathing heavily. She was ranked 5th in the pack, just above the Elf, who was the most junior wolf. She had seen several more seasons than he had, so she was stronger, faster, more agile and fit. In a normal sparring session, he wouldn't have stood a chance. But for this one, she agreed to the staff, a weapon she didn't use -- but the one in which the Elf was specializing. Ergo, the odds should be even. The Elf shrugged. "I want you to feel that you're doing well." And then he smirked. She snarled, a very un-ladylike sound that filled the cave with an atmosphere of menace, and showed teeth that looked bigger and sharper than what a lady should have. "Do _not_ hold back," she said, and sprang at him. Again the adversaries leapt, spun, danced, ducked, and dodged, this time using the walls as well as the floor, staves whirling, twirling, smacking and cracking. But the Elf did not hold back this time. The fight was brutal, vicious and intense, and not "easy" for him by any stretch of the imagination; but his prowess with the weapon inevitably overcame his sister's superiority as a fighter and his staff finally connected with her head, a blow that could well have been fatal had she not rolled with it so well. The Elf exploited the opportunity ruthlessly -- reversed momentum, came up underneath her guard, ran his staff quickly along hers until it hit her hand. With her grip lost, it was a small move to disarm her and send her staff sailing through the air, bouncing off a wall, and finally clattering to the floor -- well out of reach. The Elf howled triumphantly and laughed. "It's over, Big Sister!" he grinned. "You're beaten!" He shuffled his feet in a little dance and twirled his staff with a flourish around his head. He knew he was being cocky, but he couldn't help himself -- he had _never_ beaten her at _anything_! "Do you admit defeat?" he asked, still grinning. She simply stood there, glaring at him from underneath her eyelids, lips pulled back in a little snarl. The bump on her head had knocked her hair loose and the rich, red-brown locks hung down now in waves all around her head, in her face, and curled over her chest above the bust line, more visible now because her robe had become dishevelled from the exertion of the fight. She looked utterly alluring -- and utterly dangerous. "Defeat?" she said evenly, and blew a stray lock of hair from her face that promptly settled back to where it was. Then she smiled evilly. "Little Brother," she said, while he hands undid the knot at her waist. "Do you have any idea what a cocky little bastard you've become?" And with that, she yanked off the robe, threw it aside and stood before him with only a brassiere and thong for protection. The Elf's eyes widened and he forgot to breathe for a moment. She used the distraction to focus her will inward, call upon the power of her eurus and, with a final push, manifest claws of pulsing energy around her hands. "But --" the Elf stammered. "That's _cheating_!" She advanced a step, raised her hands threateningly, and the Elf involuntarily took a step back. "What's fair in love and war, Little Bro, hmm?" she asked in a voice that was all the more intimidating because it was low and quiet. And then she shouted the answer: "_All_ is!" And she attacked. If there had been a Bard to witness what followed, no doubt he would have composed a wondrous ballad of the heroic stand the Elf made against her, how he fought on despite the overwhelming odds against him, how he refused to give in to the inevitable for as long as humanly -- er, _elvenly_ -- possible. And of course the Bard would have sung of how the Girl disarmed the Elf and sent his staff sailing through the air, bouncing off a wall, and finally clattering to the floor -- well out of reach; how she knocked him on his back and pinned him beneath her; how the Elf struggled on, his tunic thoroughly shredded, exposing his chest and its many scratches; how the scantily-clad girl kept him pinned despite his valiant efforts, her hands-of-pulsing-energy holding his arms, her legs trapping his legs in a vice, her pelvis grinding into his. Perhaps at this point our Gentle Bard, recognizing the "implications" of the situation, would cease his singing and discretely excuse himself. But no worries, Gentle Reader, for we, at least, will remain a bit longer. "Oh dear," she said with mock sorrow. "Are you still trying to _win_? Tsk-tsk-tsk." A pout. "Poor little wolf." A risqué smile. "Why don't you forget about 'winning' and think about--" she moved her hips firmly against his "-- something else?" The Elf's heart leapt to his throat and he gasped. Part of him wanted to, if he was honest -- there was no denying the physical response she was coaxing out of him. But this was not a "seduction" -- it was a humiliation, a payback for his cockiness. That was all she wanted to accomplish here, he knew, even as his body continued to betray him. But it was hopeless -- she was too strong. And too damned _good_ at this. She pinned both his hands briefly with one paw, and with the other, ripped off what little remained of his tunic. "Ooooooooh," she crooned. "Poor little wolfie is hurt," she said, examining the scratches on his chest and doing another hip grind. Then she grinned mischievously. "Let me help you heal." Keeping her eyes on his for as long as possible, she lowered her head to his chest, and began licking the damaged skin in the vicinity of his neck. The Elf gasped involuntarily. She giggled, continued to lick him, and again ground her pelvis into his. The Elf saw only one way out of this. _Hhhhhhhhhheeeeeeeellllllllppppppppp_! His Big Sister suddenly recoiled in shock, still holding him down, but no longer doing anything with her tongue or hips. "But --" she stammered. "That's _cheating_!" Despite breathlessness, the Elf managed to respond. "What's fair in love and war, Big Sis?" He grinned. She pursed her lips together and stared at him balefully. Then she stood, extended her hand and helped him to his feet just as -- -- Shamaness entered the room. She looked aat the Elf with a little smile and said, "Hello, my name is 'Help'. I heard you calling." And then to both of them, "Tell me, my Pups -- how was today's training?" "Good, Shamaness," they replied in unison. "Are you finished, then?" "Yes, Shamaness." "Very well, then," she smiled knowingly. "Let's clean up this room, shall we? And then I have some things for you to do, Young Lady. And Young Sir? I believe Keeper needs a paw or two. But before that, why don't you both take a bath?" A little pause for effect. "Separately. With --" her smile widened just a tiny bit -- "cold water?" The two glanced at each other, both blushing. "Yes, Shamaness." The Elf and his Sister collected the staves and the remains of their clothing and departed the room, each bowing respectfully as they walked by Shamaness. When they were gone, Shamaness smiled to herself while shaking her head. "Pups!" she said. But now that she was alone, she could linger over the memory that had come flooding back to her when she saw the two half-naked, sweating pups on the floor ... a sparring session between her and Leader, before they were together, before they formed the Pack. She lost -- but only because she had _let_ him win. Sometimes a man needed that so he could feel important, otherwise he might lose his ... interest. The ruse had worked and they both ended up ... she shook it off, chuckling to herself, and left the room.

docs.title: Exorcism
docs.text: Exorcism -------- _Will_you_please_keep_UP_?! The Wolf snarled briefly, but refused to turn his head toward his pack sister. Jemi had been doing that almost the entire run and it was really getting on his nerves. Just because she's "Number 5" and I'm "Number 6". _We're_supposed_to_drag_him_CAREFULLY_, Marcus thought back to her. This was about the 6th or 7th time he'd responded that way. _SPEED_is_most_important_.__Leader_said_so_,_remember_? Also for about the 6th or 7th time. And she put on another burst of speed, forcing him to match. Behind them, secured to their lupine bodies via a crude harness, was a makeshift litter on which their still-unconscious Pack Keeper lay. "Thankfully unconscious," thought the Wolf -- else he'd loudly complain about how the litter banged and careened around the landscape thanks to his Sister's ideas about how the "lead dog" should behave. At least we're getting close, he thought. There ahead and to the left was the hill upon which Sleeping Wolf Rock stood. Seeing it filled his heart with joy, as it always did, and for a moment, he felt that all would be right in the world. This time he did glance over at his Sister -- and saw the same look on her face. Well, Gaea be praised, he thought -- she's got something else to think about for a moment besides how "slow" I run. _Sept_distress_howl_now_, she said. _Wait_, he contradicted. She was about to cuff him for insubordination -- she was, after all, the "senior wolf" in this situation -- but then she looked ahead and saw why Little Brother had said it. Ranolf the Leader glanced at Tamika the Keeper. Both were still in homid form. "Shift," he said. But Uziah the Shaman put a hand on each of their arms. "No," he said. "Claw and fang we'll not need here." Up ahead, two lupine figures came into view, running hard, but their gait was strange, as if -- ah yes, they were indeed dragging something behind them. Uziah crouched down and opened his bag. As he rummaged through it, he said, "Stop them right here, unhitch what they carry, and lay it flat on the ground." _It's_them_!, said Jemi. _The_Uktena_, replied Marcus. _How_did_they_know_? _They're_..._strange_like_that_. _Good_thing_! The two slowed down and stopped in front of the three Uktena. Without even a greeting, two of them promptly went to work on the harness, disconnecting them from their burden. The third was rubbing something between his hands and studying Keeper's face gravely. Tamika knelt down and put a hand on the head of each wolf. They looked at her, tongues hanging out, legs wobbly. "You did well," she said to them with a reassuring smile. "We'll take care of him now. Rest." The two wolves promptly hit the ground as if they'd been waiting for someone to say that. Uziah continued to rub his hands together as he studied Keeper's face. It was swollen and the boils stood out angrily, red with a small, green center. The Shaman finished rubbing his hands together, closed his eyes, and pressed a palm to each of Keeper's cheeks. Ranolf and Tamika waited silently. After half a minute, the Shaman opened his eyes, removed his hands, and dug in his bag. He came out with a small, leather charm. This he pressed between his hands while mumbling some words under his breath. His hands glowed for a moment, and when he opened them, the charm glowed. "The chest," he said. Ranolf reached over and pulled away the fabric to expose Keeper's chest, which was also covered with boils. Uziah carefully laid the still-glowing charm over Keeper's heart. Keeper suddenly stirred, gasping for breath. Uziah placed his hand on the injured Garou's head and again mumbled under his breath. Keeper's eyes snapped open and darted wildly about, and then rested on the Shaman's face. Uziah held the gaze and leaned a bit closer. "Name. Tribe. Pack. Rank," he said. Keeper's rapid breathing was the only sound. Then he clenched his teeth and trembled. Uziah gripped Keeper's jaw a little stronger and spoke again, louder than before. "NAME. TRIBE. PACK. RANK." Keeper's eyes slammed shut, his teeth chattered, and he groaned. Uziah sighed and pursed his lips together grimly. He glanced at Ranolf and Tamika, and jerked his head toward his patient. Ranolf placed a restraining hand on Keeper's left shoulder and left wrist. Tamika did the same on the right. Uziah straddled Keeper, using his legs to hold his patient's legs fast. Uziah leaned over again to stare into Keeper's face, his hand gripping Keeper's jaw again. Keeper's teeth were still locked together and he opened his eyes to return the Shaman's stare. "Whom do you serve?" demanded Uziah, keeping his eyes locked on Keeper's. Keeper's body tensed and jerked against them, but the three Uktena held him fast. Uziah demanded again, "Whom do you serve?" Keeper's body spasmed violently, but again they held him. A prolonged snarl welled up from his throat. The two lupus wolves got to their feet and whined. "Stay back," Tamika ordered sharply. "Do not fear!" Uziah leaned over more, bringing his face even closer to Keeper's and he gripped the chin harder. And with a tone of grim finality that compelled an answer, he spoke again. "WHOM ... DO ... YOU ... SERVE?" And amidst the constant snarl that boiled out of Keeper's throat, came scattered and distorted but recognizable words in response... "I ... serve ... the ... Eternal WYRM!" And with that, several things happened at once. Keeper's body bucked wildly, almost breaking free of the three who restrained him. From his throat issued a scream that was unlike any a Garou would make. His two lupus pack mates howled in fear and distress. The charm upon Keeper's chest lost its light and shattered. The sun went behind a cloud. Uziah dug quickly in his bag, came out with a small object, pressed it between his palms, and spoke swiftly in an unintelligible language. He opened his hands to reveal another glowing charm. While his two pack mates continued to restrain the jerking, screaming patient, the Shaman put his left hand behind Keeper's head. In his right hand he held the glowing charm and pressed it between Keeper's eyes. Keeper screamed again, louder and more desperate, his struggles increasing to frenzy. Uziah closed his eyes, held the charm in place, and continued to speak in that strange tongue. 20 seconds later, Keeper's body suddenly went limp. His boils broke open and oozed green pus. The charm's light had gone out and Uziah tossed it aside. He waved briefly at Ranolf and Tamika and the two released their grip. Uziah got off Keeper's legs and moved around to his side. He put a finger to Keeper's neck under the left ear, and nodded once. He lifted the left eyelid, then the right, and again nodded. He studied Keeper's face for a few minutes, saying nothing. No one moved. Finally, the Shaman leaned over and put his hand on Keeper's cheek. He tapped it gently a few times. "Awaken." Keeper stirred, groaning softly, as one might when coming out of a deep slumber. His eyes opened slowly and his gaze rested on Uziah's face above him. "Name. Tribe. Pack. Rank." Keeper coughed once, cleared his throat. And in a voice just above a whisper, answered. "Rikard ... Fianna ... Moon Runners ... Keeper." Uziah smiled gently and he spoke again. "Auspice and Devotion." Keeper again cleared his throat, and in a slightly louder voice, answered, "Dansair. Warrior of Ghosts, Master of Gaea's Strength." Uziah's smile widened and he nodded with satisfaction. "Welcome back to Gaea's embrace, Brave Warrior!" And Rikard of the Fianna, Keeper of the Moon Runners, Warrior of Ghosts and Master of Gaea's Strength, managed a tired smile in return. "Sleep now," commanded the Shaman. "Sleeeeeeeeep!" And as his hand caressed Rikard's forehead, Rikard's eyes closed and he breathed slowly and evenly. Uziah suddenly slumped forward, spent. Ranolf caught him and held him up. "Your patient is not the only one who needs rest, Shaman." Uziah nodded, breathing deeply. "A little, yes. He's out of danger, but still needs care. We may bring him to the Sept now." Ranolf and Tamika picked up the litter and walked off eastward. The two still-exhausted wolves and the equally-exhausted Shaman followed.

docs.title: The Gift
docs.text: The Gift -------- "Ah! Come in, Pup, come in!" smiled Leader. "Do sit down." They both took a seat on the rugs in Leader's study and faced each other. "How goes it with you, Pup?" The Elf blinked, a bit surprised. "Fine, thank you, Leader." "No, uhm, ill effects? From the, er, 'possession'?" The Elf sighed and ground his teeth. But he kept his eyes on Leader and answered evenly. "No, Leader." Leader chuckled. "Sorry, Pup -- couldn't resist." Leader sighed with a smile. "It seems Keeper has been doing well lately." The Elf rolled his eyes. Indeed, Keeper's feet never seemed to touch the floor since that evening of the Elf's return from his errands in the city. In fact, that's where Keeper was today -- in the city. And it wasn't too difficult to guess _where_. Leader cleared his throat and changed the subject. "Let me tell you why I want to talk to you. Here." Leader handed the Elf a sheet of parchment. On it were the same strange symbols that adorned the envelope that the Elf had picked up for Leader from the post office. The Elf looked at Leader with a little smile and shrugged helplessly. Leader returned the smile and took the letter back. "I shall translate it for you. It says: 'my dearest Nagha. Thank you kindly for your letter -- always wonderful to hear from you, my old friend! To the subject of your enquiry, the answer is an enthusiastic yes. It would be an honor for me to welcome your understudy to my humble dojo for the training you desire for him. Please have him present himself bearing this letter and all shall be taken care of. I truly look forward to working with him and I pray that my meager efforts will be a positive force on his life's journey. Gratefully yours, Hashai-Sen.'" Leader folded the parchment, placed it in its envelope, and handed it to the Elf, who frowned as he took it. "You mean to send me away. Have I displeased you in some way, Leader?" Leader blinked in surprise. "On the contrary, Pup!" He leaned forward a little and stared into the Elf's eyes. "I am very pleased with you. We all are. You have grown much since coming to us. And now you are ready for this." Leader leaned back, and got a far-away look in his eyes. "Hashai- Sen is an old friend of mine, as you heard in the letter. His dojo is in Kerei, which, as you know, is just south of Souvrael, the place of my birth. As you also know, I am a Silent Strider." The Elf knew. Among other things, that Garou Tribe was renowned for its ability as couriers, swiftly crossing even the most inhospitable areas to reliably make their deliveries over great distances. Leader was very well-travelled, and that was an understatement. Of course, he had cut back those activities after creating the Pack, but it was still in his nature, and the Elf believed that Leader would one day return to it. "Anyway," continued Leader, "to make a long story short, I happened to be in the right place at the right time to save Hashai-Sen's life. I am not one to 'collect debts', but circumstances being what they are, I find this opportunity simply too good to pass up. "There are two things at work here. The first is your ability with staves. I have watched you hone your skills and you've become quite remarkable!" The Elf dropped his eyes. "I do my best, Leader." "Indeed," replied Leader with a little smile. "Sometimes I have the impression that you prefer your elven form so that you may use the staff." The Elf shrugged a bit and smirked. "Can't wield a staff with paws." "Indeed not," grinned Leader. "The second thing is that Hashai- Sen's dojo specializes in the study of staves and polearms." The Elf's eyes widened slightly. "And he has no equal," added Leader. "Get the picture, Pup?" The Elf did, as a matter of fact, and he smiled like a child at Christmas. "When do I leave?" Leader laughed. "That anxious, are you? Well, calm down -- the Pack has a few things to take care of before you go. 'Pack', I said -- and that includes YOU, Pup. And there's a Revel coming up -- and you will be there! You may leave thee day after." Leader stood and the Elf followed. "Now then, Pup, there's something you'll need to take with you." His gaze drifted to the doorway. The Elf looked that way too and saw his older sister -- the one who always found those "exotic" weapons and gear. She entered the room with a smile. In her arms was the wrapped thing that the Elf had picked up from Taylor. She presented it to the Elf. "This is for you, little brother." The Elf took it from her gingerly, feeling a lump in his throat. It was still wrapped in the same condition in which he'd picked it up. "Go ahead," she smiled. "Open it!" Leader was also smiling. Carefully, the Elf untied the strings and pushed the fabric out of the way. Revealed before him was an ebony, hardwood staff about 2.5 meters long. The butt end of it was thicker and looked to be made for thrusting. His eyes travelled down the length of it to the forward end, which was curved. That's rather odd, he thought. Why should a wooden staff be curved? He gingerly picked it up -- how comfortably _heavy_ it was!. He moved it left and right, testing it, getting its feel. Suddenly he swung it in graceful 360 arc, grinning at the satisfying >>>WHOOSH<<< it made. He looked more closely at that strange curve on the front end. It was then that he noticed the seam about half a meter down from the forward tip. Could it be...? But of course! As his right hand held the staff in the middle, he placed his left forward of the seam -- and yanked. The sheath came off smoothly, making that delightful metal-on-metal sound as when one draws a sword. At first, he couldn't see a thing, for the blade caught the light of the room perfectly, blinding him. The Elf turned the blade away from the angle of the light so that he could gaze at it, and his breath caught. He tried to think of how to describe it -- and found that he needed another word for "beautiful". It was almost half a meter long, curved, and sharpened on one side. Frowning, he brought the blade closer so that he could better see something that was etched onto it at the point just before it joined the shaft -- and discovered that it was his name. Leader and Sister were still waiting. Finally, Sister couldn't take it any more. "Do you like it, Pup?" she asked. The Elf looked at her, his mouth hanging open. He looked back at the staff and ran a finger carefully up and down the blunt edge of the blade. Slowly and softly, he replied, "It's the most beautiful thing I've ever seen." He looked back at his Older Sister and smiled broadly, came forward, and hugged her. "Thanks so much! By the way -- what is it?" "It's called a 'naginata'," smiled Sister. "Naginata," repeated the Elf, staring at it in wonder. "And where you're going, Pup," added Leader, "you're going to learn how to use it properly!" The Elf wasn't sure at all how he would make it through the time that remained until his departure.

docs.title: Back Home
docs.text: Back Home --------- The Elf emerged from the Witch's home and let out a mighty rush of breath. Gaea help me, he thought -- if that was just "foreplay" then I'm a Dead Elf if she ever takes it _all_ the way! He reached up to touch his lips, but then decided not to -- that would defile them! He stood in the street, panting, fighting for composure. After a while, he felt that he had himself somewhat under control. He looked at the sky. The sun was setting. Time to get back home. It was dark as he returned to the pack cave to find everyone gathered in the main room. "Took you long enough!" teased his young sister. "Bet you didn't even get everything, did you?" Without a word, the Elf handed her the small bag that the Witch had given him. She took it with a sceptical look and opened it. Her breath caught. She reached in and pulled out the contents. "Ohhhhhh, they're _beautiful_!" she gushed, holding the undergarments up and turning them this way and that. "Thank you, little brother!" she said, kissing him on the cheek. Under normal conditions, he would have blushed, but after all he'd been through today, it didn't embarrass him one bit. "Thanks for the weapon pickup!" exclaimed his older sister, giving him a hug with her left arm while her right held onto the wrapped Whatever-It-Was. Leader examined the envelope and the Elf had the distinct impression that Leader could actually read the strange characters. Then Leader put the letter inside his tunic for later. "Shamaness, Moon said he needs about 10 days for the necklace repair. He's sorry that he's a bit swamped lately." "No problem, Pup, and thanks," she replied. "Hey, Pup! What about me, then?" asked Keeper. The Elf closed his eyes and sighed mightily. He'd been dreading this one. Actually, he'd been waiting for the others to leave the room. But they showed absolutely no sign of doing so. In fact, Keeper's question seemed to have made them curious and they all looked at the Elf expectantly. "Uhm, Keeper, could we do that, uh, later, please?" Keeper frowned and glanced sideways. He looked a bit like a little kid who's been told that he can have a cookie -- later. "Well, did you deliver my letter?" The Elf nodded. "And...?" The Elf blinked. "Well, what did she say, Pup? Come on, now! You're _killing_ me here," he chuckled. His two sisters snickered. Leader and Shamaness simply smiled, enjoying the show. "Didn't she have a message for me, Pup?" Keeper was starting to look really disappointed now. At the word "message", the Elf seemed to recover and remember something. With a heavy sigh of resignation, he asked, "Keeper, is it your wish that I deliver her message to you right now, right here?" Keeper blinked. "Well ... yeah!" The Elf pursed his lips together once. He glanced around at the four other pack members present and then back at Keeper. He bowed his head. "By your command." He breathed once deeply and rolled his eyes up to his head. When he brought them back down, there was ... a change. The Elf was still there ... but something else was, too. Lightning fast, the Elf swung out and struck Keeper on the cheek with an open hand. Hard. The >>>CRACK<<< made the whole room jump. Mouths fell open. "BASTARD!" spat the Elf, or The-Power-Working-Through-the-Elf. Again the Elf swung, this time striking Keeper's other cheek just as hard. Then he punched Keeper in the solar plexus. His aim was true, his strike was hard, and Keeper went down. The shock of it all was so complete that nobody moved. All simply stared, gaping at the incredible scene. Keeper lay on the floor gasping. The Elf (and whatever else was in the Elf) stood over him, sneering down. "Now listen to me, you pathetic little _worm_! Do you have any idea what you did to me? Well, I'll tell you! Worm! The spring festival! You remember it, don't you, you puke, you vomitous piece of _shit_?" Keeper coughed, trying to come out of it. He managed a nod. "You said you were just going to the bar to get some peach juice!" The Elf/Witch sneered. "Poor little mangy wolfie can't have any alcohol, can he? Corrupts and defiles, doesn't it? Has to drink his ... peeeeeach juice! And so I waited and waited and waited! Did you come back? No! I had to go look for you! And where did I find you? Speak!" Keeper coughed again and gasped, "The elm tree." "Ah yeeeessssssss! The beautiful elm tree at the edge of the festival grounds. Such a romantic spot, wasn't it? FOR YOU AND FOR _HER_, YOU LIMP-DICK METIS!!" The Elf/Witch made as if to kick Keeper, who cringed and then relaxed as the kick did not arrive. And at that moment, it did arrive. Keeper yelped. But truth be told, it was the "metis" that hurt far more than the kick. "And I caused a scene, right? I went waaaaaay overboard, didn't I? I grabbed her by the hair and pulled her away from you. I slapped her around. I put a curse on her that made her turn ugly, right? Wrinkles, warts, gray skin? Sent the poor, little, innocent thing running away screaming, didn't I? Jealousy is one thing, but I was way out of line, wasn't I? Over the top? Went too far, right? I was totally out-of-control, yes? Abusing my powers for personal revenge, wasn't I? ISN'T THAT THE _BULLSHIT_ YOU THREW AT ME?!" Keeper managed to reach his knees, panting. "Yes," he whispered. "Ohhhhh, YES!" sneered the Witch/Elf. "You were sooooo upset, weren't you? I couldn't _explain_! You wouldn't _let_ me! I couldn't get a word in edgewise on you, could I, you foolish little buffoon, you consummate ignoramus!? You just kept on going and going with your self-righteous tirade about _my_ horrid conduct! GAGH! You stupid, moronic, imbecilic, complete and total SHIT-FOR-BRAINS IDIOT!!!" The spectators were no longer gaping. In fact, they had their hands over their mouths trying to hold their laughter down, lest it distract from the scene still playing out. The Elf's younger sister didn't quite make it, and loudly cackled. "Oooohhhhhhh, but you found out later, didn't you, _worm_?" Keeper nodded, still clutching his chest. "Yes," he gasped. "SAY IT!" Keeper now stood up, if a bit unsteadily. "That she was a ... a succubus--" Everyone blinked. "--that she was about to drain my life force when you found us. You saved me. And she turned ugly because you broke the illusion, not because you cursed her. You revealed her for what she was. You chased her away. I am sorry. I should have trusted you. I'll never doubt you again. Thank you." Now the Elf/Witch relaxed, nodding. "Yes. So much you wrote in your letter, which this Elf--" pointing to him/herself "-- was kind enough to deliver to me." The voice softened, and the Elf/Witch smiled. "And so much more you wrote besides that." The Elf/Witch suddenly swung out again, and Keeper winced in anticipation. But the hand went behind his neck, and pulled him into a kiss -- a long, deep one. Eyes popped. "Oh, my Good Gaea!" gasped Older Sister, while Younger simply gaped. Leader's open mouth stretched into a disbelieving smile. Shamaness involuntarily made a blessing to ward off evil. Finally, the kiss broke. And as it did, whatever was in the Elf departed, leaving Elf and Keeper all by themselves. The Elf, realizing now what had happened, broke away from Keeper, spat several times and wiped his mouth savagely with the back of his hand. Leader, Shamaness, and his sisters, finally able to release their pent-up emotions, rolled on the floor, laughing until tears came. Keeper just stood there, an angelic smile on his face, eyes on something far away. The Elf decided that he'd fulfilled his tasks for this day -- above and beyond any _reasonable_ call of duty -- and hastily retreated to the relative serenity of his room. Behind him, the laughter continued, and Keeper let loose a howl of pure joy.

docs.title: Hunted
docs.text: Hunted ------ The young barbarian girl surveyed the carnage that was, just a short while ago, the "animal pen" ... three chickens, a pig, and the milk-cow ... all dead now. Mutilated, actually, their bellies ripped open and some of the internal organs missing. Blood everywhere. The horrific scene should have given her a fright, but it did not. Instead she felt only a cold numbness. These animals, few as they were, were her family's only livelihood. Without them, they were hopelessly destitute. Not that they were rich before -- far from it. The brutal tax policy of the Lord Landholder in these parts guaranteed that the peasants had the bare minimum for survival -- and nothing more. Her father had succumbed to illness two years back -- a curable condition, she was sure, if only the family had been able to afford a surgeon. Now she, her mother, and her younger sister did what they could. She was glad of one thing -- that the two of them were currently in the fields; they didn't need to see this. Yet. It bought her some time, time to find her center, survey the situation calmly, suppress the rage and panic that were both trying to boil up and take control. It had been either a wolf or a very large and nasty dog, that was clear from the paw prints, the random bits of fur, and the bite marks. But the killing scene was too chaotic for a normal hunt -- too much meat left on the corpses, too much blood left lying. Only the vitals -- heart and liver -- were missing from each carcass; as if the attacker had needed the maximum amount of blood and sustenance in the quickest possible time and couldn't afford to be nice about it. Had anyone been able to read the girl's mind at this time, they would have been quite surprised by her ability to see all this. After all, what did peasant girls of 14 years know about hunting and killing? At 15, they were expected to be happily married and producing babies; so at her age, this girl with no fiancé had enough to worry about, thank you! But marriage and family were far from this girl's mind. Not that she lacked for young men who were interested, mind you, and not because she didn't find men interesting; it was just that she had another passion, something that was very un-ladylike, something that would cause a scandal if it ever came out, something that she hid even from her mother. This girl was a huntress, and not too shabby about it, if anyone cared. In fact, she was certain she could feed her family well enough with the kills she brought in -- if the Lord Landholder permitted hunting on his land, which he did not, so that would make her a poacher. And there was so much work to do on the farm since her father passed that there was no real time for it anyway. So they lived, as best they could, from the animals. Which were now all dead. The numbness she felt was quickly giving itself over to iciness. There was something else about the murder scene -- it wasn't more than a few minutes old. Sudden resolve took her. Nothing more to lose, now. She would-- --horses. Coming this way fast. She emergeed from the barn just as the Landholder's soldiers -- six of them, she counted -- reined up in a swirl of dust. "Ho, girl!" said the apparent leader. "Have you seen the wolf we are tracking? A big, grey one, with massive teeth and an ill temper? It broke into the lord's stables and slew his prize stallion, if you please! Was feasting on it greedily when we attacked, too. The beast took down four of my brave men before we wounded it, and now we give chase. Our lord commands that its hide should hang from the battlements before sundown or it will be _our_ hides that hang! What know ye, girl? Speak quickly!" The man disgusted her. He and his "soldiers" were better known among the peasants for the "liberties" they took than for their ability in a fight. His bravado was meant to impress her. This girl did that to him. Oh, but if he only had the _time_ -- there were so many better things he could be doing with this girl than enquiring about a wolf. But he had his orders -- his neck was on the line, so such niceties would have to wait. Perhaps on the way back, after they took care of the wolf... The girl was well aware of the man's thinking, as women in such situations always are, even if the men are too dim-witted to realize it. She studied his body too. Specifically, the neck -- the exposed flesh just above the collar of the breastplate and below the helm. One shot was all she needed. If she only had her bow. If only there weren't five others. She said nothing, still filled with ice. She simply jerked her head toward the barn. One of the men dismounted and went inside, and then came quickly out. "We're hot on the trail, Captain!" Really, thought the girl. How can you tell? "Quickly, then!" He nodded to the girl and grinned, exposing yellow teeth. "Miss." And they galloped off. In the wrong direction. With the distraction finally ended, she ran to the corner of the barn and dug through the hay until she found the blanket. She unfolded it to reveal a bow and a quiver of arrows -- her most prized possessions in the entire world. A moment later she -- not the soldiers -- was "hot on the wolf's trail". It wasn't terribly difficult -- the wolf was indeed wounded. Not only did this slow it down, but also made it careless about hiding its tracks; not to mention the trail of blood -- blood that the wolf was still losing. She shook her head inwardly at the stupidity of the soldiers and continued on, gaining on the wolf. In not much time at all, she had closed the distance. Just up ahead, she thought, as she crawled as quietly as possible through the brush. She knew the place where the wolf was because it was a place she liked to visit, when she had time -- a pool in the forest, with a little waterfall from the rock face above it. A place for peace, tranquillity, inner reflection. And a place where this wolf has come to die, even if it doesn't know it, she thought, as she nimbly plucked an arrow from her quiver and expertly nocked it. She could hear the wolf splashing around in the water, the cadence of the waterfall altered as it broke on the wolf's body before falling into the pool. One final nudge forward, the arrow nocked and ready, she would _see_ her target, be able to make the final aim and let the arrow fly. Just another little bit and... ...she could see. And caught her breath. Her jaw fell open. For there was no wolf in the pool. It was a man. But not a "man" -- what was the word for it? Elf! That wass it. An elf. A male elf. In her pool. A male elf bathing naked in her pool. She had never seen an elf before. She had never been far enough from home to believe that such creatures exist. But here it was, straight out of a fairy tale. The girl shook her head briefly. She had momentarily forgotten why she was here. Then she remembered. She had been tracking a wolf. A wolf that had just destroyed her family's existence. She had tracked it flawlessly. The wolf _must_ be here. Right _here_. But there was no wolf -- there was only this Elf. The Elf suddenly gasped, biting his teeth together in pain, but the girl couldn't see why. Then the Elf turned around and she saw the shaft of the arrow stuck in his side, an arrow that the Elf was now slowly pulling out. With a final gasp, he pulled it out completely and tossed it aside. Now she could see two other wounds, long and jagged slices that must have come from swords. All three were still bleeding, but not as much as she would have expected. And as she watched, she was amazed to see the wounds closing right before her eyes. The elf was breathing deeply now, eyes closed, concentration inward. It occurred to her that she was close enough for him to sense her presence -- she had heard elves could do such things -- but she was unable to move, so spellbound did this strange scene hold her. The wounds were now completely closed. Only scars remained, but these too were fading. The Elf sighed with satisfaction and opened his eyes. He gathered his long blond hair in both hands, wringing it out, exposing his pointed ears. Then he slowly left the pool. And the girl carefully followed, not wanting to lose sight of him, curiosity overcoming good sense.
