Now the Elf stopped and appeared to be studying the ground, shifting his gaze from side to side as if searching for something. Suddenly his eyes locked onto a spot and he dropped to his knees. As the amazed girl watched, the Elf plunged his hands into the solid ground as if it were sand -- and _dug_! Within a few seconds, there was a hole in the ground that was bigger and deeper than a man could have made in a few minutes had he used a _shovel_. And the Elf wasn't even dirty! Out of the hole came a large sack, whose contents the Elf dumped on the ground beside him: clothing, leather armor, boots, gloves, some provisions, and an oaken quarterstaff. The elf quickly dressed, slung the sack over his shoulder, and took up the staff. He was about to leave, but then suddenly stiffened. So did the girl -- she realized now she had been too careless; but she didn't dare move now, for that would give her away immediately. She held her breath and tried to tell her heart to stop beating. The Elf sniffed. One pointed ear twitched. And then the corner of his mouth turned up a bit, he relaxed, and turned his gaze unerringly to the bush behind which the girl was hidden. The girl, eyes wide, heart in her throat, simply waited, being as still as she could. The Elf smiled and dropped to one knee. He laid his staff down, picked up a twig and appeared to be writing something on the ground. He finished, stood up, slung his sack over his shoulder, picked up his staff -- and left. The girl waited, not moving until she thought that the Elf was far enough away. Then she let out her pent-up breath in a rush and gulped in fresh air to her starved lungs. When her heartbeat slowed down somewhat, she emerged from her hiding place and carefully approached the spot where the Elf had been. He had left a leather pouch, she now noticed. But first she turned her attention to the ground next to the pouch, where the Elf had indeed written something in the dirt... "Please forgive me about your livestock, but the Wolf's need was very great." The girl blinked, trying to digest the implications of it. But before going on with that for too long, she opened the pouch. Gold coins. LOTS of gold coins! More gold coins than she had ever seen in her life. Enough gold coins to buy dozens of chickens, pigs, and cows. Enough to get a better bow, a nicer quiver, an endless supply of arrows. Enough for her, her mother and sister to move away from the Lord Landholder's realm and start a new life somewhere else. The girl tied the pouch to her belt. She smoothed over the ground upon which the Elf had written, erasing his words. Then she took up her bow and headed home. Just a few steps later she was singing.

docs.title: Initiation
docs.text: Initiation ---------- The Elf -- his entire body now covered in the strange ointment and the Beast ROARING inside him -- shouted his allegiance to the Spirit of the Wolf. A strange power seized control of his mind and body. He felt an inner pressure build and quickly push against the limits of his flesh. The Elf grimaced with the effort of holding himself in one piece, fists clenching, eyes closing tightly, teeth grinding together. And then the pressure exploded out of him, finding egress through every orifice of his body and pore of his skin. Suddenly free of his exertion, the Elf went limp. But a field of light and energy now surrounded him and held him in place, kept him from falling to the ground. And despite his closed eyes, the Elf saw very clearly that it was the Beast -- no longer merely inside him, but now all around him as well, holding him spellbound in its irresistible embrace. Yes, the Elf said, talking to the Beast, not with coarse and limited speech, but with pure and unlimited mental power. I know you now, the Elf said. You are me. And I am you. We are one. We always have been. And now we always will be. As if in answer, the light that was the Beast suddenly blazed, and in his mind's eye, the Elf saw the light take form. The Beast opened its jaws, exposed sharp, gleaming teeth -- and sank them into the Elf's shoulder. The Elf convulsed and cried out. Was it pain or pleasure? If anyone observed the scene, they would not be able to tell; indeed the Elf, recalling it later, would not know. And it didn't matter. All that mattered was that the Elf and the Beast were united; the two aspects of the Elf's being now irrevocably one. The Beast released its grip on the Elf's shoulder and, its work complete, disappeared back into the Elf. No longer held up by the Beast's energy, the Elf crumpled to the ground and knew no more. ... The sounds were the first thing the Elf registered as his consciousness slowly emerged from the darkness. Unnaturally many and loud, they were; this clearing in the woods wasn't so teeming with life when he arrived, he was sure of it. Next came the odors. There was a living thing very close by -- had to be the Old Man. By smell alone, the Elf could now detect the Old Man's advanced age but also his sturdiness. There must also be many woodland creatures close by -- bears, rabbits, deer, rodents, birds -- he could smell them all. He didn't remember the little clearing in the woods holding so much life! Was he still in the clearing? Or had the Old Man moved him somewhere else while the Elf lay unconscious? That thought brought him to ... ... open his eyes. Yes, still in the clearing. And the Old Man was there, sitting in a meditative posture in front of a bowl of creamy fluid, eyes closed, chanting, occasionally waving his hands over the bowl. But where were all the woodland creatures? The Elf still clearly smelled them; many of the scents so strong that he reasoned the animals had to be in the very clearing -- yet his eyes saw only the Old Man and himself. He heard a bird cry -- a high-pitched tone that he had never heard before, even though he knew every variety of bird in these woods. The Elf stood up stiffly, his muscles coming only slowly back to life. As he reached full height, he stretched his shoulders -- and felt pain there near to his neck. His hand found its way instinctively to the spot, and felt -- -- the Elf twisted his head around to see itt ... two markings ... puncture wounds that broke the skin, and a short, jagged rip extending from each point. A bite mark. The Mark of the Beast. And suddenly it all came back to him. And he understood. The odors he smelled so clearly were not creatures in his immediate vicinity -- they were farther away. The high-pitched bird cry was in an audio range that no humanoid ear could ever sense. He was no longer the Elf -- he was Elf, Beast, and Wolf, all rolled into one. A dull thudding sound brought him back to the present. The Old Man had finished his incantation and had just set the bowl, now refilled, down on the tree stump where it had been before the Elf had picked it up and unceremoniously dumped it over himself. And now the Old Man turned to face the Elf, one eyebrow slightly raised, eyes twinkling. And the Elf heard the Old Man speak, but it sounded more like singing, or a wolf howling, and the Elf could hear it only in his mind. That the Elf was now a Lone Wolf of the Garou; that he must learn what that means; that he must listen to the Stories; that he must find the Balance between Wolf and Human-kind; and that he must always fight the Unnatural and That Which is Against Gaia. And the Elf understood because the message spoke directly to his Intuition where, freed from the bonds of logic and materialistic delusion, one may unerringly discern the Truth. The Old Man nodded, satisfied. He then stepped to one side and gestured with one hand, indicating a hole in the ground that the Elf had not seen before, but somehow he knew that it must have been there all the time. With his heightened sense of smell, he could now perceive the mixture of odors wafting from the hole; taken altogether, it smelled like ... ... Home. The Elf wriggled down into the hole -- it was just big enough for him -- and disappeared.

docs.title: A Difficult Mission
docs.text: A Difficult Mission ------------------- The cold bath had actually been a wonderful idea, thought the Elf, smiling to himself as he dried off. He had broken quite a sweat during the just-concluded sparring session with his pack sister and wasn't it wonderful to feel clean again! And then there was the "other sweat" he had broken when she had tried to ... the Elf shuddered, trying to forget it, not quite succeeding. A part of him still couldn't believe that he had interrupted the course of nature by calling telepathically for help from the pack. Another part of him was damned glad of it. And for the cold water. The Elf dressed and, per Shamaness' request (order), went to find Keeper to see what it was that he "needed a paw or two with." He didn't need to call out, ask anyone, or even use the pack's telepathy -- one sniff of the air in the cave told him where everyone was. "Ah, pup! There you are at last," smiled Keeper as the Elf entered the room. "Your bath was good? And took care of your ... needs?" He grinned knowingly. The Elf bit his tongue and bowed his head slightly. "Keeper." The Elf liked Keeper, but then, so did everyone, even those not in the pack. (Especially the females). Keeper was a bit smaller than average in height and build, with a round face that almost always had a smile on it. His easy-going nature, quick wit, and effortless humor made him quite the hit at any social gathering. (Especially with the lady-wolves). Except when Leader was gone and Keeper was in charge -- then it was no-nonsense, strictly by- the-Litany, and Gaea help you if you didn't toe the line! But Leader was around today, so the Elf was happy to see that Keeper was his usual, jovial self. "And what may I do for you, Keeper?" enquired the Elf. "Heh-heh! Not just for _me_, Pup," he grinned and gestured with a finger. "For everybody!" "Hmph," snorted the Elf. "Let me think," he said with mock thoughtfulness. "I suppose it's my turn to--" "--go shopping for the pack?! YES, Pup! You're RIGHT! You win the dinette set and the trip to Volcano Island, woo woo!" laughed Keeper, and he broke into a little song and dance. Well, "dance" was a dubious term, because it didn't resemble any of the dances of the Garou. Keeper sort of jerked his hips from side-to-side, rotated them, thrust his pelvis back and forth, and mixed it all together. Keeper called this the "bump-and-grind". Elf believed that perhaps in some far away place in some far away time, this thing might actually be popular. And as Keeper did the "bump-and-grind", he sang a little ditty, no doubt something he'd just pulled out of the air... _Shop_!__Shop_!__'Til_ya'_drop_! Bump-grind-grind-bump. _Shop!__Shop!__NEVER_stop_! Grind-bump-bump-grind. Keeper was the absolute, hands-down hit at the revels -- all the females wanted to be near him while the males wished they could move _like_ him -- or kill him out of jealousy. Some had actually challenged him because of it, but had naturally given some other reason for it. No matter -- Keeper hadn't lost a challenge yet, which of course made him even _more_ desirable, etc. Keeper caught the Elf's eye, looked in mock confusion at his own hips, which were _still_ bumping and grinding, placed his hands on them firmly, and fought them to a standstill. When they were still, he released his hands, at which point his hips immediately did another bump, so he again slapped his hands onto them, this time wincing with the effort of making them stop, while grinning "apologetically" at the Elf. He removed his hands more carefully, intently watching his pelvic area for any sign of a relapse. When there was none, Keeper nodded with satisfaction. "Sorry about that, Pup," he smirked. "But when the rhythm takes me..." He chuckled. "Indeed," replied the Elf, trying to appear serious, but unable to suppress a grin. "Well," said Keeper, back in something-resembling-business-mode, "Let's go over the list, then, shall we? Now ... in addition to the normal provisions, etc., Leader is expecting an important letter from over the sea, so you need to stop by the post office. Shamaness needs this necklace repaired -- he handed the Elf a small leather pouch -- so that's a trip to Moon's. Your older sister needs a weapon pickup -- Taylor will know, and -- this just in! -- your younger sister was here a minute ago -- she needs a new thong." The Elf stared. "She needs a new WHAT?!" Keeper blinked. "A new thong. It's an undergarment that--" "I _know_ what it is!" replied the Elf testily. His head suddenly hurt him and he rubbed his temple. Keeper chuckled. "Well, she said that it got -- damaged -- during your little sparring match. Must have been quite a match!" mused Keeper cheerfully. The Elf groaned, hand still on his head. "And since it was a matching set, she said she'll also need a new brassiere." "Heh!" replied the Elf, throwing up his hands. "Have TWO!" Then he sighed. "Do I _have_ to?" "Now, Pup," replied Keeper gently. "You know the rules. We all take turns with these errand runs. And we all get what the other needs, no exceptions." The Elf sighed, intentionally drawing it out to calm himself, and nodded. He knew very well. "It's like this Keeper," he said. "It's always a privilege to do whatever test Leader or you put before me. Heh -- on the last two, I almost died, but that was all right, because I was doing what I'm supposed to do, what I know _how_ to do. But this! I have absolutely _no_ idea how to go about _this_! Tell me to storm the city walls alone with both hind legs tied and I'll do it. Ask me to have lunch with a dozen lava worms without _becoming_ lunch and I'll get right down to Underworld. Tell me to personally check the weather in the heart of Malfeas and I'll be on my way. But _this_?! Where in all the Land do I find a -- a thong and matching brassiere, for the love of Luna?!" Keeper's eyes twinkled. "Ah, but I've not yet told what you must do for _me_, and therein lies your solution, my lucky Pup!" Keeper grinned and handed the Elf a small scroll. "Take this to the witch who lives off the main road in the direction of the docks. You know the one?" The Elf nodded, and Keeper continued, "She'll help you with your sister's ... exotic apparel needs." He smirked. The Elf gave Keeper a deeply doubtful look as he took the scroll. Keeper just winked at him. Sighing, the Elf made his way to the exit and hit the road toward the City.

docs.title: The Ointment
docs.text: The Ointment ------------ The Elf extended his hand toward the bowl of strange ointment and dipped the tip of his right index finger into it. The total absence of warmth or cold told him that the ointment was the exact same temperature as his body. Under normal circumstances, this fact might have seemed strange to him, but then "strange" seemed to be the norm in this place, so he just went with it. He slowly pulled his hand back and held it before him at eye level. He had dipped his finger up to the first knuckle, but he noticed that the ointment was spreading all by itself. It now covered his finger almost to the second knuckle, and it continued onward. Everywhere it touched, it activated the nerves, sending an exhilarating tingle through him. But he also perceived that, as it spread, it thinned out, and he realized it was losing its potency -- whatever the ointment was meant to do, it would not come to fruition with the little bit that he had allowed to touch his skin. He was suddenly aware of the Beast again. It was still there where he had left it -- in the forefront of his conscious mind, no longer buried. And with the application of the ointment, he could see the Beast a little more clearly, but now that extra clarity was receding from his mind even as the ointment dried on his skin and dissipated. The Elf again touched the ointment, this time immersing his entire right hand in it before pulling away. Now the sensations came stronger, emanating from his creamed hand and quickly spreading to his entire body. The Elf shuddered with an obscure pleasure. His eyes rolled up to his forehead and he clearly saw the Beast lift its head and snarl. The ointment quickly spread up his right arm, reached the shoulder ... and began to thin out. The sensations receded and the Beast closed its mouth. No. The thought popped into the Elf's mind as he realized the effect was leaving him again. No. No! He thought of The Dream again, The Dream that always left him right when it was getting to the point, tantalized him with a secret that was just beyond his conscious grasp as he woke from it -- he the Hunter pursuing the Prey through the deep woods, the trees flying past him as he ran (flew?) on limbs he couldn't have. But now the ointment had worked on him and he saw the dream clearly, the parts that were previously only hinted at now in stark relief... ...he was the Wolf. His unnatural speed came from _four_ legs, not two. His front legs pulled his body forward, left the ground, the hind legs pushed him onward, left the ground, the front legs came down again, pulled, lifted, the hind legs again ... pull ... push. Pull-push-pull-push ... da da DUM da da DUM da da DUM. The coordination perfect, propelling him along with a velocity that no biped could ever match. And his incredible sense of smell? His wolfen snout with its hypersensitive nose, the foremost portion of his quadruped anatomy, stuck out in front of him as he ran, homing in unerringly on the scent of the Prey fleeing him up ahead. He smelled it again -- clearer than ever before -- its perspiration, its shit, the earth it kicked up, and above all, the wonderfully intoxicating scent of its Mortal Fear. And though he couldn't yet see it, he knew now that it was a stag -- a big one. And then, as he rounded a bennd, he saw it. Not just any stag -- the White Stag! He slobbered uncontrollably as he closed the last distance, clamped his my-what-big-teeth-I-have jaw on the underside of its neck, bit down for all he was worth, and shook. The blood of the White Stag drenched his face and as he eagerly gulped it down, he felt an ecstasy that was purer and infinitely more pleasurable than anything he'd ever experienced. And then the Elf... ...snapped out of it and realized that the ointment had again dried without completing its work. And again his mind screamed NO! No more would he be denied. He grasped the collar of his tunic with both hands and gave a mighty yank, tearing the fabric away in one swipe. He plunged both hands into the bowl and splashed the ointment unashamedly on his chest. It spread quickly over his torso, and the Beast howled its pleasure. But what if it _still_ would not be enough?! No! The Elf grasped the bowl itself, lifted it high above his head -- and turned it over. And as its entire contents splashed down upon his upturned face, saturated his long, blond hair, ran down his back and chest, spread and enveloped his entire body, and as the Beast within him ROARED -- -- the Elf shouted his allegiance to the Spiirit of the Wolf.

docs.title: The Old Man
docs.text: The Old Man ----------- The Elf stood before the Old Man and weighed a decision that would alter his life. Forever and irrevocably. The Old Man had fallen silent after talking for quite a long time -- how long exactly, the Elf did not know. Nor did he care. He had long ceased to be concerned at all about the passage of time, so fascinating had he found the Old Man's ramblings. And to be sure, the Old Man had only talked so long because the Elf had insisted on asking him so many questions -- probably more than what most visitors wanted to know -- but then the Elf was not one to be hasty about such a decision, and happy to let the Old Man take as long as he wanted. For his part, the Old Man seemed content to answer any question the Elf posed, as if he had nothing else to do in life. The Elf guessed that that was not far from the truth. The small clearing in which the Old Man and the Elf stood was part of a larger forest to the southwest of the City. It was not exactly a "secret" place, for anyone exploring the forest would, if they were thorough, eventually stumble upon it. But most people who came here -- the Elf included -- did so because they were _drawn_ here. And what drew them? The Elf could only speak for himself (were he indeed to speak of it at all, which he had never done to anyone): it had been a nagging and compelling feeling that _something_ -- some part of him -- was missing. Well, not exactly "missing". Perhaps "unfulfilled", or "suppressed". Deeply buried until some catalyst pulled it from the depths of the subconscious. It had started with dreams. Surreal visions they had been. The type of dream where one knows one is dreaming, but cannot stop it, and does not _want_ to stop it, and then it ends by itself, leaving one strangely bereft of something that one held dear, but only realizing it at the end. There was one dream that was clearer than any of them, and it swiftly passed before his mind's eye now as he stood in this clearing in the forest with the Old Man... ...running through the deep woods, only he couldn't be "running", could he? The trees on either side were flying past him far too swiftly -- even for an Elf. "Flying" would be a more apt description, but then, one's feet don't touch the ground when one flies, do they? And his feet _were_ touching the ground, but how strange ... the rhythm was all wrong for "feet" alone. It occurred to him that he might be running on all fours, but he knew that was impossible because there was no way at all for arms and hands, legs and feet, to be that perfectly coordinated. And there was something else ... something up ahead. Something moving almost as swiftly _away_ from the Elf. _Almost_. That was the important point, and the Elf found that strangely exhilarating. He was _chasing_ the Thing in front of him -- _gaining_ on it -- and it was somewhere ahead, still out-of-sight amongst those same trees that were flying past the Elf as he ran (flew). The Elf could not see the Thing -- not with his eyes, anyway. But he could _smell_ it -- with an olfactory sensitivity that he logically knew he did not possess. The Thing sweated with its exertion. It had emptied its bowels along the way. The earth it kicked up in its wake exuded freshness and hinted of the hard winter just passed and the wondrous spring just arriving. But above all, the Elf smelled its mortal FEAR. And that fear -- more than the physical scents -- allowed him to _see_ it in a way that was far clearer than he had ever seen any prey he had ever tracked with his _eyes_. Ever closer he came, the trees a blur as they flew by him on either side, the strange rhythm of his feet (and hands?) quickening, the fear-smell growing ever stronger as he drew nearer to the Thing up ahead. And then he was on it. What exactly it was he didn't remember, and it didn't matter. It only mattered that he was the Hunter, it was the Prey, and now he had his jaw (why am I not using my bow? And why does my jaw feel not like my jaw at all but like something ... else?) clamped to its neck (why are my teeth so many and so sharp?) And as his sharp teeth (that he knew he couldn't have) broke the Thing's skin, as the warm blood gushed over his muzzle, splashed his face, slid down his throat, and... ...the Elf snapped out of it, just as he had snapped awake on so many occasions, the sheets drenched in his sweat, and the taste of the Thing's blood still in his mouth. The Old Man was watching him now, a strange glint in his eye that wasn't there before; he knows, thought the Elf. By Elbereth, he _knows_! But the Old Man said nothing, simply waited patiently for the Elf to ask another question. But for the moment, the Elf had nothing to ask. Truth was, he could not find his voice. And yet he knew what he was going to do, with clarity of understanding that comes not from conscious thought, but from somewhere deeper. The Elf stood and moved toward the bowl with the strange ointment.

docs.title: Pack Hunt
docs.text: Pack Hunt --------- The idyllic peace of the meadow was suddenly disturbed by the swift arrival and departure of six quadrupeds. As the birds took wing and the rabbits dove for their holes, the creatures topped the rise and surged over the grass, three in front and three behind. And then they were gone, only wind in their wake. No tracks were visible on the ground and not a flower was broken; only the blades of grass which had been under their feet were bent, and even these were moving upright again. Now the birds returned and the rabbits ventured forth from their holes as if nothing at all had occurred. The Wolf always liked the pack hunts. Flying along with your pack mates at your side, the wind whistling in your ears and running its fingers through your fur, the landscape a blur! And that collective presence, six moving as one, the power of the pack greater than the sum of its individual members. It always made him giddy. What could stand against such awesome force? Nothing ever _had_! His pack sister -- ranked 4th of six in the pack and 2nd of three amongst the females, running on his right -- caught his eye and flashed him a grin as they raced over the meadow. The Wolf returned the grin and kept running. But there was something different about this hunt, thought the wolf, and he frowned inwardly, trying to place it. The excitement, adrenaline, rush of emotion -- all there, as usual; but something else too. A kind of ... foreboding? The Wolf shook his head as he ran, trying to clear it -- how many pack hunts had he been part of? More than a few. Sure, there had always been danger -- no danger, no fun! -- and yet... It was nothing, really, he told himself now as the pack raced along. An old fence loomed ahead, part of some farmer's attempt to mark his pasture. The three wolves in front sprang over it in a graceful arc, landing lightly on the other side and continuing to run. The three behind -- including the Wolf himself -- did the same a few seconds later. Aaaahhhhhhhhh! Flying without wings -- was there any greater thrill? For a few wonderful moments, he totally forgot his anxiety. But after he landed on the other side and resumed the pace, it reared up in his mind again. Damn it all, there was something Not Right about this hunt -- Intuition told him so. But Logic was quick to point out that no one else in the pack felt anything abnormal and even so, the Pack has never lost a wolf -- Leader is too good for that. He always anticipates danger and wouldn't lead us into anything fatal! (What if he doesn't _know_?!) The horrible implications of that thought hit the Wolf so hard that he missed the pace and nearly stumbled. Not possible! Declared Logic emphatically. Who are _you_? Just a pup! You think _you_ could sense something so important but Leader could _not_? Dammit, pull yourself together! _OK_in_back_? The message was a kind of singing and howling combined and he could only hear it in his head; in fact, the whole pack could hear it, but no one outside the pack, be they man or wolf, could pick it up. This message came from Leader, running in the front row on the left side, directly in front of the Wolf. And the Wolf realized, to his great embarrassment, that his thought to "pull himself together" had been so strong that it had escaped the boundaries of his own mind and entered the realm of "pack talk". He glanced to his right and saw a mix of amusement and concern in the eyes of his sister. _Yes_OK_sorry_think_too_loud_. _Sure_OK_? This time from Shamaness, running on Leader's right. _Yes_fine_sorry_lagged_now_on_pace_OK_now_sorry_. _No_worry_pup_ (Leader again) _almost_there_now_. Ah, good, almost there, where we will... (all die!) (Stop it!) ...hunt the prey, kill it, and feast on its corpse as we always do! We are the Pack, the Hand of Gaea, and nothing... (will save us now) (I said STOP IT!!) ...will stand in our way! _On_line_! Leader. He only ordered this when he believed the foe to be especially tough and he wanted the whole pack to strike at one time. Usually the pack kept one, two, or even three members "in reserve" to react to the situation as it developed. The order came just as they were climbing a little ridge. Six abreast, they topped it. And at that moment, the Wolf could _see_. The "ridge" was actually the lip of a "sunken bowl" in the ground. Nothing grew on the inside of the bowl -- just dirt and rock. At the bottom, in the center, was their Prey. (YOU are the prey!) (Quiet, damn you!) It had a cylindrical body of irregular shape. It stood some three meters tall with perhaps half that in diameter. Dozens of tentacles grew out of the top third of its body and it had no visible eyes, mouth, or any other facial features. And its lower body was actually embedded in the ground. It looked like some madman's concept of a tree, with tentacles for branches. The Pack cleared the bowl's rim and began the descent, quickly closing the distance. Now it would put the Battle Plan into action: Keeper would howl his rage, freezing the foe with fear, while Leader, Shamaness and Grinning Sister lunged. The Wolf and his youngest sister would distract with feints and harries. That would take care of the first seconds -- after that, the Pack would react according to how badly it hurt the Prey... (Prey hurts YOU) (Not listening!) ...and adjust its attack on-the-fly. But the Battle Plan didn't happen. Just before it should have happened, Hell broke loose. Before any wolf could rage, lunge, harry, or do anything, the Tree-creature lashed out with exactly 27 tentacles and simultaneously struck each pack member -- six for Leader, five each for Shamaness and Keeper, four each for Wolf's two other sisters, and three for Wolf himself. It understands the pack rank! That thought raced through the Wolf's mind just as the tentacles slammed into him like great fists. Everything went dark for a moment, and when he managed to open his eyes, he found his vision was blurry and his head hurt awfully. He tried to get up but there was no strength in his legs. Messages were flooding in from the Pack as his mates regained consciousness... _What_that_? _Hurt_. _Power_immense_. _Move_! _Legs_cannot_. _Must_up_. _Attack_! _Wyrm.__It_is_Wyrm_. That last one came from Shamaness, always the most sensitive member of the pack. On the surface, that was a no-brainer -- all their enemies were "wyrm". What Shamaness meant was: this one was different. Stronger. And the Wolf suddenly understood that the weakness in his legs had nothing to do with any bodily injury -- he couldn't stand because the Wyrm-Tree did not want him to stand. Sudden resolve burned in him and he struggled to his feet, even though his Wyrm-infected mind strongly assured him that he needed to lie down and take it easy, that the world would be so much nicer if he just relaxed. But with a final push of will, the Wyrm's power snapped. The Wolf gained his feet and howled his triumph. Five other howls joined his and the Pack sprang at the Wyrm-Tree. And promptly landed on their backs, victim of some invisible force the Thing unleashed. Too powerful, thought Wolf as he fought the pain. We underestimated this foe. Leader did not know! Now the tentacles were coming again, punching and grabbing. He saw one wrap around his sister and hold her aloft, squeezing. Keeper lunged and bit down on the tentacle, shaking his head furiously, biting completely through. The lifeless tentacle fell to the ground -- but his sister lay motionless. Three tentacles hit Keeper while two more picked him up and squeezed. The Wolf saw his other pack mates in the same predicament, and now it grabbed him too and the ground fell away from his feet. Breathing was difficult, but he could just manage enough to keep conscious. And that was all he could do -- all other attempts to move, attack, or break free were in vain, though he struggled mightily. And then something _really_ terrible happened and... ...the Elf awoke with a gasp, drenched in a cold sweat. A few seconds later, he realized where he was. Another few seconds and he remembered to resume breathing. A full minute after that and he felt calm enough to go for a walk -- sleep was hopeless for a while. He walked the twisty passages that led from the pack cave to the Meeting Hall and then found his way to the Spring. He dropped to his knees before the water, drew some into his cupped hands and drank. It was icy cold at first, but then its clean, wholesome taste filled the emptiness in his being. There. Much better. He sat back and breathed deeply. Someone coming. He sniffed. Shamaness. She entered the cave and sat down next to him, eyes filled with concern. Neither said anything for a while. Finally, Shamaness prompted: "Would you like to talk about it?" To his surprise, the Elf realized that he _did_ want to talk about it. And so he related the dream to her, but she didn't look satisfied. "You are holding something back, Pup." Shamaness was like that -- you couldn't fool her. She couldn't exactly read your mind, but she had a formidable intuition. You simply never lied to Shamaness! Swallowing, the Elf told her the worst part: "Just before I awoke, when the Thing had me in its grasp, I saw all of you die. But I remained alive. It kept me alive so that I could see you all die. And there was nothing I could do about it!" Saying it made him relive it. He shivered uncontrollably and couldn't stop the tears from coming. Shamaness put her arms around him. "OK, Pup, it's OK now," she soothed. "Rest. We will talk more of this later." But the Elf couldn't help asking one more thing. "Why didn't Leader know? Why did I know but Leader did not?" She became thoughtful, stroking his head in her lap to calm him. Then she sighed. "Strong I am by Gaea's grace, Pup, as is Leader; as are _you_." She smiled down at him briefly, and then continued. "But I cannot know all. Mayhap you are sensitive to this thing because there is something unique in your spirit that neither Leader nor I possess. We all have our uniqueness, and although we are a Pack, it is the combination of those uniques that, in the end, make our Pack strong." And in a softer voice: "Enough now. Sleeeeeeep." And in spite of himself, the Elf felt very drowsy and drifted off into a peaceful slumber.

docs.title: The Report
docs.text: The Report ---------- REPORT TO THE COUNCIL, DARKWIND SEPT SUBJECT: Encounter with Black Spiral Dancers and Wyrm Manifestation LOCATION: Darkwind, Wastelands, vicinity of Mendahl Village DATE/TIME: Windsday, Tarsakh, pre-dawn to dawn hours SUBMITTER: Nagha of the Silent Striders, Pack Leader of The Moon Runners SUMMARY: the Pack, six members, tracked Dancer party. Came upon Mendahl Village, discovered 27 mostly adult male corpses and no living beings. Tracked 24 Dancers northeast of Mendahl, with 57 prisoners, all adult female or children. Dancer haste unusually great. Attacked and destroyed all Dancers, freed prisoners. Found Dancers' destination, discovered apparent infant manifestation of Wyrm, destroyed or forced into remission. FRIENDLY LOSSES: none killed, all wounded -- three light (recoverable), two moderate (recoverable), one critical (uncertain). ASSESSMENT: Dancers apparently needed blood sacrifice to aid major manifestation of Wyrm on physical world. Unusually great haste, probable sensitive timetable. (Their "time" problem is main reason for our successful surprise/shock attack and thus our relatively light casualties). Wyrm manifestation best described as a kind of "tree-being", with "roots" into earth and "tentacles" for "branches". Creature was weak and fading when we found it. We ringed it, waited, and it died (or faded into remission) without our intervention, presumably for lack of energy which blood sacrifice would have provided. We dug for "roots", which rotted even as we uncovered them. We found no further evidence of growth. AFTERMATH: future of Mendahl village unclear -- lost all their adult males. We provided first aid, succor, guidance. Installed late chief's son as acting leader. VEIL: preserved. Villagers under severe shock and stress, but now mostly because of adult male deaths; the Delirium represses That Which They Should Not Remember. RENOWN: Submitted for approval -- Marcus the Ronin, six of six, for extraordinarily heightened perception of entire situation, start to finish, without which the Pack would never have found the Dancers nor discovered the Wyrm manifestation, and for uncommon valor during the ensuing battle. End of Report.

docs.title: Seeking
docs.text: Seeking ------- The Wolf paused for a moment to sniff the pre-dawn air. He'd been sprinting from one location to the other for most of the last five hours and he needed a break as much as he needed to get his bearings. His pack mates were spread out in all directions from him; the closest (Shamaness), was just over the rise of that meadow; the farthest (his older sister), was some two kilometers distant. "Seek," Leader had said by way of "briefing" before this Pack Hunt had started -- no more than that. In any other organization, the obvious question would be "WHAT are we seeking?" but in this Garou Pack, "seek" was quite enough. If there were any details about the "what?", then Leader would have shared them, using the Pack's telepathy to save time. But he had provided nothing. That meant that either he didn't know what they were seeking, or he wanted the Pack Members to seek without the bias of fore-knowledge. However, one thing was clear -- this was no "outing", no "fun" hunt. Something serious lay behind it. All of them felt it. Leader had given Shamaness the "guide" position for this hunt. That was a natural thing when so little was known/revealed about the hunt's purpose, for she was the most intuitive member of the pack. And so she determined the direction and speed of the Hunt, running on intuition alone. She changed directions often. Her speed was inferior to the Wolf's because she was in homid -- or "human" -- form. Her Garou nature still allowed her to move faster than any normal human, but only "slowly" relative to the Pack. But homid was necessary if she was to use the full range of her spiritual powers, particularly the Vision. Spread out all around her were the others ... our Wolf -- in full lupus (wolf) form, only 100 meters away at this point. Younger Sister -- also lupus -- about 500 meters west. Older Sister -- in crinos, the half-lupus and half-homid form -- some two kilometers east. Keeper (lupus) to the rear some 300 meters. And finally Leader -- crinos -- about a kilometer ahead. But these distances and locations were unimportant, for they shifted constantly as the hours of the Hunt moved along, each member driven by whatever sights, sounds, or feelings they experienced at any given moment. But always they remained in contact with each other, sharing any relevant bits of information via the Pack's telepathy. But such "bits of information" had been few and far between. Leader called the Hunt just before midnight and now it was five hours later with nothing to show for it. In another hour or so, dawn would come. That didn't matter, of course. The Pack was quite capable of hunting any time, day or night, light or dark, and in all weather conditions. Well, rain made it difficult, of course, what with lost scents. But the night was dry; a bit cool perhaps for the time of year, but otherwise quite fine for a Hunt. And so our Wolf stood in the pre-dawn darkness, paws in the dewy grass, breath misting as he panted, sniffing the air and taking a short break. He glanced up to check the moons. He didn't need to use his eyes for this -- he was perfectly capable of sensing the condition of the moons any time, whether the sky was clear or cloudy, even by brightest sunlit day. But he liked to _see_ them. And he could, for the night was only partly cloudy. Dailos -- the magenta moon of chaos -- was half-full, which was not far off the Wolf's own auspice. Markas -- the red moon of balance -- was waxing. And Tekal -- green and wise -- was full. Their combined light sparkled on the moist grass, and the Wolf took joy at the sight of it. Oops. Enough of this Pleasant Interlude -- time to get moving! This is a Hunt and I cannot remain in one place for long. Where now? His head turned automatically to a spot some 300 meters half-right from his present location. There. His leg muscles tensed for the run -- but then froze. The Wolf puzzled. What..? I'm certain I could move _now_ if I try again, but why did my legs betray me just a moment ago? he thought. Why am I not arriving at that next spot, 300 meters from where I now stand? High time, there, Pup! his Reason told him. Could we get a move on, please? Before Leader or one of the others notices that we are _not_ moving? We aren't _slacking_ tonight, are we? But still the Wolf made no move -- a _conscious_ decision this time, not the intuitive one from a moment ago that had frozen his leg muscles without any apparent reason. Because he had to understand _why_ he had not moved, even if it meant standing there all night. Because the Pack was _seeking_ tonight. He recalled his lessons... ---------- "It's like this, Pup," explained Shamaness, smiling gently as she always did when she was giving instruction. "When the Pack _seeks_ something, we sometimes don't know _what_ it is that we seek. Sister Luna simply tells us that there is something we must find." "Why doesn't Luna just be clear about it, Shamaness?" the perhaps overly-inquisitive Pup had responded. She smiled patiently. "With some things, _knowing_ the End affects your actions to attain it, and the End you arrive at is the End that _you_ envision -- but not the _true_ End." The Elf nodded, keeping his eyes fixed on her. Sometimes, he had to admit, he didn't know what the hell she was talking about. But he nodded anyway. Shamaness sensed his confusion and chuckled. (She _always_ knew). "Often, Pup," she continued, "we just need to have a clear head. Sounds easy, but it's one of the hardest lessons to learn. Because when a question confronts us, we break our heads thinking, trying to reason it out. And sometimes, we actually get the solution that way. But most times, all we really need to do is just calm down, stop thinking, and get out of the way -- and then, Pup, the solution will find _us_." Pup nodded again, but his eyes were still blank. She sighed and smiled. "For example, let's say we have a Pack Hunt." The Pup's eyes lit up. He loved the Hunts! Shamaness noticed (of course). She grinned briefly and continued. "Suppose Leader calls a Hunt, but he doesn't really know _what_ we're hunting." Pup frowned in consternation. "Leader wouldn't know?!" Shamaness smiled gently. "Yes, it is possible. Sometimes the End is hidden, as I told you. Now listen without interrupting for a while! We call that a 'seek' -- we're looking for something. We know it's out there -- but we don't know what it is. It doesn't matter _how_ Leader -- or any of us, even you, Pup! -- knows it. We just _know_ it, and that's all that matters. So we must 'seek' it. "Now on this kind of Hunt, one of us is hopefully better attuned to the purpose than the others, and this one is the 'guide'. The rest of us move in all directions at different speeds -- but the Guide determines the general direction and speed of the Pack as a whole. So far, so good?" The Elf nodded. She went on. "Now, at some point during a Seek Hunt, one of us -- maybe the Guide, but could be _any_ of us -- discovers something ... important. It could be something big and obvious, like the remains of a battlefield where the corpses are still fresh. Or it could be something seemingly trivial, like a strange scent on the wind." Shamaness shrugged. "Or we may be out all day and all night and find _nothing_. It can happen. In which case the Seek Hunt was still important -- to show us that we must better attune ourselves to the Earth Mother, so that next time we do _not_ miss what we should have found." Shamaness paused to see if it was sinking in. She nodded slightly and concluded. "So when the Pack is _seeking_, Pup, and you come across some thing, or some event, or anything out-of-the-ordinary, no matter how simple it seems -- it could very well be the 'sign' that leads us to understand the purpose of the Hunt. Don't just brush it off and continue! That's a mistake that even we older wolves are prone to make if we're not careful. Stop what you are doing. Clear your head. And let the reason find _you_!" ---------- And so the Wolf stood in the grass, relaxed his thoughts, and stretched out with his feelings. And then he heard it -- barely within the audio range of even his super-sensitive lupus ears. Perhaps carried on the breeze just before it shifted to a direction where, in another moment, he would have missed it completely, lupus-ears notwithstanding. And he suddenly realized that this was the _second_ time he'd heard it! The _first_ time was just a minute ago, when his legs had refused to move. It had been so low and subtle that it had registered only in his subconscious mind, which had then frozen the muscles in his legs. And now he'd heard it _twice_, this time on a _conscious_ level. The answer had found _him_. _Here_! The Wolf's single-word thought raced over the Pack's telepathy and instantly reached the other five, who immediately dropped what they were doing and hurried to his location. Shamaness was closest, so she arrived first, despite her homid form, and laid a reassuring hand on Wolf's head. She noticed that he was trembling slightly -- a reaction of fear ... and something else. Loathing. But she did not bother him about it -- all would be clear when he was ready to share. It took another full minute for all six of them to join up at the Wolf's location. After the last one (Older Sister) arrived, the Wolf gave them another word: _Hark_! And with that, they all became still as stone, withdrawing all energy from their other senses and concentrating only on hearing. For five long minutes there was nothing. And then that barely audible sound came again, just within the range of lupus ears. And this time, Keeper and Younger Sister -- the other two in lupus -- heard it as well. And they stiffened. Shamaness felt the Wolf tremble again. It was the call of a bird. But no bird made that sound -- rather, some other creature was calling _like_ it. It sounded again, and Keeper growled softly. It was the call of the Whippoorwill. Leader, Shamaness, and Older Sister received the information via telepathy. Shamaness exhaled softly, and a single word fell from her lips... "Dancers."

docs.title: The Shaman
docs.text: The Shaman ---------- There is a very special hill a short way to the west of the Garou Cave of the Darkwind Sept. It is a hill that anyone who ventures through the thick forest can see, but for some reason known only to the Powers That Be, only a Garou may actually find the way up. A Garou who climbs this hill may discern a strange and yet reassuring sight as he nears the summit -- a large rock formation that, with a bit of imagination, resembles the form of a sleeping wolf. "Sleeping Wolf Rock," the Garou call it, and it is second only in importance and sanctity to the Caern of the Sept itself. It is here that a Garou comes to converse with Lady Luna, choose Auspice, and define his or her destiny. Aside from that, the panoramic view atop Sleeping Wolf Rock is arguably the best vista on the entire continent. Here the land and sky both open up before the eyes and soul of the one who sits upon the rock. The experience is even better at night, for each of the stars in the sky seems to speak a word, and taken together, these words form an invisible song that plays in the head of the Garou whose spirit is tuned to hear it. Sitting atop Sleeping Wolf Rock on this fine morning was a lone homid figure -- stock still, eyes closed, heartbeat and breathing dramatically slowed down -- just fast enough to keep the body functional. His back was perfectly straight and neither the wind, the pre-dawn chill, nor the occasional flying insect compelled him to even the slightest twitch. The man had been that way, physically unchanged, for over five hours. Physically. His spirit, however, roamed through the Umbra, visiting and conversing with various spirits, or simply enjoying the serenity. Dawn. The first light of the new day gently nudged the night away. The eyes behind the closed lids twitched a bit, that barest movement signalling the spirit's return from the Umbra, across the Gauntlet, and back to the physical world. But still the man remained motionless for another half hour, heartbeat and breathing a bit quicker now, yes, but still less than "normal", as he mentally wound down from his spiritual journey. Finally, the eyelids lifted. At first, only the whites were revealed, but then the irises came into view as the man rolled them back down from their previously upward-looking position. And now the entire face moved as the man took a deep breath -- his first in almost six hours. And another deep breath. And soon he was breathing normally. The man gingerly moved his head left and right, then rolled it in a circle on his neck, stretching, restimulating the flow of blood to his brain. Dawn's light was increasing now, and revealed his facial features to any who might have been standing there: leathery, tough skin, creased and worn; dark, too -- a Souvraeli? Probably. Age? He looked to be at least 40. Could be 50. But perhaps the creased skin and deep-set eyes were less from age and more from whatever cares the man carried. And now the man moved his arms, stretching them out to either side. And then he carefully got to his feet, giving the muscles time to adjust to the change of position, stretching and twisting this way and that, the old body coming to life again -- and radiating a power that defied the appearance of age. Stretching finished, the man stood atop the rock, hands on hips, and looked out over the wide landscape. He sighed happily as the corners of his mouth turned up in a smile. I so love this time of day, he thought, enjoying the profound sense of peace and serenity. If ever I should leave this continent, this I shall miss above all. The Dawn is never so beautiful nor dearer to me than right here, on this spot, Sleeping Wolf beneath me and Sister Luna above me. The man's smile grew a little wider and he closed his eyes. Just a bit longer, he thought. Just a few more moments before I go down the hill, back to the Caern, and begin the day's duties. Just a bit more time to bathe in the bliss of this moment, this perfect moment, this-- The man suddenly and sharply frowned. His eyes snapped open, alarm written in them. Something... And then it hit him -- not physically, but on the intuitional level. The psychic blast knocked him clean off his feet and he landed on his back. The very rock beneath him shuddered for an instant. The man rolled onto his left side, propping himself up with his elbow, panting hard, eyes wide, darting around at nothing at all. He gulped in some air, choked on it for a moment, got to his feet. He removed his deerskin cap, ran a hand through his close- cropped, half-silver hair. He shivered from the cold sweat that had suddenly formed over his entire body. He put the cap back on and sped down the hill as quickly as he could. And as he started down the hill, the Shaman -- for that is what this man is, as the astute reader may have already guessed -- reached out with his mind to find his companions... _Pack_! Two full seconds passed -- must have been asleep, he reckoned. _Here_. _Here_. _Moon_Gate_in_20_seconds_!__Need_my_bag_! That would leave no time for anything except the absolute essentials -- clothing, weapons and armor -- "weapons and armor" just for Leader, who fought in crinos -- and the Shaman's "bag", which Keeper, who fought in lupus and therefore didn't need to worry about gear, would grab. Exactly 16 seconds later, the Shaman reached the bottom of the hill, took one second to calm himself, and one more second to focus his energies to the Incarnae of Phoebe. Two seconds after that, the link was formed, the bridge appeared, and a brilliant arch of moonlight formed in the air and expanded beyond sight. And sliding down the bridge of moonlight were two figures -- the Shaman's Pack Leader and Keeper. This pack had only three members. The Shaman placed his right hand over his heart and bowed his head slightly. "Ranolf. Tamika. Thank you for coming." The two bowed back. "Uziah," they said in unison. Tamika the Keeper handed Uziah the Shaman his bag. "What goes, Shaman?" inquired Ranolf the Leader. The Shaman sighed and looked into the distance at nothing. "I know not exactly, Leader. But it is not good. And it comes swiftly this way." The Shaman's eyes narrowed for a moment and he added, "The Wyrm has been about this night." The eyes of the other two Garou widened slightly. The three waited, steeling themselves for whatever was coming.

docs.title: The Test
docs.text: The Test -------- >>>TINK!<<< The sound of the crossbow bolt hitting the stone wall elicited a loud curse from the guard whod fired it. The point of impact had been exactly three centimeters to the left of the intruders right ear, seen from the guards perspective. Said intruder had recoiled instinctively from the shot, but had recovered a split second later, and was now advancing -- quickly. The guard was reaching for a new bolt, but realized hed never make it. He dropped his crossbow and had just enough time to draw his sword before the intruders quarterstaff sliced the air with a loud _whoosh_! and connected with the guards head. Or rather, connected with the guards _helmet_, which momentarily saved him from death, but left him with a horrible ringing in his ears, a distraction which the intruder now exploited, pulling the lead end of the staff towards him with his right hand whilst simultaneously pushing the back end of the staff forward with his left -- lightning fast. The result: the new end of the staff very rudely introduced itself to the guards nose. The impact flattened the cartilage and shattered the bone underneath, sending fragments into the brain. The onset of death was so quick that the guards face preserved its look of surprise even as the corpse crashed to the floor. The next guard was already waiting, had already lined up the shot, and fired as his colleague fell. The intruder dodged, his long blond hair flying, exposing pointed ears. The bolt skimmed across the front of his leather body armor, wickedly tearing the fabric, but not the skin it protected. The Elf surged forward, swinging the staff as he came. But this guard had time to fully draw his sword and swing. Staff and sword connected with each other with a loud >>>THUNK!<<< The sword bit into the oak -- and got hung up. The Elf jerked the staff back, yanking the sword out of the astonished guards grasp. The sudden movement loosened the swords bite and it clattered to the floor. Before the guard could react, the Elf swung, connected with the guards face, reversed the staff, and buried the other end in the solar plexus. The guard doubled over, suddenly bereft of oxygen, and the Elf finished him with a mighty downward stroke to the back of the neck, breaking it. But now more guards were racing toward him from down the hall as the alarm spread. The Elf turned and ran back to the room where hed despatched the first crossbowman. There he found the opposite doorway -- his escape route -- blocked by another guard, newly arrived. Without hesitation, the Elf pounced and attacked furiously. Exactly three seconds later, the man was down. But now the guards from the hallway -- four of them -- had gained the room, and the Elf fled through the doorway just before they could surround him and just as another crossbow bolt struck the archway above the Elfs head. Down the hall, a right turn and >>>SMACK!<<< into a guard who was just around the corner. Elf and guard both went down on their respective arses, but the Elf regained his feet faster, and one jab to the gut later, the Elf was racing down the hallway, leaving the guard doubled over, alive only because the Elfs time had grown short -- "escape" had become the prime directive. At the next intersection, a left, but no! The hallway was filled with guards, so the Elf doubled back as a crossbow bolt zoomed past his ear. But now the hallway from which he had come was also swarming with guards, which left him one choice -- the door to his right, which led to the courtyard, the one place where he knew he should not go, and now the only place he _could_ go. The door was locked. >>>BASH! SPLINTER!<<< Correction -- the door was UN-locked. The delay allowed the guards to close up, and as the Elf burst into the courtyard, he felt something stick him in the lower back. The pain came a moment later, and he smelled blood -- his own. Despite the pain, the Elf whirled about and >>>KLANG!<<< a guard fell to his knees, holding his head, sudden victim of a particularly wicked migraine. Now more guards were boiling out of doorways around the courtyard. In the dim light, the Elf sensed exactly eight of them. They had him surrounded on three sides and were closing the noose all the way. Again the Elf whirled, swung the staff in a wide arc, the exertion further aggravating the wound and making him grimace in pain. The staff failed to connect, but it was enough to make the guards back off, buying the Elf one precious second to keep his back free and take in his surroundings -- no exit, no place to climb, and now more guards appearing in the upper windows, bolting their crossbows. The guards knew they had him. They advanced at a leisurely pace now, grinning evilly, taunting him. "Little men with pointed ears!" a guard sneered. "We will _trim_ them for you!" promised another, and they all laughed. "Out of the way, let me through!" bellowed another, a rather large man who now pushed his way to the front -- the Captain, judging by the insignia on his shoulders. He smirked at the Elf. "Great warrior you may be," he said, "but against so many swords--" he waved his hand around to indicate his men --"I fear the battle would be short-lived." The Elf simply crouched, staff held at the ready, eyes boring into the Captain, blood trickling down his leg from the wound in his back. "Last chance, Elf -- put the staff _down_! Its over!" Eight armed men stood before him with drawn swords. Another three were in the windows around the courtyard, crossbows ready. The Elf made a decision. He sighed, relaxed, and lowered the staff. The Captain grinned. Suddenly the Elf tensed again and threw the staff toward the guards. As they instinctively recoiled in surprise, all eyes on the flying staff, the Elf turned and dove >>>KERPLOOSH!<<< into the large water trough located on this side of the courtyard. The Captain caught the staff, looked at it briefly, and then threw it away. His men were all looking at him. "Well?!" he shouted. The guards snapped out of it and quickly moved to the trough and surrounded it. The night had grown silent now, save for the random splashing and rippling of the water into which the Elf had dove. "Caint old is breath ferever, can e?" said one, and they all chuckled. "And he aint got his nasty little stick anymore, does he now?" offered the guard with the "migraine", still clutching his head. And so the guards stood around the water trough, drawn swords at the ready, waiting. What happened next was so sudden and violent, that no two men -- those that _survived_, that is -- would later give the same version of it. Something exploded out of the water, knocked one of the guards on his back, leapt to another guard, knocked him down too, and then attacked the Captain. The two guards on the ground were quite still. Closer inspection would reveal that each of them had a bloody, pulpy mess where their throats should have been. The Captain was screaming and thrashing around wildly. The Creature from the Water Trough had attached itself to his right hand, the one that held the sword. One sickening, fleshy, ripping sound later, the sword clattered to the ground as the hand separated from the arm. Now for the first time, the thing stood still. It was a wolf, a big grey one. In its mouth was what remained of the Captains right hand. The Wolf bit down on it once and swallowed, licked its bloody chops, opened its mouth, and _grinned_. The guards just stood there, jaws hanging open. The Captain clutched at his right arm, groaning and trying to staunch the flow of blood. Then, instinct overcame good sense, and the Wolf involuntarily did what all animals do when theyre soaking wet -- he shook himself. _Wet.__Get_dry_. The delay was enough for the guards to recover from their shock, assess the situation, and react accordingly -- by bravely running away. The Wolf did not pursue. After leaping from the pool, lunging at two guards, and maiming the Captain -- all of it while wounded -- it was spent. _Pain_. Its hind legs suddenly buckled. The Wolf turned its head around to lick the wound on its lower back. _Hunger_! The fresh blood of the two corpses beckoned irresistibly. Using its forelegs, the Wolf pulled itself over to the nearest dead guard, opened its jaw to reveal the razor-sharp teeth within, and plunged its snout into the corpses chest. _Hunger_! The flesh and bone gave way easily, and in no time, the Wolf had the heart in its teeth. And then in its stomach. Next came the liver. And then some meat off the ribs -- nothing like the meat thats closest to the bone! _Yummy_! Some feeling was returning to the hind legs. The wolf hacked up a hairball and went to the second corpse. Heart, liver, ribs. Uncontrollable slobber. Snout soaked in blood. _Ecstasy_! The Wolf was quite enjoying itself until something thudded into its left shoulder. The pain came a second later. _Hurt_. From a second story window, a guard waved his crossbow high in the air and whooped, "I got im! I got im! Damned, blasted mutt! How ya like that hot love up your arse, doggy, woof woof! Hahahahahaha!" Other crossbowmen were taking up positions. _Danger_! A sudden instinctive urge caused the wolf to jump to his left, right out of the path of a swinging sword; the Captain -- now fighting left-handed. _Revenge_! Thhe Wolf took him by the throat and shook. >>>TINK!<<< A bolt bounced harmlessly off the stone floor to the wolfs right. >>>THWOK!<<< Another one hit the captain, as if the wolf needed help, and a crossbowman cursed from above. _Dead_. The Wolf released the captain and dug with its teeth for the heart, ripped it out of the corpses chest, bit down twice, and swallowed. Good! The wolf knew instinctively that it didnt have time for this, but it also knew that it would never escape from this Bad Situation while wounded if it didnt have some extra energy. >>>TINK! TINK! TINK!<<< The wolfs luck held as three more bolts missed, striking the floor around him. _Flee_! The wolf moved, covering the distance to the door in one fourth of the time the Elf needed, sped along the hallway to the exit, flattened another guard along the way just for good measure -- and was free, flying away from the keep into the safety of the deep woods... ---------- ...and coming finally to the rendezvous point. The Wolf collapsed, breathing hard from the exertion and its wounds. _Pain_.__Fatigue_. The wolf lay on its right side, the bolt still in its left shoulder. _Coming_. The wolf sensed the humanoids approach even before the scent reached its nose. Then he smelled it. Leader. A kind of singing in his head ... _you_need_food_.__Eat_. The man dropped the carcass of a deer down on the ground next to the Wolf. The wolfs salivary glands went wild, and he feasted for some time. The man waited patiently while the wolf took the corpse apart, consumed all the meat it could find, licked the bones. _Sated_. The man nodded, reached over, and yanked out the bolt. The wolf gave a short yelp and sighed. _How_do_you_feel_? _Feel_.__Fine_. _Man,_now_.__And_then_rest_. The Wolf closed its eyes. Its fur began to thin and disappear. It gave a little whine and passed out. ---------- The Elf awoke and sensed that it was just before dawn. He opened his eyes and saw the man, sitting cross-legged on the grass, watching him with a little smile. The Elf sat up slowly, giving the muscles time to adjust. Then he made eye contact, bowed his head slightly and said, "Pack Leader." The man inclined his head slightly forward. "Pup". His smile widened. The Elf dropped his gaze and sighed. "I have failed." Leader smiled benignly. "What was your task?" "To retrieve the topaz from the treasure room and bring it here. But I -- could not reach it." "Tell me." The Elf related the events from his penetration of the Keep up until his dive into the water trough. And then he was silent. Leader simply waited. The Elf looked ashamed. "Continue," Leader said. The Elf could not meet his gaze. Leader sighed. "What restriction did I place upon you for this task?" Finally the Elf found his voice. "I was to -- fight only on two legs." Leader waited. "I -- I entered the water. But it was the Wolf that came out." Leader nodded. "And why did you violate my restriction?" The Elf swallowed. Then he found the courage to make eye contact. "Forgive me, my Leader. The alternative -- was death." Leader just looked at him. Summoning all his courage, the Elf held the gaze. Finally, after what seemed to the Elf like an eternity, his Leader nodded and smiled. "You did fine, Pup. You did fine." The Elf blinked. This was the last thing he expected to hear. "I feel I owe you an apology," continued Leader. "There was no topaz in the treasure room. And at your current level of skill, fighting on only two legs, it would have taken nothing short of divine intervention for you to even reach the treasure chamber, let alone escape alive." The Elfs jaw fell slightly open. He gave a little shake of his head. "Then ... why?" Leader smiled slightly. "Your true task this night was to face an impossible situation -- and master it. Even if it meant disobeying your Pack Leader." Leader stood up. The Elf did likewise. Leader smiled and laid both hands on the Elfs shoulders. "You did fine, Pup. You did _real_ fine!" Leader removed his hands and dropped to one knee, staring into the Elfs eyes. He then raised his right arm, slowly formed a fist, and bowed his head before the Elf. The honor stunned him. Then he remembered himself and repeated the rite to his Leader. Leader smiled and clapped the Elf on the back. "Come on, Pup -- lets go home. Been a long night!" And as dawn lit up the world, the two figures faded into the woods.

docs.title: In Town
docs.text: In Town ------- The Elf entered the town via the west gate and mingled with humanity. Ladies Rare Undergarments aside, it was good to go to town and mix in with the human race for a while! So much to see, hear and smell -- especially smell. This heightened sense told him more about the city and its inhabitants in a minute than he had previously been able to perceive in an entire day when he was "just the Elf." It had taken him some time to get used to it, mind you. The first time he'd ventured into town after his "change", he'd been completely unprepared for the magnitude of the olfactory barrage. Suddenly, his nose took in scents that it had never taken in before, and those that were already familiar to him were dramatically magnified. The weight of it had so overwhelmed his mind that he panicked, running away from the city and its inhabitants as fast as he could. But with time, he had learned to mentally filter the countless bits of scent information, concentrating on the ones he needed or wanted while suppressing those he didn't. Now he allowed the scents to wash over him and he took in the knowledge of each... The elderly man over there has an advanced disease and will probably pass away in a few months. The Elf wondered if the man was aware of it. The child leaning against the wall on the other side of the road has just finished a meal of bread that was starting to go stale and a slab of meat that should have been on the grill a bit longer -- oh dear ... he's going to barf it up in a few minutes. A young woman passed by him with a single glance but no change of expression, and yet the sudden increase in her pheromone output revealed that she found him attractive; another sniff told him that sex now would produce a child, and he absently wondered if that child would be a garou should he ... with a little chuckle to himself, he shook it off. And then he smelled something that immediately put him on edge. He stopped dead and inhaled more deeply through his nose. He knew it wasn't the first time he'd smelled it, but it had been a while -- about a year or a year-and-a-half? He sttood there -- and remembered... ---------- "The Lord Landholder of this region--" Leader jabbed the appropriate place on the map as the Elf looked on "--has been oppressing his charges a bit more than is healthy lately. I fear that the Wyrm's power is growing there. Go there and assess the situation. If practical, I want you to ... send him a message." The Elf gave Leader a questioning look. Leader smiled a bit. "What I mean, Pup, is this -- don't do anything 'radical' like slaying the whole keep and mounting their heads on pikes. I don't believe the situation is that far down yet. For right now, we give him something to ... 'think about.'" The Elf still frowned. Leader thought for a minute. "Ah, I know just the thing! This lord is rumoured to have a very handsome horse. Finest stallion in the region, says the rumor mill." Leader smiled knowingly at the Elf. "Would be a shame if anything happened to that prize stallion, wouldn't it, Pup?" The Elf nodded, the corner of his mouth turning up slightly. Leader nodded back and clapped the Elf on the shoulder. "Good hunting, Pup! May Luna guide you." And so the Wolf had broken into the lord's stable, killed the prize stallion, and was just starting to feast on the really fine meat when no less than 10 of the lord's guards burst in. And the Wolf realized that his approach must not have been as careful as he'd imagined it. Stupid of him. In the battle that followed, the Wolf took down four of the guards, but sustained an arrow in the side and two wicked sword hits. The wounds sapped his strength so much that he was quite unable to deal with the remaining six guards and live through it. So the Wolf fled, trailing blood. He had buried his gear in a wooded area near a natural waterfall, and he made for it now. He was sure he could lose the guards if he could just make it there. But it was hopeless -- he was too weak, and still getting weaker from loss of blood. Then the Wolf remembered the little farmhouse he'd noticed on the way to the lord's mansion and he made a detour. He burst into the animal pen and quickly despatched three chickens, a pig and a cow -- all that was there. As quickly as possible, he tore open their bellies and took the heart and liver from each, greedily gulping down the meat as if he'd never eaten before. He could feel some strength returning now. Wait! Someone coming. He smelled a human female. She must have heard the commotion. The soldiers were coming too. She would give him away. The Wolf took flight again, leaving most of the meat behind, hoping he'd gotten enough to get out of this Bad Situation. He was still losing blood, but he could run faster now. He would make it, he was sure. A bit later, the Elf stood under the waterfall, letting it wash over him. Then he pulled out the arrow, gasping with the effort. He tossed it aside and concentrated inward, calling upon the Earthmother's blessing to heal him. She answered, and he felt his wounds closing. He left the pool and found the spot where he'd buried his gear. He dug it up and dressed. He was about to leave when he smelled the girl again. She was close -- _too_ close. He cursed himself inwardly for being so careless again. Normally, even in Elf form, he should have had more warning of her approach. But he'd concentrated so hard on flight and healing that he'd neglected his environment. His ear twitched -- the subtle rubbing of an arrow nock against a bowstring! Easy, now, keep calm! She was frightened -- he could smell it. OK, use that to your advantage. The Elf turned to the bush behind which she must be hiding and smiled. Then he bent down to write her a message on the ground: "Please forgive me about your livestock, but the Wolf's need was very great." And then he took his pouch full of gold coins and set it on the ground for her -- a "tidy sum" for the Elf, but to this girl and her family, it would mean a "new life." Her animals had saved him -- he owed her that much. And then he left, praying to Gaea that he had guessed right, that the girl would be too overcome by curiosity to launch an arrow into his back. And for once that day, things _did_ work out in his favor. ---------- That episode came back to him in a flash as he caught the scent -- the very same scent of the girl that day at the farmhouse and later at the waterfall. The Elf looked around. He saw only the crowd. He'd never actually _seen_ her before, and now, for some reason, he _wanted_ to. Despite his keen sense of smell, it was just not possible to pick her out among all the people hustling and bustling along the street. No, too many of them. Damn! And he didn't have time for this -- he had errands to run before the sun went down. Have to move along. Try again another day. So the Elf reluctantly gave up the search and turned his attention back to his duties. And as the Elf turned and went his way, a young girl appeared at a doorway, anxiously looking left and right. She could swear that the elf she'd glimpsed through the window was the very same elf she'd seen about a year-and-a-half ago -- an elf she had found at the end of a _wolf's_ trail. But by the time she realized what she was seeing and run out of the building to get a better look, it was too late -- the elf was gone. She sighed. Someone called her name. Oops. In her excitement, she'd quite forgotten what she was doing and now she'd better get back to doing it lest the training master be displeased. She turned around and went back into the building. According to the sign above the door, this building belonged to the "Fighters' Guild."

docs.title: The Witch
docs.text: The Witch --------- The Elf pushed thoughts of the girl out of his mind and concentrated on the reason for coming to town in the first place -- pack business. He'd mentally broken his trip down into two categories -- the "OK" part, and the "not-OK" part. For now, he concentrated on the former. He left the marketplace with his pack full of provisions and went to see Taylor to pick up his older sister's weapon. The Elf was mighty curious about it. His sister was always bringing back the most exotic gear imaginable after defeating Gaea-knows-what Gaea- knows-where. He had no idea where or how she brought the stuff in, but she sure did bring it in -- in boatloads! So it was with some anticipation that the Elf told Taylor what it was he was there for. But the thing Taylor handed him was wrapped up in several layers of thick cloth -- all he could tell was that it was some sort of polearm, about two and half meters in length, with even thicker padding on one end. Some kind of spear, perhaps. "Good as new for your sister," said Taylor, as he handed it over. "Tell her I'm sorry the restoration took a bit longer than usual, but can't help that with these exotic, imported weapons, you know!" The next stop was Moon's, to hand over Shamaness' broken necklace. After that, the Post Office, where there indeed was a letter for Leader and, judging by the strange characters on the return address, which the Elf could not read, it certainly did look like it came from over the sea. And that concluded the "OK" part. The Elf sighed and closed his eyes. All right, then, he thought. Let's get on with it. And so he made his way toward the docks, where the Witch lived. It was easy to call this witch "_The_ Witch", because she was the _only_ one that the City allowed to practice more-or-less openly. What it was exactly that she "practiced", the Elf wasn't sure. But whatever it was, it was so important to the more prominent members of the community that their influence prevailed upon the Mayor to turn a blind eye to her activities and allow her a known residence. The Elf stood before her door and hesitated. For all her influence with the land's prominent ones, her dwelling place was, at least from the outside, nothing special. The Elf wondered why she didn't have a better one if she were so important. And above all, he wondered how in all the world she would help him with ... exotic ladies undergarments, for the Love of Gaea! That thought made him simmer. He bit down on a curse for his younger sister for putting him through this. Why during _his_ turn? Why couldn't _she_ do this? He raised his hand to knock on the door and suddenly realized how nervous he was. Come on! he thought. Pull yourself together! A moment's courage and it is done. And as his knuckles were about to strike the wood, the door creaked open... The face that peered out was deeply and completely wrinkled. With warts. It was the Witch, of course, that was obvious to the Elf, even though he'd never seen her before. She looked to be about 90. Maybe more. But ... how strange, he thought, taking a slightly stronger sniff. Her scent does _not_ indicate advanced age -- more like 30, or even younger. And yet his eyes beheld an old hag. And now she opened the door a bit wider, and he could see that she stood hunched over, as if her back were bent from some disease or merely age. She wore a simple black skirt and a matching black blouse. Her silver hair was tied up in a bun. She was sizing him up, her eyes alert and intense despite the rest of her physical appearance. The Elf bore her scrutiny and waited. "Well," she said finally, in a voice barely above a whisper. "You'd better come in." She opened the door completely, turned, and went back into the room. The Elf followed. The strong smell of incense struck him and he coughed. With his sensitive nose, he should have noted it outside, but he must have concentrated so much on the Witch that it hadn't registered. He quickly composed himself. "Lie down there," she said, gesturing with a hand toward a somewhat crude, but very sturdy-looking bench. On top of it was a lumpy cloth pad, stuffed with straw by the look of it. The Elf swallowed, again wondering what kind of "service" it was that the Witch provided. "I, uh--," he began. The Witch turned slowly and regarded him with those eyes. Again the Elf was struck by the two things he'd noted outside: first, how old she _looked_, and second, how young she _smelled_. It confused him mightily. The Witch frowned and tilted her head a bit, as if something here was Not Quite Right. "Young Elf," she said, in a voice that was a few decibels louder than her previous whisper. "If you're wasting my time..." Her eyes took on a dangerous glint. The Elf tried to speak but his throat had gone tight. "Why ... are ... you ... here?" She waved her hand in the air once. Suddenly, the Elf felt his throat loosen, but his voice was a mere squeak as it said, "Under ... wear." The Witch blinked. "What?!" she snapped with a scowl. Right then, the Elf would have sold his soul to be anywhere else in the physical or spiritual worlds than where he was right now.
