BARD ARCHETYPES
docs.text: BARD ARCHETYPES At guild level 10, Bards can choose a performance archetype: specialize specialize <archetype> Your first choice is free. Changing archetypes later costs coin, because it requires relearning how you structure a performance. Archetypes change the feel and mechanics of Bard songs and older Bard skills. They can affect Performance gains, song-field strength, field duration with favored instruments, hidden harmony resonance, role songs, social reputation work, control songs, Finales, and the flavor of your performances. Current archetypes: War Conductor Tactical battle support. Rhythm and Harmony gain more momentum and stronger fields, especially with drums, horn, or war harp. Certain hidden harmonies resolve with a sharper command of formation and tempo. Rally, Hero, follower songs, and other support moments benefit from this style. Shadow Minstrel Control, misdirection, and emotional pressure. Melody and Dissonance gain more momentum and stronger morale pressure, especially with flute, chimes, or violin. Some hidden harmonies gain shadowed, misleading resolutions. Soothe, Otto, Defame, and other control or social tricks benefit from this style. Skald Aggressive combat performance. Rhythm and Crescendo hit harder, especially with drums, horn, or war harp. Active song fields can add skaldic sound damage in combat, and some hidden harmonies become battle cries. Wail, singing weapons, follower songs, and direct pressure benefit from this style. Virtuoso Mastery through precision. Your song-chain memory extends, allowing longer hidden chains. Complex chains and favored instruments such as concert lute, violin, and chimes improve field power and momentum. Study, lore, craft, and precision-based command moments benefit from this style. Doom Singer Dissonance, dread, and morale warfare. Dissonance and Finale performances gain more pressure, especially with violin, war harp, or chimes. Certain hidden harmonies resolve into colder and more terrible patterns. Wail, Villain, Battlefield Silence, and enemy morale pressure benefit from this style. Use bscore to see your current archetype. Choosing an archetype is a playstyle decision: Pick War Conductor if you like directing a party. Pick Shadow Minstrel if you like control and misdirection. Pick Skald if you want aggressive combat music. Pick Virtuoso if you want precision and complex chains. Pick Doom Singer if you want dread, pressure, and Finales. Recommended next topics: bardhelp instruments bardhelp songs bardhelp combat

docs.title: BARD HELP
docs.text: BARD HELP Welcome to the Bard guild. Bards win through momentum, timing, morale, misdirection, and the right instrument in the right moment. This help system is meant to walk you from your first guild level into the deeper song system. If you are new, read these in order: bardhelp start Your first checklist as a Bard. bardhelp general What Bards are good at and how they play. bardhelp songs Performance, song forms, and hidden harmonies. bardhelp patterns Reviewing harmonies and pivots you have learned. bardhelp instruments Lutes, drums, flutes, harps, and other tools. bardhelp combat How to use songs during fights. bardhelp support How to help a party or a room. bardhelp archetypes Guild level 10 specializations. bardhelp commands Guild-level command list. Useful daily commands: bscore Show Bard stats, instrument, archetype, Performance. bpatterns Show hidden harmonies and pivots you have learned. bmon on Show Bard updates without typing bscore constantly. bcmds Show your Bard commands in a level-friendly format. fix lute Restore your guild lute from anywhere. instrument Show and select carried Bard instruments. help <command> Show exact syntax for one command. Other topics: bardhelp communication Guild channels and Bard communication. bardhelp ranks Old Bard rank lore and titles. bardhelp lute Instrument and lute reference. The short version: keep music moving, vary your song forms, watch Performance, learn what your instrument changes, and at guild level 10 choose an archetype that matches the way you want to perform.

docs.title: BARD COMBAT
docs.text: BARD COMBAT Bard combat is about tempo. You are strongest when you keep a song field active, vary song forms, build Performance, and choose the right Finale when the fight turns in your favor. Basic combat rhythm: 1. Start with a field. pulsebeat, emberaria, silververse, echochord, dirgeash, or ashlullaby. 2. Vary your form. Repeating one song over and over builds less Performance than moving between Rhythm, Melody, Harmony, and Dissonance. These forms use separate cooldowns, so changing forms is also much faster than repeating one form. 3. Watch Performance. Use bscore or bmon. High Performance opens stronger moments. Charisma improves Performance gain, field force, field duration, and hidden harmony payoff. 4. Use Crescendo and Finale. apexchord can help push toward a finishing moment. echoburst, battlefieldsilence, and Wail spend that moment in different ways. When bscore or bmon says Finale is ready, spend it quickly. 5. Study the fight. study can show emotional resonance. soothe, otto, and morale pressure can change the shape of the room without being simple damage. 6. Match the moment. Archetype, instrument, active fields, hidden patterns, Performance, and Charisma now all feed into Bard command strength. A Doom Singer with a violin and Dissonance already hanging in the room should feel different from a War Conductor with drums and Harmony carrying the party. Core battle commands: pulsebeat Rhythm timing support. emberaria Melody steadiness support. silververse Melody healing support. echochord Harmony timing support. dirgeash Dissonance enemy pressure. ashlullaby Dissonance mesmerize pressure. soothe Calm combat in the room. hero Heroic role song. villain Villainous role song. whispercanticle Flute song that clouds enemy focus. mirrorrefrain Chimes song that disrupts enemy timing. apexchord Crescendo for high Performance. echoburst Finale that bursts active fields. muse Harmony inspiration field. battlefieldsilence Finale that disrupts enemies. otto Force a target to dance. rally Courage and mental resilience. ssing Create a singing sword. Wail Banshee Finale. Tips: Keep bmon on while learning. Use bcmds to see cooldown time and cooldown family. Use bardhelp songs to understand forms and hidden harmonies. Use bardhelp instruments before deciding which instrument to carry. Use bardhelp archetypes before choosing specialize at guild level 10. Raise Charisma if you want your performances to matter more.

docs.title: BARD COMMAND LADDER
docs.text: BARD COMMAND LADDER Use help <command> for exact syntax. Use bcmds for a live list based on your current guild level. Probationer - guild level 1 bard Guild chat line. bemotes List Bard emotes. bmon Toggle the Bard performance monitor. bpatterns Show hidden harmonies and pivots you have discovered. bscore Show Bard stats and Performance. fix lute Retune and restore your Bardic lute anywhere. instrument Select an alternate Bard instrument. legend Read information about items. lore Rate a monster relative to yourself. play lute Play a single note for others nearby. pulsebeat Start a Rhythm song field for nearby allies. Fochlucan - guild level 2 emberaria Start a Melody song field around you. silververse Start a Melody song field that mends allies. playdead Trick people into thinking you are a corpse. scroll Create a scroll. Rhymer - guild level 3 echochord Start a Harmony song field around you. perform People toss coins into your hat. MacFuirmidh - guild level 4 dirgeash Start a Dissonance song that unsettles enemies. drunk You heal faster when drunk. Sing Attract a follower to help you. Doss - guild level 5 defame Spread nasty rumours about people. fame Give someone a good reputation. Lyrist - guild level 6 ashlullaby Start a Dissonance song that mesmerizes enemies. soothe Melody song that calms combat in a room. Canaith - guild level 7 hero Harmony role song for heroic combat. lite Cast a spell to create a light. villain Dissonance role song for villainous combat. Troubador - guild level 8 act Pretend to be someone else. brestore Undo the effects of a defaming. mirrorrefrain Chimes song that disrupts enemy timing. whispercanticle Flute song that clouds enemy focus. Sonateer - guild level 9 compose Write songs for the fiddler to play. Cli - guild level 10 : Bard emoter. apexchord Crescendo song for high Performance. echoburst Finale that bursts active song fields. specialize Choose or view your Bard archetype. vent Ventriloquism. Anstruth - guild level 11 muse Harmony song field that inspires allies. Muse - guild level 12 battlefieldsilence Finale that disrupts nearby enemies. brew Make your own white lightning. study Read a target's bardic emotional resonance. Racaraide - guild level 13 otto Dissonance song that forces a target to dance. Ollamh - guild level 14 rally Harmony song that lends courage to allies. ssing Create a singing sword. Magna Alumnae - guild level 15 Wail Finale that releases a banshee wail.

docs.title: BARD OVERVIEW
docs.text: BARD OVERVIEW Bards are flexible performers, fighters, scouts, social meddlers, and support specialists. They are not built around one perfect damage button. They are built around keeping momentum alive and turning a room's emotional state in their favor. Core ideas: Performance Your Bard momentum meter. Songs build it, especially when you vary song forms. Charisma improves how quickly this momentum builds. Some stronger powers require or spend it. Song fields Many newer Bard songs create a field that follows the Bard, pulses while it lasts, and affects allies or enemies nearby. Charisma increases song force and helps fields linger longer. Song forms Rhythm, Melody, Harmony, Dissonance, Crescendo, and Finale each do different jobs. Chaining forms can reveal hidden harmonies. Instruments Your lute works anywhere, but alternate instruments can change songs, unlock certain songs, and pair with archetypes. Archetypes At guild level 10, specialize lets you choose a deeper style such as War Conductor, Shadow Minstrel, Skald, Virtuoso, or Doom Singer. Social tools Bards can perform, spread fame or defamation, study emotional resonance, communicate well, and use lore-oriented abilities to understand the world. Attributes: Charisma is the Bard's signature attribute and now directly influences nearly every major Bard performance: song strength, song duration, Performance gain, hidden harmony reward, morale pressure, Finale impact, and several older Bard support powers. Agility and intelligence also fit the guild well. Strength, constitution, and wisdom are useful, but the guild is not meant to be a simple brute-force path. Armor and weapons: Bards can fight and use a wide range of equipment, but heavy equipment can work against some Bardic techniques. If a song or subtle ability seems poor, check your gear, instrument, Performance, and current song field. Recommended next topics: bardhelp songs bardhelp instruments bardhelp combat bardhelp archetypes

docs.title: BARD INSTRUMENTS
docs.text: BARD INSTRUMENTS Bards begin with their familiar guild lute. Alternate instruments can be carried and selected with: instrument instrument <name> instrument off The selected instrument shapes your newer battle songs. It does not replace your guild soul, and you can return to the base lute at any time. Alternate instruments are sold at the Bard Shoppe in the Darkwind Bard guildhall. Current instruments: drums Rhythm songs, Rally, follower songs, and support timing hit harder and force pulse-style propagation. flute Slightly improves Melody and Dissonance, and unlocks Whisper Canticle. Especially good for Soothe and Otto. violin Greatly improves Dissonance morale pressure, social reputation songs, and damage-oriented dread. horn Pushes songs into echo-style propagation and strengthens room-wide support, follower songs, and Finales. chimes Improves Harmony, lore reads, control precision, and unlocks Mirror Refrain. concert lute Extends song field duration and helps social, lore, and craft performances linger. war harp Improves Harmony and Crescendo battle support and helps hold enemy attention. Strong with support and damage pressure. Archetypes have favored instruments. When your archetype, instrument, active song fields, and command all point in the same direction, the command can gain more force, longer duration, stronger morale pressure, better success odds, or special flavor. Use bscore or bmon to see your currently selected instrument. New Bards should not panic about instruments immediately. Your lute works, and fix lute can restore it. Instruments become more important as you learn more song forms, unlock instrument-specific songs, and choose an archetype. Recommended next topics: bardhelp songs bardhelp archetypes bardhelp commands

docs.title: Bards are jacks-of-all-trades by nature.  If you like having a wide
docs.text: Bards are jacks-of-all-trades by nature. If you like having a wide variety of abilities, this is the right guild for you. However, in order to have this leeway, bards forfeit the opportunity to excel in any one field of expertise. Bards are first and foremost entertainers, and their skills reflect those aspects of entertainment they can incorporate into other walks of life. Bards are fair to good fighters, being able to wear nearly any armor and wield any weapon. Some of their special abilities do not function when wearing armor, for it is hard to be entertaining when you scare your audience. In their journeys, bards pick up the rudiments of mundane and magical learnings. Being somewhat roguish in nature, they also have talents to get them by when entertaining is in a slump and times are lean. Although bards get along well with others, they would be foolish not to have learned self-reliance. Thus, they are quite able to take care of themselves if they have to. In short, bards have all the benefits of being multi-classed without any of the drawbacks, such as slower advancement. Since bards are "people-people", charisma is the most important attribute. If you have further questions, just ask a bard. If you go south from the center of town in Darkwind City, you'll soon find the guild. Adaon will be glad to help you out.

docs.title: BARD PATTERNS
docs.text: BARD PATTERNS Bards can discover hidden harmonies by playing song forms in the right order. Some song fields can also pivot into deeper patterns when the room, party, instrument, archetype, or enemy state is right. When you discover either kind of pattern, your Bard soul records it. Useful commands: bpatterns Show every pattern you have learned. bpatterns harmonies Show only hidden harmonies. bpatterns pivots Show only song-field pivots. bpatterns <name> Show one learned pattern by name. Aliases: bharmonies bdiscoveries The list shows the sequence or condition that triggered the pattern, plus how many times you have seen it. Discoveries are saved with your Bard soul and remain available after relogging. Recommended next topics: bardhelp songs bardhelp instruments bardhelp archetypes

docs.title: Adaon says, "Ah, so ye be wantin' to know about the bards, eh?
docs.text: Adaon says, "Ah, so ye be wantin' to know about the bards, eh? Well, there be no one better t' ask than me. "As ye ken, bards be entertainers o' the highest degree for the most part, but that be hardly all of our skills. We are also wanderers, and seekers o' knowledge. A bard is an independent thinker: we're not much given to >politics<, we value our independence too much. "As far as performin' goes, it helps t' be versatile. Ye never know who ye may have in y'r audience! Most o' the bards that come through here learn some >music< craft. After all, the >lute< be our symbol! We have other >talents< besides this, o' course. "Ye may have seen bards walkin' about with some grandiose titles. Well, that be part of our heritage, from the elder days when we had a stricter, more formal >rank< scale. The bards were divided into ''colleges'' that did nae associate with one another. If ye ask me, I much prefer the camaraderie we have nowadays. This is the friendliest guild ye can ask for. "We bards dabble in >magic< a wee bit as well, but by no means are we masters of the art! We know enough for some tricks...>magic< is a tool for entertainment, though a bard is nae a bard if he's not imaginative! Some of our lads and lasses come up with the most interesting uses for those spells. We're not really fighters, either, but a bard can hold his own in the >fighting< department. Most o' our skills deal wi' our relations wi' others. The friendliness, persuasion, wit, and charm ye develop as a bard are your greatest allies." Adaon leans back then and says, "If ye be havin' any further questions, just ''ask about >topic<'' and I'll try t' help ye."

docs.title: "Aye, y're likely t' do a bit o' thot hereabouts," affirms Adaon.  "Nae
docs.text: "Aye, y're likely t' do a bit o' thot hereabouts," affirms Adaon. "Nae much ye ken do to get around it. >Fighting< is a way of life in the untamed wilderness. "If ye join the bards, ye'll find that ye are nae a toe-to-toe hackin' machine. Our strength lies in versatility and subtle influence than direct confrontation. Aye, we can wear quite a bit o' armor, and wield just about any weapon ye choose, even two at once, but we don't train for rigorous combat. That's what ye got fighters for. "No, bards are instead mediators. Wi' our charm and intelligent wit, we can defuse quite a few brawls before they begin, and sometimes even after. That be a valuable skill when ye travel wi' headstrong friends. They get ye all int' trouble, and ye are there t' pull y'r fat out o' the fire." Adaon chuckles. "It's happened t' me a few times, meself. "There also be some war chants to rally the spirit o' y'r comrades, if ye be of a mind t' learn them. Verra effective, too. And we teach ye a bit about what t' do after battle, as well. Aye, >fighting< is not just about swingin' a sword. That's where other guilds fall short o' the bards. The fighters can fight better, but that's all they do! We >bards< have >talents< they only dream of mastering. "T' gi' ye a bit o' advice: it dinnae matter which guild ye join, teamwork is the key t' returning alive from questing. Bein' a bard just gives ye an edge, for by havin' some talent in everything, ye can judge the strengths and weaknesses o' y'r party, and thereby be a verra effective leader. And if ye be in a small party or on y'r own, your variety of skills should give ye the resourcefulness to make it through."

docs.title: Adaon turns toward a rack on the wall behind him, and lifts an
docs.text: Adaon turns toward a rack on the wall behind him, and lifts an instrument from it. He says, "This be a >lute<, me friend, the symbol of what it is t' be a bard. It's an invaluable tool for our profession. Mark me words, if you join the >bards< and lose y'r >lute<, y'll find y'rsel' nigh helpless. O' course, if ye come back here, I can get ye another one. Always have a few extras about, for in my younger days, when I wooed women wi' me >music< and braved the world >fighting< impossible dangers, I managed to lose mine occasionally. Twas nae a fun thing, let me tell you. "Most o' a bard's >talents< are derived from the >lute<. It allows much greater expression o' y'rsel' than mere speech or song alone does." A bard may also play single clear notes on the lute with: play lute <note> Available notes are C4 D4 E4 F4 G4 A4 B4 C5 D5 E5 F5 G5 A5 B5 C6. Those nearby may hear the note through Darkflow if their sound is enabled.

docs.title: Adaon rubs his chin thoughtfully.  ">Magic<, eh?  Aye, the bards
docs.text: Adaon rubs his chin thoughtfully. ">Magic<, eh? Aye, the bards dabble in >magic<. We dinnae use it so much as a tool for combat, but as a toy, a tool for entertainment. "O' course, if ye ha' nae heard me say it before: a bard is nae a thing if not imaginative. Some o' these bairns come up with the most ingenious uses for simple magicks. But on the other hand, it is nae something we depend on. A bard relies on his wit, >talents<, and >music< more than >magic<. That is the province o' the mages. "Do ye have any another question for me?"

docs.title: Adaon smiles brightly.  "Aha, >music<!  Now ye are askin' some
docs.text: Adaon smiles brightly. "Aha, >music<! Now ye are askin' some sensible questions. A bard's >music< be his life, his very soul. Take thot away, and he be little more than a two-bit street-corner fool. ">Bards< are the masters of the musical arts. With the >lute< we craft sound, j'st as others may craft wagons, or horseshoes, or crystal goblets. Wi' our merry tunes we can influence those around us, for nothing stirs the heart quite so much as a moving melody. Sometimes they feel stirred enough to reward us for our efforts, and justly so. We put alot of effort and training int' our >music<. >Music< also tames the savage beast. I know this for a fact; it's saved me life on many an occasion. "If ye only want a single note, try >play lute C4<, or any other note between C4 and C6 that yuir lute knows." "O' course, there be many other tricks o' the trade that y'll discover for y'rsel' if ye decide to join the >bards<."

docs.title: Adaon nods, and says, "Ah, >politics<.  Aye, I know about >politics<.
docs.text: Adaon nods, and says, "Ah, >politics<. Aye, I know about >politics<. I know enough about it to say I hate em. We >bards< are nonpolitical, for the most part. Our system o' >rank< reflects that. Any that reach Anstruth be guild masters, and that be that. No special requirements, no special responsibilities. We figure that if ye made it that far, ye likely had help, so ye must have friends that respect ye. There's nothin' ye can do to force people to give ye respect; if ye can earn it then ye deserve it. "Now, I not be sayin' it's useless to advance within the guild structure; that's not true. It's just that there be no pressure upon ye to do so. Oh, there be a few bonuses to achievin' such status, like the increased training ye receive, but there is not the emphasis on guildmastership here that other guilds have. We're more easy-going, I suppose ye might say." Adaon looks thoughtfully off into space then.

docs.title: ">Rank< is nae so important t' >bards< as it is t' others," says Adaon.
docs.text: ">Rank< is nae so important t' >bards< as it is t' others," says Adaon. "It is really only used as a rough determination o' when y'r elders teach ye new skills. We don't put much emphasis on it, as far as guild >politics< goes, though. "There be fifteen ranks o' bards. In order, they are Probationer, Fochlucan, Rhymer, MacFuirmidh, Doss, Lyrist, Canaith, Troubador, Sonateer, Cli, Anstruth, Muse, Racaraide, Ollamh, and Magna Alumnae. "Some outsiders are often befuddled by our titles, when they are actually some of the most elegant and clear expressions of who we are. They are nae just an indication to other >bards< of our >rank<, but also an indication to outsiders of our standing in the world. We ha' adopted a system of naming that reflects many of our >talents<, so that upon the mere mention of a bard's title, those in the know immediately recognize his standing. "Simple and elegant, like the bards ourselves," concludes Adaon with a wink.

docs.title: Adaon says, "As a bard ye would ha' a wide range o' >talents< at
docs.text: Adaon says, "As a bard ye would ha' a wide range o' >talents< at your disposal. If there's one thing a bard is, it's versatile. Jack of all trades, y'know. "One o' the first things ye learn as a bard are a few feats of manual dexterity. Sleight o' hand, ye could call it." Adaon smiles. "Aye, sleight of hand. Ye also get a bit of schoolin' o' old tales and legends. They are nae only a good story t' tell to folks, but are also a might useful on y'r travels. The guild will supply ye wi' a >lute<, which aids in the use o' y'r >talents<. "We teach ye a bit of ventriloquism then, and how t' earn y'rsel' a bit o' money if y' nae be in shape to fight for it. After that, ye will learn a wide variety of musical styles with a range of applications in adventuring life. It be nigh impossible t' list all the things ye can do with >music<, and we >bards< are always coming up wi' more. We throw in a bit o' acting, and mime, so ye can be more impressive and expressive without saying a word. "O' course," Adaon chuckles, "we bards're no stranger to strong drink. Ye'll be able to drink anyone else under the table, all the while maintainin' a clear head yerself... well, more or less. Now that's what I call talent, eh? "Ye can eventualy will learn some chants that inspire and otherwise aid in combat." Adaon leans upon the desk, awaiting another question.

docs.title: BARD SONGS AND PERFORMANCE
docs.text: BARD SONGS AND PERFORMANCE Battle songs are different from simple lute practice. They create a bardic song field in the room for a short time, pulse effects while they last, and feed the Bard's Performance. Performance is a 0-100 momentum meter shown with bscore. It rises when you keep songs moving and falls when combat momentum stalls or your voice is disrupted. Repeating the same kind of song builds less Performance than keeping the music varied. Charisma improves Performance gains, song field strength, song field duration, and the rewards from hidden harmonies. Battle songs use musical cooldown families. Each song form has its own short recovery, so a Rhythm song does not lock out Melody, Harmony, or Dissonance. This is intentional: Bards are meant to build momentum by changing forms. A tiny song cadence cooldown still prevents button-mashing, and repeating the same form waits on that form's timer. When Performance crests into a Crescendo, you have a brief Finale window. Use bmon or bscore to watch for it, then spend it with echoburst, battlefieldsilence, or Wail. Song forms: Rhythm timing, movement, attack cadence Melody morale, recovery, emotional control Harmony group amplification Dissonance disruption and weakening Crescendo burst pressure Finale high-impact endings Current battle songs: Pulsebeat March Command: pulsebeat Alias: pulsebeat_march Form: Rhythm Timer: short Rhythm recovery Effect: Starts a song field around the Bard that follows as the Bard moves and periodically sharpens nearby party members' attack timing. Ember Aria Command: emberaria Alias: ember_aria Form: Melody Timer: short Melody recovery Effect: Starts a song field around the Bard that follows as the Bard moves and periodically steadies nearby party members' footing. Silver Verse Command: silververse Alias: silver_verse Form: Melody Timer: short Melody recovery Effect: Starts a song field around the Bard that follows as the Bard moves and periodically mends nearby party members. Echo Chord Command: echochord Alias: echo_chord Form: Harmony Timer: short Harmony recovery Effect: Starts a song field around the Bard that follows as the Bard moves and periodically binds nearby party members into shared timing. Dirge of Ash Command: dirgeash Alias: dirge_of_ash Form: Dissonance Timer: short Dissonance recovery Effect: Starts a song field around the Bard that follows as the Bard moves and presses against nearby enemies' courage. Lullaby of Ash Command: ashlullaby Alias: lullaby_of_ash Form: Dissonance Timer: short Dissonance recovery Effect: Starts a song field around the Bard that follows as the Bard moves and presses enemies into a mesmerized haze. Whisper Canticle Command: whispercanticle Alias: whisper_canticle Form: Melody Timer: short Melody recovery Effect: A flute-unlocked song that mesmerizes nearby enemies. Mirror Refrain Command: mirrorrefrain Alias: mirror_refrain Form: Harmony Timer: short Harmony recovery Effect: A chimes-unlocked song that scatters hostile timing and focus. Soothe Command: soothe Form: Melody Timer: short Melody recovery Effect: Attempts to end combat in the room and presses hostile creatures into a brief mesmerized calm. Hero Command: hero Form: Harmony Timer: short Harmony recovery Effect: A role song for good-aligned Bards that reinforces heroic combat. Villain Command: villain Form: Dissonance Timer: short Dissonance recovery Effect: A role song for evil-aligned Bards that reinforces villainous combat. Apex Chord Command: apexchord Alias: apex_chord Form: Crescendo Timer: Crescendo recovery Effect: Requires high Performance. Starts a short, powerful song field that helps push a fight toward a Finale. Echo Burst Command: echoburst Alias: echo_burst Form: Finale Timer: Finale recovery Effect: Spends an active Crescendo to make all active song fields pulse with much greater force. Battlefield Silence Command: battlefieldsilence Alias: battlefield_silence Form: Finale Timer: Finale recovery Effect: Spends an active Crescendo to disrupt nearby enemies and deepen morale pressure. Muse Hymn Command: muse Form: Harmony Timer: Harmony recovery Effect: Starts a song field around the Bard that follows as the Bard moves and periodically inspires nearby party members. Otto's Irresistible Dance Command: otto <target> Form: Dissonance Timer: Dissonance recovery Effect: Tangles a target's rhythm and forces them to dance away. Rally Command: rally Form: Harmony Timer: Harmony recovery Effect: Lends courage and mental resilience to nearby players. Wail Command: Wail or Wail <target> Form: Finale Timer: Finale recovery Effect: Spends an active Crescendo to release a focused or room-wide banshee wail. More than twenty sequences of song forms can resolve into hidden harmonies. These are not listed here. Bards are expected to discover them through performance. Archetypes can deepen certain hidden harmonies, adding extra momentum, lingering resonance, and distinct thematic messages. When you discover a hidden harmony or cause a song field to pivot into a deeper pattern, your Bard soul records it. Use bpatterns to review what you have learned. Use bpatterns harmonies, bpatterns pivots, or bpatterns <name> to narrow the list and see how to trigger a learned pattern again. Charisma matters to hidden harmonies. A more charismatic Bard can draw more momentum out of a resolved pattern and hold the resonance longer. Active songs also matter to other Bard commands. A Bard with the right field already moving can make related powers stronger: Rhythm helps timing, followers, combat pressure, and support tempo Melody helps healing, calm, social influence, and control Harmony helps party support, role songs, lore, and precision Dissonance helps fear, morale damage, tricks, and enemy control Crescendo helps burst pressure, Finales, and dramatic command moments For example, Soothe benefits from Melody or Dissonance, Rally benefits from Harmony or Rhythm, Wail benefits from Dissonance, Crescendo, and Finale pressure, and Study benefits from Harmony or precise hidden patterns. Some songs can also shift enemy morale. At higher guild levels, use study on a target to read the emotional resonance your music has left behind. INSTRUMENTS AND ARCHETYPES Alternate Bard instruments can change how battle songs behave. Buy them at the Bard Shoppe in the Darkwind Bard guildhall. Use instrument to list carried instruments, instrument <name> to select one, and instrument off to return to your base lute. See bardhelp instruments. At guild level 10, specialize chooses a Bard archetype. Archetypes shape song momentum, field strength, instrument affinity, field flavor, and hidden harmony resonance. See bardhelp archetypes. SIMPLE LUTE PRACTICE These simple songs can be practiced with your lute by playing each note in order: play lute <note> Mary Had a Little Lamb E4 D4 C4 D4 E4 E4 E4 D4 D4 D4 E4 G4 G4 Twinkle Twinkle C4 C4 G4 G4 A4 A4 G4 F4 F4 E4 E4 D4 D4 C4 Ode to Joy E4 E4 F4 G4 G4 F4 E4 D4 C4 C4 D4 E4 E4 D4 D4 Scarborough Fair A4 E5 E5 B4 C5 B4 A4 G4 A4 B4 C5 A4 A4 Recommended next topics: bardhelp instruments bardhelp combat bardhelp archetypes

docs.title: BARD QUICK START
docs.text: BARD QUICK START This is the practical path for a new Bard. 1. Check yourself. bscore bmon on bcmds bscore shows your Bard state. bmon keeps important Bard updates visible. bcmds shows what you can use now and what unlocks later. 2. Fix your lute. fix lute Your guild lute is your fallback instrument. If it is missing or damaged, this restores it without needing to return to Adaon. 3. Learn your first combat song. pulsebeat Pulsebeat March is your first song field. It follows you, pulses while it lasts, helps nearby allies, and teaches you the rhythm of the Bard system. 4. Watch Performance. Performance is Bard momentum. It rises when you keep songs moving, especially when you vary forms instead of repeating the same thing. Charisma improves that momentum, makes songs stronger, and helps song fields linger. Stronger Bard powers and Finales care about Performance. Song forms have separate cooldowns, so pulsebeat into emberaria into echochord feels much faster than repeating the same song form. 5. Practice simple music. play lute <note> bardhelp songs Simple note practice is separate from battle songs. It is useful for flavor, roleplay, and learning note names. Battle songs are full commands such as pulsebeat, emberaria, echochord, and dirgeash. 6. Earn and explore. perform legend <item> lore <monster> Bards are social explorers. perform can earn coins, legend reads objects, and lore helps you judge creatures. 7. Build your Bard legend. gscore Bard bscore glevel Bards earn Bard XP by contributing to level-appropriate battles. Bard XP advances your guild level automatically when your character level, total guild levels, and Charisma allow it. Excess Bard XP remains banked until a blocked level becomes available. The glevel command at a Bard hall explains any current gate; it no longer spends ordinary character experience. 8. Buy instruments when you can. Alternate instruments are sold in the Bard Shoppe in the Darkwind Bard guildhall. Use instrument to choose one. Instruments change newer battle songs and unlock a few songs. 9. Choose an archetype at guild level 10. specialize specialize <archetype> Archetypes are not just labels. They change momentum, field strength, instrument affinity, hidden harmonies, and message flavor. Next topics: bardhelp songs bardhelp instruments bardhelp combat bardhelp commands

docs.title: BARD SUPPORT
docs.text: BARD SUPPORT Bards are strong party support because many songs follow the Bard and pulse in the room. You help allies by improving timing, courage, recovery, and emotional control. You hinder enemies by disrupting morale and focus. Ally support: pulsebeat Helps nearby party members keep sharper timing. emberaria Steadies nearby party members. silververse Mends nearby party members. echochord Shares timing through Harmony. muse Inspires nearby party members. rally Lends courage and mental resilience. Enemy control: dirgeash Presses enemy courage. ashlullaby Pushes enemies into a mesmerized haze. whispercanticle Clouds enemy focus. mirrorrefrain Scatters hostile timing. soothe Attempts to calm combat in the room. otto Forces one target into a dance. Finishing moments: apexchord Crescendo setup. echoburst Bursts active song fields. battlefieldsilence Disrupts nearby enemies. Wail Releases a banshee Finale. Support is not passive. Keep moving through forms, use your instrument, and watch Performance. Charisma improves your support pressure: stronger pulses, longer fields, better morale influence, and stronger Rally and Soothe outcomes. If you stay on one note forever, the room learns your trick. Support commands now look at your whole Bardic context. War Conductors, drums, horns, war harps, active Harmony, and active Rhythm can all make support moments feel stronger. Shadow Minstrels, flutes, chimes, Melody, and Dissonance can make calming or control support sharper. Recommended next topics: bardhelp songs bardhelp combat bardhelp instruments

docs.title: BARD COMMUNICATION
docs.text: BARD COMMUNICATION Bards are social by design. These commands help you stay connected with other Bards and with the guild. bard <message> Speak on the Bard guild channel. : <message> Send a Bard emote. bemotes List available Bard emotes. bardhist Review recent Bard channel history. bards List Bards currently online. bgm <message> Guild master channel. Requires guild level 11. bgmhist Review recent Bard guild master channel history. Bards also learn more racial languages than most guilds. Communication is part of the guild's identity, not just a convenience.

docs.title: Berserker Armour
docs.text: Berserker Armour Berserkers are unrestricted martial combatants. They may wear light, medium, or heavy armour, including shields, without disabling Berserker abilities or combat progression. Armour material is likewise unrestricted. Individual items may still impose their own race, level, size, slot, or other wear restrictions. Those restrictions belong to the item rather than the Berserker guild. Use "berhelp armour" or "berhelp armor" to read this information again.

docs.title: The Berserker Guild
docs.text: The Berserker Guild Berserkers are warriors who refuse to let pain remain merely pain. Injury, pressure, and a hard fight build Fury. At its peak, that Fury breaks loose as Frenzy: a rapid series of attacks that empties the Berserker's rage into whoever is standing in front of them. Fury is not the only danger. A Berserker who learns to hold back Frenzy can turn excess rage into Madness. Madness makes the Berserker harder and more violent, but each step gives up another measure of control. The "bvent" command can clear Fury and Madness once the fighting has stopped. At Madness 4, each main-hand attack can gain extra swings. Most surges add one, but increasingly rare rolls add two, three, or four at once. Momentum mastery improves every tier of that long-tail chance, and Madness 5 improves it again. Uncontrolled bonus rounds are non-reentrant and are not generated by Frenzy pulse rounds, preventing either mechanic from recursively multiplying combat. Madness 5 also leaves the Berserker Exposed and, outside combat, deals 2% of maximum health every ten seconds until the Madness subsides. A strong Black Scar reduces that self-damage. Use "berhelp madness" for the exact chances and the effects of every Madness level. Berserkers follow their own course of advancement. Combat earns Berserker Rank, and each Rank grants one Vex. Vex can be spent through "vex train" to deepen the Blood, Momentum, and Defiance branches. Every branch contains both active abilities and lessons that change how those abilities behave. Use "vex tree" to see the path ahead. Hunting across varied areas keeps combat awards strongest; bosses are exempt from this hunting adjustment. Once a branch has been completed, further Vex can be placed into its mastery. Mastery has no final rank. Its greatest combat gains come early, while later ranks stand as a record of dedication. Scars mark the fights a Berserker has survived. They are permanent once earned. With the Flare ability, one scar can be awakened for a short time. Use "scars" to review the marks carried on your baldric. An awakened scar appears as Flared Scar in the "buffs" display while at full strength. Each scar remembers a different ordeal: Blood comes from victory while badly wounded, Iron from enduring brutal blows or control, Packbreaker from winning while heavily outnumbered, Frenzy from carrying a frenzy through several kills, and Black from pushing Madness to its limit. These are hints rather than exact formulas; the "scars" command repeats them when needed. The scars command also explains their effects. Blood converts part of damage dealt into healing, Iron improves weapon and control resistance, Packbreaker rewards fighting several enemies, Frenzy adds one or two pulses to a Frenzy, and Black reduces Madness 5's out-of-combat self-damage. Enrage costs 8% of maximum health, falling to 6% at rank 3. Blood Price still rewards fighting below 35% health, but at Blood Price rank 3 Enrage receives that Fury bonus at any health. Thick Hide grants its listed base weapon resistance while Mad and scales to twice that value at 25% health or lower. The "berskills" command lists active abilities, their commands, current costs, cooldowns, and Vex training. "berskills available" shows only the abilities already trained. Help for a particular command is available through "berhelp <command>". Every Berserker also knows several core techniques outside the Vex tree. Vent spends SP to force accumulated rage away. Incite creates a timed effect that trades SP for a stream of Fury during combat. Wildrage wakes a temporary chaos proc in the main weapon for three to ten minutes depending on level. Heave spends SP on a Constitution-assisted, weight-driven weapon strike that can damage a breakable weapon; Sheave trades some damage to strike safely with a worn shield. Berserkers may use light, medium, or heavy armour, including shields. Type "berhelp armour" for details about guild and item restrictions. Other useful commands include: bstatus Review Rank, XP, Vex, resources, and active states frenzymode Choose automatic or directed Frenzy berserk, ber <message> Speak on the Berserker guild channel berserkers, bers List active Berserkers bhist [lines] Review recent guild conversation The Darkwind trainer handles joining, experience conversion, and Vex retraining. "convert berserker <normal-xp|next>" trades normal experience for Berserker experience. "retrain vex confirm" refunds trained Vex for an escalating coin fee without removing Rank, scars, or other lasting progress.

docs.title: Madness
docs.text: Madness When Fury is already full, further Fury gain builds overflow. Enough overflow raises Madness instead of starting another Frenzy. Madness is cumulative: each level retains the effects of the levels below it. The "bvent" command clears Fury and Madness outside combat, though high Madness can make Vent fail. Every Madness level adds 5% base weapon resistance before Thick Hide, Defiance mastery, and scar effects. Madness also removes the Fury cost from Fury-spending abilities, though their other costs and cooldowns still apply. At any Madness level, combat can briefly disrupt concentration. Madness 1: grants 5% base weapon resistance. Madness 2: raises base weapon resistance to 10%, adds 15% critical damage, and prevents voluntary retreat during combat. Madness 3: raises base weapon resistance to 15%, gains a 15% chance to counter a weapon hit with the current main-hand or unarmed attack without changing targets, and gains a 25% chance to resist paralysis or entanglement. Madness 4: raises base weapon resistance to 20%, raises the critical damage bonus to 30%, can add extra main-hand swings, and has a 35% chance per attack to provoke an uncontrolled attack. Madness 5: raises base weapon resistance to 25%, raises paralysis and entanglement resistance to 50%, gives each hit a 25% chance to leave its target Exposed, and leaves the Berserker Exposed. Outside combat it also deals 2% maximum health as blunt damage every ten seconds. A strong Black Scar reduces this self-damage; a fully effective Black Scar suppresses it. At Madness 4, each main-hand attack has a 15% chance to gain at least one extra swing, a 4% chance to gain at least two, a 1% chance to gain at least three, and a 0.25% chance to gain four. One roll determines the whole result, so most surges are small and the larger bursts are increasingly rare. At Madness 5 those baseline chances become 20%, 6%, 2%, and 0.5%. Momentum mastery improves every tier of the distribution. A surge can never add more than four swings. Madness is powerful by design, but holding its highest levels carries the risk of lost control, Exposed, failed Vent attempts, and persistent self-damage. An uncontrolled attack cannot schedule another uncontrolled attack while it is pending or executing. Frenzy pulse attack rounds also cannot generate uncontrolled attacks. Normal combat rounds may still trigger one at Madness 4 or 5, but the resulting bonus round is bounded and non-reentrant.

docs.title: Blood Mage
docs.text: Blood Mage Blood Mages are dangerous spellcasters whose magic is bound to vitality, sacrifice, and the manipulation of blood. Their path trades safety for power and demands careful management of both magical and physical resources. Current roster status: CLOSED TO NEW APPLICANTS. This page remains in the tome so returning players can recognize the name. Use help guilds for the current roster; a closed path cannot be chosen by a new character.

docs.title: An Inventory of Tricks, Devices, and Plausible Denials
docs.text: An Inventory of Tricks, Devices, and Plausible Denials Use 'chskills' for the full ledger: spell-point cost, recovery time, Rank, road, and trade requirements. 'chskills available' shows only the tricks you can pull off right now. At Rank 35 and every five Ranks through 105, Drina opens another scheme. Schemes are horizontal modifications to these tricks rather than new road ranks. Use 'schemes' to inspect the catalogue and active cloak notes. Misdirection confuse [foe] Talk, feint, and insist until a foe's attention goes somewhere harmless. Available from Rank 1; deeper Misdirection makes the lie stick. suckerpunch [foe] Available from Rank 1. Cash in an opening with one profoundly unfair melee hit. Misdirection adds force and eventually brings a second weapon into the argument. distract [foe] Rank 3, Misdirection 2. Throw your voice somewhere inconvenient. With enough practice, a foe may briefly forget whom they were fighting. avoid Rank 4, Misdirection 3. Revive the Confidence's fancy footwork and make yourself substantially harder to hit for a short, buff-visible window. Volatility brewacid Rank 2, Volatility 1, Alchemy 25. Prepare the owner-bound base flask used by Cook Ash. It can also be thrown by Charlatans with poor impulse control. brewelement <fire|ice|lightning> Rank 3, Volatility 2, Alchemy 75. Bottle some deeply uncooperative weather for throwing. Every successful throw splashes part of the blast back. cookash <grey|red|blue|mixed> Rank 2, Volatility 1. Empty every relevant ash from a corpse burner into an acid flask. Quaffing grants an ash-specific combat rush shown in buffs. concoct <red salt|blue mixer|cutting bitters> Rank 2, Volatility 2. Prepare a seasoning for carried food or drink. Benefits vary; fine print is compulsory. Contraband loadweapon <weapon> with <corrosive|dazzling|oiled|silvered|flaming|frozen|poisoned|shocking> Rank 2. Fit a temporary and dubiously safe treatment to an unwielded, ordinary weapon. Better tricks require deeper Contraband and trade skill. cdip <dart|darts> in <acid flask|element flask|poison> Rank 2, Contraband 1, Alchemy 25. Spend one real dose to coat up to ten clean caravan darts. Liquid Assets removes the limit. Acid can Sunder; other liquids retain their nature. stretchpoison <poison> onto <weapon> Rank 3, Contraband 2, Alchemy 100. Make one proper poison last longer at reduced strength. The poison always gets one vote about your technique. pocketsand [foe] Rank 4, Contraband 2. Attempt to blind a nearby foe using tactical grit stored in a pocket no tailor admits sewing. Caravan stock Ordinary throwing darts remain for sale and use 'throw <target>'. Acid and elemental flasks are brewed rather than shop stock. Cdip restores the useful part of the old poison-dart trick by requiring a real flask or prepared poison. Flying potions, smoke packets, and special bottles remain retired.

docs.title: Avoid: Fancy Footwork, Honest Name
docs.text: Avoid: Fancy Footwork, Honest Name Syntax: avoid At Rank 4 and Misdirection 3, prepare a short span of deeply unfair footwork. Avoid makes you substantially harder to hit and appears in 'buffs'. Once the performance ends, your feet need a while before they will agree to an encore.

docs.title: Brew Acid: The Necessary Bad Idea
docs.text: Brew Acid: The Necessary Bad Idea Syntax: brewacid At Rank 2, Volatility 1, and Alchemy 25, prepare one owner-bound acid flask. Cook Ash consumes that flask and all relevant ash to make a combat stimulant. Only one uncooked flask may be carried at a time. It lasts two hours and can instead be thrown for modest acid damage. Throw it with 'throw acid flask at <target>'. While fighting, 'throw acid flask' uses your current foe. Throwing engages combat, consumes the flask, and splashes one fifth of the dealt damage back onto you.

docs.title: Brew Element: Weather, Now Available in Glass
docs.text: Brew Element: Weather, Now Available in Glass Syntax: brewelement <fire|ice|lightning> Alias: elementpotion At Rank 3, Volatility 2, and Alchemy 75, prepare one owner-bound flask of bottled fire, ice, or lightning. Only one elemental flask may be carried at a time. It lasts two hours and delivers the advertised weather when thrown. Use 'throw <element> flask at <target>'. While fighting, omit 'at <target>' to throw it at your current foe. Each successful throw consumes the flask, engages combat, and kicks some of the blast back onto you. Drinking one is technically possible and medically discouraging.

docs.title: The Charlatan Line: Confidential, Naturally
docs.text: The Charlatan Line: Confidential, Naturally charlatan <message> Speak to the Confidence cchat <message> A shorter lie for the same line echarlatan <emote> Emote manually ecchat <emote> The shorter manual emote charlatan :<soul emote> Use a channel soul Media links and soul emotes work as they do on the other guild lines. guild Charlatan muff guild Charlatan unmuff guild Charlatan color <color> Muffling the line is called "incognito" on cwho. It sounds much better than "ignoring everyone."

docs.title: CCook
docs.text: CCook 'Ccook' is the old shorthand still accepted for 'cookash'. Use 'charlhelp cookash' before combining heat, corpse ash, and optimism.

docs.title: The Confidence: A Charlatan's First Honest Document
docs.text: The Confidence: A Charlatan's First Honest Document Welcome to the Confidence. The name is impressive, the paperwork is questionable, and your cloak has more pockets than anyone remembers sewing. Charlatans win by making the wrong thing look certain. Some talk a foe into forgetting the fight. Some turn corpse ash into something fizzy and legally distinct from medicine. Some improve weapons with substances best handled by someone else. The wisest learn a little of all three and deny everything. Your reputation is measured in Charlatan Rank and guild XP. Worthy fights and boss victories earn guild XP. Each Rank after the first gives you one road point until you have earned thirty, enough to complete all three roads: Misdirection - lies, openings, thrown voices, and weaponized confidence Volatility - unstable brews, additives, ash, and regrettable chemistry Contraband - loaded weapons, stretched poison, and excellent excuses Use: chskills [available] Inspect the tricks in your cloak gscore charlatan See Rank, guild XP, roads, and profession skills croads train <road> Spend an uninvested road point schemes Inspect Rank 35+ cons and active cloak notes charlhelp commands Read the full command ledger charlatan <message> Work the guild line Every new Charlatan can confuse a mark and suckerpunch the opening. Roads add specialties after Rank 1; they do not make you earn your first unfair fight. At Rank 35 and every five Ranks through 105, Drina opens another horizontal scheme. You can learn every scheme eventually, but only a few cloak notes can be active at once. Alchemy, Herbalism, and Smithing are learned through their own trades. Your roads decide what sort of rascal you are; those professions decide whether you can safely execute the technical parts. "Safely" is used generously. The old Alchemist and Illusionist focus ledgers are closed. The practical old poison-dart idea survives as 'cdip', using real modern flasks and prepared poisons. If an ancient page promises flying potions or a personal shadow army, check the date, check your pockets, and use 'chskills'.

docs.title: Charlatan Help: The Index Nobody Swears Is Complete
docs.text: Charlatan Help: The Index Nobody Swears Is Complete Syntax: charlhelp [topic|command] Alias: chelp Useful entries in the Confidence's little black book: intro Who the Confidence claims to be commands Every trick currently admitted into evidence abilities A guided tour of the dangerous pockets roads Misdirection, Volatility, and Contraband schemes Rank 35+ cons, cloak notes, and active loadouts chat Etiquette for the Charlatan line, allegedly members The Confidence's active roll You can also ask about a trick by name: charlhelp confuse charlhelp brewacid charlhelp brewelement charlhelp cookash charlhelp loadweapon charlhelp schemes If a crossed-out entry disagrees with 'chskills', trust the cloak. The cloak is newer, armed, and standing closer to you.

docs.title: The Confidence Remembers Everything Except Liability
docs.text: The Confidence Remembers Everything Except Liability Syntax: chist [lines] Review recent Charlatan-line chatter. With no number, you receive the last twenty entries. You may request as many as three hundred, should your case against your colleagues require that much evidence.

docs.title: The Charlatan's Working Ledger
docs.text: The Charlatan's Working Ledger Information, reputation, and gossip: charlhelp [topic|command] The little black book; alias: chelp chskills [available] Your trick ledger; alias: cskills gscore charlatan Rank, guild XP, roads, and professions croads train <road> Invest one available road point schemes [list|info <name>] Inspect Rank 35+ scheme notes schemes learn <name> Pay Drina to learn an open scheme schemes activate <name> Fill an empty active slot at Drina schemes swap <old> for <new> Pay Drina to rewrite the active loadout charlatan <message> Guild line; alias: cchat chist [lines] Recent Confidence gossip cwho Visible Charlatans; alias: charlatans Misdirection -- for marks who insist on paying attention: confuse [foe] suckerpunch [foe] Alias: spunch distract [foe] avoid Volatility -- chemistry with an exit strategy: brewacid brewelement <fire|ice|lightning> Alias: elementpotion cookash <grey|red|blue|mixed> Alias: ccook concoct <red salt|blue mixer|cutting bitters> Alias: cmix Contraband -- improvements without warranties: loadweapon <weapon> with <corrosive|dazzling|oiled|silvered|flaming|frozen|poisoned|shocking> cdip <dart|darts> in <acid flask|element flask|poison> Aliases: cpoison, poisondart stretchpoison <poison> onto <weapon> pocketsand [foe] The caravan shops also sell ordinary throwing darts. Carry one and use 'throw <target>'. Cdip can turn one real flask or poison dose into as many as ten coated darts; Liquid Assets removes that limit. Acid coatings can leave a victim Sundered. Use 'charlhelp <command>' or 'chskills' for costs and requirements.

docs.title: Concoct: Season to Taste, Disclose Nothing
docs.text: Concoct: Season to Taste, Disclose Nothing Syntax: concoct <red salt|blue mixer|cutting bitters> Alias: cmix At Rank 2 and Volatility 2, prepare one additive that lasts thirty minutes. Use 'mix <additive> into <carried food or drink>'. One packet treats an entire snack, meal, jug, or keg, provided the fare is not above the maker's level. Red restorative salt Alchemy 75; four red ash. Improves health recovery and adds brief health regeneration, but collects spell points at the door. Effervescent blue mixer Alchemy 75; four blue ash. Improves spell-point recovery and adds brief spell-point regeneration, but takes a small bite out of the customer. Cutting bitters Herbalism 50; three grey ash. Improves both kinds of healing and makes the meal easier to stomach, but briefly ruins concentration. Higher Alchemy helps the red and blue mixtures, within reason. The packet is transferable; the warranty is not. Inspect treated fare for exact values. When consumed, it tells the customer how strong the lingering recovery is and how long it will last. A humble meal does not secretly water down the dose.

docs.title: Confuse: Certainty Applied Incorrectly
docs.text: Confuse: Certainty Applied Incorrectly Syntax: confuse [foe] Point out the ambush that is not there. Correct your foe's stance with great authority. Ask whether they remembered to lock the door. For a few precious moments, the mark may be too tangled in your certainty to act properly. Confuse is available from Charlatan Rank 1. Misdirection makes the lie easier to sell, keeps it alive longer, and makes it less exhausting. The cloak will never stake more than 150 SP on one story. Confuse takes longer to recover than the distraction lasts. Success tells you when Sucker Punch is primed. A foe who sees through you still costs the effort and recovery time; embarrassment is not a refund policy.

docs.title: Cook Ash: Waste Not, Warn Nobody
docs.text: Cook Ash: Waste Not, Warn Nobody Syntax: cookash <grey|red|blue|mixed> Alias: ccook At Rank 2 and Volatility 1, use an acid flask made with 'brewacid' and empty all relevant ash from a carried corpse burner into it. A single-colour batch needs at least 10 matching ash. Mixed needs at least 10 of every colour and empties all three stores. Grey - Alchemy 25; accuracy and defensive footwork Red - Alchemy 75; direct combat damage Blue - Alchemy 75; accuracy and one extra swing Mixed - Alchemy 150; a smaller blend of red and blue benefits Aim for 100 ash when you want a proper batch. Feeding it more still stretches the rush, but the difference soon becomes difficult to notice. The resulting owner-bound vial goes flat after two hours. Quaffing starts a Cookash Rush shown in 'buffs'; only one rush can be active. Throwing the cooked vial keeps its elemental surprise and always splashes the Charlatan too. This is called quality control. The cloak needs only a few seconds before it can cook another, provided you have another acid flask and enough ash.

docs.title: Three Roads, No Refunds
docs.text: Three Roads, No Refunds Syntax: croads train <misdirection|volatility|contraband> Every Charlatan Rank after the first earns one road point. Spending it is immediate and permanent, which is why the clerk asks you to spell the road. Road awards stop after 30 points, enough to raise all three roads to ten. Ranks after 30 build reputation and open advanced schemes instead. Misdirection Confuse the mark, manufacture openings, and throw your voice. Improves confuse and suckerpunch, and opens distract. Volatility Make corpse ash useful and meals suspicious. Opens cookash and concoct. Alchemy or Herbalism may still be required for a particular recipe. Contraband Load weapons and stretch acquired poisons. Alchemy and Smithing decide which dangerous ideas you can put into practice. Use 'gscore charlatan' to see your Rank, guild XP, roads, spare points, and relevant trade skills. Use 'chskills available' when you want the short answer to, "What can I get away with today?"

docs.title: The Confidence's Dubiously Official Roll
docs.text: The Confidence's Dubiously Official Roll Syntax: cwho Alias: charlatans List the visible Charlatans currently abroad. The roll includes reputation, dominant road, present activity, and whatever credential the clerk invented for that Rank. Road callings include Misdirector, Volatilist, Contrabandist, Eclectic, and Undeclared. "Incognito" means the Charlatan line is muffed, not that the member has become especially subtle.

docs.title: Distract: Throw Your Voice, Keep Your Teeth
docs.text: Distract: Throw Your Voice, Keep Your Teeth Syntax: distract [foe] At Rank 3 and Misdirection 2, place an insult, warning, or deeply personal observation just over your foe's shoulder. The interruption spoils their concentration. With deep enough Misdirection, the mark may briefly disengage while searching for the imaginary speaker. A foe who refuses the bait still costs you the effort and recovery time.

docs.title: Charlatan
docs.text: Charlatan Charlatans are tricksters who turn misdirection, volatile mixtures, contraband, and bad ideas into an adventuring discipline. Their toolkit favors control, prepared surprises, temporary weapon tricks, and victories whose fine print arrives later. Current roster status: CLOSED TO NEW APPLICANTS. This page remains in the tome for existing and returning characters. Use help guilds for the current roster; a closed path cannot be chosen by a new character.

docs.title: Load Weapon: Improvements Made While You Wait Nervously
docs.text: Load Weapon: Improvements Made While You Wait Nervously Syntax: loadweapon <weapon> with <corrosive|dazzling|oiled|silvered|flaming|frozen|poisoned|shocking> Treat a carried, unwielded, ordinary weapon. Unique pieces refuse the work, presumably on advice from better lawyers. Dazzling Contraband 1, Alchemy 50. A shifting finish leaves the weapon Razzled. "Flash" remains accepted when ordering. Oiled Contraband 2, Alchemy 70. Makes the weapon markedly easier to place. The benefit takes hold as soon as the weapon is ready again. Corrosive Contraband 2, Alchemy 75, and one fresh acid flask. Acid strikes can leave a living victim Sundered, but the treatment lowers weapon class by one while it remains applied. "Acid" remains accepted when ordering. Poisoned Contraband 2, Alchemy 100. Adds a direct poison treatment. Stretch Poison remains the better way to preserve a prepared poison's special payload. Flaming / Frozen Contraband 3, Alchemy 100. Adds fire or cold to each convincing strike, which may leave the victim Burning or Chilled. Silvered Contraband 4, Alchemy 125, Smithing 50, and one saved Silver Bar. Leaves the weapon Silvered. "Quicksilver" remains accepted when ordering. Shocking Contraband 4, Alchemy 150. Adds lightning and a slim chance that the victim's muscles briefly reconsider their obligations. Greater trade skill improves the treatment's strength and lifetime. Every load has a drawback. Dazzling can very rarely steal concentration; Sharpened weapons made elsewhere can very rarely leave a foe Bleeding. If it did not have fine print, someone reputable would sell it.

docs.title: Pocket Sand: Tactical Geology
docs.text: Pocket Sand: Tactical Geology Syntax: pocketsand [foe] At Rank 4 and Contraband 2, fling a handful of allegedly tactical grit at a nearby foe. Dexterity, Charisma, and Contraband improve the chance to blind. The attempt begins combat, and you will need a moment to find another pocketful afterward.

docs.title: Advanced Schemes: Notes Nobody Admits Dictating
docs.text: Advanced Schemes: Notes Nobody Admits Dictating Syntax: schemes [list] schemes info <name> schemes learn <name> schemes activate <name> schemes swap <active> for <learned> Charlatan Rank opens one new scheme every five Ranks from 35 through 105. Drina teaches each open scheme for gold and you permanently scribble its notes inside your cloak. Learning automatically activates the scheme when an empty slot is available. A learned, inactive scheme may fill a newly earned empty slot for free; replacing an occupied slot costs gold. One scheme may be active initially. Rank 50 opens a second active slot, Rank 100 opens a third, and every fifty Ranks thereafter opens another. By Rank 105 every scheme can be learned, but only three can be active. Rank 35 Hair Trigger Loading a weapon in combat immediately throws a carried elemental or acid flask at the current foe. Rank 40 Unstable Mixture Elemental flasks deal 20 percent less direct damage but leave Burning, Chilled, or lost concentration behind. Rank 45 Bad Batch Cookash gains two potency and loses one quarter of its duration. One batch in four reveals itself as the wrong colour when quaffed. Rank 50 Hot Merchandise Weapon loads last 50 percent longer and double their fitting side effect. Rank 55 Cut Product Stretch Poison leaves a second owner-bound weaker dose that preserves the source poison's unusual nastiness. Both coatings lose one strength. Rank 60 Loaded Question Successful Confuse blocks concentration for three extra seconds instead of fully paralyzing the mark. Rank 65 Second Story A resisted Confuse may still spoil concentration for two seconds. Rank 70 Improvised Exit Avoid breaks the current fight as it begins, but Fancy Footwork lasts half as long. Rank 75 Fine Print Red salt and blue mixer halve their immediate bonus and double their regeneration duration. Rank 80 Plausible Deniability Volatile flasks stop splashing their thrower and deal 30 percent less direct damage. Rank 85 Marked Cards Pocket Sand used on an already distracted mark exposes instead of blinds. Rank 90 False Bottom Carry two acid and two elemental flasks at once. Flasks brewed while the scheme is active lose one potency. Rank 95 Double Bluff Distract exposes a fooled mark instead of trying to end the fight. Rank 100 The Long Con An opening-powered Sucker Punch trades half its bonus burst for a longer Exposed condition. Rank 105 Liquid Assets Cdip coats every clean caravan dart carried or stored in the cloak instead of stopping after ten. Listing and inspecting schemes works anywhere. Drina must be present to teach, activate, or swap cloak notes. She does not extend credit and denies ever having seen your handwriting.

docs.title: Spunch
docs.text: Spunch 'Spunch' is the street name for 'suckerpunch'. Use 'charlhelp suckerpunch' for the complete and entirely unbiased sales pitch.

docs.title: Stretch Poison: One Dose, More Regret
docs.text: Stretch Poison: One Dose, More Regret Syntax: stretchpoison <poison> onto <weapon> At Rank 3, Contraband 2, and Alchemy 100, consume a prepared poison and cut it into a weaker dose that clings to a compatible weapon for longer. Better Alchemy improves the result. You must bring the poison; Charlatans improve delivery rather than replacing the poison trade. The weapon must be carried, unwielded, ordinary, and able to take a poison treatment. The installer is always poisoned during the work. This proves the mixture is genuine and saves money on laboratory animals.

docs.title: Sucker Punch: Fairness Was Never in the Contract
docs.text: Sucker Punch: Fairness Was Never in the Contract Syntax: suckerpunch [foe] Alias: spunch Every Rank 1 Charlatan can exploit a melee opening with a current weapon or their own regrettably effective hands. A foe already paralyzed or unable to concentrate leaves room for a much harder blow, making confuse and distract excellent opening arguments. When that opening is there, Sucker Punch says so explicitly. Misdirection adds force to the trick. At Misdirection 4, a second wielded weapon joins the pitch. This is a close-range trick; no amount of confidence lets your fist cross a room.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Cleric muff
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Cleric muff SPELL SYNTAX: Cmuff <on/off> SPELL COST : NONE DESCRIPTION : Though much of the Cleric's power comes from his relationship with his fellow guild members, there are times when the devote Cleric will want to commune privately with Mitra. The Cleric uses this power to choose when he or she wishes to open their mind to their fellow Clerics or when they wish to commune privately with Mitra.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Clerics
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Clerics SPELL SYNTAX: Clerics SPELL COST : NONE DESCRIPTION : Mitra grants her Clerics the knowledge of those currently in Darkwind who share the Cleric's faith and vocation. This power will list all of the Clerics currently venturing the realms.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Continual light
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Continual light SPELL SYNTAX: Clight SPELL COST : 25 SP DESCRIPTION : The devote Cleric may form the power and love of Mitra into a tangible form that will light the area with holy light. The light source may be carried around until it fades away.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Cloud of Shining Sparks
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Cloud of Shining Sparks SPELL SYNTAX: Cloud <target> SPELL COST : 20+2*Guild Level DESCRIPTION : The Cleric may summon the essence of good spirits from another plane to aid the Cleric by distracting his foe and even by causing minor pain to his foe. The distraction will end when all the sparks have been destroyed.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Cure Light Wounds    | Ranged Cure Light Wounds
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Cure Light Wounds | Ranged Cure Light Wounds SPELL SYNTAX: Clw <target> | RClw <target> SPELL COST : 10 SP | 20 SP DESCRIPTION : When cast normally, this spell heals the recipient a random amount of hit points.

docs.title: The convert command allows you to make a player a guild member.
docs.text: The convert command allows you to make a player a guild member. The syntax for the command is 'Convert <player_name>'. The player has to be present, and meet all the requirements of the guild, including the 5th level requirement and the alignment requirement. Mitra is very generous to members who perform a conversion. Caution if you convert unwilling players, Mitra can also be very harsh!

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Create Food or Drink
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Create Food or Drink SPELL SYNTAX: Create food || Create drink SPELL COST : 40 SP (food) || 50 SP (drink) DESCRIPTION : This spell enables the caster to bring forth nutritious food or drink from the planes of goodness. Imbibing the food or drink will heal the consumer.

docs.title: COMMAND NAME  : Cleric Variable Set  | Cleric Variable Unset
docs.text: COMMAND NAME : Cleric Variable Set | Cleric Variable Unset COMMAND SYNTAX: Cset <var> <value> | Cunset <var> COMMAND COST : None | None DESCRIPTION : These commands allow you to set certain Cleric variables that affect certain aspects of your life as a Cleric. To see the available variables, do 'Info variables'. To see the value of all variables, use the Cset command without arguments.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Cure Serious Wounds  | Ranged Cure Serious Wounds
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Cure Serious Wounds | Ranged Cure Serious Wounds SPELL SYNTAX: Csw <target> | RCsw <target> SPELL COST : 20 SP | 40 SP DESCRIPTION : When cast normally, this spell heals the recipient a random amount of hit points.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Cleric tell               | Emote Cleric tell
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Cleric tell | Emote Cleric tell SPELL SYNTAX: ctell <message> | Ectell <emoted message> SPELL COST : NONE | NONE DESCRIPTION : This ability sends out the <message> to all on-line clerics.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : ctitle
docs.text: SPELL NAME : ctitle SPELL SYNTAX: ctitle <title> SPELL COST : NONE DESCRIPTION : This command allows the cleric to set his/her guild title on the members list. Although you can set it to anything, keep in mind that your guild coder (and God) won't appreciate crude or vulgar titles.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Cure Affliction
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Cure Affliction SPELL SYNTAX: Cure <target> SPELL COST : 25 + 30 sp/affliction cured DESCRIPTION : When cast normally, this spell will relieve the target of any infections disease, poison, or deleritous condition acquired around the world of Darkwind.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Remove Curse
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Remove Curse SPELL SYNTAX: Remove <target> <object> SPELL COST : 30 SP DESCRIPTION : This spell serves two different purposes. First, it relieves the target of any curses inflicted ON the player around the mud. These are curses like diseases, and the like. Note: Does not include viking. The correct syntax to remove a curse like this is: Remove <target players name> The second type of curse are curses on objects that players carry. I.e. Weapons and Armour. To remove a cursed item from a player, you use the following syntax: Remove <target players name> <name of cursed object>

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Holy Power
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Holy Power SPELL SYNTAX: Empower <target> SPELL COST : 50 SP DESCRIPTION : Imbues the target with the strength of the righteous.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Flamestrike
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Flamestrike SPELL SYNTAX: Flamestrike SPELL COST : 150 SP DESCRIPTION : This spell causes flames to shower down from the heavens and cause massive damage to all the creatures in the room except the caster, his pets and allies. Note : Non-PK players will never get hit with this skill and PK players only get hit if the caster is PK too. Due to a recent update of the skill you will now be able to always cast this spell, even if there are players in the room that will not be affected.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Spiritual Hammer
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Spiritual Hammer SPELL SYNTAX: Hammer SPELL COST : 10+5*GL SP DESCRIPTION : This spell calls forth the powers of good and embodies them in the form of a great hammer. The hammer is not permanent, but instead, lasts for a duration based upon the Cleric's guild level. You may 'unsummon' your hammer, should you be so inclined.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Hold Person
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Hold Person SPELL SYNTAX: Hold <target> SPELL COST : 40 SP DESCRIPTION : This spell binds the target creature in a powerful energy field, rendering all of their commands useless for a time depending on the level and guild level of the caster.
