docs.text: SPELL NAME : High Mitra tell | Emote High Mitra tell SPELL SYNTAX: Htell <message> | Ehtell <emoted message> SPELL COST : NONE | NONE DESCRIPTION : This ability sends out the <message> to all on-line High level Clerics and Paladins. These are the guild level 15 clerics and paladins.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Insulate
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Insulate SPELL SYNTAX: Insulate <target> SPELL COST : 25 SP DESCRIPTION : Calling upon the power of Mitra, the cleric surrounds the target with a shield of warmth which protects the target from harsh cold weather for 30 minutes.

docs.title: Devoted to spreading the word of beloved Goddess Mitra, all her
docs.text: Devoted to spreading the word of beloved Goddess Mitra, all her Clerics are bestowed with a wide range of healing and defensive powers that can protect and strengthen self and friend alike. They are based in the one temple in the main city and from there, wage the war against all manner of evil. For this purpose, Clerics receive considerable fighting abilities, including the mighty guild hammer that is said to be the essence of the cleric's own faith and the power to devastate evil beings with a holy light. Clerics are also well known for their ability to provide various useful services, including heals from afar, the removal of curses and diseases and even death. Though it is by no means easy, those who reach the pinnacle of their faith can bring the fallen back from the dead. Clerics also share their faith with Mitra's pure warriors, her Paladins. The two groups share much in common both in terms of beliefs, as well as communication channels and even a common storage facility. With their offensive and defensive powers combined, the two make a mighty force against evil. If you like a guild that isn't built around hack and slash and the thought of being able to heal, bless and strengthen yourself and others appeals to you, then talk a little more to an actual Cleric of Mitra to find out more.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Know Alignment
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Know Alignment SPELL SYNTAX: Know <target> SPELL COST : 5 SP DESCRIPTION : This spell enables the caster to determine the alignment of the target creature. It will not reveal the actual value of the alignment, but will show the general traits of the target in question.

docs.title: Cleric of Mitra Guild Levels
docs.text: Cleric of Mitra Guild Levels Clerics rise through righteous battle. Every worthy kill earns Cleric XP, and your guild level rises automatically when you have earned enough. Type 'cost' or 'advance guild' at the guild hall to see your progress. Level Title Cleric XP to reach ===== =============== ================== 1 Aspiring Acolyte 0 2 Acolyte 1000 3 Adept 2000 4 Evangelist 3000 5 Ecclesiastic 5000 6 Curate 7000 7 Predicant 10000 8 Canon 13000 9 Minister 16000 10 Patriarch 20000 11 Spiritual One 24000 12 Blessed One 28000 13 Divine One 32000 14 Chosen One 36000 15 Saviour 40000 Your guild level can never exceed your character level, and your combined guild levels can never exceed your character level. Mitra grants nothing while your alignment is evil - XP earned while you stray is banked, and the levels pop when you atone. At guild level 15 her Champions join the himitra and saviour channels. Your battle record survives leaving the guild. Should you return in good standing, your guild level is restored.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Light
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Light SPELL SYNTAX: Light SPELL COST : 10 SP DESCRIPTION : This spell enables the caster to bring magical light to be able to see their surroundings. The light's brightness is dependant on the cleric's level, and is not moveable. It will only light the room you're standing in.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Locate Player
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Locate Player SPELL SYNTAX: Locate <player_name> SPELL COST : 30 SP DESCRIPTION : This spell will enable you to see the environment of any player.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Mitra's Hand
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Mitra's Hand SPELL SYNTAX: Mhand [<target>] SPELL COST : 50 SP DESCRIPTION : Calls the hand of Mitra upon the target, or the cleric himself if no target is specified. Mitra rewards those who follow the path of good with protection and ability in combat. Evil creatures and people, however, experience condemnation and shame when Mitra's righteous hand is upon them, and become less able. Either way, the target is only affected for a short time.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: ===== Introduction ===== The Clerics of Mitra maintain a position of prestige and power among the guilds of Darkwind. We are a benevolent guild focused around serving the ways of our goddess Mitra. For remaining obedient to her will, she grants our prayers when we call for her help by using our guild powers. ===== Prospective Members ===== 1. Race -------- The follwing races may join our guild: dwarf, elf, faerie, gnome, halfling, or human. If you are not a member of one of these races you may change your race prior to joining by visiting the hall of races (refer to the newbie tome). 2. Alignment ------------ As a member of the guild, you will need to have your alignment at "good" or better in order for your spells to work. It is also important that your alignment be good or better when you initially try to join the guild. 3. Weapon Specialization ------------------------ Clerics can only wield blunt weapons without restricting their abilities. It is recommended you train in at least "medium blunt." This is because one of our primary powers is to summon a hammer which is classified as a medium weapon. 4. Armour Restrictions ---------------------- At this point in time there are no armour restrictions for the Clerics of Mitra. 5. Roleplay ------------ The only forced roleplay within the guild is one's alignment. In order for spells to function the Cleric must be at least "good." In addition, the fellow Clerics have the ability to vote on a "ban" for certain people that defy the collective "guild interest." Once a ban is in place, Clerics are free to make their own decision, but are highly encouraged to follow the ban for the better good of the guild. 6. Guild Powers --------------- Our powers are almost totally defensive. The heart of our skill lies in our ability to heal ourselves and others in varying fashions. In addition to being able to heal hit points, Clerics can also remove curses from weapons/armour and cure most forms of diseases known to Darkwind. A premier power which a Cleric will possess from guild level 8 and above is the ability to summon a magical unique-class hammer. Although not everyone uses this as his/her primary weapon..it makes life after reboots a lot easier. For more specific info on our other spells, I would recommend checking <who> for Clerics and find out who the current GM is. This would be a good place to start with questions, although any member really should be able to assist you. ===== Conclusion ===== Hopefully now that you have read this, you have a general idea about how we function. We are a tight-knit group of friendly players that enjoy extremely functional guild powers. (We hardly ever are in a bind we cannot save ourselves from). If you think we sound like something you would enjoy, please join. If you are still undecided feel free to take your time and ask us plenty of questions.

docs.title: =   Clerics of Mitra Guild News   =
docs.text: =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= = Clerics of Mitra Guild News = =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= Well, things are changing a bit around here. A few of the recent changes: + You can no longer resurrect players in thieves or priest. + Bless and Guard are self-cast only. + Unparalyze was removed. + The costs/damage/timers were changed on most spells.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Offer
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Offer SPELL SYNTAX: Offer corpse SPELL COST : 5 DESCRIPTION : This command will offer up a corpse to Mitra to gain her favour. Offering up corpses to Mitra will help to bring your alignment more towards good, although after a point it no longer affects it that much.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Remove Paralysis
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Remove Paralysis SPELL SYNTAX: Unparalyze <target> SPELL COST : 40 SP DESCRIPTION : This spell removes the paralysis spell from any held target.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Portal
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Portal SPELL SYNTAX: Portal SPELL COST : 100 SP DESCRIPTION : Summons a portal to the astral plane such that it leads back to the Darkwind church. Inside the plane is a 'way' to the church blocked by an astral being of fair power. Cleric is advised not to drop anything or wander around in this plane.

docs.title: SPELL NAME  : Resurrection
docs.text: SPELL NAME : Resurrection SPELL SYNTAX: Resurrect <target> SPELL COST : Special: 225 to cast, but takes a total of 450. DESCRIPTION : This spells allows the caster to call upon the powers of Mitra and raise the target (player) from the dead. They might not get back everything they lost, but it will be far better than the normal means of praying. Resurrection of evil souls is possible, but Mitra will fill that person with her love and goodness. Players who have not gained her notice (level 8 and below) can't be resurrected at all. Note that Mitra holds a special place in her heart for her Clerics and Paladins so they can be resurrected at any level and their resurrections tend to be a bit more successful.

docs.title: Deathknights
docs.text: Deathknights Deathknights are a dark martial order associated with grim bargains, heavily committed combat, and powers that blur the boundary between warrior and death-touched magic. Current roster status: CLOSED TO NEW APPLICANTS. This page remains in the tome so returning players can recognize the name. Use help guilds for the current roster; a closed path cannot be chosen by a new character.

docs.title: Chromatic dragons are of an evil alignment.
docs.text: Chromatic dragons are of an evil alignment. Evil dragons receive a STR and DEX bonus, and an INT and WIS penalty. They gain an advantage in melee combat to make up for their weaker damage from SP. Black dragons have a damage type of acid. Red dragons have a damage type of fire. White dragons have a damage type of cold. Blue dragons have a damage type of lightning. Green dragons have a damage type of disease. Gem dragons are of a neutral alignment. Neutral dragons do not get any stat bonuses or penalties. They gain a much higher HP and SP regen however. They have the advantage of being able to pick melee or sp damage as their main choice. Crystal dragons have a damage type of light. Topaz dragons have a damage type of cold. Amethyst dragons have a damage type of poison. Emerald dragons have a damage type of disease. Sapphire dragons have a damage type of sound. Metal dragons are of a good alignment. Good dragons receive a STR and DEX penalty, and an INT and WIS bonus. They gain an advantage in damage from SP to make up for their weaker damage from combat. Brass dragons have a damage type of disease. Copper dragons have a damage type of acid. Bronze dragons have a damage type of lightning. Silver dragons have a damage type of cold. Gold dragons have a damage type of fire. Except for transforming, you will need to stay in your declared alignment to perform your Dragon abilities.

docs.title: Dragon Basic Info
docs.text: Dragon Basic Info Dragons become self-aware at the age of 17. Before that, as a hatchling, you are barely better than an animal. You feed, you have some instincts, but not the self-awareness of what you truly are. Once you are self-aware, you find yourself in your Darkwinder form to fit in with the people around you. Dragons come in many forms, the basics groups are the Chromatic, the Gem, and the Metal. Each group has different types, and each group gets a different bonus and penalty. Each Dragon type also deals with a different damage type, and becomes immune to that type of damage. Before you are able to transform back to your true Dragon form, you have to 'declare' your choice. That is the form you will take the rest of your life, so choose wisely. You can 'dhelp align' to see those choices. In your Dragon form, you have certain limitations. You cannot drink alcohol. You cannot carry more than one item in your clutches. In your Dragon form, you do have some advantages. Your Dragon hide is tough, and only gets tougher as you age and level. Your ability to fly is magical, and therefore you don't get blown off course in the sky. Your claw and bite attacks get fiercer, and you get more of them as you level. Your stat bonuses and penalties increase with your stats. As far as your Dragon age, you only age while you are online. If you are online playing moderately, you should age one year every week. If you are found to be abusing triggers to stay online just to age, you will be banished and will lose the ability to have any mythic characters. The time it takes to age is one of the key balancing points to the guild, and if you abuse it, you only weaken the guild, or get yourself banished. No matter where you log out, you will always log in at the Oracle of Aal in DarkWind. That is the spiritual home of the Dragons, and puts you next to your lair. Every lair has a copy of the Dragon board so you can post messages without worry about spam. Objects you leave in your lair should last until we reboot. Your lair is private, and only for you. Other Dragons, and those not of Dragon blood are not permitted inside. There are more than enough other places in the world to meet up with them. If you come across any bugs, please bug them. If you have ideas, please idea them, or post them on the board if you wish others to discuss it. If there is something about the guild which makes it difficult to play, or really kills the "fun" don't be afraid to post about that as well.

docs.title: -- Spirit Aura -----------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Spirit Aura ----------------------------------------------- This simple Marken invocation allows a druid a glimpse of the target creature's aura. By reading the spiritual aura, the druid can tell whether or not a creature is in balance. At higher levels of mastery, the reading becomes more precise, and the druid begins to gain more information. At the highest level of mastery, the druid has enough skill to judge the creature's strength in comparison to his own. Command: aura <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 10 Marken nwyfre Base Recovery: fast Base Effect: information (creature) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 1

docs.title: -- New Druid Flow ---------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- New Druid Flow --------------------------------------------- The modern druid guild is built around two related ideas: Invocations are your fast active powers. Rituals prepare and shape the nwyfre that fuels them. Your first useful path is: 1. Check nwyfre. nwyfre This shows your four vessels: Tellurian, Daloan, Marken, and Tekali. The bars show how much power you have. Regen and cost change with terrain, moon phase, current planet, groves, and active rituals. 2. Check your druid status. dscore gscore Druid These show your guild level and combat-earned Druid XP alongside study points, learned invocations, grove status, and profession materials. Druid XP advances your guild level automatically when your regular level permits it. Any blocked XP remains banked. Druid XP and rank progress survive remort; the current progression curve is designed to reach guild level 30 within one normally played remort life. The cost and advance guild commands in the advancement cavern explain your next rank, but do not spend ordinary experience. 3. Learn a first invocation. learn spirit aura Study invocations in the Druids' Meditation Grove inside the guild hall. Use dhelp spells to see every active invocation. 4. Gather profession materials. gather herbs mine ore skin corpse reagents Druid rituals and companions use the profession material stores: herbs, creature reagents, skins and leathers, ores and bars, bolts, and special shards. Use reagents search <item> to check exact balances. Your silver sickle serves as a gardening spade, mining pick, and skinning knife, so you do not need to buy those three profession tools. At Druid level 7, Verdant Refrain can also help by casually storing herbs and saved reagents as you travel through natural places. 5. Plant your Sacred Grove. grove plant Plant it in a wild place you want to return to. Later, commune returns you to your grove. dhelp grove explains grove growth, return, the inner sanctum, and how the grove rests safely between remort lives. 6. Learn and perform a first ritual. learn ritual drawing of the tide ritual drawing of the tide marken Drawing of the Tide consumes profession materials matching the current you name and restores that current. Use nwyfre ritual <name> before learning or performing a ritual to see its requirements. Long-running rituals use the same ritual command, but toggle on and off. For example: learn ritual verdant refrain ritual verdant refrain ritual stop verdant refrain 7. Cast your first invocation. spirit aura Invocations spend nwyfre instead of spell points. If an invocation says you lack nwyfre, use nwyfre to see which current is low, then use rituals, time, terrain, or a grove to recover it. -- Useful Commands -------------------------------------------- nwyfre Show currents, active rites, and next steps. nwyfre learnable Show rituals you have not learned yet. nwyfre ritual <name> Inspect a ritual. dscore Show study, grove, and material guidance. dhelp spells List active invocations. dhelp ritual Learn the ritual system. dhelp grove Learn Sacred Groves.

docs.title: Guild Chat Lines
docs.text: Guild Chat Lines There are three guild chat lines, the druid, heirophant, and gaea lines. The druid line is heard by all druids, The gaea line is heard by both druids and garou, while the heirophant line is heard only by those of GL 28 and up. dchat, edchat - Talk or emote on the druid line. hd, ehd - Talk or emote on the heirophant line. gaea, egaea - Talk or emote on the Gaea line.

docs.title: -- Druid Companions ------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Druid Companions ------------------------------------------ Druids can keep a living menagerie. Each companion unlocks at a different guild level, can be summoned beside the others, and grows stronger as it fights with you. companions Show every companion, its role, current, nwyfre cost, level, XP to next level, and status. companions summon <animal> Call one unlocked companion. The call consumes that companion's required nwyfre current and profession materials, then completes after a short preparation timer. Moving or entering combat breaks the pattern. companions dismiss <animal> Release one active companion back to the wild. companions dismiss all Release the whole menagerie. companions name <animal> <name> companions rename <animal> <name> Give one unlocked companion a personal name. Names must be 3 to 11 letters, and can be used in companion commands. companions unname <animal> Clear a companion's personal name. Unlocked companions: Jaguar guild 5 stalker Wolf guild 9 hunter Boar guild 13 breaker Stag guild 17 warden Bear guild 21 guardian Lion guild 25 apex Companions gain experience from battle participation and auto-level from their saved XP. A companion that dies is wounded, not erased. It keeps its XP and level, but must recover before it can answer your call again. Companion XP and chosen names survive remort. XP can continue banking while your current character level limits the companion's manifested level, then becomes available as you advance in the new life. Leaving the Druid guild voluntarily ends these bonds and clears their progress. Each companion answers a different current and material pattern. Use companions to see your adjusted nwyfre costs and exact profession material requirements.

docs.title: -- Worldroot Confluence --------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Worldroot Confluence -------------------------------------- Current: All four currents Command: confluence Guild Level: 30 Worldroot Confluence is the Druid capstone invocation. It braids all four currents through you for a short time, reducing invocation costs and improving the nwyfre momentum you gain while fighting. While the confluence lasts, your invocations also feed your weakest current. This is the moment when a prepared Druid should feel like a true ritual caster rather than a weapon fighter.

docs.title: -- Druid Monitor ----------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Druid Monitor ---------------------------------------------- dmon toggles a compact nwyfre monitor in your normal combat monitor output. Commands: dmon Toggle the Druid monitor. dmon on Turn it on. dmon off Turn it off. When enabled, the standard mon / monitor output includes one extra line with all four currents: T Tellurian D Daloan M Marken K Tekali Each current shows a compact bar and percentage so you can see which vessel is being spent during combat.

docs.title: -- Drown -----------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Drown ----------------------------------------------------- Current: Tekali Command: drown <target> Guild Level: 25 Drown bends Tekali water geometry into impossible pressure around a single target. It is a high-cost, high-impact finishing invocation. Mastery increases damage and makes it one of the Druid's most pivotal single-target attacks.

docs.title: -- Eagle Eye -------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Eagle Eye ------------------------------------------------- Current: Tekali Command: eagleeye <target> Guild Level: 16 Eagle Eye sharpens the target's combat sight, improving hit and critical pressure. It defaults to the caster. Higher mastery improves the effect, extends duration, and allows the druid to share the sight with allies.

docs.title: -- Earth Meld -----------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Earth Meld ----------------------------------------------- Earth Meld has been replaced by Stump. Use dhelp stump for the current Tellurian resting invocation.

docs.title: -- Earthquake -----------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Earthquake ----------------------------------------------- Exerting control through the Tellurian current, the druid causes a massive upheaval of the earth, similar to an earthquake. While this invocation will not harm the druids or their followers, others will take a certain amount of damage, regardless of armor, and will be unable to move or fight effectively for some time. Command: earthquake Base Cost: 160 Tellurian nwyfre Base Recovery: long Base Effect: damage (moderate, area), stun (area) Base Duration: instant (damage), medium (stun) Guild Level: 22

docs.title: Druid Guild Emotes
docs.text: Druid Guild Emotes None at the moment - suggest some.

docs.title: -- Engulf ----------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Engulf ---------------------------------------------------- Current: Daloan Command: engulf <target> Guild Level: 4 Engulf folds ragged Daloan flame around a single enemy. It is the first direct chaos-fire strike in the new invocation path. Mastery increases the burn pressure and damage, giving Daloan a reliable focused attack before the larger area fires arrive.

docs.title: -- Entangle --------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Entangle -------------------------------------------------- The druid draws on the Tellurian current, causing tough, clinging vines to grow almost instantly out of the ground and wrap around the target, rendering it incapable of attacking or broad motions. Some small range of movement is possible, however. Command: entangle <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 55 Tellurian nwyfre Base Recovery: long Base Effect: entangle Base Duration: medium Guild Level: 10

docs.title: -- Flame Blade -----------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Flame Blade ----------------------------------------------- The druid draws on the Daloan current to temporarily enchant a weapon with savage flame, causing it to burst into fire. This causes the weapon to deliver additional damage, and have a greater chance to hit. Command: flameblade <weapon> Base Cost: 60 Daloan nwyfre Base Recovery: long Base Effect: enhance (low) Base Duration: long Guild Level: 8

docs.title: -- Frenzy ----------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Frenzy ---------------------------------------------------- The druid opens to the savage Daloan current and lets its heat flood muscle, breath, and instinct. While the frenzy lasts, the druid strikes harder and with greater violence, but is less able to move defensively. Command: frenzy Base Cost: 90 Daloan nwyfre Base Recovery: long Base Effect: offense increase, dodge penalty Base Duration: short Guild Level: 12

docs.title: -- Frost Bolt -----------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Frost Bolt ----------------------------------------------- This potent Tekali invocation draws upon the chill of winter to damage the target with a ray of frost. The wiser the druid, the more power he may focus. This invocation also has a chance to stun the target for a short time. Command: frostbolt <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: min(level + 30, wisdom) Tekali nwyfre Base Recovery: medium Base Effect: damage (high) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 7

docs.title: -- Druid Help --------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Druid Help -------------------------------------------------- beginner First-hour path for new druids. grove Sacred Grove: planting, commune, sanctum. nwyfre The four nwyfre currents and spirit vessels. ritual Ritual status, prepared rites, and toggles. spells Master list of active druid invocations. companions Druid menagerie: summon, dismiss, level, status. mastery Invocation mastery and study slots. dscore Study points, learned powers, grove, materials. dmon Toggle compact nwyfre bars in your monitor. attune Read the current room's terrain. chat About the guild lines. emotes Druid guild emotes. other Other guild commands. restrictions Details about guild restrictions. There is also help available on each active invocation. Use dhelp spells to see the exact help-file names. Your silver sickle also serves as a Druid profession tool. You can use it as a gardening spade for gather herbs, a mining pick for mine ore, and a skinning knife for skin corpse. -- New Druid Quick Path --------------------------------------- nwyfre dscore learn spirit aura gather herbs mine ore skin corpse reagents grove plant learn ritual drawing of the tide ritual drawing of the tide marken spirit aura At Druid level 7, learn ritual verdant refrain unlocks a long-running ritual that can gather small profession herb and reagent finds while you travel through natural places. Newly initiated druids should start with dhelp beginner.

docs.title: -- Sacred Grove -----------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Sacred Grove ----------------------------------------------- A Sacred Grove is a druid's living anchor in the wild. Plant it once, tend it over time, and use it as a place for ritual work, recovery, and return. -- Commands --------------------------------------------------- grove plant Root your grove here. grove Show grove status in this room. commune Return to your own grove. commune to <name> Visit a mature public grove. groves List mature groves open to guests. grove stash Legacy stash status. out Leave your inner sanctum. -- Planting --------------------------------------------------- Use grove plant in the wild. City rooms and inside rooms cannot hold a Sacred Grove. The grove token remains in that wilderness anchor; nurture and regen pulses begin there. -- Growth ----------------------------------------------------- Stage 0 Seedling for the first 10 minutes. Stage 1 Sapling after 10 minutes. Stage 2 Young grove after 30 minutes. Stage 3 Mature after 90 minutes; unlocks the inner sanctum. Stage 4 Ancient after 4 hours; sanctum becomes safe. When the grove becomes mature, commune takes you into a private spirit-room tied to your grove instead of the shared wilderness tile. Use out to step back to the wild anchor. Ancient groves carry full sanctuary law. Younger mature groves use the same kind of spirit-room, but combat is not forbidden there. -- Guests ----------------------------------------------------- Guests may use commune to <name> once the host grove is mature. Use the full player name if it has spaces, for example: commune to anna marie Guests share the host's inner sanctum. Guest travel fails if the anchor is barred, no-teleport, or otherwise unsafe for grove travel. Two PK druids who are not in the same party cannot commune to each other's groves. -- Profession Materials --------------------------------------- Druid rites now use saved profession materials instead of the old Grove stash. Use reagents and reagents search <item> to inspect what you carry. Any old stash contents are migrated into profession materials when possible. Remorting makes your grove dormant while you are between Druid lives. Its location, age, and nurtured growth remain saved; the anchor and sanctum return when you rejoin. A dormant grove is not public and provides no benefits. Leaving the Druid guild voluntarily still removes the registration, destroys the anchor token, and releases the sanctum. -- Limits ----------------------------------------------------- You cannot commune while fighting or from a no-teleport room. Guest commune also refuses barred paths such as guild halls, player housing paths, and similar protected areas. Note: commune and grove plant use room spell-limit cooldowns internally.

docs.title: -- Inferno ---------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Inferno --------------------------------------------------- The ultimate violent expression of the Daloan current, this invocation creates flame and heat of an intensity not far removed from that inside of an active volcano. All living creatures except druids and their followers will be badly burnt, and inanimate objects, whether on the ground or carried by affected creatures, have a chance of burning to ash. Command: inferno Base Cost: 200 Daloan nwyfre Base Recovery: long Base Effect: damage (high, area) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 24

docs.title: -- The Druids -------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- The Druids ------------------------------------------------- In the world of Geshtai, there are many powers, but the oldest of these is Gaea, the incarnation of Nature itself. The sea and stone, the storm and sun, the raw power of fire and lightning and wind, and the animals and plants of Geshtai... all of this is Gaea's domain. Gaea has no clerics, but she does have followers, and the druids are counted among their number. A group of secretive warrior-priests, they study the mysteries of Gaea and draw upon her power in their efforts to serve Nature. Gaea's power is broad in scope, and each druid may develop different rituals and invocations -- yet they do not rely solely on magic, and can fight as fiercely as any cleric. If you would join their ranks, seek out the circle of stones hidden in the forest west of town. Today's circle tends Sacred Groves rooted in the wild, reads the moons for nwyfre, and shapes battle through Tellurian, Daloan, Marken, and Tekali invocations. A new initiate should begin with: dhelp beginner

docs.title: -- Call Lightning -------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Call Lightning ------------------------------------------- Current: Tekali Command: lightning <target> Guild Level: 20 Call Lightning draws storm-force from the Tekali current into a single target. It must be used outside and on the surface. Flying or ranged targets are especially vulnerable. Mastery improves damage and the chance to stun or break concentration.

docs.title: -- Locust Swarm ---------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Locust Swarm --------------------------------------------- Current: Daloan Command: lswarm Guild Level: 17 Locust Swarm pours Daloan hunger through the room as biting insects. It harms valid enemies in the area while sparing druids and protected targets. Mastery increases the swarm's damage and makes it a stronger room control choice.

docs.title: -- Primal Maelstrom ------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Primal Maelstrom ------------------------------------------ Current: All four currents Command: maelstrom Guild Level: 29 Primal Maelstrom is an Archdruid battlefield invocation. It spends all four currents to tear open a storm of root, fire, moonlight, and thunder through the room. The maelstrom damages enemies and briefly disrupts their concentration. It is expensive, but it is pure spellcraft: no weapon, no form, no melee setup.

docs.title: -- Mastery And Study -----------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Mastery And Study ----------------------------------------- The mysteries of Gaea are many, and not easily understood. Every secret discovered reveals a new question, a possible point of further study. Druids now shape their craft through nwyfre invocations and rituals. Invocation mastery still has five levels. The first level is basic knowledge: the druid can invoke the power at minimum effectiveness. Deeper mastery improves the effect, duration, or recovery of that invocation depending on its nature. In order to learn an invocation, your Druid guild level must be equal to the level listed in dhelp spells. For each additional level of mastery, your Druid guild level must be one higher. Use dscore to see study points, learned invocations, Sacred Grove state, and profession-material guidance. Use nwyfre to see your current spirit vessels, active rites, planet, time, and conjunction state. Invocations may only be studied at the Druid Grove inside the guild hall. Rituals are learned there with: learn ritual <name> New druids should read: dhelp beginner

docs.title: -- Mire ------------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Mire ------------------------------------------------------ Current: Tellurian Command: mire Guild Level: 19 Mire wakes the ground into clutching mud and stone. It is an area control invocation that hinders enemies in the room. Mastery strengthens the mud's grip and extends the control window. Mire requires solid ground.

docs.title: -- Moonwell Draught ------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Moonwell Draught ------------------------------------------ Current: Chosen when cast Command: moonwell <current> Guild Level: 27 Moonwell Draught binds one current of nwyfre into three short-lived draughts. Each draught restores that current when you drink it. The draughts are bound to the druid who made them, cannot be sold, and fade after a short time. This is the high-level Druid answer to long hunting sessions: prepare with profession materials, then keep moving. Use reagents search <item> to check the needed profession materials. The exact materials depend on the current you name. Example: moonwell daloan drink draught

docs.title: -- Nature Step ----------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Nature Step ---------------------------------------------- Current: Tellurian Command: naturestep Guild Level: 13 Nature Step loosens the druid into root, stone, and leaf-shadow, placing the druid at range for a short time. Higher mastery extends the duration. Use it to create space before large invocations or to survive pressure from melee attackers.

docs.title: -- Nwyfre -----------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Nwyfre ----------------------------------------------------- Nwyfre is the living current druids use for rituals and invocations. It replaces spell points for active druid invocations. There are four vessels: Tellurian - Darkwind, earth, roots, body, grove Daloan - Dailos, turmoil, flame, savagery Marken - Markas, healing, renewal, stability Tekali - Tekal, knowledge, frost, sight, wind Use nwyfre to see all four vessels. Each line shows a bar, regen rate, cost modifier, and source world. The Planet line shows where you are standing for nwyfre purposes. Darkwind favors the Tellurian current; each moon favors its own current and weakens the others. -- Useful Commands ------------------------------------------- nwyfre Show all vessels. nwyfre <current> Inspect one vessel. nwyfre active Show active rites, timers, and toggles. nwyfre moons Show current moon phases. nwyfre rituals List learned rituals. nwyfre learnable List rituals you can learn. nwyfre ritual <name> Inspect one ritual. Rituals and celestial conditions change regen and cost. Long-running rituals also appear here when active. These are toggle rites, such as Verdant Refrain, that remain active until you end them with ritual stop <name>. The moon currents are strongest when their moon is visible and weakest during the new moon. Tellurian is strongest in living earth and your Sacred Grove. When Dailos, Markas, and Tekal are all new at once, all three lunar currents are starved together. Use moonless drawing during that rare dark to restore enough Daloan, Marken, and Tekali nwyfre to keep working. -- Conjunctions ---------------------------------------------- When two or more moons are full in the night sky, nwyfre enters a rare conjunction. 'nwyfre' shows the current conjunction line. Most nights this says 'none'. During a two-moon conjunction, Twin-Moon Pact can bind the aligned lunar currents together. When Dailos, Markas, and Tekal are all full at once, an ancient Sacred Grove can work Triple Confluence Calling. This is an endgame ritual window, not a daily tool. New druids should read dhelp beginner for the first useful sequence: check nwyfre, learn an invocation, gather profession materials, plant a grove, learn a ritual, perform it, then cast.

docs.title: Befriend Animal or Plant
docs.text: Befriend Animal or Plant This spell, in combination with a druid's animal empathy, may allow him to befriend a wild animal. If successfully befriended, the animal will serve the druid willingly to the best of its ability, even fighting to the death if the druid requests it. Plant-like monsters may also be charmed with this spell, but not humanoids or other creatures. Command: befriend <target> Base Cost: 125 SP Base Recovery: slow Base Effect: follower Base Duration: permanent (until logoff) Guild Level: 13

docs.title: Calm Animal or Plant
docs.text: Calm Animal or Plant The most basic manifestation of a druid's connection with Nature is the animal empathy many develop. This ability enables the druid to use that empathy to attempt to calm an attacking animal. It also works on plant-like creatures, but not on humanoids or other beings. Command: calm <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 25 SP Base Recovery: fast Base Effect: stop fight Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 1

docs.title: Conjure Elemental
docs.text: Conjure Elemental This spell allows the druid to request aid from Gaea, in the form of an elemental servant. The elemental will freely serve for one hour, and is capable of assisting in combat. These elementals are also empowered to fly through the skies, following the druid. An air or earth elemental may be summoned at mastery level one, water at level two, and fire at level three; further levels of mastery also increase the power of the elemental. See 'dhelp elemental' for more information. Command: conjure <air|earth|fire|water> Base Cost: 150 SP Base Recovery: slow Base Effect: follower Base Duration: one hour (or until logoff) Guild Level: 26

docs.title: Create Water
docs.text: Create Water This spell causes a small amount of water to pour out of thin air, even in the most barren desert. It will refill a waterskin. At higher levels of mastery, the druid will also be able to conjure the waterskin itself. Command: cwater Base Cost: 10 SP Base Recovery: short Base Effect: create items (water) Base Duration: permanent Guild Level: 3

docs.title: Drown
docs.text: Drown Arguably the most powerful single-combat spell known to druidic lore, Drown is also one of the hardest to master. It was named for its apparent effect, but it does not literally drown the target, as water- breathing and even non-breathing creatures are affected in the same manner. Command: drown <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: Minimum 100, based on damage Base Recovery: long Base Effect: damage (extreme) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 25

docs.title: Eagle Eye
docs.text: Eagle Eye The eagle is famed for its eyesight. Through this spell, the druid may confer that eyesight upon himself or another, increasing their chance of scoring a hit in combat by noting openings in their opponents' defenses. The chance of scoring a critical hit is also increased. Command: eagleeye <target> (defaults to caster) Base Cost: 50 SP Base Recovery: medium-long Base Effect: boost (hit and critical chances, moderate) Base Duration: medium-long Guild Level: 16

docs.title: Earth Meld
docs.text: Earth Meld With the aid of this ritual, a druid may become one with nature, sinking bodily into the earth and emerging in the Heart of Geshtai, an ancient druid sanctum. From there, it is possible to meld through the earth to a variety of locations -- those who master the power have more to choose from. Command: earthmeld Base Cost: 65 SP Base Recovery: long Base Effect: travel (teleport) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 21

docs.title: An elemental follower is capable of all of the
docs.text: An elemental follower is capable of all of the commands listed in 'dhelp follower'. In addition, all elementals are magic resistant and capable of flight, and they also have specific properties: Air - These elementals are very fast, but physically weak. Their magical attack is a lightning spell, making them useful against water creatures or those wearing metal armor. They are healed by lightning and weak against water attacks and weapon blows. Earth - These are the strongest but slowest of the elementals. Their magical attack, a stone bolt, is the weakest of the four types, but their melee attacks are quite strong. They are resistant to weapon blows and other forms of physical attack, but weak against disintegration effects. Fire - These tend to be the strongest all-around in combat, with no stats standing out as particularly strong or weak and a devastating magical firebolt attack. They are healed by fire but weak against water and cold attacks. Water - Another fairly balanced elemental in terms of stats, they tend to be stronger but slower than fire elementals. Their magical attack is a rush of water, which both batters and drowns opponents. They are healed by water attacks and strong against cold, but weak against fire and lightning.

docs.title: Endurance
docs.text: Endurance The earth and stone endure through ages, and this spell enables the druid to borrow a portion of that power for himself. It provides an immediate boost in vitality which slowly wears off over time. Command: endurance Base Cost: 50 SP Base Recovery: medium-long Base Effect: boost (constitution, moderate) Base Duration: long (moderate fade) Guild Level: 6

docs.title: Engulf
docs.text: Engulf This spell calls up a spiral of flame that wraps around the target, burning it with focused natural fire. Command: engulf <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 28 SP Base Recovery: medium Base Effect: damage (fire) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 4

docs.title: Enlarge Animal or Plant
docs.text: Enlarge Animal or Plant As the druid continues to develop his rapport with nature, he becomes capable of infusing animals and plants with life force, causing them to grow to incredible size and strength. This spell will make an animal or plant-like creature much stronger. Be warned, however: it cannot be cast on a befriended creature, or it would break the charm, so it must be cast prior to befriend, making the charm more difficult. On the other hand, the more dangerous creature will be worth more experience... Command: enlarge <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 35 SP Base Recovery: medium Base Effect: boost (all stats) Base Duration: permanent Guild Level: 1

docs.title: Exterminate
docs.text: Exterminate While druids act in harmony with nature, there are times when they find themselves in conflict with some of nature's creatures. Some druids resolve such conflicts peacefully; however, some, particularly those druids more inclined toward evil, choose more violent methods. This spell is one of those; it calls upon the darker side of nature in an attempt to eliminate a life force from the cycle. It can target only vermin, such as insects, mice and rats, spiders, and toads. Higher animals and humans are immune to its effects, and the life force of plants is sufficiently different to render them immune as well. Command: exterminate <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 60 SP Base Recovery: medium-long Base Effect: damage (extreme, vermin only) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 3

docs.title: You may give the following commands to your followers:
docs.text: You may give the following commands to your followers: release <name> - Allows you to release your follower early, in case (for instance) you wish to charm a different animal or conjure a different elemental. dismiss <name> - Same as 'release'. secure <name> - Stops other people from taking items your followers are carrying. allow <name> - Allows other people to take items your followers are carrying. unleash <target> - Causes your follower to attack the target, assuming the target is valid (PK checks, etc., apply.) heel - Causes your follower to stop fighting. toggle - Sets whether or not your follower automatically helps you in combat.

docs.title: Frighten
docs.text: Frighten With this spell, the druid can cause a primal, unreasoning fear to arise in any natural creature native to this world. Unlike most of a druid's emotion-influencing powers, this spell works on humanoids as well as animals and plants. However, elementals, demons, undead, and other unnatural creatures are immune. Command: frighten <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 25 SP Base Recovery: fast Base Effect: target flees Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 5

docs.title: Frost Blade
docs.text: Frost Blade The druid may temporarily enchant a weapon with the power of elemental ice, causing frost to coat its striking surface. This causes the weapon to deliver additional damage. It does not grant the bonus to hit that Flame Blade does; however, the damage is greater. Command: frostblade <weapon> Base Cost: 60 SP Base Recovery: long Base Effect: enhance (moderate) Base Duration: long Guild Level: 8

docs.title: Growth
docs.text: Growth This retired spell once produced old Druid-only spirit components. Modern Druid rites use saved profession materials instead; see dhelp beginner and reagents. Command: growth Base Cost: 15 SP Base Recovery: short Base Effect: retired Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 3

docs.title: Gust
docs.text: Gust This spell calls a biting wind against the target. The gust harms the creature and leaves dust and grit swirling around it for a short time. Command: gust <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 22 SP Base Recovery: short Base Effect: damage, minor hindrance Base Duration: short Guild Level: 2

docs.title: Ice Storm
docs.text: Ice Storm Control of the weather provides much of a druid's destructive power, and this spell demonstrates that. With but a word, the druid conjures a hailstorm to pelt everything in the area. This spell is often used against numbers of magic-resistant creatures, since the hail is not itself magical; however, the damage is not great, and heavily armored creatures may escape unscathed. You need not fear harming another druid or their charmed or summoned creatures with this spell. Command: icestorm Base Cost: 90 SP Base Recovery: medium-long Base Effect: damage (low, area) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 9

docs.title: Water of Life
docs.text: Water of Life While not as skilled in the healing arts as a cleric, a druid does have a fair amount of knowledge of the healing arts. This spell is their simplest magical tool to that end: a spray of enchanted water to literally wash wounds away. Command: life <target> (defaults to caster) Base Cost: 10 + 2 X guild level SP Base Recovery: short Base Effect: heal (moderate) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 2

docs.title: Call Lightning
docs.text: Call Lightning A druid of sufficient power may channel the power of the storm, drawing forth lightning out of even the clearest skies. Aside from the damage it causes, this spell has a high chance of stunning its target for a short time. It also causes greater damage against flying targets, since it is an air-element spell. Command: lightning <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 5 * guild level SP Base Recovery: medium Base Effect: damage (high) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 20

docs.title: Locust Swarm
docs.text: Locust Swarm Through this potent charm, the druid summons a ravenous swarm of locusts to the area. The insects will bite and torment creatures, slipping into the gaps in armor; at the same time, they will eat all of the food they can find. Only druids and their summoned or charmed followers are protected against their rampage. Command: lswarm Base Cost: 120 SP Base Recovery: long Base Effect: damage (moderate, area) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 17

docs.title: Mire
docs.text: Mire Upon casting this spell, the druid commands the ground to rise up and grasp at the feet of all creatures in the area -- only other druids and their followers are protected. Affected creatures are unable to flee, and, while they can still fight, their restricted range of movement slows them down. A particularly strong creature has a chance to break free immediately, and stronger creatures will struggle free before weaker ones in any case. Command: mire Base Cost: 85 SP Base Recovery: medium-long Base Effect: drain (dexterity, high, area), entangle (area) Base Duration: varies Guild Level: 19

docs.title: Nature Step
docs.text: Nature Step Through this ancient ritual, the druid may become one with his immediate surroundings, gaining the ability to sink into the ground and reappear a short distance away at will. That effect makes it nearly impossible to melee with the affected druid. Command: naturestep Base Cost: 25 SP Base Recovery: medium Base Effect: protection (high) Base Duration: short Guild Level: 13

docs.title: Produce Flame
docs.text: Produce Flame With this spell, the druid can conjure into existence a small globe of pure elemental flame. The flame will serve as a light source, and can also be commanded to burn an enemy for a small amount of damage, although doing this will reduce the flame's lifespan. Command: produce Base Cost: 35 SP plus 10 SP per 'burn' Base Recovery: medium Base Effect: light, damage (low) Base Duration: very long Guild Level: 2

docs.title: Purify Blood
docs.text: Purify Blood This spell is one of a druid's limited number of healing rituals. It acts to purge poisons from the target's bloodstream, preventing them from doing any further damage. At higher levels of mastery, it also has influence over alcohol in the bloodstream. Command: purify <target> (defaults to caster) Base Cost: 35 Base Recovery: short Base Effect: heal (poisons), detox Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 11

docs.title: Rainbow Aura
docs.text: Rainbow Aura The rainbow aura is a construction of druidic power which protects the subject against elemental attacks: fire, cold, lightning, and water. (Note: You do not have to wear the rainbow object. It protects you automatically.) Command: rainbow <target> (defaults to caster) Base Cost: 40 SP Base Recovery: medium Base Effect: protection (moderate) Base Duration: medium-long Guild Level: 4

docs.title: Call Ravens
docs.text: Call Ravens This spell, which must be cast outdoors, summons dozens of ravens to torment the target. The birds swarm around its head, plucking at its eyes and obscuring its sight. A creature thus blinded is unable to fight as well as usual and may be unable to utilize certain skills, if it possesses them. Command: ravens <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 40 SP Base Recovery: medium Base Effect: blind Base Duration: medium Guild Level: 14

docs.title: Resist Poison, Resist Cold, Resist Lightning, Resist Fire
docs.text: Resist Poison, Resist Cold, Resist Lightning, Resist Fire An experienced druid often grows resistant to elemental attacks and to creatures' poisons. Each of these powers, which must be separately acquired, grants the druid a resistance to the specified attack form. If fully mastered, the druid is all but immune to such attacks, and (for cold and fire) may travel with impunity in Hyperborea or Souvrael. These powers do nothing about other types of damage, however -- a druid bitten by a snake may be resistant to poison, but he will still be injured by the teeth. Command: none necessary Base Cost: none Base Recovery: none Base Effect: protection (moderate) Base Duration: permanent Guild Level: 14-17

docs.title: Shatter
docs.text: Shatter With this spell, the druid attempts to cause metal objects possessed by his target to shatter into useless shards. Command: shatter <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 50 SP Base Recovery: medium Base Effect: destroy items (metal) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 12

docs.title: Sky Blade
docs.text: Sky Blade Calling on the power of Gaea, the druid forges a piece of the sky into a scythelike weapon. This weapon is weightless and in addition, can be commanded at the time of its creation to deal different types of damage. Depending on the Druid's mastery level and alignment, these may include: magic - pure magical damage fire - flame damage (good only) holy - holy damage through Gaea's light side (good only) unholy - unholy damage through Gaea's dark side (evil only) cold - cold damage (evil only) void - damage from the night lightning - damage from the storm rain - damage from immersion Command: skyblade <type> (defaults to magic) Base Cost: 60 SP Base Recovery: medium-long Base Effect: create items (weapon) Base Duration: long Guild Level: 9

docs.title: Wild Speed
docs.text: Wild Speed Using this spell, the druid may borrow for a short time the speed of such creatures as the hare, hawk, and cheetah. He may also confer this speed on another person. Command: speed <target> (defaults to caster) Base Cost: 50 SP Base Recovery: medium-long Base Effect: boost (dexterity, moderate) Base Duration: medium-long Guild Level: 4

docs.title: Wild Strength
docs.text: Wild Strength Using this spell, the druid may borrow for a short time the strength of such creatures as the bull, bear, and elephant. He may also confer this strength on another person. Command: strength <target> (defaults to caster) Base Cost: 50 SP Base Recovery: medium-long Base Effect: boost (strength, moderate) Base Duration: medium-long Guild Level: 4

docs.title: Sunray
docs.text: Sunray This powerful ritual focuses the light of the sun into a searing beam of power. Among the most powerful of druidic attacks, it is also especially effective against undead creatures. Command: sunray <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 75 SP Base Recovery: medium Base Effect: damage (high) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 18

docs.title: Taint Blood
docs.text: Taint Blood An evil ritual which calls upon the dark totemic spirits of nature. After casting this spell, a druid need only touch his target to send a virulent poison through its blood. Armor is no help, and the poison will continue to do damage beyond its initial amount, should the victim survive. Command: taint <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 90 SP Base Recovery: medium Base Effect: damage (moderate, continuing) Base Duration: long Guild Level: 11

docs.title: Thorns
docs.text: Thorns One of the most basic druidic spells, this charm allows the druid to strike a target with a barrage of sharp thorns. Though its damage is limited, especially against armored targets, its low cost and rapid recovery time mean that even some heirophant druids consider it a useful part of their arsenal. Command: thorns <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 25 SP Base Recovery: fast Base Effect: damage (low) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 1

docs.title: Warp Wood
docs.text: Warp Wood This spell targets a victim's possessions, causing wooden items to bend, twist, warp, and otherwise render themselves useless. Command: warpwood <target> (defaults to attacker) Base Cost: 50 SP Base Recovery: medium Base Effect: destroy items (wood) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 2

docs.title: Water Walk
docs.text: Water Walk An experienced druid may use this spell to gain the protection of the ocean spirits, allowing him to walk on the surface of water without drowning. At higher levels of mastery, the druid can impart this ability to others. Command: waterwalk <target> (defaults to caster) Base Cost: 40 SP Base Recovery: long Base Effect: travel (over oceans) Base Duration: long Guild Level: 7

docs.title: Wild Shape
docs.text: Wild Shape Wild Shape lets a druid wear a spirit animal form. Each form is learned as its own druid spell, and higher mastery of that form improves its strength and duration. Commands: wildshape wolf wildshape bear wildshape hawk wildshape serpent unshift Forms: Wolf Guild level: 6 Cost: 45 spell points Duration: 60 seconds + 30 seconds per wolf mastery level Effect: changes your race and visible form to a spirit-wolf and grants a dodge bonus. Bear Guild level: 10 Cost: 55 spell points Duration: 60 seconds + 35 seconds per bear mastery level Effect: changes your race and visible form to a spirit-bear and grants a constitution bonus. Hawk Guild level: 12 Cost: 60 spell points Duration: 55 seconds + 32 seconds per hawk mastery level Effect: changes your race and visible form to a spirit-hawk and grants a dexterity bonus. Serpent Guild level: 14 Cost: 68 spell points Duration: 55 seconds + 33 seconds per serpent mastery level Effect: changes your race and visible form to a spirit-serpent and grants a strength bonus. Terrain: Wolf and bear last longer in forest, plains, jungle, swamp, hills, farm, and path terrain. Hawk lasts longer in sky, mountain, forest, plains, jungle, hills, and path terrain. Serpent lasts longer in swamp, jungle, forest, underground, river, and lake terrain. When the terrain is favorable, the duration is increased by half. Restrictions: Shifting automatically unequips your worn and wielded gear. While shifted, many speaking, study, spell, and guild power commands are blocked because the spirit body cannot perform them. Use unshift to return to your natural form early. You may only wear one spirit form at a time. When a form ends, the spirit requires a short recovery before you can wildshape again. See also: dhelp spells dhelp restrictions

docs.title: Wind Walk
docs.text: Wind Walk An experienced druid may use this spell to gain the protection of the spirits of wind and storm, allowing him to walk on the air as though it were solid. At higher levels of mastery, the druid can impart this ability to others. Command: windwalk <target> (defaults to caster) Base Cost: 35 SP Base Recovery: very long Base Effect: travel (through sky) Base Duration: medium-long Guild Level: 15

docs.title: -- Miscellaneous Druid Commands ------------------------------
docs.text: -- Miscellaneous Druid Commands ------------------------------ Guild commands live under /cmds/guilds/druid/ (dhelp, dchat, druids, dscore, dhist, dtitle, resettitle, resettitlealt, nwyfre, ritual, etc.) and /cmds/guilds/druid/spells/ (active invocations and grove utility commands). See dhelp general for the full help menu. attune - Read the terrain(s) of the immediate area. dhist <#> - List recent messages on the druid channel. <#> is the number of lines it goes back, with a maximum of 300 and a default of 30. dscore - List your druid score report. This includes available study slots, learned powers, grove status, and material guidance. dtitle - Changes your title on the druids report. resettitle - Changes your title to your Druid guild title (the one you get when you advance guild level). This is not the title on the druids report, but the title used in who, finger, and other places. resettitlealt - Changes your title to a more feminine version of your Druid guild title, eg. 'mistress' instead of 'master'. druids (also dwho) - Lists all druids on the mud, along with a status report. The status codes are: D - dead E - wiz+ editing a file F - fighting I - input mode (reading, writing, listing 'who', etc.) M - muffed [Idle] - idle druids2 - Much like druids, just a different format.

docs.title: -- Purify Blood ---------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Purify Blood --------------------------------------------- Current: Marken Command: purify <target> Guild Level: 11 Purify Blood draws on Marken stability to clear poison, intoxication, and fever from the target. It defaults to the caster. Higher mastery improves the cleansing strength and adds a small restorative wash.

docs.title: -- Call Ravens ----------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Call Ravens ---------------------------------------------- Current: Tekali Command: ravens <target> Guild Level: 14 Call Ravens sends raven-shadows around a target, blinding and disrupting it. Mastery extends the blindness. This is a control invocation, not a raw damage tool.

docs.title: -- Return to Earth ------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Return to Earth ------------------------------------------ Invocation: return to earth Command: reclaim [corpse] Aliases: returnearth, compost Current: Tellurian Return to Earth lets a Druid kneel beside a fallen creature and return its body to the living soil. The corpse is removed, but any items or reagents inside it fall into the room first. The rite restores nwyfre based on the moons that are present. Dailos feeds Daloan, Markas feeds Marken, and Tekal feeds Tekali. Fuller phases return more, while crescent phases return less. If no moon is visible, the corpse returns to the earth as Tellurian nwyfre instead. Larger, stronger, and less-harvested corpses return more to the cycle. A corpse that has already been skinned, gutted, deboned, decapitated, or stripped of teeth still works, but gives less. Training Return to Earth makes the rite more efficient. As your mastery improves, the invocation costs less Tellurian nwyfre to begin, returns more nwyfre from each corpse, and can draw a larger offering before reaching your current's natural limit. If you perform the invocation at your own Sacred Grove, the grove also deepens from the offering. Training the invocation increases this grove growth as well. Player corpses are never consumed by this invocation.

docs.title: -- Reincarnate ----------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Reincarnate ---------------------------------------------- Very powerful druids sometimes draw deeply from the Marken current to pierce the veil of death and draw on Gaea's power to create a new living body for themselves. By returning from death in this manner, a druid can avoid much of the physical and mental damage associated with death. Command: reincarnate Base Cost: 600 Marken nwyfre Base Recovery: long Base Effect: resurrect Base Duration: permanent Guild Level: 26

docs.title: -- Renewal ---------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Renewal --------------------------------------------------- While not as skilled in the healing arts as a cleric, a druid does have a fair amount of knowledge of those arts. This Marken invocation, representing the renewal of all things in the natural cycle, is their most potent magical tool to that end. It will rejuvenate a target, completely healing all but the greatest wounds. Command: renewal <target> (defaults to caster) Base Cost: 140 Marken nwyfre Base Recovery: short Base Effect: heal (high) Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 23

docs.title: Druids are more martial than mages, roughly on par with
docs.text: Druids are more martial than mages, roughly on par with clerics, though their religious restrictions mean they are often less effective in combat than clerics. A druid forswears wearing most metals, preferring to make use of natural materials such as wood or leather. Many silver and gold objects are also allowed to them, because of these metals' association with the moon and sun. However, heavy armors such as platemail are forbidden to them. A druid may use some shields -- small shields of wooden or leather construction, primarily. Druids have significantly more leeway with weapons. A druid may use most daggers, sickles, staves, spears, and other polearms, in addition to most missile weapons, even if these contain metallic components. In addition, the druid may use hammers and other blunt weapons permitted to clerics, so long as those weapons are not metallic. Druids follow a wide range of philosophies, and may be good or evil, lawful or chaotic, as they please. However, a druid must maintain a certain personal balance in order to retain his powers; a druid who goes too far to any one extreme will find himself unable to call upon nature. A druid's primary characteristics are wisdom and charisma. Wisdom is necessary to understand the mysteries of Gaea, and charisma aids in establishing the necessary sense of empathy with Nature.

docs.title: -- Rituals ----------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Rituals ---------------------------------------------------- Druid rituals are prepared workings that shape your nwyfre before or between fights. They may restore vessels, expand capacity, or improve regeneration for a time. Later rites can also conserve nwyfre, convert one current into another, or bind short-lived companions and spirits. Some newer rites are long-running rituals. These toggle on and off, stay with you while you travel, and react to movement or other future events instead of ending after a fixed timer. Learn rituals in the Druid Grove inside the guild hall: learn ritual <name> Use these commands to inspect them: ritual Show your current rite and active effects. ritual list List rituals you know. ritual stop <name> End a long-running ritual. nwyfre rituals List rituals you know. nwyfre learnable List rituals you can learn. nwyfre ritual <name> Show requirements and effect. Ritual material costs come from the profession material stores shown by reagents. Use reagents search <item> to check an exact herb, creature reagent, skin, ore, bolt, or special shard. Perform a ritual with: ritual <name> Some rituals require an argument: ritual drawing of the tide tellurian ritual lunar draught marken ritual vessel expansion daloan Current-based rituals show the exact profession materials for each current in nwyfre ritual <name>. Conversion rituals require two currents: ritual tide exchange tellurian daloan ritual equinox channel daloan marken When all three moons are new, the lunar currents are all weak at once: ritual moonless drawing This rite uses common Daloan, Marken, and Tekali herbs to restore part of each lunar vessel without needing lunar nwyfre first. Some rituals may leave you with a companion or tool: raven pact Adds raven scout for nearby paths. hearth spirit Adds a quiet healing spirit for a short time. Long-running rituals remain active until you end them: verdant refrain Quietly hum and sing while traveling, sometimes gathering profession herbs and saved reagents in natural places. For the Druid menagerie and its companion-summoning rites, use dhelp companions. Conjunction rituals are rarer. They only work when the sky agrees: twin-moon pact Needs two full moons at night. triple confluence calling Needs all three full moons and an ancient Sacred Grove. Most prepared rituals require you to stand still until the rite completes. Moving or entering combat breaks the pattern. Long-running rituals are different: they are toggles, and their active effects simply pause when conditions are wrong. New druids should start with: learn ritual drawing of the tide ritual drawing of the tide marken Use dhelp beginner for the full first-hour path.

docs.title: -- Scry ------------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Scry ------------------------------------------------------ A druid may use the Tekali current to create a scrying pool -- a tiny, short-lived pool of water which can be used to magically locate others. This is not foolproof -- even a druid who has both mastered this invocation and is very wise may be detected by a perceptive target, and the effort involved in scrying is not trivial. Yet it is still considered a useful talent by those who practice it. Scrying only works if both you and the object of your attention are outside, on solid ground, and in natural settings. Command: scry <target> Base Cost: 20 Tekali nwyfre Base Recovery: slow Base Effect: locate Base Duration: instant Guild Level: 5

docs.title: -- Silverback -----------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Silverback ----------------------------------------------- Current: Tellurian Command: silverback Aliases: gorilla, silverbackguardian Guild Level: 21 Silverback calls a massive guardian gorilla out of the Tellurian current. The gorilla appears in the room, follows the druid from place to place, and stays close while growling, pacing, and watching for incoming blows. While the guardian remains, it throws itself between the druid and incoming combat damage. The druid takes none of the damage from a blocked hit; the silverback spends its own strength instead. The silverback has a pool of guardian strength based on Druid guild level, Silverback training, and your maximum health. Higher training protects between one-half and two full health bars, with the old guild-level calculation retained as a minimum. Its time in the world is tracked separately, so taking damage no longer shortens its natural duration. If the final blow exceeds its remaining strength, only the remaining amount is blocked. The silverback is a protector, not a normal target. Other players and creatures cannot attack it directly.

docs.title: -- Sky Blade -------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Sky Blade ------------------------------------------------- Current: Tekali Command: skyblade <type> Guild Level: 9 Sky Blade shapes a temporary scythe-like weapon from the sky. Its weapon class and duration follow the same scale as a cleric's spiritual hammer. The default type is magic. Other types become available through alignment and mastery. Mastery expands the available damage forms. At Druid guild level 10, Twin Sky Blades lets you shape two Sky Blades at once: twinskyblades <type> It costs the same Tekali nwyfre as casting Sky Blade twice, but avoids waiting through the cooldown between the two invocations.
