~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK BASICS ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ "Look within. Be still." -Zen saying Make no mistake, the life of a monk is not easy. When you took the vow to become a monk, it was a serious one. Monks live a solitary life, unable to marry or swear an oath. Monks are without worldly possessions; monks cannot own boats, nor have any level of wealth beyond the very basics needed. Monks live to train. Monks have at their disposal an array of skills, spells, and attacks, many of which at the pinnacle of training, can do some impressive things. Monks rely on their own sense of chi. A monk's chi is essential to everything they do - from basic combat, to strengthening and hardening their own body through the staff soul, to unleashing chi-based attacks on their opponents. But, like everything in life, chi must be maintained and guided. Without attention, a monk's chi will drain and drift away. Modern monk combat is not about isolated skills. It is built on rhythm. Openers generate tags and momentum, finishers cash that pressure in, and bridge techniques carry your chain from one style into another without forcing a reset. Use "mskills" to see what each technique is for, and "mcombo" to see your current combo state and route guidance. Monks earn Monk XP in battle. It advances guild level automatically, but the road to mastery still passes through formal challenges at guild levels 4, 9, 14, and 19. Monk XP earned while a challenge or regular level blocks advancement remains banked. Use "msc" or "gscore Monk" to review your progress. The "cost" and "advance guild" commands explain the next gate but never spend ordinary experience. On the surface, monks are but a ripple on the water. But, as that ripple carries, so it grows. ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK CHALLENGES ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Monks must go through challenges throughout their life, to insure that they are ready to move up. Currently, in order to get their next fighting style, they must complete mastery challenges in order to advance to guild level 5, 10, 15 and 20. Monk XP continues to accumulate while a trial is incomplete. Completing the trial immediately releases every rank your banked Monk XP and regular level permit. Dragon Rebind becomes available at guild level 19 as the graduation technique for the final mastery trial. Full Dragon style remains the reward for reaching guild level 20. These are no longer simple duels. Each trial asks you to prove that you understand a sequence of forms. The early trials focus on one style at a time, while the final trial demands that you flow through several styles in order. The mastery trial now expects a true bridge chain rather than a handful of manual stance swaps. A successful monk will move from Crane into Monkey, from Monkey into Snake, and from Snake into Tiger without letting the form collapse. Be forewarned, challenges are real. At any time you can "escape" the challenge, but with a penalty. Watch your monk monitor during a trial. It now reports the current trial objective directly, so you can tell whether the chamber is asking for a style swap, a bridge, or a finisher. ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK CHI ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Chi is the active life force present in every living thing. Chi is best described as "natural energy", or your life force. Everything in the monk guild requires a monk to manage and know their chi at all times. It's vital. Chi governs the ability to invoke skills, spells and monk abilities. It ebbs and flows in combat, and also serves as your reference for how well you can take an attack. In practice, chi now does three jobs: it fuels monk abilities, it powers your inner defense, and it determines how long you can keep a route alive before you must reset your rhythm. Chi is managed by your monk soul itself. The walking staff is the guild object that carries your training, your combo state, and the defensive discipline created by your current chi. Chi tends to rise during active combat and drift away while idle. Good monks use that flow rather than waiting until they are empty. A monk's chi is everything. It is vital, and it must be managed well. ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK COMBOS ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Monk combat is built around chains. A chain is the short history of techniques you have used recently. Good chains build tempo, create openings, move between stances, and then spend that setup on a hard finisher. The short version: 1. Use a starter in your current stance. 2. Add pressure, control, or a bridge before the chain expires. 3. Build tempo and stance diversity. 4. Spend the chain on a finisher or Dragon capstone. The combo window Every combo step gives you a short window to continue the chain. If you wait too long, the chain falls back to Stillness. Bridge moves usually refresh the window. Stabilizing moves preserve the chain but give a shorter window. Finishers cash out the chain and leave only a brief follow-up window. Stances Most combo techniques belong to a stance. You normally must be in that stance to use the technique. The main stances are: Crane - balance, redirection, and controlled openings. Monkey - flow, trips, and weapon disruption. Snake - precision, breath control, and pressure. Tiger - aggression, burst setup, and finishers. Dragon - advanced capstone routing. Normal `mswitch` changes style but resets the chain. Bridge techniques are the special way to move between styles while keeping the chain. Roles Every combo move has a role. `mskills` shows the role column. Starter - begins a clean chain in a stance. Bridge - changes stance while preserving combo flow. Pressure - builds offensive setup for later moves. Control - creates control setup and improves control effects. Utility - stabilizes or recovers without fully cashing out. Finisher - spends tempo and setup for a stronger payoff. Burst - heavier payoff, usually with stricter requirements. Tempo Tempo is the chain's stored momentum. Starters and bridges usually add tempo. Finishers and burst moves spend it. Many stronger moves require a minimum tempo before they can be used. If a move says the chain has not built enough tempo, keep chaining legal starters, bridges, pressure, or control steps before trying that finisher again. Step and stance diversity Step is how deep the current chain is. Some moves require at least a certain step before they unlock. Stance diversity is how many different stances are represented in the recent chain. Advanced Tiger and Dragon routes care about this, especially `tpunch`, `tdeath`, and `drebind`. Tags and openings Many moves place short-lived tags on you or on the target. These tags are the real "openings" in the system. Some examples: crane_balance - Crane has established balance. monkey_flow - Monkey flow is active. serpent_focus - Snake pressure is active. tiger_drive - Tiger drive is active. off_balance - The target has been knocked off balance. compressed_breath - The target's breath has been compressed. opened_guard - The target's guard has been opened. shaken - The target has been shaken. locked_down - The target has been controlled. death_mark - The target has been marked for death routes. tempo_window - Some cooldowns and bridges become easier. If a move complains that you need a tag, you are missing part of the setup. Use `mcombo <skill>` to see what that skill needs and which moves commonly lead into it. What the monk monitor means Turn the monk monitor on or off with `mmon`. The line looks like this: [S: Tiger Chi: 18 (24) [F] [S] [C: Tiger 2/5 | step 3 | tempo 5 -> Thousand Punch {tiger_drive,death_mark}]] Read it as: S: Your current fighting style. Chi: Your current chi and maximum chi. [F] or [X]: Chi focus is active, or not active. [S/C/D/A/X]: Active power word, or none. C: Current combo summary. The combo summary is: <style> <resonance>/5 | step <step> | tempo <tempo> -> <best legal follow-up> {active tags} `Stillness` means you do not currently have a live chain. Resonance Resonance rises as you keep working in the same style or bridge cleanly through the chain. It improves combo damage and control. Finishers, burst moves, and control moves reduce resonance because they commit the chain's pressure. Common route families Crane Kick -> Drifting Reed -> Monkey follow-up Start in Crane, then bridge into Monkey while keeping the chain. Crane Kick -> Wind Thread -> Snake pressure Start in Crane, then bridge into Snake for precision routes. Leg Sweep -> Coiled Rise -> Snake pressure/control Start in Monkey, create off-balance, then move into Snake. Leg Sweep -> Grapple Weapon Monkey control route. Stronger when the target is off-balance or isolated. Snake Hand Strike -> One-Inch Punch -> Pressure Point Snake pressure into a finisher, then deeper control if the guard has opened and tempo is high enough. Roar -> Thousand Punch Tiger starter into Tiger finisher. Works best after the chain has enough tempo, setup, and stance diversity. Tiger route -> Falling Plume -> Crane Use Tiger pressure, then bridge back into Crane instead of letting the chain die. Multi-stance chain -> Dragon Rebind Advanced Dragon route. You need several stances, a bridge, tempo, and the right pressure or control setup. Why a move may fail Wrong stance: Switch or bridge into the stance that owns the move. Not enough tempo: Add more legal combo steps before using the finisher. Need more stance diversity: Bridge through another stance before trying the payoff. Missing bridge: Use a bridge move somewhere in the chain. Missing pressure or control: Add a pressure or control role before the payoff. Missing target opening: Use the setup move that applies the required target tag. Useful commands mskills Lists your monk skills, guild level, stance, and combo role. mcombo Shows current style, combo state, window, step, tempo, resonance, active tags, and legal follow-ups. mcombo <skill> Explains one skill's stance, role, requirements, tags, bridge behavior, and strong next steps. mmon Toggles the monk monitor line. Practice advice Start by learning one route at a time. Watch `mcombo` after each move. When a follow-up appears in Legal Followups, try it immediately. If the monitor returns to Stillness, your window expired or the chain was reset. The most important habit is this: do not manually `mswitch` in the middle of a combo unless you mean to reset it. Use bridge moves to carry momentum from one stance into another. ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK COMMANDS ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Monks have a variety of other commands available to them that aren't necessarily skills or spells. The following other commands are available: "mhp" "monk/emonk" "monkhelp" "monks" "msc" "mskills" "mswitch" "mtithe" "mtitle" "mmon" "mcombo" "notch" "msc" gives you your monk score sheet and training details. "mskills" lists monk skills with stance and combo role. "mmon" toggles the monk monitor line. "mcombo" shows your current combo state, legal follow-ups, and can explain likely next steps if you pass a skill name. "monkhelp combos" explains chains, tempo, tags, and the monitor. "monkhelp training post" explains the safe Wooden Man Post room. "notch" records or reviews the places marked on your staff. View more details at "monkhelp <command>". ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK CRANE STYLE ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Crane is the disciplined entry style. It is about balance, space, and clean starts. Crane routes usually begin a chain rather than end one. "crane kick" is your basic opener. "cyclone" cashes that balance into an early payoff, while bridge moves like "drifting reed" and "wind thread" send that balance into Monkey or Snake. Think of Crane as: open cleanly establish rhythm choose the next style on purpose Common examples: crane kick -> cyclone -> chi blast crane kick -> drifting reed -> leg sweep crane kick -> wind thread -> snake hand strike ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK DRAGON STYLE ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Dragon is not simply "the strongest stance". It is the capstone layer that rewards real mastery across the other styles. Dragon is at its best after you have already woven several stances together. The current capstone is "dragon rebind", which takes a sufficiently diverse route and collapses it into a fresh payoff. Think of Dragon as: prove you can route through the whole guild preserve enough structure to remain dangerous convert multi-style mastery into a final strike Dragon is not meant to replace Crane, Monkey, Snake, or Tiger. It exists to unify them. ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK FIGHTING STYLES ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Monks core ability outside of their skills and spells, are base training in various fighting styles. Many of these styles mimic the behaviours of animals in the wild. And, many skills require that the monk be using a certain style. Many of these styles have various advantages and disadvantages. Some fighting styles are great at offense, some are more defensive postures, some allow you to be more agile on your feet with quick strikes, some allow you to focus on healing. Styles are now more than passive bonuses. Monks build rhythm by chaining the right techniques together. A clean opener builds resonance in that style, and certain follow-up techniques act as finishers when your sequence is correct. As a monk advances, some techniques stop being simple attacks and become bridges. These moves preserve combo momentum while shifting you into a new style, letting Crane open into Monkey control, Monkey feed Snake precision, Snake turn into Tiger violence, and Dragon collapse a multi-style chain into a capstone strike. Normal "mswitch" is still important for setup and discipline, but it is not what creates advanced combo flow. Bridge moves are what let you cross stance lines without dropping momentum. You can watch this flow through your monk monitor. It now reports resonance, active combo tags, and the next legal route the guild believes you are ready to take. The Wooden Man Post training room lets you practice stance flow and combo chains safely. Use "monkhelp training post" for details. Fighting styles: "crane" "snake" "monkey" "tiger" "dragon" ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

docs.title: -- Monks ------------------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Monks ------------------------------------------------------ Monks are disciplined martial artists who turn the body, breath, and mind into weapons. They live by restraint: a monk cannot marry, swear an oath, own boats, or gather wealth like other adventurers. In return, they gain a focused path built around chi, bare-handed combat, fighting styles, and carefully chained techniques. Chi is the center of the guild. It fuels monk abilities, strengthens inner defense, and helps keep combat routes alive. A monk who manages chi well can flow from opener to bridge to finisher, building rhythm instead of simply repeating isolated attacks. Modern monk combat uses several fighting styles, including tiger, crane, snake, monkey, and dragon. Techniques can create combo tags, carry momentum between styles, and finish a route with a stronger effect. Monks also earn notches through training and challenge, and must prove themselves over a long road toward mastery. This guild is best suited for players who want a disciplined melee path with resource management, combo planning, and a strong ascetic theme. It is not a guild for players who want easy wealth or heavy equipment. Useful starting notes: Guild name: Monks Newbie checkout: checkout monk Theme: chi, martial arts, restraint, combos, mastery Help command: monkhelp Good first topics after joining: monkhelp basics monkhelp chi monkhelp fighting styles monkhelp combos monkhelp commands monkhelp mmon Ask a current Monk, or an immortal, if you need help finding the path to the monastery or deciding whether this life fits your character.

docs.title: Syntax: mmon
docs.text: Syntax: mmon This command allows you to enable and disable your monk monitor. The monk monitor now shows: style current chi and max chi whether chi focus is active the current power word, if any your combo summary the active trial objective, if you are in a mastery trial The two bracket indicators are: first bracket: chi focus second bracket: power word Examples: [F] means chi focus is active [X] means it is not [S] [C] [D] [A] indicate the active power word

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK MONKEY STYLE ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Monkey is disruption and movement. It is less interested in a clean duel than in forcing the opponent out of shape. "leg sweep" and "grapple weapon" define the basic Monkey lesson: break footing, isolate the target, and take away control. Later, Monkey becomes one of the guild's main bridge styles, feeding into Snake with "coiled rise" or Tiger with "predator coil". Think of Monkey as: create chaos force openings hand the route into a deadlier style Common examples: leg sweep -> grapple weapon leg sweep -> coiled rise -> one-inch punch leg sweep -> predator coil -> roar ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK OVERVIEW ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ "The most precious gift we can offer others is our presence. When mindfulness embraces those we love, they will bloom like flowers." -Thich Nhat Hanh Topics: "basics" "wealth" "alcohol" "chi" "armor" "weapons" "fighting styles" "challenges" "training" "notches" "commands" "skills" "mmon" "mcombo" "combos" "training post" Please see "monkhelp <topic>" for more details. ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

docs.text: Syntax: notch [add|list] This command allows you to add a notch to your staff, or list the notches already carved into it.

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK NOTCHES ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Monks are worldly. They spend much of their lives exploring and seeing the world. Their experience is everything. It's that wisdom that allows them the knowledge of how to fight so well. As a monk travels, it's important that each new place be recorded on their staff as a "notch". Please type "monkhelp notch" to see the command details. ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK SNAKE STYLE ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Snake is precision and exploitation. By the time you are in Snake, the target should already be unstable enough for you to punish very specific weaknesses. "snake hand strike" creates the line. "one-inch punch" and "pressure point" convert that line into debuff, lockdown, or setup for a later kill. Snake also owns two important transitions: "white feather" for a controlled reset back into Crane and "fanged advance" for a hard conversion into Tiger. Think of Snake as: mark the weakness punish the weakness choose reset or execution Common examples: snake hand strike -> one-inch punch snake hand strike -> one-inch punch -> pressure point snake hand strike -> one-inch punch -> fanged advance -> roar ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK TIGER STYLE ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Tiger is the style of commitment. It turns setup into fear, burst, and execution pressure. "roar" starts the intimidation. "thousand punch" is the main burst cashout. "touch of death" is not a casual button; it is strongest when the route has already created the right target state. Tiger becomes much stronger when entered through a bridge rather than through a manual stance swap, because the route arrives with real tags and momentum behind it. Common examples: roar -> thousand punch fanged advance -> roar -> thousand punch roar -> thousand punch -> touch of death ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ WOODEN MAN POST ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ The Brotherhood keeps a Wooden Man Post northeast of the main training hall. It is built for repetition: striking, checking, trapping, stance changes, and full combo chains. From the main training room, go "northeast". Once there, use: kill post attack post stop practice mswitch <style> <monk skill> post The post is safe. It does not attack, deal damage, die, leave a corpse, grant experience, count as a kill, or advance quests. It exists only to let monks practice form and rhythm. When you are done, "stop practice" steps back from the post and ends the practice fight immediately. Practice is still real practice. Monk skills used on the post spend normal chi, spell points, and cooldowns, and your combo state and monk monitor update as they would in combat. ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK WEALTH ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Monks cannot carry or bank any substantial wealth beyond what is simply needed for their next level. Any wealth accumulated above that will be tithed to the guild coffers. Above and beyond that, any extra worldly possessions, such as boats, are seen as a simple luxury. Monks would never own a material item such as a boat or ship. ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ MONK WEAPONS ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Monks cannot use any other weapons other than their staff. A monk is given their staff upon committing themselves to the guild, and the two are never separated. The staff grows in power with the monk, and with the monk's experience in the world. It's important to make note of your surroundings as you journey through the world. Simply make a "notch" on your staff whenever you've found a new part of the world previously unseen. ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

docs.title: Welcome to the Morpher guild!
docs.text: Welcome to the Morpher guild! There are a few commands that you should be aware of to start out with. mhelp...........Display this help file mskills.........Display a list of Morpher skills mchat...........Talk on the Morpher guild line mhist...........View the Morpher guild line history mwho(mowho).....View other Morphers online motto...........Set the title that shows up in "mwho" endmorph........Ends a Morph prematurely Any of these abilities can be found out more about by typing; "help <ability>", for example: "help endmorph". It should be noted that Morphers are slightly different from most other guilds on Darkwind in how they advance and how far one can advance their power within the guild. There are a total of 15 guild levels one can advance through in Morphers. The first 10 levels are regular guild levels, guild levels 11 through 15 are set to an extremely high cost. Your power within the guild also cannot be 1/2 or higher of your characters level. Besides when very first starting out of course, at level 1 and Morpher level 1. This is to ensure that you are growing at a rate that is appropriate to maintain and perform the morphs that a Morpher must be able to perform. You will find that you cannot advance passed guild level 10 until character level 45. This is to prevent such power from entering the hands of the inexperienced. You will also find that guild levels 11 and up are quite expensive in terms of EXP cost. They are designed to be a power ramp-up to help Morphers reach their maximum potential at the right time. Your power within the guild will increase automatically as soon as you have reached the correct level and exp requirements for each power level. You can type "sc" to view how much XP is needed to gain more power within the guild. Now you're probably a little curious as to what weapons and armours a Morpher can use. Well, it's pretty straight forward. Weapons: ** NO large weapons. ** NO huge weapons. ** NO missile weapons. Armours: ** NO plate armour. ** NO chain armour. Pretty simple, right? Well, things get a tad more complex when you start looking deeper at who Morphers are and what you do. Morphers morph their bodies, pretty straightforward. You have hands, why not make them into weapons! You have skin on your torso and legs, why not turn them into some wicked armour! In order to morph these body parts though, you can't be wearing other armour or weapons and successfully morph these body parts though. As such, most of the time, you'll see other Morphers walking around wearing no armour over their torso, or legs, and never wielding an actual weapon, but instead morphing their hands into the most deadly weapons they would ever want.

docs.title: Advancement
docs.text: Advancement Necromancers can advance their studies of the dark arts in the ~>GuildHouse<~, or through the use of the ~>nritual<~ command. There are a total of twenty-five guild levels. A Necromancer cannot advance their guild level above their normal level. Additionally, they will need to possess a fair amount of training to reach the upper guild levels. This requirement is based on the Necromancer's intelligence and wisdom, and to a lesser extent, their charisma and constitution.

docs.title: Alarian
docs.text: Alarian Once a powerful sorcerer, little is now known of Alarian. Legend states that he was the spark that brought the inhabitants of Geshtai out of their barbaric existence and into the thriving modern era. Other whispers say he forced the gods into existence with his own magic. A consistent legend is that he grew bored with his creations, and sought to do more. Fascinated with the lives of mortals, he eventually faced his most difficult challenge: mastering the mysteries behind the "spark of life" that the inhabitants of DarkWind possessed. He could create life, but it was of a different caliber. He soon learned to shift and mold existing lifeforces instead of creating his own. This type of sorcery soon came to be called Necromancy. Alarian's fate is as hidden as his life. Though early DarkWinders built crypts for his "corpse," the graves never stayed occupied for long.

docs.title: Equipment
docs.text: Equipment Necromancers do not rely on physical defenses that can disrupt or interfere their magical abilities. As such, they are restricted in the weapons and armour available to them. Necromancers may not use medium, large, or huge weapons that are of the pierce, cleave, or slash types. Additionally, they may not use any plate armour, or shields. As a general rule, they may use padded cloth armour, rings, and amulets. They may also use leather armour, but only for boots, gloves, and cloaks. Any scale, banded, studded, chain, or padded armour that consists of metal, leather, rock, or wood material will restrict the Necromancer's abilities.

docs.title: Followers
docs.text: Followers As a master of death, a Necromancer learns to summon various undead creatures. Several of these creatures (such as the skeleton and the ghoul) can be used as a fierce weapon in combat. Using the "unleash" command, a Necromancer can force this type of follower to fight opponents. Other followers serve other purposes, and more information can be found in the ~>nraise<~ command's help.

docs.title: Guildhouse
docs.text: Guildhouse The Necromancers do not have a traditional ~>guildhouse<~. You will find that it is actually one of ~>Alarian<~'s first crypts, before he and his followers discovered his power over death. This tomb has long been sealed off to the world, and buried under a millennia worth of soil and stone. Alarian shaped the tomb with his magic to provide a shelter to both himself and his followers. Now, the ~>guildhouse<~ acts as a hub of death energy, providing Necromancers with several benefits. Here, they may advance their studies in the dark arts, as well as spend their worldly experience to better their body, mind, and soul. Additionally, a Necromancer will notice that the guild hall is capable of creating a personal crypt for them. Finally, the tomb is magically tied into a series of collapsed graves, and will allow the Necromancer to quickly travel to these locations. Since the tomb is sealed, a Necromancer must use the ~>nentomb<~ spell to return.

docs.title: Necro
docs.text: Necro Necros study death, undeath, runes, and supernatural power. They are physically fragile spellcasters who can deal heavy damage, raise followers, and shape a fight through magic rather than ordinary armour and weapons. Their power flows through two runes. Those runes support a broad spell catalog and the undead followers that fight beside them. Necro is best suited to a player who enjoys managing spells, minions, and a dangerous caster toolkit. Current roster status: OPEN Useful starting references: nechelp intro Read the guild introduction nechelp spells Review spellcasting nechelp followers Review undead followers help guilds equipment Joining requirements and directions can change. Check help guilds and ask a current Necro before committing.

docs.title: Necromancers
docs.text: Necromancers Necromancers are masters of death, undeath, and the powers of the supernatural. They are extremely fragile physically, but have the potential to deal a large amount of damage through both their variety of ~>spells<~ and their ~>followers<~. These powers flow through their two ~>runes<~. Topics of interest (use "nechelp <topic>"): ~>advancement<~, ~>Alarian<~, ~>equipment<~, ~>followers<~, ~>GuildHouse<~, ~>monitor<~, ~>runes<~, ~>spells<~, and ~>stats<~,

docs.title: Monitor
docs.text: Monitor Necromancers can quickly access information concerning their current well-being through the use of the 'hp' command. In addition to standard information about HP and SP, a Necromancer will see two meters labeled "BLIGHT" and "DEATH". These two meters correspond to the two ~>runes<~ that augment their spells. A Necromancer will also notice a health bar for each of their ~>followers<~, and information about current effects that are active.

docs.title: s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s {9} Doom  s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s
docs.text: s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s {9} Doom s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s Syntax: ndoom <parvus|mediocris|amplus> Cost: Varies s s s s The doom curse is one of the most dangerous spells available to a s s Necromancer. The Necromancer pulls together their blight magic into s s a powerful mist that will choke the life from all of the enemies in s s the area. The damage is split among all valid targets. A Necromancer s s can choose one of three modes for the doom spell, which will default s s to using 'parvus'. The 'parvus' mode is the weakest, which will s s cause a small amount of damage, but only have a short cooldown and s s small cost. The 'mediocris' mode costs more and has a longer s s cooldown, but does more damage. The strongest mode, 'amplus', does a s s large amount of damage but has the highest costs. s s s s The 'parvus' setting requires 25% of maximum sp to cast. The s s 'mediocris' and 'amplus' settings require 50%, and 75% of maximum s s sp to cast, respectively. s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s

docs.title: s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s  Raise Undead  s s s s s s s s s s s s s s
docs.text: s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s Raise Undead s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s {1} Syntax: nraise [skeleton] Cost: 10 SP s s {5} Syntax: nraise [ghoul] Cost: 50 SP s s {8} Syntax: nraise [zombie] Cost: 80 SP s s {17} Syntax: nraise [wraith] Cost: 170 SP s s {24} Syntax: nraise [lich] Cost: 240 SP s s {25} Syntax: nraise [ghost] Cost: 500 SP s s s s A Necromancer's power over death can be molded into a deadly force. s s With this ability, a Necromancer can raise an unholy creature to aid s s them in combat. The simplest creature is a skeleton that will fade s s over time. At guild level 5, a Necromancer can raise a combat- s s oriented ghoul. Next, at guild level 8, the Necromancer can raise a s s zombie. Though the zombie cannot fight, it will follow its master s s and provide carrying space. At guild level 17, a Necromancer can s s summon a wraith: a powerful, but temporary creature. At guild level s s 24, a Necromancer can summon a powerful spell-casting lich. s s Finally, as the Necromancer closes on their education in the dark s s arts, they have the ability to summon a ghost using the corpse of a s s foe. This requires the Necromancer to be at least level 50. Even s s so, the ghost will only last a maximum of 30 minutes. s s s s Necromancers can "feed" a corpse to their ghoul to help it regain s s some of its health. s s s s Each of these spells require a corpse as part of the ritual. s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s s

docs.title: Runes
docs.text: Runes A Necromancer's amulet has two runes carved into it. These runes are the rune of death, and the rune of blight. These runes contain the same ancient magic ~>Alarian<~ used a millenium ago. Some Necromantic spells dervive their power from death or blight. These spells (indicated by a 'D' or 'B', respectively, in ~>necspells<~) can drain a rune of its power momentarily, adding an extra effect to the spell. Over time, these runes will recharge.

docs.title: Spells
docs.text: Spells Necromancers can access a list of their spells with the ~>necspells<~ command. Additionally, they may list only those spells which are available to them by using the 'avail' argument. In addition to these abilities, they have access to the ~>necro<~, ~>necros<~, ~>nechist<~, and ~>nritual<~ commands. Help for these commands can be accessed through using: help <command>, where <command> is the ability's syntax, such as 'help nspray'.

docs.title: Stats
docs.text: Stats A skilled Necromancer is both experienced and intelligent. As such, intelligence provides the biggest contribution to maximum spell points. The next most effective stat is constitution. A Necromancer must have a great deal of stamina to summon ranks of the undead, which constitution provides. Additionally, constitution improves the minions summoned. Two other important stats are wisdom and charisma. Wisdom strengthens a Necromancer's bond with the otherwordly. Charisma helps Necromancers maintain the bond over their undead minions. As stats are increased with the Metaphysician, they provide additional power to a Necromancer's ability to recharge their ~>runes<~. Necromancers receive a single hit point per constitution. For energy, a Necromancer will receive 6 SP per intelligence, 3 SP per constitution, and 3 SP per every two wisdom or charisma (independently of each other). An additional, but highly influential stat, is a Necromancer's study and perversion of the dead. This is measured by the number of corpses desecrated. As a Necromancer desecrates more corpses, their body can be consumed by the spirits of those they've condemned, instantly clearing their ability cooldowns. Higher desecration will also increase their damage capabilities, as well as enhancing other spells.

docs.title: Skills and Abilities
docs.text: Skills and Abilities Ninja abilities unlock at their listed <guild level> and begin at 70% reliability. A failed reliability roll costs one fifth of the ability's spell-point cost, but does not consume its item, start its cooldown, or add a combo piece. Ninja rank is separate from guild level. Every rank after rank 1 earns one training session. Use <practice> to spend a session and improve one ability by 5%, up to 100%. Rank costs 250 guild XP (GXP) each time. Valid skill attempts, completed combos, and qualifying combat kills award GXP. Battle GXP tapers for NPCs more than five levels below you and reaches zero at fifteen levels below you. Use <nskills> to review rank, GXP, sessions, marks, and reliability. Many offensive techniques also add a piece to the Ninja combo system. When enough recent pieces are present, the wraps may release a special combat sequence. See <ninhelp combo> for details.

docs.title: Ninja Combos
docs.text: Ninja Combos Ninja combat techniques build momentum in the wraps. When you use combat abilities, the wraps remember recent techniques for a short time. If three recent pieces line up, the wraps release a combo during combat. Resolving any three-piece combo also awards 10 Ninja GXP, in addition to the GXP earned by its component skill attempts. Some combinations have special results. Tsuki with Blind and Pummel focuses armor-piercing force. Tsubo with Pummel strikes pressure points. Pummel with Dimmak helps clear intoxication. Shuriken in a combo can call a storm of throwing stars. Tsuki in a combo can add an extra strike. Other combinations still release as a general burst of attacks. Use <nskills> to review your abilities and watch the ninja line in your monitor for recent combo pieces. Combo pieces fade quickly, so combos reward active combat timing rather than long preparation.

docs.title: Guild Levels and Advancement
docs.text: Guild Levels and Advancement Ninja guild level and Ninja rank are separate. Guild level unlocks abilities and rises only when the <Training Master> accepts proof of a newly completed <mark>. General experience and GXP are never spent on guild level. The final guild level is 50. Ninja rank is earned with GXP. Every rank costs 250 GXP and every rank after rank 1 supplies one training session. Rank never raises guild level. See <abilities> for training and <marks> for assassination advancement.

docs.title: <*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*> The Guild of the Ninja <*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*>
docs.text: <*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*> The Guild of the Ninja <*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*> The Ninja are trained assassins that specialize in stealth, information, and combat prowess. They do not directly worship Gaea, but do see the need for balance in all things. Ninjas raise guild level only by completing unique assassination marks and proving each kill to the Training Master. Guild XP separately raises Ninja rank and supplies skill training. Several enhancement skills require the Ninja to enter a meditative trance. These meditations can increase physical prowess, increase natural healing, and other effects. They also have impressive physical training, including turning their barehands into weapons, and the ability to cripple an opponent's movement. Additionally, they can combo their abilities together to produce produce powerful effects. <*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*> The following races are restricted from joining: Desert Dwarf | Ice Ogre | Rift Duergar Stone Dwarf | Sylph <*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*> Ninja can only be joined by other Gaea-aligned guilds (.e.g., Garou, Lunar), and non-aligned guilds (e.g., Bard, Fighter). Joining requires level 5 and at least 10 unmodified Dexterity. The guild focuses on Dexterity, Intelligence, and Wisdom. They can use blunt and polearm weaponry, including large and huge varients. For armour, Ninja forgo shields, as well as metalic plate, scale, banded, and chain equipment. <*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*> If you are interested in joining the ranks of the Ninja, you will have to "lever"age your knowledge of the Kerei fortress, seeking out the assassination box. <*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*>

docs.title: The Ninja Guild
docs.text: The Ninja Guild The Ninja are trained assassins that specialize in stealth, information and combat prowess. Ninja have an indepth knowledge of combat that they may leverage to bring down a target. Dexterity and intelligence are especially important to the guild. Dexterity supports the precision and speed expected of a Ninja, while intelligence supports study, technique and control. Joining requires level 5 and at least 10 unmodified Dexterity. A list of abilities can be shown with the <nskills> command. The <practice> command spends rank-earned training sessions to improve an ability from its starting 70% reliability toward 100%. Ninja rank comes from guild XP, while guild level comes only from unique assassination <marks>; neither progression track spends or advances the other. Several combat abilities add pieces to the Ninja combo system. Recent pieces can combine into special combat bursts; see <ninhelp combo>. The <ninhelp> command can also be used to find information on the following subjects: <abilities>, <marks>, <training master>. From the shadow-covered room where you joined, you can reach the main guild hall in Kerei by going: u,w,n,n,e,e,d,sw,s,s. From that guard room, you can then "slide down" to enter the guild hall. There is also a Ninja presence hidden in Darkwind. The Darkwind guild rooms connect back into the same order, but Yagyu the training master keeps his formal training hall in Kerei.

docs.title: Guild Levels and Advancement
docs.text: Guild Levels and Advancement Unique assassination marks are the only way a Ninja raises guild level. The <Training Master> assigns an incomplete mark, with suggested level used to favor an appropriate target rather than block advancement. Kill the exact assigned target yourself, then use <bloody> to dip the assigned <kunai> in the corpse's blood and give it to Yagyu. Each unique completion raises guild level once, to a maximum of 50. Each assignment includes one free "reroll challenge". The replacement is a different incomplete mark, and the rejected mark returns to the future pool. A reroll never costs GXP, rank, or training sessions. Ask Yagyu to "list challenge" to review the current assignment and progress.

docs.title: Training Master
docs.text: Training Master Yagyu, the training master in the Kerei guildhouse, offers guidance and assigns the unique <marks> that raise Ninja guild level. Ask him to "accept challenge", "list challenge", or "reroll challenge". Each assignment permits one free reroll, and neither assignment nor completion costs experience or GXP. He is the formal trainer for the order, even for Ninja who entered through the hidden Darkwind rooms.

docs.title: Paladin Guild Advancement
docs.text: Paladin Guild Advancement ------------------------- Paladins rise through righteous battle. Every worthy kill earns Paladin XP, and your guild level (1 to 15) rises automatically when you have earned enough. Earning Paladin XP: - Any NPC kill where you struck the killing blow, or dealt at least a tenth of the victim's health, awards Paladin XP to everyone in the group who qualifies. - Tougher prey is worth more. Rewards taper when prey is more than five levels beneath you and reach nothing at fifteen levels beneath you. Bosses carry large bonuses. - Variety pays. Hunting the same spawn over and over decays the reward; ranging widely keeps it at full value. Guild levels: - Levels advance on their own the moment you have earned enough XP. - Your guild level can never exceed your character level, and your combined guild levels can never exceed your character level. - Your charisma must grow with your rank - roughly three charisma for every two guild levels. Guild level 15 requires charisma 22. - Mitra grants nothing while your alignment is evil. XP earned while fallen is banked, and the levels pop when you atone. - XP earned while you are held back by any of these is never lost. - Guild level 15 is the pinnacle; Mitra's Champions join the himitra and lord channels. Commands: - 'cost' and 'advance guild' at the guild hall report your progress. - Devotion points still come with each guild level; spend them with 'devote'. Use 'devote reset' to preview renewing all of your devotion choices before Mitra's statue in the guild hall. Your first renewal is free; later renewals require an escalating coin offering. - A confirmed renewal returns every allocated devotion point and ends all active Paladin effects, including blessings, sanctifications, consecrations, summoned seals, and holy javelins. - Titles remain yours to choose via 'ptitle' and 'title'. Your battle record survives leaving the guild. Should you return in good standing, your guild level is restored.

+-------------------------------------------------------------------+ Devotion -------- 'devote' displays every trainable devotion and your available points. 'devote <skill>' allocates one point to that devotion. 'devote reset' previews a complete devotion reset and its offering. 'devote reset confirm' performs the reset before Mitra's statue in the Paladin guild hall. You cannot reset while fighting. Your first reset is free; later resets use an escalating coin offering. Resetting returns all allocated points and ends active Paladin blessings, sanctifications, consecrations, seals, and holy javelins. GL Skill Description +-------------------------------------------------------------------+ 1 Divine Favor Elevates your healing. 1 Eyes of the Faithful Judge the holy standings of those around them. 1 Smite Call Mitra to smite your enemy 2 Holy Light Summon a holy ball of light. 3 Seal of Healing Summons a seal in the room to heal you and others. 4 Courage Beseach Mitra for courage in battle 5 Seal of Binding Summons a seal in the room to help bind your enemies. 6 Repel Undead Brings Mitra's wrath upon the undead 7 Holy Shield Creates a holy shield 8 Holy Javelin Creates a holy javelin 9 Mitra's Gift Ask Mitra for a gift for you or an ally 10 Seal of Piercing Summons a seal in the room to help you in battle 11 Sanctify Sanctifies armour or weapons with Mitra's blessing 12 Holy Presence Bringing in Mitra's presence, you inflict your will upon others by your very presence alone 13 Consecrate Consecrating the room for Mitra's purpose, it becomes a holy room 14 Retribution You invoke Mitra's retribution upon anyone willing to take up arms against you 15 Seal of Warding Summons a seal in the room to help ward you against attacks 15 Warhorse Summon your trusty warhorse to aid you +-------------------------------------------------------------------+ +-------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: Mitra's Paladins are Her holy and devout warriors. Her last line
docs.text: Mitra's Paladins are Her holy and devout warriors. Her last line of defense against the evils that serve Her arch-nemesis Set. They take a more active role in the forms of spreading Mitra's word and ridding the world of evil influences. The Paladin guild provides a means to play in a more combat oriented guild than the somewhat passive Clerics. However, the road to being Mitra's ultimate warrior is not an easy one. You will be required to demonstrate your skills in a wide variety of areas. These areas include knowledge of all types of weapons and combat techniques, horsemanship, and reputation. For the Paladin able to meet all of the requirements to finally advance to Lord Paladin, the rewards will be well worth the effort. Paladins rise through righteous battle: worthy kills earn Paladin XP and guild levels advance automatically -- read 'palhelp advancement' for the details.

+-------------------------------------------------------------------+ The Paladin Monitor +-------------------------------------------------------------------+ One thing you probably noticed (if you have your monitor turned on; if not, type "mon") is that Paladin's have their own monitor that helps you keep track of things. If used correctly, this bar is very important. During battle you will be juggling various buffs, de-buffs and spells, and this gives you an at-a-glance view of what's going on. For example: [Javelin: 97% [D] [C] [G] [H] [R] [W] ] Legend: ^ (1) (2) (3) (4) (5) (6) (7) (1) = This is the current charge of your javelin, if you have one on you. The greater the charge, the greater the power. (2) = Indicator telling you if Divine Favor is active. (3) = Indicator telling you if Courage is active. (4) = Indicator telling you if Gift is active. (5) = Indicator telling you if Holy Presence is active. (6) = Indicator telling you if Retribution is active. (7) = Indicator telling you if Seal of Warding is active. Now, if any of these are inactive, you will instead get a red "X" as a visual indicator. Also note that Courage, Gift and Divine Favor can all be viewed and managed via the "buffs" command. +-------------------------------------------------------------------+ +-------------------------------------------------------------------+

_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_ Welcome to Paladins! _____________________________________________________________________ Paladins is a heavy theme-based solo guild that is a TON of fun to play! But, with that, there is just a lot going on that you'll need to know about. Specifically: "palhelp commands" - The important stuff. This doc will help you know what commands you have to work with. Any of those that you find there you can also "palhelp <command>" for more details. "palhelp monitor" - Paladins have a custom monitor that helps keep track of things for you. You'll definitely want to research this a bit. "palhelp warhorses" - High level Paladins have the ability to summon Warhorses to aid them. This document explains their basic abilities. Your Guild Wizard is Acer. Feel free to reach out to him with any feedback, questions or ideas! Have fun, Paladin! _____________________________________________________________________ _+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_+_

docs.title: Paladin code of conduct
docs.text: Paladin code of conduct 1: Obey the knights of higher station in all things. 2: Value the honour of our order above our personal honour, value our order above our lives. 3: Render aid to those in need as you would a fellow knight. Indulge the ignorant or witless even unto fault, but suffer no slur or insult to our honour from those who lack such excuse. 4: Never violate an oath you swear. Never swear an oath you can not keep. 5: Engage the enemy forthrightly that he may know the origin of his doom, set no ambush nor indulge in trickery to overcome a foe. 6: Give quarter to those who yield honorably. 7: Show great courage and bravery, but value your wisdom above all else. 8: Refuse no honourable truce or parley. 9: Do not break the laws of the realm thus to bring about the wrath of those who make this place run. 10: Suffer not to shelter among us any who would violate, ignore, or dishonour our Code.

+-------------------------------------------------------------------+ Paladin Warhorses +-------------------------------------------------------------------+ Paladin warhorses are an important thematic part of your game play experience with the guild. Warhorse commands: "horsename [name]" - Give your horse a name. "horsedesc" - Describe what people see when they look at your horse. "mount/dismount" - Mount and dismount your horse. This is important. See details below under hstatus "hitch/unhitch" - Hitch and unhitch your horse, if you want it to not follow you. "dismiss" - Send your horse away until you call it back later. "autoassist" - Enable your horse to attack your foes along side of you. "reign" - Reign in your horse's attacks, temporarily. "rear" - A fun emote. "clamp" - A fun emote. "hstatus" - Get the details of your horse's level and basic stats. Your horse gains level, just like you do. However, your horse only gains levels when you are mounted. The overall effectiveness of your horse is tied directly to it's level. It's important to try to level your horse. +-------------------------------------------------------------------+ +-------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: Priest of Set - Advancement
docs.text: Priest of Set - Advancement --------------------------- The Order advances those who spill blood in Set's name. Every worthy kill and every committed prayer bargain earns Priest XP, and your guild level (1 to 20) rises automatically when you have earned enough. Earning Priest XP: - Any NPC kill where you struck the killing blow, or dealt at least a tenth of the victim's health, awards Priest XP to everyone in the group who qualifies. - Tougher prey is worth more. Rewards taper when prey is more than five levels beneath you and reach nothing at fifteen levels beneath you. Bosses carry large bonuses. - Variety pays. Hunting the same spawn over and over decays the reward; ranging widely keeps it at full value. - A committed prayer that reserves HP or SP earns one Priest XP per ten points of its base reservation, with a minimum of 1 and maximum of 25. Prayers with no reservation earn none. Dispensation's added reserve does not increase this reward. Guild levels: - Levels advance on their own the moment you have earned enough XP. - Your guild level can never exceed your character level, and your combined guild levels can never exceed your character level. - Set grants nothing to those who walk in the light. XP earned while your alignment is good is banked, and the levels pop when you return to darkness - just as your prayers demand. - Guild level 20 is the summit of the priesthood. Commands: - 'cost' and 'advance guild' at the Church of Set report your progress. Prayers still unlock by guild level; see 'prayers'. Your record survives leaving the Order. Should you return, your standing is restored - to the truly evil.

docs.title: The Priests of Set do not actively seek to destroy good, but they are
docs.text: The Priests of Set do not actively seek to destroy good, but they are neutral at best. Most priests are evil, seeking power and the destruction of anything that would prevent them from obtaining that power. Set only lends his power to his followers that follow this evil path. Additionally, a priest may find that some or most of their beneficial prayers will only apply to other evil aligned players. At guild level 6, 'dispensation' petitions Set for a five-minute exception to the priest's own alignment restriction. It does not bypass target alignment or any other rule. During the exception, all direct and reserved HP and SP prayer costs, and all prayer cooldowns, are 25 percent higher. Dispensation itself has no HP or SP cost and has a ten-minute support cooldown.

docs.title: Prayers to Set require more than just a temporary cost. Set requires
docs.text: Prayers to Set require more than just a temporary cost. Set requires something greater, an extended bargain. This bargain "reserves" part of the priest's HP or SP for a few minutes. During this time, the health or energy isn't available for other prayers, and cannot be healed nor restored. In the "prayers" command, these show as the "HPR" and "SPR" costs, short for health and spell point reservations.

docs.title: A overview of basic commands available to Priests of Set:
docs.text: A overview of basic commands available to Priests of Set: priest Talk to other priests priests See a list of priests currently online priesthist View the Priest channel priesthelp View documentation on parts of the guild pbuffs Information about current HP/SP reservations prayers View powers available to priests dispensationTemporarily bypass the priest alignment restriction

docs.title: Priests are hearty warriors, but lack the ability wear plate armour.
docs.text: Priests are hearty warriors, but lack the ability wear plate armour. They can use almost all weapons, but seasoned priests usually focus on medium and large weapons. The priest prayer 'Scythe' summons a large, slashing, two-handed weapon.

docs.title: Often confused with cultists, misguided heretics, or crazed fanatics,
docs.text: Often confused with cultists, misguided heretics, or crazed fanatics, the Priests of Set dedicate their lives to a ambitious pursuit of power. They gain this power through a series of bargains with Set, the god of Chaos. These priests are terrifying in combat, mixing heavy-hitting blows with the divine dominance of their god. Priests typcially opt for scale or banded armor, forgoing full plate for the rush of battle. For weapons, priests vary from dual-wielding daggers to large blunt polearms. The guild has two main abilities that all initiates learn: Bolt and Mend. Bolt sacrifices some of the caster's own vitality to Set, which is rewarded with a devastating attack on a foe. Similarly, Mend uses some of the caster's vitality to restore health over time for a target. Trained priests learn other divine abilities, several of which empower Bolt and Mend. Priests value wisdom over all attributes so that they can strengthen their connection with Set. They also focus on charisma to get their way and to guide others, and constitution so that they can make more powerful bargains.

docs.title: Priests use both their vitality and their energy in the manifestation
docs.text: Priests use both their vitality and their energy in the manifestation of their prayers to Set. For vitality, priests receive: - 11 HP per Constitution For energy, Priests receive: - 5 SP per Wisdom - 3 SP per Charisma - 5 SP per every 2 Constitution

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Damage Absorption" The idea of this power is it allows the psionicist to alter his own aura to absorb kinetic energy. The power adds about 100 hit points which will fade over time, very quickly at low guild levels but slower and slower as guild level rises. Until this power wears off, both wounds and healing will affect these 'temporary' hit points first. However, the gradual loss of hit points will never cause you to go below the number you had when you invoked the power (damage from other sources WILL). SP Cost: Variable Guild Level: 3 Potential Points: 3 Command: absorption

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Adrenaline Control" The psionicist alters the flow of adrenaline in his own body to provide himself with short boosts of speed or strength. The psionicist gets a temporary increase in either strength or dexterity based on guild level. SP Cost: Variable Guild Level: 5 Potential Points: 2 Command: adrenalize <str/dex>

docs.title: This document will explain how to raise your stats, levels, and
docs.text: This document will explain how to raise your stats, levels, and powers. It is important that you understand what the different types of points represent. Experience Points: You get these for killing monsters, and use them to purchase everything except powers. Guild Experience Points: You get guild experience points for successfully using psionic powers. They are used to make you ELIGIBLE for advancement in guild levels. Potential Points: Also called purchase points, you earn these when you go up in guild level and use them to learn new powers by "realizing your potential." Physical stats: Strength: This determines your carrying capacity and is 80% of your stat related hand to hand damage. Constitution: Determines your hit points. Dexterity: This is 80% of your stat related dodging ability. Mental stats: Intelligence: This is 20% of your hand to hand stat related damage and provides 2.25 SP per stat point. Wisdom: This is 20% of your stat related dodging ability and provides 2.25 SP per stat point. Charisma: This determines your bonus/penalty when selling items and provides 1.5 SP per stat point. Guild Level: Your guild level ranges from 1-15 with each level requiring both guild experience points and regular experience points for advancement. Your guild level determines which powers are available for purchase and also increases the effectiveness of the vast majority of the powers you have. As your guild level goes up you should find all your powers lasting longer, doing more damage, having greater effect, etc as well as going up in SP cost to reflect their greater potential. Your psychic potential also depends on your guild level. All psionicists gain 7 potential points per guild level. Level: Your regular character level requires experience points and gold coins to raise. You have probably noticed by now that unlike all other uses of exp, attaining a new level requires an accumulated total. Levels are not 'bought' like guild levels and stats. In the Psionicist Guild your level does 2 things for you. First, the total amount of points in all your stats may not exceed 6 times your level +3. That is to say, if you are level 10, your stats cannot average greater than 13 for example. The second thing your level does is regulate how far you can advance your guild level. Your total guild level can never be greater than your regular level. This is to prevent 5th level characters running around with Ultrablast. Powers: You can learn powers and you can master powers. Learning new powers requires that your guild level is higher than the power's minimum and that you have enough potential points available to spend on the new power. Once you have learned a new power, you will immediately be able to begin using it. Once you have learned Power Mastery you may begin to master other powers. See the description of the Power Mastery power for details, but in general there are 3 levels of mastery to each power with the first level increasing the effectiveness of the power, the second level reducing the concentration time, and the third level making the power cheaper in SP to use.

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Animate Weapon" This allows a psionicist to cause a weapon to pick itself up and wield itself in battle! One of the most useful combat spells in the guild. It has a duration and hit points of the weapon dependent on the psionicist's guild level. The psionicist must stay in the same room but may perform other powers, attack the monster himself, or whatever. Another great advantage of this power is that it is not subject to weapon restrictions. A weapon not normally usable by the guild MAY be animated. If the animated weapon "dies", it will be permanently broken. SP Cost: 1 per second Guild Level: 11 Potential Points: 3 Command: animate <object (must be weapon)>

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Alter Aura" This allows the psionicist to do just what it says. The psionicist is displayed the alignment choices of demonic, evil, nasty, neutral, nice, good, and saintly and can pick which one to become. Of course future actions will immediately begin to alter this. As the psionicist guild does not depend on alignments at all this is largely a roleplaying power. However, it can be used to simultaneously wield magic items requiring wildly different alingments. Such is the power of the mind. It takes a flat 15 sp. SP Cost: 15 Guild Level: 3 Potential Points: 1 Command: paura <saintly/good/nice/neutral/nasty/evil/demonic>

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Awe" This temporarily increases the psionicist's personal magnetism by a large margin. Adds an amount of charisma dependent on guild level for a short length of time. It is mostly useful for obtaining better prices when selling treasure, but with some planning it is possible to immediately regenerate the cost of the spell before the effects wear off, thus increasing your spell points for a short while. You'll have to be fast and have a good plan to accomplish this, however. SP Cost: Variable Guild Level: 1 Potential Points: 1 Command: awe

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Ballistic Attack" This allows the psionicist to hurl a small object at superhigh speeds into a target. The object must contain within it a spark of mental energy implanted for the psionicist to contact. The guild shop sells rocks with this special modification made to them for 5 coins apiece. The power is the newbie psionicist attack power, doing a small amount of damage but being extremely cheap in SP and having a very low concentration time. Command: *THIS POWER HAS BEEN REMOVED*

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Banish" An expensive but powerful effect, the target of the power will be teleported away to otherdimensional space unless it resists the spell. Such strenous mental efforts cannot be maintained long, however, and the target will soon return to Darkwind. Make good use of the time provided to search, move on, or escape! SP Cost: Variable Guild Level: 12 Potential Points: 5 Command: pbanish <target>

docs.title: This document explains the way banishment works in the psionicist
docs.text: This document explains the way banishment works in the psionicist guild. It's based on a number of posts to the hipsi board in November 1996. This is subject to change according to the general consensus of the high psionicists. Banishment is the ultimate penalty that can be imposed upon a member of the guild. A banished player is cast out of the guild, and is prevented from joining any other guilds. As such, this isn't a step to be taken lightly. What's grounds for banishment in the psi guild? That's largely up to the high psionicists - they are free to set guild policies, so long as those policies do not contradict MUD rules. One thing that's sure to bring you up for banishment is knowingly abusing bugs, -especially- guild-related ones. The banishment process is as follows: First, a complaint is posted on the high psionicist board, by either the wizard guildmaster (in the case of bug abuse) or by a player hipsi (in the case of anything else). This complaint should give the players' name and the reason why banishment should be considered. Next, -before- any other posts on the matter, the player accused will have the chance to offer a defense. If he chooses not to, the wizard guildmaster will post to say so. After the defense or notice is posted, other hipsis will post a yes or no vote to the hipsi board. Banishment will occur if a) at least 1/4 of the active hipsis, with a minimum of 5 (or all, if there are fewer than 5 active hipsis) vote, and b) at least 2/3 of those votes are 'yes'. In the event of a banishment vote, the player in question will be offered the chance to leave the guild of their own accord through Grimtila first; otherwise, they will be banished. One last word: Do -not- attempt to buy votes. It is illegal, and it is the only way in which you can (and will) be banished without a vote.

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Inertial Barrier" A simple protective power. For a length of time dependent on the psionicist's guild level, the target receives a shielding of mental energy which will increase armor. SP Cost: Variable Guild Level: 4 Potential Points: 3 Command: barrier <target>

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Mental Beacon" Through the use of this power, the psionicist can temporarily anchor the Convergence to his current location. This will allow him or her to subsequently Teleport to that location. A psionicist may have only one beacon at a time, and may not create a second until the first one disappears. A beacon may be created to be either private or shared, and will last for several minutes - its duration is proportional to guild level. The cost for creating a private beacon is 100sp, and the cost for a shared beacon is 150sp. SP Cost: 100/150 Guild Level: 14 Potential Points: 4 Command: beacon, beacon here (to immediately dismiss an old beacon), or beacon shared [here] (to make a shared beacon)

docs.title: Here are a few considerations for those interested in joining
docs.text: Here are a few considerations for those interested in joining the Guild: - Take a look at the powers list and talk to members of the guild who have ones you're interested in. Start thinking about what you'll want to get. - Psionicist SP are based on Int, Wis, and Chr. Those stats are slightly cheaper in guild and the physical ones (str, con, dex) are slightly more expensive. Either buy up your mental stats early to have more SP, or buy up your physical stats at the Adventurer's Guild before you join (although the price difference isn't all that much). - Psionicists can use short and medium weapons and most forms of non-torso armor. Body armor is restricted to leather. Start looking around for good armor usable by the Guild and if you're going to specialize in a weapon, pick something usable by the guild and start earning spec bonuses now.

docs.title: This is a brief but thorough overview of the Psionicist Guild
docs.text: This is a brief but thorough overview of the Psionicist Guild aimed primarily at those interested in joining, but containing information for those simply curious as well. While mages harness the power of magic, Druids that of Nature, Clerics act as agents of the Divine, and Necromancers of Darkness, the Psionicist utilizes the power of his own mind. Psionicists' power comes from within themselves and is developed and expanded through exploring an individual's inner potential. This makes it hard to classify what the focus of the guild is. There are many directions open and each member chooses a different combination of abilities to develop. Some specialize in aiding others, some in the social aspects of expanded communication, some in avoiding combat and obstacles, others in smiting their enemies with mightly telepathic and/or telekinetic blows. The powers of the mind are wondrous and diverse.

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Blindness" Using this power, the psionicist can scramble a target's mind in such a way as to prevent the signals from the optic nerve from being interpreted. Effectively, this blinds the target. The duration is based on guild level. This ability is PK checked, as with any other attack. SP Cost: 20 Guild Level: 3 Potential Points: 1 Command: blind <targetname>

docs.title: The powers of a psionicist fall into 2 classes.  The first is
docs.text: The powers of a psionicist fall into 2 classes. The first is the effects and the second is the modifiers. The effects comprise about 80% of the 55+ powers and they affect various things on the mud. They allow the psionicist to teleport, strike enemies with mental blows, reduce the weight of objects, see and hear things far away, increase armor protection, alter their alignment, etc. The modifiers affect the other powers. They allow a psionicist to take a power that he or she already has and make it better. Make it do more damage, cost less SP, take less time to use, or last for a longer duration. Each psionicist gets a number of 'psionic potential' points with each guild level and uses these points to buy new powers. The powers cost different amounts of points depending on how powerful they are. The psionicist is free to buy many cheaper powers, a few expensive ones, or save the points to get more powers next level. How a psionicist spends these points determines what sort of character that psionicist becomes. The following is a mostly but not quite complete listing of Guild powers. A complete list along with full descriptions of each is available only to guild members. Recall Combat Teleport Enlighten Imprint Mindlink Dream Reality Create Image Precognition Suggestion Enhance Psionic Profile Judge Psychometry Clairvoyance Clairaudience Awe Crystalize Teleport Object Rejuvenation Channel Dual Mind Project Thought Reduce Weight Animate Weapon Probe Mental Blow Adrenaline Control Inflict Pain Double Pain Teleport Psionic Blast Thought Shield Inertial Barrier Psychic Splice Brainwave Power Mastery Psionic Prodigy Displace Limit Timeshift Banish Psychic Reserve Obscure Telekinetic Storm Emotion Control Ultrablast Telepathic Strike Repulsion Field

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Brainwave" This sends a mental wave through the room hitting everyone in its wake. It has a low efficiency, costing more than a psionic blast but doing less damage to each individual target but it will hit every monster (and player, except the psionicist) in the room. It does less damage to players and pets. SP Cost: Variable Guild Level: 9 Potential Points: 3 Command: bwave

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Channel" The channelling power allows a psionicist to send his own mental energy to others. Each use of the power will restore 10 spell points (but no hp) to another player. SP Cost: 15 Guild Level: 3 Potential Points: 2 Command: pchannel <target>

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Clairaudience" This places a "presence" in a room. The presence is like a monster which can neither attack nor be attacked and it will tell whatever it "hears" to the psionicist. Note: the presence IS visible so it is not a means of invading privacy. SP Cost: 30 Guild Level: 2 Potential Points: 1 Command: clairaudience <target> | endaudience (To end early)

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Clairvoyance" This allows the psionicist to see the location of a target within his mind. It displays the room description (including contents) of the target's location. SP Cost: 10 Guild Level: 2 Potential Points: 1 Command: clairvoyance <target>

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Clear Mind" This power will remove many traces of drunkenness from the mind of the target. It can be extremely useful when quick healing is desired, as more alcohol can be drunk immediately for its instant healing benefits. SP Cost: 20 Guild Level: 4 Potential Points: 2 Command: clearm <targetname>

_______________________________________________________________________________ "Combat Teleport" This allows the psionicist to teleport an object he is carrying into an enemy, resulting in damage from system shock. The weight of the object, and the skill of the psionicist determine the amount of damage inflicted. The item that is used in this attack will probably be destroyed, but there is a chance that it will survive and can be recovered when the target is killed. Note: The psionicist must be in combat with the intended target. SP Cost: Variable Guild Level: 5 Potential Points: 2 Command: ctel <object> OR tctel <object> at <target>
