docs.title: -- Priests of Set --------------------------------------------
docs.text: -- Priests of Set -------------------------------------------- The Priests of Set, also known as the Dark Clerics, are devoted to Set's old and absolute evil. They do not heal the world, defend the innocent, or pretend that their power is gentle. They make bargains with darkness, perform cruel rituals, and draw strength from obedience to their god. Set's priests are ritualists. Their powers include evil prayer, summoned darkness, curses, malign rites, soul-scratching torments, leprosy, destruction, feigned death, raising the dead, stealing alignment, and other works that are not meant for clean hands. Their ceremonial dagger is the center of their devotion and many of their rites. This guild is best suited for players who want a dark, religious, ritual-focused path. Expect an evil theme, hostile magic, and a relationship with Set that is not forgiving. The guild is not a neutral priesthood with a different color of robe; it is a commitment to a god of corruption, fear, death, and power. Joining begins at the Temple of Set. The temple does not welcome the good-hearted, and Set's doors judge those who approach. If you are accepted inside, the initiation is performed with the ceremonial dagger. New adventurers should understand the tone before taking that step: the Priests of Set are meant to be sinister, dangerous, and devoted. Useful starting notes: Guild name: Priests of Set / Dark Clerics Internal guild: Cleric_Set Newbie checkout: checkout set Theme: evil rituals, curses, darkness, death, devotion Ask a current Priest of Set, or an immortal, if you need help finding the temple or understanding whether this path fits your character.

docs.title: Cold Signal
docs.text: Cold Signal Cold Signal is passive thermal-control firmware unlocked with the torso-mounted Thermal Exchange Manifold. Older systems may still call this implant the Coolant System. It operates automatically while the implant is installed and the Street Samurai contract is active. It has no activation command and no SP, Edge, or Heat cost. What it does Cold Signal watches new Heat created by firmware. When a burst is large enough for the coolant loop to help, it vents part of that burst before the load reaches the Cortex. It also gives the platform more room to operate in redline before the monitor reports overheat. Cold Signal does not erase existing Heat, raise maximum Heat, replace ordinary cooling, or guarantee that a large burst cannot cause lockout. Its value is sustained thermal control: repeated routines leave less load for the Cortex to clear. What affects it Thermal Exchange Manifold grade and maintenance condition influence how much pressure the passive can handle. Damaged or fragmented hardware still functions but may vent less. When Cold Signal intervenes, the Cortex reports the amount of Heat removed from that burst. Checking the passive Samskills reports whether the Thermal Exchange Manifold is installed. Dashboard lists its grade, condition, and COLD SIGNAL state. Samstatus shows whether the passive is online, while monitor shows the resulting live Heat band. Thermal Purge uses the same manifold in reverse to drive a short-range flame projector. The attack creates Heat normally and does not disable Cold Signal. In an emergency, "thermalpurge vent" can dump all existing Heat immediately, including during thermal lockout, but the backwash inflicts severe integrity wear on both the Cortex OS and Thermal Exchange Manifold. Cold Signal and Overclock solve different problems. Cold Signal reduces incoming thermal pressure throughout a fight. Overclock temporarily raises the thermal ceiling by stressing the Cortex OS. Overdrive handles an engagement's opening Heat burst.

docs.title: Street Samurai Contracts
docs.text: Street Samurai Contracts A contract is Street Samurai membership. An active contract authenticates the Cortex OS, firmware commands, battle GXP, Edge and Heat, maintenance automation, the guild strain contribution, clinic coverage, and access to the private Cortex network. Contract states Primary means Street Samurai is the character's main guild. Secondary means another guild is primary while Street Samurai remains active. Both states can use Street Samurai progression, firmware, hardware, services, and the private network normally. Inactive means membership still exists, but equipped gear conflicts with a guild restriction. Firmware, battle GXP, Edge and Heat activity, maintenance automation, and the guild strain contribution pause until the conflict is removed. Installed implants and network membership remain in place. Diagnosing a paused contract Samstatus and dashboard identify the contract as inactive. Review recently equipped armour, weapons, or other restricted gear, remove the conflict, and check the status again. Inactivity is not caused by low integrity, high fragmentation, low health, or an unfinished quest. Leaving Leaving is different from becoming inactive. It removes membership and guild systems and permanently destroys installed Street Samurai signature implants. Unrelated cyberware is unaffected. Read samhelp leaving before making that decision. Use samwho to see the primary, secondary, or inactive state of visible connected operators. Use samhelp hardware for what remains installed and samhelp maintenance for problems that do not involve contract state.

docs.title: Street Samurai Cortex Fabrication
docs.text: Street Samurai Cortex Fabrication Location and access The Cortex Fabrication Bay is east of Rin Kade's private ripperdoc clinic. Only registered Street Samurai may enter or operate its fabrication table. Builders may enter for administration, but fabrication still requires an active Street Samurai contract. Cybernetics Salvaging and fabrication use the Cybernetics profession, with normal profession progression from 0 to 1000. Salvaging lower-grade hardware stops improving Cybernetics earlier than salvaging advanced hardware. Fabrication blueprints also have skill and Street Samurai guild-level requirements. Salvage Only extracted cyberware directly in your inventory may be salvaged. Kept, installed, equipped, unique, temporary, auto-loaded, contract-bound, and explicitly protected hardware is rejected. Use unkeep <hardware> first only when you intend to destroy a kept item. Salvaging is permanent. Use: salvage <hardware> salvage <hardware> confirm The first command previews and reserves the exact component yield for sixty seconds. The confirmation destroys that same hardware only after all recovered components can be deposited. Use reagents cyber or fabricate materials to see your persistent component balances. Fabrication Use: fabricate list fabricate inspect <recipe> fabricate <recipe> The initial blueprints create field and reinforced hardware repair kits. A failed blueprint or material transaction consumes nothing. Field repair Carry a fabricated kit and use repairkit <process_id>. Process IDs match dashboard and logs, such as cortex_os or targeting_suite. A field kit repairs 15 integrity and a reinforced kit repairs 30. Kits work on one installed Street Samurai process, cannot be used during combat, never exceed 100 integrity, and are consumed only after a successful repair. They do not clear fragmentation, patches, ICE, runtime faults, or Heat.

docs.title: Street Samurai Firmware
docs.text: Street Samurai Firmware The Cortex OS hosts every Street Samurai routine. Firmware needs an active contract, an installed Cortex OS, the required Guild Level, enough SP, acceptable Heat, and any paired signature implant. Edge is normally an optional amplifier rather than an activation requirement. Samskills reports readiness; samhelp <routine> explains the command's intended use and interactions. Execution cycle Active routines have no separate long cooldowns. A successful activation uses the shared Cortex execution cycle and Darkwind's normal damage or support action pacing. Persistent effects generally cannot be activated again while their existing instance remains online. Active and passive firmware Active firmware is deployed with a command. Passive firmware comes online automatically when its Guild Level and required hardware are present. Passive systems appear in samskills even though they do not have activation commands. Dashboard and the combat monitor show whether many of those systems are active or ready. Notable interactions Threat Scan reports a target's armour and resistances. Ripcut consumes its lock for a stronger armour-piercing strike. Photon Lance calibrates its wavelength from the lock, Micro-Missile Swarm adds a guided missile, and deployed Monowire reads the lock without consuming it. Most active routines automatically route one available Edge into a stronger version of their normal effect. Damaging Photon Lance and Micro-Missile Swarm executions also generate Edge. Specialized routines can route more or spend it only when a particular response occurs. Overclock creates temporary thermal headroom and improves movement and attack response, but every activation stresses the Cortex OS. Cortex Rank improves its duration, avoidance response, and thermal headroom. Armor Weave turns Dermal Plating into persistent shielding whose strength and thermal load follow Guild Level, Cortex Rank, grade, and condition. When the shield collapses it creates another Heat burst and produces Edge. Smart Smoke and Jammer Field solve different defensive problems. Smart Smoke is personal physical cover: it strongly disrupts ranged attacks aimed at the operator and offers only modest protection in melee. It can be deployed before a fight. Jammer Field is active battlefield control: it suppresses the outgoing damage of hostiles fighting the operator or nearby party members and periodically desynchronizes one attack swing. It protects the team by degrading hostiles rather than making the operator harder to target. Signal Shroud supplies the operator's passive dodge telemetry. Jammer Node instead reserves additional SP bandwidth for interference firmware. Edge adds a real point of Smart Smoke cover. In Jammer Field it strengthens suppression, accelerates the desynchronization pulse, and extends field duration. Ghoststep and Zero Signal solve different pressure states. Ghoststep is an in-fight reposition: it keeps the primary target engaged, drops secondary attackers and hunts, and arms the Reflex Lattice to improve avoidance against the next incoming attack sequence. Zero Signal is the full escape routine: it erases current combat and hunts, rejects remote tracking or scrying locks, and uses the Ghost Circuit to mask a limited number of attempts to start combat again. Ghost Circuit grade establishes that reacquisition capacity, while Cortex Rank expands it over continued progression. Monowire deploys as an unbreakable weapon for thirty minutes. It adjusts to the operator's combat progression and remains useful with different weapon loadouts. Threat Scan guides additional armour-piercing cuts, monowire edge arms a stronger breach, and Second Spur can join that breach. At CR200, cyberblade reconfigures the Monofilament Spur into the Ronin Edge, a temporary primary weapon governed by Cortex throughput, blade grade, and maintenance. Its Cortex Sever route executes at a regular hit cadence. Threat Scan can guide the Sever through armour, a badly wounded target exposes a stronger execution line, and the first damaging Sever against each opponent generates Edge. Cyberblade retract collapses the weapon early. Required hardware Every routine depends on the Cortex OS. Neonwake, Snap Cut, Jolt, Overclock, Ripcut, and the Ronin-sama Kernel use the Cortex as primary hardware. Other firmware also requires the following paired implant: Threat Scan - Photon Targeting Suite Photon Lance - Photon Targeting Suite Armor Weave - Dermal Plating Smart Smoke - Signal Shroud Ghoststep - Reflex Lattice Trauma Buffer - Trauma Buffer Node Monowire - Monofilament Spur Ronin Edge - Monofilament Spur at Cortex Rank 200 Jammer Field - Jammer Node Micro-Missile Swarm - Dorsal Tempest Driver Nanomend - Repair Coprocessor Predictive Sight - Predictive Coprocessor Cold Signal - Thermal Exchange Manifold Thermal Purge - Thermal Exchange Manifold Zero Signal - Ghost Circuit Second Spur - Second Spur Overdrive - Overdrive Module Chrome Tempest - Dorsal Tempest Driver Some optional hardware strengthens a routine without being required. Blade hardware supports Snap Cut and Ripcut; reflex hardware supports Jolt and Overclock. Samskills reports only missing required hardware, so use dashboard or implants when checking optional enhancements. What changes effectiveness Hardware grade improves the firmware paired with that implant. Cortex Rank gradually improves host throughput. Character capabilities and current Heat shape combat routines where relevant. Low integrity or high fragmentation weakens the affected hardware and poor Cortex condition can influence the entire platform. These factors work together, but maintenance never makes a routine completely useless. Failures and readiness Read the command's failure message first. Samstatus checks contract, Edge, Heat, and the Cortex cycle. Samskills checks Guild Level and required hardware. Dashboard checks the Cortex, implant condition, active effects, strain, and maintenance alerts. An invalid target, an existing copy of an effect, normal room safeguards, or insufficient SP can also reject a command.

docs.title: Street Samurai: First Deployment
docs.text: Street Samurai: First Deployment 1. Verify the installation Joining installs a prototype-grade Cortex OS automatically. Run dashboard and confirm that the contract is active, the Cortex OS is online, and no alert requires attention. A normal new member does not need samrepair. Neonwake is available immediately. Run neonwake to wake every installed implant into a carried lighting mesh if darkness prevents you from seeing a room; run it again to switch the mesh off. 2. Review available firmware Run samskills to see every routine, its Guild Level, resource use, and current readiness. READY means the routine is available. A red HARDWARE status means its required implant is missing. Use samhelp <routine> before deploying unfamiliar firmware and samhelp firmware for the complete implant map. 3. Learn the combat loop Snap Cut produces Edge whenever it deals damage, making it a dependable way to establish momentum. Jolt offers lightning damage and becomes another source of Edge while the Cortex is running hot. At GL2, Threat Scan reports a foe's armour and resistances and establishes a lock that strengthens the next Ripcut. A scanned Ripcut consumes that lock and produces Edge when it lands. When Edge is available, most active routines automatically route one point into a stronger version of their normal effect. The base routine still works at zero Edge. Watch for the shell's EDGE ROUTE message to see when damage, duration, shielding, healing, or control strength has been amplified. Most successful active routines add Heat and all active routines use the shared Cortex execution cycle. Redline can improve some offensive firmware, but reaching the thermal ceiling locks Heat-producing routines until the system cools. Overclock adds temporary headroom without producing Heat, at the cost of wear to the Cortex OS. Watch the live state with monitor or samstatus. 4. Build the loadout Rin Kade operates the restricted clinic beyond the contract office. Engage Rin to inspect every current and future unlock. The catalog shows the implant slot, grade, strain, and exact price before confirmation. Active members pay for hardware but not guild-covered installation, extraction, or signature repair services. 5. Maintain the hardware Combat damage can wear down implant integrity, while firmware use can add fragmentation. Dashboard names the affected process and shows whether to use defrag, patch, purge, or reboot. Rin repairs physical integrity. Use logs when you need to understand how a process reached its current state. 6. Use the network Samwho lists connected Street Samurai, samchat transmits on the private Cortex network, and samhist reviews recent transmissions. Samhelp network explains the available syntax and visibility rules. If a routine will not start, read its failure message first. Then check samstatus for contract, Edge, Heat, and the Cortex cycle; check samskills for Guild Level and hardware; and check dashboard for implant or maintenance problems.

docs.title: Street Samurai Hardware
docs.text: Street Samurai Hardware Every Street Samurai routine depends on one or more signature implants. The Cortex OS hosts the platform and is installed automatically when joining. Rin Kade and Othra Veyr sell the remaining signature lines as they unlock from GL2 through GL14. Integrated weapon systems The right-eye Photon Targeting Suite supports Threat Scan and unlocks Photon Lance at GL4. The left-shoulder Dorsal Tempest Driver becomes available at GL8 for Micro-Missile Swarm and later coordinates Chrome Tempest. The torso Thermal Exchange Manifold provides Cold Signal and unlocks Thermal Purge at GL11. Older names such as Targeting Suite, Tempest Driver, and Coolant System remain valid when speaking with the Cortex or a ripperdoc. Choosing hardware Engage a ripperdoc and inspect the signature catalog before buying. Each entry shows its paired implant, internal location, strain, grade, Guild Level requirement, and exact price. Buying places the hardware in your inventory; installation is a separate confirmed procedure. The clinic refuses an implant when its location conflicts or its strain would exceed current capacity. Street Samurai signature hardware remains contract-locked: no ripperdoc can install it in someone who is not a registered Street Samurai. Grades The grade order from weakest to strongest is Prototype, Street, Military, and Ghost. Prototype is available first, with Street at GL7, Military at GL10, and Ghost at GL13. A specific implant's own unlock can require a later Guild Level. Higher grades improve their paired firmware and built-in equipment benefits, resist accumulated physical wear more effectively, and usually consume more strain. Grade does not replace maintenance: even exceptional hardware should be repaired and defragmented when its condition declines. Strain and slots Installed cyberware consumes strain capacity and occupies an internal location. Character level, remort progress, and the Street Samurai contract all contribute to capacity. Reaching Ronin-sama at Guild Level 16 provides a substantial final capacity surge for installing new hardware or upgrading an existing implant. Use cyberware or implants to review the complete internal layout and live strain limit; dashboard shows Street Samurai implant load and condition. Inspecting the loadout Use implants for all installed internal equipment, cyberware for available and occupied implant locations, dashboard for Street Samurai grade, integrity, fragmentation, and runtime state, and samskills for missing required hardware. Samhelp firmware contains the complete routine-to-implant map.

docs.title: Street Samurai
docs.text: Street Samurai Street Samurai are cybernetic combat specialists whose Cortex OS links signature implants into one platform. They create and spend Edge, manage Heat, maintain installed hardware, and unlock firmware through sixteen guild levels and long-term Cortex Rank progression. The guild rewards players who enjoy a technical melee toolkit with active firmware, cyberware upkeep, resource decisions, and a private Cortex network. Joining installs the starter Cortex OS and begins a Street Samurai contract. Current roster status: OPEN Useful starting references: samhelp start First-deployment checklist samskills Firmware unlocks and readiness samstatus Combat resources and hardware state samxp Guild Level, Cortex Rank, and GXP help guilds street_samurai The public contract office is near Moongate Plaza. Read the contract and maintenance help before accepting it; leaving permanently destroys installed Street Samurai signature hardware.

docs.title: Leaving the Street Samurai
docs.text: Leaving the Street Samurai Leaving removes the Street Samurai contract, command soul, Guild Level and Cortex progression access, Edge and Heat, guild strain contribution, firmware authentication, active guild effects, maintenance automation, clinic coverage, private network membership, and all installed Street Samurai signature cyberware. What remains Every installed Street Samurai signature implant is permanently decommissioned and destroyed when membership ends. It is not extracted into inventory, dropped, refunded, or converted into salvage. Unrelated cyberware remains installed. Uninstalled hardware carried in inventory also remains yours. Only installed implants identified as Street Samurai signature hardware are destroyed. After leaving Former members can use an ordinary staffed ripperdoc for unrelated cyberware. Rin's contract-covered service and the private Cortex network require active membership. Rejoining uses the normal enrollment procedure and installs a fresh intake Cortex OS; previously installed signature implants do not survive the severed contract. Inactive is different An inactive contract preserves membership and usually clears after conflicting equipment is removed. Do not leave merely to solve an inactive state. Check samstatus, remove the conflicting gear, and review samhelp contract first. Leaving permanently destroys every installed Street Samurai signature implant. Review your loadout before severing the contract.

docs.title: Street Samurai Maintenance
docs.text: Street Samurai Maintenance Maintenance applies only to Street Samurai signature hardware. It does not add integrity wear or fragmentation to ordinary cyberware or another guild's equipment. Integrity Integrity is physical implant condition. Incoming damage, severe thermal events, and specific high-load firmware can accumulate wear. Dashboard begins warning before output is affected. Below 50% integrity, the paired routine's damage, duration, mitigation, or other output is reduced, but the hardware continues to function. The Cortex OS is shared by the entire platform, so poor Cortex integrity can influence routines that also use another implant. Higher hardware grades are more durable and lose visible integrity more slowly under comparable wear. Rin Kade restores signature hardware integrity for active members. Fragmentation Fragmentation is firmware disorder created by routine use. Above 50%, it reduces the affected process's effectiveness and produces warnings. Use defrag <process> to clean one implant or defrag all to service the entire loadout. Defrag does not repair physical integrity. Alerts and actions Dashboard names the process and the required response. PATCH READY uses patch <process>. ICE INTRUSION uses purge <process>. RUNTIME FAULT uses reboot <process>. These commands also accept all, but each addresses only its own issue type. Logs [process] shows recent changes and their causes. Maintenance commands cannot run while the contract is inactive, and some require you to be out of combat. A Repair Coprocessor can perform limited automatic stabilization in severe cases, but it does not replace clinic repairs or routine defragmentation. Repair workflow Start with dashboard. Use the named maintenance command for fragmentation, patches, ICE, or faults. If integrity is damaged, visit Rin Kade, engage him, and choose repair for one implant or all damaged signature hardware. Field and reinforced hardware repair kits can instead restore one process while away from the clinic. Use repairkit <process_id>; kits cannot be used during combat and do not affect fragmentation, patches, ICE, faults, or Heat. Use logs afterward if you need to confirm what changed. Samrepair is different from all of these tools. It recovers a corrupt or incomplete guild installation and is not needed after a normal join.

docs.title: Street Samurai Combat Monitor
docs.text: Street Samurai Combat Monitor Using the monitor The standard monitor command can print HP, SP, and Cortex combat state when your HP or SP changes. Use monitor on for the compact display, monitor bar for resource bars, or monitor off to disable automatic updates. The hp and . commands always request a current snapshot manually. The Cortex line begins with the cortexmesh shell prompt. It shows current and maximum Edge, current and maximum Heat, the live thermal state, and compact process indicators. PAUSED means the contract is inactive. UNMANAGED means the Cortex OS is missing. LOCKOUT means Heat-producing firmware cannot run until the system cools. Process indicators A green {X} means a process is online, active, or ready. A red {X} means it is offline, unavailable, or spent. The indicators are: OC - Overclock is currently running. OD - Overdrive readiness is available for the current engagement. AW - Armor Weave shielding is active. SM - Your Smart Smoke is active in the current room. TB - Trauma Buffer is delaying incoming damage. MW - Monowire is deployed; this does not show whether a breach is armed. RE - The CR200 Ronin Edge cyberblade is deployed. JF - Your Jammer Field is active in the current room. PS - Predictive Sight is active. GS - A Ghoststep avoidance frame is armed. ZS - Zero Signal is active. TS - Threat Scan has at least one active target lock. OD represents readiness rather than a persistent buff. It turns red after Overdrive has handled the opening Heat burst for the current engagement. TS does not identify which target is locked; Threat Scan output and combat messages provide that context. Room-local indicators turn red after you leave the room containing their effect. Refresh timing The line refreshes when the normal HP or SP monitor redraws. Heat may cool, a lock may expire, or an effect may end between redraws. Use hp or . for an immediate reading, samstatus for a detailed local state query, and dashboard for implant condition and alerts. Screen-reader mode replaces the compact abbreviations with complete process names and status sentences. Turning the automatic monitor off does not disable Street Samurai resources or firmware; it only stops automatic display updates.

docs.title: Street Samurai Cortex Network
docs.text: Street Samurai Cortex Network The Cortex network is restricted to authenticated Street Samurai members. Its messages, emotes, media shares, history, login notices, and logout notices are not sent to nonmembers or external channel bridges. An inactive contract still retains membership and network access. Transmitting samchat <message> sends a normal transmission. samchat :<emote> uses channel-emote syntax. esamchat <message> uses narrative egossip-style syntax. The channel supports the same speech, emote, and shared-media forms as gossip. Sending while reception is muted restores the channel automatically. Display color Use color street_samurai to select the foreground, background, and effect used for Cortex network traffic. This preference applies when sending, receiving, or reviewing newly recorded transmissions through samhist. History and operators samhist shows recent Cortex transmissions; supply a line count when you need more or less than the normal view. samwho runs a shell-style listing of visible connected members. Invisible operators remain hidden when the viewer would not normally be able to see them. samwho fields samwho reports name, Guild Level, Cortex Rank, Edge, Heat, strain, contract state, and current activity. PRIMARY and SECONDARY are active membership states. INACTIVE means guild systems are paused by an equipment conflict. SIGNAL LOST, IDLE, IN COMBAT, and COMMS MUTED describe connection or activity rather than hardware condition. Troubleshooting If you can read but not transmit, check silence effects and normal channel restrictions. If the channel was muted, sending samchat restores reception. Samhist confirms whether a message reached the network; samwho confirms which visible operators are currently connected.

docs.title: Overdrive
docs.text: Overdrive Overdrive is passive burst-control firmware unlocked at Street Samurai Guild Level 14. It requires the right-ear Overdrive Module and has no activation command, SP cost, Edge cost, or Heat cost. Opening burst control When firmware first tries to add Heat during an engagement, Overdrive can automatically vent most or all of that opening burst. Once it intervenes, the profile is spent for the current engagement. Samstatus and the combat monitor report whether Overdrive is ready or spent. Overdrive reduces one incoming Heat request. It does not raise maximum Heat, accelerate normal cooling, remove Heat already present, or prevent all later lockout risk. If part of the burst remains, Cold Signal can still reduce that remainder before it reaches the Cortex. What affects it Hardware grade determines how aggressively the opening profile can vent, while integrity and fragmentation affect its reliability. The module also provides passive intelligence and spell-point hardware benefits even after its Heat profile has been spent. Using it well Overdrive gives an engagement a cleaner opening, so it is most valuable when the first successful routine would otherwise create substantial Heat. Watch OD on the monitor or overdrive in samstatus, then plan the rest of the fight around ordinary Heat, Cold Signal, and available headroom.

docs.title: Street Samurai
docs.text: Street Samurai Street Samurai are cybernetic combat specialists whose Cortex OS links signature implants into one fighting platform. Their combat rhythm is to read the encounter, create Edge, spend it on decisive routines, and manage Heat before the Cortex enters thermal lockout. Your first steps The public contract office is east of Fountain Court near Moongate Plaza. Joining installs a prototype-grade Cortex OS automatically. The secured clinic beyond the office is open to members and wizards; engage Rin Kade there to inspect, purchase, install, extract, or repair signature hardware. Contract services are covered for active members, but new hardware still costs coins. A new member should run dashboard, samskills, and samhelp start. Dashboard shows the contract, resources, strain, installed implants, and maintenance state. Samskills shows what is unlocked and whether required hardware is present. Samrepair is only for a damaged or incomplete guild installation; it is not part of normal onboarding. Progression and combat Street Samurai earn GXP from combat and boss victories recognized by Darkwind's shared battle progression, not by repeating firmware commands. Guild Level unlocks routines and hardware through GL16. Cortex Rank continues through CR200 and gradually improves the host OS after Guild Level stops advancing. Snap Cut is the most reliable early source of Edge. Threat Scan prepares a target for Ripcut and later interacts with Monowire. Most active routines add Heat when they succeed. Available Edge is automatically routed into stronger versions of most routine effects, but an empty Edge pool never blocks the base routine. Overclock trades Cortex wear for temporary thermal headroom. Use the combat monitor, samstatus, or dashboard to decide when to press an advantage and when to cool down. Where to look Use samhelp start for onboarding, samhelp commands for the full index, samhelp resources for Edge and Heat, samhelp firmware for routine and hardware relationships, and samhelp maintenance when dashboard reports a problem. Samhelp <routine> explains any active firmware command.

docs.title: Street Samurai Prices
docs.text: Street Samurai Prices Hardware purchases Rin Kade and Othra Veyr show the authoritative live price for every unlocked signature implant. Engage the ripperdoc, open the Street Samurai catalog, choose an implant and grade, and review its slot, strain, Guild Level, hardware price, and separate procedure quote before confirming anything. No single Street Samurai signature implant costs more than 100,000 coins in the guild catalog. Earlier implants and lower grades scale below that ceiling. The contract covers services, not purchases: buying hardware still costs the listed amount and places the item in your inventory. Installation, extraction, and repair An active Street Samurai contract waives installation and extraction fees with Rin Kade in the guild clinic. Rin also repairs Street Samurai signature hardware integrity without a labor charge. A paused or former contract does not receive those benefits. Othra's public clinic charges 10,000 coins per point of strain to install and 5,000 coins per point of strain to extract, with a one-point minimum for either procedure. His dialogue always shows the exact fee and requires confirmation before surgery. Installation still requires an open internal location and enough strain capacity. Extraction returns the hardware to inventory. Ripperdocs do not perform procedures during combat.

docs.title: Street Samurai Progression
docs.text: Street Samurai Progression Street Samurai have 16 Guild Levels and 200 Cortex Ranks. GXP comes from combat and boss victories recognized by Darkwind's shared battle progression. Repeating firmware commands does not award GXP. Guild Level and Cortex Rank Use samxp or gscore to see Guild Level, Cortex Rank, current GXP, and the next rank requirement. Through the early ranks, Cortex Rank also advances Guild Level. If a character-level requirement temporarily blocks an early Guild Level, earned GXP remains banked and advancement resumes when the requirement is met. After GL16, Guild Level remains fixed while Cortex Rank continues through CR200. Later Cortex Ranks take more sustained combat progress. The host OS continues gaining bounded throughput improvements across that full progression, but hardware grade, character capabilities, Heat, and maintenance still matter independently. Dashboard reports the current Cortex throughput. Cortex Rank 200 Reaching CR200 grants final bladeware authorization. With an installed Cortex OS and Monofilament Spur, cyberblade deploys the Ronin Edge as a temporary primary weapon. This is a Cortex Rank capstone, not another Guild Level. Use samhelp cyberblade for its operating requirements and combat interactions. Unlocks Firmware and signature implants unlock from GL1 through GL16. Prototype hardware is available first, followed by street grade at GL7, military grade at GL10, and ghost grade at GL13. The paired routine's Guild Level can still delay a specific implant even when its grade is otherwise available. When progress seems stalled Check samxp for the current requirement, confirm the contract is active, and continue fighting opponents that the shared battle system recognizes as appropriate progression. Samskills shows the next routine unlock; Rin Kade's catalog shows hardware that is available now and future contract unlocks.

docs.title: Street Samurai Resources
docs.text: Street Samurai Resources Edge Edge represents positioning, telemetry, and openings created during a fight. It is a temporary combat resource, not experience. The monitor, samstatus, and dashboard always show the current amount and live maximum. An installed Second Spur can expand that maximum. Snap Cut produces Edge whenever it deals damage. A Threat Scan lock lets a damaging Ripcut pierce armour, deal additional damage, consume the lock, and produce Edge. Jolt can produce Edge while the Cortex is already under elevated thermal load. A damaging Photon Lance or Micro-Missile Swarm salvo also produces Edge. The Ronin-sama Kernel can establish Edge when a new attacker enters its telemetry. Most active routines automatically route one available Edge as an optional bonus. That bonus improves what the routine already does: damage, duration, shielding, healing, or control strength. The shell reports an EDGE ROUTE when this happens. No ordinary routine requires Edge to perform its base effect. Smart Smoke routes Edge into one additional point of personal cover and a longer deployment. Jammer Field routes Edge into stronger hostile-output suppression, a faster attack-desynchronization pulse, and additional duration. These bonuses remain distinct: Smoke protects its operator, while Jammer degrades hostiles fighting the operator's nearby team. Ghoststep repositions without Edge, keeps the primary engagement, sheds secondary pressure, and arms a short-lived avoidance frame. Its follow-up can route up to two Edge into the primary target; the full two-Edge route makes the cut armour-piercing. Zero Signal uses available Edge differently: one routed Edge extends concealment and adds another blocked combat reacquisition attempt. Armor Weave creates Edge when its shielding is fully depleted. Predictive Sight commits Edge only when it actually prevents damage and can refund it on a particularly strong response. A deployed Monowire produces Edge on its first confirmed cut against each opponent. The command monowire edge deliberately spends Edge to arm the next confirmed hit as an armour-piercing breach; it never spends Edge without that command. Chrome Tempest works with an empty pool and converts any accumulated Edge into a stronger finishing sequence. Tempest stabilize still reserves one Edge specifically to avoid thermal lockout. Heat Heat is the Cortex's live thermal load. The monitor labels the current band as CLEAN, REDLINE, OVERHEAT, or LOCKOUT. Some offensive routines become more effective outside the clean band, but reaching the current thermal ceiling causes thermal lockout. While locked, routines that would create Heat cannot start until the system cools far enough to authenticate them again. Redline and lockout Most active routines add Heat only after they produce their intended effect. Rejected commands, missing targets, and failed validation do not create thermal load. Active routines have no individual cooldowns; they use a short, shared Cortex execution cycle alongside Darkwind's normal action pacing. Heat clears automatically over time and cools faster outside combat. Overclock does not add Heat; it temporarily raises the thermal ceiling while placing wear on the Cortex OS. Cold Signal reduces some incoming thermal bursts, and Overdrive can absorb the opening burst of an engagement. These systems provide headroom but do not make Heat irrelevant. At Guild Level 11, "thermalpurge vent" provides an emergency escape from accumulated Heat and thermal lockout. It clears the entire thermal load at once, but the forced backwash causes severe integrity wear to both the Cortex OS and Thermal Exchange Manifold. It is an emergency trade, not routine cooling. Armor Weave and Monowire report their applied thermal load when used. Armor Weave's Heat follows the shield charge it creates and its collapse adds another burst when the shielding is fully consumed. Chrome Tempest normally drives the Cortex to lockout; tempest stabilize uses the sequence's reserved Edge to stop just short of that shutdown. Reading the system Use samstatus for a compact resource and cycle report, dashboard for full hardware diagnostics, and samhelp mon for the combat-monitor legend. If a routine says the system is thermally locked, stop issuing Heat-producing firmware and allow the live Heat value to fall.

docs.title: Ronin-sama Kernel
docs.text: Ronin-sama Kernel Ronin-sama Kernel is the passive Street Samurai capstone unlocked at Guild Level 16. It uses the brain-mounted Cortex OS and has no activation command, SP cost, Edge cost, or Heat cost. Cortex ascension Reaching the capstone reconfigures the installed Cortex OS to ghost grade. The kernel remains active while a GL16 Street Samurai has that ghost-grade Cortex installed and the contract is active. Dashboard identifies RONIN KERNEL as the Cortex process state. Engagement telemetry When a new attacker enters the engagement, the kernel reads the hostile telemetry and attempts to establish Edge if capacity is available. It can also answer incoming swings with an automatic slashing counterattack. These are passive responses; no command is required. Keeping it effective The counter protocol benefits from the operator's combat development and the Cortex's firmware effectiveness. Continued Cortex Rank improves both the counter protocol's response rate and the force of its return strike. Poor Cortex integrity or fragmentation can make the response less dependable, so the capstone does not remove the need for maintenance. Cortex Rank continues after the kernel comes online. Use samxp for rank progress, dashboard for throughput and Cortex condition, and samhelp maintenance when the host OS reports a problem.

docs.title: Second Spur
docs.text: Second Spur Second Spur is passive off-hand firmware unlocked at Street Samurai Guild Level 13. It requires the left-hand Second Spur implant and has no activation command, SP cost, Edge cost, or Heat cost. Expanded Edge capacity While the implant is online, it raises maximum Edge above the normal cap. Better grades can provide additional headroom when the spur is well maintained. The monitor, samstatus, dashboard, and samwho all report the resulting live maximum rather than assuming a fixed value. Off-hand cutting line Second Spur gives Chrome Tempest an additional cutting line. Stronger, well-maintained hardware can contribute more to the sequence. The spur must be installed and online when Tempest begins; installing it after the sequence starts does not alter that activation. The second line also joins an armed Monowire Edge breach. It does not arm the breach itself: deploy Monowire, use monowire edge, and let the next confirmed hit trigger both lines. Hardware benefits The implant adds +4/+6/+8/+10 damage stat and +2/+3/+4/+5 critical stat from prototype through ghost grade. Every confirmed weapon hit can invoke an independent off-hand cut. Better grades increase its chance from 11% to 20% and reduce its cooldown from 12 seconds to 6 seconds. The cut deals armour-piercing slash damage that scales with your level, Street Samurai Guild Level, hardware grade, Cortex power, and firmware effectiveness. A damaging cut generates 1 Edge. If another valid enemy is already attacking you, the filament cleaves that enemy for half damage. This proc has no SP, Edge, or Heat cost. Low Second Spur or Cortex integrity and high Second Spur fragmentation weaken the cut, Edge-cap bonus, and Chrome Tempest contribution without taking the spur completely offline. Use dashboard and implants to inspect it.

docs.title: Call to Arms - teamwork skill
docs.text: Call to Arms - teamwork skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Although many swashbucklers are loners, all are bound to each other by mutual respect. When swashbucklers come together to fight as a team, each becomes more effective than he would be individually. The more swashbucklers gather, the greater the improvement when they fight in tandem. When a group of swashbucklers gather, one of them, usually the leader, will issue a call to arms. Each swashbuckler who hears the call will join in, both adding to and sharing in the benefits of the call. Swashbucklers who cannot give the call to arms due to inexperience can still add to the effect of others' calls, while benefitting themselves. Once the call is made, the effect will continue for the duration even if the group disperses. The effect of the original call to arms can be renewed periodically in a smaller group, as long as it is done before the effect expires. GL: 5 SP: 30 command: scall duration: long

docs.title: Called Shot - blade technique
docs.text: Called Shot - blade technique ------------------------------------------------------------ By making a called shot, a swashbuckler can strike at a weak point in his opponent's armor, or at an unprotected area of the opponent's body. Achieving this precise aim requires both a steady hand and knowledge of weaknesses. These well- placed strikes, when they land, will cause greater damage to the enemy. Damage increases at each character-level bracket: +12 below Hero, +15 at Hero, +18 at Legend, +21 at Epic, and +24 at Mythic. GL: 5 SP: 3 / proc, reduced by Flow command: calledshot duration: technique mode

docs.title: Calledshot - Guild Level 5
docs.text: Calledshot - Guild Level 5 By making a called shot, a swashbuckler can strike at a weak point in his opponent's armor, or at an unprotected area of the opponent's body. Achieving this precise aim requires both a steady hand and knowledge of weaknesses. These well- placed strikes, when they land, will cause greater damage to the enemy. SP: 3 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Chance of bracket-scaled damage on hit: +12 below Hero, +15 at Hero, +18 at Legend, +21 at Epic, and +24 at Mythic.

docs.title: Candle - utility skill
docs.text: Candle - utility skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Being the intrepid explorers that they are, swashbucklers usually carry candles in their belt pouches in case they find themselves exploring a dark place. You can light one of your candles with this command. GL: 1 SP: 20 command: candle duration: very long

docs.title: Challenge - offensive trick
docs.text: Challenge - offensive trick ------------------------------------------------------------ A swashbuckler can deliver a challenge in an insulting manner. If the foe accepts, he will refuse to run away until he feels his honor is satisfied. Generally this happens at the end of the fight, or after a short time regardless. A challenged foe can also be pressed with the press skill while they remain your current opponent. GL: 4 SP: 40 command: challenge <target> (defaults to opponent if in combat) duration: short see also: press, flair

docs.title: Charm - utility skill
docs.text: Charm - utility skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Swashbucklers tend to be charming or impressive by nature, but when they actually exert effort, their poise and presence increases even further. The swashbuckler can boost his charisma by a few points for a short time. GL: 4 SP: 15 command: charm duration: short

docs.title: Choose Weapon - utility skill
docs.text: Choose Weapon - utility skill ------------------------------------------------------------ When a swashbuckler nears the end of his training, he often chooses a pair of blades that have served him particularly well through his training. He will become so attuned to those blades that they almost seem like extensions of himself. Thereafter, whenever he uses his chosen blades, he will fight with more skill when using swashbuckler techniques. The choice may be made only once per boot and of course both weapons must be blades. The swashbuckler is so attuned to the chosen blades that even other blades of the same kind will not be as good in his hands as the two specifically chosen by him. GL: 12 SP: 0 command: choose [main|secondary] <weapon> duration: remainder of uptime

docs.title: Counter - blade technique
docs.text: Counter - blade technique ------------------------------------------------------------ As a swashbuckler increases in skill, he is able to exploit openings left by an opponent's attack to strike a quick counterattack. While using this skill, the swashbuckler will counter a percentage of incoming attacks. This skill does not provide any defense against the incoming attacks, only allows the counterattacks. GL: 9 SP: 15 / counterattack command: counter duration: technique mode

docs.title: Critical Strikes - blade technique
docs.text: Critical Strikes - blade technique ------------------------------------------------------------ A skilled swashbuckler can drive their blades deep, concentrating on powerful strikes that will result in large, critical blows. This ability will enhance the swashbuckler's natural abilities. GL: 9 SP: 8 / attack command: cstrike duration: technique mode

docs.title: Critical Strikes - Guild Level 8
docs.text: Critical Strikes - Guild Level 8 A skilled swashbuckler can drive their blades deep, concentrating on powerful strikes that will result in large, critical blows. This ability will enhance the swashbuckler's natural abilities. SP: 10 SP (round) *Effects(s)*: 15% increased critical chance

docs.title: Disarm - Guild Level 6
docs.text: Disarm - Guild Level 6 A swashbuckler soon becomes adept at relieving enemies of their weapons. A successful attempt will cause an opponent to drop its weapon. There is no effect on targets using natural weaponry--claws, fists, fangs, etc. SP: 40 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Chance to disarm opponent

docs.title: Dodge - Guild Level 3
docs.text: Dodge - Guild Level 3 Dodge is a simple technique that allows a swashbuckler to nimbly dodge incoming attacks. Naturally, the effectiveness of this technique depends on the skill and dexterity of the swashbuckler. SP: 5 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Chance of dodge incoming hits

docs.title: Doubloon - lucky charm
docs.text: Doubloon - lucky charm ------------------------------------------------------------ Lore is filled with stories surrounding charms, trinkets, and jewelry that Swashbucklers would carry into battle. Though these varied, one repeated motif is the "lucky" doubloon. Though no one could ever prove these coins provided any real protection, Swashbucklers continue to carry them when possible. With this ability, a Swashbuckler can offer up some of their own booty to temporarily receive the buff of the golden doubloon. While active, a Swashbuckler may find they get the most out of their armour. GL: 11 SP: 25 command: doubloon duration: medium

docs.title: Endtech - blade technique
docs.text: Endtech - blade technique ------------------------------------------------------------ The endtech command is used to stop using your techniques. Using endtech with a style name as an argument will end just that technique. Without an argument, endtech alone will end all of your techniques. GL: 1 SP: 0 command: endtech [style] duration: instant

docs.title: Eviscerate - attack skill
docs.text: Eviscerate - attack skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Eviscerate represents the blademaster swashbuckler's ability to swiftly strike a decisive blow. It deals hideous damage to the enemy--the stronger the enemy,the more damage it does. An eviscerating attack is usually used to finish off an already seriously wounded opponent, and should the attack fail to slay the enemy, the swashbuckler will find himself off-balance and disadvantaged in combat. Naturally, such a bold move cannot be repeated even on the densest of enemies. GL: 14 SP: variable (60-300) command: eviscerate <target> (defaults to opponent if in combat) duration: instant

docs.title: @}--- Finesse ---{@
docs.text: @}--- Finesse ---{@ Finesse is a measure of a Swashbuckler's combative abilities. As a Swashbuckler becomes more skilled, they will learn to fight with more finesse. Different fighting styles will require more or less finesse depending on their difficulty. More about these finesse requirements can be found in sbhelp 'styles'. A Swashbuckler starts with 1 point of finesse and gains one additional point of finesse per guild level. They can then run up to or equal to that finesse in different styles. Here are some examples: Bodach is a guild level 9 Swashbuckler. He could run: 'cstrike', 'calledshot' and 'slash' OR 'riposte', 'calledshot', 'ospin' and 'parry' OR 'riposte', 'ospin', 'sdodge', and 'slash' ... Cowman is a guild level 15 Swashbuckler. He could run: 'sdance', and 'impale' OR 'tblades', 'flourish' and 'flurry' OR 'sdance', 'sdodge', and 'parry' ...

docs.title: Finesse
docs.text: Finesse Finesse is a measure of a Swashbuckler's combative abilities. As a Swashbuckler becomes more skilled, they will learn to fight with more finesse. Finesse is distinct from Flow: Finesse limits which styles can be active together, while Flow discounts their triggered SP costs. Different fighting styles will require more or less finesse depending on their difficulty. More about these finesse requirements can be found in *'sbskills'*. A Swashbuckler starts with very little finesse and gains additional points through higher amounts of Guild Level, dexterity, intelligence, and charisma. Rank-derived Tier synchronizes the legacy guild level used by this calculation. They can then run up to or equal to that finesse in different styles.

docs.title: Flair - combat resource
docs.text: Flair - combat resource ------------------------------------------------------------ Flair is a Swashbuckler's combat momentum: style, nerve, timing, and the room's attention turning toward the blade. Flair starts at zero and cannot be stored between logins. It builds while fighting and decays while out of combat. Maximum Flair is 10 plus one tenth of the Swashbuckler's charisma. During each combat round, a Swashbuckler has a chance to gain one Flair. Wielding a weapon personalized with nameweapon gives an additional chance. Flourish improves both opportunities. A critical hit grants one Flair, at most once per combat round. Flair is spent by certain guild skills, including slip and press. see also: slip, press, flourish, nameweapon, challenge

docs.title: Flourish - blade technique
docs.text: Flourish - blade technique ------------------------------------------------------------ The penultimate blade technique, flourish represents the full realization of a swashbuckler's blade training. The swashbuckler executing this technique twirls his weapon(s) in an intricate, beautiful, and deadly series of flourishes. A swashbuckler executing this technique mesmerizes his opponent with his skill, enabling the swashbuckler to land his blows more easily and more powerfully. Rather than relying on speed, this technique's effectiveness is based on the swashbuckler's ability to charm and entrance his opponent. GL: 13 SP: 6 / attack command: flourish duration: technique mode

docs.title: Flourish - Guild Level 13
docs.text: Flourish - Guild Level 13 The penultimate blade technique, flourish represents the full realization of a swashbuckler's blade training. The swashbuckler executing this technique twirls his weapon(s) in an intricate, beautiful, and deadly series of flourishes. A swashbuckler executing this technique mesmerizes his opponent with his skill, enabling the swashbuckler to land his blows more easily and more powerfully. Rather than relying on speed, this technique's effectiveness is based on the swashbuckler's ability to charm and entrance his opponent. SP: 3 SP (round) *Effects(s)*: Improves other techniques as well as abilities

docs.title: Flurry - blade technique
docs.text: Flurry - blade technique ------------------------------------------------------------ Speed is the swashbucklers' greatest advantage in combat, and nowhere is that more obvious than the flurry skill. By concentrating on the offensive, a swashbuckler can take advantage of the slightest openings and strike at his enemy more often. Every successful Flurry proc grants one extra swing. Hero-level Swashbucklers can gain a second extra swing, and Legend-level Swashbucklers can gain a third. Rank provides most of each chance; character level adds a smaller bonus. GL: 12 SP: 8 / proc, reduced by Flow command: starttech flurry duration: technique mode

docs.title: Flurry - Guild Level 12
docs.text: Flurry - Guild Level 12 Speed is the swashbucklers' greatest advantage in combat, and nowhere is that more obvious than the flurry skill. By concentrating on the offensive, a swashbuckler can take advantage of the slightest openings and strike at his enemy more often. Every successful Flurry proc guarantees one extra swing. At Hero level, it can gain a second extra swing; at Legend level, it can gain a third. Raw Swashbuckler Rank is the dominant part of both chances, while character level adds a smaller bonus. The second swing chance caps at 85%; the third caps at 50% and is rolled only when the second extra swing succeeds. SP: 8 SP (proc, reduced by Flow) *Effects(s)*: Extra swing(s)

docs.title: Swashbucklers' Guild Information
docs.text: Swashbucklers' Guild Information Welcome to the swashbucklers' guild. This is a short list of commands, GL requirements, SP costs, and other information about the guild. To get more complete information on a specific ability, type 'sbhelp <ability>'. You can also view the list of guild emotes by typing 'sbhelp emotes', or the list of skills (without this preliminary information) by typing 'sbhelp skills'. There are several other commands you should be aware of. To speak on the guild line, use 'sb <text>' or 'esb <text>'. If you are GL 15, you can speak on the Blademaster line with 'sbm <text>' and 'esbm <text>'. You can view the swashbucklers online with 'swho'. Finally, you can change your guild title by typing 'stitle <text>'. Many of a swashbuckler's attack powers work only with 'blades'. This includes any knife or dagger, as well as all one-handed swords, sabres, rapiers, etc. If you find a weapon which you think fits this category, but which does not allow use of powers, please inform your guild coder, or use the bug command to report it. Most guild powers increase in effect as GL increases. This is most evident in the blade styles, but also applies to many other powers such as sconsider. Flair is a spendable combat momentum resource. It starts at zero, builds during combat, and decays outside combat. Critical hits and wielding a weapon named with 'nameweapon' can generate additional Flair. Use 'sbhelp flair' for details. A one-line summary of the various blade styles is available under 'sbhelp styles'. Information about recent changes to the guild is available on the guild board and under 'sbhelp new'. 'sbhelp skills' lists the special powers available to swashbucklers, as well as guild level, SP, and Flair cost requirements. Note that the costs listed are for neutral swashbucklers. You will find that skills are cheaper for chaotic swashbucklers and more expensive for lawful ones. Good and evil have no effect on swashbucklers' skill costs.

docs.title: Swashbuckler Guild Information
docs.text: Swashbuckler Guild Information Welcome to the Swashbucklers' guild. There are several commands you should be aware of: Use *'sb <text>'* or *'esb <text>'* to speak on the guild line. Use *'swho'*, *'sbwho'*, or *'swashies'* commands to view the Swashbucklers that are online. Many of a Swashbuckler's attack powers work only with 'blades'. This includes any knife or dagger, as well as all one-handed swords, sabres, rapiers, etc. If you find a weapon which you think fits this category, but which does not allow use of powers, please inform your guild coder, or use the bug command to report it. Swashbuckler Rank is earned through guild XP (GXP), including qualifying combat kills, sustained active combat, and triggered techniques. Rank is open-ended. It produces an ability Tier using *1 + floor(2 * sqrt(rank - 1))*; Tier replaces the old manual guild-level advancement and unlocks abilities automatically. Flow is the baseline combat rhythm meter. It rises by 5 during each eligible combat heartbeat and caps at 100. When combat ends, Flow holds for six seconds before falling by 10 per heartbeat. Flow discounts triggered technique SP costs by as much as 50%. Full Flow gives each eligible combat round a 5% chance to steal one guaranteed weapon hit. At Tier 15 and full Flow, the rare passive Dance of Death can also make the next paid technique free. Flair is a spendable combat momentum resource. It starts at zero, builds during combat, and decays outside combat. Critical hits and wielding a weapon named with *'nameweapon'* can generate additional Flair. Use *'sbhelp flair'* for details. Being unable to flee does not prevent in-room combat maneuvers such as Slip, Press, Wound, Sap, Thrust, or Flank. Entanglement and paralysis still prevent the physical maneuvers they obstruct. Skulk actually leaves the room and therefore remains unavailable while movement or fleeing is blocked. A one-line summary of the various blade styles is available under 'sbhelp techniques'. Information about recent changes to the guild is available on the guild board and under 'sbhelp new'. 'sbskills' lists abilities, Tier and SP requirements, Rank, GXP, Flow, Flair, Finesse, and active-technique information. Good and evil have no effect on Swashbucklers' skill costs.

docs.title: Impale - blade technique
docs.text: Impale - blade technique ------------------------------------------------------------ Using the impale blade technique, a swashbuckler tries to inflict deep wounds by following through on each impaling attack. A swashbuckler must be light on his feet to successfully make such a deep attack without becoming excessively vulnerable to counterattack. Damage increases at each character-level bracket: +45 below Hero, +56 at Hero, +67 at Legend, +78 at Epic, and +90 at Mythic. GL: 11 SP: 9 / proc, reduced by Flow command: impale duration: technique mode

docs.title: Impale - Guild Level 11
docs.text: Impale - Guild Level 11 Using the impale blade technique, a swashbuckler tries to inflict deep wounds by following through on each impaling attack. SP: 9 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Chance of bracket-scaled damage on hit: +45 below Hero, +56 at Hero, +67 at Legend, +78 at Epic, and +90 at Mythic.

docs.title: Insult - offensive trick
docs.text: Insult - offensive trick ------------------------------------------------------------ The flip side of the swashbuckler's charming wit is his ability to taunt and enrage an opponent, making them more careless and prone to mistakes. If the swashbuckler is successful in his taunt attempt, the foe's wild swings will be easier to dodge, and his defense will be easier to penetrate. The chance of success depends largely on the swashbuckler's charisma. Note that an enraged opponent, while hitting much less often, will hit *harder* than usual when it does connect. To customize your taunt, use 'setinsult <taunt>'. GL: 6 SP: 40 command: insult <who> (defaults to opponent if in combat) duration: medium

docs.title: Dashing rogues, gallant courtiers, outlaw kings, adventure-seeking
docs.text: Dashing rogues, gallant courtiers, outlaw kings, adventure-seeking kensai--these are the faces of the Order of Swashbucklers. These diverse warriors are bound by their skill with blades and their continual search for new lands and new opponents against which to test their prowess. From the highest courts to the meanest dockside taverns, a swashbuckler is always at home, and always ready with a jest or a blade as they search for fame and fortune. Swashbucklers are courageous warriors, often going into combat with only the lightest of armor, trusting to their skill to protect them. Their training encompasses many weapons, but they particularly excel with blades--daggers and swords, both common and exotic. With one-- or two--of these in hand, they utilize their famous blade techniques, choosing offense or defense as the situation demands. The most skilled among them master the infamous 'Dance of Death', which can decimate opponents. If you wish to learn more about the Swashbucklers, visit their guild and speak to the blademistress. The guild is located near the docks of Darkwind, 3 east, south, west from the center of town. There is also a Kerei guild branch, the Kensai, located near the docks, just outside of Odako's fortress. In Souvrael, you can visit the Desert Legion headquarters just south of Souvrael City, and in Hyperborea, we maintain a small cave near the docks as a base for our activities.

docs.title: Name Weapon - thematic skill
docs.text: Name Weapon - thematic skill ------------------------------------------------------------ This command will 'name' most generic weapons. This is only a cosmetic change; in order to prevent possible abuse, the weapon will NOT ID to its name, except for the purposes of the 'wield' and 'unwield' commands, where the weapon may be referred to by the capitalized version of its name. Wielding a weapon named with this skill gives a swashbuckler an additional chance to gain Flair during combat. Please use discretion with this ability, just as with selecting a title after level 20. Abuses will not be tolerated. GL: 1 (It's essentially an emote.) SP: 0 command: nameweapon <weapon> to <name> duration: permanent see also: flair

docs.title: Guild News
docs.text: Guild News ---------- Your guild coder is: Bob - Lots of changes made. Check the guild board for details.

docs.title: Offensive Spin - blade technique
docs.text: Offensive Spin - blade technique ------------------------------------------------------------ The offensive spin is the third blade technique to be learned. The swashbuckler uses his manual dexterity to spin his weapons around his body, striking unpredictably. As a result, his swings become difficult to defend against, and will land more often upon his opponent. GL: 3 SP: 3 / attack command: ospin duration: technique mode

docs.title: Offensive Spin - Guild Level 4
docs.text: Offensive Spin - Guild Level 4 The offensive spin is another early blade technique to be learned. The swashbuckler uses his manual dexterity to spin his weapons around his body, striking unpredictably. As a result, his swings become difficult to defend against, and will land more often upon his opponent. SP: 5 SP (round) *Effects(s)*: 15% increased hit chance

docs.title: Parley - defensive trick
docs.text: Parley - defensive trick ------------------------------------------------------------ The swashbuckler can attempt to halt combat in a room by negotiating a truce. Success depends on the intelligence and charisma of the swashbuckler, and the charisma and wisdom of the people in the room. The swashbuckler need not be in combat himself; he can attempt to stop any combat in the room. GL: 8 SP: 30 command: parley duration: permanent (until attacked again)

docs.title: Parry - blade technique
docs.text: Parry - blade technique ------------------------------------------------------------ Parry is the simplest of the blade techniques. A parrying swashbuckler concentrates on deflecting incoming hits that would otherwise have hit him. Whenever a swashbuckler successfully parries an incoming attack, the entire force of the blow will be deflected, doing no damage. Naturally, the effectiveness of this technique depends on the skill the swashbuckler has attained in the guild. GL: 1 SP: Free command: parry duration: technique mode

docs.title: Parry - Guild Level 1
docs.text: Parry - Guild Level 1 Parry is the simplest of the blade techniques. A parrying swashbuckler concentrates on deflecting incoming hits that would otherwise have hit him. Whenever a swashbuckler successfully parries an incoming attack, the entire force of the blow will be deflected, doing no damage. Naturally, the effectiveness of this technique depends on the skill the swashbuckler has attained in the guild. SP: Free (proc) *Effect(s)*: Chance to deflect damage on-hit

docs.title: Phantom Strikes - blade technique
docs.text: Phantom Strikes - blade technique ------------------------------------------------------------ A swashbuckler can call on the ghosts and phantoms of their fallen brethren. These powerful spirits will attack with them, lashing out at opponents and haunting their defenses. GL: 10 SP: 8 / attack command: phantom duration: technique mode

docs.title: Phantom Strikes - Guild Level 10
docs.text: Phantom Strikes - Guild Level 10 A swashbuckler can call on the ghosts and phantoms of their fallen brethren. These powerful spirits will attack with them, lashing out at opponents and haunting their defenses. SP: 7 SP (round) *Effects(s)*: Added chaos (plus occasional armour piercing) damage

docs.title: Press - attack skill
docs.text: Press - attack skill ------------------------------------------------------------ A Swashbuckler can spend most of their Flair to press a controlled current opponent. Your own active Challenge remains the strongest opening and grants a full immediate attack round. Paralysis, freezing, or restraint of both arms and legs grants one main-weapon attack sequence. Blindness, loss of concentration, chilled, a movement lock, or lesser entanglement grants one main-weapon swing and leaves a surviving foe Exposed for four seconds. Silence and damage-over-time effects are not openings. Press costs no spell points and has no timer. Every version costs the same 8 Flair and requires the target to be your current opponent. GL: 8 Cost: 8 Flair command: press <target> (defaults to opponent if in combat) duration: instant see also: flair, challenge, status effects

docs.title: Press - Guild Level 8
docs.text: Press - Guild Level 8 A Swashbuckler can spend most of their Flair to press a controlled current opponent. Your own active Challenge remains the strongest opening and grants a full immediate attack round. Paralysis, freezing, or restraint of both arms and legs grants one main-weapon attack sequence. Blindness, loss of concentration, chilled, a movement lock, or lesser entanglement grants one main-weapon swing and leaves a surviving foe Exposed for four seconds. Silence and damage-over-time effects are not openings. Press costs no spell points and has no timer. Every version costs the same 8 Flair and requires the target to be your current opponent. Cost: 8 Flair Command: `press <target>` (defaults to opponent if in combat) See also: flair, challenge, status effects

docs.title: Riposte - blade technique
docs.text: Riposte - blade technique ------------------------------------------------------------ Riposte is a mid-level blade technique. The swashbuckler, by anticipating an attack is able to respond to an incoming blow from a third party (someone he's not attacking) with a quick strike of his own. Note that parrying is not necessary to execute ripostes. GL: 7 SP: 3 / riposte command: riposte duration: technique mode

docs.title: Riposte - Guild Level 7
docs.text: Riposte - Guild Level 7 Riposte is a mid-level blade technique. The swashbuckler, by anticipating an attack is able to respond to an incoming blow from a third party (someone he's not attacking) with a quick strike of his own. Note that parrying is not necessary to execute ripostes. SP: 5 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Chance to redirect an attack from a secondary opponent

docs.title: Sb/Esb/Sbm/Esbm - guild chatlines
docs.text: Sb/Esb/Sbm/Esbm - guild chatlines ------------------------------------------------------------ The guild chat lines. The sb line is the main channel, heard by all members; esb emotes over it. Sbm and esbm are the Blademaster channels, which can be used (and heard) only by Blademasters (GL 15). GL: 1 (sb) or 15 (sbm) SP: 0 command: sb/esb/sbm/esbm <text>, sbhist sbmhist duration: N/A

docs.title: Kiss of True Love - healing skill
docs.text: Kiss of True Love - healing skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Passion is in the nature of a swashbuckler, and his kiss will revitalize both the recipient and himself. Each will be healed a small amount. Both participants must be players, alive, gendered, present, and outside combat. GL: 2 SP: 30 command: sbkiss <who> duration: instant

docs.title: Call to Arms - teamwork skill
docs.text: Call to Arms - teamwork skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Although many swashbucklers are loners, all are bound to each other by mutual respect. When swashbucklers come together to fight as a team, each becomes more effective than he would be individually. The more swashbucklers gather, the greater the improvement when they fight in tandem. When a group of swashbucklers gather, one of them, usually the leader, will issue a call to arms. Each swashbuckler who hears the call will join in, both adding to and sharing in the benefits of the call. Swashbucklers who cannot give the call to arms due to inexperience can still add to the effect of others' calls, while benefitting themselves. Once the call is made, the effect will continue for the duration even if the group disperses. The effect of the original call to arms can be renewed periodically in a smaller group, as long as it is done before the effect expires. GL: 5 SP: 30 command: scall duration: long

docs.title: Check Styles - information skill
docs.text: Check Styles - information skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Use 'scheck' to check which techniques you are currently using. It will give you a list of all active techniques, or it will tell you 'None.' if none are in use. GL: 1 SP: 0 command: scheck duration: instant

docs.title: Consider - information skill
docs.text: Consider - information skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Swashbucklers are able to consider an opponent with a fair degree of accuracy. Relative experience, weapon strength, and physical ability will be determined, as well as relative armor strength. At higher guild level, ethical behavior may be determined, and there is a chance that the monster's weaknesses will be found. GL: 1 SP: 5 command: sconsider <target> duration: instant

docs.title: Dance of Death - ultimate technique
docs.text: Dance of Death - ultimate technique ------------------------------------------------------------ The Dance of Death, the kensai's legendary 'whirlwind attack', is the swashbuckler's ultimate technique. A synthesis of mind, body, and blade which is deceptively delicate and lethally beautiful. It combines the aspects of many of the swashbuckler's individual techniques to create a cocoon of steel round the warrior. In order to engage in the Dance of Death, the swashbuckler must become one with his blade in the heat of combat. As he approaches this state, he will find his technique gradually improving until he reaches the pinnacle of his skill, and his movements become almost effortless. A swashbuckler will all his faculties - speed, intellect and charm in order to execute the Dance of Death to the utmost effect. Dance is passive. At 100 Flow, each eligible combat round has a 5% chance to steal one guaranteed weapon hit. At GL 15, full Flow also has a separate, very rare chance to make the next paid technique free. GL: 15 SP: Passive command: sdance (compatibility information only) duration: passive at full Flow

docs.title: Dance of Death - Passive Flow Technique (Tier 15)
docs.text: Dance of Death - Passive Flow Technique (Tier 15) The Dance of Death, the kensai's legendary '*whirlwind attack*', is the swashbuckler's ultimate technique. A synthesis of mind, body, and blade which is deceptively delicate and lethally beautiful. It combines the aspects of many of the swashbuckler's individual techniques to create a cocoon of steel round the warrior. Dance is no longer started or stopped. Combat builds Flow automatically. At 100 Flow, each eligible combat round has a 5% chance to steal one guaranteed weapon hit. At Tier 15, full Flow also has a separate, very rare chance to execute the Dance message and make the next paid technique that triggers cost no SP. The token ends with combat if unused. Commands: *starttech sdance* and *stoptech sdance* explain the passive rule.

docs.title: Disarm - offensive trick
docs.text: Disarm - offensive trick ------------------------------------------------------------ A swashbuckler soon becomes adept at relieving enemies of their weapons. A failed attempt will cause the target to become enraged and attack, but a successful attempt will cause it to drop its weapon. There is no effect on targets using natural weaponry--claws, fists, fangs, etc. GL: 6 SP: 40 command: sdisarm <target> (defaults to opponent if in combat) duration: instant

docs.title: Dodge - defensive technique
docs.text: Dodge - defensive technique ------------------------------------------------------------ Dodge is a simple technique that allows a swashbuckler to nimbly dodge incoming attacks. Naturally, the effectiveness of this technique depends on the skill and dexterity of the swashbuckler. GL: 3 SP: 5+ per dodge command: sdodge duration: technique mode

docs.title: Evaluate Weapon - information skill
docs.text: Evaluate Weapon - information skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Swashbucklers are well trained in the lore of weapons, including those weapons which they themselves choose not to use, such as polearms. They may call upon this knowledge in order to evaluate a weapon. Aside from anaccurate evaluation of the weapon's strength, some additional information may be gleaned, such as whether the weapon is unique, whether it causes a special effect when it strikes, and so on. It will not, however, determine hidden information about a weapon in the manner an identify spell would; it is still a non- magical skill, no matter how accurate. GL: 1 SP: 5 command: sevaluate <weapon> duration: instant

docs.title: Inspire - teamwork skill
docs.text: Inspire - teamwork skill ------------------------------------------------------------ A skilled swashbuckler in action is an imposing sight. A swashbuckler experienced enough to use this ability knows how to use his example of skill, and his sheer force of presence to inspire others to fight better. Its effect is similar to that of the Call to Arms, but non-Swashbucklers can benefit from it as well. GL: 14 SP: 60 command: sinspire duration: long

docs.title: Spectral Siphon - Tier 18 Technique
docs.text: Spectral Siphon - Tier 18 Technique Use *starttech siphon* to let the Order's spectral blades drink magical strength from enemies you hit. A trigger costs 6 SP before its Flow discount, drains up to 12 SP from the target, and restores exactly what was drained. An empty target still consumes the triggered technique's cost. Finesse: 4 Trigger chance: 20%, improved by Flourish

docs.title: Skewer - retired blade technique name
docs.text: Skewer - retired blade technique name ------------------------------------------------------------ Skewer was the former name for the Impale blade technique. Use 'starttech impale' to concentrate on deep piercing strikes. Impale's damage now increases at each character- level bracket: +45 below Hero, +56 at Hero, +67 at Legend, +78 at Epic, and +90 at Mythic. GL: 11 SP: 9 / proc, reduced by Flow command: starttech impale duration: technique mode
