docs.title: Skulk - utility skill
docs.text: Skulk - utility skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Swashbucklers of the more roguish sort often have reasons for wanting to leave--or enter--a room unnoticed. This ability allows them to do just that. If you wish to move silently further than one room, you must use skulk each time. GL: 1 SP: 10 command: skulk <direction> duration: instant

docs.title: Slash - blade technique
docs.text: Slash - blade technique ------------------------------------------------------------ Slashing can often be an effective, if somewhat crude way of attacking an opponent. Using brute strength alone, a swashbuckler attempts to make direct, powerful attacks against his opponent. While the attacks are no more likely to hit than usual, blows that land cause greater damage. Damage increases at each character-level bracket: +6 below Hero, +7 at Hero, +9 at Legend, +10 at Epic, and +12 at Mythic. GL: 2 SP: 2 / proc, reduced by Flow command: slash duration: technique mode

docs.title: Slash - Guild Level 2
docs.text: Slash - Guild Level 2 Slashing can often be an effective, if somewhat crude way of attacking an opponent. Using brute strength alone, a swashbuckler attempts to make direct, powerful attacks against his opponent. While the attacks are no more likely to hit than usual, blows that land cause greater damage. SP: 2 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Chance of bracket-scaled damage on hit: +6 below Hero, +7 at Hero, +9 at Legend, +10 at Epic, and +12 at Mythic.

docs.title: Slip - attack skill
docs.text: Slip - attack skill ------------------------------------------------------------ A Swashbuckler can spend a little Flair to slip inside an opponent's guard and land a quick weapon strike. Slip costs no spell points. It requires a slashing or piercing weapon in the main hand. GL: 3 Cost: 2 Flair command: slip <target> (defaults to opponent if in combat) duration: instant, micro damage timer see also: flair

docs.title: Slip - Guild Level 3
docs.text: Slip - Guild Level 3 A Swashbuckler can spend a little Flair to slip inside an opponent's guard and land a quick weapon strike. Slip costs no spell points. It requires a slashing or piercing weapon in the main hand. Cost: 2 Flair Command: `slip <target>` (defaults to opponent if in combat) Timer: micro damage timer See also: flair

docs.title: Locate Swashbuckler - information/theme skill
docs.text: Locate Swashbuckler - information/theme skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Swashbucklers are a close brotherhood, and tend to know each other very well. Drawing on this knowledge, it is possible for one swashbuckler to imagine himself at the side of another, and actually catch a glimpse that other's immediate surroundings. Should you not desire to be found, use 'slocate off' to prevent others from locating you. 'Slocate on' will allow them to do so once more. GL: 6 SP: 10 command: slocate on/off/<who> duration: instant

docs.title: Pants - offensive trick
docs.text: Pants - offensive trick ------------------------------------------------------------ A good swashbuckler revels in the chance to both show off his blade skills and embarrass his opponent to boot. By deftly relieving an enemy of his trousers, he accomplishes both in spades. GL: 7 SP: 25 command: spants <target> (defaults to opponent if in combat) duration: instant

docs.title: Srestore - fix your guild soul
docs.text: Srestore - fix your guild soul ------------------------------------------------------------ Using 'srestore' is the same as 'fix'ing your hat at Diana. You can use this command from anywhere on the mud. GL: 1 SP: 0 command: srestore duration: N/A

docs.title: Sap - blade utilty skill
docs.text: Sap - blade utilty skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Sap allows you to tap into the spirits of fallen Swashbucklers. Performing this action will bind a part of that otherworldy energy onto a blade, allowing for a quick slash against an opponent. When the blade makes contact, the attacker will drain some of the target's dexterity. More experienced Swashbucklers will gain more from the maneuver. GL: 14 SP: 25 command: ssap <target> duration: 30+ seconds

docs.title: Sharpen - utility skill
docs.text: Sharpen - utility skill ------------------------------------------------------------ A swashbuckler always takes good care of his blades. He can hone them to razor-sharpness, improving their quality. GL: 2 SP: 40 command: ssharpen <weapon> duration: permanent

docs.title: Slice - attack skill
docs.text: Slice - attack skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Slice is the most basic of attack skills learned by a budding, young swashbuckler. Using a slashing main blade, the swashbuckler slices at his opponent in an attempt to inflict a fatal wound. While not a particularly elegant attack, a well-timed slice can be effective at dispatching a weakened enemy. This attack can only be attemped once per opponent though, as they will quickly catch on to the swashbuckler's tricks. Note that this attack is much more effective as a final, killing stroke on an enemy near death. GL: 1 SP: 10 command: sslice <target> (defaults to opponent if in combat) duration: instant

docs.title: Technique Control
docs.text: Technique Control Techniques can be controlled with the *starttech* and *stoptech* commands.

docs.title: Thrust - attack skill
docs.text: Thrust - attack skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Like slice, a thrust is a single direct attack, aiming to dispatch an opponent who is already at death's door. Rather than making a crude swing at an enemy, a thrusting attack is precise and requires greater concentration. By using finesse instead of brute force, the swashbuckler will find that larger opponents will fall to his blade. Opponents that are not near death will still be able to twist away from a thrusting attack though, taking much less damage than intended, and will be very wary of any future moved by any swashbuckler. GL: 8 SP: 40 command: sthrust <target> (defaults to opponent if in combat) duration: instant

docs.title: Swashbuckler Title - theme skill
docs.text: Swashbuckler Title - theme skill ------------------------------------------------------------ Changes the swashbuckler guild title, which is displayed as part of the swho command. GL: 1 SP: 0 command: stitle <text> duration: N/A

docs.title: Useful Swashbuckler Commands
docs.text: Useful Swashbuckler Commands ---------------------------- sb, esb - Talk to other Swashbucklers swho - See which Swashbucklers are online stitle - Set your title on the swho screen srestore - Fix problems with your hat when not in town endtech - End a technique earlier than normal nameweapon <wpn> to <name> - Personalize your weapons scheck - Check which techniques are in use sbhelp new - Shows recent changes to the guild sbhelp styles - Quick reference file for blade styles sbhelp general - More in-depth guild information, including skills sbhelp skills - A list of skills and their costs (included in 'general') sbhelp titles - Shows titles for all guild levels sbhelp emotes - Shows Swashbuckler emotes

docs.title: Swash Who - information skill
docs.text: Swash Who - information skill ------------------------------------------------------------ The swho comand will list all active Swashbucklers on Darkwind, along with a status report for each. The status is noted by one or more letters: D - dead E - wiz+ editing a file F - fighting I - input mode (reading, writing, listing 'who', etc.) M - muffed [Idle] - idle Swashbucklers can change the guild title displayed under swho by using the stitle command. GL: 1 SP: 0 command: swho duration: N/A

docs.title: Techniques
docs.text: Techniques A young Swashbuckler may use only one technique at a time. With guild levels, a Swashbuckler will have more *finesse*, and may increase the depth and number of styles usable at one time. Using multiple defensive styles together will cause additional strain on the Swashbuckler, as will multiple offensive styles together. Note: You can check what styles you are using by typing *st* or *hp*, and you can finish using all styles by typing *stoptech*. Techniques are either *proc* based, or *round* based. This means the technique either activates under some condition (when hit, when performing a hit, etc), or once per round. The costs happen when the technique is activated, which means a proc-based technique may activate multiple times per round. Each triggered technique awards 2 GXP at most once per ten seconds across all techniques. Flow discounts positive technique costs from 0% at empty to 50% at full Flow. Zero-cost techniques remain free. While Flow is full, each eligible combat round also has a 5% chance to steal one guaranteed weapon hit. ## Techniques ### Parry - Guild Level 1 Parry is the simplest of the blade techniques. A parrying swashbuckler concentrates on deflecting incoming hits that would otherwise have hit him. Whenever a swashbuckler successfully parries an incoming attack, the entire force of the blow will be deflected, doing no damage. Naturally, the effectiveness of this technique depends on the skill the swashbuckler has attained in the guild. Of course, critical hits are hard to parry, catching adventurers of all types, including swashbucklers, off guard. SP: Free (proc) *Effect(s)*: Chance to deflect damage on-hit ### Slash - Guild Level 2 Slashing can often be an effective, if somewhat crude way of attacking an opponent. Using brute strength alone, a swashbuckler attempts to make direct, powerful attacks against his opponent. While the attacks are no more likely to hit than usual, blows that land cause greater damage. SP: 2 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Chance of +6/+7/+9/+10/+12 damage below Hero and at the Hero, Legend, Epic, and Mythic brackets. ### Dodge - Guild Level 3 Dodge is a simple technique that allows a swashbuckler to nimbly dodge incoming attacks. Naturally, the effectiveness of this technique depends on the skill and dexterity of the swashbuckler. Of course, critical hits are hard to dodge, catching adventurers of all types, including swashbucklers, off guard. Attempting to dodge a critical hit like this may still consume SP. SP: 5 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Chance to dodge incoming hits ### Offensive Spin - Guild Level 4 The offensive spin is another early blade technique to be learned. The swashbuckler uses his manual dexterity to spin his weapons around his body, striking unpredictably. As a result, his swings become difficult to defend against, and will land more often upon his opponent. SP: 3 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: 15% increased hit chance ### Calledshot - Guild Level 5 By making a called shot, a swashbuckler can strike at a weak point in his opponent's armor, or at an unprotected area of the opponent's body. Achieving this precise aim requires both a steady hand and knowledge of weaknesses. These well- placed strikes, when they land, will cause greater damage to the enemy. SP: 3 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Chance of +12/+15/+18/+21/+24 damage below Hero and at the Hero, Legend, Epic, and Mythic brackets. ### Disarm - Guild Level 6 A swashbuckler soon becomes adept at relieving enemies of their weapons. A successful attempt will cause an opponent to drop its weapon. There is no effect on targets using natural weaponry--claws, fists, fangs, etc. SP: 40 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Chance to disarm opponent ### Riposte - Guild Level 7 Riposte is a mid-level blade technique. The swashbuckler, by anticipating an attack is able to respond to an incoming blow from a third party (someone he's not attacking) with a quick strike of his own. Note that parrying is not necessary to execute ripostes. SP: 5 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Chance to redirect an attack from a secondary opponent ### Critical Strikes - Guild Level 8 A skilled swashbuckler can drive their blades deep, concentrating on powerful strikes that will result in large, critical blows. This ability will enhance the swashbuckler's natural abilities. SP: 5 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: 15% increased critical chance ### Weaponbreak - Guild Level 9 A practised swashbuckler can catch an enemy's weapon on his blade and, with a sharp twist, break it, rendering the enemy much weaker. This skill is more intricate and difficult to learn than disarm, but can also be more effective at weakening your enemy. Weapons broken in this manner are considerably reduced in effectiveness SP: 40 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Chance to break an opponent's weapon ### Phantom Strikes - Guild Level 10 A swashbuckler can call on the ghosts and phantoms of their fallen brethren. These powerful spirits will attack with them, lashing out at opponents and haunting their defenses. SP: 6 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Added chaos (plus occasional armour piercing) damage ### Impale - Guild Level 11 Using the impale blade technique, a swashbuckler tries to inflict deep wounds by following through on each impaling attack. SP: 9 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Chance of +45/+56/+67/+78/+90 damage below Hero and at the Hero, Legend, Epic, and Mythic brackets. ### Flurry - Guild Level 12 Speed is the swashbucklers' greatest advantage in combat, and nowhere is that more obvious than the flurry skill. By concentrating on the offensive, a swashbuckler can take advantage of the slightest openings and strike at his enemy more often. Each proc guarantees one extra swing. Hero level unlocks a chance for a second extra swing, and Legend level unlocks a chance for a third. SP: 8 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: Extra swing(s) ### Flourish - Guild Level 13 The penultimate blade technique, flourish represents the full realization of a swashbuckler's blade training. The swashbuckler executing this technique twirls his weapon(s) in an intricate, beautiful, and deadly series of flourishes. A swashbuckler executing this technique mesmerizes his opponent with his skill, enabling the swashbuckler to land his blows more easily and more powerfully. Rather than relying on speed, this technique's effectiveness is based on the swashbuckler's ability to charm and entrance his opponent. SP: 6 SP (round) *Effects(s)*: Improves other techniques as well as abilities ### Thousand Blades - Guild Level 14 This technique provides another way of exploiting your dexterity, allowing a swashbuckler to spin their blades in rapid succession, distracting an opponent momentarily. This distraction will allow more of the swashbuckler's hits to land. SP: 5 SP (proc) *Effects(s)*: 25% increased hit chance ### Dance of Death - Tier 15 passive The Dance of Death, the kensai's legendary '*whirlwind attack*', is the swashbuckler's ultimate technique. A synthesis of mind, body, and blade which is deceptively delicate and lethally beautiful. It combines the aspects of many of the swashbuckler's individual techniques to create a cocoon of steel round the warrior. Dance is now passive: at Tier 15 and 100 Flow, it can very rarely make the next paid triggered technique free. SP: Free; it discounts one later technique *Effect*: One-shot free-technique token ### Spectral Siphon - Tier 18 The spectral brethren drink magical strength from an opponent on a successful hit. A proc costs 6 SP before its Flow discount, drains up to 12 currently available SP, and restores exactly that amount to the Swashbuckler. Command: *starttech siphon*

docs.title: -= Break In =-
docs.text: -= Break In =- This Thief skill is mastered by only the most experienced, patient Thieves. Boldly go where no normal man has gone before! (behind closed doors without a key!) GLVL required: 11 Syntax: breakin [direction] Cost: 15

docs.title: -= Cant =-
docs.text: -= Cant =- Throughout the centuries, thief brethren have developed "alternative" means of communication to avoid having their plots discovered by the likes of the common God-fearing citizen. Many variations of thieves cant have spread through the alleyways and dark corners of the realms - the known cant among Darkwind brethren is one spoken entirely by hand. This command is most effective when used in conjunction with hide, as the common citizen will not be able to see your subtle hand signals. Common uses include: -Silent communication while hiding in the shadows setting up for a hit. -Making fun of a non-thief. GLVL required: 1 Syntax: cant <message> Cost: Free

docs.title: Case
docs.text: Case --------------------------------------------------------------------- Syntax: case <target> Case reports a mark's visible inventory and makes that living your one Studied target for two minutes. Studying a fresh mark creates two Opportunity. Meaningful successful jobs against NPCs award small Thief GXP scaled by the shared kill tracker. Repeating one target within thirty minutes pays 100%, 50%, 25%, then no job GXP. Switching Studied targets normally carries at most two Opportunity. Ghost mastery can raise that carry limit to three, four, and five.

docs.title: -= Circle =-
docs.text: -= Circle =- The ability of a thief to use his or her cunning and quickness to outsmart an opponent has always been of utmost advantage in battle. Once a thief reaches the 8th guild level, they are able to circle quickly around an opponent and deliver a well placed slash in the opponent's back. This skill takes time for a thief to recover from but as the thief progresses in level, quickness, and within the guild, they will see the time it takes to recover from this maneuver lessen. A thief may also see increased precision on a strike when an opponent is temporarily blinded. GLVL required: 8 Syntax: circle <target> Cost: Varied

docs.title: -= Conceal =-
docs.text: -= Conceal =- There are two things which sets apart a good Thief, from a poor one. One is the ability to swipe an item without getting caught. The second one is stashing the item and getting out without being detected. Conceal is the ability of the higher Thieves to obscure an item from others view, usually by sneaking it into a cloak. GLVL required: 8 Syntax: conceal <item> Cost: ~30

docs.title: Contacts
docs.text: Contacts --------------------------------------------------------------------- Syntax: contacts Consult the local criminal network for a compact report on your current incident, city-guard warnings, active guard pass, local corruption, and expected bribe price. Contacts no longer tracks or reveals other players. Corrupt city guards still own the normal 'bribe guard' interaction. Silver Tongue and the Fence Method can reduce the price quoted by the guard network. Cost: 20 spell points

docs.title: -= Critical Hit =-
docs.text: -= Critical Hit =- Focusing on their combat, a thief can have greater success in critically wounding their foes. The duration improves with Thief guild level, starting short when the skill is first learned and reaching about a minute at guild level 20. GLVL required: 6 Syntax: crit Cost: ~45

docs.title: -= Clever Strike =-
docs.text: -= Clever Strike =- Thieves can learn to use their dexterity to flick their wrists, thereby slashing their foe wildly. Unlike Quick Strike, Clever Strike also relies on a Thief's wits and strength. GLVL required: 8 Syntax: cstrike <target> Cost: Varied

docs.title: This skill allows a thief to throw a specially designed dagger
docs.text: This skill allows a thief to throw a specially designed dagger available for purchase at the guild poison shop at an unsuspecting opponent. As your skills with a dagger increase, you will see your accuracy and time between throws improve as well. You will find that if your aim is true, you will be able to hit a target from several screens away as well. The syntax to use this skill is "dthrow <target>". This skill costs 25 sps.

docs.title: Dirty Fight
docs.text: Dirty Fight --------------------------------------------------------------------- Syntax: dirtyfight <feint|punch|sand> [target] Spend one Opportunity on one of three distinct tricks. Feint applies Exposed. Punch deals blunt damage and disrupts Concentration. Sand attempts to Blind the target. Establishing a fresh condition finds one Opportunity. If a target is immune to Punch or Sand's control, the attempt uses half SP, half its normal recovery, and has a 50% chance to retain the Opportunity.

docs.title: Disarm
docs.text: Disarm --------------------------------------------------------------------- Dismantle a deployed Thief trap or tripwire. Your own device is always safe to remove. Removing another setter's device tests Dexterity, Intelligence, Thief training, Locksmith, and the Cat Method; failure may trigger it. GLVL: 9 Syntax: disarm <trap|tripwire>

docs.title: Disembowel
docs.text: Disembowel --------------------------------------------------------------------- Syntax: disem <target> Spend three Opportunity to exploit an existing canonical Bleeding wound for burst damage. Bleeding supplied by another guild or party member works. Disembowel benefits from the wound but does not consume or replace it. Guild level: 17

docs.title: Disembowel

docs.title: -= Enter Message =-
docs.text: -= Enter Message =- Emess is the command used to change your entrance message that only thieves will see when you log into Darkwind. Emess followed by no value will reset your entrance message to the standard message. Emess <message> will set your entrance message correctly. Placing a $N in the message will put your name into the entrance message, just as it does when setting your title when you advance a level. GLVL required: 1 Syntax: emess <message> Cost: Free

docs.title: Envenom Strike
docs.text: Envenom Strike --------------------------------------------------------------------- Syntax: envenomstrike [target] Alias: venomstrike [target] Spend one Opportunity to force a landed delivery attempt from your wielded weapon's Thief poison coating. The maneuver trades direct damage for reliable poison delivery and consumes one coating charge even when the poison's damage or control is resisted. Guild level: 7

docs.title: -= Exit Message =-
docs.text: -= Exit Message =- Exmess is the command used to change your exit message that only thieves will see when you log off of Darkwind. Exmess followed by no value will reset your exit message to the standard message. Exmess <message> will set your exit message correctly. Placing a $N in the message will put your name into the exit message, just as it does when setting your title when you advance a level. GLVL required: 1 Syntax: exmess <message> Cost: Free

docs.title: -= Fast Talk =-
docs.text: -= Fast Talk =- Good Thieves must be able to talk themselves out of sticky situations all the time, be they in a big bar fight or got caught with the diamond in the hand. This command will allow you to stop combat within a room. You must be attacking (fighting) to use this. GLVL required: 12 Syntax: fasttalk Cost: ~50

docs.title: This command allows you to send a message to all members
docs.text: This command allows you to send a message to all members of the guild. It costs no spell points, and is therefore a nice substitute for 'tell'.

docs.title: <<--Welcome to your Thiefly News-->>
docs.text: <<--Welcome to your Thiefly News-->> July 28th, 2026 Thief has moved to Guild XP and the Ghost, Grifter, and Knife Knack system. Opportunity, Studied targets, common Bleeding and Exposed, runtime poison coatings, incidents, disguises, and intelligent NPC schemes are live. Start with 'thelp revival', 'tstatus', 'knacks', and 'poisons'. June 29th, 2019 Wow, what's this? More changes?? As you may have seen from 'help guilds', 'help guilds archetypes', and 'help guilds roles', Thieves are a Hybird guild excelling at the Specialist and Nuker roles. The poison room should be working mostly again. We're working how poison operates for Thiefs. With the new changes, you can purchase poison packets from the guild house. These will get stored on your character without you having to do anything. You can see how many you're carrying by using the "sc" command. See: "thelp poison" We've reduced the duration of the Critical Hit ability and limited it to one strike per round. We've moved the majority of the damage Clever Strike does into the follow-up critical hit. There are two other new abilities: Pilfer and Deep Pockets. Pilfer will let you try and steal something off a humanoid mark. Right now, you can find some profession-related items. We'll be experimenting to see what makes sense reward-wise. Deep Pockets allows you to re-arrange what you're holding and increase your carrying capacity as you focus on smuggling as much of your... totally legitimate items as possible. I know there are still some decently big bugs and we're working through them as we get the cycles. Upcoming features: * The poison system is going to be expanded. Some poisons will be craftable via the profession system. * Working on making hide/unhide cleaner and easier * The rank system is going to be replaced by specialities. Currently, I'm looking at Cutpurse, Burglar, and Plunderer. - Cutpurse will have an increase to roll, reduced cooldowns on plant/pick, etc. - Burglars will get cheaper hide, better breakin, etc - Plunderers will likely get better pilfer/trick/circle If you have ideas/feedback, send them my way. I won't guarentee I'll include them, but I promise to read them.

docs.title: The guildmuff command will allow you to block all gtells from
docs.text: The guildmuff command will allow you to block all gtells from guild members. This is useful for when someone is bartering over the price of some weapon and you are not interested, or if you want to be isolated for some other reason.

docs.title: -= Hide =-
docs.text: -= Hide =- The quintessential Thiefly hiding skill. This command will allow you to turn invisible for a limited amount of time. Being invisible has a bounded duration and costs SP when activated. Your degree of invisibility will be dependent on the level standing of the potential victim you are hiding from. The higher you advance within the guild ranks will aid in shortening the level gap at which a potential victim may discover you lurking in the shadows. GLVL required: 5 Syntax: hide <on/off> Cost: Varied

docs.title: Thieves
docs.text: Thieves --------------------------------------------------------------------- Thieves turn information, access, and timing into power. Case a mark, build Opportunity through meaningful setup, then spend it on dirty control or a prepared finish. Thieves work in ordinary PvE, parties, and dual-guild builds: Bleeding and Exposed are the common conditions used by every guild. Thief advancement uses Guild XP, not gold. Ranks 1 through 20 open the command kit; later uncapped ranks support Knacks, diminishing mastery, and utility progression. Each rank grants one Knack point. Useful starting commands: tstatus Current GXP, Opportunity, study, and incident knacks Ghost, Grifter, and Knife training case <target> Study one mark and create two Opportunity quickstrike <target> Open a canonical Bleeding wound dirtyfight <option> Spend Opportunity on feint, punch, or sand sidestep Spend Opportunity on short evasive footwork detect Find trap signs and hidden exits extract <corpse> Harvest a poisoncraft reagent prepare <poison> Prepare a persistent dose Use 'thelp revival' for the complete system overview.

docs.title: This command allows you to accept a player into the guild.
docs.text: This command allows you to accept a player into the guild. Presently, the guidelines for acceptance are as follows: Player must be 5th level and registered PK. syntax: Accept <player> This is a Guildmaster command.

docs.title: This command allows you to banish a player from the guild.
docs.text: This command allows you to banish a player from the guild. This should not be done without good reason. All banishments are logged, so be prepared to explain your actions upon questioning. This is a Guildmaster command.

docs.text: This thief skill is mastered by only the most experienced, patient Thieves. The art of lockpicking and breaking and entering is a level 16 Thief skill. Why find a key when you can just Breakin? Syntax: breakin <direction>

docs.title: "Man..check him out...he's loaded..."  Casing targets.
docs.text: "Man..check him out...he's loaded..." Casing targets. Syntax: case <target> Game wise, you start off with a limited ability of determining these things at Glevel 2. As you progress in Glevel, you will find out more information about them, and get better at judging values of items. Here is a short list of what will change. Glevel 1-4: Level comparison Glevel 5-9: Strength comparison Glevel 10-14: Dexterity comparison Glevel 15-19: Constitution comparison Glevel 20+: AC comparison Items are listed from highest value to lowest value, Stealable to Non-stealable. For example, if you saw the following set: Comparing yourself to Joe you determine: You're more experienced. You're stronger. You're faster. You could handle more damage. Joe's inventory: Value Stl Description =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= 642 Y The Cape of the Night 250 Y A keg of exodus's newbie ale (mostly empty) 241 Y [2] A blackened shortsword 157 Y A large sack 79 Y A pair of tough boots 26 Y Swordsman's fighting gloves 0 N A fighter's torch 44 N A padded leather helm (worn on head) 43 N A pair of tough leather gloves (worn on hands) 183 N Leather boots (worn on feet) 1009 N Razor sharp scimitar (sharpened) (main weapon) 736 N Razor sharp scimitar (sharpened) (secondary weapon) 1396 N A golden suit of Platemail (lightweight) (worn on body =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= Joe is Registered. Steal away. You could steal the Cape, the keg, the shortswords, the sack, the boots and the gloves. Everything down from there is prefaced with a "N" indicating that for some reason, it is unstealable. Glevel: 2 SP Cost: 10

docs.title: Thieves
docs.text: Thieves --------------------------------------------------------------------- Thieves are the masters of sleight-of-hand. If they desire something they don't bother with formalities like asking permission from the owner or paying for a desired item, they just take it (hopefully unnoticed). If they are short on cash they find an unwitting donor and 'borrow' a few coins from them just to get them by. Thieves tend to be loners or work with others of their class, as it seems many do not like the thieves' way of making a living. It is also not uncommon for there to be bounties placed upon the heads of thieves, from their disgruntled 'victims'. Because of the need to move silently thieves cannot be encumbered with heavy armours or huge weapons. They tend to prefer to wear lighter armours such as leather, and carry weapons such as daggers or shortswords. Because thieves work with their hands a lot, dexterity is a prime requisite for them being able to perform their skills. Thieves are also masters in the ability of not being noticed, so they are very good at blending into the woodwork. Remember to choose your guild carefully, because once chosen, its a lifetime commitment.

docs.title: This command allows you to see how much money a player has.
docs.text: This command allows you to see how much money a player has. It is a convenient tool to check the honesty of a player. At lower levels, the target must be present, but the guildmaster can check the money of anybody on the mud. This command, can also be used to help your members locate those who are ripe for stealing. :-) This ability costs 5 spell points.

docs.title: This command allows you to access the thief guild news
docs.text: This command allows you to access the thief guild news service. This will keep you up-to-date with all the changes that may take place within the guild. Members are expected to keep up with the news as well as the information posted on the guild bulletin board.

docs.title: This command allows you to pick up items without anyone
docs.text: This command allows you to pick up items without anyone else knowing you picked them up. It works exactly like "get" or "take". You can use "palm all". A thief must always be the master of deception, so quickly palm that item and don't let others see you've picked it up. You must be guild level 4 to use this power. Syntax: palm <item> or "all", or palm <item> from <target>, as well as 'palm all from <target>'.

docs.title: Peeking into a victim's container allows the master thief
docs.text: Peeking into a victim's container allows the master thief to be little bit more choosy in what he steals. Using your stealth like abilities, you are able to sneak a peek into their container and see if it's worth stealing. This is a Glevel 12 skill. Syntax: peek <container> on <target>

docs.title: The highlight of being a thief is stealing objects from
docs.text: The highlight of being a thief is stealing objects from players or monsters. The pick command allows you to do so at some predetermined percentage level. This ability can only be used by ranks 9 or above.

docs.title: This is a guild level 13 skill. The thief is able to frame another
docs.text: This is a guild level 13 skill. The thief is able to frame another individual by skillfully sneaking an object into someone else's inventory. Steal an object from victim A, and plant it on victim B. And then accuse victim B of the crime!

docs.title: This command helps the thief to remember all the skills that he/she
docs.text: This command helps the thief to remember all the skills that he/she has learned, and all the powers that are possible to acquire through continued training in the Thieves Guild. It is also a continually updated list of changes to powers. Syntax: powers This is a free 'information' skill.

docs.title: This command allows you to promote a fellow guild member.
docs.text: This command allows you to promote a fellow guild member. I would suggest only using it if a player's level has accidently been erased (autoload strings have been known to corrupt), or for players who are extremely loyal to the guild. This entails things like doing things for the guild for nothing, donating objects to the guild, continually helping new members or recruiting new members. This command is logged, so be prepared to explain your actions upon questioning. Only Alarian or the Senior Guildmaster can do this.

docs.title: Roll corpse is the thief's innate ability to find the "secret" places
docs.text: Roll corpse is the thief's innate ability to find the "secret" places people hide their loot. Through training, you are able to search a corpse effectively, and find that extra money they had stashed.

docs.title: Rules For Play in the Thief Grid
docs.text: Rules For Play in the Thief Grid The thief grid offers an opportunity for thieves of all ranks to engage in a bit of friendly competition. The object of the game is simple - try to steal as many of your opponent's flags while trying to keep as many of your own flags. Each player starts with a certain number of flags as determined by their guild level. The current flag divisions are: level 1-5: 6 2-point flags level 6-10: 4 3-point flags level 11-15: 3 4-point flags level 15-20+: 2 6-point flags This method of division accounts for the extra powers that upper-level thieves get. One game lasts for 4 minutes, at the end of which points are counted and guild points are awarded. The method of reward is simply 50 guildpoints * (total points - 12). For example, if you come out of the game with 16 points, You gain 50*(16-12) = 200 guild points. Of course, if you end up with less points...well... *grin*

docs.title: The scout command enables you to peek into adjacent
docs.text: The scout command enables you to peek into adjacent rooms without risking any harm to yourself. The currently available directions are all standard compass directions plus up and down. This is a Glevel 3 skill. Syntax: scout <direction>

docs.title: This command allows you to follow a player or monster.
docs.text: This command allows you to follow a player or monster. Using this skill takes 25 spell points; there is a chance that your target can escape from you. You must be rank seven to use this ability.

docs.title: The silent command enables you to leave a room without
docs.text: The silent command enables you to leave a room without showing which direction you left. Available directions are all standard compass directions plus up and down. This is a Glevel 5 skill. Syntax: silent <direction>

docs.title: The thief's ability to let his/her eyes adjust and see better in
docs.text: The thief's ability to let his/her eyes adjust and see better in the dark, as well as see others who are "hiding". Using this skill will allow you to use other Thief skills on the otherwise invisible target. You have a short period of time (approx 10 seconds) after you Squint to take action against the invisible target. This is a Glevel 4 skill. Syntax: squint

docs.title: This command allows you to sneak up on your target and
docs.text: This command allows you to sneak up on your target and suprise them with a stab in the back. This command can be used on monsters and players. This is a very powerful skill and can only be used when you have suprise. The real strength of this skill is attacking in numbers. When 'jumping' a target, after the first stab, other thieves will have 10 seconds in which they may also stab. After that time, the target will be too 'aware' of its surroundings to be taken by anyone else. You *must* be Hidden to stab a fellow player. This skill is based on your Dex & Int, as well as your Glevel. It is a Glevel 11 skill. Syntax: stab <target>

docs.title: This command allows you to steal a random amount of
docs.text: This command allows you to steal a random amount of coins from a player. Your chance of success is based on your dexterity and guild rank. This is a Glevel 2 power. Syntax: steal <player> The cost of this skill is lower for up to 10th Glevel. At 10th level, you will begin to pay 20 for the increased effectiveness of the skill.

docs.title: -- ** Thief Guild Help ** --
docs.text: -- ** Thief Guild Help ** -- During your membership, you will learn the following talents: Basic Communications: gtell <message>, gmote <message> Information Commands: thelp - this command (duh) powers - Gives a list of talents and their costs with Glevel requirements. levels - Monetary breakdown of costs for Glevel. Help files are available for the following skills: Roll corpse, Steal, Money, Scout, Trick, Palm, Silent, Trap, Shadow, Stab, Peek, Pick, Squint, Hide, Circle, Plant, Fasttalk, Conceal, Unhide, Sewers, and Breakin. For help on any specific ability, type thelp <ability>

docs.title: This command will allow you to quickly construct a lethal
docs.text: This command will allow you to quickly construct a lethal trap that can be placed in a room. Anybody, except thieves, that attempt to leave the room, or pick up the trap will set it off, causing damage to that person. This ability costs 40 spell points and is available to players of rank 6 or greater.

docs.title: This skill allows the thief to pull some dirty fighting tactics
docs.text: This skill allows the thief to pull some dirty fighting tactics during battle and use them to his advantage. It's a small attack skill that can be used at guild level 4.

docs.title: Simply the thief's skill of revealing his/her concealed object
docs.text: Simply the thief's skill of revealing his/her concealed object without anyone noticing. This is a Glevel 7 skill. Syntax: unhide <concealed item>

docs.title: -= Money =-
docs.text: -= Money =- This command allows you to see how much money a player has. It is a convenient tool to check the honesty of a player. This command requires that your target be present. GLVL required: 2 Syntax: money <target> Cost: 5

docs.title: -= Palm =-
docs.text: -= Palm =- This command allows you to pick up items without anyone else knowing you picked them up. It costs a mere 20sp, and works exactly like "get" or "take". Also can use the "palm all". A Thief must always be the master of deception, so quickly palm that item and don't let others see you've picked it up. GLVL required: 2 Syntax: palm <item/all> Cost: 10

docs.title: -= Peek =-
docs.text: -= Peek =- Peeking into a victim's container allows the master Thief to be little bit more choosy in what he steals. Using your stealth like abilities, you are able to sneak a peek into their container and see if it's worth stealing. GLVL required: 6 Syntax: peek <container> Cost: 35

docs.title: Pick
docs.text: Pick --------------------------------------------------------------------- Choose one visible, ordinary item from a mark's inventory and try to steal it. Worn, wielded, kept, unique, auto-loading, protected, no-drop, and otherwise unsafe items cannot be taken. A failed delivery leaves the item and both inventories unchanged. Successful theft from a suitable NPC can grant Thief GXP. GLVL: 6 Syntax: pick <item> from <target>

docs.title: Pilfer
docs.text: Pilfer --------------------------------------------------------------------- Blindly lift one random ordinary carried item from an unprotected, intelligent humanoid NPC. Pilfer cannot create loot and observes the same item-safety and transactional movement rules as Pick. Each NPC becomes wary of another Pilfer attempt for one hour. GLVL: 4 Syntax: pilfer <npc>

docs.title: -= Plant =-
docs.text: -= Plant =- Plant slips one ordinary carried item into a suitable intelligent NPC's inventory. Unique, kept, no-drop, worn, wielded, and auto-loading items cannot be planted. GLVL required: 6 Syntax: plant <item> on <npc> Cost: ~1% max SP

docs.title: Poisoncraft
docs.text: Poisoncraft --------------------------------------------------------------------- Extract a suitable corpse for one recipe reagent, then prepare that reagent into a persistent dose: extract <corpse> prepare <poison> [count] poison <poison> [on <weapon>] envenom <weapon> with <poison> A coating is runtime-only. It lasts for three landed delivery attempts or fifteen minutes, and consumes a charge even if the victim resists. It is never saved on the weapon. Effects and damage belong to whoever is wielding the weapon when it lands. A victim can carry no more than two distinct Thief poison effects. Reapplying one refreshes the stronger effect; a third distinct poison expires the oldest. Use 'envenomstrike <target>' in combat to spend one Opportunity and force a coating delivery attempt at reduced direct damage. Recipes: greenbite, widows_kiss, grave_milk, nerve_lace, black_lotus, throatdust, glassblood, dreamrot, and nightshade. Recipes open every two Thief Ranks from 3 through 19. Glassblood uses common Bleeding. Forced NPC dosing uses 'lace <poison> into <npc>' on a suitable local intelligent NPC. At Rank 16, the same command can lace a deployed pressure trap: 'lace <poison> into trap'.

docs.title: Thief Powers
docs.text: Thief Powers --------------------------------------------------------------------- Use 'tpowers' for the live, rank-sorted command list. Use 'tpowers available' to show only abilities your current unlock level can use. The modern core kit is: case, quickstrike, dirtyfight, trip, sidestep, circle, envenomstrike, disembowel, hamstring, backstab World and escape play includes: scout, detect, reveal, hide, slip, vanish, shadow, palm, pilfer, pick, plant, breakin, tripwire, disarm, trap, disguise, covertracks, forge, frame, and fasttalk Poisoncraft includes: poisons, extract, prepare, envenom/poison, and lace/dose Progression and customization: tstatus, knacks, and method Clever Strike, Sucker Punch, Trick, Shadowstep, and Critical Hit are compatibility command names redirected into the smaller core combat kit. The old leadership-only combat powers are retired; Don, Guild Master, and Quarter Master records remain administrative. The listing is driven by this supported command registry. Dead repair and emote debris is not exposed as guild kit merely because a file exists.

docs.title: -= Quick Strike =-
docs.text: -= Quick Strike =- Thieves can learn to use their dexterity to flick their wrists, thereby slashing their foe wildly. This is a small attack skill that will be useful to beginner thieves. Quick Strike now leaves behind a clean opening wound, making it a reliable early pressure tool. Reapplying it to a foe you have already opened will rip the wound wider and force an immediate extra gush of damage. Against your Studied mark, each landed Quick Strike has a 60% chance to find one Opportunity. Establishing fresh Bleeding finds another, so one strike can produce two Opportunity. GLVL required: 1 Syntax: qstrike <target> Cost: Varied

docs.title: Modern Thief Systems
docs.text: Modern Thief Systems --------------------------------------------------------------------- Advancement: Thief uses automatic Guild XP advancement, not carried gold. Each Rank grants one Knack point. Meaningful combat skill use grants about 5 GXP behind one 10-14 second guild-wide practice delay. Use 'tstatus' and 'knacks'. Combat: Case one target for two Opportunity, build up to five, then spend it on dirtyfight, trip, sidestep, circle, envenomstrike, hamstring, disembowel, or backstab. Quickstrike uses canonical Bleeding and has a 60% chance to find Opportunity when it lands on the Studied mark. Establishing a fresh qualifying condition also finds Opportunity. Disembowel benefits from any guild's Bleeding and does not consume it. Circle cooperates with any guild's Exposed. Abilities have a two-second category recovery and a separate reuse time for that exact skill. Change techniques to keep a combination moving; repeating the same move requires longer. Backstab's personal reuse time is twenty-four seconds. Sidestep spends one Opportunity for a large dodge bonus lasting about two combat rounds. Runner extends it; Opportunist recovers the point if no attack lands during the effect. Customization: Ghost, Grifter, and Knife each contain six five-rank Knacks. Complete a branch to open diminishing mastery. After training 10 Knack ranks in a discipline, choose one Method; swaps are free in a Thieves Guild hall. Use 'knacks reset confirm' there for a paid full retrain. World play: Detect hidden exits and traps. Disguise as a laborer, courier, pilgrim, or merchant to interact with guard notice without changing real reputation. Contacts reports guard attention, passes, and the current bribe estimate. Incidents replace a separate Heat meter. Dangerous NPC schemes work on suitable local intelligent NPCs without custom monster hooks. Frame throws your voice so one nearby NPC appears to insult another; Agitators and master Masterminds can choose the pair. Pilfer randomly takes one safe loose NPC item; Pick chooses one. Coin theft takes only part of a purse. Slip and Vanish use normal exits, while Shadow can be noticed after each followed move. Traps: Tripwire is a movement alarm. Trap is a pressure weapon that also springs on stationary NPCs once they fight its setter. Disarm owns removal, and 'lace <poison> into trap' adds a prepared dose to the pressure strike. Poisoncraft: Extract, prepare, then envenom. Prepared doses remain in your poison inventory between sessions; weapon coatings do not. See 'thelp poison'.

docs.title: -= Roll Corpse =-
docs.text: -= Roll Corpse =- Roll corpse is the thief's innate ability to find the "secret" places people hide their loot. Through training, you are able to search a corpse effectively, and find that extra money they had stashed. GLVL required: 1 Syntax: roll corpse Cost: Free

docs.title: -= Thieves Guild Rules =-
docs.text: -= Thieves Guild Rules =- By order of the GuildMaster: 1) Thieves are to remain loyal to the guild in all situations. Thieves come before clans, secondary guilds, marriage, oaths, etc. 2) There is to be no in-guild killing. Those who do will be hunted to the point of newbification and/or removed from the guild. 3) Lower level thieves are to listen to all requests made by the GuildMaster(GM) or QuarterMaster(QM). 4) Leaving the guild breaks the sworn bloodoath. You will be hunted forever. Treachery is not taken lightly. These rules are subject to change on the whim of the GM.

docs.title: -= Scout =-
docs.text: -= Scout =- The scout command enables you to peek into adjacent rooms without risking any harm to yourself. The currently available directions are all standard compass directions plus up and down. GLVL required: 3 Syntax: scout <direction> Cost: 10

docs.title: Shadow
docs.text: Shadow --------------------------------------------------------------------- Tail a visible player or monster through the same ordinary exit command they use. Every followed move contests your Dexterity, Intelligence, Ghost mastery, Keen Eye, and Cat Method against the target's awareness. A failed contest exposes you and ends the trail. GLVL: 5 Syntax: shadow <target>

docs.title: -= Shadowstep =-
docs.text: -= Shadowstep =- Shadowstep is a compatibility name for Quick Strike. Use Slip to break away from combat. GLVL required: 4 Syntax: shadowstep <target> Cost: Varied

docs.title: Sidestep
docs.text: Sidestep --------------------------------------------------------------------- Syntax: sidestep During combat, spend one Opportunity and 15 SP to gain a large dodge bonus for about two combat rounds. Sidestep cannot be stacked or refreshed while active and has a twelve-second reuse time. The Runner Method extends Sidestep by one heartbeat. The Opportunist Method returns its Opportunity when the effect ends if no attack landed on the Thief while it was active.

docs.title: -= Silent =-
docs.text: -= Silent =- The silent command enables you to leave a room without showing which direction you left. Available directions are all standard compass directions plus up and down. GLVL required: 5 Syntax: silent <direction> Cost: 5

docs.title: Slip
docs.text: Slip --------------------------------------------------------------------- Break from combat through an ordinary visible exit and hide briefly in the destination. Slip executes the real movement command, so doors, locks, movement blocks, and exit hooks still apply. A failed move still commits the attempt. GLVL: 4 Syntax: slip <direction>

docs.title: -= Sucker Punch =-
docs.text: -= Sucker Punch =- Finding a weakness in their enemy's defenses, a quick thief can deliver a devastating sucker punch. GLVL required: 8 Syntax: spunch <target> Cost: Varied

docs.title: -= Squint =-
docs.text: -= Squint =- The Thief's ability to let his/her eyes adjust and see better in the dark, as well as see marks who are hiding. GLVL required: 4 Syntax: squint Cost: 15

docs.title: -= Back Stab =-
docs.text: -= Back Stab =- Backstab is a thief's most powerful skill, one that he or she learns in the last level of guild experience. It takes a thief of the utmost dexterity, intelligence, and strength to find that perfect opening in a target's exposed back and land a dehabilitating blow. If that blow is accurate enough, it could bring an opponent to its knees, rendering it unable to run, and opening up a window of opportunity for other thieves to launch additional assaults on the crippled victim. Only a thief with comparable or exceeding skill and experience to the target will effectively be able to stun an opponent consistently, but as the brotherhood likes to hunt in packs, it is not difficult to find thieves from varying levels of skill. NOTE: A thief must be hiding with at least one Opportunity. The target must be Studied or Exposed. Backstab spends all current Opportunity and gains 20% damage for each point spent. GLVL required: 20 Syntax: stab|backstab|astrike <target> Cost: Varied

docs.title: -= Thieves Guild =-
docs.text: -= Thieves Guild =- Thieves are specialists in information, access, and unfair timing. Case a mark, create Opportunity through meaningful setup, then spend it on control, poison, escape, or a prepared finish. Thief uses automatic Guild XP advancement, not carried gold. Battle contribution, successful jobs, and meaningful combat practice grant GXP. Combat practice grants about 5 GXP no more than once every 10-14 seconds against a suitable foe. Ranks 1 through 20 open the command kit; uncapped ranks beyond that support utility and reliability progression. Every rank grants a Knack point. Start with: tstatus Rank, GXP, Opportunity, study, incident, poison knacks Ghost, Grifter, and Knife customization case <target> Study one mark and gain two Opportunity dirtyfight ... Spend Opportunity on an unfair opening tpowers Complete command and unlock listing The world kit uses bounded theft and ordinary movement contracts. Pilfer and Pick reject protected items, coin theft takes only a fraction, Slip and Vanish travel through real exits, and Shadow can be noticed. Pressure traps can catch stationary enemies in combat and can be poison-laced. Thieves use the common Bleeding and Exposed conditions, so other guilds and party members can build openings for them. Weapon attacks do not require daggers or a particular damage type; the normal guild equipment allow/restrict rules still apply. A landed Quick Strike against the Studied mark has a 60% chance to find Opportunity. Directly establishing a fresh Bleeding, Exposed, Blind, Concentration disruption, or movement block finds another. Read 'thelp revival' for the complete system overview, 'thelp poison' for poisoncraft, and 'thelp rules' for guild conduct.

docs.title: Steal Coins
docs.text: Steal Coins --------------------------------------------------------------------- Lift a bounded fraction of a target's carried coins. Training and Light Fingers improve the fraction, but even a perfect attempt never empties a whole purse. Suitable NPC theft can grant Thief GXP; noticed crime can start an incident. GLVL: 2 Syntax: steal|tsteal|lift <target>

docs.title: Trap
docs.text: Trap --------------------------------------------------------------------- Conceal a pressure trap in the room. It springs when a valid non-Thief threat leaves or handles it. It also springs on a stationary NPC once that NPC begins fighting the setter in the trapped room. Before combat, use 'lace <poison> into trap' to spend one prepared dose and add its normal poison effect to the trap strike. Traps expire after five minutes and are removed with 'disarm trap'. GLVL: 15 Syntax: trap

docs.title: -= Trick =-
docs.text: -= Trick =- Trick is a compatibility name for Dirty Fight. Use feint to apply Exposed, punch for blunt damage and Concentration disruption, or sand to attempt Blind. GLVL required: 5 Syntax: trick [target] Cost: 1 Opportunity

docs.title: Trip
docs.text: Trip --------------------------------------------------------------------- Syntax: trip [target] Spend one Opportunity to block a target's movement briefly and leave them Exposed. Establishing either fresh condition finds one Opportunity. If the target cannot be movement-blocked, Trip uses half SP, half its normal recovery, and has a 50% chance to retain the Opportunity.

docs.title: Tripwire
docs.text: Tripwire --------------------------------------------------------------------- Lay a hidden alarm wire across the room. When a valid threat crosses it, the Thief Alarm channel reports the victim and location. It deals no damage and expires after five minutes. GLVL: 9 Syntax: tripwire Remove: disarm tripwire

docs.title: Hamstring
docs.text: Hamstring --------------------------------------------------------------------- Syntax: tstrike <target> Alias: hamstring <target> Spend two Opportunity to strike a target's movement. The control lasts longer when the target is already Bleeding, including Bleeding supplied by another guild or party member. Guild level: 18

docs.title: -= Thief Tell =-
docs.text: -= Thief Tell =- This command allows you to send a message to all members of the guild. It costs no spell points, and is therefore a nice substitute for 'tell'. GLVL required: 1 Syntax: ttell <message> Cost: Free

docs.title: -= Unhide =-
docs.text: -= Unhide =- Simply the Thief's skill of revealing his concealed object without anyone noticing. GLVL required: 7 Syntax: unhide <item> Cost: 5

docs.title: Vanish
docs.text: Vanish --------------------------------------------------------------------- Turn combat or an active incident into a clean directional escape. The move uses an ordinary visible exit, ends active pursuit after a successful move, establishes cover, and reduces the incident by one step. Vanish unlocks at GLVL 14 and also requires ten trained Ghost Knack ranks. Syntax: vanish <direction>

docs.title: Bastet and Gurahl
docs.text: Bastet and Gurahl Bastet and Gurahl are Changing Breeds tied to Gaea. Bastet follow the feline path of watchfulness and agility, while Gurahl follow the bear path of patience, endurance, and protection. Current roster status: CLOSED TO NEW APPLICANTS. This page remains in the tome so returning players can recognize the name. Use help guilds for the current roster; a closed path cannot be chosen by a new character.

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · CORE LOOP  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · CORE LOOP ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ † Hunt bloodsense identifies useful prey. † Feed Feeding restores Vitae and sets your blood profile. † Spend Discipline powers consume Vitae; it does not renew. † Hide Witnesses and obvious powers create Exposure. † Rest Your bound coffin restores you and unwinds evidence. Running low is intentional. Power always leads back to predation. Next: vamphelp feeding, hunger, or exposure

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · HUNTED  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · HUNTED ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ At 75+ regional Exposure, you are Hunted. Fallows witnesses may recognize you, Dawnward sentinels grow more aggressive, and blood hunters may be dispatched. Leave the region, reduce evidence, or reach your haven. Defeating a pursuer does not erase the evidence behind the hunt. Next: vamphelp haven or vamphelp exposure

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · EXPOSURE  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · EXPOSURE ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Exposure is regional evidence of your predation. Feeding, visible powers, witnesses, corpses, masks, holy ground, and blood identity all affect it. Quiet → Whispers → Suspected → HUNTED Quiet time, coffin rest, and some powers reduce ordinary evidence. Holy proof fades more slowly. Inspect the current region with bloodsense or vscore.

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · WITNESSES  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · WITNESSES ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Living observers make obvious feeding and supernatural powers harder to hide. Careful feeding can leave no durable evidence when nobody notices. Obfuscate, Noble blood, Presence, House Vesper, and the Nameless can alter specific outcomes. They do not erase violence or sanctified proof. † If secrecy matters, inspect the room before feeding.

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · BLOOD  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · BLOOD ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ PROFILE Martial, Predatory, Mystic, Noble, Vital, or Feral / Profane QUALITY Common, Potent, Exceptional, or Mythic Profiles strengthen related disciplines while that blood remains active. Greater quality grants a larger, bounded mutation. Feeding again replaces your active profile. Inspect your current blood with bloodsense. Next: vamphelp profiles

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · HUNGER  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · HUNGER ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Remaining Vitae determines your Hunger: Sated → Stirring → Ravenous → FRENZY Ravenous blood can sharpen physical predation. Low reserves also increase the risk that spending Vitae awakens the Beast. Frenzy blocks precise sensing and control, but never bypasses legal targets, PvP rules, or safe rooms. Read your current band with vscore.

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · FEEDING MODES  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · FEEDING MODES ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ careful Slow, controlled, and best for avoiding witnesses. quick Faster and rougher, with more evidence. deep More blood from wounded prey at greater risk. drain Maximum predation against prey already near death. corpse Limited feeding from an eligible non-player corpse. Syntax: vamphelp feed Consequences: vamphelp exposure

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · FEEDING  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · FEEDING ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Feeding is your only dependable source of Vitae. It also establishes one active blood profile and quality based on the prey. † Inspect with bloodsense <target>. † Choose a feeding mode deliberately. † Remember: greater yield means greater harm and evidence. Topics: vamphelp feeding prey, feeding modes, or blood

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · FEEDING PREY  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · FEEDING PREY ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Valid prey must be an eligible NPC with living blood. Rejected: protected NPCs, players, player corpses, bloodless creatures, and prey you did not earn in shared combat. Deep and drain feeding require sufficiently wounded prey. bloodsense warns about bloodless targets and likely blood identity. Next: vamphelp feeding modes

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · VITAE  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · VITAE ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Vitae is your 100-point blood resource. A new Vampire begins with 60. Restore it Feed on eligible prey. Spend it Invoke disciplines or prepare rituals. Remember Vitae does not regenerate or decay. Remaining Vitae determines Hunger. Expensive powers can starve later choices and push you toward frenzy. Next: vamphelp feeding, hunger, or powers

docs.title: Vampires power of flight. Commands are:

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · GETTING STARTED  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · GETTING STARTED ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ SEVEN STEPS INTO NIGHT 1. Read Vitae, Hunger, blood, and Exposure with vscore. 2. Inspect prey with bloodsense <npc>. 3. Begin carefully: feed <npc> careful. 4. Browse your powers with discipline list. 5. Choose a loadout with attune <discipline, ...>. 6. docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · IDENTITY ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Three layers make every Vampire distinct: Active blood Temporary; profile and quality change by feeding. As they increase in age( I dont think I will have guild levels, maybe they spend thier experience to age or something. So a GL20 Vampire would be an Ancient or something. This blood siphoned will add to the Vampires store of blood. (I wont call it a blood pool if you dont want but I feel its a generic enough term :) As a vampire wanders through life thier blood will slowly be used up. As it gets lower and lower the vampire will get penalties to thier actions and start to get massive cravings. They will have a base blood pool level based on thier age. If they go below this base they will get the penalties. The vampire may also go above this base and receive increased strength and a sense of euphoric drunk- eness. docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · DISCIPLINES ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Celerity speed Potence force Fortitude endurance Auspex senses Obfuscate concealment Presence authority Protean predatory forms Animalism instinct Blood Sorcery vitae rites Dominate mental control Oblivion death and shadow Browse individual powers and gates with discipline list.

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · FORMS  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · FORMS ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Protean forms are mutually exclusive. Beginning a new form removes the old one and its combat adjustments. Feral Mantle Early predatory stance. Shape of the Beast Stronger scouting and combat expression. War Form Dangerous capstone. vscore and GMCP show your active form. Effects clean up on expiry.

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · MAJOR POWERS  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · MAJOR POWERS ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Each discipline ends in an encounter-defining major power. These capstones have high Vitae costs and share one major power cooldown. Using one delays every other capstone. vscore reports whether the shared timer is ready. Major powers remain bounded by bosses, banes, PvP rules, and world wards.

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · POWERS  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · POWERS ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Browse every power with discipline list. Invoke one with: discipline <power> [target] Every power checks knowledge, attunement, milestone, Blood Mastery, Vitae, cooldowns, targets, world restrictions, and Exposure. Example: vamphelp quickening Topics: vamphelp disciplines, major powers, forms, or power targets

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · POWER TARGETS  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · POWER TARGETS ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Offensive and controlling powers target eligible NPCs, never players. Before costs commit, powers check can-kill rules, protected roles, bloodless creatures, no-teleport rooms, and combat restrictions. Against bosses: executions and hard control become bounded damage or shorter debuffs instead.

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · ATTUNEMENT  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · ATTUNEMENT ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Known disciplines are permanent. Attuned disciplines are your active loadout. You normally have three slots; First Night grants four. Change the entire loadout with: attune <discipline, discipline, ...> Attune at your coffin, the First Grave, Covenant vault or Red Chapel, Vespercourt crypt, or Blood Archive. Known but unattuned disciplines cannot be invoked.

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · VAMPIRE GXP  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · VAMPIRE GXP ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Vampire GXP is permanent class progression, separate from ordinary experience and guild advancement. Earned predation and significant Blood Memories add it. † Unlocks milestones. † Supplies most of the Blood Mastery curve. † Survives remort and is never spent on powers or attunement. Next: vamphelp milestones or vamphelp mastery

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · BLOOD MASTERY  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · BLOOD MASTERY ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Blood Mastery grows from permanent Vampire GXP and remorts through R1000. It gates advanced powers and improves bounded effects, feeding, haven recovery, Torpor, and the Night Familiar. Mastery never: raises maximum Vitae or removes Hunger, sunlight, fire, or holy banes. See every requirement with discipline list.

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · MILESTONES  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · MILESTONES ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ The Embrace Starter disciplines and the predation loop. Bloodline Rite Bloodline choice; Potence, Fortitude, Obfuscate. Night Court Presence, Protean, and normally Dominate. Crimson Dominion Animalism and stronger ritual capacity. First Night Oblivion, a fourth attunement slot, and capstones. Read your current milestone and GXP with vscore.

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · PROGRESSION  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · PROGRESSION ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Vampire GXP permanently advances five milestones and survives remort. Milestones add disciplines, bloodline choice, attunement capacity, rituals, and end-game powers. Blood Mastery is the continuous power curve between milestones. Topics: vamphelp milestones, mastery, or attunement

docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · RITUAL CATALOG ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Ward of the Threshold Bounded defensive ward. docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · PREPARED RITUALS  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · PREPARED RITUALS ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Rituals are durable Blood Sorcery preparations, not instant powers. Preparing requires attuned Blood Sorcery, Vitae, an open slot, no combat, and an approved anchor such as the Covenant's Red Chapel or coffin vault. ritual prepare <name> ritual invoke <name> [target] Invocation consumes one prepared use. Prepared uses survive logout and remort. Next: vamphelp ritual catalog

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · READING VSCORE  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · READING VSCORE ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ vscore is the compact state of your Vampire. Each label is also a focused vamphelp topic: Hunger & blood Vitae, Hunger, active blood Progression milestone, GXP, Blood Mastery, bloodline Powers active form, attuned disciplines, loadout, rituals World Exposure, sky, haven, Torpor, chronicle Example: vamphelp vitae

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · CRIMSON COVENANT  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · CRIMSON COVENANT ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ The First Grave beneath Stoker's church is public. The living may enter it and accept the Embrace, but only Vampires may descend farther. † Vault of Sealed Earth — bind and rest in a coffin. † Red Chapel — attune disciplines and prepare rituals. † Court of Five Chalices — study the bloodlines. † Hall of Names — reflect on memories and Chronicle. † Crimson Hall — gather with the online Covenant. The sanctuary is safe, not a blood bank. It grants no free Vitae and does not erase Hunger, daylight, Exposure, cooldowns, or other limits. Next: vamphelp haven, attunement, or rituals

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · HAVEN AND COFFIN  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · HAVEN AND COFFIN ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Bind your coffin at the First Grave, the Covenant's Vault of Sealed Earth, or Vespercourt crypt. That location becomes your refuge and Torpor destination. † Restores health and steadies low Vitae toward 75; never refills it. † Reduces Exposure across known regions. † Receives escape powers when combat and world wards permit. Syntax: vamphelp coffin

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · SURVIVAL  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · SURVIVAL ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Vampires are powerful at night, but must manage permanent banes and refuge. † Open daylight burns. † Fire, light, good, and sanctified harm remain dangerous. † Your coffin provides recovery, Torpor, and evidence control. Topics: vamphelp sunlight, haven, or torpor

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · SUNLIGHT AND BANES  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · SUNLIGHT AND BANES ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Open dawn and twilight are dangerous; full day is worse. Indoors, underground rooms, and sufficient canopy provide shade. Light, fire, good, and sanctified damage are permanent weaknesses. Fortitude and wards reduce bounded harm; no milestone, form, or bloodline erases a bane. Read the sky with vscore. The Vampire channel announces dawn, full day, twilight, and night to every online Vampire, even those currently under cover.

docs.title: ☾  VAMPHELP · TORPOR  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPHELP · TORPOR ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Once per reboot, a non-hardcore Vampire death can become Torpor at the bound coffin instead of following the ordinary death flow. Blood Mastery improves restored health, but grants no extra uses. Later deaths during the same reboot proceed normally. vscore reports whether Torpor is available.

docs.title: Death Avengement
docs.text: Death Avengement --------------------------------------------------------------------- Death avengement is the process by which a player avenges another player's recent death, collecting a bounty and restoring the victim's lost experience. When you die, you may ask another player to avenge you. The bounty - experience and coins - scales with the toughness of whatever killed you: mightier killers pay far better. If the avenger succeeds, they collect the bounty, and your death penalty (10% of your experience on hand) is restored to you, unless a resurrection already refunded it. The rules of the system: * From the time of death, the avenged has 30 real time minutes to find an avenger, and for that avenger to track and kill the target mob. * Neither the avengee or the avenger may log off during that time, else that avenge is forever lost. * An avenged player can only have one avenger per death. * An avenger can only attempt to avenge one player at a time. * If the original killing mob is killed, the avengement is cancelled. In the case of PKs, if the killing player logs off, the avengement is cancelled. See also: askavenge, avengeinfo

docs.title: When you are killed, you become a ghost and your spirit is
docs.text: When you are killed, you become a ghost and your spirit is whisked away to the church of the land you died in. Your corpse, holding all of your belongings and gold, travels with you - it is tucked safely into your inventory, so there is no corpse run and nobody can loot you. If you are level 5 or under, death carries no penalty at all. Above level 5, death costs you 10% of your experience on hand. Nothing else is lost: no stats, no levels. At the church you have two choices: <pray> Resurrect yourself. The experience loss stands. guild rez Have another player resurrect you with a guild ability. This restores the lost experience. Once alive, take your equipment back out of your corpse and get back to adventuring. The emptied corpse rots away on its own. You can also have your death avenged. A friend who avenges your death earns a bounty of coins and experience scaled by your killer's toughness, and your lost experience is restored. See help deathavengement. See also: ghost, ghostemotes, deathavengement

docs.title: SYNTAX
docs.text: SYNTAX ====== drops DESCRIPTION =========== Shows the registered drops you have discovered in your current area. Items you have not found remain unnamed, but the command reveals how many remain and their rarity. A discovery is recorded when an item successfully drops for you in that area.

docs.title: SYNTAX
docs.text: SYNTAX ====== engage engage <npc> engage <choice number> DESCRIPTION =========== Engage opens a dialogue with an NPC in your current room. If the NPC has something to say, Darkflow will show the NPC's portrait, dialogue, and any available choices. You can click a choice in Darkflow, or use engage <choice number> from the command line. If the NPC has no special dialogue configured, the dialogue window still opens with a silent response and an option to disengage. Using engage by itself works when there is only one NPC nearby that can be engaged. If there are several, use engage <npc> instead. EXAMPLES ======== engage crier engage guard engage 1 SEE ALSO ======== look, talk, say

docs.title: -=< EQUIPMENT >=-
docs.text: -=< EQUIPMENT >=- There have been several changes made to equipment on DarkWind. We believe that in total, they will make for a more vibrant playstyle for our players. Saved Gear ========== You will now save the gear you are carrying on you when you leave the game. If you're wearing/wielding equipment, you will wear/ wield it when you re-enter the game. Not every item will be saved to your character, including the following items: -- Gear that was previously donated, or is currently broken. -- Food and/or Drinks. -- Uniques. -- Anything directly restricted by the immortals of DarkWind. -- Anything that you normally cannot drop on your own. -- Anything inside of a container (the container may save though) Any modifications to the equipment will also be stripped when you re-enter the game (harden, lighten, flaming, etc.). There is also a limit to the number of items that will safely be stored. It is many hundreds of items, and you would have to work to break it. Therefore, any items lost when you re-enter the game can not, and will not be refunded. SLOTS ===== Characters and monsters can wear equipment on the head, body, legs, hands, feet, shield arm, cloak/body, shoulders, aura, two fingers, and two neck slots. Ordinary rings and amulets will fill the first available matching slot. Use eq or myeq to see what you are currently wearing, wielding, or using as active non-cybernetic internal equipment. Use smartequip to fill open armour and weapon slots and replace weaker standard equipment using the same power scores shown by gearcheck. Use loadout to save named armour and weapon presets and switch between them outside combat. Loadouts do not change installed cyberware or other internal equipment. Strength and level both help determine how much gear you can carry before becoming encumbered. ITEM LEVEL ========== Equipment may have an item level showing where it belongs in game progression. Ranked weapons penetrate part of the physical protection from lower-level worn armour; ranked armour gains protection against lower-level weapons. Equal-level ratings cancel. Item level is not automatically a minimum character level—actual restrictions are listed separately. Most equipment found in a cataloged area inherits the midpoint of that area's recommended level range; special rewards may use their own level. Monsters fighting with natural attacks or intrinsic armour use their monster level when no effective weapon or worn armour supplies an item level.

docs.title: Syntax: "exa" or "exa <string>"
docs.text: Syntax: "exa" or "exa <string>" DESCRIPTION =========== With no string, examine the room you are currently standing it. With a string, you can 'exa <string>'. See also: examine, l, gl

docs.title: Syntax: "examine" or "examine <string>"
docs.text: Syntax: "examine" or "examine <string>" DESCRIPTION =========== With no string, examine the room you are currently standing it. With a string, you can 'examine <string>'. See also: examine, l, gl

docs.title: Syntax: get <object> [from <object>]
docs.text: Syntax: get <object> [from <object>] get all <object> [from <object>] DESCRIPTION =========== Get an item. You can also "get all". If the thing you want is in something else, type "get <object> from <object>" such as "get knife from bag". Similarly if you're getting something from a corpse. You would type something like "get coins from corpse" or "get knife from corpse". The second method allows you to get all of one specific object instead of everything. You do do things such as: get all sword OR get all sword from bag. See also: drop, put, give

docs.title: When you are killed, you become a ghost and lose many of the
docs.text: When you are killed, you become a ghost and lose many of the abilities you had while alive. Your spirit is whisked away to the church of the land you died in, and your corpse - holding all of your belongings and gold - travels with you in your inventory. If you are level 5 or under, death carries no penalty at all. Above level 5, death costs you 10% of your experience on hand. Nothing else is lost: no stats, no levels. To return to life, <pray> at the church (the experience loss stands), or have another player resurrect you with a guild ability, which restores the lost experience. Ghosts cannot pick things up, so resurrect first, then unpack your corpse. If you are somehow trapped as a ghost away from a church, the gocot command will carry you to safety. See also: death, ghostemotes, deathavengement

docs.title: Syntax: give <object> to <player>
docs.text: Syntax: give <object> to <player> give all <object> to <player> DESCRIPTION =========== Give an item to a living object. Give all of one particular thing to a living object. give all swords to <player> See Also: drop, get, put

docs.text: Money on DarkWind is measured in terms of gold coins; no self-respecting adventurer would bother dealing with lesser denominations.
