docs.title: Movement
docs.text: Movement Movement within the MUD is quite simple. There are obvious exits listed after the room description in every room. However, pay close attention to those descriptions because there may be secret exits or such actions possible in special rooms. Compass directions have been automatically aliased for you. North = n, South = s, East = e, West = w, Northeast = ne, Northwest = nw, Southeast = se, Southwest = sw, Up = u, Down = d.

docs.text: NPC stands for non-player character. Basically, any creature or person in the game not controlled by a player.

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text: DESCRIPTION =========== Change to a new password. The old password must be given correctly. You will then be prompted twice for the new password. Passwords must be 8 to 16 printable characters long. Spaces are allowed, and every character in the password is significant. If your existing account has no password, use the exact syntax "password <none>" to set one. The angle brackets are required. Do not use your character's name, any combination of it, or 'qwerty'. If someone guesses your password and wreaks havoc with your character, YOU will still be held responsible for your character's actions! Syntax: password <the old password>

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text: DESCRIPTION =========== Put something in or on something else, such as "put bottle in bag." The second form allows you to put all of one specific item on or in something else, such as put all sword in bag OR put all swords in bag Syntax: put <object> <preposition> <object> put all <object> <preposition> <object> See also: drop, give, get

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text: DESCRIPTION =========== Quits the game. Immediately drops all objects in your inventory, saves your character, and logs you out of reality, returning you back to an altered form of reality which some people will try to fool you into thinking is the real reality. Don't believe them. They are wrong. This is reality. Syntax: quit See also: save

docs.title: DarkWind reboots periodically to clear out the junk from memory, catch
docs.text: DarkWind reboots periodically to clear out the junk from memory, catch global code updates, reset once-per-boot areas and whatnot. When the mud reboots, all equipment stored in guilds, shops, boats etc. will disappear, as will ponies and similar helpers. Boats will not disappear, nor will money on or your person or in the bank. The "uptime" command shows how long DarkWind has been up since the last reboot, and when the next scheduled reboot is. Unfortunately, sometimes unscheduled reboots are necessary for a variety of reasons. Players will not be compensated for any losses incurred due to reboots.

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text: DESCRIPTION =========== Save all data about your character. This is also done automatically when quiting the game. Thus, 'save' is only for paranoid players. A restore is done when you log into the game, and only then. Syntax: save See also: quit

docs.title: Syntax: switch, switch <character>
docs.text: Syntax: switch, switch <character> =========== Use switch to list the other characters on your account that can be selected from your current connection. Use switch <character> to move to one of those characters without disconnecting. Switching preserves your connection and parks your current body in the linkdead room. Inventory and equipment stay with each character's body, so switching does not move gear between characters. Parked characters idle out normally after roughly 45 to 60 minutes. You cannot switch while in combat. The same attack-quit cooldown that blocks quitting after combat also blocks switching. Aliases, triggers, highlights, chat history, and scrollback in your client persist because they are scoped to the same server and port.

docs.text: When referencing to items, a number can be used to pick one item of a number of similar items. For example: sell knife 3, exa corpse 2 ,get axe from corpse 2

docs.title: Tutorial
docs.text: Tutorial Darkwind starts a short tutorial for new characters. It teaches the basics without locking you into a separate training area. Commands: tutorial Show your current tutorial step. tutorial status Show whether the tutorial is active, skipped, or finished. tutorial continue Begin the objective shown in the current lesson. tutorial hint Repeat a concrete command suggestion. tutorial skip Stop the tutorial for this character. tutorial restart Start over if you skipped or did not finish. The tutorial covers looking, examining, movement, inventory, the newbie channel, getting starter equipment from Erga, wearing and wielding gear, traveling to the newbie farm, basic combat safety, newbie combat commands, score, and accepting a first newbie quest. In Darkflow, a non-blocking tutorial hover opens automatically and stays with you while the tutorial is active. It shows the current objective, progress, hint, example command, and travel directions without taking focus from the command line. Continue begins each objective. Minimizing the hover does not skip the tutorial. Other clients and screenreader mode receive the complete tutorial in terminal text. Use tutorial continue in place of the hover's Continue button. Every objective, hint, skip, and restart remains available from the command line. During travel lessons, directions are computed from wherever you are actually standing. Tutorial hint includes the current route. If you walk the wrong way for a couple of rooms, the text fallback calls out a correction. If no route can be charted, ncot returns you to the Center of Town so the route can be plotted again. Each lesson also names a help topic to read for the bigger picture, and the journey continues after the tutorial in help guide. Erga's Newbie Shop gives level 1-5 characters free starter gear with the equipment command. The tutorial shows how to wear the leather and shield, wield the dagger, find the newbie farm, and practice kill, wimpy, mon, nheal, nbolt, nkick, npunch, and ncot. # see: guide, stage1

docs.title: Clans: The Basics
docs.text: Clans: The Basics ----------------- Clans cost 1,000,000 coins to start, and require 200,000 coins in monthly dues every 28 days. The Darkwind Clan Registrar automatically deducts the fee from the leader's bank account each month and sends a mudmail detailing the charge. Clans can be formed at the Darkwind Clan Registrar office. Ask other players for directions to this location. At the office you will receive additional information about how to form a new clan. Clans have two ranks: leader and member. There is exactly one leader, and everyone else in a clan is a member. Clans are ranked according to clan reputation. Base clan reputation is calculated from the average clan member level, clan member best kill, and clan member charisma. Additional reputation can be gathered through clan warfare. Every time a clan wins a war, the clan receives additional reputation points based upon the reputation of the defeated clan. Defeating a more reputable clan results in more reputation points. Clan warfare is only one aspect of clans. A clan isn't required to engage in warfare. A war can only start if two clan leaders agree to go to war. Thus, it's possible to have peaceful clans where the leader never agrees to go to war. Please see "help clans" for a basic overview. Please see "help clans war" for warfare information. Please see "help clans cmds" for clan command information.

docs.title: Clans: An Overview
docs.text: Clans: An Overview ------------------ Clans are first and foremost a social medium, allowing players the ability to form organized groups outside the confines of guilds. In addition to the purely social aspect of clans, clans also add to the game by allowing for clan warfare. Non-warfare features of clans: -- Clan channel -- Clan headquarters ** Place to store items and equipment ** Place to deposit money into a shared clan coffers -- Customized clan emote -- Clan rankings and reputations Warfare-specific features of clans: -- Ability to mutually agree to a war with another clan leader -- Detailed post-war information (# kills, best kill, etc) -- Opportunity to increase clan reputation rapidly -- All clan wars are set in duration (minimum of 3 days) -- Clan warfare ignores normal PK status (ie. Non-PKers can kill/be killed) Please see "help clans basics" for a more detailed intro to clans. Please see "help clans war" for warfare information. Please see "help clans cmds" for clan command information.

docs.title: Clan: Commands
docs.text: Clan: Commands -------------- Available to the entire MUD: cwar <#> -- Look at information from wars that have already ended. cwar list The information accessed via this command is deleted over time. Older wars vanish after awhile, etc. clans -- List the available clans on Darkwind. claninfo <clan> -- Read information about a particular clan. who <clan> -- See who is logged on from a particular clan. wclan -- Show all clan members logged on, sorted by clan reputation. wclan leader -- Show all clan leaders logged on, sorted by clan reputation. Available to anyone in a clan: cl/ecl <msg> -- Talk/emote on your clan channel. clhist -- Display clan channel history. clwho -- See who is logged in from your clan. cstat -- See statistics about your clan. clleave -- Leave your clan. clemote -- Clan emote. Works on channels like normal emotes. Leaders can talk to James to have the emote customized for their clan. cvote -- Vote on outstanding clan issue (listed in cstat). checkclan -- Check if you have unread message on your clan board. Available to clan members while in the Clan Operations Room: cdeposit <coins> -- Deposit money into clan coffers. cwithdraw <coins> -- Withdraw money from clan coffers. cbalance -- Show the number of coins currently in the coffers. Available to clan leaders: leadercmds -- List all your leader-only commands. cinitiate -- Add someone to your clan. cdismiss -- Dismiss someone from your clan. cdeclare -- Ask a clan leader if he/she wants to start a war. changedesc -- Change description of a room in clan headquarters. Can only be used while in one of the rooms. cdescribe -- Change the information shown in 'claninfo' caddissue -- Add issue for members to vote on. cdelissue -- Remove outstanding issue, preventing additional votes. ctithe -- Set your clan automatic tithe amount. Please see "help clans" for a basic overview. Please see "help clans basics" for a more detailed intro to clans. Please see "help clans war" for warfare information.

docs.title: Clans: Warfare
docs.text: Clans: Warfare --------------- The clan system allows two clans to agree to go to war with each other. This decision is made by the leader of each clan. All wars are set in duration, with the smallest war allowed being 3 days. Please read the information in "help clan_cmds" for details about starting a war. Once a war starts, it is impossible to initiate new members into the clan and current members of the clan aren't allowed to leave. There are no exceptions to this rule. During a war, clans gain points. The points are gained by killing members of the opposing clan. The number of points awarded per kill is largely based by the level difference between the killer and the victim. Members who kill enemies of greater or equal level than themselves receive more points than members who kill enemies at lower levels. A clan is much more likely to win a war if everyone goes after the hardest opponent they can successfully kill, rather than going after the weakest opponent over and over. During a war clan members can look at ongoing war statistics via the 'cstat' command. After a war, a variety of details are saved and can be accessed via the 'cwar' command. There is no way to stop a war early. Once a war starts, the clans involved must deal with it. As mentioned in 'help clans', normal PK status is ignored during a war. Non-PKers can, and will, be killed during a clan war. Of course, Non-PKers can kill as well. During a low-risk clanwar, you will not lose level, stats, etc. During a high-risk clanwar, deaths will be treated as if you were actually PK. Enjoy, and may the best clan win. Please see "help clans" for a basic overview. Please see "help clans basics" for a more detailed intro to clans. Please see "help clans cmds" for clan command information

docs.text: Darkwind supports Giphy integration on supported channels and in the web client. docs.text: Syntax: ignore <name> ignore list unignore <name> DESCRIPTION =========== This command allows you to ignore certain players' tells and emotes. This is handy when a player (Or wizard) is bothering you and won't leave you alone. This command will allow you to ignore more than one person as well. If you decide at a later time that you want to start talking to that person again, just 'unignore <name>', where name is the person you want to quit ignoring. You can also 'ignore list' to see who you are ignoring. If someone has you ignored, do not attempt to go around the ignore. This counts in PK as well. Just leave them alone. Failure to do so will result in punishment.

docs.title: Although many languages exist on DarkWind, adventurers can get away, for
docs.text: Although many languages exist on DarkWind, adventurers can get away, for the most part, by using the language known as "common". The common tongue originated among the humans living in and around the City of Darkwind, and grew in popularity as the city gained in prominance in the affairs of the world. All players can automatically speak common, by using the "csay" command. In addition, many socities are fluent in one or more other languages. Some of these languages are racially based, while some are more regional in nature. Players can speak in their native language using the "rsay" command. Those that do not have a native language will speak in common. It is possible for those of sufficient intellect to study at a language academy and learn additional languages as well. The "say" command will allow you to speak in your default language. If you know more than just common, you can switch your default language using the "set language" command.

docs.title: Syntax: auction <item> <starting bid> [extra info]
docs.text: Syntax: auction <item> <starting bid> [extra info] ===================================================================== The auction block is a live, world-wide auction called over the auction channel. Only one item can be on the block at a time, mud-wide. Selling: auction <item> <bid> hands an item from your inventory to the auctioneer, who holds it in escrow while the bidding runs. The starting bid must be at least 1000 coins. Worn, wielded, no-drop, temporary, and soon-expiring unique items cannot be auctioned. If nobody bids within 90 seconds the auction closes and the item comes back to you; you can also stopauction before the first bid. Either way, the auctioneer keeps a 100 coin handling fee. Bidding: bid <amount> places a bid, and bid up offers the next valid amount. Each bid must top the last by at least 250 coins. Bids are backed by your bank account, not your pockets: the coins must be available in the bank, and a lien is held on them until you are outbid or the auction ends. See help bank. Winning and collecting: a minute after the last bid the auctioneer calls going once, going twice, sold. The winner's coins are withdrawn from the bank and the item is handed over on the spot (or set at your feet if it is too heavy to carry). The seller's proceeds, minus the auctioneer's 10% cut of the winning bid, are deposited straight into the seller's bank account, even if the seller has since logged out. auctioninfo shows the current item, seller, and high bid, and auctionhist reviews recent auction traffic. You cannot start or bid on an auction from rooms that block teleportation. See also: bank, market, economy # alias: auctions, auctionhouse

docs.title: Syntax: balance, deposit <amount>, withdraw <amount>,
docs.text: Syntax: balance, deposit <amount>, withdraw <amount>, transfer <amount> from <alt>, lien ===================================================================== Banks keep your coins safe and power the bidding economy. All branches share a single account, opened automatically the first time you walk into a bank. The commands above only work inside a bank. deposit <amount> Move coins from your pockets into the bank. withdraw <amount> Take coins back out. balance Show balance, liens, and amount available. transfer <amount> from <alt> Pull coins from one of your own registered alts' accounts into this character's account. lien Show any lien held against your account. Use "all" in place of an amount to move everything at once. Ghosts cannot bank; get resurrected first. Liens: part of your balance can be held in escrow for a pending deal, most commonly an outstanding auction bid or a pub purchase. Liened coins stay yours but cannot be withdrawn until the deal completes or falls through. balance always shows how much is free and clear. The bank pays no interest -- it offers safekeeping, not growth. Coins must be on deposit to back auction bids, so keep your bidding money banked (see help auction). Branches operate in most large settlements, including the Bank of DarkWind in DarkWind City, the Souvrael Money Handlers in Souvrael, and the Grimsfjord Banking House in Hyperborea. Any branch reaches the same account. See also: auction, economy, money # alias: banks, banking

docs.title: THE BROOD APOTHECARY
docs.text: THE BROOD APOTHECARY ==================== The Brood Apothecary is a DarkWind City shop that sells parasite carriers: larvae, worms, cysts, fleas, and stranger living bargains. These carriers can be swallowed or eaten to grant elevated hit point regeneration, spell point regeneration, or both for a finite amount of online time. The shop is south of Xenor Road. Its stock is level-gated, and some parasites have additional host requirements. SHOP COMMANDS ============= list parasites Shows available parasite carriers. describe parasite <number or name> Shows the required level, regen per pulse, cost, duration, appetite, and penalties for a parasite. buy <number> Buys the numbered parasite carrier from the shop list. purge parasite Removes your active parasite for a fee. After buying a carrier, hold it and use swallow <parasite> or eat <parasite> to install it. Use parasite afterward to inspect the infection. See also: help parasites.

docs.title: DarkWind's economy covers markets, goods, money sinks, and the ways players
docs.text: DarkWind's economy covers markets, goods, money sinks, and the ways players earn and spend coin across the world. Common topics in this section include: help economy market help economy lottery help economy brood apothecary Use help list economy to see every topic in this section.

docs.title: Darkwind Lottery
docs.text: Darkwind Lottery ----------------------------------------------------------------------- The Darkwind lottery system allows players to gamble to try to better themselves, and their pocket books. The lottery is played once per boot, with a winner chosen 2 days into a boot. A reminder is given 30 minutes, 10 minutes, and 1 minute before the end of the lottery. The lottery system works much like a raffle - players buy tickets for the lottery, bettering their overall odds of winning. Players may only buy 75 tickets, per lottery, at 1000 coins per ticket. The prize pot is directly dependent on the total number of tickets sold to the lottery, therefore it's important to get as many of your friends to buy tickets as possible. It is not guaranteed that a winner will be chosen for each lottery. If no winner is chosen, the prize pot will be saved and added to the next boot lottery. -----------------------------------------------------------------------

docs.title: The Darkwind world-wide market is a player driven economy system
docs.text: The Darkwind world-wide market is a player driven economy system that allows players to sell things on a price they set. Players can sell things from each city's market (found near the main shop in each city). Other players may buy from the market from most any room on Darkwind. Commands involved in the market are: marketcmds - The prompt to show all commands available for the market system. marketbuy # - This will allow a player to buy the item from the room in which the player is in. The money must be on hand. marketlist - This will display all items available for purchase on the market. marketshow # - This will display the description of the item that is availabe on market. marketmylist - This will show all the items that you have for sale on the market this boot. marketmysales - This will show you all the items that have been bought from you this boot.

docs.title: Combat Archetypes
docs.text: # Combat Archetypes Guild and class abilities can be described through three combat archetypes: Caster, Melee, and Hybrid. This describes how a toolkit plays; it does not make a class into a learned guild. ## Caster Caster toolkits have few inherent bonuses to ordinary weapon combat. They generally have large SP pools and efficient abilities. ## Melee Melee toolkits are almost the reverse: they have strong inherent bonuses to combat, including additional swings. ## Hybrid Hybrid toolkits fall in between. They have some bonuses to combat but typically have higher SP pools than melee toolkits and more efficient abilities. ## See also help guilds help classes

docs.title: Bard
docs.text: Bard Bards are flexible performers who mix combat, support, control, scouting, and social manipulation. They trade narrow specialization for a broad toolkit that can keep a party moving or adapt when a fight changes shape. How it plays Songs build Performance, especially when the Bard varies rhythm, melody, harmony, dissonance, crescendo, and finale forms. Many songs create fields that follow the Bard and pulse over nearby allies or enemies. Charisma strengthens those performances, while instruments and a later archetype choice reshape the songbook. Core skills pulsebeat builds momentum, soothe and rally support allies, dirgeash and wail pressure enemies, and battlefieldsilence disrupts hostile casting. Perform, fame, defame, lore, and study give the guild useful tools away from direct combat. Best fit Choose Bard if you enjoy rotating abilities, reacting to the room, helping a group, and discovering combinations instead of repeating one attack. Bards can use broad equipment, though heavy gear interferes with subtler techniques. After joining, use bardhelp general, bardhelp songs, and bardhelp archetypes for the full guide. # alias: bards

docs.title: The Berserker Guild
docs.text: # The Berserker Guild Berserkers are melee warriors who turn injury and combat pressure into Fury. When Fury peaks, it can erupt as Frenzy: a rapid series of attacks that spends the accumulated rage against the Berserker's current enemy. Experienced Berserkers can restrain Frenzy and let excess Fury become Madness. Madness increases their violence and resilience, but its highest levels carry serious risks. The bvent command can clear Fury and Madness after combat. ## Core skills Berserkers can use benrage to trade health for Fury, frenzymode to control automatic or directed Frenzy, and bvent to recover control. Vex techniques such as primal_strike, rend, and wildrage add offense and momentum, while awakened scars and Flare provide permanent late-game identity. ## Rank, Vex, and scars Berserkers advance through a separate Berserker Rank earned in combat. Each Rank grants Vex that can be trained through the Blood, Momentum, and Defiance branches. Permanent scars record exceptional ordeals and can later be awakened with Flare. ## Equipment and joining Berserkers may use light, medium, or heavy armour, including shields. Their training pit lies west of the plain on Darkwind's southern shore. Join there with join berserker when you meet the guild requirements. ## Useful commands berhelp Read the full member guide bstatus Review Rank, XP, Vex, Fury, and Madness berskills List abilities and trained Vex techniques vex tree Review the three advancement branches scars Review permanent scars and their effects frenzymode Control automatic or directed Frenzy berserkers List visible Berserkers online ## See also help guilds help guilds equipment help guilds gscore # alias: berserkers

docs.title: Charlatan
docs.text: Charlatan Charlatans are tricksters who weaponize misdirection, unstable chemistry, contraband, prepared surprises, and confidence. Their victories often begin with the enemy believing the wrong thing at exactly the wrong time. How it plays Combat earns Charlatan Rank and guild XP. Rank grants road points for Misdirection, Volatility, and Contraband; higher ranks unlock Schemes that can be slotted as active cloak notes. Alchemy, Herbalism, and Smithing remain real professions that support the guild's technical tricks. Core skills confuse creates an opening, suckerpunch exploits it, distract and pocketsand control a foe, brewacid and brewelement create unstable mixtures, loadweapon and stretchpoison prepare contraband, and concoct or cookash turn questionable materials into useful results. Best fit Choose Charlatan if you enjoy setup, control, crafting support, horizontal build choices, and a toolkit with several indirect answers instead of a single clean combat identity. After joining, use charlhelp commands, chskills, croads, and schemes to inspect the full confidence game. # alias: charlatans

docs.title: Classes
docs.text: # Classes Classes describe what a character innately is. They alter the character's body, mind, nature, or relationship with the world. Unlike guilds, classes are not learned disciplines. See help guilds for skills and traditions a character can learn. ## Class roster Developer Class Status (Cales) Artificer [COMING] (Acer) Dragon [OPEN] (Acer) Morpher [CLOSED] (Cales) Psionicist [OPEN] (Acer) Vampire [OPEN] ## See also help guilds help guilds archetypes help guilds roles help guilds equipment # alias: class

docs.title: Cleric of Mitra
docs.text: Cleric of Mitra Mitra's Clerics are holy healers and defensive battle-priests. They protect and strengthen companions, remove dangerous afflictions, and bring divine force against evil rather than relying on a pure damage rotation. How it plays A Cleric shifts between triage, prevention, and punishment. Healing and renewal keep allies standing; blessings, insulation, holy light, and summoned guardians prepare a group for danger. At the highest levels, a Cleric can even restore the dead to life. Core skills cure and renew restore allies, bless and insulate provide protection, hammer creates the guild's sacred weapon, sunray and flamestrike attack evil, turn repels undead, and resurrect returns a fallen adventurer. Best fit Choose Cleric if you want a supportive caster who can fight, value group survival and utility, and are comfortable serving Mitra and opposing evil. Clerics share faith, facilities, and purpose with Mitra's Paladins. After joining, use clerics and the Cleric help topics for spell and service details. # alias: clerics, cleric_mitra, cleric of mitra, mitra cleric

docs.title: Guild and Class Developers
docs.text: # Guild and Class Developers ## Guilds Acer: Bard, Cleric of Mitra, Fighter, Paladin, Druid, Monk, Ranger, Street Samurai Cales: Berserker, Mage, Ninja, Priest of Set, Swashbuckler, Thief, Necro, Charlatan, Blood Mage, Deathknights Dink: Garou, Bastet/Gurahl ## Classes Acer: Dragon, Morpher, Vampire Cales: Artificer, Psionicist ## See also help guilds help classes

docs.title: Guild Combinations
docs.text: # Guild Combinations You may hold at most two learned guilds, and a second guild opens at level 50. Both guilds must accept the pairing; race, allegiance, and each guild's own joining requirements still apply. Classes describe what a character innately is and are not part of the dual-guild system. ## The groups Neutral: Bard, Berserker, Charlatan, Fighter, Psionicist, Street Samurai, Swashbuckler Gaea: Druid, Garou, Lunar, Ninja Mitra: Cleric of Mitra, Mage, Paladin Set: Priest, Thief ## What pairs with what Neutral guilds pair with each other and with any Gaea, Mitra, or Set guild -- with one exception: Street Samurai. The Gaea guilds will not take one whose flesh is threaded with chrome, and no street samurai will kneel to the green. Street samurai may still pair with the other neutrals and with the Mitra and Set guilds. Gaea guilds (Druid, Garou, Lunar, Ninja) pair with each other and with the neutral guilds except Street Samurai. In addition: * Garou may also pair with Thief and Ranger. Mitra guilds (Cleric of Mitra, Mage, Paladin) pair with each other and with all seven neutral guilds. They do not mix with Gaea or Set. Set guilds (Priest, Thief) pair with each other and with all seven neutral guilds. Thief may also pair with Garou. Ranger pairs only with Garou. ## Solo guilds Dragon, Monk, Morpher, Necro, Vampire, and BloodMage walk alone: their disciplines permit no second guild. BattleMage, Deathknight, Glyph, and UberGarou are special orders with their own entry requirements -- ask their halls, not this list. ## See also help guilds help classes help dual guilds

docs.title: Druid
docs.text: Druid Druids are warrior-priests of Gaea who combine elemental invocations, prepared rituals, Sacred Groves, companions, and gathered materials. Their magic changes with terrain, planets, moons, and the natural world around them. How it plays Invocations spend four Nwyfre currents: Tellurian, Daloan, Marken, and Tekali. Rituals restore or reshape those currents, while mastery improves each learned invocation. A Druid also gathers herbs, creature reagents, skins, ores, and special materials for rituals and companions. Core skills spirit aura is an early invocation; entangle, frostbolt, lightning, flameblade, renewal, and earthmeld show the elemental range. Grove plant creates a personal wilderness sanctuary, commune returns to it, ritual prepares longer effects, and companions add animal allies. Best fit Choose Druid if you want a deep hybrid with multiple resources, preparation, world-sensitive magic, gathering, and a permanent place in the wilderness. The guild rewards planning more than a fixed spell rotation. After joining, begin with dhelp beginner, then explore dhelp nwyfre, dhelp ritual, and dhelp grove. # alias: druids

docs.title: Dual Guilding.
docs.text: Dual Guilding. ___________________________ Players have the option of joining a second guild once they have attained CHAMPION status at level 50. Classes describe what a character innately is. They are separate from learned guild membership and are not choices in the dual-guild system. There are many restrictions on the available guilds that can be chosen as your 'second' guild, including, * Your Race * Your Allegiance to a particular god. * Your existing guilds philosophical beliefs. * The Exisiting restrictions already in place for joining that guild. There might be guilds that remain solo guilds purely due to the stringent requirements and discipline required to undertake those role. You may not join more than 2 guilds. Grimtilla will remove either guild for the nominated fee. You can checkout the guilds you are able to join via "help combos" See Also: coders, guilds, classes, combos

docs.title: Guild Emotes
docs.text: Guild Emotes Guild emotes are social actions reserved for active members of a guild. They behave like standard feelings: they can have untargeted, targeted, and free-text forms, work in rooms, and can be used through guild channels that support colon emotes. Player commands feelings guild - list every guild emote available to you feelings guild <guild> - list emotes for one of your guilds feelings guild <guild> <prefix> - filter that guild's list semote <emote> - preview each supported form emoteapropos guild [<guild>] <text> - search guild emote messages random [<player>] - invoke a random available global or guild emote A guild emote stops working immediately if you leave the guild or if that guild's abilities become inactive. Seeing the result of an emote does not grant access to use it. Architect commands addemote -guild <guild> <name> [<rule>] showemote -guild <guild> <name> rmemote -guild <guild> <name> [<rule>] The guild name is matched case-insensitively against the configured guild list. Guild emotes use the standard addemote rule grammar, messages, preview, and optional variable-emote redirects. They are stored separately from global emotes and persist with the emote daemon. New names must not collide with a global emote, another guild's emote, or an available command. Use showemote -guild before editing or removing a definition. Omitting -guild operates on the global emote with that name, not the guild definition. See also: addemote, emotes, emoteapropos, feelings, random, rmemote, semote, showemote # alias: guild_emotes, guildemotes

docs.title: Guild and Class Equipment Guidance
docs.text: # Guild and Class Equipment Guidance Guild and class equipment rules are checked when you try to wear armour or wield a weapon. These are practical guidelines for normal equipment; special items can still directly allow or restrict specific guilds or classes. Important notes - Specific bans are checked before specific allows. - Specific allows are checked before broad bans. - Item-level guild or class allow/restrict flags override the normal table. - Size, damage type, armour composition, slot, and material can all matter. ## Guilds Fighter Weapons: any normal weapon. Armour: any normal armour or shield. Materials: no normal material restriction. Paladin Weapons: any normal weapon. Armour: any normal armour or shield. Materials: no normal material restriction. Bard Weapons: any normal weapon. Armour: no plate, scale, or shields. Materials: no normal material restriction outside those armour types. Cleric of Mitra Weapons: blunt weapons only. Slash, cleave, and pierce weapons are not allowed. Armour: any normal armour or shield. Materials: no normal material restriction. Priest of Set Weapons: any normal weapon. Armour: no plate armour. Materials: no normal material restriction outside plate armour. Garou Weapons: avoid magical, missile, silver, and most metal weapons. Polearms are the normal weapon exception. Armour: avoid magical, silver, plate, and metal armour. Rings and amulets are explicitly supported. Some Gaea-touched auras are specially allowed. Materials: silver is forbidden; most metal equipment is forbidden unless a specific exception applies. Mage Weapons: no medium, large, or huge slash, pierce, or cleave weapons. Small weapons, blunt weapons, focus-style items, and other non-blade options are the safer choices. Armour: no plate or shields. Padded cloth, leather boots, leather gloves, leather cloaks, rings, and amulets are explicitly supported. Materials: broad armour restrictions hit metal, leather, rock, and wood unless a specific allowed slot/material exception applies. Necro Uses the same normal equipment profile as Mage. Weapons: avoid medium or larger slash, pierce, and cleave weapons. Armour: no plate or shields; light cloth/leather utility slots are safest. Materials: broad armour restrictions hit metal, leather, rock, and wood unless a specific allowed exception applies. Blood Mage Uses the same normal equipment profile as Mage. Weapons: avoid medium or larger slash, pierce, and cleave weapons. Armour: no plate or shields; light cloth/leather utility slots are safest. Materials: broad armour restrictions hit metal, leather, rock, and wood unless a specific allowed exception applies. Thief Weapons: no large, huge, or pole weapons. Armour: small shields, rings, amulets, hide, padded, and studded armour are explicitly supported. Avoid plate, scale, chain, banded, and most shields. Materials: avoid metal, rock, glass, and crystal armour unless a specific allowed type applies. Ninja Weapons: no large or huge weapons in general. Polearms and blunt weapons are explicit exceptions. Armour: no shields. Rings, amulets, and auras are explicitly supported. Avoid plate, scale, banded, and chain. Materials: avoid metal armour unless a specific allowed slot applies. Swashbuckler Weapons: no huge weapons, large cleaving weapons, missile weapons, or polearms. Armour: no plate or shields. Amulets, boots, hide, padded armour, and rings are explicitly supported. Avoid banded, chain, scale, plate, and shields. Materials: avoid crystal, glass, metal, rock, and wood armour unless a specific allowed type applies. ## Additional guilds Druid Weapons: nature-friendly gear is safest. Small weapons, large or huge blunt weapons, missile weapons, polearms, and weapons made from rock, natural, wood, bone, glass, crystal, gold, or gem materials are explicitly supported. Avoid metal medium weapons and metal slash/cleave/pierce weapons. Armour: small shields, rings, amulets, and wood, rock, natural, bone, glass, crystal, gem, gold, or silver armour are explicitly supported. Avoid large and huge shields, and avoid metal plate, chain, scale, banded, and shields unless a specific material exception applies. Materials: natural materials are best. Metal is usually trouble; gold and silver have specific armour exceptions. Ranger Weapons: any normal weapon. Armour: no plate or scale. Studded leather, studded cloth, magical chain, rings, and amulets are explicitly supported. Materials: no broad material restriction outside the plate/scale armour ban. Monk Weapons: only the supported staff-like profile is allowed: medium polearm and blunt. Armour: only auras are allowed. Materials: all normal weapon and armour materials are restricted unless the item fits the allowed weapon profile or aura slot. Berserker Weapons: any normal weapon. Armour: light, medium, or heavy armour, including shields. Materials: no normal material restriction. ## Classes Class restrictions reflect what a character innately is rather than a learned guild discipline. Psionicist Weapons: avoid large and huge weapons, especially slash, pierce, and cleave weapons. Blunt polearms with the supported size/type combination are the notable exception. Armour: no helmets, plate, chain, scale, banded, or shields. Materials: leather, natural, and cloth armour are explicitly supported. Morpher Weapons: no large, huge, or missile weapons. Armour: no plate or chain. Materials: no normal material restriction outside those weapon and armour types. ## Quick material reminders Metal includes steel, iron, silver, gold, mithril, adamantite, bronze, brass, tin, lead, copper, and platinum. Natural-friendly materials usually include natural, wood, rock, bone, glass, crystal, gem, cloth, leather, skin, fur, flowers, and similar non-metal materials, though each guild or class still checks slot and armour/weapon type. ## See also help basics equipment help mechanics equip help guilds help classes

docs.title: Fighter
docs.text: Fighter Fighters are durable weapon masters built for direct, dependable combat. They can use almost any weapon or armour and develop a large set of attacks, defensive reactions, rescue tools, and battlefield controls. How it plays Worthy combat earns Fighter XP and raises Guild Level automatically. Defensive toggles such as counter, feint, guts, and shieldblock spend Endurance when they trigger; fsurge restores that reserve. The result is an active front line that can change stance and protect others instead of merely absorbing hits. Core skills bash disrupts a foe, cleave attacks with force, disarm removes a weapon, fcharge closes on an enemy, fdefend guards an ally, and shield techniques, counterattacks, frenzy, and surge cover defense and sustained pressure. Best fit Choose Fighter if you want broad equipment freedom, clear martial tools, strong survivability, and a guild that rewards learning when to attack, interrupt, defend, or recover Endurance. After joining, use fhelp advancement, fhelp endurance, and fs for the full skill list. # alias: fighters

docs.title: Garou
docs.text: Garou Garou are shapechanging defenders of Gaea who fight through physical power, spiritual gifts, and three distinct forms: human, crinos, and wolf. Each form changes equipment access, communication, defenses, and available techniques. How it plays Human form handles ordinary equipment and spiritual work, crinos blends weapons with natural strength, and wolf form gives up equipment for the guild's strongest natural combat. Garou also dedicate themselves toward Warrior, Guardian, or Shaman priorities and must respect Gaea's equipment and behavioral restrictions. Core skills transform changes form, enrage builds violence, fclaw and fbite use natural weapons, howl and scent coordinate the hunt, eat restores a wolf from a corpse, and sanctify, summon, and other spiritual gifts support Gaea's cause. Best fit Choose Garou if you want form management, aggressive natural combat, self-recovery, and a strong nature-bound identity with meaningful equipment tradeoffs. After joining, use ghelp basics, ghelp dedication, and ghelp equipment for the full guide. # alias: werewolf, werewolves, garous

docs.title: Guild Score (gscore)
docs.text: Guild Score (gscore) ___________________________ The 'gscore' command (alias 'guildscore') shows one block per learned guild or innate class recorded on your character: * Guild or class level or Rank, and the maximum where one applies. * What your next advance costs - guild XP earned in battle (Fighter, Paladin, Cleric of Mitra, Priest, Berserker), experience, or carried gold for the Thief guild. * Berserkers also see how much Vex they have to spend. Your main learned guild is marked (main). A guild or class your current equipment restricts is marked (inactive). See Also: guilds, classes, dual_guilds, guild, sc

docs.title: Guilds
docs.text: # Guilds Guilds are disciplines, organizations, faiths, and traditions that teach skills. A guild is something your character learns to do; it is not something your character innately is. See help classes for innate character classes. ## Guild roster Every open guild has a public preview. Use help <guild>, such as help bard, help monk, or help street samurai, to see its combat identity, core mechanics, representative skills, and playstyle before joining. Developer Guild Status (Acer) Bard [OPEN] (Cales) Berserker [OPEN] (Acer) Cleric of Mitra [OPEN] (Acer) Fighter [OPEN] (Dink) Garou [OPEN] (Cales) Mage [OPEN] (Cales) Ninja [OPEN] (Acer) Paladin [OPEN] (Cales) Priest of Set [OPEN] (Cales) Swashbuckler [OPEN] (Cales) Thief [OPEN] (Acer) Druid [OPEN] (Acer) Monk [OPEN] (Cales) Necro [OPEN] (Acer) Ranger [OPEN] (Dink) Bastet/Gurahl [CLOSED] (Cales) Charlatan [OPEN] (Cales) Blood Mage [CLOSED] (Cales) Deathknights [CLOSED] (Acer) Street Samurai [OPEN] ## See also help classes help guilds roles help guilds archetypes help guilds equipment help dual guilds

docs.title: Mage
docs.text: Mage Mages are adaptable spellcasters who turn research, repeated field use, runes, and specialized equipment into increasingly refined magic. Their range includes direct damage, defense, control, travel, detection, and recovery. How it plays Combat and useful casting earn Arcane progress. Each working advances from Copied through Instinctive mastery, reducing costs and opening rune sockets. Practiced combat workings can become automatic barrages, while FOCUS weapons and AURA equipment create a battlemage path alongside ordinary casting. Core skills mshard and missile provide early attacks; analyze and detect reveal information; protection, stasis, phase, and gate control danger and movement; recollection restores spell power; inscribe and runes customize mastered workings. Best fit Choose Mage if you enjoy a large spellbook, long-term mastery, build customization, and deciding whether each fight calls for a cast, a barrage, control, or utility. After joining, use magehelp, spellbook, spells, and research to explore the full system. # alias: magi, mages

docs.title: Monk
docs.text: Monk Monks are ascetic martial artists who turn body, breath, and discipline into weapons. They give up wealth, heavy equipment, marriage, oaths, and other ordinary ambitions for bare-handed combat, Chi, styles, and chained techniques. How it plays Chi fuels abilities and inner defense. Techniques create combo tags and flow from opener to bridge to finisher; changing among tiger, crane, snake, monkey, and dragon styles alters how those routes behave. Training and challenge award notches along a long path toward mastery. Core skills meditate and chifocus manage Chi, opunch and ckick begin martial routes, grapple and lsweep control opponents, chiblast projects force, resuscitate aids an ally, and tdeath represents the lethal end of the discipline. Best fit Choose Monk if you want deliberate melee combos, resource timing, style switching, and strong thematic restrictions. Do not choose it for wealth, heavy armour, or effortless weapon swapping. After joining, use monkhelp basics, monkhelp chi, and monkhelp combos for the complete discipline. # alias: monks

docs.title: Guilds and Classes
docs.text: # Guilds and Classes The old "mythic guild" category mixed learned guilds with innate classes. That category is retired. Guilds are skills, disciplines, faiths, and traditions a character learns. Classes describe what a character innately is. Use help guilds for the current learned-guild roster and help classes for the current innate-class roster. ## See also help guilds help classes help dual guilds # alias: mythic_guilds

docs.title: Necro
docs.text: Necro Necros are physically fragile death-mages who combine destructive spells, curses, runes, battlefield control, and undead followers. They rely on magical preparation and minion management rather than ordinary armour and weapons. How it plays Two personal runes support the Necro's spell catalog and supernatural power. The guild can raise and direct undead, spread diseases and curses, protect itself with deathly wards, and escalate a fight through rituals and sustained spell pressure. Core skills nraise creates an undead follower, nliege and nmarch direct minions, ncurse, npox, nfester, and nplague weaken enemies, nburst and ndeath provide damage, nbshield and nward defend the caster, and nritual prepares deeper necromancy. Best fit Choose Necro if you enjoy caster fragility, commanding followers, combining afflictions, and managing a dangerous toolkit whose strength comes from death rather than direct martial durability. After joining, use nechelp intro, nechelp spell, and nechelp follower for the full grimoire. # alias: necromancer, necromancers, necros

docs.title: Ninja
docs.text: Ninja Ninja are stealthy assassins who combine practiced martial techniques, meditative enhancement, information gathering, and chained attacks. They value Dexterity, Intelligence, and Wisdom and accept tighter armour restrictions than ordinary warriors. How it plays Unique assassination marks prove Guild Level, while combat GXP raises Ninja Rank and supports skill training. Individual techniques improve through practice. Focus and meditation prepare enhancements, and compatible attacks can be linked into combinations with stronger resulting effects. Core skills fade and onmitsu conceal the Ninja, shuriken attacks at range, tsuki, kekomi, pummel, and tsubo build martial sequences, cripple controls movement, dimmak and heartstop provide lethal finishers, and ntrack follows a mark. Best fit Choose Ninja if you enjoy training individual skills, planning combos, stealth, and deliberate target hunting more than broad armour access or a simple automatic rotation. After joining, use ninhelp, skills, practice, and ncheck for progression details. # alias: ninjas

docs.title: Paladin
docs.text: Paladin Paladins are Mitra's armoured holy warriors. They combine direct martial combat with protection, judgment, mobility, and support, taking a more aggressive front-line role than Mitra's Clerics. How it plays Worthy battle earns Paladin XP and raises Guild Level. Each level also grants Devotion points that shape a personal selection of holy benefits. Alignment and Charisma matter: evil cuts a Paladin off from Mitra, while higher ranks demand stronger spiritual presence. Core skills smite and retribution punish enemies, courage and hpresence strengthen the faithful, repel drives back evil, sanctify and consecrate prepare holy ground, javelin provides divine reach, rush closes distance, and warhorse summons a sacred mount. Best fit Choose Paladin if you want a principled tank or holy bruiser with armour, party protection, customization through Devotions, and a strict commitment to Mitra's alignment. After joining, use palhelp advancement, palskills, and devote for the full path. # alias: paladins

docs.title: Priest of Set
docs.text: Priest of Set Priests of Set are evil ritualists who wield curses, darkness, decay, coercion, and death. Their ceremonial dagger anchors a hostile divine toolkit that is intentionally very different from Mitra's protective faith. How it plays A Priest manages dark conviction and pacts while weakening enemies before the decisive rite. The guild mixes direct spell damage with afflictions, life-draining, summoned aid, resurrection, and religious utility. Its powers and identity require commitment to Set and an evil path. Core skills fragility opens defenses, dreadspike and gstrike deal damage, anathema and objurgate condemn targets, leech steals vitality, familiar calls dark assistance, mend and respite provide limited recovery, and resurrection returns the dead under Set's influence. Best fit Choose Priest of Set if you want a sinister caster built around debuffs, ritual pressure, resource planning, and explicitly evil roleplay rather than a neutral healer in darker colours. After joining, use priesthelp, prayers, dfavor, and dpact for the complete doctrine. # alias: priests, priest_set, priest of set, set priest, dark cleric

docs.title: Ranger
docs.text: Ranger Rangers are self-sufficient wilderness specialists who combine tracking, terrain knowledge, crafting, archery, close combat, camps, concealment, nature magic, and animal companions. How it plays A Ranger chooses primary and secondary terrain, favored quarry, and a personal skill tree. Terrain changes damage, costs, recovery, and available companions. Survival work turns wood, hide, ore, herbs, and trophies into tools, weapons, ammunition, salves, poisons, and camps. Core skills survey and rtrack read the land, forage and harvest gather supplies, camp creates a field base, attract finds a companion, conceal and ambush prepare an opening, quickshot and heartshot support archery, and strike, gash, impale, winterbite, and naturestrike cover close combat and magic. Best fit Choose Ranger if you enjoy preparation, exploration, crafting, pets, and adapting to terrain. It offers exceptional breadth, but expects more fieldwork and planning than a purely martial guild. After joining, use ranhelp general, skilltree, survey, and rscore for the full field guide. # alias: rangers

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: # Roles How a guild or class fulfills its theme and story can be thought of as a role. Different guilds and classes can share roles, so their adventuring tools may overlap without changing what they fundamentally are. Roles describe capabilities. Guilds remain learned skills and traditions; classes remain innate parts of a character. ## Bruiser Typically melee-based damage dealers, bruisers have a mix of self preservation and enhancement abilities - typically directly impacting how they fight. Their direct damage abilities are not usually efficient. ## Healer Healers excel at... healing. They usually have ways to heal themselves or others, can prevent damage, and might have increased regeneration. Resurrection abilities are generally limited to healer toolkits. ## Nuker Nuker toolkits generally have good or great resource efficiency with powerful damage abilities. ## Specialist Rather than direct effects, specialists manipulate themselves, allies, enemies, or the environment for a benefit. Information-gathering toolkits typically fall into the specialist role. ## Tank Tank toolkits excel at taking damage. They can generally handle the threat of relatively higher-level creatures, are often found in the toughest armour, and generally have high health pools. ## See also help guilds help classes

docs.title: Street Samurai
docs.text: Street Samurai Street Samurai are cybernetic combat specialists whose Cortex OS links signature implants into one platform. They earn guild experience through Darkwind's shared battle progression, create and spend Edge, manage Heat, and maintain their installed hardware. Most active firmware remains usable at zero Edge. When Edge is available, the Cortex automatically routes it into stronger damage, duration, shielding, healing, or control effects. Specialized routines have their own Edge behavior, explained through samhelp resources and samhelp <routine>. Guild Level unlocks firmware and signature implants through GL16. Cortex Rank continues through CR200 as long-term progression. The public contract office is east of Fountain Court near Moongate Plaza; joining installs the starter Cortex OS automatically. At CR200, members with a Monofilament Spur unlock the Ronin Edge. Use cyberblade to deploy this temporary primary weapon, cyberblade retract to collapse it early, and samhelp cyberblade for operating details. Rin Kade operates the restricted guild clinic beyond the contract office. Active members pay for signature hardware but receive covered installation, extraction, and signature repair services. Samrepair is only for a corrupt or incomplete guild installation, not normal onboarding. Core skills and combat loop Snap Cut, Jolt, and Ripcut establish early offense; Smart Smoke, Armor Weave, Ghoststep, Jammer Field, Nanomend, and Zero Signal provide defense, control, recovery, and escape. Build Edge through effective combat, spend it through firmware for stronger results, and keep Heat below thermal lockout. Every routine depends on its signature implant and that hardware's condition. Starting commands dashboard [-text] - graphical Cortex dashboard or terminal diagnostic samskills - routine unlocks, costs, and readiness samstatus - compact combat and resource state samxp - Guild Level, Cortex Rank, and GXP progress samspam [verbose|brief|off] - implant activation message detail samsignature [profile] - selectable arrival and departure firmware samhelp start - first-deployment checklist and combat loop samhelp commands - complete command and topic index Use samhelp <routine> for focused firmware guidance. Samhelp resources, firmware, hardware, maintenance, mon, contract, prices, and network explain the guild's major systems and the decisions each one supports. # alias: street samurai

docs.title: Swashbuckler
docs.text: Swashbuckler Swashbucklers are agile blade specialists who win through style, timing, mobility, and nerve. They favour knives and one-handed swords with light armour, using layered techniques instead of the Fighter's broad equipment approach. How it plays Combat builds Flair, with critical hits and a personally named weapon creating extra momentum. Finesse determines how many blade techniques can be sustained together. Alignment affects skill costs, and combining offensive or defensive styles creates additional strain. Core skills parry, dodge, riposte, called shot, impale, flurry, flourish, and Dance of Death form the technique ladder. Slip and press spend Flair, challenge sets the terms of a duel, wound creates lasting pressure, and nameweapon personalizes a favoured blade. Best fit Choose Swashbuckler if you enjoy fast blade combat, maintaining several styles, spending momentum at the right instant, and accepting lighter defenses in exchange for mobility and flourish. After joining, use sbhelp general, sbhelp flair, and sbhelp techniques for the full repertoire. # alias: swashbucklers, swashie, swashies

docs.title: Thief
docs.text: Thief Thieves turn information, access, preparation, and timing into power. They support stealthy exploration and ordinary PvE as well as dirty combat, poison, traps, burglary, and social manipulation. How it plays Case studies a mark and creates Opportunity. Setup actions create Bleeding, Exposed, concealment, or positional advantages; dirty techniques then spend Opportunity for control or a prepared finish. Combat earns Guild XP, while each Rank grants a Knack point for Ghost, Grifter, or Knife specialization. Core skills case prepares a target, quickstrike opens a wound, dirtyfight spends Opportunity on tricks, sidestep provides evasive footwork, conceal and vanish manage stealth, detect finds hidden dangers, and poisons, traps, pick, palm, pilfer, and breakin support criminal work. Best fit Choose Thief if you enjoy setup and payoff, stealth, utility, crafting poisons or traps, and solving encounters through preparation rather than standing still and trading blows. After joining, use thelp revival, tstatus, and knacks for the complete system. # alias: thieves

docs.title: Darkflow is Darkwind's official web client. Point a browser at
docs.text: ===================================================================== Darkflow is Darkwind's official web client. Point a browser at play.darkwind.ai and play -- nothing to install. It is a real terminal with everything telnet offers, plus a graphical layer driven by the game itself. Panels: dockable panels for vitals, stats, worth, an XP monitor, your room and an illustrated room image, inventory, group, chat, quests, achievements, buffs, the sky, fishing, and more. Drag panels into the side docks or float them; your layout is remembered between sessions. Live map: a graphical tile map built from the exploration of all players. Click any room on the map and the client walks you there step by step, verifying each step with the game before taking the next. Area maps: areas map <number> opens a cataloged area's map for browsing in its own Area Map pane, separate from the live map. See areas. Sound: game-driven sound effects and ambient audio, with volume and mute controls. Help: help topics open in a pop-up window instead of scrolling away in your terminal. Automation: aliases, triggers, highlights, and scripts, plus settings export and import as JSON. See alias and scripts. Comfort: dark and light themes, command history, tab completion, and screenreader support (see screenreader). See also: monitor, alias, scripts, areas, screenreader # keywords: web, browser, map, speedwalk, panels, sound, themes # alias: darkflow, webclient

docs.title: The colorlist command displays the compact legacy color combinations
docs.text: The colorlist command displays the compact legacy color combinations on DarkWind, plus a few expanded examples. Here is how the color system works: Color codes are used by typing |<code> where you want the color to begin and where it should stop. The spaces shown in examples like "| XX0" are only there so the help text can show the code without triggering it. Legacy compact codes use three characters after the pipe: |XYZ. The first character, X, is the foreground color. Acceptable colors are: R red G green B blue K black Y yellow C cyan W white M magenta The second character, Y, is the background color. The acceptable colors are the same as the foreground list. X means no foreground or background change. The third character, Z, is the effect. Acceptable options are: B bold U underscore K blinking 0 no affect A few examples: The code | XR0 produces This. The code | BYK produces This. The code | GKB produces This Expanded color codes use bracketed markup: | [fg=<color>,bg=<color>,<effect>]text| 000 Remove the spaces after | when you use these codes. They are included here only so the help file can show the syntax. Supported color values are: red, green, blue, black, yellow, cyan, white, magenta bright-red, bright-green, bright-blue, bright-black, bright-yellow, bright-cyan, bright-white, bright-magenta gray or grey ansi-0 through ansi-255 xterm-0 through xterm-255 #rrggbb truecolor hex values, such as #ff8800 Supported effects are: bold, italic, underline, underscore, blink, inverse, hidden, strikethrough, fraktur, double-underline, overline, reset, normal Effects are comma-separated standalone tokens. For example, use blink as an effect token, not as a background color: | [fg=#ff8800,bg=black,blink]blinking orange| 000 Expanded examples: | [fg=bright-cyan,bg=black,bold]bright cyan bold| 000 | [fg=ansi-202,bg=black]xterm orange| 000 | [fg=#ff8800,bg=black,underline]truecolor orange| 000 | [fg=white,bg=black,bold,italic,overline]combined effects| 000 The color command accepts the same expanded color values for channel foreground and background colors: color gossip bright-cyan black bold color gossip ansi-202 black none color gossip #ff8800 black underline color gossip white black italic color gossip bright-red black bold,italic Darkflow and players using "set term modern" receive the richer colors. Older ANSI terminals fall back to the nearest basic color. Players with color off see the text without the color markup.

docs.title: SYNTAX
docs.text: SYNTAX ====== help colors DESCRIPTION =========== Darkwind supports several ways to color text in places where player customization allows it, such as channel colors and some display settings. The traditional Darkwind color code is three characters after a | symbol. In the examples below, remove the space after | when using the code: | YKB yellow text, black background, bold | RK0 red text, black background, normal | XX0 reset to normal The three positions mean: 1. foreground color 2. background color 3. effect Common foreground and background letters are: K black R red G green Y yellow B blue M magenta C cyan W white X unchanged Common effect letters are: B bold U underline K blink 0 normal O normal Modern clients, including Darkflow, also support expanded color markup: | [fg=#ff8800,bg=black,bold]orange bold text| 000 | [fg=bright-cyan,bg=black,italic]italic cyan text| 000 Expanded markup allows truecolor hex values like #ff8800 and text effects such as italic, strikethrough, fraktur, double-underline, hidden, and overline when the client can display them. USEFUL COMMANDS =============== truecolor Shows gradients of common truecolor hex values from dark to bright. Use this when you want to pick a specific color. ansieffects Shows the ANSI text effects supported by modern terminals and Darkflow. Use this when you want to test italics, hidden text, strikethrough, fraktur, double underline, overline, and related effects. color Sets channel colors. See help color for syntax. set term Sets your terminal type. See help set for more settings. NOTES ===== Not every telnet client displays every color or text effect the same way. If something looks strange, try truecolor and ansieffects from your current client to see what it supports.

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text: DESCRIPTION ============ Combatbrief allows you to customize various aspects of the way combat messages are displayed. Each toggle is its own setting. It is possible to have all, none, or a few toggled on at a time. combatbrief - Displays your current combatbrief status combatbrief short - All combat messages are displayed as 'A hits B' or 'A misses B' combatbrief self - Only attacks by or against you will be displayed. combatbrief hit - Only hits will be displayed. Dodges and misses will be ignored. combatbrief damage - Damage numbers will be shown at the end of your combat messages. This setting is available at any level and is on by default. combatbrief visual - When a compatible Darkflow Combat pane is ready, routine weapon swings are shown visually instead of filling the terminal. If the pane or client is not ready, normal combat messages continue automatically. This setting is enabled by default for new characters. Visual mode is independent of short, self, hit, and damage. The self and hit filters still decide which exchanges reach the pane, while damage decides whether exact numbers are shown. Screenreader combat summaries take priority. Closing or collapsing the Combat pane restores terminal combat messages without changing your saved visual preference. Triggers, highlights, and client logs that depend on routine swing text will not receive those replaced lines while the visual pane is active.

docs.title: DarkWind's interface help covers client display options, local settings, and
docs.text: DarkWind's interface help covers client display options, local settings, and quality-of-life commands that change how information is shown to you. Common topics in this section include: help interface ansi help interface set help interface monitor help interface combatbrief help interface timezones Use help list interface to see every topic in this section.

docs.title: Syntax:  monitor
docs.text: Syntax: monitor Aliases: mon The monitor command toggles your hit point and spell point monitoring on and off. Monitor will show your current hit points and spell points each time one or the other changes, whether it be through healing, combat, etc. If the monitor is toggled to bar, then hp and sp will be shown as a bar graph, proportional to your maximums. For heroes and above, monitor also shows Wrathful Avatar charge. In bar mode, the avatar bar fills while charging and drains while Avatar is active.
