docs.title: Syntax: set screenreader <on/off>
docs.text: Syntax: set screenreader <on/off> ===================================================================== Screenreader mode reshapes Darkwind's output for players who use a screenreader. While it is on: - Colors, screen decoration, and decorative divider lines are stripped, and boxed headings are simplified to plain text. - Lists and tables, such as room contents and your settings, are printed as short numbered lines instead of drawn boxes. - Combat is summarized into a sentence or two each round instead of a stream of blow-by-blow lines. - Channel chatter is rephrased as plain speech, for example: Aeon says on Gossip, "Hello." - Ambient background noise is suppressed. Enabling: you are asked at character creation whether you use a screenreader. Answering yes turns the mode on and applies friendly defaults -- plain terminal, monitor off, popups off, and quieter channel settings. Review them with set list. You can also toggle the mode at any time: set screenreader on set screenreader off Darkflow's visual tutorial hover closes immediately when screenreader mode is turned on, and the current objective is repeated as linear terminal text. Turning screenreader mode off restores the hover automatically when the tutorial is still active. The tutorial remains fully controllable with tutorial continue, tutorial hint, tutorial skip, and tutorial restart. Help: while the mode is on, the help command reads a screenreader-specific version of a topic when one exists and falls back to the regular topic otherwise. Plain help opens a start page written for screenreader users, and topics are shown through the pager rather than in pop-up windows. See also: set, monitor, client # keywords: accessibility, blind, visually impaired, vihelp, audio # alias: accessibility

docs.title: SYNTAX
docs.text: SYNTAX ====== set set list set <option> <value> DESCRIPTION =========== The set command lets you view and change saved character options. Use set or set list to show your current settings. Use set <option> <value> to change one setting. OPTIONS ====== allow <off|on> Controls whether your session may be snooped. anonymous <off|on> Hides player specifics from finger and who. autoexits <off|on> Sets whether detailed exit information is shown. autoburn <off|on> Uses a carried corpse burner to run burn corpse after autorefine or autosell, autoloot, and autogold have finished processing an NPC corpse. This uses the normal burn command and destroys anything left inside. autogold <off|on> Automatically takes only gold from NPC corpses you kill. This is redundant while autoloot is on. autokill <off|on> Makes a manually entered bare kill target the first visible NPC. It does not start combat automatically and can still choose an NPC you did not intend to attack. autolevel <off|on> Controls whether non-remort characters automatically spend experience to gain levels. autoloot <off|on> Automatically takes gold and gettable loot from NPC corpses you kill. autorefine <off|on> Permanently converts ordinary refinery-eligible equipment from NPCs you kill into saved profession materials. This uses the same yields as the Refinery and disables autosell. Magical, unique, limited, customized, scripted, and otherwise protected items remain in the corpse, exactly as with autosell. Leave it off if you want to inspect equipment drops before deciding what to do with them. autosell <off|on> Uses a carried corpse burner to sell ordinary loot from NPC corpses directly to Taylor when his shop would buy it. His normal Charisma and reputation pricing applies, followed by a 10 percent handling charge. Magical, unique, limited, customized, scripted, and otherwise protected items remain in the corpse. Enabling this disables autorefine. brief <off|on> Sets the amount of room descriptions that are shown. colorblock <off|on> Blocks other players' custom color codes in channel messages. combatbrief-damage <off|on> Shows damage numbers at the end of combat messages. combatbrief-hit <off|on> Hides misses and dodges from combat messages. combatbrief-self <off|on> Shows only attacks by or on you. combatbrief-short <off|on> Uses shorter combat messages. combatbrief-visual <off|on> Moves routine combat swings into a ready Darkflow Combat pane. Normal combat text continues whenever a compatible pane is unavailable. email <email@domain.com> Sets your current e-mail address. forwarding <off|on> Controls whether MUD mail is forwarded to your e-mail address. giphy <off|on> Controls whether shared GIFs auto-open in Darkflow. itemdetail <off|on> Shows an item's AC or WC in its description. language <language> Sets your default language to speak with. monitor <off|on|bar> Sets how your remaining HP/SP are shown. morelen <1-75> Sets the more paging length. notifylooks <off|on> Controls whether you are notified when others look at you. npcdetail <off|on> Shows a level and indicator on non-player characters. pavail <off|on> Controls whether you are marked as looking for a party. pk <off|on> Sets your player killing flag. prompt <string> Sets the string used as your prompt. Wizards can use: %d current working directory %i current invis level %wi whoinvis indicator %f fakeidle indicator %e environment, D/P for dev/prod realm <off|on> Newbie-only setting for whether you start in the realm where you quit. screenreader <off|on> Enables output adjustments for screenreader users. sharedvideo <off|on> Controls whether shared YouTube videos auto-open in Darkflow. showmultis <off|on|main> Controls whether finger shows your registered multies, only your main character, or neither. teapotspam <off|on> Controls whether your enchanted teapot emits idle room chatter. term <none|ansi|modern|vt100|vt52> Sets which terminal type you are using to connect. timestamps <off|on> Sets timestamps on or off when viewing channel histories. virginears <off|on> Turns your personal profanity filter on or off. visemail <off|on> Allows your e-mail address to be seen by others. website <http://...> Adds your web page address to your finger info. wimpy <0-100> Sets the HP percentage where you automatically run away. wimpycmd <command|none> Sets the command attempted when you wimpy, or clears it with none. SEE ALSO ======== help screenreader help monitor help combatbrief

docs.title: Time zones are based on GMT (Greenwich Mean Time)
docs.text: Time zones are based on GMT (Greenwich Mean Time) HST Hawaiian Standard Time Honolulu GMT - 10 AKST Alaska Standard Time Anchorage GMT - 9 PST Pacific Standard Time Los Angeles GMT - 8 MST Mountain Standard Time Phoenix GMT - 7 CST Central Standard Time Dallas GMT - 6 EST Eastern Standard Time Detroit GMT - 5 NST Newfoundland Standard Time St. John's GMT - 3.5 GMT Greenwich Mean Time London GMT CET Central Europe Time Paris GMT + 1 EET Eastern Europe Time Helsinki GMT + 2 AWST Australian Western Standard Time Perth GMT + 8 ACST Australian Central Standard Time Darwin GMT + 9.5 AEST Australian Eastern Standard Time Brisbane GMT + 10 The machine hosting Darkwind is in the Eastern Standard timezone (GMT - 5)

docs.title: Artificer
docs.text: Artificer Artificer is not currently available for player selection. The class is under wizard testing and the Brass Crucible route and attunement rite are disabled. Artificer is a remort class, not a guild. Its membership and GXP survive future remorts even though level, stats, and guilds reset normally. An Artificer's Cinis Engine replaces the ordinary corpse burner. It retains burn corpse, burn all corpse, check burner, and cinis while also storing class status, ash, essence, prototypes, and active workings. Commands: artificer crucible artificer abilities artificer progression artificer study <body|soul|confluence> resonate <item|living> bellowsblow [foe] temper <equipment> with <cinder|ichor|confluence> bulwark awaken <carried weapon> fabricate aether mount artifice <primary unique armour> with <carried unique armour> prototype <coil|ward|starburst> deploy <coil [foe]|ward|starburst> unmake [number|all] Bosses yield cinder when their physical nature dominates and ichor when their mental or spiritual nature dominates. Boss tier controls the amount. Harvests, tempering, and inventions award permanent Artificer GXP. Permanent Artificer GXP determines rank and available Load. Mastery uses the same cumulative GXP with diminishing returns. It is roughly 90 percent at 31,500 GXP, 94 percent at 60,000, and 99 percent at 350,000. It strengthens bounded parts of class abilities but never replaces current level and stats. Body costs five cinder per rank. Soul costs five ichor. Confluence requires at least one rank in each and costs three of each. Discipline ranks cap at five. Prepared inventions persist through logout and remort. Coil requires Soul 1, ward requires Body 1, and starburst requires Confluence 1. Prototype slots grow slowly with permanent mastery. Chimera armour opens at Confluence 2 and 50 percent mastery. It costs ten cinder and ten ichor to fold part of one carried unique armour into a worn or carried unique using exactly the same non-accessory slots. Each seam uses 2 Load and reserves 5 percent maximum HP and 8 percent maximum SP. The donor remains reserved at full carried weight. Removing the primary suspends its benefits; the seam ends on expiry or unmaking. Higher GXP permits multiple seams, to a hard cap of three. Unique scripts are never copied. Confluence 3 also echoes the donor's strongest positive resistance. Portable Bulwark opens at rank 3 and Body 2. It spends grey ash and reserves 4 percent HP, 4 percent SP, and one Load. Awaken Weapon opens at rank 4 with Body 2 and Soul 2; it reserves a real non-unique weapon inside a temporary combat construct and returns it when the working ends. At rank 5 and Soul 3, Fabricate creates a persistent shoulder implant whose automatic aether shot consumes SP and blue ash.

docs.title: Remort Boons
docs.text: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Remort Boons ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Boons are permanent bonuses bought with boon points. You earn one boon point each time you remort (see help remort). Boons survive death, rebirth, and every remort that follows: once a boon is part of your soul, it is never lost. Choosing boons: remort boons List all boons, your ranks, and costs remort boon <name> See the details of one boon remort choose <name> Spend a point on a rank of a boon marks Review the boons on your soul Each boon can be taken multiple times, up to its maximum rank. Choices are permanent, so weigh them carefully. The boons: Boon of Vitality +2% maximum hit points per rank Boon of Spirit +2% maximum spell points per rank Boon of Might +2 strength per rank Boon of Grace +2 dexterity per rank Boon of Endurance +2 constitution per rank Boon of Intellect +2 intelligence per rank Boon of Insight +2 wisdom per rank Boon of Presence +2 charisma per rank Soul Memory +5% experience gained per rank Souls tempered by many lives unlock greater boons: Mythic Vitality +5% maximum hit points per rank (requires remort 5, costs 2 points) Mythic Spirit +5% maximum spell points per rank (requires remort 5, costs 2 points) Stat boons stack on top of your trained stats and are not limited by the normal stat caps. More boons will be added over time, including some that only open at higher remort levels. See also: help remort. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

docs.title: Newbification
docs.text: Newbification ----------------------------- On Darkwind, we give players the option to newbify their characters should they choose to do so. This entails 'killing' them down to level 1, reducing all stats down to 1, and resetting a couple other things the character has learned throughout their life. It's merely a quick way for you to start somewhat over, but not quite from scratch. You will need to find someone to help you accomplish this dasterdly deed though. If you ask around you can probably find such a person willing to help you 'see the light' a little early. NOTE: Attempting to newbify yourself by repeatedly killing yourself off is against the spirit of the game and is punishable by the Gods of Darkwind.

docs.title: Darkwind Renown
docs.text: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Darkwind Renown ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ At level 100, your level display is replaced by a renown label on the who list. Your heroism reputation determines whether you appear as [HERO], [ADV], or [VILN]. Heroism is changed by notable actions in the world, not by guild membership alone. Several advantages are given to those who reach this level band. Along with the prestige of renown, players may change their title at will with the 'ltitle' command (unlocked earlier, at CHAMPION, level 50). In addition, level 100+ players have the option of adding a second guild, broadening their skills and overall scope. This second guild is governed by a variety of restrictions which are outlined in the dualguilds help file. See help mechanics reputation for more about how deeds can affect your public renown. Use reputation to see the broad shape of how the world speaks of you. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

docs.title: Darkwind Legends
docs.text: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Darkwind Legends ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Attaining Legend status on Darkwind is mostly a status symbol at the moment. To earn the title of Legend, you must reach level 150. Players that have reached this status will have [LGND] in place of their level on the who list. The benefit to reaching LEGEND is the ability to register a free mythic character. They retain the 'ltitle' command from reaching CHAMPION. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

docs.title: DarkWind Player Levels
docs.text: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ DarkWind Player Levels ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ADVANCEMENT: Advancing a level costs experience. Characters can advance manually by visiting an Adventurer's Guild, or by using autolevel on to spend exp and gain levels automatically. Remort characters always level automatically. NEWBIE: Players are considered newbies until their 6th level, though most guilds will allow membership at level 5. 5: Players at level 5 gain the 'whotitle' command. CHAMPION: Players who reach level 50 show CHMP on the who list, gain the 'ltitle' command, earn a free multichar slot, and can join a compatible second guild. RENOWN: Players who reach level 100 receive a renown label on who: HERO, ADV, or VILN. LEGEND: Players who reach level 150. LEGEND+ players gain the ability to register a free mythic character, and earn a second free multichar slot. EPIC: Players who reach level 200 show EPIC on the who list. MYTHIC: Players who reach level 250 stand at the mortal peak. Mythic characters may optionally remort: return to level 1, keep their wealth and belongings, and earn a permanent boon point for every rebirth. See help remort and help boons.

docs.title: Newbification
docs.text: Newbification ----------------------------- On Darkwind, we give players the option to newbify their characters should they choose to do so. This entails 'killing' them down to level 1, reducing all stats down to 1, and resetting a couple other things the character has learned throughout their life. It's merely a quick way for you to start somewhat over, but not quite from scratch. You will need to find someone to help you accomplish this dasterdly deed though. If you ask around you can probably find such a person willing to help you 'see the light' a little early. NOTE: Attempting to newbify yourself by repeatedly killing yourself off is against the spirit of the game and is punishable by the Gods of Darkwind.

docs.title: Darkwind Remort
docs.text: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Darkwind Remort ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Remort is Darkwind's late-game rebirth loop. When you reach level 250, you may choose to remort: your character returns to level 1 and climbs again, carrying a permanent remort level that grows by one with every rebirth. Remorting is always optional. You can stay at level 250 forever and never remort. What you give up each remort: - Your level (back to 1) and any unspent experience - Your base stats (back to 1, rebuilt with stat raises) - Your guild memberships (you leave all guilds) What you keep, always: - Your name, history, and account progress - Your gold, bank balance, boats, and property - Your inventory - Your remort level, boon points, and every boon you have chosen What you gain: - One boon point per remort level, spent on permanent bonuses that persist through every future life (see help boons) - Automatic leveling: remort players advance the moment they have enough experience, with no guild-hall visit - 6 stat raises per level (spend with advance at a guild hall; stats are capped at 3 x your level) - A remort tag (R1, R2, ...) on the who list The cost: Remort use a variation of the normal level experience curve. Each remort level adds 2% to that cost. A soul that has lived many lives climbs more slowly, but carries far more power with it. You must be alive, out of combat, and in your natural form to remort. Commands: remort Show your remort status and eligibility remort boons List the permanent bonuses you can choose remort choose Spend a boon point remort confirm Remort (only at level 250, asked only once) marks Show the boons marked on your soul See also: help boons, help leveling. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

docs.title: Newbification
docs.text: Newbification ----------------------------- On Darkwind, we give players the option to newbify their characters should they choose to do so. This entails 'killing' them down to level 1, reducing all stats down to 1, and resetting a couple other things the character has learned throughout their life. It's merely a quick way for you to start somewhat over, but not quite from scratch. You will need to find someone to help you accomplish this dasterdly deed though. If you ask around you can probably find such a person willing to help you 'see the light' a little early. NOTE: Attempting to newbify yourself by repeatedly killing yourself off is against the spirit of the game and is punishable by the Gods of Darkwind. Real Life Talk: If you are feeling suicidal, please reach out to someone. Depression lies. If you are in the USA, Call 1-800-273-8255 If you are in the UK, Call 116 123 If you are in Australia, Call 13 11 14 If you are in the Netherlands/nu hulp nodig? Call 0900-0113 Or send a tell, shout, gossip, etc to anyone online.

docs.title: ☾  VAMPIRE · THE CRIMSON COVENANT  ☽
docs.text: ☾ VAMPIRE · THE CRIMSON COVENANT ☽ ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Vampire is an open remort class. It is a permanent supernatural nature, not a guild, and composes with your guild. A character may have only one class. Remort level 1 characters may find the First Grave below Stoker's church and type attune shrine to accept the Embrace. The First Grave is the public threshold to the Crimson Covenant. After the Embrace, descend into its safe sanctuary: gather in the Crimson Hall, bind a coffin in the Vault of Sealed Earth, and work Blood Sorcery in the Red Chapel. The sanctuary supplies no free blood and bypasses none of the class's limits. The class revolves around Vitae, Hunger, prey selection, prepared discipline loadouts, and regional Exposure. Vitae does not regenerate or decay. Feeding restores it; discipline powers spend it. Hunger is derived from the remaining Vitae: Sated, Stirring, Ravenous, or Frenzy. ESSENTIAL COMMANDS vamphelp [topic|command|power] vampwho / vwho / vampires vamprepair vampire / vscore vampire abilities vampire progression feed <prey> [careful|quick|deep|drain] feed <carefully|quickly|deeply> from <prey> feed from <corpse> bloodsense [target|memories] attune <discipline, discipline, ...> discipline list discipline <power> [target] ritual [list|prepare <name>|invoke <name> [target]] bloodline [list|choose <name>|vault <store|list|use #>] coffin [bind|rest] mask shed vchat <message> HUNGER, BLOOD, AND THE HUNT Feeding establishes one active blood profile: Martial, Predatory, Mystic, Noble, Vital, or Feral / Profane. Quality ranges from Common through Mythic. Only living NPC prey and non-player corpses are valid; bloodless creatures, players, protected prey, and unearned shared-combat targets are rejected. Careful feeding can leave no evidence when no one notices. Obvious feeding is seen by nearby living witnesses, and each confirmed witness worsens the local record. Deep or lethal feeding creates much more Exposure even in private; feeding on Dawnward's sanctified ground creates especially durable evidence. EXPOSURE AND BLOOD MEMORIES Exposure is tracked separately in every area. Its tiers are Quiet (0-9), Whispers (10-39), Suspected (40-74), and Hunted (75-100). 'bloodsense' shows the local tier, latest cause, witness count, and known regional totals; 'bloodsense memories' lists significant prey preserved permanently in your blood. Fallows witnesses can also be asked what rumors name you. Ordinary evidence fades during quiet time, sanctified evidence fades more slowly, and coffin rest or a Nameless mask can actively reduce it. Hunted Vampires may be recognized by Dawnward sentinels or pursued by a blood hunter. Most significant boss feedings become permanent Blood Memories and grant Vampire GXP. Four curated bosses also leave a resonance with a permanent behavioral reward. Lady Vesper strengthens Presence's Awe and changes court recognition. Lord Blackbriar lets active Obfuscate defeat one witness during careful feeding. Nhal Serev teaches Bloodsense to identify bloodless prey. Vaelkor teaches Bloodsense to identify the deep-feed and drain thresholds. Because Lady Vesper, Lord Blackbriar, and Nhal Serev have no living blood, meaningful participation in defeating a curated boss can preserve its memory through the normal class kill-award contract. Use 'bloodsense memories' to see each known resonance and its exact reward. Attuned Auspex previews a curated resonance when Bloodsense examines its boss. PROGRESSION AND BLOOD MASTERY Vampire GXP survives remort and advances five milestones: The Embrace, Bloodline Rite, Night Court, Crimson Dominion, and First Night. The final milestone also requires remort level 750. Knowledge widens as milestones open, but only three disciplines may normally be attuned; First Night grants a fourth slot. Attunement changes only at a bound coffin, the First Grave, the Covenant's Red Chapel, or approved Vespercourt anchors. GXP and remorts also increase Blood Mastery continuously. Seventy-five percent of its eventual power comes from an asymptotic GXP curve; the final twenty-five percent grows across the remort journey through R1000. Blood Mastery improves bounded discipline damage, healing, duration, and passive combat effects. It also modestly improves feeding yield, haven recovery, Torpor recovery, and the Night Familiar. It never raises maximum Vitae or removes Hunger, sunlight, fire, or holy weaknesses. Use 'vscore' to see the current percentage. BLOODLINES At 1,000 GXP choose one permanent bloodline: House Vesper, The Nameless, The Bloodwrights, The Red Hunt, or The Graveborn. Bloodwrights may vault up to three active blood profiles, which degrade to Common when recalled. DISCIPLINES AND POWERS Each discipline is now a complete mastery track. Foundation powers open when the discipline is learned; deeper powers require 15%, 35%, 55%, 75%, or 85% Blood Mastery as listed by 'discipline list'. Celerity, Potence, Fortitude, Auspex, Obfuscate, Presence, Protean, Animalism, and Blood Sorcery retain their existing passive and legacy invocations. Dominate opens at Night Court, or at Bloodline Rite for House Vesper. First Night opens Oblivion. Existing invocations such as Mend, Mist, Awe, Claws, and the Night Familiar remain available for compatibility. Every catalog power declares its Vitae cost, cooldown, discipline, mastery, target, Hunger behavior, day/night behavior, profile and bloodline mutations, regional Exposure, boss fallback, and cleanup policy. Ancient encounter powers share a Vampire major cooldown so several capstones cannot be chained. Bosses receive bounded damage or debuffs instead of executions or hard control. Players are never valid targets for Vampire control powers. Blood profiles mutate matching powers: Martial favors Potence and Fortitude; Predatory favors Celerity and Animalism; Mystic favors Auspex and Blood Sorcery; Noble favors Presence, Dominate, and Obfuscate; Vital favors Fortitude and blood recovery; Feral / Profane favors Protean, Animalism, and violent Potence at greater frenzy risk. Potent, Exceptional, and Mythic blood add bounded depth without permanently unlocking abilities. PREPARED RITUALS Blood Sorcery can prepare Ward of the Threshold, Sanguine Compass, Seal of Quiet Earth, Draught of False Life, and Hunter's Malediction. Preparation costs Vitae and requires an approved Vampire anchor outside combat. The Red Chapel and Vault of Sealed Earth are Covenant anchors. Prepared uses persist through logout and remort and are consumed on invocation. Bloodwrights prepare more efficiently and receive one additional ritual slot. WHERE TO BEGIN New Vampires should begin with vamphelp start. Use vamphelp status to decode every field shown by vscore. Use 'vamphelp commands' for the compact topic tree, or ask for a command or power directly, such as 'vamphelp feed' or 'vamphelp quickening'. REPAIRING THE COVENANT Vamprepair is a recovery command, not routine maintenance. It preserves Vampire progression while refreshing the live Covenant soul, autoload, registered command paths, Vitae registration, runtime hooks, and client status. It preserves the exact current Vitae amount and never refills it. Use it after a Vampire update, when class commands are missing, or when an architect directs you to repair the installation. Active Vampire power effects end during the refresh. OLD RIVALRIES Moonwold werewolves recognize Vampires as ancestral rivals. In their caverns, each side gains a small offensive edge against the other. Vespercourt instead recognizes lineage and the Blood Memories carried into court. SUNLIGHT, HAVEN, AND TORPOR Open daylight burns Vampires unless the room is inside, underground, or under canopy. Dawn and twilight are less severe than full day. The class always retains sunlight, fire, and holy banes. 'discipline mist' provides an emergency route to the bound coffin when local wards and combat permit it. The Vampire channel announces dawn, full day, twilight, and night once per transition so every online Vampire receives the warning even while under cover. 'coffin bind' binds the First Grave, the Covenant's Vault of Sealed Earth, or Vespercourt crypt as a haven. Resting there restores wounds, steadies low Vitae toward 75 without lowering a higher pool, and reduces evidence in every known region. It is recovery, not a full refill or a way around feeding. Once per reboot, a non-hardcore Vampire death becomes Torpor at the bound coffin. Torpor begins at one hit point for a new Vampire and recovers up to ten percent maximum health as Blood Mastery approaches its limit. Later deaths use the normal death system. # alias: vampirism

docs.title: Achievements track long-term progress across combat, exploration,
docs.text: Achievements track long-term progress across combat, exploration, social activity, economy, quests, and guild-specific milestones. Each achievement line has named tiers: Bronze Silver Gold Platinum Mythic Use these commands: achievements view your achievement journal achievements titles list your unlocked achievement titles atitle equip or clear an achievement title leaderboard view the top 50 achievement rankings Achievement progress is driven by tracked game stats. Most progress is permanent once earned. New unlocks can grant titles that you may equip separately from your normal title. See also: help achievements, help achievement_titles, help leaderboard

docs.title: Achievement titles are special public titles earned by unlocking
docs.text: Achievement titles are special public titles earned by unlocking achievement tiers. They are separate from your normal player title. Equipping an achievement title does not overwrite your regular title text. Use: achievements titles Lists your unlocked titles and shows the exact command for each one. atitle <title-id> Equips a title you have unlocked. atitle clear Removes your equipped achievement title. Examples: atitle slayer:bronze atitle locksmith:silver If you are not sure what the id is, do not guess. Run: achievements titles That output shows the exact command to use. See also: help achievements, help atitle, help leaderboard

docs.title: Achievements track long-term progress across the game using stats you
docs.text: Achievements track long-term progress across the game using stats you already build naturally while playing. They cover areas such as: combat quests and progression economy and donations exploration-flavored world activity guild-specific milestones Each achievement line has five tiers: Bronze Silver Gold Platinum Mythic Useful commands: achievements Opens your achievement journal and shows your current progress. achievements titles Shows every unlocked achievement title and the exact command to equip it. atitle <title-id> Equips an achievement title. atitle clear Clears your equipped achievement title. leaderboard Opens the top 50 achievement leaderboard. Achievements are meant to reward depth and consistency over time rather than a single burst of damage or one lucky fight. See also: help achievement_titles, help atitle, help leaderboard

docs.title: SYNTAX
docs.text: SYNTAX ====== addicts DESCRIPTION =========== Gives a list of the current users and what percentage of their maximum possible online time they have been logged in for. ie. The higher the number the more that player has been here since their creation date. Note: Assumptions have been made of people sleeping at least part of every day. :P

docs.title: SYNTAX
docs.text: SYNTAX ====== alias list alias <alias> alias <alias> <command> talias list talias <talias> talias <talias> <player> HELP - ALIAS ============ The "alias" commmand allows you to abbreviate commonly used commands to make them quicker and simplier to use. The commands usable with alias are as follows: alias list simply shows you all the aliases you currently have saved. You may have up to 200 different aliases at any given time. alias <alias> This displays the setting for alias <alias> from your list of valid aliases. alias remove <alias> This removes the alias <alias> from your list of valid aliases. alias <alias> <command> This command is how you actually set your alias. Instead of trying to give you some fancy explanation, I think it would be much easier to just give you some examples. examples: "alias ga get all" enables you to type in "ga" (without the quotes), and pick up everything that you can hold in the room. "alias la look at" enables you to type in "la <something>" (again, without the quotes and the <>'s), and you will then look at that object. You can set an alias to do multiple things by using the 'script' command. "alias twon script n,n" would move you two spaces north. 'help script' for more info. HELP - TALIAS ============= The "talias" command stands for 'tell alias.' It is used to shorten players names which you use frequently. The syntax is similar to that of the "alias" command. This can be used when you are talking to people via the tell command, and also when you are performing an emotion at someone. An explanation of the different talias commands follows: talias list Simply shows all the taliases you currently have saved. You may have up to 200 different taliases at any given time. talias <talias> This displays the setting for talias <talias> from your list of valid taliases. talias remove <talias> This removes the talias <talias> from your list of valid taliases. talias <talias> <person> This command is how use actually set your talias. Instead of trying to give you some fancy explanation, I think it would be much easier to just give you some examples. examples: "talias nf nightflyer" adds a talias for 'nf' to be Nightflyer. You may now type "gwave nf" instead of "gwave nightflyer", and you will wave in greeting to Nightflyer. This also works in combination with regular aliases. Assume that you have an "alias t tell" and a "talias nf nightflyer". Now you can "t nf Hi." and Nightflyer (assuming he's logged on, of course!) will see you say "Hi." to him! See Also -------- clearaliases Commands you can not alias: drop, get, equip, unequip, wear, keep, take or unwield

docs.title: Alignment is a player's outlook on life. In general, there are only
docs.text: Alignment is a player's outlook on life. In general, there are only two aspects to alignment, good and evil. There are an infinite number of "shades of grey" between them however. Almost all monsters on Darkwind have their own alignment. Killing these monsters affects what your alignment is, shifting it in the opposite direction. For example, killing a holy paladin of Mitra (which is of good alignment) would shift your alignment towards the evil side of the spectrum. See also: help ethics

docs.title: Darkwind announcements are the game's official bulletin-board style
docs.text: Darkwind announcements are the game's official bulletin-board style messages for important news, updates, and notices. The current announcement system keeps track of read and unread messages for each player separately. Useful commands: checkannounce Shows how many announcement posts you have not read yet. announcehist Shows recent announcement history. If you use the web client, announcements also appear in the dedicated Announcements interface with read and unread status. Announcements are staff-managed. Reading one marks it as read for you, but it does not change whether the announcement itself is globally active or archived. See also: help checkannounce

docs.title: Usage: assess <target>
docs.text: Usage: assess <target> Assess gives you a very basic feeling of whether your target is more experienced or less experienced than you are. It does not tell you if you would do well against the target. A vastly more worldly message however would mean your chances alone would be slimmer. Available to all players.

docs.title: Usage: assist <player>
docs.text: Usage: assist <player> This command allows you to assist another player in killing a monster. This is very helpful in parties!

docs.title: The atitle command equips or clears an achievement title that you have
docs.text: The atitle command equips or clears an achievement title that you have already unlocked. Syntax: atitle atitle <title-id> atitle clear Examples: atitle slayer:bronze atitle resurrectionist:gold atitle clear To see the exact ids you can use, run: achievements titles To see the overall achievement rankings, run: leaderboard See also: help achievements, help achievement_titles

docs.title: Wrathful Avatar
docs.text: Wrathful Avatar Hero (level 100+) players build Wrathful Avatar charge over real time while they are alive and active. Charge normally reaches full after 30 minutes, though potions and other influences can quicken or slow the gathering wrath. When the charge reaches full, use: avatar avatar end Wrathful Avatar spends the full charge and grants 30 minutes of heightened combat power. While active, you gain +10 strength, dexterity, and constitution, better accuracy and criticals, harder hits, faster attacks, sharper dodges, and a chance to absorb incoming blows in avatar fire. The power also grants all weapon-specialization, weapon, armor, and dual-wield permissions while it lasts. It does not stack with itself or with another Wrathful Avatar. Use score or meter to check your current charge and charge rate. Use avatar end while Wrathful Avatar is active to end it immediately. This uses the normal Avatar cleanup and leaves your avatar charge at 0%. Divine patronage can change your charge rate. Use patron for your current patron modifier and omens for the current world state.

docs.title: Bosses are major named encounters that are stronger, tougher, and more
docs.text: Bosses are major named encounters that are stronger, tougher, and more rewarding than normal mobs. Many bosses are assigned a visible tier: T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 In general, higher boss tiers mean: more health and staying power more dangerous pressure or mechanics stronger reward expectations a bigger fight that is less suited to casual overlevel farming Boss kills are often announced on the Events channel. A few bosses may explicitly opt into mocking much higher-level killers, but normal boss announcements do not shame players for being overlevel. Only a character's first kill of a particular boss during each reboot is announced; repeat kills remain quiet. When a boss defeats a character, its Events-channel taunt also remains quiet if that character has already defeated that particular boss during the reboot. Bosses are not all meant for the same stage of progression. Treat the tier as a clue to the seriousness of the encounter. See also: help bosses, help boss_tiers, help events

docs.title: Boss tiers are a quick shorthand for how dangerous a boss fight is
docs.text: Boss tiers are a quick shorthand for how dangerous a boss fight is expected to be. Tier labels appear as: T1 T2 T3 T4 T5 As the tier rises, expect the fight to demand more from a player or group. Higher tiers usually bring more punishment, more durability, and more meaningful rewards. A boss tier is not a promise that every class or every level range will handle the fight the same way. It is a difficulty signal, not a perfect matchmaking number. In the Eternal Dungeon, leader encounters eventually grow into true boss tiers as floors climb higher and higher. See also: help boss, help eternal_dungeon

docs.title: Usage: 'buffs' or 'clearbuff'
docs.text: Usage: 'buffs' or 'clearbuff' buffs - Lists your active buffs. * Not all buffs are visible to the system. clearbuff - Allows you to remove one of your current buffs. The ' clearbuff all' option removes all buffs. Debuffs, such as curses, hexes, or lingering poisons, appear under their own header in 'buffs'. They cannot be removed with 'clearbuff'. Debuffs expire on their own, or via cures and dispels designed for them. Wizards may use 'dispelall' for stuck debuffs. An active parasite appears at the end of 'buffs' with its real remaining online time and starvation state. Parasites are not normal buffs and cannot be removed with 'clearbuff'. Use 'parasite' for full details or 'purge parasite' to remove one. See also: help effects

docs.title: Combat in DarkWind runs on heartbeats. Every round, each of your
docs.text: Combat in DarkWind runs on heartbeats. Every round, each of your attacks -- wielded weapons, or fists and natural attacks without them -- produces one or more swings, and every swing rolls on its own to crit, hit, be dodged, be absorbed, and finally deal damage. Starting a fight: kill <target> opens combat, and most offensive guild abilities do the same. Judge a target's experience first with assess <target>. Attacking other players requires Player Killing registration; read help pk first. See help kill. Landing hits: how often you swing depends on your weapon's size and speed and on your strength and dexterity, with diminishing returns at high stat values. Whether a swing lands pits your level, intelligence, and dexterity, plus your weapon's accuracy, against the defender's dodge. Roughly one swing in twenty is a critical hit for multiplied damage. Weapon training sharpens all of this -- see help specialization. Dealing damage: damage comes from your damage stat and your weapon's damage class. Heavier and two-handed weapons hit harder but swing slower and less accurately. Damage carries types (slashing, fire, and so on) that are checked against the defender's resistances. Defending: dodge avoids swings outright. Armour's absorb class applies reliable flat and percentage reduction to physical weapon damage, and can also absorb a landed blow down to nothing. Armour-piercing attacks halve that reliable reduction. Resistances and magical shields shave typed damage away. Spells and potions layer on more protection -- see help buffs and help shields. Check your armor class and weapon class anytime with sc. Running away: you can flee any fight by simply leaving the room, though a pursuer who catches you gets a free swing. wimpy <percent> makes your legs flee automatically at low health; see help wimpy. Dying: death costs 10% of your experience on hand (nothing at level 5 or under) and your corpse stays safely with you. See help death. Fighting together: assist <player> joins a friend's fight, and parties split the work and the reward; see help party. Trim combat spam with combatbrief, or use combatbrief visual to move routine swings into a ready Darkflow Combat pane. Important ability, warning, flee, death, and reward text continues in the terminal. See also: kill, assess, assist, party, wimpy, buffs, shields, death, pk # keywords: fighting, battle

docs.title: If an object is cursed, you can't get rid of it by any normal
docs.text: If an object is cursed, you can't get rid of it by any normal methods. You can remove a cursed item by typing 'uncurse <object>' to Plum in the church. This will cost 5000 coins per item. Members of the Cleric Guild can also remove curse.

docs.title: Syntax: cyberware [player] / cyberscan <implant> / install <implant> /
docs.text: Syntax: cyberware [player] / cyberscan <implant> / install <implant> / extract <implant or location> / uninstall <implant or location> ===================================================================== Cyberware is machinery grafted into your own body. An installed implant grants its bonuses - stats, resistances, or chance-based "proc" effects - for as long as it stays inside you. Every implant occupies one or more body locations: eyes, ears, brain, skull, jaw, throat, neck, spine, heart, lungs, torso, skin, shoulders, arms, hands, legs, and feet. Only one implant may occupy a location. Implants also strain the body. No implant can cost more than 10 strain, and the 24 cyberware locations create an absolute capacity of 240. Your natural limit starts at 6 and grows with your level: +1 per 10 levels, plus larger bonuses at levels 50, 100, 150, 200, and 250. Cyber-touched origins grant +2 strain each, to a maximum of +10. Each remort closes part of the distance between your natural limit and 240, reaching full capacity at remort 50. You cannot install an implant that would push your total strain past your limit, and an implant may demand a minimum level or stranger things before your body accepts it. World cyberware is built in four broad qualities. Standard chrome offers dependable basic benefits; refined chrome is more efficient or specialized; military chrome carries stronger combat systems; and artifact chrome can transform a build at the maximum strain cost or several body locations. Quality does not replace item level: hardware recovered deeper into Tekal is generally stronger even when it shares a grade with earlier equipment. Commands: cyberware Show installed technological implants, occupied body locations, and cybernetic strain. cyberware <player> Wizards may inspect a currently connected player's installed cyberware and strain. implants Show every object-backed implant by family, including cyberware and bound relics. cyberscan <implant> Inspect an implant's type, grade, locations, strain, visibility, and procs before installing. Street Samurai receive additional contract details for signature hardware. Their own installed implants also show integrity, fragmentation, firmware effectiveness, software issues, and recommended maintenance actions. install <implant> Install an implant you are carrying. extract <implant or location> Remove an installed implant, returning it to your inventory. Alias: uninstall. Installation and extraction require a staffed ripperdoc clinic, and the ripperdoc will not operate while you are fighting. The Forbidden Replacement Table in Nethrys Undercity's Ripperdoc Quarter is a formal clinic. You may use engage ripperdoc there to review carried or installed hardware, see the exact service fee, and confirm a procedure. You may use cyberware and cyberscan anywhere. Street Samurai diagnostics are private. A carried signature implant shows its contract requirements and hardware profile, but current maintenance state appears only when that exact implant is installed in the scanning Street Samurai. Ordinary implants and scans by other players retain the standard report. Installation costs 10,000 coins per point of implant strain, with a 10,000 coin minimum. Extraction costs 5,000 coins per strain, with a 5,000 coin minimum. Installed implants cannot be dropped and stay with you across sessions. They are hidden from normal inventory while installed, but remain visible through cyberware or implants. Implant grade does not change this: standard, refined, military, and artifact chrome all persist normally. Only an implant explicitly created as temporary or nonpersistent is excluded, and normal clinic installation rejects hardware that cannot be preserved. A saved implant may also be temporarily unavailable if its blueprint cannot load or a one-of-a-kind implant is already active elsewhere; its installation record is retained for a later retry. Only active restored implants consume strain, so missing or inactive hardware releases its strain automatically. Relics and other non-technological implants can occupy the same anatomical slots, but do not consume strain unless their own rules say otherwise. Some implants are outwardly visible - anyone who looks at you will see them - while hidden ones stay your secret. Procs trigger on their own in combat: on your hits, when you take damage, when you are badly hurt, or when you make a kill, each with its own chance and cooldown. General Tekal forbids cybernetics, so recoverable implants are uncommon and normally expose an illicit source: contraband wetware dealers and surgeons, augmented criminals, Green Door and Reca operatives, forbidden experiments, or repurposed machinery. Rarer grades are normally found on specialists, elites, or named threats. Shimmerdeep's Miura do not implant themselves; cyberware recovered there comes only from corrupted external machinery and mechaplants. See also: help effects, help equip, help parasite # keywords: implants, chrome, strain, augmentation, procs, ripperdoc, uninstall # alias: implant, implants, cyberscan, uninstall # see: effects, equip, parasite

docs.title: <<<<---- Daily Rewards ---->>>>
docs.text: <<<<---- Daily Rewards ---->>>> DarkWind has a daily rewards system that will reward a player with anything from experience and gold to interesting items. Items are claimable once every 24 hrs via the 'daily' command. After claiming a new 24 hr lockout starts followed by a 24 hr claim period. They are not claimable by calendar day and do require a player be active for 30 mins prior to claiming. Registered multies share one daily streak. Any registered multi can claim the shared daily reward after that character has been active for 30 minutes, and the reward items go to the character who runs daily. So, how does this work? Day 1 (Monday): Dink logs in at 9:00 AM. At 9:30 AM, she is eligible to claim Day One's daily reward. This starts a 24 HR lockout before she can claim her Day Two reward. Day Two will NOT be available prior to 9:30 AM the next day. Day 2, Scenario 1 (Tuesday): Dink logs in at 8:30 AM. Her daily reward lockout timer expires at 9:30 AM. Since Dink has been on since 8:30 AM, Dink can claim her daily reward at 9:30 AM. Day 2, Scenario 2 (Tuesday): Dink logs in at 9:32 AM. Her daily reward lockout timer expired at 9:30 AM, however, Dink still has to put in 30 mins in game before she can claim. This means Dink will be eligible to claim her Day Two reward at 10:02 AM. This means her Day Three reward will not be available to claim until 10:02 AM on Day Three, as there is always a 24 hour lockout after claiming, followed by a 24 hr claim period. Day 2, Scenario 3 (Wednesday): Dink logs in at 2 AM, (36 hours after claiming Day One). Dink is still eligible to claim her Day Two reward, as she's still in her 24 hr claim period. However, she cannot claim unti she has spent 30 minutes online. At 2:30 AM, Dink claims her Day Two reward and starts a new 24 hr lockout period, followed by a 24 hr claim period. This mean her Day Three reward will not be available to claim until 2:30 AM on the following day, as there is always a full 24 hour lockout after claiming. Day 2, Scenario 4 (Wednesday after 10:03 am): Dink completely forgets to log in for over 48 hours. Dink is returned to Day One and starts over. Regardless of what day of the week it is, or what time you claimed, there is ALWAYS a 24 hour lockout following claiming. So if you claim at 6:00 PM, you are not eligibile to claim again until 6:00 PM on the next day. However, you also ALWAYS have a full 24 hours to claim. This means that if you're claim time happens to be inconvienent for you one day you can adjust it so that it is. You will always have a FULL 24 hour lockout from the time you claim. Followed by a FULL 24 hour claim period based on when you claimed. This means that this is a rotating 24/48 hours. That means Day 30 could actually fall 36 actual days or more after the first day you claim.

docs.title: The deaths command shows locally tracked NPC-caused player death statistics.
docs.text: The deaths command shows locally tracked NPC-caused player death statistics. Syntax: deaths deaths here The global view shows the top 10 entries in each of these groups: Players Who Have Fallen Most Deadliest NPCs Most Fatal Rivalries The first group also names each player's most common NPC killer. The second includes the number of unique players killed by each NPC. Use "deaths here" to restrict all three groups to the cataloged area where you are standing. Player kills, player-controlled creatures, and environmental deaths are not included in these rankings. The tracker records deaths immediately when they happen and preserves its summaries across reboots. Its tracking date is shown in the command output. See also: help combatbrief, help score
