docs.title: Divine Omens and Patronage
docs.text: Divine Omens and Patronage The divine omen system tracks the influence of Mitra, Gaea, and Set across the world. Player action can push pressure toward a god. If one god has enough pressure, and enough distance from the others, that god becomes ascendant. If no god clears that threshold, the world is Godless. Personal patron ranks still work during Godless periods, but ascendance bonuses and Set's ascendant pressure do not. Useful commands: omens Read the current world omen. portents Alias for omens. patron Read your personal patronage. patron gods Learn the three patron identities. patron pledge <mitra|gaea|set> Pledge yourself to a patron. patron renounce Break your current pledge. patron favor Read your broad favor standing. patron pilgrimage start Begin a shrine pilgrimage. patron pilgrimage status Check your active pilgrimage. tithe <amount> to <god> Offer coins toward a god's pressure. tithe <amount> at shrine Tithe at the shrine in your room. pray at shrine Pray at the shrine in your room. meter Check Wrathful Avatar charge and rate. score Check Wrathful Avatar charge and rate. Shrines, tithes, pilgrimages, Holy Hours, marked enemies, and rare events all feed into the divine cycle. Shrines can currently be found at: Mitra The Temple of Mitra in DarkWind City. Gaea The rose garden near the chapel. Set The black altar in the temple of Qazaash. Patron ranks and world omens affect Wrathful Avatar charge. The system hides raw favor and pressure numbers on purpose; the public commands describe broad standing, current omens, and visible divine events without exposing exact tables. Related help: help patron help omens help avatar help shrine help pilgrimage

docs.title: donate <item> | donate all [item] | donate unkept
docs.text: donate <item> | donate all [item] | donate unkept The command donate allows you to donate an item in your inventory. The item is sent to the donation room in the main city of DarkWind. All donated items have no value, and therefore cannot be sold in the shops.

docs.title: Status Effects: Buffs and Debuffs
docs.text: ===================================================================== Status Effects: Buffs and Debuffs ===================================================================== Most temporary conditions on your character are effects. Helpful effects are buffs; harmful ones are debuffs. The buffs command lists both, numbered, with the time each has left. Buffs come from guild abilities, potions, equipment, implants, and special events. Timed buffs count down in real time. Buffs supplied by an item you are using last as long as the item does and are shown as "Permanent". You can end your own buffs early with clearbuff. Debuffs are poisons, diseases, hexes, and similar afflictions. Most deal damage every few seconds until they expire. Landing the same affliction again either refreshes its timer or simply fails while the first still runs - debuffs do not stack into stronger versions of themselves. clearbuff cannot remove them; they end on their own or through the right cure or dispel. Bodily conditions are a special family of debuff: Burning, Bleeding, Chilled, Freezing, Exposed, and Sundered. Burning, Bleeding, and Sundered grow in strength when fed by further attacks - buffs shows the current strength as a number - up to a cap that scales with your level. Being chilled again while already chilled deepens into Freezing, Exposed leaves your defenses open to critical attacks, and each Sundered stack lowers armour class by one, to a maximum of three. These conditions fade with time, and some also yield to the world itself: a warm hearth will thaw a deep chill. Not every ability registers with this display, so buffs may not show everything acting on you. See also: help buffs, help parasites, help cyberware # keywords: buff, debuff, poison, disease, burning, bleeding, sundered, hex # alias: debuff, debuffs, status # see: buffs, parasites

docs.title: Syntax: equip
docs.text: Syntax: equip DESCRIPTION =========== This command will quickly wear all your armour and wield your weapon. Be warned though, it is not a foolproof way to get equiped with the best of all your equipment you might be carrying. After equipping, make sure you are wearing and using the correct armours and weapons. Use loadout when you want to save and switch between named, repeatable equipment configurations. Use smartequip when you want the game to compare directly carried armour and weapons with gearcheck scores, fill open slots, and attempt to equip the stronger choices.

docs.title: SYNTAX
docs.text: SYNTAX ====== gearcheck gearcheck <item> upgrades DESCRIPTION =========== Compares the equipment in your inventory with the equipment you are currently using. It accounts for weapon class, armour protection, equipment stats, resistances, sigils, known combat effects, cyberware strain, durability, the equipment slots that an item would replace, and the normal bonus or penalty from your trained weapon specialization. The normal report shows every comparable item, including upgrades, sidegrades, downgrades, and items with effects that cannot be scored confidently. Use gearcheck <item> for the full numeric breakdown. Ranked equipment also shows its item level. Item level describes the part of the game's progression for which the equipment was designed; it does not prevent a lower-level character from using the item. Ranked weapons penetrate some worn armour, while ranked armour resists weapons below its own level. Equal-level weapon and armour ratings cancel each other. When you have an empty equipment slot, gearcheck shows a separate ➕ EMPTY SLOT section and recommends the strongest compatible item in your inventory. For ring and amulet slots, it can show multiple choices when more than one slot is open. 🟢 UPGRADE means the carried item is measurably stronger. 🟡 SAME POWER (SIDEGRADE) means its overall score is close, but its strengths may be distributed differently. 🔴 DOWNGRADE means the currently equipped item or loadout is stronger. ⚠ UNCERTAIN means an item has a scripted effect that cannot be scored until its builder declares a power value. Gearcheck never equips, removes, installs, or otherwise changes an item. Scripted item effects are only included when the item explicitly declares their power value. Use smartequip to automatically apply positive, high-confidence armour and weapon improvements from your direct inventory.

docs.title: Syntax: gocot
docs.text: Syntax: gocot This command will magically transport you back into the center of Darkwind. This command will only work if you are presently deceased, or if you are trapped in a bugged room. SEE ALSO ======== recall, ncot

docs.title: Gods
docs.text: Gods Mitra, Gaea, and Set are the active divine patrons in the current omen cycle. Use patron gods for a short description of each god, or help divine for the full patronage system. Useful topics: help divine help patron help omens help shrine help pilgrimage

docs.title: Invasions can happen regularly on Darkwind.  They are announced by a
docs.text: Invasions can happen regularly on Darkwind. They are announced by a siren [DIPPS] and involve regular messages broadcast to the players. During invasions, NPCs and shops in town are regular targets, and the shops may be destroyed. It takes some time to repair the shops and get them working again, and they may not be usable in the meantime. Lower level players are advised to stay out of the city of Darkwind during an invasion, as players may be targetted by powerful mobs roaming through town. A siren [DIPPS] will signal the all-clear when the invaders have been vanquished or succeed in their invasion.

docs.title: Kingdoms are player-ruled realms of Darkwind. Each kingdom has a Ruler,
docs.text: ===================================================================== Kingdoms are player-ruled realms of Darkwind. Each kingdom has a Ruler, a charter, a roster of citizens, its own nobility titles, and a heraldic sigil carried by every citizen. Founding: new kingdoms are chartered and activated with the help of the game administration. If you dream of a throne, speak with the admins. Joining: citizenship is by induction, in person. A noble with the power to induct must stand in the same room as you and make the offer through the kingdom's management menu. You are then asked whether you wish to become a citizen; answer yes or no. You must be at least level 5 and cannot already belong to another kingdom. Citizenship: you carry your kingdom's sigil, which cannot be dropped, sold, or stolen, and it marks you as a citizen to anyone who looks at you. You also gain the kingdom channel: kchat <message> speaks to every citizen, and ekchat <message> emotes to them. Nobility: the Ruler may create custom titles, each granting any mix of four powers: inducting members, removing members, assigning titles, and owning a castle. New citizens start as "Citizen"; the title "Ruler" is reserved for the kingdom's owner. Management: the Ruler types managekingdom to hold court with the Ministry of Administrative Affairs. Its sections are: Deeds And Titles - set and view the charter, create, edit, and remove titles, view citizens, induct new members, bestow titles, and strip citizenship. Heraldry And Propaganda - name the sigil, choose its colors, and write its descriptions. Castle Keep And Environs - the office of the Royal Engineer. The whole kingdom hears arrivals and departures on the kingdom channel. See also: clans, kchat, who # keywords: kingdom, citizenship, induct, sigil, charter, ruler, title # alias: kingdom, nobles, noble

docs.title: Syntax: laston <player>
docs.text: Syntax: laston <player> DESCRIPTION =========== Tells the last time <player> was logged on or if they are on, how long since they logged on.

docs.title: The leaderboard command shows the top 50 players on the achievement
docs.text: The leaderboard command shows the top 50 players on the achievement ladder. Syntax: leaderboard This leaderboard is based on total achievement tiers unlocked. It also shows completed achievement lines and each player's equipped achievement title. If you want the endless dungeon rankings instead, use: eternal leaderboard If you want your personal achievement journal, use: achievements See also: help achievements, help eternal_dungeon

docs.title: SYNTAX
docs.text: SYNTAX ====== loadout loadout list loadout save <name> loadout update <name> loadout show <name> loadout use <name> loadout rename <old> <new> loadout delete <name> gearset ... DESCRIPTION =========== Equipment loadouts are named presets for your worn armour and wielded weapons. Save your current equipment with loadout save <name>, then use loadout use <name> to return to that setup. A loadout is a complete equipment state. Standard armour or weapons not named in the preset are removed when it is used, which allows a preset to preserve intentionally empty slots. Installed cyberware and other internal equipment are never changed. Every saved item must be directly in your inventory before a loadout can be used. Loadouts do not retrieve items from containers, banks, rooms, or other storage, and they never clone or replace missing gear. If an item is missing or cannot be identified safely, nothing is changed. Normal equipment rules remain in force. Cursed items, scripted restrictions, guild requirements, race and size limits, shields, and weapon combinations can prevent a switch. If a restriction stops a switch after it begins, DarkWind attempts to restore your original equipment and tells you whether that restoration succeeded. You cannot switch loadouts during combat, while dead, or while phased out. You may save up to ten loadouts. Names may contain up to twenty lowercase letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens. The gearset command is an alias for loadout. # alias: gearset

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Commands ======================================== mail - loads your mail reader checkmail - checks to see if you have mail readmail - puts you into the mail system (see arguments below) closemail - removes your reader mail <person> (only works if you have a mail reader loaded) - sends mail to another character. Using the "set" command, you can set your mud mail to be forwarded to your internet email address. See "help set" for more information. The following commands are issued from the mail prompt. (1-max_num) -- Show that message number . -- Show the current message again + -- Show the next message +<number> -- Show the message <number> ahead of this one - -- Show the previous message -<number> -- Show the message <number> before this one d <number> -- Delete message <number> from your mail. h -- Show message headers l -- Save the current message to /log/<you>.mbox n -- Goto and show next message R -- Reply to the current message's sender r -- Reply to the current message's sender and Cc's q -- Quit mail x -- Quit mail without erasing any messages ? -- Show this help information

docs.title: DarkWind's mechanics help covers the core systems behind everyday play, from
docs.text: DarkWind's mechanics help covers the core systems behind everyday play, from parties and buffs to quests, scripts, specialization, and PK. Common topics in this section include: help mechanics party help mechanics buffs help mechanics quests help mechanics divine help mechanics patron help mechanics omens help mechanics parasites help mechanics reputation help mechanics specialization help mechanics scripts Use help list mechanics to see every topic in this section.

docs.title: Your blood oath gives you several abilities related to the person you
docs.text: Your blood oath gives you several abilities related to the person you have sworn the oath with. Available commands are: otell: This allows you to send a message over your oath line. It is essentially a free tell. oemote: When given with <msg> it will display <yourname> <msg>. If you are Brunhilda and you type oemote "is fighting an orc" then the person you are sworn to will see 'Brunhilda is fighting an orc'. ohist: This lists the past 15 messages on the oath channel. olook: This ability will allow one oath taker to see where the other is located. It costs a nominal (5) amount of spell points to use. oinspire: This may only be performed when both blood oath takers are in the same room. It will inspire you, adding to your combat abilities and your statistics for a time. renounce: If you 'renounce oath' your blood oath will be cancelled. You will suffer the penalties for failure to uphold your oath and in addition will lose respect and be marked as an oathbreaker. You may remove the oathbreaker status by swearing a new oath, but must earn the lost respect back yourself. Do not take oath renunciation lightly.

docs.title: Omens
docs.text: Omens The omens command reads the current divine balance of the world. omens portents Omens never shows raw pressure numbers. It gives broad prophetic language about whether Mitra, Gaea, or Set is ascendant. If no god has enough pressure to rule the realm, the world is Godless and the omens are silent. Omens also reports major active divine events, such as Holy Hour or Eclipse. Use patron to inspect your personal pledge, rank, debt, and current avatar charge modifier. World states: Ascendant One god has enough pressure to lead the others. Godless No god has enough pressure to rule the realm. Eclipse Set has dragged a temporary shadow across the cycle. Holy Hour A god's hour is active and patron blessings may strengthen. Omens are affected by tithes, shrine activity, pilgrimages, marked enemies, and reputation-bearing deeds with clear divine meaning. The command intentionally describes the state in prophetic language instead of showing raw pressure numbers. Related help: help divine help patron help shrine

docs.title: SYNTAX
docs.text: SYNTAX ====== parasite swallow <parasite> / eat <parasite> DESCRIPTION =========== Parasites are finite living infections that improve hit point recovery, spell point recovery, or both while carrying real costs. Carriers -- larvae, worms, cysts, and stranger things -- are sold at The Brood Apothecary in DarkWind City, south of Xenor Road. Inside the shop, list parasites and describe parasite <name> preview each strain before you commit. Once swallowed, the infection is represented as active internal equipment. Its burden and any sigils therefore use the same stat and sigil machinery as worn gear, while remaining separate from cyberware location conflicts. Infection is voluntary: buy a carrier, hold it, and swallow or eat it. Each strain has a minimum level, some accept only hosts of a particular guild, and only one parasite can live in you at a time. While you are hurt or drained, the parasite mends you each pulse: some strains restore hit points, some restore spell points, and the strongest do both. It never heals past your maximums. In exchange it exacts a burden that varies by strain: reduced maximum hit or spell points, weakened dodge, damage, or swings, and sometimes an appetite that drinks your spell points while it works. If you cannot feed a hungry parasite's full appetite, it goes starved and does not mend you that pulse. A parasite lives for a fixed amount of online time; its clock pauses while you are logged out, and it goes still for good when the time runs out. It dies with you if you die, and guild-bound strains die if you leave their guild. Use parasite to inspect your infection: healing, burden, appetite, fed or starved state, and time remaining. To be rid of one early, return to The Brood Apothecary and use purge parasite for a 2500 gold fee. See also: parasites, brood apothecary, buffs, inventory

docs.title: SYNTAX
docs.text: SYNTAX ====== help parasites parasite DESCRIPTION =========== Parasites are living healing bargains bought at The Brood Apothecary in DarkWind City. A parasite can be swallowed to live inside you for a finite amount of online time. While it is alive, it can restore hit points, spell points, or both during heartbeat pulses when you are depleted. Only one parasite may live in you at a time. Parasites do not restore past your maximum hit points or spell points, and do not last forever. Their remaining time pauses while you are offline, but they do not survive death. Stronger parasites can carry serious costs. Depending on the parasite, these may include reduced maximum hit points, reduced maximum spell points, spell point appetite while regenerating, weaker damage output, or other combat burdens. If a parasite needs spell points as appetite and you cannot pay the full appetite, it becomes starved for that pulse and does not mend you. COMMANDS ======== parasite Shows your active parasite, healing pulse, burden, appetite, starvation state, and remaining online time. swallow <parasite> Installs a parasite carrier you are holding, if you meet its requirements. eat <parasite> Also installs a parasite carrier you are holding. list parasites Used inside The Brood Apothecary to see available parasites. describe parasite <number or name> Used inside The Brood Apothecary to inspect requirements, healing, cost, duration, appetite, and burdens before buying. purge parasite Used inside The Brood Apothecary to pay for removal of your active parasite. LOCATION ======== The Brood Apothecary is south of Xenor Road near the DarkWind City shop district. From the road, look for the narrow apothecary doorway. See also: help brood apothecary, help economy apothecary, help buffs, help inventory.

docs.title: The Darkwind Party System allows players to join groups of 2-6
docs.text: The Darkwind Party System allows players to join groups of 2-6 players in order to combine their efforts battling against the dangers of Darkwind. No longer is this ability contained in a simple object that can be lost or misplaced, but is now part of the essence of every adventurer. While in a party, you may communicate easily with your fellows, gain a share of experience from each others' kills, and, at your option, split any earned gold. The following commands relate to the party system: epsay partyhist pauto pautosplit pboot pemote pfollow pleader pleave pname poffer psay psplit pstatus preset To get more information on a command, use "help <command>"

docs.title: Divine Patronage
docs.text: Divine Patronage Patronage lets a player pledge to Mitra, Gaea, or Set. A pledge affects the rate at which heroes build Wrathful Avatar charge. Use: patron patron gods patron pledge <mitra|gaea|set> patron renounce patron favor patron pilgrimage start patron pilgrimage status Your patron rank rises as you earn favor. Favor comes from patron activity such as tithes, shrines, pilgrimages, marked enemies, and deeds whose reputation matches your patron. The exact favor numbers are hidden, but patron favor describes your broad standing. Each rank grants an avatar charge-rate bonus. If your patron is ascendant, the bonus is stronger. During your patron's Holy Hour it is stronger again. Mitra rewards fellowship. Mitra followers gain a small extra charge-rate bonus for nearby Mitra followers in the same room. Gaea rewards endurance. Gaea's blessing is weaker at full health and becomes strongest when your health is low. Set rewards shadow and pressure. When Set is ascendant, good-aligned non-Set followers may suffer a charge-rate penalty unless protected by special events or shrine actions. Renouncing a patron leaves a temporary debt that slows Wrathful Avatar charge. Use score or meter to see your current charge rate. The patron command also shows Signs. Signs describe whether your recent reputation fits your pledge or strains it. A strained vow can briefly slow Wrathful Avatar charge, but it does not remove your patron. Patron activity: Tithes Offer coins with tithe <amount> to <god>, or tithe at shrine. Shrines Pray or tithe at a divine shrine. Pilgrimage Start with patron pilgrimage start after pledging. Combat Marked enemies may appear as the divine cycle stirs. Shrines can currently be found at: Mitra The Temple of Mitra in DarkWind City. Gaea The rose garden near the chapel. Set The black altar in the temple of Qazaash. Related help: help divine help omens help shrine help pilgrimage

docs.title: Divine Pilgrimage
docs.text: Divine Pilgrimage Pilgrimage is a patron activity. After pledging to Mitra, Gaea, or Set, you may begin a pilgrimage and visit divine shrines before the omen-thread grows cold. Commands: patron pilgrimage start patron pilgrimage status look token You must have a patron before beginning a pilgrimage. Completing one can earn patron favor and help tie your character more closely to the divine cycle. Related help: help divine help patron help shrine

docs.title: Darkwind PK Overview
docs.text: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Darkwind PK Overview ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ - Darkwind has a fairly simple PK (player killer) system. - Once a player registers as a PKer, returning to non-PK status is possible with some very stiff penalties. Becoming a PKer is a decision that should not be taken lightly. - A player must register PK before level 30 to do so without penalty. If a player registers after level 29, they will be subject to loss of levels and stats dropping the player to level 20. This includes those that have attained the maximum level of 250. - Balance of skills between guilds will not encompass PK. Balance issues will strictly be considered by the admin for the benefit of the mud as a whole. Complaints such as a hold spell lasting too long, or poison doing too much damage in PK, will not be addressed since they are in balance for general combat. In PK, you must plan around these shortcomings. Only bugs in skills will be addressed for PK purposes. - Registering and unregistering PK is done two west and two south of the center of Darkwind city. - It is possible to unregister PK if you've gone an appropriate amount of playing time without PK activity. Visit the PK Registration room for more information. - Anyone that is registered as PK can kill anyone else that is registered. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Darkwind PK Rules ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 1. In PK to PK combat, no non-PK interference is allowed - period. This means no healing of PK players during PK combat, no locates, no clearminds, no supplying food or drink in any form - not even in the moments after combat has ended. If a considerable amount of time has passed since the PK interaction, and the player requests a heal, clearmind, or other type of assistance, then this is acceptable. If you are worried you are toeing this line, don't take the risk as the penalty for violation of this rule is the loss of five levels, and five stats from each stat category and you will be force-regged PK. 2. Do not post anything concerning issues you have with PK to any boards. If a player violates the rules of PK, send a mudmail with a log of the incident to the administration of Darkwind (IMP+), and if the rules have been violated, penalties will be enforced accordingly. Corresponding emails from witnesses will help your cause, as we all know logs have been known to be fabricated. Failure to adhere to this rule will result in a loss of one level, and one stat from each stat category. 2a) Do not use shout, gossip, or other public channels for pk related chatting. The newbie channel may be used to inform newbies on the nature of PK on DarkWind. 3. No complaints will be accepted in the violation of these rules if they are accompanied by complaining, or insulting tones towards the administration of Darkwind. What this means is, proofread what you write before you mudmail the administration about an incident, state only the facts and no opinions. The situation will be handled in as timely a fashion as possible. If your mudmail is in violation of these rules, you will lose one level, and one stat from each stat category. 4. Deliberate repeated abuse of a bug in PK will result in the demotion of your character to level 1, with 1 in each stat, while maintaining your current PK status. Banishment will also be considered, all the way up to a site ban. What constitutes bug abuse is totally at the discretion of the Darkwind administration, so if you are not sure if it is a bug or not, don't do it. Report it to the administration via mudmail, adhering to rule 3. 5. If we all follow these simple rules PK should run more smoothly than it has in the past on Darkwind. Please help us keep things under control, so PK can remain a part of Darkwind. 6. You cannot deliberately resurrect a player (in any way) to immediately PK that person again, in order to get guaranteed contiguous kills. If caught, this will result in an immediate punishing of both the resurrecting player and the killing player. 7. Stacking mobs -- If a player chooses to stack mobs from an area. They must NOT leave aggro monsters for other players to wander into. This is considered as unsanctioned PKing. Any player caught doing this and/or it causes the death of another player, the offensing player will face the loss of 5 levels, 5 from all stat categories (including meta), and will be force-regged PK. Dragons found in violation of this will also lose 5 from their age. Additional punishments will happen with each violation, up to and including banishment from creating mythic characters, purging, and total banishment. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Happy Hunting! - the Darkwind Administration ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text: DESCRIPTION =========== The pnote command allows you to read your personal notebook. All adventurers carry scrolls, on which they may store important information. pnote a- <text> This will add the note <text> to your personal scroll. The new note will appear at the end of the scroll. pnote d- <number of message> This will delete a message from the information scroll. Any message 'beneath' the deleted message will be bumped up one number. (If you have 3 messages and delete number 2, then number 3 will become the new number 2.) Syntax: pnote

docs.title: You can set up your command prompt using the command: "set prompt <string>".
docs.text: You can set up your command prompt using the command: "set prompt <string>". See also: set

docs.title: Questing is a personal challenge, but it sometimes requires
docs.text: Questing is a personal challenge, but it sometimes requires a little bit of help. Stuck on a more difficult part? Ask a friend! Please keep all quest info off public lines, like shout.

docs.title: Syntax: recall
docs.text: Syntax: recall The recall command lets you beg the powers of Darkwind to whisk you back to the center of town (COT) from anywhere in the world that allows teleportation. After each successful use, the powers must replenish for 15 minutes before you can recall again. You will be told when the cooldown has elapsed and recall is available once more. Notes: * Cannot be used if you are already at COT. * Cannot be used in rooms that block teleportation. * The 15-minute cooldown is independent of ncot and any guild teleport abilities. * Newbies and applicants typically use ncot instead, which has no cooldown. SEE ALSO ======== ncot, gocot

docs.title: Darkwind Reputation
docs.text: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Darkwind Reputation ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Your reputation is shaped by what you do in the world. At higher levels it affects whether you are known as a Hero, an Adventurer, or a Villain. Guild membership alone does not decide your reputation. A paladin can fall, a thief can do useful work, and a mage can be feared or admired depending on what their magic does. Reputation changes come from actions: quests, divine offerings, public praise or slander, resurrection, theft, desecration, and other notable deeds. Some deeds also leave hidden marks that help the world understand why you are known the way you are. Mercy, terror, honor, faith, nature, crime, secrecy, blood, service, and public notoriety may all shape what people remember about you. When a deed affects your reputation, you may feel a small sign of it. Those signs are intentionally broad. DarkWind will not show the exact weights, thresholds, or every hidden mark, but it will increasingly let you know when your actions have begun to matter. Use reputation to reflect on your public renown, common whispers, and recent signs. This command describes the shape of your reputation without turning it into a ledger. Deeds with clear divine meaning can also tug the omen cycle. Merciful and service-minded acts may carry toward Mitra, nature and restoration toward Gaea, and fear or shadowed ambition toward Set. During a god's Holy Hour, matching deeds carry farther. Current public reputation labels: Hero A positive heroism reputation. Adventurer A neutral heroism reputation. Villain A negative heroism reputation. See also: help leveling hero help mechanics quests help mechanics divine help mechanics tithe ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

docs.title: After many warning shouts and messages I am going to formally
docs.text: After many warning shouts and messages I am going to formally post about the use of clients for scripting aka client-side scripting. Use of in-game scripting is allowed. THIS ONLY APPLIES TO CLIENT-SIDE SCRIPTING. Definition ---------- In the eyes of the admin a script is the use of some sort of terminal assistance program/code that will allow the user of DW to execute multiple mud commands that require multiple <enter>'s with just one command and <enter> by the user of the terminal program. Scripts do not include guild abilities or the built in scripting ability of the mud. Built-in Scripting ------------------ The built in script command may be used to run short, comma-separated command lists. It also supports pacing a command with delay <seconds> <command> or delay <seconds>s <command>, such as: script look,delay 5s north,look Each delayed step may wait up to 60 seconds, and a single script may contain up to 300 total seconds of delay. Global emotes and guild emotes currently available to your character may be used as script steps. A guild emote becomes invalid immediately if you leave that guild or its abilities become inactive. Examples -------- The following are examples of what we consider scripting. This is in no way an all inclusive list. - Using a command such as 5e in a client program to move you 5 square east by means of only hitting 1 button. - A single command that will burn a corpse and take everything that was on the corpse. - A single command that will take you from for example COT to hyper. - A single command that will log you in, buy kegs/meals, get a pony, take you to an area, and begin killing. Justification ------------- Everyone here hates lag. Scripts are the major causes of LAG here on DW. Some may ask how a script causes lag. Remember that the mud can execute only one command at a time. When a player has a computer enter multiple commands as fast as the computer can these commands get queued up in the driver until they are executed. These commands get issued faster than the mud can process them. When multiple people use scripts the queue grows larger and larger until the mud's driver can catch up with it. To the normal user, this person must wait until his turn in the queue get issued. Hence, to this person is a sense of lag. Punishment ---------- Currently the punishment for the first offense in the the use of scripting as determined by nthe admin of DW is loss of 1 lvl, 1 of each stat, and twice as much exp has the player has on hand. This may change to half the players levels, half the stats, and twice the EXP on hand. Repeated offenses will be dealt with by banishment. Such punishment can be dealt as deemed necessary by the admin of DW. Conclusion ---------- Please do not ruin the fun of all on DW with scripting. All it does is ruin the fun for us all. The administration of Darkwind also frowns upon the use of clients which are capable of executing scripts, for obvious reasons.

docs.title: Sigils
docs.text: ===================================================================== Sigils ===================================================================== Sigils are arcane markings worked into rare equipment. Each marking carries a level. While you wield, wear, or internally bind the item, its levels count toward your total for that sigil. Marked pieces work as a set: equip several and their levels add together, up to the sigil's maximum useful level. Sigils are part of an item as it is found - you cannot inscribe them yourself. A sigil briefly glows when you pick up a marked item. Examine a piece of equipment to see any recognized markings it bears, each listed with its level and that sigil's maximum. Ordinary marked equipment usually supplies one level, so building around a sigil means choosing several compatible pieces. Marked gear can be found in both older and newer regions. A few powerful signature items supply two levels from one item. Some sigils may be occult. Their markings and effects cannot be identified, and they do not appear in your catalog until your character uncovers the secret that reveals them. Discovery is permanent for that character. Unrecognized markings still function and still count toward equipment power. What sigils can do: Early marks improve practical rewards such as corpse ash, profession materials, salvage returns, and seated recovery. Later marks improve offense, defense, and elemental affinities, or react to events such as excess healing, killing blows, repeated hits, and otherwise fatal damage. No sigil grants a new command. Type sigils catalog for every sigil your character recognizes, its maximum useful level, where it tends to appear, and a concise description. Type sigils for a table of your active sigils: each combined level against its maximum, and which piece of equipment supplies it. The columns are head (H), cloak (C), shoulders (Sh), aura (A), neck (N1/N2), body (B), legs (L), shield (S), feet (F), rings (R1/R2), gloves (G), main and secondary weapons (MW/SW), internal equipment (I), and other sources (O). A total shown in bright color has reached that sigil's maximum. See also: help equip, help uniques # keywords: markings, set bonus, critical strike, evade, ruthless, catalog, discovery # alias: sigil # see: equip, uniques

docs.title: SYNTAX
docs.text: SYNTAX ====== smartequip smartequip -v DESCRIPTION =========== Uses the same equipment-power scores as gearcheck to improve your currently equipped armour and weapons. Smart equip fills open equipment slots and replaces equipped items only when the new combination has a higher, high-confidence score. Hand equipment is evaluated as a complete setup rather than one item at a time. Smart equip compares a two-handed weapon against compatible dual-wielded weapon pairs and weapon-and-shield combinations. A secondary weapon's offense is weighted for its reduced attack rate, and your trained weapon specialization adds its normal combat advantage or disadvantage to the score. Only armour and weapons carried directly in your inventory are considered. Equipment stored inside bags or other containers is left where it is. Installed implants and other internal equipment are never changed. Smart equip applies the best compatible hand setup atomically, then checks other armour improvements one at a time. If an item cannot be worn or wielded because of a character requirement, curse, size restriction, weapon combination, or another equipment rule, your displaced equipment is restored and that setup or item is skipped. You cannot use smart equip during combat, while dead, or while phased out. Use gearcheck afterward when you want to inspect the detailed score behind each decision. Use loadout to save the resulting equipment as a named preset. VERBOSE MODE ============ smartequip -v performs the same equipment changes and then shows every standard equipment slot. For each slot it lists the currently equipped item, all inventory candidates that can use that slot, the candidate and displaced item scores, score difference, gearcheck classification, confidence, items that would be replaced, rejection reason, and final decision. Each slot begins with a bright SELECTED summary. Winning equipment is shown first with a ★ WINNER badge, while kept current gear, rejected items, replaced gear, and unselected candidates use distinct labels and colors. Equipment inside containers and implants also appear with an explanation of why smart equip did not consider them.

docs.title: Specialization
docs.text: Specialization ============== Specialization allows a player to gain extra bonuses in combat at the cost of flexibility. Over time, a specialist's skill with his chosen weapons or armors will increase, while his ability to use other kinds of equipment will decrease due to disuse. There are two areas in which a player may specialize: weapons and armour. While similar, there are a few differences in the way specialization works in the two cases that are worth noting. Weapon Specialization --------------------- On DarkWind, weapon types are characterized by their sizes, damage types, and miscellaneous characteristics. The following lists give some examples of typical weapons and their characterizations: Size: Small weapons: daggers, saps, small short swords, hand axes Medium weapons: larger short swords, maces, clubs, longer swords Large weapons: longswords, battleaxes, long maces, shorter staves Huge weapons: awl pikes, two-handed swords, greatbows, long staves Damage type: Slash: most sword variants, naginata, some polearms Pierce: daggers, rapiers, spears, bows, wooden stakes Blunt: staves, maces, clubs, hammers, rocks Cleave: axes, halberds, cleavers, some polearms Miscellaneous: Missile: bows, crossbows, slings, throwing daggers, darts Pole: most staves, halberds, spears, tridents Note that weapons may have multiple damage types if they can be used in muliple ways. For example, shortswords can generally be used as slashing and also piercing weapons. In addition, size and miscellaneous character- istics affect a player's ability to dual wield certain weapons. Normal sized players can dual wield one large (or smaller) weapons, and one medium (or smaller) weapon. Players who are smaller or larger due to race may find their choices more limited. Missile and pole weapons can never be dual wielded. The first step in weapon specialization is to pick a size. Although you only pick one size category, you will automatically get the next larger size as well in your specialization. Every specialist must pick a size. Optionally, a specialist may pick one or two damage types. Choosing one damage type will give a bonus with any weapon that has that damage type, even if it's in combination with another type. If you pick two types the weapon used must have BOTH damage types to get a bonus. Finally, a specialist may also choose a miscellaneous type, which further restricts the bonus to those weapons with that miscellaneous characteristic. The nature of weapon specialization is that the more precisely one specializes, the larger the bonus he gets. The corresonding penalty for using a weapon not in his specialization is also larger. So, while a specialization in large, cleave, pierce, polearm may give a very large bonus when using some halberds, there is a tradeoff in flexibility. In order to specialize, you must find the specialization trainer in Darkwind city and train in the type desired. Once you've specialized, you will gain experience using that weapon. Every so often you may notice that your skill is improving with that weapon as well. When you have accumu- lated enough experience with your specialized weapon type, you can return to the training hall and advance your weapon specialization level. At some point, you may choose to change your weapon specialization. Depending on the difference between your current specialization and your desired one, you may find that your skill level drops somewhat when changing your specialization. This can be done at the training hall as well. Armour specialization --------------------- Armour specialization works much like weapon specialization but the choices are much smaller. You may choose one of four kinds armor: clothes: normal clothing, padded armours, small shields light: leather, studded leather, medium shields medium: chain mail, scale mail, large shields heavy: plate mail, splint mail, banded mail, large/huge shields The effect of armour specialization is much more pronounced in the lighter varieties of armour than the heavier ones due to the constricting nature of such heavy armours. Experienced specialists in lighter armour varieties have been known to dodge and deflect blows with such skill that their overall defense rivalled that of knights wearing the heaviest suits of plate armour. Armour specialization is trained in the same training hall as weapon specialization in DarkWind city. Why Specialize? --------------- Specialization is NOT required to play DarkWind. Generally speaking specialization trades off effectiveness using all equipment against increased effectiveness using a smaller set of equipment. In the case of weapons, selecting more types and miscellaneous characteristics will increase the bonus given, but will also increase the penalties for using out-of-spec equipment, and also decrease the number of in-spec items available. For armours, the bonus or penalty for specialization is higher for the lighter types and lower for the heavier types (in order from highest to lowest: clothes, light, medium, heavy). Note that in the case of armours, even if a piece of armour feels awkward to you, it will usually still contribute substantially to your defensive abilities over being naked (unless that armour plain sucks to begin with). While specialization does give substantial bonuses in combat, it is worth noting that other factors affect offense and defense. Specific to equipment use, certain unique items may be so powerful as to dwarf the effects of specialization, and may be worth using despite being awkward. Raising Specialist Level ------------------------ During the course of adventuring, your will gain experience in your specilized weapon and armour. Occasionally, you will find that you notice yourself becoming better in the use of your equipment. When you reach the point that you can no longer advance without training, go to the combat trainer in DarkWind city and advance your weapon or armour specialization level. You will only gain experience in your specialized weapon if the weapon you are using as your main weapon is in your specialized type (you gain the benefits of specializion for both weapons though, for dual wielders) and you will only gain experience in your specialized armour if you wear the armour type you're specialized in. The more pieces of armour you wear in that type, the faster your specialization will advance. Additionally, you can only gain experience in your specializations by fighting in reasonably challenging combats. If you fight monsters that you easily overwhelm, you will not progress much. Finally, wisdom and intelligence influences how fast you learn how to use your equipment as well.

docs.title: Currently, Darkwind does not support spells for players without guilds.
docs.text: Currently, Darkwind does not support spells for players without guilds. The exception is the introductory Dark Wind powers. Unguilded newbies through level 5 may use ncot, ndomain, nbolt, nkick, npunch and nheal. Players from levels 6 through 49 may use their adventurer forms: acot, adomain, abolt, akick, apunch and aheal. While fighting, characters through level 20 may occasionally feel the Dark Wind refresh a small amount of SP. Both its chance and strength taper with level. SEE ALSO ======== kill, ncot, ndomain, nbolt, nkick, npunch, nheal, acot, adomain, abolt, akick, apunch, aheal
