docs.title: Syntax: uniques [tabular] [weapon | armour | claimed | available]
docs.text: Syntax: uniques [tabular] [weapon | armour | claimed | available] uniques [favorites | hoarders | playerfavorites] [count] ===================================================================== Unique weapons and armour are one of a kind: only a single copy of each can exist in the game at a time. While one is out in the world - or in someone's hands - no second copy will appear. Uniques come from their usual places in the world; mighty foes guard many of them. Uniques do not expire on a timer. If one is accidentally sold to an ordinary shop or lost in the quit room, it is transferred to the world market so that it can return to circulation. The first player to pick up, wield, or wear a unique after a reboot claims it. Claims are announced on the events channel and recorded forever in the unique leaderboards. Claimed status clears at reboot, so every boot is a fresh race. Destruction releases the unique to spawn again, but does not erase that boot's first claim. A market status shows when the live copy is currently listed for sale. Commands: uniques List known uniques and whether each is claimed this reboot or still available, with its source continent or domain. uniques weapon Only weapons; uniques armour for armour. uniques claimed Only claimed; uniques available for the unclaimed. uniques tabular [filter] Force aligned columns instead of the sentence-style rows used for narrow terminals and screen-reader mode. uniques favorites [count] Most-claimed uniques ever. uniques hoarders [count] Players with the most claims. uniques playerfavorites [count] Each player's most-claimed unique. Counts run 1-50 and default to 10. Just after a reboot the catalog rebuilds itself, so entries may keep appearing for a few minutes while the refresh completes. See also: help sigils, help equip # keywords: unique, rare, leaderboard, claimed, hoarders # alias: unique # see: sigils, equip

docs.title: SYNTAX
docs.text: SYNTAX ========== wimpy # Where # is equal to the percentage of remaining HP you want to run at DESCRIPTION =========== Toggle wimpy mode. If you are in wimpy mode, your legs will run away if your hit points goes below whatever percent of your HP you have designated. Default for a new player is brave mode. You will not run away. This is no secure thing. It might save you, however some monsters hack away more than your allowed % of your HP, and you might find yourself dead without warning. Also, some monsters can run as fast as your legs.

+---------------------------------------------------------------------+ MINI QUESTS +---------------------------------------------------------------------+ Mini quests are fun, typically fairly simple quests that players of various levels can accomplish. Each quest is made up of one or more objectives, and a set of rewards when all objectives are complete. Some quests are open for all levels, but some quests have a minimum and maximum level. Additionally, some quests require that you must have completed a previous quest. All and all, mini quests should be a lot of fun to complete! For more information, see: "help quest_commands" +---------------------------------------------------------------------+ +---------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: Your Journey Through Darkwind
docs.text: Your Journey Through Darkwind ===================================================================== A stage-by-stage walkthrough from your first steps to seasoned adventurer. Each stage is its own short help page -- read them as your character grows, not all at once. help stage1 Your first minutes: the tutorial, looking, useful display settings, and finding your way around town help stage2 Gear up and learn to fight (levels 1-5): safer combat and corpse-loot settings help stage3 Choose your path: guilds, remote advancement, and leveling help stage4 See the world (levels 5-30): areas, wayshards, quests, and what death really costs help stage5 Money and craft: remote banking, the market, and professions help stage6 Find your people: channels, parties, clans, and kingdoms help stage7 Sharpen the blade (levels 30-100): bosses, dungeons, and uniques help stage8 Renown and rebirth (level 100+): hero, legend, and the remort endgame At every stage: play at play.darkwind.ai for the live map and panels (help client), browse all topics with help list, and report anything odd with bug, idea, or typo. See also: help stage1, help basics, help client, help feedback # keywords: walkthrough, beginner, start, getting started, new player # alias: walkthrough, journey, newplayer, getting_started, gettingstarted

docs.title: Welcome to Darkwind!
docs.text: Welcome to Darkwind! Most of the basic information about Darkwind can be found in the Newbie Tome. You can obtain one from the Newbie Tome Dispenser at Center of Town. Use the command ncot if you need to return there. Do not forget to look at the machine, then pull lever and read tome. The following are basic directions to help you start your adventuring career. This information can also be found in the Newbie Tome. ============================================================================== Equipment, Stores and Bank ============================================================================== Erga's newbie store. Erga hands out free equipment that is perfectly suited for anyone under level 5. Do not waste your time looking elsewhere. He has some good quality stuff. From Cot: w,w,w,w,s [4w,s] Do not forget to read the sign. ______________________________________________________________________________ Donation room. The mighty heroes and legendary adventurers that inhabit the realms of Darkwind may be inclined to donate equipment to the more inexperienced adventurers. You can visit the Donation room to see what they may have to offer you. From Cot: n,n,n,n,n,e [5n,e] ______________________________________________________________________________ Bank. You are able to keep your money safe at the bank. That way, if you die, you will not lose your hard-earned cash. From Cot: w,w,w,w,w,s,s,s,e [5w,3s,e] ______________________________________________________________________________ Taylors. Taylors is the general store in town. He will be happy to buy your goods from you. Selling treasures you find on your adventures is a great way to earn a pretty penny. From Cot: w,w,w,w,w,s,s,w [5w,2s,w] ============================================================================== Newbie Areas ============================================================================== All directions from Cot: Abandoned Village - 6w, exit, 4w, 2n, w, s, w, enter, n, w Ashkenazy's hunting grounds - 5s, exit, s, 4w, s Cemetery - 5w, 2n Farmland - 6w, exit, 4w, 3n, 2e, n Glaverton Forest - 6w, exit, 4w, 2n, e, 3n, e, n, e, n, 5e, 2ne, nw, n Haunted Keep - 5s, exit, 11s, w North Forest path - 6n, exit, 9n, 9nw, w Pegasi - 6n, exit, 8n, 2e, n Pirate Ship - 5e, 4n, climb rope For a more comprehensive listing and descriptions of newbie areas, read chapter 5 of the Newbie Tome. ============================================================================== Further Helpfiles of Interest ============================================================================== help newbie The newbie command allows you to talk on the newbie channel. help set The set command allows you to customize several different features. help wimpy Wimpy allows you to automatically flee combat when your HP drop too low. help mon The monitor allows you to set an HP/SP monitor. help ncot - help nbolt - help npunch - help nkick - help nheal These are your newbie skills. help combatbrief This setting allows you to filter your combat messages. help score - help sc Information on your score tables. help int - help wis - help dex - help con - help str - help chr Information about your stats. help races Information on how to become one of the races that inhabit Darkwind. help guilds A list of existing guilds on Darkwind. Specific info can be obtained from the tome. help rules The rules for Darkwind. Read them, know them, live them. help pk Information on Darkwind's player killing system. ============================================================================== Addendum ============================================================================== Any extra info you feel needs to be added to this file? Use the idea command to suggest it. See help idea.

docs.title: Stage 1 of 8: Your First Minutes
docs.text: Stage 1 of 8: Your First Minutes ===================================================================== A short tutorial starts automatically for new characters and teaches looking, moving, gear, and safe combat. Darkflow shows it in a hover window. Type tutorial to see your current step and tutorial continue to continue in any client. Learn to look at everything (look <thing>), check your inventory, and read your score. If you ever get lost, ncot returns you to the Center of Town, and the Newbie Tome Dispenser there (pull lever, read tome) holds the town directions. Make the interface work for you before you roam. set list shows your saved options. Useful first choices are set autoexits on for named exits, set npcdetail on for NPC levels, and set itemdetail on for raw weapon and armour ratings. Use monitor bar for live HP/SP. If you use a screenreader, run set screenreader on to enable screenreader-friendly output. Read: help tutorial, help basics, help movement, help new, help set, help monitor, help screenreader Next: help stage2 Index: help guide # keywords: tutorial, first steps, settings, autoexits, itemdetail, npcdetail

docs.title: Stage 2 of 8: Gear Up and Learn to Fight (levels 1-5)
docs.text: Stage 2 of 8: Gear Up and Learn to Fight (levels 1-5) ===================================================================== Erga's newbie store (from the Center of Town: 4w, s) hands out free equipment fit for anyone under level 5; the donation room (5n, e) has castoffs from generous veterans. Wear and wield everything, then practice on the newbie farm. Death carries NO penalty at level 5 and under, so this is the time to take risks and learn kill, assess, and wimpy. Ask questions freely on the newbie channel -- everyone started here. Choose your corpse automation: set autogold on takes coins only, while set autoloot on takes coins and every gettable item, making autogold redundant and filling your inventory faster. set autokill on does not attack by itself; it only makes a manually entered bare kill choose the first visible NPC. Keep naming targets until you are comfortable. set wimpy 25 retreats below 25 percent HP when an escape is possible. set combatbrief-short on trims combat text; in busy groups, set combatbrief-self on keeps attacks by or on you, and set combatbrief-hit on hides misses and dodges. Read: help kill, help equipment, help wimpy, help combat, help communication, help set, help combatbrief Next: help stage3 Index: help guide # keywords: erga, newbie farm, free equipment, autoloot, autogold, autokill

docs.title: Stage 3 of 8: Choose Your Path
docs.text: Stage 3 of 8: Choose Your Path ===================================================================== Once the farm feels easy, pick a guild -- it defines your abilities for the climb ahead. Browse the roster, the playstyle archetypes, and which pairings work before committing. Level at the adventurers guild with advance; experience costs grow with each level, and your stats shape what your abilities can do. You can handle normal advancement from anywhere. remcost is a safe, read-only report of stat costs, available raises, caps, and experience needed. Use remadvance <stat> to raise one stat or remadvance level to buy every level you can currently afford. Guild advancement still happens at your guild hall with advance guild. Despite their names, the rem commands work before remort. Non-remort players may use set autolevel on to spend experience on levels automatically; leave it off when you want to bank experience for stat raises. Remort souls always level automatically. Read: help guilds, help archetypes, help combos, help roles, help leveling, help costs, help stats, help set Next: help stage4 Index: help guide # keywords: guild choice, advance, archetype, remcost, remadvance, autolevel

docs.title: Stage 4 of 8: See the World (levels 5-30)
docs.text: Stage 4 of 8: See the World (levels 5-30) ===================================================================== The world is far bigger than town. The areas command catalogs every region with level ranges; characters up to level 10 already know the newbie-area wayshards, so touch shard networks open fast travel as you explore. Pick up quests for structured goals and bonus experience. Above level 5 death starts to cost 10% of your experience on hand -- your corpse keeps your gear, the church will whisk you back, and other players can avenge you to restore what you lost. Read: help areas, help wayshards, help recall, help quests, help death, help avengement Next: help stage5 Index: help guide # keywords: explore, travel, fast travel

docs.title: Stage 5 of 8: Money and Craft
docs.text: Stage 5 of 8: Money and Craft ===================================================================== Coins pile up: open a bank account early -- auction bids and some purchases are backed by bank liens, and your balance is shared across every branch. rembank or rembank balance opens the account on first use and reports its balance, lien, and spendable amount. From anywhere that is not warded against teleportation, rembank deposit all banks every carried coin and rembank withdraw <amount> brings coins back. Use rembank lien to check reserved funds. Use rembank transfer <amount|all> from <alt> to pull funds from one of your registered alts into the current character. Balance and lien checks still work in warded rooms. Learn the player-driven economy: shops, the remote market, and the live auction channel. When you want a break from fighting, professions like fishing, mining, and smithing earn steadily and feed the market. Read: help economy, help bank, help market, help auction, help professions, help fishing Next: help stage6 Index: help guide # keywords: gold, coins, trading, rembank, remote banking

docs.title: Stage 6 of 8: Find Your People
docs.text: Stage 6 of 8: Find Your People ===================================================================== Darkwind is social. Channels connect the whole game; parties share the fight and the spoils; clans are player-run organizations with wars and coffers; kingdoms crown player rulers with their own nobility. Pick a divine patron when the gods start to notice you -- alignment and devotion open their own doors. Read: help communication, help party, help clans, help kingdoms, help patron, help deities, help discord Next: help stage7 Index: help guide # keywords: social, groups, friends

docs.title: Stage 7 of 8: Sharpen the Blade (levels 30-100)
docs.text: Stage 7 of 8: Sharpen the Blade (levels 30-100) ===================================================================== Mid-game is about power and polish: track your buffs and debuffs, hunt boss monsters and invasions, brave the eternal dungeon, duel in the arena, and chase achievements, daily rewards, and leaderboard rank. Unique weapons and armour -- one copy in the whole game -- are out there for the claiming. Read: help effects, help buffs, help bosses, help invasions, help eternal, help arena, help achievements, help daily, help uniques Next: help stage8 Index: help guide # keywords: midgame, bosses, dungeon

docs.title: Stage 8 of 8: Renown and Rebirth (level 100 and beyond)
docs.text: Stage 8 of 8: Renown and Rebirth (level 100 and beyond) ===================================================================== At level 100 your level becomes renown -- HERO, ADV, or VILN by your deeds. Level 150 makes you a LEGEND and unlocks a free additional multichar slot. New mythic multichar registration is disabled. At 250 the true endgame opens: remort, a rebirth that trades your level for permanent boon points and starts the climb again, stronger each cycle. Specialization and the metaphysician path round out a veteran's power. Read: help hero, help legend, help remort, help boons, help specialization, help meta, help multichars Index: help guide # keywords: endgame, rebirth, renown

docs.title: Dark Elves live deep underground where they worship forgotten gods of
docs.text: Dark Elves live deep underground where they worship forgotten gods of evil and chaos. They are adapted to living in darkness and rarely seeing the light of day. Dark Elves are quite agile and mentally superior to most races, but lack a certain degree of constitution.

docs.title: Draconians are an artificial race created ages ago when bizarre,
docs.text: Draconians are an artificial race created ages ago when bizarre, ancient magicks were used to adapt unhatched dragonets into humanoid form. They retain the vast intellect of their dragon ancestors and much of the strength as well, but their strange appearance has hampered their acceptance as a race until just recently. Physically, they are about the same height as humans, but there the similarity ends. They have scales of varying shades, as well as a tail and vestigial wings. Their eyes have slitted pupils, like a reptile or a cat. Draconians have a special breath attack they may use periodically using the breath command. Draconians cannot join the following guilds: Bard, Charlatan, Cleric of Mitra, Druid, Garou, Paladin.

docs.title: Dwarves are a noble race of squat demihumans who usually dwell
docs.text: Dwarves are a noble race of squat demihumans who usually dwell underground. They are great builders of tools and cities, and of weapons when the time comes for war. They love precious metals and gems, and some people call them greedy. Dwarves are a very hardy folk, and quite strong. They have to be in order to maintain their extensive mining operations. They do not like magic, and have not much aptitude for it either. Their fingers are short, like the rest of them, making feats of manual dexterity difficult. Dwarves are often bluntly honest, which does not endear them to many, and taciturn. Dwarves have a small amount on innate magic resistance. Dwarves cannot join the following guilds: Druid, Mage, Necromancer, Swashbuckler, Thief.

docs.title: Elves are an ancient race of highly intelligent demihumans who
docs.text: Elves are an ancient race of highly intelligent demihumans who typically make their homes in forests, far away from most other races. They are very fair colored, and seem quite fragile. However, they are very lithe and quick. They have fine features and pointed ears, which many humans tend to find quite compelling. Elves are usually cautious adventurers, preferring to become great scholars instead. They have amassed some of the greatest libraries in the world. Elves value their independence and tend to hold themselves aloof from other people's affairs. Elves are able to see in the dark. Elves cannot take the Psionicist class.

docs.title: Faeries are a race of woodland sprites, usually diminutive in stature.
docs.text: Faeries are a race of woodland sprites, usually diminutive in stature. This group encompasses brownies, dryads, atomies, sylphs and pixies, as well as sprites themselves. They are known to be extremely agile as well as friendly and typically good-looking, but due to their generally small size they are not very strong or sturdy. They have a reputation, deserved or not, for being pranksters, and tend to be a bit flighty at times. Faeries get a bonus with their spell points to work with. Faeries cannot join the following guilds: Fighter, Garou, Paladin.

docs.title: Gnomes are a diminutive race related to dwarves.  They like mining
docs.text: Gnomes are a diminutive race related to dwarves. They like mining for precious gems, their favorite being the diamond. They have large noses and large imaginations. They do not have the reputation for being dour like dwarves do. Perhaps this is because they do not live deep in the darkness of the earth like dwarves do, but rather in the sides of hills. Many live in houses as well. They are fond of strong drink, but have a strong sense of propriety as well, to head off excessive foolishness. This does not hamper their proclivity toward practical jokes, however. Gnomes cannot join the following guilds: Necromancer.

docs.title: Halflings are a race of short people (hence the name) much given to
docs.text: Halflings are a race of short people (hence the name) much given to the simpler pleasures in life, including good food, a warm bed, a window overlooking a pleasant little garden, a shady tree to lie under in the afternoon, and a full pipe after dinner. They do not often become adventurers, but those that do are quite good at it. They are not too strong, because of their small size, and their homebody nature means they tend to be not as wary. But halflings have truly incredible reflexes and are remarkably nimble and quick with their hands. Halflings are most interested in having fun in life, and they take this attitude with them wherever they go. Halflings are able to drink and eat more than the other races. Halflings cannot join the following guilds: Druid, Fighter.

docs.title: Humans are the most predominant race in the world of Darkwind.
docs.text: Humans are the most predominant race in the world of Darkwind. They are the not the strongest, quickest, smartest, or otherwise best race, but they are the most adaptable, and this is its own strength. That and sheer numbers ensure the continued survival of the human race. Human are generally liked, or at least tolerated, by other races, and in return generally tolerate all the others. This makes them more capable of ruling large dominions and becoming great heroes in many realms. Humans' main advantage is their versatility. They can be in any guild, and receive a small bonus to all experience earned. Humans may join any guild.

docs.title: The race of orcs is one of a short, fierce people, who have had to
docs.text: The race of orcs is one of a short, fierce people, who have had to struggle constantly to make their place in the world. They are almost universally disliked by others, even though their society is nearly as advanced as many other peoples'. They are a strong and sturdy race, which is one of the primary reasons they have survived. Orcs do slightly more damage in combat than the other races. Orcs cannot join the following guilds: Bard, Charlatan, Cleric of Mitra, Mage, Swashbuckler, Paladin.

docs.title: A troll is a member of a race of rubbery-skinned grayish-green
docs.text: A troll is a member of a race of rubbery-skinned grayish-green humanoid carnivores which most people find truly repugnant and fearsome. Trolls usually stand about eight feet tall, and have dirty claws and pointed teeth. Their arms and legs are long and ungainly- looking. They are very strong and can take alot of damage, but are dim-witted and lacking intelligence. In combat, they sometimes rip gobbets of flesh off their opponents to eat while continuing to fight. Trolls regenerate hit points and spell points faster than the other races. Trolls cannot join the following guilds: Bard, Charlatan, Cleric of Mitra, Mage, Necromancer, Paladin, Psionicist, Swashbuckler, Thief.

docs.title: Alchemy
docs.text: Alchemy Alchemists turn gathered herbs and saved reagents into potions, field supplies, and profession recipe outputs. The core alchemy room is in the profession building, 4e, n from Center of Town. Getting started: 1. Buy profession tools in the profession building. 2. Gather herbs with 'gather herbs' or buy/hire workers for materials. 3. Go to the alchemy room and use 'potions' to see potion names. 4. Use 'quickcraft <potion>' to brew a potion. Each potion has 4 strengths, matching the level requirement to quaff it. Level 1 potions can be quaffed by anyone. Level 2 potions require level 20. Level 3 potions require level 45. Level 4 potions require level 65. Level 1 potions can be made by anyone and can raise your skill to 100. Level 2 potions need Alchemy 60 and can raise your skill to 200. Level 3 potions need Alchemy 100 and can raise your skill to 500. Level 4 potions need Alchemy 200 and can raise your skill to 1000. Alchemy also uses recipe cards. Read a recipe card to see its saved material requirements, then use 'manufacture card' while carrying the card. Recipe cards may come from work orders and other profession rewards. Weapon oil is one such recipe output. Use 'oil <weapon>' while carrying crafted weapon oil to give the weapon a modest temporary hit bonus and make it less likely to break while the oil lasts. Better Alchemy skill improves the bonus and duration. Useful commands: help potions help herbalism help workorders professions crafting professions check potion str1 quickcraft str1 manufacture card

docs.title: Carpentry
docs.text: Carpentry Carpentry turns saved Forestry timber into planks, furniture, and construction framing. Work in the Kingdom Commons or inside any homestead. carpentry list carpentry mill [quality] <oak|ash|pine> [amount] carpentry craft [quality] <oak|ash|pine> <plan> Use 'reagents wood' first. One timber mills into two matching planks, and the species and quality must match through every step. Valid qualities are standard (omitted), fine, superior, and masterwork. For example: carpentry mill pine 1 carpentry craft pine stool carpentry mill fine oak 2 carpentry craft fine oak chair Furniture plans: Stool 2 planks 0 Carpentry skill Chair 3 planks 50 Carpentry skill Table 6 planks 100 Carpentry skill Bookshelf 8 planks 175 Carpentry skill Bed 10 planks 250 Carpentry skill Inside your own homestead: place <furniture> homestead furnishings remove furniture <id|type> You must own the homestead and carry the crafted furniture when placing it. Use a specific name such as 'place pine stool'. Placed furniture is saved with that room and returns after logout or reboot. Each room holds up to eight furnishings. 'homestead furnishings' shows stable ids such as furniture_1; remove by that id or by type. Removing one returns it to inventory or leaves it on the floor if it is too heavy to carry. The physical furniture plans are stool, chair, table, bookshelf, and bed. Decorations such as rugs, lanterns, paintings, blankets, and crockery are room descriptions rather than crafted objects; represent those with 'homestead look', 'homestead smell', and 'homestead action'. Remove an old descriptive placeholder when replacing it with a physical furnishing to avoid duplication. A Framing Bundle costs five matching planks. Deliver completed bundles to Brant in the Kingdom Commons: deliver framing bundles deliver <amount> framing bundles Post-hut upgrades consume both coins and delivered framing. Use 'homestead upgrades' for exact requirements and 'homestead status' for current delivery progress.

docs.title: Fishing
docs.text: Fishing Fishing is an art form. Not everyone can just grab a stick, some twine, and stick some glob of something on the end of a hook... NO! You must buy a real fishing pole, and some real bait. Once you've found the proper place to fish, bait your hook and cast your line. When something bites, fight it to the shore. Commands: bait hook - put a glob of bait on your hook fish - cast your line (opens the Fishing panel on the web client) fish stop - give up on the current session Fishing works in beach, swamp, lake, sea, river, and underwater terrain. Playing on the web client (play.darkwind.ai): Typing 'fish' opens the Fishing panel. Hold to charge your cast - more power reaches rarer fish, but they fight harder. When the bobber plunges, hook the fish fast, then hold and release to keep your line on the fish as it runs. Watch the tension meter: too tight and the line snaps, too slack and the fish wriggles free. Fill the catch bar to land it. Playing from other clients: The same 'bait hook' and 'fish' commands work anywhere; your cast resolves on its own after a few moments. What you can catch: Sixteen species swim Darkwind's waters, from the humble mud toad fish to legends like the Leviathan Fry - each with its own waters, moods, and fight. Rarer fish demand higher Fishing skill to even take your hook. Every fish can be eaten (better catches nourish more) or sold, and a clean fight lands a higher-quality catch. Getting started: 1. Buy a fishing pole and bait in the profession building, 4e, n from Center of Town. 2. Travel to beach, swamp, lake, sea, river, or underwater terrain. 3. Use 'bait hook', then 'fish'. 4. Land the fish! Your Fishing skill improves with successful catches. Higher skill attracts rarer fish, quickens their bite, steadies your line, and raises the quality of what you land. Successful catches can also recover profession reagents from the fish: fish bones, fish gills, bloody fins, and fish tails. Fishing materials can be used by recipe cards, guildcraft, and profession work orders. Fishing workers can also gather fish-part reagents for you over time. Enjoy! And, be careful about those fish lies. We all know the truth.

docs.title: Forestry
docs.text: Forestry Forestry gathers construction wood from marked timber stands in the Kingswood. The profession building is 4e, n from Center of Town. In its general store, use 'list' and 'buy forestry axe'. Carry the axe to a visible harvestable timber stand in the Kingswood and use: chop tree The stand is exhausted after a successful harvest and returns when its virtual room resets. Forestry skill increases yield and can produce fine, superior, or masterwork oak, ash, and pine timber. Timber is saved automatically rather than carried as a normal inventory object. reagents wood Show saved timber, planks, and framing bundles. carpentry list Show timber refinement and crafting plans. help carpentry Explain refinement, furniture, and construction supply. Carpentry works in the Kingdom Commons or inside any homestead. Preserve the harvested species and quality when milling and crafting. For example: carpentry mill pine 1 carpentry craft pine stool If 'reagents wood' shows Fine Pine Timber, use 'carpentry mill fine pine 1' and 'carpentry craft fine pine stool'. One timber becomes two matching planks.

docs.title: Guildcraft
docs.text: Guildcraft Guildcraft lets guild members consume saved profession materials for guild-themed preparations. These preparations support guild roleplay, guild command hooks, and material demand loops. Commands: guildcraft list guildcraft <guild> <use> Examples: guildcraft bard strings guildcraft ninja smoke bomb guildcraft mage scribing ink guildcraft cleric incense guildcraft ranger poultice guildcraft druid verdant bundle Each preparation consumes saved materials from your profession storage and sets a timed preparation on you. If you do not belong to the matching guild, the preparation is refused. Druids, Bards, Ninjas, Mages, Clerics, Paladins, and Rangers all have starter reagent uses. Use guildcraft list to see the current catalog. Getting started: 1. Use 'guildcraft list' to see the current guild material uses. 2. Use 'reagents search <item>' when you need source hints. 3. Gather the materials through professions, workers, monster reagents, fishing, or work-order rewards. 4. Use 'guildcraft <guild> <use>' while in the matching guild.

docs.title: Herbalism
docs.text: Herbalism Herbalism lets you gather herbs from terrain across the world. Herbs are saved as profession materials and are used by Alchemy, work orders, guildcraft preparations, and some recipe cards. Getting started: 1. Buy profession tools in the profession building, 4e, n from Center of Town. 2. Travel to a natural area. 3. Use 'gather herbs'. 4. Use 'reagents' or 'reagents herb' to review saved herbs. Terrain matters. Different herbs are associated with different outdoor areas, and some are more useful for certain potion or guildcraft recipes. Use 'reagents search <herb>' when you want hints about where something comes from, and 'professions gathering' for a command overview. Herbalism can also be worked indirectly. In the profession building, you can hire herbalism workers for a terrain target. Workers bring back materials over time and take their payment from your bank account. Useful commands: gather herbs reagents herb reagents search Rose Hip professions gathering professions check potion str1 help alchemy help workers Druids can use their silver sickle instead of a gardening spade.

docs.title: Syntax: homestead [return|status|survey|map|upgrades|furnishings|customize|help]
docs.text: Syntax: homestead [return|status|survey|map|upgrades|furnishings|customize|help] Homesteads are the foundation for future player-built homes, crafted rooms, and shared kingdom spaces. The kingdom commons is meant to be explored in character: speak aloud near the surveyor, clerk, and foreman, and they will answer what they understand. Current commands: homestead Travel to the kingdom commons, or return if already there. homestead return Return to the room remembered when you entered. homestead status Show your current homestead state. homestead survey Review what is currently available. homestead map Show the indoor floor plan and room connections. homestead upgrades Show larger home costs, build times, and room limits. homestead visit <player> Visit another player's public or invited plot. homestead public Let anyone visit your plot. homestead private Restrict visits to yourself and invited players. homestead invite <player> Invite a player to visit your private plot. homestead uninvite <player> Remove a plot invitation. Useful things to try in the commons: say I want land say how much does a plot cost say I accept the charter say take me to my plot say what should I build first read charter study map read ledger workorders workorder <number> A frontier charter costs 1,000,000 coins. The clerk draws from clear bank funds first, then coin on hand. The charter alone grants no land: walk out of the commons into the Kingdom Frontier -- open plains, the Charter Fields, the Kingswood, or the Greywall foothills -- and use 'homestead claim' standing on the exact spot you want. First come, first served; one plot to a name. Your claim appears as a real structure on the land that anyone passing can see, and it grows with each build tier. Roads, the commons, mine gates, bridges, and the Reedmurk cannot be claimed. The whole frontier is a safe zone. Choose with the future in mind: forest means timber, riverside means fishing, foothills sit near the mines. Visible profession nodes are scattered through suitable frontier terrain: mineral-streaked outcrops in the Greywall foothills, wild herb patches in the Kingswood and Reedmurk, harvestable timber stands in the Kingswood, and promising fishing positions beside rivers and lakes. Use the normal profession tools and commands: 'mine ore', 'gather herbs', 'chop tree', and fishing poles. Visible nodes provide an extra yield or quality bonus, then a successful harvest or catch exhausts the opportunity until the virtual room's normal reset restores it. Frontier terrain has its own weighted material tables: surface foothills favor practical copper, tin, iron, and lead, while each mine gate previews the deposits found deeper inside. The work-order board uses the same rotating contracts and rewards as the profession halls. Three working mines open through the eastern Greywall. Ironroot lies at the northern gate and favors iron and lead. Crownshaft meets the east road and favors silver and gold. Blackglass lies at the southern gate and carries rare mithril, platinum, and adamantite deposits. Mineable rooms contain a visible vein. A successful 'mine ore' exhausts that vein until the room resets. Brant explains starter work, but construction happens on your own plot: build camp marker 25,000 coins, about 1 minute build lean-to 75,000 coins, about 5 minutes build foundation 250,000 coins, about 15 minutes build hut 750,000 coins, about 45 minutes build status show the current project and its remaining build time Build timers are saved by the homestead daemon. They continue across logout, reboot, or crash because the completion time is stored with your plot. The finished hut is the first real home. It begins with one interior room and may contain no more than four indoor rooms total. 'enter hut' opens the main room with: - A hearth that speeds the owner's healing while resting inside. - A banded chest: 'store <item>', 'retrieve <item>', and 'chest' to list. Stored goods survive relog and reboot exactly as you left them, using the same preservation as saved login equipment - crafted and special items keep their qualities. The chest refuses uniques, cursed or broken goods, coins, and anything too fleeting to survive storage. Items left lying on the ground of a plot do NOT persist; use the chest. Expanding a home: build room Show current rooms, capacity, price, time, and openings. build room north Add a room north of the room where you are standing. build room south Add a room south of the current room. build room east Add a room east of the current room. build room west Add a room west of the current room. build room up Add a room one floor above the current room. build room down Add a room one floor below the current room. homestead map Draw every occupied floor and list room connections. Rooms are connected when their saved build timer completes. Construction creates the outgoing passage and its opposite together. Existing passages, occupied three-dimensional coordinates, active jobs, and the home's room limit block new work before payment. Room timers persist across logout and reboot. The homestead map draws floors from highest to lowest, and each room entry shows its saved (x,y,z) coordinate plus horizontal and vertical passages. Larger homes must be built in order: cabin, cottage, house, manor, keep, then castle. You must build every room allowed by the current home before starting the next upgrade. Existing rooms, links, custom descriptions, the hearth, and chest all carry forward into the larger structure. Use 'homestead upgrades' for exact prices, times, capacities, and Framing Bundle requirements. Mill Forestry timber and craft bundles with 'carpentry', then 'deliver framing bundles' to Brant in the commons. Delivered supplies persist with the plot and are consumed when the upgrade begins. Furnishing a home: help forestry reagents wood carpentry list carpentry mill [quality] <oak|ash|pine> [amount] carpentry craft [quality] <oak|ash|pine> <plan> place <furniture> homestead furnishings remove furniture <id|type> Buy a forestry axe in the profession building's general store, harvest marked Kingswood timber with 'chop tree', then mill it in the Kingdom Commons or any homestead. One timber becomes two matching planks; species and quality must match when milling and crafting. Plans are stool (2 planks/0 skill), chair (3/50), table (6/100), bookshelf (8/175), and bed (10/250). Only the owner can place or remove furniture. Each room holds up to eight crafted furnishings. Placed furniture is saved as part of that room and returns across logout and reboot. Use 'homestead furnishings' for stable ids when several pieces share a type. Physical plans currently cover the five items above; use custom looks, smells, and actions for descriptive decorations such as rugs, lanterns, blankets, paintings, and crockery. Once you are standing on your plot, use 'commons' or 'return to commons' to walk the survey road back. Shaping a room: homestead customize homestead short <room title> (alias: homestead title) homestead short reset homestead long <room description> (alias: homestead describe) homestead long reset homestead look add|edit <noun> = <description> homestead look remove <noun> homestead look list homestead smell add|edit <noun> = <description> homestead smell remove <noun> homestead smell list homestead action add|edit <command> = <response> homestead action remove <command> homestead action list These commands work while you are standing inside your own homestead. Text is bounded and saved by the homestead daemon. Adding an existing look, smell, or action name edits it in place. 'smell <noun>' and 'sniff <noun>' reveal saved smells; a single room smell also appears for a bare 'smell'. Custom actions return the saved response when a visitor types the exact saved phrase. They are descriptive data, not LPC scripts, and cannot replace movement, combat, communication, inventory, or administrative commands. Each room currently supports 20 looks, 12 smells, 12 actions, and eight crafted furnishings. The short description is the room heading. The long description is only the authored atmosphere and physical description; do not repeat exit directions, building instructions, storage commands, or other help text in it. The normal room display lists obvious exits separately. Use 'homestead map' for the full floor plan, 'look <noun>' for a saved custom look, and 'look chest' or 'look <furnishing>' for object-specific instructions. This keeps room prose compact while leaving commands discoverable from the objects and this help file.

docs.title: Profession Inlays
docs.text: Profession Inlays Profession-crafted gear can be improved after it is made by adding a saved shard as an inlay. Inlays are done in the profession building, 4e, n from Center of Town. Command: inlay <crafted item> with <shard> Example: inlay breastplate with mithril inlay robe with amber Inlaying consumes one saved shard from your reagent/material storage and adds a small stat or resistance bonus to a profession-crafted item. Each item can only hold one profession inlay. The item must be profession-crafted gear. Ordinary loot, quest gear, and items that already have a profession inlay cannot be inlaid again. Shards can come from profession work orders and other profession systems. Use 'reagents' to check the shards you have saved, and 'reagents search <shard>' to look for source hints. Metal, leather, and gem shards grant different bonuses. Smithing, leatherworking, and tailoring help files list the common material and shard bonus themes used by profession-crafted gear. Related help: help professions help workorders help smithing help leatherworking help tailoring

docs.title: Leatherworking
docs.text: Leatherworking Leatherworking allows you to create armour from various hides you've skinned from various monsters around the world. The hides are processed into leathers, which you then use to make the armour. It takes 5 hides to make 1 leather. Getting started: 1. Buy profession tools in the profession building, 4e, n from Center of Town. 2. Use 'skin corpse' after killing a skinnable creature, or hire a skinning worker. 3. Convert hides into leathers in the leatherworking room. 4. Use 'quickcraft <type> <slot> <main leather> <secondary>'. Druids can use their silver sickle instead of a skinning knife. Leatherworkers can make two types of armour - hide and studded. They can make boots, chests, legs, and helmets of either kind. The four main leather types are cow, bear, reptile, and dragon. All crafted cow armour starts with no level restriction, bear starts at level 20, reptile at 45, and dragon at level 65. Cow armour can be made by anyone, but your skill will max at 100 crafting them. Bear armour needs a skill of 60, and will max at 200. Reptile armour requires a skill of 100, and will max at 500. Dragon armour needs a skill of 200 to craft, and will max at 1000. When making hide armour, you can add other leathers for extra bindings to strengthen the armour. When making studded armour, you can add metal studs to the armour to strengthen the armour. The added bindings and studs add extra effects to the armour. All armour uses 6 Cow Leather as the base, even if you are making a piece of Dragon Leather armour. Bear, Reptile and Dragon armour each require 6 leathers of their type. If you are adding bindings or studs, each piece uses 4 leathers/studs. When making cow hide, your secondary has to be none, as cow hide cannot be enhanced with bindings. When making cow studded armour, the secondary metal can only be copper. Neither the cow hide nor cow studded armour will have extra enhancements however. All Bear, Reptile and Dragon armours have an innate of bonus of 1 hp. Bear armours will have special enhancements of 1. Reptile armours will have special enhancements of 3. Dragon armours will have special enhancements of 5. The enhancements are based off the bindings or studs of the armour, or the base hide if you don't add a binding to hide. In the leatherworking room in the profession building, you can convert hides into leathers. It takes 5 hides to make 1 leather, regardless of the type of hide. Leatherworking also supports utility recipe outputs such as crafted bags and repair kits. Recipe cards can be read, then used with 'manufacture card' while the card is in your inventory. Leather goods and materials may also be requested by profession work orders. Crafted profession gear can be improved with 'inlay <crafted item> with <shard>' in the profession building. Leatherworking inlays use saved shards from your profession materials: Amber Shard - Poison Resist Onyx Shard - Constitution Beryl Shard - Strength Pearl Shard - Charisma Bloodstone Shard - Disease Resist Sapphire Shard - Dexterity Garnet Shard - Wisdom Sunstone Shard - Fire Resist Jade Shard - Intelligence Topaz Shard - Lightning Resist Moonstone Shard - Cold Resist The leather and metal lists above describe legacy quickcraft secondary materials. The inlay command uses shards; see 'help inlays' for the shared inlay syntax.
