docs.title: DarkWind Professions
docs.text: DarkWind Professions DarkWind has eleven professions. Herbalism, Mining, Skinning, Fishing, and Forestry gather resources from the world. Alchemy, Leatherworking, Smithing, Tailoring, Cybernetics, and Carpentry turn saved materials, reagents, and equipment into useful outputs. Refining is a profession service. Where to go: The profession building is 4e, n from Center of Town. It contains tools, craft rooms, workers, the work order board, and profession services. Getting started: 1. Go to the profession building and buy the tools you need. 2. Use 'professions guide' for a practical first route. 3. Gather materials with 'gather herbs', 'mine ore', 'skin corpse', 'bait hook', 'fish', and 'chop tree'. 4. Check saved materials with 'reagents' and source hints with 'reagents search <item>'. 5. Use 'professions craftable' or 'professions check ...' before crafting so you know what you are missing. Herbalism gathers herbs for potions, guildcraft, work orders, and recipe cards. Mining gathers ore for bars, smithing, work orders, and some guild preparations. Skinning gathers hides that become leather for armor, bags, recipes, and guild preparations. Fishing catches food and fish-part reagents used by recipes, guildcraft, and orders. Forestry uses a forestry axe at marked Kingswood stands to save oak, ash, and pine timber in standard through masterwork quality. Alchemy creates potions and recipe-card outputs. Leatherworking creates hide and studded armor, converts hides to leather, and supports crafted bags and utility recipes. Smithing creates metal armor and bars. Tailoring creates padded armor and light clothing. Refining breaks old equipment back into saved profession materials. Use 'set autorefine on' to apply the same refining rules automatically to equipment from NPCs you kill. Autorefine is mutually exclusive with autosell. Carpentry works in the Kingdom Commons or inside a homestead. It mills timber into matching planks, crafts persistent placeable furniture, and makes Framing Bundles required for every home upgrade after the hut. Species and quality must match through timber, planks, and the finished piece. Inside your own home, use 'place <furniture>', 'homestead furnishings', and 'remove furniture <id|type>'. Rooms hold eight persistent furnishings. Use 'carpentry list', 'reagents wood', 'help forestry', and 'help carpentry' for the complete workflow and plan skill requirements. Useful commands: professions professions guide professions gathering professions crafting professions craftable professions check <type> <target> reagents reagents search <item> workorders guildcraft list Work orders are posted in the profession building. They ask for saved materials or crafted goods and reward coins, experience, profession practice, shards, or recipe cards. See 'help workorders'. Profession-crafted gear can be improved with saved shards using 'inlay <crafted item> with <shard>'. See 'help inlays'. Guild members can use 'guildcraft' to spend saved profession materials on guild-themed preparations. See 'help guildcraft'. Workers can be hired in the profession building for herbalism, mining, skinning, fishing, and reagent scavenging. See 'help workers'. Skillups are determined by your skill and the tier of what you make. Gathering professions always have a chance to improve, though the chance gets lower at higher skill. Gathering skill also improves yield. When manufacturing, lower-tier items stop giving skill once you outgrow them, until you reach final-tier crafting. Note: Druids can use their silver sickle as a gardening spade, mining pick, and skinning knife. Garou in wolf form and dragons in dragon form do not need those tools.

docs.title: Refining
docs.text: Refining Refining allows you to break down equipment to base materials. What you receive after refining will depend on the material the equipment is composed of. If the equipment isn't made of cloth, metals, or leathers, it will not be refined. If you 'refine verbose' while in the refinery, it will tell you the item name as well what was recovered. If you simply type 'refine' it will just list what was recovered. You may also use 'set autorefine on' to automatically refine eligible equipment from NPCs you kill. Automatic and manual refining use the same material rules and yields. Autorefine is permanent and runs before autoloot, so leave it off when you want to inspect equipment drops first. Autorefine skips the same magical, unique, limited, customized, scripted, and otherwise protected items that autosell refuses to sell; those stay in the corpse for you to inspect or loot normally. Autorefine and autosell cannot be enabled at the same time; enabling either one disables the other. Autorefine does not require a corpse burner. The refinery is in the profession building, 4e, n from Center of Town. Refining is a good way to turn unused equipment into saved profession materials for crafting, work orders, recipe cards, and guildcraft. Most equipment that contains metal will break down to their base metals. Leather equipment will always break down into Cow Leather. Cloth equipment will always break down into Cotton Bolt(s). There is always material loss while refining, so do not be surprised by that fact. If you identify an object (using an identify scroll for example), you will see if the object refines into anything, and what the result will be.

docs.title: Smithing
docs.text: Smithing Smithing allows you to create armour from various metals you've mined from across the world. The ore is processed into bars, and the bars are shaped into the objects you're creating. Getting started: 1. Buy profession tools in the profession building, 4e, n from Center of Town. 2. Use 'mine ore' in suitable terrain, or hire a mining worker. 3. Convert ore into bars in the smithing room. 4. Use 'quickcraft <type> <slot> <main bar> <secondary>'. Druids can use their silver sickle instead of a mining pick. In the smithing room in the profession building, you can convert ore into bars. It takes 5 ore to make 1 bar. Bronze Bars take 4 Copper Ores and 1 Tin Ore. Steel Bars require 4 Iron Ores and 1 Mithril Ore. Smiths can make banded, chain, plate and scale armour. They can make boots, chestplates, helmets and legplates of each type. Bronze armours don't have a level restrictions. Iron Armours have a level restriction of level 20. Steel Armours have a level restriction of level 45. Adamantite Armours have a level restriction of level 65. All armours require 6 Bars of their type to craft, plus 4 Bars for any secondary metal you add to the armours. Bronze armour can be made by anyone, but your skill will max at 100 crafting them. Iron armour needs a skill of 60, and will max at 200. Steel armour requires a skill of 100, and will max at 500. Adamantite armour needs a skill of 200 to craft, and will max at 1000. All Iron, Steel, and Adamantite armours have an innate bonus of 1 hp. Iron armours will have special enhancements of 1. Steel armours will have special enhancements of 3. Adamantite armours will have special enhancements of 5. The enhancements are based on the secondary metal, or the base metal if you do not add any secondary metal. Crafted profession gear can also be improved later with 'inlay <crafted item> with <shard>' in the profession building. This is separate from the secondary metal used during smithing. Adamantite - Strength Mithril - Wisdom Bronze - Fire Resistance Platinum - Intelligence Copper - Disease Resistance Silver - Dexterity Gold - Charisma Steel - Constitution Iron - Poison Resistance Tin - Lightning Resistance Lead - Cold Resistance

docs.title: Tailoring
docs.text: Tailoring Tailors can make padded armour and light clothes. Tailors convert piles of cloth found among the corpses of dead monsters into bolts of cloth. The bolts can then be made into armour or clothing in the tailoring room of the profession building, 4e, n from Center of Town. Getting started: 1. Save cloth reagents by picking them up and saving them, or by using 'reagents search <cloth>' to find likely sources. 2. Convert cloth piles into bolts in the tailoring room. 3. Use 'quickcraft <type> <slot> <shard>' for padded armour. Cotton armour uses 'none' for the shard. 4. Use 'quickcraft clothes <type> <slot>' for light clothing. Converting Cotton Bolt: 6 x Piles of cotton Silk Bolt: 4 x Piles of pure silk 1 x Velvet Larz Emberweave Bolt: 4 x Piles of dark fibre 1 x Dinkweed Lunar Cloth Bolt: 4 x Piles of lunar cloth 1 x Star Flower Sun Cloth Bolt: 4 x Piles of sun cloth 1 x Sun Flower Mage Fibre Bolt: 4 x Piles of mage fibre 1 x Mithril Bar Tailors can make 6 kinds of padded armour - boots, breeches, cloaks, doublets, hoods and robes. The tailors can use any of the 6 types of bolts to make the armour. Cotton armours doesn't have a level restriction. Silk armour has a level restriction of level 20. Emberweave, Lunar Cloth, and Sun Cloth armours have a level restriction of level 45. Mage Fibre has a level restriction of level 65. All armours with a level restriction have an innate bonus of 1 sp. Cotton armour can be made by anyone, but your skill will max at 100 crafting them. Silk armour needs a skill of 60, and will max at 200. Emberweave, Lunar Cloth, and Sun Cloth require a skill of 100, and will max at 500. Mage Fibre needs a skill of 200 to craft, and will max at 1000. All of the crafted armour take 6 Bolts to craft. Those with a level restriction also need 1 Shard from the special reagents. The shards infuse the armours with special benefits. Silk armours will have an increase of 1, while Emberweave, Lunar Cloth, and Sun Cloth will have an increase of 3, and Mage Fibre will have an increase of 5. Cotton armour is the starter padded armour path and does not take a shard during quickcraft. If you want a shard bonus on cotton gear, craft it with 'none' first and then use the inlay system. Tailors can also make simple clothing from the same bolt types. Clothing is light, wearable, and made for style rather than protection. It does not use shards and takes 2 Bolts to craft. Clothing slots are boots, cloak, gloves, hat, pants, robe, and shirt. Quickcraft examples: quickcraft cotton cloak none quickcraft silk robe amber quickcraft clothes silk cloak Tailored goods may also appear in profession work orders. Crafted profession gear can be improved with 'inlay <crafted item> with <shard>' in the profession building. Amber Shard - Poison Resist Onyx Shard - Constitution Beryl Shard - Strength Pearl Shard - Charisma Bloodstone Shard - Disease Resist Sapphire Shard - Dexterity Garnet Shard - Wisdom Sunstone Shard - Fire Resist Jade Shard - Intelligence Topaz Shard - Lightning Resist Moonstone Shard - Cold Resist Piles of cotton: Can be gotten randomly from bears, deer, dogs, goats and pigs. Piles of pure silk: Can be gotten randomly from gypsies, kobolds and spiders. Piles of dark fibre: Can be gotten randomly from gnomes, goblins, lizardmen and spiders. Piles of lunar cloth: Can be gotten randomly from elves, giants, humans and trolls. Piles of sun cloth: Can be gotten randomly from dwarves, faeries, gnolls, halflings and yetis. Piles of mage fibre: Can be gotten randomly from elementals, faeries, genies, orcs and spiders.

docs.title: DarkWind Profession Workers
docs.text: DarkWind Profession Workers Workers allow players to concentrate on their adventures while still bringing in materials to work on later. In the profession building, 4e, n from Center of Town, you can 'hire' or 'fire' workers, as well as type 'workers' for a list of your workers. Syntax: hire <profession> <target> <amount> <repeat?> fire <profession> <#> workers Worker professions: herbalism - hires a worker for herb terrain mining - hires a worker for ore terrain skinning - hires a worker for hides by creature race fishing - hires a worker for fish-part reagents by fishing terrain reagent - hires a scavenger for saved reagents by creature race The workers cost between 1000 and 5000 coins. The more you pay, the more materials they're likely to bring back. It's no guarantee however, and there's always the chance they'll pocket some and just claim that's all there was to be found. If you hire them to repeat the job, they'll go back out over and over as long as you have the funds to pay them, unless it's close to reboot time, then they'll take a break. They will repeat every 15 minutes. They will take funds directly from your bank account, so you will have to make sure you can fund them as long as you want them to go out. If you want them to stop working for you, you can fire them. You can type 'workers' to get a list of your workers, then fire the # of worker you wish to fire. The # of the worker will increment over the course of the boot, and is not an indication of your personal worker count. Currently, every player can get 1 worker for each profession. At HERO you can hire another worker, then another at LEGEND, and finally one more at the maximum level (250). You also get 1 worker when you reach 500 in the profession, then 1 more when you reach 1000. That is a max of 6 workers per profession. Reagent scavengers use your level-based worker count because they are not tied to a single profession skill. You can't double up the same worker target for the same profession. If you're a ghost, linkdead, or relogged while your worker was out, you will not receive any materials.

docs.title: Profession Work Orders
docs.text: Profession Work Orders Profession work orders are posted in the profession building, 4e, n from Center of Town. The board rotates every DarkWind day with requests for saved materials and crafted items. Commands: workorders workorder <#> workorder complete <#> Work orders may ask for herbs, ores, bars, skins, leathers, reagents, potions, bags, tailored clothing, bandages, or other profession-crafted goods. Saved-material orders pull directly from your reagent/material storage. Crafted-item orders require the item in your inventory and consume it when completed. Rewards include coins, experience, profession practice, and sometimes bonus shards or recipe cards. Some rare utility recipes, such as masterwork polish, are available through work orders. Profession-crafted gear can also be improved in the profession building: inlay <crafted item> with <shard> Inlaying consumes one saved shard and adds a small stat or resistance bonus to a profession-crafted item. Each item can only hold one inlay. See 'help inlays' for more detail. Getting started: 1. Go to the profession building, 4e, n from Center of Town. 2. Use 'workorders' at the board. 3. Use 'workorder <#>' to inspect the material or item needed. 4. Gather, craft, or manufacture the requested turn-in. 5. Use 'workorder complete <#>' to claim the reward.

docs.title: Purging
docs.text: Purging ----------------------------- There is no way for you to suicide or purge your own character. To do so requires the help of an Immortal, and is not something taken lightly. No request will be considered by the Immortals unless it is for a very, very good reason or some unforseeable situation. Mythic alts however can purge their characters at Max. Type 'suicide' to read the syntax at Max if you're a mythic alt.

+---------------------------------------------------------------------+ MINI QUEST COMMANDS +---------------------------------------------------------------------+ There are various commands that you'll need when doing quests: * "engage waysteward" Quest givers stand beside area wayshards. A bright yellow [?] means new work is available and [!] means completed work can be turned in. Engage them to review details, accept work, report progress, or collect rewards. * "myquests" This command lists all quests that you have accepted. New quests are accepted from local waystewards. * "qactive [#]" This command is kept for compatibility. Active quests are no longer required. * "qstatus" This gives you an at a glance status of your accepted unfinished quests. * "escort" If one of your accepted quests has an escort objective, and the mob does not automatically begin his journey you use this command to begin the escort of the target mob. +---------------------------------------------------------------------+ +---------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: QUEST COMMANDS
docs.text: =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= QUEST COMMANDS =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= The following commands and interactions manage quests: engage waysteward Reviews local quests at an area's wayshard or entrance. A bright yellow [?] means new work is available; [!] means a completed quest can be turned in. The dialogue shows suggested levels, objectives, prerequisites, and rewards before you accept. myquests Lists all quests you have accepted and their current status. qstatus Shows detailed progress for accepted unfinished quests. Use qstatus <number> with numbers from myquests. qactive <number> Compatibility command. All accepted quests track automatically. escort Begins an escort objective when its NPC does not start automatically. =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= See also: help quests, help quests objectives =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=

docs.title: QUEST OBJECTIVES
docs.text: =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= QUEST OBJECTIVES =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= Each quest has one or more objectives that must be completed. There are several types of objectives you may encounter: Kill Defeat a specific creature, or a number of creatures. Progress is tracked automatically as you fight once you have accepted the quest. Example: "Slay 3 wolves in the Endrael Forest" Retrieve Find and collect one or more items and deliver them to a quest master NPC. When you give the item to the NPC, your progress is updated. Example: "Collect 5 alligator teeth from the Hyndor swamp" Rescue Locate a captured or stranded NPC and free them. When you find the NPC, use the appropriate command (such as rescue or free) to complete the objective. Example: "Find and rescue the priest from the mines" Escort Guide an NPC safely from one location to another. Use the escort command to start the journey. The NPC will move on their own - stay in the same room and protect them from enemies. If the NPC dies or you wander too far away, the objective resets and you will need to try again. Example: "Escort the elf child safely through the forest" Tracking Progress: Use qstatus at any time to see how many objectives you have completed and how much remains across your accepted quests. When all objectives for a quest are finished, the quest completes automatically and you receive your rewards. =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= See also: help quests, help quests commands, help quests rewards =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=

docs.title: THE QUEST SYSTEM
docs.text: =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= THE QUEST SYSTEM =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= DarkWind features a quest system that gives you objectives to complete for experience and gold rewards. Quests range from simple tasks like slaying a few monsters to multi-step adventures involving item retrieval, rescues, and escorts. Getting Started: 1. Find the waysteward beside an area's wayshard or entrance. 2. A bright yellow [?] means the steward has work available. 3. Use engage waysteward to review and accept a quest. 4. Complete its objectives; a bright yellow [!] then appears. 5. Engage the same area's waysteward to turn in the quest and collect rewards. Key Concepts: You may accept multiple quests. All accepted quests track progress automatically, so you do not need to choose an active quest. Each quest has one or more objectives. These tell you what to do - kill certain creatures, find specific items, rescue someone, or escort an NPC to safety. Use qstatus to check your progress. =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= See also: help quests commands, help quests objectives, help quests rewards =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=

docs.title: QUEST REWARDS
docs.text: =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= QUEST REWARDS =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= When you complete all objectives for a quest, return to the quest's area waysteward and turn it in. Rewards are granted when the waysteward records the completion. Reward Types: Experience - Bonus experience points added directly to your total. The amount is shown by the waysteward before acceptance. Gold - Coins deposited into your inventory. The amount is shown in the waysteward's quest dialogue. Quest Points - Permanent quest progress points used by the wider level progression system. The amount is shown before acceptance. Items - Some quests grant a special object on first completion. It is placed in your inventory. If you cannot carry it, it is placed at your feet instead. Difficulty and Rewards: Higher-level quests with tougher objectives tend to offer better rewards. The waysteward dialogue shows the suggested level range relative to your level: |gKB green - Well below your level. Easy, smaller rewards. GREEN - At or near your level. Moderate challenge. YELLOW - Slightly above your level. Good rewards. RED - Significantly above your level. Great rewards, but dangerous. Completion: Non-repeatable quests can only be completed once. Repeatable quests become available again after their cooldown and grant scaled experience and gold, but no additional quest points or item rewards. Daily quests become available again at midnight UTC (00:00). Use myquests to review your quest history. =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= See also: help quests, help quests objectives =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=

docs.title: The Arctic Elves are a subrace of the elves that have adapted to living in
docs.text: The Arctic Elves are a subrace of the elves that have adapted to living in the far north of Hyperborea. Like all elves, they are bright and agile, but suffer from somewhat fragile bodies. Arctic elves are often at odds with the humans of northern Hyperborea, constantly fighting over territory and ancient artifacts of power in order to expand their evil society. This race cannot join the following guilds: Paladin, Cleric of Mitra. This race has an increase to DEX, INT, and WIS. This race has a decrease to CON. This race has a tendency to align more with evil. This race is more susceptible to FIRE damage. This race is Hyperborean in nature. This race speaks Common, Northern, and Elvish. This race is available in the Hyperborean Race Hall.

docs.title: The Barbarians are an offshoot of modern human society that settled south
docs.text: The Barbarians are an offshoot of modern human society that settled south of Darkwind City in a settlement known as Canith. Their rugged lifestyle tends towards the development of stronger, healthier bodies than most humans. Canith society values order, and pursuit of the common good. Barbarians are generally friendly to strangers and always eager to learn about exotic people and places. This race cannot join the following guilds: Necro, Priest, Swashbuckler. This race has an increase to EXP, CHR, STR, and CON. This race has a tendency to align more with goodness. This race is available in the Darkwind City Race Hall.

docs.title: The humans that live around Darkwind City are collectively known as
docs.text: The humans that live around Darkwind City are collectively known as Darkwinders. Darkwinders are about average among the civilized races in terms of physical and mental powers, but are well accepted by most other cultures due to the importance of the city in world affairs. Darkwinders are outgoing and adventurous, always seeking out new experiences. They are also expert traders and negotiators. Being adventurous in nature, Darkwinder souls are more inclined to take on other forms. Thus they do not suffer from reincarnating into other races. This race can join any guild. This race has an increase to CHR and EXP. Available in Darkwind City Race Hall. Players begin as this race.

docs.title: The Desert Dwarves live in a small settlement in the deserts of Souvrael.
docs.text: The Desert Dwarves live in a small settlement in the deserts of Souvrael. The Dwarves live in a peaceful, just society, generally unaffected by outside influences. Physically, they are a short, hardy race. In addition to an innate resistance to magic and psionics, they tend to be quite healthy and strong, but suffer somewhat from a stubbiness in their limbs. Despite their strength, their small size often also creates difficulties in wielding larger weapons. This race cannot join the following guilds: Ninja, Thief, Garou, Necro. This race has an increase to STR, CON, and WIS. This race has a decrease to DEX. This race is smaller than average. This race had a tendency to align more with goodness. This race is less susceptible to MAGIC and PSIONIC damage. This race can see in the dark. This race is Souvraeli in nature. This race can drink more than average. This race speaks Common, Souvraeli, and Dwarvish. This race is available in the Souvraeli Race Hall.

docs.title: The Desert Nomads are the wanderers of Souvrael. They are a deeply religious
docs.text: The Desert Nomads are the wanderers of Souvrael. They are a deeply religious people who follow the teachings of their prophet. The are quick learners who have adapted to living in the open desert. Desert Nomads are known for their great hospitality, despite the harshness of their habitat. This race can join any guild. This race has an increase to EXP, CHR, and CON. This race has a tendency to align more with goodness. This race is Souvraeli in nature. This race is more susceptible to WATER damage and less susceptible to FIRE damage. This race speaks Common and Souvraeli. This race is available in the Souvraeli Race Hall.

docs.title: Faeries are a race of woodland sprites, usually diminutive in stature.
docs.text: Faeries are a race of woodland sprites, usually diminutive in stature. This group encompasses brownies, dryads, atomies, sylphs and pixies, as well as sprites themselves. They are known to be extremely agile as well as friendly and typically good-looking, but due to their generally small size they are not very strong or sturdy. They have a reputation, deserved or not, for being pranksters, and tend to be a bit flighty at times. Faeries cannot join the following guilds: Fighter, Garou, Morpher. This race has an increase to WIS. This race is smaller than average. This race is less susceptible to PSIONIC damage. This race is winged and can fly. This race speaks Common and Faerie. This race is available in the Wayfarian Race Hall.

docs.title: Glavians are humans that hail from the mountain kingdom of Glavia. Glavians
docs.text: Glavians are humans that hail from the mountain kingdom of Glavia. Glavians are a generally good-aligned people used to opposing demonic forces. Their society is otherwise peaceful and pastoral. Glavians are an inoffensive, likeable lot, with an open mind to new experiences. This race cannot join the following guilds: Necro This race has an increase to EXP and CHR. This race speaks Common. This race is available in the Darkwind City Race Hall.

docs.title: Halflings are a race of short people (hence the name) much given to
docs.text: Halflings are a race of short people (hence the name) much given to the simpler pleasures in life, including good food, a warm bed, a window overlooking a pleasant little garden, a shady tree to lie under in the afternoon, and a full pipe after dinner. They do not often become adventurers, but those that do are quite good at it. They are not too strong, because of their small size, and their homebody nature means they tend to be not as wary. But halflings have truly incredible reflexes and are remarkably nimble and quick with their hands. Halflings are most interested in having fun in life, and they take this attitude with them wherever they go. This race can join all guilds. This race has an increase to DEX and CHR. This race has an decrease to WIS and STR. This race is smaller than average. This race can eat and drink more than average. This race speaks Common. This race is available in the Darkwind City Race Hall.

docs.title: The elven kingdom south of Darkwind City is the home of the High Elves. High
docs.text: The elven kingdom south of Darkwind City is the home of the High Elves. High Elf culture as a whole tends towards goodness and lawfulness in the context of harmony with nature. High Elves have keen senses and are generally superior mentally to most civilized races. Physically however, they can be somewhat fragile and lack the robustness of other races. This race cannot join the following guilds: Thief, Charlatan, Swashbuckler. This race has an increase to DEX, INT, WIS, and CHR. This race has a decrease to CON. This race has a tendency to align with good. This race is less susceptible to LIGHT damage. This race can see in the dark. This race can speak Common and Elvish. This race is available in the Darkwind City Race Hall.

docs.title: Hyperborean gnomes are a race of small humanoids that inhabit the more
docs.text: Hyperborean gnomes are a race of small humanoids that inhabit the more habitable rural areas of Hyperborea. They are bright and nimble, with a natural resistance to variations in the environment. They have a slight tendency to work towards the causes of good, if only because they are subject to attack by the forces of evil. Like all gnomes, they are quite small compared to other races, and have difficulty managing larger weapons. This race cannot join the following guilds: Necro, Fighter. This race has an increase to DEX, WIS, and INT. This race is smaller than average. This race has the tendency to align towards goodness. This race is less susceptible to FIRE, ACID, and POISON damage. This race is Hyperborean in nature. This race can drink more than average. This race can speak Common, Northern, and Gnomish. This race is available in the Hyperborean Race Hall.

docs.title: Ice Gnolls are an evil warrior race that appears to be a cross of some
docs.text: Ice Gnolls are an evil warrior race that appears to be a cross of some humanoid and a hyena. They are physically powerful but are lacking somewhat in intellect. Ice gnolls live to kill and eat; who their victims are is largely irrelevant. This race cannot join the following guilds: Bard, Cleric of Mitra, Mage, Morpher, Paladin, Psionicist, Swashbuckler, Thief. This race has an increase to STR, CON, and DEX. This race has a decrease to CHR and INT. This race has a tendency to align with evil. This race is Hyperborean in nature. This race can eat more than average. This race speaks Common. This race is available in the Hyperborean Race Hall.

docs.title: Ice Ogres are large brutish humanoids that live in the cold wastes of
docs.text: Ice Ogres are large brutish humanoids that live in the cold wastes of Hyperborea. Large numbers of them are regularly hired as mercenaries by the giants to wage war against more civilized races. They are immensely strong and rugged, but dimwitted and clumsy as well. They have no real culture to speak of except a penchant for violence. While not quite giant sized, ice ogres are large enough that they can wield large weapons much more easily than most other races. This race cannot join the following guilds: Bard, Charlatan, Cleric of Mitra, Mage, Morpher, Necro, Ninja, Paladin, Psionicist, Swashbuckler, Thief. This race has an increase to STR and CON. This race has a decrease to DEX, INT, WIS, and CHR. This race is larger than average. This race has a tendency to align with evil. This race is more susceptible to PSIONIC damage and less susceptible to DISEASE damage. This race is Hyperborean in nature. This race can eat and drink more than average. This race speaks Common. This race is available in the Hyperborean Race Hall.

docs.title: Northmen are humans who settled in the frigid north. Northmen are widespread
docs.text: Northmen are humans who settled in the frigid north. Northmen are widespread throughout Hyperborea, although most live in the city of Grimsfjord. Northmen are expert traders and hagglers, due to the need to trade with the southern cities for various goods not produced in Hyperborea. This race can join any guild. This race has an increase to EXP and CHR. This race is Hyperborean in nature. This race speaks Common and Northern. This race is available in the Hyperborean Race Hall.

docs.title: The pixies are a race of small mischievous little fae. These smart little
docs.text: The pixies are a race of small mischievous little fae. These smart little critters excel at finding ways to scare and trick their unsuspecting victims. They have beautiful silk-like wings that enable them to explore the skies and are naturally protected from the magical abilities of those who would hunt them. This sadistic little fae folk cares little about morality. This race cannot join the following guilds: Fighter, Garou, Necro, Swashbuckler, and Thief This race has an increase to INT. This race is smaller than average. This race has a tendency to align with evil. This race is less susceptible to MAGICAL damage. This race is winged and can fly. This race speaks Common, Talamh, and Faerie. This race is available in the Wayfarian Race Hall.

docs.title: There are many civilized and not so civilized races available on DarkWind.
docs.text: There are many civilized and not so civilized races available on DarkWind. Players can learn about and become many of these races at the Hall of Races in Darkwind City. Race may be changed without penalty through level 5. After level 5, changing race clears all the experience you have on hand, unless your race grants free race changes or you are at the maximum player level. After changing race, you must wait one hour before reincarnating again. As you explore the lands, you may come across other Halls of Races where you may learn about and become other races. The following races are available at the Darkwind Hall of Races: Darkwinder Glavian Barbarian Faerie Halfling High elf Rift duergar Shel-zaranite Silver Elf Stone dwarf Uruk The following races are available at the Hyperborea Hall of Races: Northman Arctic elf Hyperborean gnome Ice ogre Ice gnoll The following races are available at the Souvrael Hall of Races: Souvraeli Desert nomad Desert dwarf The following races are available at the Talamh Darag Hall of Races: Wayfarian pixie Sidhe Each race has a unique set of abilities and penalties due to their physical and mental characteristics, as well as cultural aspects of their societies, some of which will be explained in more detail: STATS ----- Racial modifications to stats are made to the base stat, before other modifications such as from magical equipment. Racial modifications are also based on a percentage of the base stat. Thus even with an extremely strong race, if you never raise your strength, your strength will be only one. Because stats are always whole numbers, sometimes when you advance a stat you have a penalty in, you may not see the effect of that stat raise. Conversely, if you raise a stat you have a bonus in, you may see a rise of two points instead of one. ALIGNMENT --------- Adventurers are made, not born. By the time they choose the adventuring life, adventurers have a lot of silly notions ingrained into their minds, especially opinions about the role of alignment in society. Having been indoctrinated from an early age, they will always have a tendency towards the predominant attitudes of their culture. If you have a tendency towards one alignment, you will be less affected by changes away from that alignment. You will also be more affected by changes towards it. docs.title: Darkwind offers many ways to customize your character, including
docs.text: Darkwind offers many ways to customize your character, including races, guilds, alignment, equipment, and many others. This document serves to document those items. --<< STANDARD RACES >>-- The following races are available at the Darkwind Hall of Races: Darkwinder- The humans that live around Darkwind City are collectively known as Darkwinders. Darkwinders are about average among the civilized races in terms of physical and mental powers, but are well accepted by most other cultures due to the importance of the city in world affairs. - This race can join any guild. - +EXP +RACE CHANGE Barbarian- The Barbarians are an offshoot of modern human society that settled south of Darkwind City in a settlement known as Canith. Their rugged lifestyle tends towards the development of stronger, healthier bodies than most humans. Canith society values order, and pursuit of the common good. Barbarians are generally friendly to strangers and always eager to learn about exotic people and places. - This race cannot join: NECRO, PRIEST, SWASH - +CHR +CON +STR +EXP +GOOD Glavian- Glavians are humans that hail from the mountain kingdom of Glavia. Glavians are a generally good-aligned people used to opposing demonic forces. Their society is otherwise peaceful and pastoral. Glavians are an inoffensive, likeable lot, with an open mind to new experiences. - This race cannot join: NECRO, PRIEST - +CHR +EXP +GOOD Faerie- Faeries are a race of woodland sprites, usually diminutive in stature. This group encompasses brownies, dryads, atomies, sylphs and pixies, as well as sprites themselves. They are known to be extremely agile as well as friendly and typically good-looking, but due to their generally small size they are not very strong or sturdy. They have a reputation, deserved or not, for being pranksters, and tend to be a bit flighty at times. - This race cannot join: FIGHTER - +WIS +PSION +WINGS +FLIGHT -SIZE Halfling- Halflings are a race of short people much given to the simpler pleasures in life, including good food, a warm bed, a window overlooking a pleasant little garden, a shady tree to lie under in the afternoon, and a full pipe after dinner. They do not often become adventurers, but those that do are quite good at it. They are not too strong, because of their small size, and their homebody nature means they tend to be not as wary. But halflings have truly incredible reflexes and are remarkably nimble and quick with their hands. Halflings are most interested in having fun in life, and they take this attitude with them wherever they go. - This race can join any guild. - +CHR +DEX -STR -WIS +DRINK +EAT -SIZE High elf- The elven kingdom south of Darkwind City is the home of the High Elves. High Elf culture as a whole tends towards goodness in the context of harmony with nature. High Elves have keen senses and are generally superior mentally to most civilized races. Physically however, they can be somewhat fragile and lack the robustness of other races. - This race cannot join: NECRO, PRIEST - +DEX +INT +WIS +CHR -CON +DAM_LIGHT +VISION Kender- The Kender have always been hidden somewhere around the realms of Darkwind. They are small jovial creatures with a love of adventure and no fear. They are extremely agile, but are not known for a high level of common sense. - This race can join any guild. - +STR +DEX -WIS +PSION -DAM_EVIL +VISION -SIZE Rift duergar- The Rift Duergar are a race of evil subterranean dwarves who have been twisted by dark forces into hateful caricatures of surface dwarves They are short, stout and have hardy constitutions, enabling them to hold their liquor and resist small amounts of magic and mental influence. Despite being quite strong, Rift Duergar have problems balancing larger weapons due to their stature. - This race cannot join: BARD, CLERIC, GAROU, LUNAR, MAGE, NINJA, PALADIN, SWASH - +STR +CON -INT -CHR +MAGIC +PSION -DAM_LIGHT +EVIL +VISION +DRINK -SIZE Shel-zaranite- The Shel-zaranites are an ancient offshoot of the elves that live deep underground. In their secluded city, they worship forgotten gods of evil. Dark Elves are quite agile and mentally superior to most races, but are often sickly and lack constitution. Being an underground race however, they are well adapted to lightless conditions. - This race cannot join: CLERIC, GAROU, LUNAR, MAGE, PALADIN - +DEX +INT +WIS -CON -DAM_LIGHT +EVIL +VISION Silver Elf- The elven kingdom located on the highway between Darwind City and the frozen tundra is the home of the Silver Elves. Silver elves are also known as Moon Elves. Silver elf culture tends towards goodness and as to please Luna, the moon Godess. Silver Elves have keen night vision, exude charisma, and are typically more intelligent, though less wise, than other races. Pyshically they are more nimble than what is typical, though they are rather fragile of constitution. - This race cannot join: FIGHTER, NECRO - +DEX +INT +CHR -WIS -CON +GOOD +VISION Stone dwarf- Stone Dwarves are a society of surface dwarves who long ago dedicated their lives to working in the underworld in the service of Mitra. Like most dwarves, they are short and stout and can hold their liquor, but Stone Dwarves also have a high degree of goodness ingrained into them at an early age. Their small size makes it difficult for them to wield larger weapons, and working in cramped mines have a detrimental effect on their joints, limiting their agility. - This race cannot join: GAROU, NECRO, NINJA, PSION, PRIEST, THIEF - +STR +CON -DEX +PSION +GOOD +VISION +DRINK -SIZE Uruk- The Uruk are a loose tribe of marauding orcs which live in the Darkwind area, looting and pillaging small settlements. The Uruk value strength and stamina over useless thought or a pretty face. They are a warlike race that trains for battle from birth to death, acquiring a degree of proficiency in the use of all weapons. They are particularly adapted to living in marginal areas like shallow caves, or fetid swamps. - This race cannot join: BARD, CLERIC, GAROU, LUNAR, MAGE, NECRO, NINJA, PALADIN, PSION, SWASH - This race CAN join: DRAGON, FIGHTER, MORPHER, THIEF - +STR +CON -INT -WIS -CHR +DAM_DISEASE +DAM_POISON +EVIL +VISION +WEAPON SPEC The following races are available at the Hyperborea Hall of Races: Arctic elf- The Arctic Elves are a subrace of the elves that have adapted to living in the far north of Hyperborea. Like all elves, they are bright and agile, but suffer from fragile bodies. Arctic elves are often at odds with the humans of northern Hyperborea, constantly fighting over territory and ancient artifacts of power in order to expand their evil society. - This race cannot join: CLERIC, LUNAR, MAGE, PALADIN - +DEX +INT +WIS -CON -DAM_FIRE +EVIL Hyperborean gnome- Hyperborean gnomes are a race of small humanoids that inhabit the more habitable rural areas of Hyperborea. They are bright and nimble, with a natural resistance to variations in the environment. They have a slight tendency to work towards the causes of good, if only because they are subject to attack by the forces of evil. Like all gnomes, they are quite small compared to other races, and have difficulty managing larger weapons. - This race cannot join: FIGHTER, NECRO, PRIEST - +DEX +INT +WIS +DAM_FIRE +DAM_ACID +DAM_POISON +GOOD +DRINK -SIZE Ice gnoll- Ice Gnolls are an evil warrior race that appears to be a cross of some humanoid and a hyena. They are physically powerful but are lacking somewhat in intellect. Ice gnolls live to kill and eat; who their victims are is largely irrelevant. - This race cannot join: BARD, CLERIC, LUNAR, MAGE, PALADIN, PSION, SWASH, THIEF - +STR +CON +DEX -INT -CHR +EVIL +EAT Ice ogre- Ice Ogres are large brutish humanoids that live in the cold wastes of Hyperborea. Large numbers of them are regularly hired as mercenaries by the giants to wage war against more civilized races. They are immensely strong and rugged, but dimwitted and clumsy as well. They have no real culture to speak of except a penchant for violence. While not quite giant sized, ice ogres are large enough that they can wield large weapons much more easily than most other races. - This race cannot join: BARD, CLERIC, LUNAR, MAGE, NECRO, NINJA, PALADIN, PSION SWASH, THIEF - +STR +CON -DEX -INT -WIS -CHR +DAM_DISEASE -DAM_PSION +EVIL +EAT +DRINK +SIZE Northman- Northmen are humans who settled in the frigid north. Northmen are widespread throughout Hyperborea, although most live in the city of Grimsfjord. Northmen are expert traders and hagglers, due to the need to trade with the southern cities for various goods not produced in Hyperborea. - This race can join any guild. - +CHR +EXP The following races are available at the Souvrael Hall of Races: Desert nomad- The Desert Nomads are the wanderers of Souvrael. They are a deeply religious people who follow the teachings of their prophet. The are quick learners who have adapted to living in the open desert. Desert Nomads are known for their great hospitality, despite the harshness of their habitat. - This race cannot join: NECRO, PRIEST - +CHR +CON +EXP +DAM_FIRE -DAM_WATER +GOOD Desert dwarf- The Desert Dwarves live in a small settlement in the deserts of Souvrael. The Dwarves live in a peaceful society, generally unaffected by outside influences. Physically, they are a short, hardy race. In addition to an innate resistance to magic and psionics, they tend to be quite healthy and strong, but suffer somewhat from a stubbiness in their limbs. Despite their strength, their small size often also creates difficulties in wielding larger weapons. - This race cannot join: GAROU, NECRO, NINJA, PRIEST, SWASH, THIEF - +STR +CON +WIS -DEX +MAGIC +PSION +GOOD +DRINK +VISION -SIZE Souvraeli- Souvraelis are the native humans of Souvrael who choose to live in cities instead of leading a nomadic existence. Their culture has evolved over time towards a more cosmopolitan lifestyle based on trade and education. As such, they are cunning negotiators, and have a thirst for knowledge. - This race can join any guild. - +INT +CHR +EXP -DAM_WATER The following races are available at the Talamh Darag Hall of Races: Crannian gnome- A race of small, misshapen, dwarf-like creatures that dwell in the earth. The name 'gnome' was given to them by the medieval scholar Paracelcus, in an attempt to describe the most important of the earth spirits. Gnomes live under the earth, where they guard treasures. According to Paracelcus, they move as easily through the earth as humans walk upon the ground. They cannot stand the light of the sun, for even one ray would turn them to stone. Some sources claim they spend the hours during daylight as a toad. They are in some way related to goblins and dwarfs. They have been known to steal neglected human babies to raise as their own. - This race cannot join: GAROU, THIEF - +DEX +INT +CHR -CON +EXP +VISION -DRINK -EAT -SIZE Pixie- The pixies are a race of small mischievous little fae. These smart little critters excel at finding ways to scare and trick their unsuspecting victims. They have beautiful silk-like wings that enable them to explore the skies and are naturally protected from the magical abilities of those who would hunt them. This sadistic little fae folk cares little about goodness. - This race cannot join: CLERIC, GAROU, FIGHTER, MAGE, LUNAR, PALADIN - +INT +MAGIC +EVIL +WINGS +FLIGHT -SIZE Sidhe- The Sidhe are a race of vile demonic creatures originating from the influential fae population of Talamh Darag. These Sidhe were infected by a vampiric condition affecting their society on a large level. The now unseelie Sidhe are known for their evil acts, magical abilities and the moth-like wings that enable them to ascend from the ground. The magical nature of the Sidhe fae allows them to regenerate their abilities with greater ease then any other race would be able to. Their weak body is able to purge toxics from their bloodstream at an increased rate, but suffers greatly where raw physical power is concerned. - This race cannot join: CLERIC, FIGHTER, GAROU, LUNAR, MAGE, PALADIN - +DEX +INT -CON -STR +EVIL +WINGS +FLIGHT +DRINK +SPREGEN -SIZE Wayfarian- The wayfarians are a race of elves that have been oppressed by forces of evil for as long as they have been around. A powerful Paladin heroine 'Enelya Ar-Feiniel' who is now revered as their patron of adventurers sought out Mitra's blessing to empower and protect her proud folk. This blessing resulted in a holy and virtuous aura surrounding each member of the Wayfarian race. This aura formed a defense against the evil acts of their foes and enabled them to strike out with a holy fury. Finally the Wayfarians were able to beat off their oppressors and build a new city. Their combined auras helped form a powerful holy dome to protect this city against those who would seek to destroy it. - This race cannot join: GAROU, NECRO, PRIEST, THIEF - +DAM_EVIL +DAM_CHAOS +GOOD +DAM TYPE GOOD --<< EXOTIC RACES >>-- Gypsy- The Gypsy people are a skilled, artful traveling people. They are very smart, charismatic and light fingered. Singing, dancing, telling stories, fortune telling and lifting money from the rubes are the everyday events in the life of the Gyspy. They prefer to wear bright colors, and usually speak freely, looking to make the next big score. - This race cannot join:CLERIC, FIGHTER, NECRO Scro- The Scro are an advanced form of orc that is well adapted to the rigors of travelling in wildspace. While they are not quite as strong nor robust as their more primitive cousins, they make up for this by possessing greater mental faculties and resistances to forces encountered in their more exotic travels. - This race cannot join:BARD, CLERIC, MAGE, PALADIN Sylph- The sky, mountains, and high places such as the tops of very tall trees are the favorite home of the Sylphs. Members of the Faerie race, Sylph are roughly human in appearance with the exception of the almost transparent wings on their backs. The Sylph are a culture that tends towards goodness and lawfulness, but also one known for being able to hold their own when it comes to the hearty consumption of the strong libations served at the various festivals they hold. The Sylph are an attractive race with looks to match their mental powers and quickness, though they tend to be weaker and less robust than other races. - This race cannot join:NINJA, SWASH, NECRO Thraxian- Thraxian draconians hail from the village of Thrax in eastern Hyperborea. While roughly humanoid in shape, they bear a striking similarity to their dragon cousins, including vestigial wings and a fiery breath weapon. They maintain some of the dragons' raw physical power and intellect as well. Their alien natures are not well received by other races, and their clawed hands are not well adapted to using most tools. - This race cannot join:BARD, CLERIC, SWASH, THIEF Exotic races are those races found in areas throughout the game. Exotic races are only available for players of level 45 and above. Racial attributes for exotic races are available in their respective race room. docs.title: Player retribution against others.
docs.text: Player retribution against others. This is about how Darkwind's player used punishment systems work. If you vote to have someone pilloried or a bounty hunter to be sent after them, then you are giving up your right to take personal further action against that person unless they do something else wrong. If the person you voted for being pilloried is pilloried, at that point, you have given up any other claim to take further action against that person. The purpose of the player used punishment systems isn't so you can punish them three times for one offense, it's for punishing them when you yourself can't or are unwilling to take the job of retribution into your own hands. If a person has been, say pilloried, he has served his punishment for his crime. When players continue to harass him afterward over it and in the end kill him, or send a bountyhunter after him it will then be the killers that we will personally frown upon and most likely take action against. If you attempt to take multiple methods of retribution against a player, you will end up in just as bad a situation as the original offender did. It should also be pointed out that if you feel the need to hunt a player to the ends of the earth as his punishment for doing an action against you, that's fine, but once you use one of the player punishment systems, you have given up the right to further pursue the matter on your own. Their purpose as stated earlier isn't so you can have Darkwind punish the offender while at the same time punish them yourselves. It's so that you can have the offender punished if you are incapable or unwilling to do it yourself.

************************************************************* ***** DarkWind's Rules on Multicharacters ***** ************************************************************* 1) The only acceptable form of multicharacters are ones created by the game. If you create a second/third/etc character on your own, you are in violation of the rules, and all characters are subject to banishment. You can only create those characters in Darkwind, in the Multiple Character Registration Room. 2) If you are repeatedly found to create illegal characters, your site will be banned from the game. 3) If you create and register multiple characters, all punishments and warnings apply to all. 4) If any character is banished, you can not create a new character to take its place above the max character limit. 5) You may only have ONE of your characters logged in at a time. 6) In addition to your main character, you may register additional normal characters. Existing registered mythic multichars remain valid. 7) You may only register a normal multi once your main character reaches CHAMPION (50). A second free slot is granted at LEGEND (150). 8) New mythic multichar registration is currently disabled. Existing mythic multichars remain registered and playable. 9) You will login to your multi through your main account. This means that you will only need to remember one username/password combination, so please ensure you keep this login secure. 10) You can purchase additional multichar slots up to 10 total. Each slot will cost additional gold (10 million increase per). 11) You can get a quick overview of your multichars with the multirep command. 12) You can copy your main characters alias list with the multicopy command. 13) All of your multis can access funds from your bank accounts with the transfer function built in at the bank. 14) All of your multis can access items from your storage room at the bank with the store, retrieve, list functions in the storage room.

docs.title: Following is a list of what is not allowed on Darkwind.  Failure
docs.text: Following is a list of what is not allowed on Darkwind. Failure to observe these rules will result in punishment. Lack of knowledge of these rules is not an excuse for not following them. This document will be broken down into two sections: players, and wizards. Everyone will know what is illegal for all to do. Players are expected not to ask wizards to break wizard rules, and wizards are expected not to break rules that bind players. Players ------- 1. Players must obey all requests from wizards. If a player feels that a request is out of line, the player should notify a higher level wizard AFTER complying with the request. 2. Players may not abuse (or use once it's been determined as a bug) any bug. Failing to report a known bug is also illegal. Players who abuse bugs will see their characters wiped. Future abuse by the same player may result in site bans. On the flip side, reporting large bugs might be rewarded. If something is 'too good to be true', it probably is. Always report it. If found to be intended, hey great! See also: help bug. 3. Personal attacks, racial and ethnic slurs, sexual harassment, and other forms of attack will not be tolerated. Threatening other players or wizards with violence will not be tolerated. If someone is ignoring you, do not try to get around the ignore by using alternate means. They're ignoring you for a reason, respect that. The Golden Rule applies here. 3a. No bulletin board (including the PK board and private clan boards) may be used to flame, ridicule or otherwise denigrate other players or wizards. They may also not be used to accuse others of cheating/bug abuse, nor threaten them in any matter (whether in or out of game). 3b. PK issues may only be discussed on the PK board, clan boards, and guild boards(where appropriate to the guild). 3c. The DarkWind forums are considered an extension of the bulletin boards on the mud. 3d. Channels are also governed by the same rules as bulletin boards (rule 3a and 3b) with the exception that IN-GAME threats may be made on the PK channel ONLY. See also: help profanity, help virginears, help ignore, help pk 4. Having multiple (second, third, etc) non-registered main characters will not be tolerated. Darkwind's current rule is to allow one main character per person. If we find that one person has more than one main character, then ALL characters will be removed. Further offenses may result in a siteban. 4a. Darkwind does allow for the registration of secondary characters. Players that have attained the level of 20 on their main character may register a secondary character through the Multiple Character Registration Room. (2:w,s,w of COT)Additional secondary characters are availble depending on level. Please see help multichars for further information. 5. Botting is not allowed. This is defined as creating client- or server-side scripts that will perform an unlimited number of actions without requiring a live person to be sitting at the keyboard of the computer. Use of robots will result in removal of the character. 5a. see "help triggers" for information regarding their usage and further clarification. 5b. Note that use of the Darkwind-provided "script" command is excluded from this rule. However, using a client to string together multiple "script" commands is still illegal as is using a trigger to activate the script. 5c. The use of client side 'aliases' is allowed. 5d. The use of anything to keep your character from idling, ie triggers, events, scripts, etc is illegal. 5e. The use of anything that automates killing without a live person at the keyboard is also illegal. This includes sitting, unattended in aggro rooms. If you aren't at your keyboard, you're character shouldn't end up in combat. 6. Kill stealing is not allowed. If someone is actively killing a mob, the mob is 'theirs' as is the equipment/money in the room. If the player leaves the room, it's fair game, though common courtesy would suggest you leave the mob alone. This does also apply to Garou who are fighting in a room. The items and gold on the ground they are in are not open, just because they can't pick them up. If the Garou leaves the room, again, it's fair game. 6a. Camping a mob. -- If a player is ACTIVE in the room, then everything in that room is theirs, as is any equipment/ money in the room. If the player is IDLE, then the items are fair game. [NOTE: If everyone involved is PK, these rules do not apply as you have recourse through PK] Wizards ------- 1. Wizards may not provide access to their character to any other person. 2. Wizards may not erase or otherwise edit other wizards' files. The same applies to system files. Access to these files is generally protected, but it's conceivable that some things may be overlooked. If the wizard discovers that s/he has greater access than they should, it should be reported to an IMP+. 3. Wizards may not copy another wizard's work without prior consent. 3. Wizards may not interfere with players in any way. this includes healing players; providing additional stats, XP, money, levels, alignment, etc. through patching; and giving players objects. This is not a comprehensive list by any means. In general: if the character isn't your test character, don't mess with 'em. Period. 3a. The occasional boon or similar global blessing given by an IMP+ is not considered interference. 4. Wizards may not abuse wizard powers. 5. Wizards may not disobey higher-up wizards. Punishments ----------- If you are found to have violated one of the above rules, your character may be: 1. Warned 2. Demoted (wiz or player) 3. Jailed 3. Removed 4. Sitebanned

docs.title: Definition
docs.text: Definition ---------- A trigger is defined as using a client or some other program to scan the incoming text from a terminal session and issue a particular command when the incoming text matches a particular string set by the user. Regulations ----------- 1. The use of triggers (both directed and automated) is legal provided that at no time is your character left unattended and that they do not activate upon merely walking into a room. 1a. Example: Bodach, Dink and Klaughihin are in a party. Bodach is the leader and says "heal me". Dink could then have a trigger set up to "heal bodach". 1b. Example: The use of an 'assist' trigger in a party setting is allowed, provided your character is attended at all times. 1c. Example: The use of a 'burn corpse' trigger is allowed, provided it activates ONLY upon your kill. Not your pet's, etc. This includes all forms of corpse skills. Eating them, burning them, turning them into scorching piles of ash, etc. If you didn't kill it, don't trigger it. 1d. Example: The use of a 'kill <mob>' trigger is allowed, provided it does not attack a mob as soon as you walk into a room, or as soon as a mob spawns. If it does, that is considered botting. 2. Any trigger (automated or directed) which allows your character to move is illegal. Movement by use of the in-game scripting ability is allowed, however, this does NOT exclude using a script to kill. Please do NOT script kill an entire area. This is considered botting. This does NOT mean you can trigger the usage of the in-game scripting. DO NOT TRIGGER (or otherwise) AUTOMATE MOVEMENT. 3. Any trigger (automated or directed) which keeps your character logged into the game, and active, without attendance (ie, anti-idle for dragons, autokill on room spawns, etc) is prohibited. DO NOT TRIGGER (or otherwise) AUTOMATE KILLING. 4. Any trigger that is an open variable which allows another player to control your character without you being at your computer is prohibited. Penalties ----------- Failure to adhere to our trigger policy is punishable by up to the loss of half your levels, all your gold, half your stats, mythic character creation bans, and possible banishment. Other penalities may occur in lieu of the afformentioned punishments. Just don't do it. Sit at the keyboard, have a good time. If you get up, turn everything off. This will make DarkWind enjoyable for everyone.

docs.title: Shields are a form of damage mitigation. They act like simple forms of
docs.text: Shields are a form of damage mitigation. They act like simple forms of temporary health. A generic shield will block all forms of damage, but there are specific types of shields that will only block that type of incoming damage. Current shields are viewable through 'hp' or '.'

docs.title: Welcome to Darkwind!
docs.text: Welcome to Darkwind! Most of the basic information about Darkwind can be found in the newbie tome. You can obtain one if you head southwest from the adventurers guild, which is the room you started your adventure in. Alternatively you can obtain one at the center of town (Cot) [Use the command 'ncot' to transport you there]. Do not forget to look at the machine in these two locations! Following will be some basic directions to help you start off your adventuring career, do note this information can also be obtained from the newbie tome. ============================================================================== Equipment, Stores and Bank ============================================================================== Erga's newbie store. Erga hands out free equipment that is perfectedly suited for anyone under level 5. Don't waste your time looking elsewhere, he has some good quality stuff! From Cot: w,w,w,w,s [4w,s] Don't forget to read the sign. ______________________________________________________________________________ Donation room. The mighty heroes and legendary adventurers that inhabit the realms of Darkwind may be so inclined to donate equipment to the more inexperienced adventurers. You can visit the Donation room to see what they may have to offer you. From Cot: n,n,n,n,n,e [5n,e] ______________________________________________________________________________ Bank. You are able to keep your money safe at the bank. That way, if you die, you won't loose your hard earned cash. From Cot: w,w,w,w,w,s,s,s,e [5w,3s,e] ______________________________________________________________________________ Taylors. Taylors is the general store in town, he will be happy to buy your goods off you. A great way to earn a pretty penny selling the treasures you may find on your adventures. From Cot: w,w,w,w,w,s,s,w [5w,2s,w] ============================================================================== Newbie area's ============================================================================== All directions from Cot: Abandoned Village - 6w, exit, 4w, 2n, w, s, w, enter, n, w Ashkenazy's hunting grounds - 5s, exit, s, 4w, s Cemetery - 5w, 2n Farmland - 6w, exit, 4w, 3n, 2e, n Glaverton Forest - 6w, exit, 4w, 2n, e, 3n, e, n, e, n, 5e, 2ne, nw, n Haunted Keep - 5s, exit, 11s, w North Forest path - 6n, exit ,9n, 9nw , w Pegasi - 6n, exit, 8n, 2e, n Pirate Ship - 5e, 4n, climb rope For a more comprehensive listing and descriptions of newbie area's read chapter 5 of the newbie tome. ============================================================================== Further helpfiles of interest ============================================================================== help newbie [The newbie command allows you to talk on the newbie channel] help set [The set command allows you to customize several different features] help wimpy [Wimpy allows you to automatically flee combat when your HP drop too low] help mon [The monitor allows you to set a HP/ SP monitor] help ncot - help nbolt - help npunch - help nkick - help nheal [These are your newbie skills] help recall [Once you have left newbie status, recall lets you teleport back to COT on a 15-minute cooldown] help combatbrief [This setting allows you to filter your combat messages] help score - help sc [Information on your score tables] help int - wis - dex - con - str - chr [Information about your stats] help races [Information on how to become one of the races that inhabit the world of DW] help guildlist [A list of existing guilds on DW, specific info can be obtained from the tome] help rules [The rules for Darkwind, read them, know them, live them, be them!] help pk [Information on Darkwind's player killing system.] ============================================================================== Addendum ============================================================================== Any extra info you feel needs to be added to this file? Use the idea command to suggest! (help idea)

docs.title: Charisma:                    Range: 1-200
docs.text: Charisma: Range: 1-200 Charisma is a measure of force of personality. It measures how well a character is able to influence others by word or action. A charismatic character is more likely to be listened to, respected, and trusted by others. If you have a high charisma, the shopkeepers might give you some extra gold just because they like you. Charisma is useful for guilds that require some subtlety in their dealings, or who seek to guide people along a particular path.

docs.title: Constitution:                Range: 1-300
docs.text: Constitution: Range: 1-300 Constitution is a measure of physical toughness and stamina. High constitution allows a player to perform strenuous tasks for a longer time. It increases the amount of hit points the player has, and therefore increases the amount of damage that can be taken before needing to rest or heal. Your guild determines constitution's base hit-point multiplier. That multiplier increases by one at levels 50, 100, 150, 200, and 250.

docs.title: Dexterity:                   Range: 1-200
docs.text: Dexterity: Range: 1-200 Dexterity encompasses a number of physical attributes including hand-eye coordination, agility, reflexes, balance, precision, and speed of movement. Dexterity affects a character's accuracy with missile weapons (darts, arrows, cats, etc.) and in the ability to swing weapons at moving targets. Dexterity is also important for dodging attacks. Dexterity is particularly important for roguish guilds which rely on quick reflexes and the manipulation of small objects.

docs.title: Syntax: finger <player>
docs.text: Syntax: finger <player> Syntax: finger -text <player> ========== Give some detailed information about a player. They do not have to be logged in at the time when you finger them. Darkflow clients open a GUI modal by default; use finger -text for text.

docs.title: Intelligence:                Range: 1-200
docs.text: Intelligence: Range: 1-200 Intelligence is similar to what is currently known as intelligence quotient, but also includes mnemonic ability, reasoning, and learning ability outside those measured by any written test. In melee combat, more intelligent characters are able to better use their equipment, and discern their enemies' weaknesses, leading to greater success at hitting their enemies, and also in deflecting incoming blows using their armor. Intelligence is essential for guilds that make heavy use of mental powers to manipulate the world directly, or indirectly through arcane spells.

docs.title: Metaphysician Help
docs.text: Metaphysician Help ------------------ The Metaphysician has entered our world to help adventurers increase their physical and mental beings. For a cost, he can help you raise your CON, STR, INT, DEX, WIS, CHR, HP, or SP. The higher your stats become, the harder it is for him to help you, and the higher the cost becomes. At this time, the primary stats of CON, STR, INT, DEX, WIS, and CHR can only be increased a total of 100; 1 per 'meta'. HPs and SPs have no such restriction, but only increase between 2 and 7 each 'meta'. The Metaphysician will only help those that have reached the maximum level of 250, as his time and energies are costly.

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text: DESCRIPTION =========== There are two different verions of this command, although both do basically the same function. That being to show you your current level, XP, GP, how much gold you have in the bank, your HP (and max HP), SP (and max SP), your stats, and your age. If you type 'score' you will get a more abbreviated version of your score, while typing 'sc' will give you more more detailed, and if you have it, ansi color, version of your score. Syntax: score or sc
