docs.title: STATISTICS
docs.text: STATISTICS A player's statistics (or "stats") are measures of advanced a player is in certain aspects of his development. There are currently six stats that you can raise on Darkwind. They are: strength, constitution, dexterity, intelligence, wisdom, and charisma. For help on a specific stat, type "help <stat_abbrev>" at the prompt, where <stat_abbrev> is the three-letter abbreviation for the statistic you want to see the information of. eg. help str (for strength)

docs.title: Strength:                    Range: 1-200
docs.text: Strength: Range: 1-200 Strength is a measure of how muscular a person is. High strength allows a character to lift heavier objects, and carry more weight while adventuring. All things being equal, strong characters will find their packs less encumbering than weaker ones. Strength is also very important in combat, influencing how much power a character is able to put into each swing. Naturally, a stronger character will be able to do more damage with each swing than a weaker one. As adventurers gain levels, they also become more practiced at managing their gear. Strength remains the primary factor for carrying capacity, but level also helps support a fuller set of equipment.

docs.title: Wisdom:                      Range: 1-200
docs.text: Wisdom: Range: 1-200 Wisdom is both a measure of a character's common sense, and also of his general awareness of the world around him. Wisdom is important for all characters since awareness of one's immediate situation is essential for survival. The use of priestly powers is often heavily influenced by wisdom since the character must tap into his awareness of a divine source. Wisdom is especially important in the heat of combat, where the wrong choice can lead to a hasty demise. A wise character can often see a battle unfolding and where an enemy's next strike may land. Wisdom is also important in using armor more effectively to deflect the blows that do land.

docs.title: Usage: areas
docs.text: Usage: areas areas <world or region> areas level <number> areas search <word> areas info <number> The areas command lists public cataloged places to explore. Areas are grouped by world and region, such as Geshtai / Darkwind, Geshtai / Hyperborea, or Dailos / Dailos. Use areas search <word> to find places by name, designer, tag, note, world, or region. After any list or search, use areas info <number> to see more detail about that area, including its credited designer when one is recorded. The level range is a rough guide based on cataloged monster levels. Some places contain unusual monsters, bosses, puzzles, or variable-level creatures, so explore carefully.

docs.title: Welcome to the Darkwind Arena! No more endless bashing on hapless
docs.text: Welcome to the Darkwind Arena! No more endless bashing on hapless monsters even your grandmother can thrash. Here, you get real fights against real players with real intelligences. But first, you need to know how to conduct yourself in an arena battle.... To start a battle at the arena, type "challenge <player>". If your foe types "accept" within 30 seconds, the die is cast and the duel proceeds. Both players are moved into their respective preparatory rooms from which an exit leads into the battlefield proper. Note that you may only leave the battlefield via the preparatory room you start in and the other gladiator cannot enter it at any time. Now, all of this coolness doesn't come for free, the challenger has to pay a cost based upon the combined levels of the two gladiators. Of course, should the fight not come off, the entry fee is returned. Once in the arena, all restraints are removed and players may proceed to use whatever tactics necessary to bring about their opponent's downfall. The loser will not experience a real death, though both players will lose any SP they expend during the battle. One may not quit in the arena or the preparatory rooms, though one can "forfeit" while on the arena floor. The following safety features have been created for your safety. First, when the battle is ended all combat and hunt status is clear as the players are returned to the arena lobby. Any poisoned food or drink not present on a player when a battle begins will cause a warning to be given to the player. Any "standard" Darkwind poisons, Black Lace poison, and disembowel wounds will be removed. Be particularly cautious of any after effects of the battle beyond the ones mentioned above. Blocking powers and such will eventually wear off. Please take note that no pets are allowed in the arena. You'll need to stable any other pets or give them to another player. Summonable pets, eg garou wolves may be summoned once in the arena. Also, if you're poisoned or currently suffering the effects of a disembowel, then you'll have to wait those out before you can fight. If you find a particularly bad one, please notify Admin and they'll see about adding protection against it. Viewing: The stands above the arena entrance will be serviced by reporters who will bring news from all parts of the battlefield. Spectators can also do remote looks at the rooms and at objects in the rooms. They may also shout into the arena battlefield. There is also a command "arenabattle" which can be used to tune into arena battles from anywhere in Darkwind. WARNING: The use of the arena is at the player's risk we've made every effort to make it safe but there are endless combinations of powers and objects. If you lose equipment in a battle then it's gone. That's the price you pay so don't use your best stuff unless you want a Bard whistling it into oblivion. However, stolen items, equipment, and money are expected to be returned to the player. If they're not, the offending player will be banned from the arena.

docs.title: Ashad is an AshPunk desert continent west of the Darkwind mainland. Reach
docs.text: Ashad is an AshPunk desert continent west of the Darkwind mainland. Reach the Oasis of Life across the Ocarian Sea, then follow its soot roads through the Cinder Flats toward the continent's cities and hunting regions. Severe and extreme Ashad heat ramps up while you remain exposed. Its first check applies Exposed. Continued checks refresh Exposed and apply urning stacks. Daylight checks every 20 seconds at full strength; dawn and twilight check every 25 seconds at reduced strength; night checks every 30 seconds at half strength. Marked shelters and rooms with light or no heat stop new exposure. Resist Heat prevents the hazard. Ranger desert survival halves its Burning stacks, Souvraeli adaptation reduces them further, and fire resistance mitigates the damage Burning deals. Existing Burning decays normally after reaching safety; Exposed expires shortly afterward. Type heat in any Ashad room to see its tier, whether it protects you, the current cadence, and the Burning stacks expected for your character.

docs.title: Auralis is a wandering prismatic sky continent intended for adventurers
docs.text: Auralis is a wandering prismatic sky continent intended for adventurers around level 200 and above. Its level ranges are recommendations, not gates. Reach Auralis aboard the Prismatic Wayfarer from the elevated berth at DarkWind Port. The skyship accepts an ordinary ferry ticket. On arrival, touch the wayshard in the Veil Below to unlock return travel through the wayshard network. Characters with a current means of flight can also reach Auralis through the greater Aeolus sky. The prismatic wake lies west of the skies above Wayfare. From that sky anchor, fly up beneath Solenne and land at the lower chain harbor. The route is two-way; non-fliers cannot launch from the harbor, and civic safety chains recover anyone whose flight ends in the open undercity air. The lower city includes chainworks, moving counterweights, living rootworks, a liquid-light cistern, memorial, bell foundry, lantern exchange, cloudwatch, an old civic dragon roost, and multiple routes back into the original Veil. The inhabited layers of Solenne are protected by a golden ward. Beyond them, the Shifting Spectrum cycles through Crimson, Azure, Emerald, Violet, and Golden phases every fifteen minutes. Exposed wilderness can burn, freeze, shock, or distort travelers; Golden light offers a brief recovery outside combat. Grounded prism shelters block every phase hazard. While in Auralis, type spectrum to see the current phase, the time until it changes, and whether your location is protected. Far above the first Crimson shelters, fixed shadows converge on the hidden First Impact Scar. Its prism vanes teach the same controls used against Vaelkor, the Ash Regent. During that encounter, threat messages name a vane and give an exact response window. Use vanes for plain-text status, turn <direction> vane toward Vaelkor to reflect a breath attack, and shatter core before a suspended ember core heals him. Missed counters deal damage but never stun or suppress commands.

docs.title: Darkwind's calendar is based on a 300 day year, Each Day is
docs.text: Darkwind's calendar is based on a 300 day year, Each Day is approximately 20 hours, and 1 week is a ten-day long. There are 3 ten-day in a month (or 30 days), and 10 months in a year. There are three moons that orbit high above Geshtei all of which are distinctly diferentiable because of their colors. The largest is Dailos, also known as the Magenta moon. The next largest is Markas, the Red moon, and the smallest, Tekal, is called the Green moon. The names of the days of the week and months of the year are as follows: Days of the week Short Name Full Name ----------- -------------------------------- Godsday Day of the Gods Moonday Day of the Placid Moon Seasday Day of the Open seas Windsday Day of the Whispering Winds Treesday Day of the Towering Trees Hearthday Day of the Hearth Fire Starday Day of the Blinking stars Sunday Day of the Living Sun Peaksday Day of the Soaring Peaks Marketday Day of the Golden Harvest Months of the Year Month Nickname ----------- ---------------------- Hammer Deepwinter Alturiak The Claws of Winter Ches The Claws of Storms Tarsakh The Melting Mirtul Time of Flowers Kythorn Summertide Flamerule Highsun Marpenoth Leafall Uktar The Rotting Nighal The Dawning Down The commands 'time' and 'date' will show you the current time and date here on Darkwind. The year is calculated from the time Darkwind first opened.

docs.title: Dramasa is a barren ice land of white plains, frozen roads, and
docs.text: Dramasa is a barren ice land of white plains, frozen roads, and aurora-lit ruins. Heffenpurt, its western port, is the first safe foothold. Heffenpurt's public fire burns in Hearth Square. Use: sit by fire to clear Chilled and Freezing and gain 15 minutes of Hearth-Warmed protection. The protection appears in buffs and will suppress Dramasa's outdoor cold exposure when that system is active. Touch Heffenpurt's aurora-pale wayshard to remember the city for later travel. Heffenpurt lies on the eastern side of the Cold Sea. A scheduled passenger ferry has not yet been assigned to the route.

docs.title: The Eternal Dungeon is an instanced endless dungeon run for a solo
docs.text: The Eternal Dungeon is an instanced endless dungeon run for a solo player or a small group. Once you enter, your run is private to your party. Each floor is generated for that run, filled with themed rooms, enemies, objectives, affixes, and a final leader encounter. Basic commands: eternal enter [floor] eternal status eternal shop eternal buy <item> eternal leave eternal rejoin eternal leaderboard [v2|legacy] eternal choose <1-3> How it works: 1. Enter the dungeon. 2. Complete the floor objective. 3. A portal opens with one or more route choices. 4. Use portal <route> or enter portal <route> to advance. 5. Repeat until the run wipes. Some objectives happen before the final leader. If the dungeon asks you to recover a relic or cleanse a shrine, the object will appear in an earlier chamber and the room description will show the exact command: recover relic or cleanse shrine. The final portal will not open until the objective and the leader are both handled. Routes can include safe, elite, boss, or unstable paths. Harder routes pay more Eternal Shards, but they also make the next floor more dangerous. Every few floors the dungeon may offer a bargain. The run leader can use eternal choose <1-3> to accept one of the offered boons or curses before advancing. Deaths inside the Eternal Dungeon are not normal deaths. If the run fails, players are returned safely and rewarded based on how far the run advanced. Your progress is tracked, including runs, kills, defeats, and highest floor reached. Eternal v2 has its own leaderboard and shard progress. Legacy records remain visible with eternal leaderboard legacy. Checkpoints unlock every 5 floors. Solo checkpoints belong to the player who unlocked them. Group checkpoints belong to the exact party composition that unlocked them, so the same players must reunite to use those group checkpoints. Use eternal enter [floor] to start from an unlocked checkpoint. Use eternal status to view your available solo checkpoints and, when your party is assembled, any group checkpoints for that composition. Leaderboard entries show the starting floor when a run began from a checkpoint. Skipped floors do not grant reward compensation. V2 and legacy leaderboards are separate because the dungeon rules are different. Leader and boss kills leave personal reward chests. Daily limits govern premium treasure, while materials use separate supply rolls: gilded and plain chests guarantee ember materials and repeat shard caches retain a smaller material chance. Tier-appropriate recipe cards gain a guaranteed drop after five eligible misses. Use eternal status to inspect chest and card-pity counters. The shard shop sells persistent materials and recipe cards at fixed prices for a deterministic alternative. See also: help eternal_dungeon, help leaderboard

The run leader can use eternal choose <1-3> to accept one of the offered boons or curses before advancing. Deaths inside the Eternal Dungeon are not normal deaths. If the run fails, players are returned safely and rewarded based on how far the run advanced. Your progress is tracked, including runs, kills, defeats, and highest floor reached. Personal best floors can also be announced on Events when you surpass your old record. Eternal v2 has its own leaderboard and shard progress. Legacy records remain visible with eternal leaderboard legacy. Checkpoints unlock every 5 floors. Solo checkpoints belong to the player who unlocked them. Group checkpoints belong to the exact party composition that unlocked them, so the same players must reunite to use those group checkpoints. Use eternal enter [floor] to start from an unlocked checkpoint. Use eternal status to view your available solo checkpoints and, when your party is assembled, any group checkpoints for that composition. Leaderboard entries show the starting floor when a run began from a checkpoint. Skipped floors do not grant reward compensation. V2 and legacy leaderboards are separate because the dungeon rules are different. See also: help eternal, help boss_tiers Reward Chests ------------- Every leader or boss kill leaves a personal reward chest for each member present in the run. Chests are name-locked, fade after ten minutes, and do not follow you through the portal - open yours before advancing. Chest quality is earned, not farmed: - The FIRST chest of each reward tier you earn per real day is GILDED: full rolls, a guaranteed rare roll, and the only grade that can ever hold a permanent relic. - The next two chests of that tier the same day are PLAIN (fewer rolls, no guarantees). - After that, and whenever you fight roughly ten or more floors below your personal best, chests dim to SHARD CACHES: a small Eternal Shard payout, no premium treasure, and a modest chance at crafting material. Each member's chest is scaled to their own record, so carrying a lower-floor friend gives them real chests while your own reflect your personal best. Chest contents include consumables, ember crafting materials and recipe cards for the professions, timed emberforged gear that burns away when its ember is spent, and - very rarely, from deep gilded chests - permanent relics that the dungeon yields at most once per adventurer in their lifetime. Crafting supply is rolled separately from premium treasure. Gilded chests guarantee two materials, plain chests guarantee one, and shard caches may still yield one. Recipe cards only appear in gilded or plain chests and match the effective reward tier: Emberdraught at low tiers, Phoenix Tonic through the middle tiers, and Emberforged Whetstone at the deepest tier. Each eligible chest without a card advances that tier's pity counter; once five misses are shown, the next eligible chest guarantees a card. Use 'eternal status' to inspect those counters. The shard shop ('eternal shop') also carries permanent items at fixed prices, likewise one per adventurer, ever. It also sells persistent, tradeable ember materials and recipe cards at fixed prices so shard caches remain a deterministic path into Eternal crafting. 'eternal status' shows how many premium chests of each tier you have earned today.

docs.title: DarkWind has a simple, but intricate ferry system. There are currently five
docs.text: DarkWind has a simple, but intricate ferry system. There are currently five ferries that will sail you around the lands of DarkWind. Near the docks you will find someone selling tickets. Tickets are free to those level 5 and under, and 85 coins for everyone else. * The M.S.S Fairweather sails from DarkWind to Souvrael and back. * The whaling ship Pequod sails from Hyperborea to DarkWind and back. * The Oshimara Maru sails from Souvrael to the Odako province of Kerei and back. * The Island Skipper sails from DarkWind to the Isle of Dwork, then to Volcano Isle, then back to DarkWind. * The Prismatic Wayfarer climbs from the elevated berth at DarkWind Port to the Veil Below in Auralis and back. It accepts an ordinary ferry ticket.

docs.title: It was nearly 1800 years ago that the dark wind appeared and ravaged
docs.text: It was nearly 1800 years ago that the dark wind appeared and ravaged our cities, countries, towns and villages. From where this evil came and what the cause was, I regret to say is not known to us, for most of the immortals were still children at the time. Some say it was an evil birthed of the foul arts of Alarian, the great Necromancer, and that he was its first victim, but that is just a legend from the mists of time. Whatever the cause, the effects were obvious. Not even the longest of wars could have killed as swiftly and effortlessly as that unliving wind of malice. The dark wind has come and gone several times during my life, during the life of the city, and during the rebuilding. Not even Mitra, Gaea and Set could fully stop the destruction. But the first occurrence of the wind was the worst by far. We shall start our history at that time, for history of the time before the coming is lost, just as the lives and cities were lost. The races of Darkwind were thrown into confusion, and the blancmanges, who had been decimated by the wind, were pushed to the brink of extinction by the resulting race wars. The race wars were bloody affairs. The ogres, orcs and trolls banded together, and with their combined raw strength launched raids and besieged the elves, gnomes and dwarves as they attempted to rebuild. The humans fell victim to massive infighting. The faerie and the halflings managed to escape most of the bloodshed, however they found themselves unable to do much rebuilding of their shattered culture. The death and barrenness caused by the dark wind caught the eye of three gods: Gaea, the earth mother; Mitra, the goddess of goodness; and Set, the god of chaos. Gaea set about to restore the land, the plants, and the animals. Mitra and Set, however, made themselves known to the inhabitants of Darkwind. Gaea worked so very hard at rebuilding life. Mitra and Set, however, attempted to lead the people to a better life. Co- existence between the factions, the races, and families was not to be at this time. The religious wars that followed were unfortunate, and only served to dilute the population even more. No one but the gods know what happened to change things. 24 years after the cleansing by the dark wind, representatives from the different races met at the bay where Darkwind City now stands. Many say that Gaea herself came to the representatives and entranced them, giving them power from her own body, as well as power from both Set and Mitra. Thus she bestowed upon them immortality; the ability to command flesh, stone, air, water, and spirit, and the determination to create a better life. With the immortals in place, she forbade Set and Mitra from taking a direct hand in the world, allowing them to only work through the priests and the immortals. The age of immortals had begun. The first act was the creation of a city on the very ground where they were given their power. And the city was called Darkwind, and it was open to one and all. The races of Darkwind thrived, and explored the surrounding countryside and the oceans. The immortals created many things, guided by Mitra, Set and Gaea.

docs.title: Moongates connect Darkwind to Dailos, Markas, and Tekal. At the old
docs.text: ===================================================================== Moongates connect Darkwind to Dailos, Markas, and Tekal. At the old Lunar Gate, use enter dailos, enter markas, or enter tekal. The matching portal chambers in the Plaza of Three Moons work the same way. Moon phases change how quickly a gate opens, but never close a route: - A visible destination moon provides immediate passage. - If the destination is new, the Afterlight Relay borrows light from the brightest visible moon. Hold still for 3 seconds. - If all three moons are new, the Eclipse Reserve releases stored afterlight. Hold still for 8 seconds. Borrowed and reserve passages cost nothing and use no limited charge. Moving away, disconnecting, dying, or entering combat before the gate opens breaks the gathering pattern; simply return and try again. Look at a lunar gate, portal, or moonstone to see its current phase and travel mode. Returning from a moon to Darkwind is always immediate. See also: world, wayshards, ferries # keywords: lunar travel, moons, afterlight relay, eclipse reserve # alias: moongate, lunar gate, moon gate, moon travel

docs.title: How to purchase a new Ship
docs.text: How to purchase a new Ship ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ We are currently offering four different types of ships: Cog, Galley, Catamaran, and Carrack. Your first step is to "purchase" one of the ship types at the ship shop located: 5:s,e,s,3:e,n,e,s of COT. A cog costs 120,000 gold. A galley cost 180,000 gold. A carrack costs 400,000 gold. The catamaran is only available at the Wayfarian ship shop on Talamh Darag. At a ship shop, use 'inquire <ship name>' to learn where a registered ship is currently docked and who owns it. Ship names must be one word. To buy a ship, simply 'request application' in the ship shop. Then 'read application' to see the information required. Please "fillin [number] [text]" to complete the application. When you are finished, "turnin" the application at a ship shop. Congratulations, then you own a new ship, which will be placed in port for you. Orders ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ A small list of orders you can give while onboard ship. Captains Quarters ---------------------- The captain can create his own room description by typing "rename <description>" where the description is one continous line with a return at the end. Also, anyone one in the room can custom emote by typing "em <stuff>". Bridge ---------------------- This is where the captain can do the most. demote - Demotes a captain to a passenger dock - Orders the crew to dock the ship. forbid - Repeals a passenger's boarding privilges furl - Orders the crew to pull down the sails. hoist - Orders the crew to raise the sails. list - Gives you a current list of the ship's passengers or captains. peer - To look overboard and see what's around. permit - Grants a player permission to board your ship only promote - Promotes a passenger to captain (can sail the ship) push off - Orders the crew to pull away from the dock. sail <dir> - To move the ship. yell - Yells a message to the area outside your ship Deck ---------------------- disembark - Disembark the ship peer - To look overboard and see what's around. While onboard, you can type "orders" in any room to see the list of orders you may give while in that room. Not all rooms have orders to report.

docs.title: Thanks to the work of Cliff the Adventurer, an ancient tree that was
docs.text: Thanks to the work of Cliff the Adventurer, an ancient tree that was discovered deep within the surrounding forests of DarkWind has been transplanted into the DarkWind Arboretum. As the inhabitants of DarkWind soon discovered, this tree, known as Stellaer, will grant wishes. We still do not know the source of the tree's powerful magic. From what have seen, the wishes are limited: 1) The tree will only grant certain items or buffs. We're not sure why it chose these. 2) The tree's magic takes time to initially charge, and therefore can't be used directly after a reboot. 3) Adventurers given gifts have to wait twenty-four hours to receive another gift, unless the MUD reboots. 4) The tree will only supply an adventurer with one gift at a time. As grow with this tree, the information we know about it may increase.

docs.title: Wayshards are towering ancient crystals found across the world, one
docs.text: ===================================================================== Wayshards are towering ancient crystals found across the world, one linked to each charted area. A shard remembers every traveler who has touched it, and together the shards form a fast travel network. Attuning: find a wayshard and touch shard. The first touch attunes you to it as the shard learns your touch. Look at a shard to see whether it already knows you. Ghosts cannot touch the shards, and they will not answer during or shortly after combat. New adventurers: characters up to level 10 automatically know the wayshards of the newbie areas. Traveling: at any wayshard, touch shard again to see your possible destinations, grouped by world and region with a level range for each. Each destination has a stable waymark ID. Choose with travel <id> or travel <area>, or cancel to dismiss the menu. Anywhere at all, waypoints lists every shard you have attuned to; entries marked unavailable are known to you but cannot currently be used for fast travel. Costs and limits: - Travel costs nothing, but the shards need a minute to settle: you must wait 60 seconds between trips. - A shard can only reach other attuned shards on the same planet. - You cannot depart while fighting, shortly after combat, as a ghost, or from places that dampen teleportation. Wayshards look different from world to world -- deep violet in Darkwind, frost-blue in Hyperborea, sea-green in Souvrael, and more -- but all of them answer to a touch. See also: areas, ferries, world # keywords: fast travel, attune, teleport, waystone, shard # alias: wayshard, waypoint, waypoints
