docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_AUTO_INCLUDE, value) <value> being: string <text> string <closure>(string base_file, string current_file , int sys_include) DESCRIPTION Optional hook specifying a string to be included before the source of every compiled LPC object. Hook setting can be a string or a closure. If the setting is a string, it will be automatically included before the source of every compiled LPC object. If the setting is a closure, it is called for every file opened by the compiler. <base_file> will be the filename of the compiled object, <current_file> the name of a file included directly or indirectly by the <base_file>. When the <base_file> itself is opened, <current_file> will be 0. For an included file, <sys_include> will be TRUE if it is a <>-type include. If the result from the call is a string, it will be included before the actual text of the file. In both cases, the string will be included as-is; in particular no terminating '\n' will be added. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C), include_dirs(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_CLEAN_UP, value) <value> being: int <closure>(int ref, object ob) void|int <name>(int ref) DESCRIPTION Optional hook to clean up an object. Hook setting can be any closure, or the name of the function to call in the object. This hook is called for an object if it hasn't been used for at least TIME_TO_CLEAN_UP seconds, to give it the opportunity to self destruct. If the hook is a closure, it is called with the refcount of the object to clean up as first argument, and with the object itself as second. Lambda closures are also bound to the object prior to the call. If the hook is the name of an lfun, it is called in the object with its refcount as argument. In both calls, the refcount is constructed as: ref = 0: the object is a clone, or a blueprint with replaced program. ref = 1: the object is a swapped or unused blueprint. ref > 1: the object is a used blueprint with <ref> references. The cleanup method has the possibility to destruct the object. To survive this time, but try again some time later, the call has to result in a non-zero value. If the hook specifies a non-existing lfun, or if the call returns 0, no further attempt to clean up this object will be done. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_CLONE_UIDS, value) <value> being: mixed <closure>(object blueprint, string objectname) DESCRIPTION Mandatory hooks to determine the uid and euid of cloned objects. Hook settings can be any closure. When an object is cloned, the H_CLONE_UIDS hook is called with the blueprint object as first and the clone's designated name as second argument. The new object already exists, but has 0 uids. For the result, the following possibilities exist (<num> is a non-zero number, <no-string> is anything but a string): "<uid>" -> uid = "<uid>", euid = "<uid>" ({ "<uid>", "<euid>" }) -> uid = "<uid>", euid = "<euid>" ({ "<uid>", <no-string> }) -> uid = "<uid>", euid = 0 If strict-euids is not active, the following results are possible, too: <num> -> uid = 0, euid = 0 ({ <num>, "<euid>" }) -> uid = 0, euid = "<euid>" ({ <num>, <no-string> }) -> uid = 0, euid = 0 HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C), uids(C), load_uids(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_COMMAND, value) <value> being: int <closure>(string command, object command_giver) int <name>(string command, object command_giver) DESCRIPTION Optional hook to parse and execute commands. If this hook is used, it bypasses the normal command parsing done by the driver (including the MODIFY_COMMAND and NOTIFY_FAIL hooks). The hook is called with two parameters: the command received from the living (interactive user or NPC), and the living object (the 'command giver') itself. The hook has to return non-0 if the command was found and executed, and 0 otherwise. At the time the hook is called, query_command() returns the command string and this_player() returns the living object. query_verb() and query_notify_fail() return 0. If the hook is a string, it is the name of an lfun in the command giver; if the hook is a lambda closure, it is bound to the command giver before the call. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C), modify_command(H), modify_command_fname(H), notify_fail(H), send_notify_fail(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_CREATE_CLONE, value) <value> being: void <name> (0) int <closure> ( void ) int <closure> (object obj_to_init) DESCRIPTION Optional hooks to initialize a cloned object after creation. Hook setting can be unbound lambda closures, or the name of the function to call in the object. If the hook is a closure expecting an argument, it is bound to the current object and called with the created object as argument. If the hook as a closure without arguments, it is bound to the object to be initalized and called. If the result of the closure call is a non-zero number, it is used as the interval to wait before the first reset(), else the default interval computed from TIME_TO_RESET is used. If the hook is defined as the name of an lfun in the object, it is called in the object with 0 as argument, and any result is ignored. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C), create_ob(H), create_super(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_CREATE_OB, value) <value> being: void <name> (0) int <closure> ( void ) int <closure> (object obj_to_init) DESCRIPTION Optional hooks to initialize an explictely loaded object/blueprint after creation. Hook setting can be unbound lambda closures, or the name of the function to call in the object. If the hook is a closure expecting an argument, it is bound to the current object and called with the created object as argument. If the hook as a closure without arguments, it is bound to the object to be initalized and called. If the result of the closure call is a non-zero number, it is used as the interval to wait before the first reset(), else the default interval computed from TIME_TO_RESET is used. If the hook is defined as the name of an lfun in the object, it is called in the object with 0 as argument, and any result is ignored. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C), create_super(H), create_clone(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_CREATE_SUPER, value) <value> being: void <name> (0) int <closure> ( void ) int <closure> (object obj_to_init) DESCRIPTION Optional hooks to initialize a blueprint which is loaded by inheritance after creation. Hook setting can be unbound lambda closures, or the name of the function to call in the object. If the hook is a closure expecting an argument, it is bound to the current object and called with the created object as argument. If the hook as a closure without arguments, it is bound to the object to be initalized and called. If the result of the closure call is a non-zero number, it is used as the interval to wait before the first reset(), else the default interval computed from TIME_TO_RESET is used. If the hook is defined as the name of an lfun in the object, it is called in the object with 0 as argument, and any result is ignored. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C), create_ob(H), create_clone(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_DEFAULT_METHOD, value) <value> being: int <name>(mixed & result, string fun, varargs args) int <closure>(mixed & result, object ob, string fun, varargs args) DESCRIPTION Optional hook to provide default implementation for unresolved calls. Hook setting can be any closure, or the name of the function to call in the object. This hook is called whenever a call_other(), call_resolved() or call_out() on named function (as opposed to a closure) couldn't be resolved. The hook has then the opportunity to provide a default implementation. Exempt from this behaviour are calls to the master object, to simul-efuns, and calls done with call_direct() and call_direct_resolved(). If the hook is the name of an lfun, it is called in the target object; otherwise if it is a closure, the target object is passed as parameter <ob>. The other parameters passed are the name <fun> of the called function, the arguments <args> passed to the call (if any), and a reference <result> to a variable for the call result. If the hook can resolve the call, it has to return the call result in <result> and 1 as function result. If the hook can not (or doesn't want to) resolve the call, it has to return 0. HISTORY Introduced in LDMud 3.3.113 SEE ALSO hooks(C)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_DEFAULT_PROMPT, value) <value> being: string <closure>() DESCRIPTION Optional hook for the command prompt. If this hook is not used, the driver will use "> " as the command prompt. The hook can be given as string or as closure. If it is a closure, it is called with the commandgiver being the calling object. If the result is a string, it will be printed, otherwise ignored. HISTORY Introduced in LDMud 3.3.163. SEE ALSO hooks(C), print_prompt(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_ERQ_STOP, value) <value> being: void <closure>() DESCRIPTION Optional hook to notify the mudlib about the termination of the erq demon. Hook setting may be any closure. The closure is called without arguments and may do whatever it likes to clean-up after the erq. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C)

docs.title: CONCEPT
docs.text: CONCEPT driver hooks DESCRIPTION To allow a greater flexibility of the muds, the gamedrivers since 3.2.1 moved several once hardcoded 'underground' activities from the driver into the mudlib. This includes for example the differences between compat and native mode. The hooks are set with the privileged efun set_driver_hook(). Some of the hooks are mandatory, some not. Most hooks accept unbound lambda closures as values, some also lfun closures or even strings. The hooks are identified by an ordinal number, for which symbolic names are defined in /sys/driverhooks.h. SEE ALSO native(C), set_driver_hook(E)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_INCLUDE_DIRS, value) <value> being: string *<dirs> string <closure>(string include_name, string current_file) DESCRIPTION Semi-mandatory hook specifying the directories where <>-type include files are searched (this includes ""-includes not found as specified). Hook setting may be any closure or a string array. If not set, only ""-type includes may be used in LPC programs. The hook is called only if a call to master::include_file() does not return a usable filename. If the hook setting is a string array, it has to contain the path names of those directories where <>-type includes are to be searched. The directories are searched in the order they appear in the array. The directory name and the name of the actual include file are concatenated, therefore the directory names have to end in '/'. Leading slashes may be omitted. If the setting is a closure, it is called with the name of the desired include file as first, and the name of the compiled LPC file as second argument. Result has to be the complete path name of the include file to use. Leading slashes may be omitted. If the closure is a lambda closure, it is bound to this_object() prior to execution. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C), auto_include(H), include_file(M)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_LOAD_UIDS, value) <value> being: mixed <closure> (string objectname) DESCRIPTION Mandatory hooks to determine the uid and euid of loaded or cloned objects. Hook settings can be any closure. When an object is newly loaded, the H_LOAD_UIDS hook is called with the object name as argument. The new object already exists, but has 0 uids. For the result, the following possibilities exist (<num> is a non-zero number, <no-string> is anything but a string): "<uid>" -> uid = "<uid>", euid = "<uid>" ({ "<uid>", "<euid>" }) -> uid = "<uid>", euid = "<euid>" ({ "<uid>", <no-string> }) -> uid = "<uid>", euid = 0 If strict-euids is not active, the following results are possible, too: <num> -> uid = 0, euid = 0 ({ <num>, "<euid>" }) -> uid = 0, euid = "<euid>" ({ <num>, <no-string> }) -> uid = 0, euid = 0 HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C), uids(C), clone_uids(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_RESET, value) <value> being: int|string <closure>(string cmd, object player) int|string <name>(string cmd) <mapping> DESCRIPTION Optional hook to modify commands (both entered or given by a call to command()) before the parser sees them (this includes special commands like 'status'). Hook setting can be any closure, the name of the function to call in the object, or a mapping. For interactives this hook is used only if the interactive object has no command modifier already set by the efun set_modify_command(). If the hook is a closure, it is called with the entered command as first, and the command giving player as second argument. Lambda closures are bound to the command giving player, unbound-lambda closures remain unbound. If the hook is a string, it is used as the name of an lfun in the command giving player, which is called with the command as argument. If the hook is a mapping, it is queried with the given command as index, and the data retrieved is used as new command (defaults to 0 if no data is stored for a given command). If an entry is a closure instead of a string, it is called as int|string <closure>(string cmd, object player) and the result from the call is used as 'the' command. The result is treated equal in all three cases: - If the result is a string, it is the new command to execute instead of the given one. Note that it is not possible to make several commands from one this way! - If the result is a non-zero number, the given command is to be ignored. In case of the closure/lfun setting this may mean that the closure/lfun already executed it. - If the result is 0, the originally given command is to be used. It is possible for the hook to change the command giver (this_player()) for the execution of the command. This means that even though the commands are execute for the original commandgiver, this_player() will return the changed commandgiver. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C), command(H), modify_command_fname(H), notify_fail(H), send_notify_fail(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_MODIFY_COMMAND_FNAME, value) <value> being: int|string <name>(string cmd) DESCRIPTION Mandatory hook specifying the name of the 'modify_command' lfun to call for newly entered commands as result of a set_modify_command(). Hook setting must be a string. If set_modify_command() is used for an interactive user, all newly entered commands are first passed to the function named by this hook. The function is called with the command as argument. If the result is a string, it is the new command to execute instead of the given one. Note that it is not possible to make several commands from one this way! If the result is a non-zero number, the given command is to be ignored. In case of the closure/lfun setting this may mean that the closure/lfun already executed it. If the result is 0, the originally given command is to be used. It is possible for the hook to change the command giver (this_player()) for the execution of the command. This means that even though the commands are execute for the original commandgiver, this_player() will return the changed commandgiver. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C), command(H), modify_command(H), notify_fail(H), send_notify_fail(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_MOVE_OBJECT0, value) set_driver_hook(H_MOVE_OBJECT1, value) <value> being: void <closure>(object item, object dest) DESCRIPTION Mandatory hooks to implement the efun void move_object(). Hook setting must be an unbound lambda closure. Upon call, the hook has to perform the move itself (by using set_environment()) and all depending actions (like the calls to init() to add actions). The difference lies in the binding of the set hook prior to the call: the H_MOVE_OBJECT0 closure is bound to the current object, the H_MOVE_OBJECT1 to 'item'. If both hooks are set, H_MOVE_OBJECT0 is ignored. HISTORY SEE ALSO move_object(E), set_environment(E), hooks(C)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_TELNET_NEG, value) <value> being: void <name>(int flag, object user) void <closure>(int flag, object user) DESCRIPTION Optional hook to specifiy how to perform the telnet actions to switch the echo mode (used for e.g. password input_to()s). Hook setting may be any closure or a string. If not set, a default handling is performed. If the setting is a string, it used as name of an lfun to call in the interactive <user>, where <flag> is the echo-flag passed to the input_to() statement. If the setting is a closure, it is called with the same arguments, and unbound lambda-closures being bound to this_player() prior to execution. When set, the hook is called whenever the driver needs to change the echo mode, thus you can negotiate about things that are coupled with it, like LINEMODE or character-at-a-time. IMPORTANT: If this hook is used, the control of all telnet negotiation is transferred to the mudlib: all incoming negotiations are passed to H_TELNET_NEG, and the sending of no-echo negotiations is handled by this hook. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C), telnet(C), telnet_neg(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_NO_IPC_SLOT, value) <value> being: 0 string <msg> DESCRIPTION Optional hook specifying the message given to logins rejected due to space limitations (MAX_PLAYER). Hook setting has to be string. If set to 0, the default message "Lpmud is full. Come back later." is issued. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_NOTIFY_FAIL, value) <value> being: string <msg> string <closure>(string entered_command, object cmd_giver) DESCRIPTION Mandatory hook to issue the default message if an entered command couldn't be parsed and no notify_fail() command is in effect. Hook setting can be a any closure, or a string. If set to a string, it is the message returned to the player. If set to a closure, it is called with the command and the command giver as arguments, and the result is used as failure message. Lambda closures are bound to this_player() prior to execution. <cmd_giver> is the object which received the command in the first place. It is usually identical with this_player(), unless the H_MODIFY_COMMAND hook changed it. HISTORY LDMud 3.2.7 added the new 'command_giver' argument. SEE ALSO hooks(C), command(H), modify_command(H), modify_command_fname(H), send_notify_fail(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_PRINT_PROMPT, value) <value> being: void <name>(string prompt). void <closure>(string prompt) DESCRIPTION Optional hook to print the current command prompt. If this hook is not set, the driver will just print the prompt to the user. The hook is called with the prompt string as single argument and has to print the prompt, e.g. using write() or binary_message(). If the hook is a string, it is the name of an lfun in the command giver. If the hook is a closure, it is called with the command giver as previous object. HISTORY Introduced in LDMud 3.3.163. SEE ALSO hooks(C), default_prompt(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_RESET, value) <value> being: void|int <closure> ( void ) void <name>(1) DESCRIPTION Optional hook to reset an object. Hook setting can be unbound lambda closures, or the name of the function to call in the object. If the hook is a closure, it is bound to the object to be reset and called with no argument. If the result of this call is a positive number, it is used as the interval to wait before the next reset(). If the result is 0, the default interval computed from TIME_TO_RESET is used. If the result is a negative number, the object will not be reset again, unless directed otherwise by set_next_reset(). If the hook is defined as the name of an lfun in the object, it is called in the object with 1 as argument, and any result is ignored. In this call the previous_object() is the object initiating the reset. If the function does not exist, the object won't be reset again. Note that an object is only reset by call to this hook if it has been used since the last reset. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_SEND_NOTIFY_FAIL, value) <value> being: void <name>(string msg, object msgobj, object orig_cmd_giver) void <closure>(string msg, object msgobj, object orig_cmd_giver) DESCRIPTION Optional hook to send the notify fail message, regardless of how it was determined, to the player. If the hook is not set, the message is delivered using tell_object() internally. Hook setting can be a string or a closure. If the hook is a string, it is the name of a (possibly static) function to call in the current command giver. If the hook is a closure, it is the function to be called. Lambda closures are bound to the current command giver first. The arguments to the call are: - <msg> is the notify fail message to be delivered. - <msgobj> is the object which set the message. It is 0 for the default message. - <orig_cmd_giver> is the object for which the original command was first received. It is usually identical with the current command giver this_player(). HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C), command(H), modify_command(H), modify_command_fname(H), notify_fail(H)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS #include <sys/driver_hooks.h> set_driver_hook(H_TELNET_NEG, value) <value> being: void|mixed <name>(int action, int option [, int * opts ] ) void|mixed <closure>(int action, int option [, int * opts ] ) DESCRIPTION Optional hook to specifiy how to perform a single telnet negotiation. Hook setting may be any closure or a string. If not set, most telnet options are rejected (read: only a very minimal negotiation takes place). The hook is called whenever the driver receives a demand for option negotiation for: SB: Suboption negotiation TELOPT_LINEMODE: linemode TELOPT_NAWS: window size TELOPT_TTYPE: terminal type TELOPT_TM: timing mark TELOPT_NEWENV: remote environment variables TELOPT_ENVIRON: remote environment variables TELOPT_XDISPLOC: remote X display address TELOPT_TSPEED: terminal speed TELOPT_BINARY: binary data, needed for non-ASCII charsets TELOPT_EOR: TinyFugue prompt marker (together with EOR) TELOPT_COMPRESS: Mud Compression Protocol TELOPT_COMPRESS2: Mud Compression Protocol TELOPT_MSP: Mud Sound Protocol TELOPT_MXP: Mud Extension Protocol The hook has then to perform the negotiation using the efun binary_message(). Alternatively, if H_NOECHO is set, this hook is called for _all_ telnet data received. If the setting is a string, it used as name of an lfun to call in this_player(). Closures are just called, with unbound lambda-closures being bound to this_player() prior to execution. The hook is called for a 'DO/DONT/WILL/WONT <opt>' with the action (DO/DONT/...) as the first, and <opt> as the second argument. For example:, if the driver receives the sequence IAC SB <opt> <opts>... followed by IAC SB/SE, the hook is called with 'SB' as first argument, <opt> as second, and <opts> as an array of integers as third argument. HISTORY SEE ALSO hooks(C), telnet(C), no_echo(H)

docs.title: varargs void add_living_thorns(int iRatio, string sMessage,int ibDamType)
docs.text: varargs void add_living_thorns(int iRatio, string sMessage,int ibDamType) This function will return damage to the Living's attacker. iRatio is the sp:dam ratio, where the cost is dam / ratio in sp. The default ratio is 2. sMessage is the message told to the Living. It is in room_message format. "$N1 $v1hurt $r1 on $p thorns." is the default. ibDamType is the damage type that is returned. The default is WEAPON_PIERCE. The damage is not reduced by AC, but is reduced by resists. eg. living->add_living_thorns(); That would put everything in as the defaults. eg. living->add_living_thorns(4); That would make it 1 sp for every 4 damage, with the rest being the defaults. eg. living->add_living_thorns(0,0,DAM_ACID); That would give the default ratio and message, but use DAM_ACID as the damage type. Also: status query_living_thorns() returns 0/1 if living_thorns is active int query_living_thorns_ratio() returns the ratio set int query_living_thorns_damtype() returns the damage type set string query_living_thorns_message() returns the message set

docs.title: void add_money(m)
docs.text: void add_money(m) int m; Objects that can pick up the special "money" object, should have this function. It will be called with the amount of gold coins.

docs.title: NAME
docs.text: NAME add_shield SYNOPSIS void add_shield(int iAmount) void add_shield(int iAmount, int iType) void add_shield(int iAmount, int iType, closure cDepleted) DESCRIPTION Increase a living creature/player's shield for damage iAmount is the amount of damage being added to the shield [Required] iType is an optional parameter (bitmask) specifying the type of damage the shield will block/absorb. If not specified, this shield will block all types of damage. May be useful to check <types.h> cDepleted optionally supplies a depletion callback and acts as the stable handle for the shield points it owns. Callback-owned points absorb before unowned points in the same shield pool. When those points reach zero, the closure is called with the protected living and damage type: funcall(cDepleted, protected_living, iType) The caller must retain and reuse the exact same closure for later top-ups, queries, and cleanup. Existing one- and two-argument callers remain unowned and retain their previous behavior. add_shield() is defined in /secure/living.c SEE ALSO set_shield(L), query_shield(L), query_shield_callback(L), clear_shield_callback(L), remove_shield(L)

docs.title: int add_weight(w)
docs.text: int add_weight(w) int w; An object that can contain other objects must define this function. It is called with the extra weight of the new object. If this is ok, then it has to increment the local weight count, and return true. Otherwise, return false, and the new object can not be entered into this object.

docs.title: varargs status apply_status_effect(int effect, int strength, int duration,
docs.text: varargs status apply_status_effect(int effect, int strength, int duration, object source, status silent) Apply one living-owned status effect from <status_effects.h>. effect must be one exact STATUS_* bit. duration is in seconds; Burning ignores duration and derives its lifetime from strength. source may be 0. Set silent when refreshing or transforming an effect without application messages. State and GMCP still update. Named wrappers are preferred: apply_burning(int stacks, object source, status silent) apply_bleeding(int strength, int duration, object source, status silent) apply_chilled(int duration, object source, status silent) apply_freezing(int duration, object source, status silent) apply_exposed(int duration, object source, status silent) apply_sundered(int strength, int duration, object source, status silent) Use query_status_effect(mask), query_status_effect_strength(effect), query_status_effect_remaining(effect), query_status_effect_source(effect), and remove_status_effect(mask, silent) to inspect or cure effects. See `wizhelp 9.16` for stacking, caps, and lifecycle.

docs.title: void attacked_by(ob)
docs.text: void attacked_by(ob) object ob; This routine is called by the object attacking this object. Define it if this object wants to know who the attacker is.

docs.title: int can_put_and_get(str)
docs.text: int can_put_and_get(str) string str; Define this function if you want to make it possible to put something into current object. Return true if ok, otherwise 0. That means that default is that it is not possible to put something into an object. When a player does "look at xxx", then "xxx" will be sent to can_put_and_get(), to test if the player can look at the inventory. Otherwise, 'str' will be 0. This is trivial for containers. If the are open, they return 1. If id() accepts other things, like "lock" (in a chest for example). Then "lock" will be sent to can_put_and_get(), which should return false, because the lock has no inventory (of course). See also lfun/id(), lfun/long().

docs.title: When tell_object() sends a message to a noninteractive player,
docs.text: When tell_object() sends a message to a noninteractive player, it will get to the function catch_tell(string). This will enable communications between NPC's and from a player to an NPC. The only exception is shout, which the monster won't hear. The monster must be living, that is, call enable_commands(). See also efun/enable_commands()

docs.title: NAME
docs.text: NAME clear_shield_callback SYNOPSIS int clear_shield_callback(closure cDepleted) int clear_shield_callback(closure cDepleted, int iType) DESCRIPTION Removes and returns the shield points owned by the exact cDepleted closure in the generic pool or optional damage-type pool. This is explicit cleanup, so it does not invoke the callback. The same retained closure passed to add_shield() must be used. clear_shield_callback() is defined in /secure/living.c SEE ALSO add_shield(L), query_shield_callback(L), remove_shield(L)

docs.title: int drop(silently)
docs.text: int drop(silently) int silently; This function must be defined by all objects that want to control when they can be dropped. if 'silently' is true, then don't write any messages. drop() should return 1 to prevent dropping. This is the opposit of the get() function. That is because if drop() is not defined, it will always be possible to drop an object. If the object self-destructs when drop() is called, be sure to return 1, as the destructed item surely not can be dropped. Similarly, if drop() is called in another object, always test if the object did self-destruct, as the object variable will turn to 0.

docs.title: exit(): The opposite of init. Called when someone leaves the room.
docs.text: exit(): The opposite of init. Called when someone leaves the room. Be very careful when using this function. If there is an error in it, the occupants of the room can't quit, die, leave the room or perform anything that involves them or anything moving out of the room. And if this should happend to you despite this warning (which it most problably will, *sigh*) DON'T call for help. Anyone who enters the room will only get stuck as well. The only thing you can do is hope for a reboot of the game within the near future :) . void exit(ob) object ob; This function is called in rooms everytime a living object 'ob' leaves. The function this_player() will return a random value, don't use it at this point. See also: lfun/init

docs.title: string extra_look()
docs.text: string extra_look() If this function returns a string, and the object is carried by a player, then the string returned by this function will be printed after the character data, but before the list of what the character is carrying. This can be used to introduce curses for players, that gives some visual result. See also lfun/short(), lfun/query_auto_load().

docs.title: int get(str)
docs.text: int get(str) string str; If an object wants control over when it is possible to pick it up, then it must define get(), and return 1 if ok to pick up. The "str" is comes from "get str" from the player command. id() has been called before this to identify the object.

docs.title: void heal_self(h)
docs.text: void heal_self(h) int h; This routine is called when the object is allowed to heal by 'h' points. Of course, this is only interesting for living objects.

docs.title: void heart_beat()
docs.text: void heart_beat() This function will be called automatically every 2 seconds. The start and stop of heart beat is controlled by set_heart_beat(). Be careful not to have objects with heart beat running all the time, is it uses a lot of resources. If there is an error in the heart beat routine, the heart beat will be turned off until this object is recompiled, and can not be restarted with set_heart_beat. The function this_player() will return this object, but only if it is living. Otherwise, this_player() will return 0. See also: efun/set_heart_beat efun/call_out efun/enable_commands

docs.title: int hit_player(dam)
docs.text: int hit_player(dam) int dam; If the object can fight and get hit by other objects, it must have a hit_player function. The "dam" is the maximum damage the other object wants to give. Return the actual damage. This function should also tell other players in the current room that someone got hit (using say()). See example in player.c. See also efun/enable_commands, efun/living, lfun/attacked_by.

docs.title: int id(str)
docs.text: int id(str) string str; This function is used to identify an object. If it identifies with the string "str", then return 1, else 0. See also lfun/long(), lfun/can_put_and_get().

docs.title: void init()
docs.text: void init() This function is called everytime a living objects can "see" the object. It is good to the set up of add_action() and add_verb() in the init() routine. See also lfun/exit

docs.title: void long(str)
docs.text: void long(str) string str; This function prints out a elaborate description of it self. Minimum requirement is to print the value of short(). If there is an argument, then print description of that argument. An argument can only be passed to long() if id() has agreed. For example, a room with a door can allow id("door") to be true. Then it is possible to do "look at door". The long command will then have to print info about the door. To prevent the listing of all things in this room when "look at door", let can_put_and_get("door") return false. See also lfun/short(), lfun/can_put_and_get(), lfun/id().

docs.title: varargs make_and_equip(string sFile, int iHowMany)
docs.text: varargs make_and_equip(string sFile, int iHowMany) An lfun defined for monsters. Clones iHowMany objects into the monster using make_obj and then proceeds to have the monster equip each object. iHowMany is optional and defaults to 1 when not specified. Keep in mind that most monsters cannot equip two of the same type of item, so iHowMany is typically unneeded most of the time. Dual-wielding monsters, however, are one case when such would be useful. Example: make_and_equip("/obj/sword"); make_and_equip("/obj/helm"); make_and_equip("/obj/plate"); See also: make_obj, make_limited_and_equip, make_unique_and_equip

docs.title: make_limited_and_equip(string sFile, int iLimit)
docs.text: make_limited_and_equip(string sFile, int iLimit) An lfun defined for monsters. Clones an object into the monster using make_limited_obj with the limit iLimit and then proceeds to have the monster equip the object. See make_limited_obj for more details about limited objects. Note: Like make_limited_obj, this lfun returns 0 when it cannot create a new clone. Useful for cloning non-limited items on failure. Example: make_limited_and_equip("/obj/sword",4); if(!make_limited_and_equip("/obj/platemail", 5)) make_and_equip("/obj/leather"); See also: make_limited_obj, make_and_equip, make_unique_and_equip

docs.title: make_limited_obj(string sFile, int iLimit)
docs.text: make_limited_obj(string sFile, int iLimit) An lfun defined for all objects inheriting CLONE, which includes rooms and monsters. Attempts to create a limited-instance object and move it to the calling object. Won't create an object if doing so would result in more objects in-game than specific by iLimit. Of course, this limit only counts objects that have been created through previous calls to make_limited_obj or clone_limited_object. Note: make_limited_obj returns 0 if the clone is unsuccessful. Example: if(!make_limited_obj("/obj/exceptional_sword", 4)) make_obj("/obj/regular_sword"); See also: make_limited_and_equip, make_obj, make_unique_obj, clone_limited_object

docs.title: varargs make_obj(string sFile, int iHowMany)
docs.text: varargs make_obj(string sFile, int iHowMany) An lfun defined for all objects inheriting CLONE, which includes rooms and monsters. Clones up to iHowMany objects into the calling object, making sure to count how many objects are already cloned as to not exceed iHowMany. iHowMany is optional. When not specificied, it will default to 1. Example: make_obj("/obj/goblin", 4); make_obj("/obj/wolf"); See also: make_and_equip, make_limited_obj, make_unique_obj, clone_object

docs.title: make_unique_and_equip(string sFile)
docs.text: make_unique_and_equip(string sFile) An lfun defined for monsters. Clones an unique object into the monster using make_unique_obj and then proceeds to have the monster equip the object. See make_unique_obj for more details about unique object cloning. Note: Like make_unique_obj, this lfun returns 0 when it cannot create a new clone. Useful for cloning non-unique items on failure. Example: if(!make_unique_and_equip("/obj/uniq_sword")) make_and_equip("/obj/regular_sword"); See also: make_unique_obj, make_and_equip, make_limited_and_equip

docs.title: make_unique_obj(string sFile)
docs.text: make_unique_obj(string sFile) An lfun defined for all objects inheriting CLONE, which includes rooms and monsters. Attempts to create a unique object and move it to the calling object. Won't create an object if the object has already been created through make_unique_obj or clone_unique_object previously and such object is still in-game. Note: make_unique_obj returns 0 if the clone is unsuccessful. Example: if(!make_unique_obj("/obj/uniq_sword")) make_obj("/obj/regular_sword"); See also: make_unique_and_equip, make_obj, make_limited_obj, clone_unique_object

docs.title: This function is messed up enough that it needs its own documentation.
docs.text: This function is messed up enough that it needs its own documentation. nomask varargs void move_player(string sDirDest, string sDest, string sArrive) OK, sDirDest can be one of several things: 1) direction#destinationFileName 2) direction only, if sDest has the filename 3) !msgout#destinationFileName 4) !msgout only, if sDest has the filename But, it gets better. If 1) or 2), then the message printed to the room being left is query_msgout... UNLESS 'direction' is 'X', in which case it uses query_mmsgout. If 3) or 4), the the message is the msgout portion of sDirDest. In any case, if the direction isn't X and doesn't begin with !, it is substituted for $D in the entrance message. Now, on to sArrive. 1) direction 2) !msgin If the direction portion of sDirDest is 'X', then query_mmsgin is used as the entrance message to print to the room the person is arriving in. Otherwise, if sArrive is a direction, then the query_msgin message is used with sArrive being substituted into $D. If sArrive is missing, then the code figures out which exit in the current room leads back to the previous room, and that is substituted for $D. If sArrive begins with !, then all of the above is scrapped and sArrive is used for the incoming message. Does your head hurt now? Good. Just be glad you didn't have to rewrite the damned thing like I did, while still maintaining backwards compatibility. -mal 2002-03-26 The following is an example using messages for leaving and arriving in the new room. The ! strip out all min and mout messages that would have been included, so only the specified strings get sent to the room. this_player()->move_player("!"+this_player()->query_cap_name()+ \ " leaves through the 'Dionysus' door.", AREA_MYTHOS_ROOM_DIR+ \ "temple_1", "!"+this_player()->query_cap_name()+" steps out \ of the shadows.");

docs.title: object query_attack()
docs.text: object query_attack() All objects that can come under attack should define this function. It shall return the attacking object or 0.

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS int query_auto_load() DEFINED IN ob.c DESCRIPTION Returns the bit_flag on an object showing if it is an auto_load object or not. NOTE: This flag is automatically set on an object that is created from a players autoload list when they login. It is also set on an object that is passed to the function 'register_auto_obj' EXAMPLE // This example checks if an object 'hat' on the player is an // autoload or not, and if so tells the player object oObj = present("hat", this_player()); if (oObj->query_auto_load()) write("That hat is an autoloader!\n"); SEE ALSO register_auto_obj, remove_auto_obj, query_auto_obj, set_auto_load

docs.title: string query_gender_string()
docs.text: string query_gender_string() This function is defined by living monsters and players. It will return either "neuter", "male" or "female". There are other such query_functions, but they are not guaranteed to remain, so only use this one. See also: lfun/query_npc

docs.title: string query_info()
docs.text: string query_info() Declare this function if the object has some information that is hidden. A scroll of identify would call query_info() to find out. The standard objects weapon.c, armour.c and treasure.c all have a function set_info(), to enable setting an information string.

docs.title: int query_level()
docs.text: int query_level() All mobile (living) objects must define this. The lowest level is 1. An apprentice wizard have level 20, and a full wizard with a castle have level 21.

docs.title: int query_money()
docs.text: int query_money() Objects that can carry money, should define this function to return the amount of gold coins.

docs.title: string query_name()
docs.text: string query_name() All living objects, weapons and armour must return the name of itself. See also lfun/short().

docs.title: status query_no_increase()
docs.text: status query_no_increase() This function will disallow the Psionicist spell 'increase density' to be used on whatever object returns 1 for this function call. Usually used on very high AC items to keep it from getting out of hand when hardened.

docs.title: status query_no_reduce()
docs.text: status query_no_reduce() This function will disallow the Psionicist spell 'reduce weight' to be used on whatever object returns 1 for this function call. Usually used on items that you don't want the weight to be reduced for any reason.

docs.title: int query_npc()
docs.text: int query_npc() This function is defined by all living objects and monsters. It will return 1 for monsters, and 0 for players. NPC = Non Player Character. See also: lfun/query_gender_string

docs.title: mixed query_race_data(string)
docs.text: mixed query_race_data(string) Defined in players. The player's race data is queried for the racial attribute mapping entry. If that entry does not exist (or the player has an invalid race) the function returns 0.

docs.title: NAME
docs.text: NAME query_shield SYNOPSIS int query_shield() int query_shield(int iType) mapping query_shield(-1) DESCRIPTION Query a living creature/player's shield. Output changes based on argument passed. If no argument is passed (or 0 is passed), the player's generic shield amount is returned. This shield will block damage, regardless of damage type. If a valid damage type (see <types.h>) is passed, the specific shield amount is returned. This shield will only block that type of damage. If a value less than 0 or greater than ALL_DAM_TYPES is passed, a mapping in the form of <type>:<shield> is returned. query_shield() is defined in /secure/living.c SEE ALSO set_shield(L), add_shield(L), remove_shield(L)

docs.title: NAME
docs.text: NAME query_shield_callback SYNOPSIS int query_shield_callback(closure cDepleted) int query_shield_callback(closure cDepleted, int iType) DESCRIPTION Returns the shield points currently owned by the exact cDepleted closure in the generic pool or optional damage-type pool. It does not include unowned shield points or points owned by another callback. The same retained closure passed to add_shield() must be used. query_shield_callback() is defined in /secure/living.c SEE ALSO add_shield(L), clear_shield_callback(L), query_shield(L)

docs.title: object *query_targetable([int limit])
docs.text: object *query_targetable([int limit]) Returns living objects in the caller's current room that are generically valid hostile targets for the caller. The living layer excludes: - the caller - objects that are not living - targets rejected by can_kill() - dead or ghost targets - nohassle targets - the caller's party members - pets owned by the caller or a party member The optional limit bounds the returned array. It defaults to 100 and is always capped at 100. This function does not apply ability-specific rules. Commands must still filter for requirements such as hearing, visibility, race, terrain, range, or an existing combat relationship. pick_random_melee() uses query_targetable() and then applies its private random_melee_no_target exclusion before selecting one result.

docs.title: int query_value()
docs.text: int query_value() Return the value of this object. If it is not possible to sell this object, then the value 0 should be returned. One gold coin corresponds to one experience point, as a reference.

docs.title: int query_weight()
docs.text: int query_weight() This function is called to query the weight of this object. A design choise TAKEN, is that objects inside another objects, does not change the weight of that object. This makes it possible for a player to carry more if he puts it into a bag or something. Note that objects doesn't have a size, only weight.

docs.title: This directory describes functions that may or may not be declared in an
docs.text: This directory describes functions that may or may not be declared in an object. If they are declared, they will be called when apropriate. It might be important to declare some functions, so always check all of them.

docs.title: Receive Damage is the function that allows living creatures to take damage.
docs.text: Receive Damage is the function that allows living creatures to take damage. The function is defined as: varargs int receive_damage(int iAmount, int ibDamType, int iAbsorbFlag, object oFrom, status iNoExp, status tFromPlayer) iAmount is an int defining the amount of damage taken by the target. ibDamType defines the weapon type being used, defined in /secure/include/types.h iAbsorbFlag flags are defined in /secure/include/living.h #define AFLAG_APIERCE 1 #define AFLAG_ARMOR 2 #define AFLAG_ABSORB 3 #define AFLAG_ALL 4 *AFLAG_APIERCE will reduce the damage the living will absorb, but does not negate armor altogether. *AFLAG_ARMOR will increase the damage the living will absorb based on their AC. *AFLAG_ABSORB will bypass AC to determine damage. AFLAG_ALL will return the initial iAmount bypassing resists and AC. *Initial damage is first reduced by any damage resists. oFrom is the object giving the damage, or in the case of an object, should be the holding/wearing living. tNoExp is a 0 if the living gets experience for the damage, 1 if no exp is to be awarded the player. tFromPlayer should be 0 if it's an object/room/npc, or 1 if the damage is being done by another player. receive_damage() is defined in /secure/living.c

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS varargs void register_auto_obj(mixed xObj, string sParam) DEFINED IN player.c DESCRIPTION Adds an object to a players autoload list. '<xObj>' may be either a string containing the pathname to the object, or the object itself. An optional string '<sParam>' can be passed to give starting parameters for the autoloading object when it is created on player login. NOTE: '<sParam>' really only needs to be passed if '<xObj>' is passed as an object. If '<xObj>' is passed as a string, the starting parameters can be added by simply putting ':<parameters>' on the end of the string. When a player logs in, everything in their autoload list will be cloned and have the function 'init_arg' called in them with whatever starting parameters are supplied. EXAMPLE // This first example will add an autoload by using a string path // and an initial starting parameter of "justloading" this_player()->register_auto_obj("/objects/hat:justloading"); // This second example will add an autoload by using an object // and an initial starting parameter of "justloading" object oHat = clone_object("/objects/hat"); this_player()->register_auto_obj(oHat, "justloading"); SEE ALSO init_arg, remove_auto_obj, query_auto_obj, query_auto_load, set_auto_load

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS status remove_armour(int ibFlags) DEFINED IN armour.c DESCRIPTION Attempts to remove a piece of armour from a living. Returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. The passed flags can be used to bypass failure checks and otherwise modify removal behavior. See armour.h for macros to use as flags. EXAMPLE remove_armour(A_REMOVE_IGNORE_COMMAND_COSTS|A_REMOVE_SILENT) will silently remove armour without checking to see if the wearer has enough command points remaining.

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS void remove_auto_obj(mixed xObj) DEFINED IN player.c DESCRIPTION Removes an object from a players autoload list. '<xObj>' may be either the string entry in the autoload list in the form 'path:load parameters' or the object itself that is to be removed. EXAMPLE // This first example will remove an autoload by using a string path // with an initial starting parameter of "justloading" this_player()->remove_auto_obj("/objects/hat:justloading"); // This second example will remove an autoload by using an object object oHat = clone_object("/objects/hat"); this_player()->remove_auto_obj(oHat); SEE ALSO init_arg, register_auto_obj, query_auto_obj, query_auto_load, set_auto_load

docs.title: NAME
docs.text: NAME remove_shield SYNOPSIS void remove_shield(int iAmount) void remove_shield(int iAmount, int iType) DESCRIPTION Decrease a living creature/player's shield for damage iAmount is the amount of damage being removed from the shield [Required] NOTE: there is no such thing as a negative shield. A shield with value less than 0 ceases to function as a shield. iType is an optional parameter (bitmask) specifying the type of damage the shield will block/absorb. If not specified, this shield will block all types of damage. May be useful to check <types.h> remove_shield() is defined in /secure/living.c SEE ALSO set_shield(L), query_shield(L), remove_shield(L)

docs.title: void reset(flag)
docs.text: void reset(flag) Reset is called everytime the object is resetted. The first time is when the object is loaded. If a room creates things when reset(), it should check that these objects has moved out before creating new. When reset is called for the first time, a null argument is passed. The second time reset is called, flag will have vaule 1. Every object will repetedly get resetted by a daemon. The game wouldn't be fun if no challenges remained.

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS void set_auto_load(int iArg) DEFINED IN ob.c DESCRIPTION Sets the bit_flag on an object to '<iArg>' showing it as either an auto_load object or not. NOTE: This flag is automatically set on an object that is created from a players autoload list when they login. It is also set on an object that is passed to the function 'register_auto_obj' EXAMPLE // This example flags the object as an auto_load object object oObj = clone("/objects/hat"); oObj->set_auto_load(1); SEE ALSO register_auto_obj, remove_auto_obj, query_auto_obj, query_auto_load

docs.title: void set_heartbeat_function(string sEffectID, int iTicks,
docs.text: void set_heartbeat_function(string sEffectID, int iTicks, status tReverse, mixed xTickMessage, mixed xEndMessage, string sFunction, mixed *axVariables, int iNoTick) sEffectID - this should be a unique ID. it does a check -- on that ID, and fails if it's already in use. iTicks - how many heartbeat ticks will it go for. tReverse - reverse whatever arg you called onto the player. -- this means the value is only set at the start, and removed -- at the end, and not every tick. xTickMessage - will give a room_message(({TO}),ENV(TO), -- sTickMessage) each tick. if you don't wish to have a message, -- you need to put in a 0. xEndMessage - will give a room_message(({TO}),ENV(TO), -- xEndMessage) at the last tick. if you don't wish to have -- a message, you need to put in a 0. sFunction - the function that will be called on TO. -- Examples: "add_con", "receive_damage" -- To dispatch to an object carried by TO, use "call_inventory_lfun" and -- pass ({ object ID, function name, ({ persistent arguments }) }). The -- carried object's function receives TO as its first argument. This avoids -- saving an object reference in the heartbeat effect. axVariables - the args that will get passed to the sFunction. -- Examples: ({ -10 }),({10,WEAPON_PIERCE,0,TP}) iNoTick - if set to 1, the function will only be called at the -- the start, and not every tick and end. if set to 0, the function -- will be called every tick, unless tReverse is also set. if set -- to -1, the function will only be called on the last tick, and -- not at the start or every tick. if set to 1 or -1, tReverse -- should never be set, as they are contradictory. The room_message for the messages will only use the target object for the messages, and not the object instigating the action. That is why it doesn't have a start message, that would still be done in a guild command, room, object, etc. The functions that can make use of tReverse are the simple functions where you only set and remove single args. For functions that require more args, you would make use of iNoTick, and make 2 unique calls with opposite values. Example calls: oTarget->set_heartbeat_function("thomas_test",15,1,"$N $vfeel\ weaker.","$N $vfeel better.","add_con",({-10}),0); oTarget->set_heartbeat_function("thomas_test_dot",15,0,"$N $vare\ wracked by pain!","$N $vare no longer wracked by pain.", "receive_damage",({100,DAM_MAGIC,0,TP}),0); Example calls using iNoTick: oTarget->set_heartbeat_function("thomas_MR_start",30,0,0,0, "add_natural_resistance",({ DAM_MAGIC, 10 }),1); oTarget->set_heartbeat_function("thomas_MR_end",30,0,0, "$N $vare no longer protected against magic!", "add_natural_resistance",({ DAM_MAGIC, -10 }),-1); Example calling a carried object without persisting that object: oTarget->set_heartbeat_function("example_inventory_tick",15,0,0,0, "call_inventory_lfun", ({ "example_soul", "effect_tick", ({ 10, "source" }) }),0); // Calls example_soul->effect_tick(oTarget, 10, "source"). mapping query_heartbeat_functions() will return the mapping so you can check for unique IDs. int check_heartbeat_function(string sEffectID) will check if the "sEffectID" is an active heartbeat function on the living object. Returns 0 if it is not present, 1 if it is. void clear_heartbeat_function(string sEffectID) This function will try and clear the heartbeat function. It will change the ticks to 0, and end the function, doing whatever the function would have done. If you have multiple functions like a _start and _end, you should clear them all at the same time. If a player logs off while the function is running, it will pick up the ticks from where it left off, while applying the args again as if it had just started. Therefor, make sure that any args you set on a player are ones that clear when a player logs off, like add_<stat>, add_natural_resistance, etc. If you are not sure, test it :) To register an effect as a *debuff* (visible in the player's `buffs` list but not removable via `clearbuff`), add an entry to GLOBAL_DEBUFF_MAPPING in secure/include/buffs.h. Effects not in either mapping remain invisible to the `buffs` UI but still tick down normally. Do not use heartbeat callbacks to implement Burning, Bleeding, Chilled, Freezing, or Exposed. Those are living-owned status effects; use the apply_status_effect() API documented by `funhelp apply_status_effect` and `wizhelp 9.16`.

docs.title: NAME
docs.text: NAME set_shield SYNOPSIS void set_shield(int iAmount) void set_shield(int iAmount, int iType) DESCRIPTION Set a living creature/player's shield for damage iAmount is the amount of damage the shield will absorb or block [Required] iType is an optional parameter (damage type) specifying the type of damage the shield will block/absorb. If not specified, this is set the generic shield. May be useful to check <types.h> set_shield() is defined in /secure/living.c SEE ALSO add_shield(L), query_shield(L), remove_shield(L)

docs.title: void set_standard_block(int ibBlock, int iTicks, string sEffectId,
docs.text: void set_standard_block(int ibBlock, int iTicks, string sEffectId, string sStart, string sStop) An lfun that will set the standard blocks we use on the mud. See /open/INCLUDE/blocks.h for the list. You must #include <blocks.h> when using set_standard_block. ibBlock is the block or blocks you are setting (eg BLK_BLIND|BLK_PARALYZE). iTicks is the number of seconds the block will be set (the function will round up to the next multiple of 2). sEffectId is the unique name of your effect. Without a unique name, you run the risk of the default id being overwritten by other effects without names as well. sStart and sStop are messages relayed to the object having the block set, and to the room. If the string doesn't end with \n, the function will add it. If either/both are not set, the function will use the default messages (eg. You have been blinded. / You are no longer blind.). Example: oTarget->set_standard_block(BLK_PARALYZE|BLK_BLIND, 2, "test_block_id","$N $vpoke $no in the eye, before throwing \ out $p back.","$N $vrecover from $p self-inflicted ordeal."); ** Note: if you have more than one block set, sStop will be used for each block.

docs.title: string short()
docs.text: string short() All objects must have a short() function. This function returns a short message describing what it is. Invisible object will return the value 0. See also: long().

docs.title: void show_stats()
docs.text: void show_stats() Living objects should define this function. It should print all important stats about the object.

docs.title: stop_fight()
docs.text: stop_fight() Defined by all monster and player objects. If you call this function, that player or monster will stop fighting. If you want to stop a fight, you have to call stop_fight() in both opponents.

docs.title: void stop_wielding()
docs.text: void stop_wielding() Objects able to wield weapons, should have this function. It is called by the weapon when it is not possible to continue wielding the weapon. It should adjust the weapon class of the current object.

docs.title: ! /usr/local/bin/gawk -f
Some notes concerning the Archangel Michael
docs.text: Some notes concerning the Archangel Michael For some time now I have endeavored to learn of the mystery of one of the Archangel Michael. For millenia, he had served Mitra with loyalty and zeal. Something happened, however, that turned him from the path of good. What event caused the change remains a mystery that I seek to unfold. Meanwhile, I have composed these notes to aid those brave adventurers who seek to convince Michael to return to the path of righteousness. I often wander the dungeons of the foreboding fortress and have been approached by many brave souls seeking a path to the evil plane where Archangel Michael, now an Ordainer, resides. This path I open willingly if provided with the component that triggers the Gate spell. However, I must interject a warning. Do not assail the Bastion Stair unless you are fully prepared to face the challenges that await you there. It is a plane of evil and death where demons rule the living. The power of a White Witch could aid you greatly there. Unfortunately, the only Witch of White known to me is poor Regina, who has lost many of her memories. Perhaps a way could be found to restore those memories. Indeed, I did locate a Sacred Grove of the Witches of White, but its location I dare not tell for to do so would compromise it to those who would destroy it. I myself traveled to the evil plane of the Bastion Stair several times. Each time, but the last, I was stymied by an immense wall of skulls that surrounded the Bastion Stair. On my last visit, I crossed the wall by a most unusual means. A small worm had unaccountedly climbed into the pocket of my vest. Where I had picked up the strange creature, I know not. When I took him from my pocket, however, he grew to enormous size and burrowed a path for me under the wall! There I stood. The Bastion Stair rose thousands of feet into the air before me. Demons walked the courtyard that surrounded the stair. Hiding myself with magic, I began to explore, making many notes. Now, as I sit in my study above the Scrollworks Scriptorium, I study these notes again and again. There is much horror at the Bastion Stair which my current melancholy does not permit to put to written word. Of this, however, I will say. Convincing the Ordainer who was the Archangel Michael to return to the fold of Mitra will not be easy. You must first seek out the Book of Pious Acts. This too, is not an easy task for the book is not whole. The simple binding and several of the pages are missing. Yet all, I believe, may be found in the vicinity of the Bastion Stair for such is the way of this magical tome. Once you have gained the book and found the binding and missing pages, you must assemble it and make it whole. What must be done with the book once it is assembled, however, you must learn for yourself, for my research could no uncover this mystery. Sir Lutra Canad of the Scribes of Nomikos

docs.title: Some Notes compiled by Donagal McBain of the House McBain of his
docs.text: Some Notes compiled by Donagal McBain of the House McBain of his learnings concerning the ancient armour of the King of Tmassah. I have come to know these armours as the Desert Leathers, of which there are five. A fine helm formed into the shape of a dragon's head; A coat emblazoned with the figure of a rearing dragon; A pair of gauntlets of which I have learned little; A pair of rigid greaves; and A fine pair of comfortable boots. I have learned that it is not enough to simply possess all five of these ancient armours. Ney, the priests and priestesses of the Symbayan people will not allow such power to fall into the hands of those not worthy. Upon gathering the five pieces, one must seek out a priest or priestess to bless the items before they will gain their true power. In my wanderings throughout Souvrael, I have attempted to learn the whereabouts of the five pieces. I have been only partially successful. Of the Fine Leather Coat: Until very recently, the Coat of the King of Tmassah was a prize possession of the Desert Dwarves in northern Souvrael. However, the coat was stolen by marauding Thunes. Rumor has it that in their haste to return to their brethren, they vanished beneath the sands and were never seen again. Of the Dragon Helm: Research in the City of Souvrael has led me to believe that halm was once a prized posession of a power Sultan who often came to the city. On one trip, the henchmen of a powerful desert Lord ambushed the Sultan as he returned home and spirited the helm into the desert. Of the Supple Leather Boots: In the ancient ruins of ancient Tmassah I located an eldritch Suzerain Dragon. For the price of simple opal, she allowed me to converse with her for a time. I learned that the boots were given to her in trade long ago. Unfortunately, she couldn't remember where they had disappeared to, though she did remark she hadn't left South Souvrael for as long as she could remember. Of the Rigid Greaves: They were worn by a Symbayan warrior until but a short time ago when the warrior disappeared. He had been attempting to retrieve the rest of these powerful objects, but on one excursion into the desert, he was captured by a mysterious cult. Though he escaped, he was never able to tell his story, nor the whereabouts of the greaves as his tongue had been cut from his mouth and his fingers removed from his hands. Of the Supple Leather Gauntlets: The gauntlets were worn by the Sultan of Arabia, Shahriyar, for many years. On a hunting trip, he was separated from his guards and became lost in the desert. While trying to find his guards again, he removed the gauntlets and put them on the sand. While he drank from his waterskin, a strange creature grabbed the gauntlets and disappeared before he could stop it.

docs.title: In ages past, there existed a powerful weapon in the neverending
docs.text: In ages past, there existed a powerful weapon in the neverending battle against evil. This weapon was forged by the angels of Mitra so that it could be used by any champion who desired to combat evil, be that champion a mage, a warrior, a cleric or any other calling. There were those, however, that sought the destruction of this powerful weapon. Foremost among these was Thanatos, the Hater of Life. Through craft and force he wrested the rod away from mortal hands and cast it into the Mouth of Hell, a legendary volcano whose eruption is said to mark the beginning of Armageddon. If this is true, then Armageddon is upon us, for the volcano erupted seven days later. Lava and ash rained down throughout the world. So ended the Rod of the Seven Worlds. Or so the world thought for many centuries. Then, a piece of the rod was found by a simple peasant in the village of Glaverton in Glavia. Before more could be learned, however, Glaverton was over- run by demons and the piece was lost. Perhaps if the Glavia piece could be found, it might lead to the location of the remaining parts of the ancient artifact. Game Notes: There can only be one Rod of the Seven Worlds in existence at any one time. Before you begin a lengthy quest you would be well-advised to take some digging implements with you (perhaps a pick and shovel). Some gnomes have recently begun work on the foreboding fortress. Maybe one of them would be willing you loan you a shovel if you ask nicely.
