docs.title: Being level 20 signifies many things.  To some, it is the end of a long
docs.text: Being level 20 signifies many things. To some, it is the end of a long journey. To others, it is the beginning of a new adventure. Still others feel it is the gateway to wizship. But...if you are having fun playing, why leave the game? Thus, we at Darkwind are proud to present the Nobles System! At level 20, with 500 quest points and 50,000 gold, you can become a full fledged noble. You get a castle, plus the opportunity to increase your power by various means. Castles will not directly increase your power, though with certain additions, you will be able to have services that you and you alone possess. You can recruit others to your castle. If you have a large castle with lots of services, you may be able to charge a significant amount of money for each player in your service. You can attack other castles and steal their flags. You can build towns and raise armies to march against your enemies. Grow in financial and military power until you are ready to take on the King! Many surprises await those who join the Nobles system, though be warned: A player who joins the Nobles and enjoyes the advantages of being part of a Noble's house can be pk'ed at anytime, for any reason. You are safe in the castle, but nowhere else. Also be warned that this does not give you the right to pk non-noble players, unless they provoke the attack. We hope you enjoy the Nobles, and be sure to always keep your eye on new additions, and modifications.

docs.title: When a player reaches level 20, he has several options.  If he
docs.text: When a player reaches level 20, he has several options. If he has successfully completed all the quests, he may apply for wizardhood and become part of the coding team here at Darkwind. If he has a quest or 2 left, he can continue adventuring, gaining additional levels, until he finishes the quest at which point he can apply for wizardhood. If you have no desire to become a wizard but enjoy playing, you can continue advancing your levels all the way up to level 90. For those who don't want to wiz but also want more out of life, you can become a noble. Nobles are discused in more detail in chapter 14.

docs.title: Player Killing on Darkwind (or PK'ing).
docs.text: Player Killing on Darkwind (or PK'ing). This has to do with players killing other players here on the mud. It is allowed, but only among those that register for it. Be warned though that registering for PK is a one way street. Once you register for it you are stuck with it for the rest of your life. If you are killed repetedly and constantly for no other reason than you happen to be registered, then so be it, you will have to live with the consequences of your decision. Registering is not a decision to be taken lightly, so make sure you think it though thouroughly. What does registering do for you you might ask? First, it allows you to basically kill anyone else who is also registered as a PK'er. If someone wrongs you, you can kill them for it plain and simple (or at least attempt to). It also means that ANY other registered player can kill you any time the mood hits them, they don't need a reason other than they felt like it, even if they kill you 20 times in a row, or every time you log on for that matter. If you find yourself in a bad situation, dont come complaining to the admin, becasue you chose your fate. You need to try and find friends and alliances to help you out of your situation, or start over.

docs.title: RACES on DarkWind
docs.text: RACES on DarkWind There are ten races on DarkWind. They are: draconian, dwarf, elf, faerie, gnome, halfling, human, ogre, orc, and troll. Each of these races has inherent advantages as well as drawbacks that typify their racial attributes. Choosing a race is very different than choosing a guild. Races generally involve small-scale effects of encompassing aspects of your character. Guilds generally involve large scale abilities that are very specific in their use. Another note about races is that the good points and bad points of each tend to negate each other, so that you are no better or worse off choosing one over another, or choosing none at all (as in the times before the Gods of DarkWind saw fit to bestow variety upon the people of the realm). Most of what you will notice being a member of a specific race is that you have more natural aptitude at certain kinds of attributes. This is reflected in the varied cost for your stats. This is the most noticeable effect. There may be some other, very minor, talents or abilities, as well. Note that the "say" command on Darkwind does not speak in the common tongue, but in your own racial language. You can learn other races' languages, as well, so that other players' speech is more comprehensible than an unintelligible mumble.

docs.title: SHOPS and INNS in the realm of Darkwind
docs.text: SHOPS and INNS in the realm of Darkwind There are a variety of shops, inns, pubs, and stores in the city of Darkwind, to provide for your every adventuring need. In addition to the main shop, which you may be familiar with from your journeys in similar lands, there are several "specialty" stores that deal exclusively with certain types of items of specific interest. The shopkeep of the main general store is something of a miser and haggles shrewdly. Thus it will be to your benefit to explore Darkwind City and find the specialty shops, which buy at much better prices. Some stores, such as the town armoury, do not buy equipment, only sell. This is because no one really wants a used weapon that may break more easily, so only new weapons and armour are sold there. Likewise, you are probably familiar with the village pub. You will stop by there often, because the operator has a nearly exclusive license to sell alcohol in the realm. As alcohol is widely known for its curative properties, there is little doubt you will want to drink deeply and often. Adventuring is a rough life, after all. You may find alternative methods of healing, but they are somewhat more rare, and thus very valuable if you come across them. Darkwind has a small chapel in which amorous players may wed. Directly south of the church is a flower shop where you can purchase bouquets for the wedding, or just deliver flowers to your friends to express your affection. There is also a delivery service, next door to the post office. They will deliver almost any parcel, within certain restrictions. As a closing note, it should be said that just as in real life, the shops and inns of Darkwind fall prey to burglars and robbers occasionally and are thus forced to close for a period of time. They will open again when they have regained enough financial stability to do so. Although it is an inconvenience to mortals, the wizards of the realm have had little success in policing such larcenous activities.

docs.title: Weapon specialization has the ability to allow you to become very skilled
docs.text: Weapon specialization has the ability to allow you to become very skilled over time with a weapon type of your choice. As time progresses, if you stick to your weapon of choice you will begin to do more and more damage to your opponents with each blow. The downside to this of course is that weapons in which you are not specialized you will not do quite as much damage as a non-specialized person using the same weapon. Many people out there have chosen weapon specialization, so if you have additional questions, it shouldn't be too difficult to find someone to talk to.

docs.title: THEME OF DARKWIND
docs.text: THEME OF DARKWIND ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Darkwind's theme is one of medieval fantasy. A place where swords and sorcery meet to create an exciting but potentially lethal world for brave adventurers to make a name for themselves. You will not, nor ever will find things from themes such as Science Fiction, Cybperpunk, Comedy, Cartoons, Modern Day, etc. We are dedicated to providing a consistant environment where everything makes sense and blends well together. This rule will NEVER change, so if you would like to one day aspire to become a wizard here, be warned now. You will never be allowed to place anything that doesn't fit into this theme into the realm.

docs.title: Darkwind's Guide to New Adventurers
docs.text: Darkwind's Guide to New Adventurers ----------------------------------- Welcome to Darkwind. This edition of the Newbie Tome follows the same road as help guide: first steps, safe combat, exploration, guilds, the economy, community, and the long climb beyond level 100. A short tutorial starts automatically for new characters. In Darkflow it appears in a hover window; every client can use tutorial to review the current step and tutorial continue to continue. The tutorial teaches by doing, while this tome explains why those actions matter. Carry the tome and use: read tome Show the table of contents read introduction Read this page read chapter <number> checkout guilds List current guild checkout pages checkout <guild> Read about one guild The help system is always more detailed and easier to update than any book. Use help <topic>, help list, and help guide whenever you want the latest reference. The tome marks your reading progress as you go. More importantly, ask questions on the newbie channel. Darkwind is large, and nobody is expected to learn it alone. Segovia Loire High Sage of the Library of Telthar

docs.title: Chapter 1 - How do I MUD?
docs.text: Chapter 1 - How do I MUD? ----------------------------------- A MUD is a shared text world. Player characters explore it alongside non-player characters, creatures, objects, and other players. The place around you is called a room. Start with look, then examine interesting details with look <thing>. The room lists its available exits; move by typing the exit name or a standard direction such as north, south, east, west, up, or down. Common abbreviations such as l, n, and e work too. Useful first commands: inventory Show what you carry score Show your character and resources who Show connected players finger <player> Read public character information commands List commands available to you Speak in the room with say <message>, speak privately with tell <player> <message>, and ask the whole community with newbie <message>. If language causes confusion, use set language common. The help system accepts help <topic>. Use help list for its sections, help list <section> for every topic in one section, and help guide for a stage-by-stage path through the game. Before traveling, review set list. Helpful options include set autoexits on, set npcdetail on, and set itemdetail on. Use monitor bar for live health and spell points. Screenreader users should run set screenreader on. Read next: help tutorial, help basics, help movement, help set

docs.title: Chapter 10 - Money and Professions
docs.text: Chapter 10 - Money and Professions ----------------------------------- Keep spare coins in the bank. rembank or rembank balance opens an account on first use and reports its balance, liens, and spendable funds. Away from teleport-warded rooms: rembank deposit all rembank withdraw <amount> rembank lien rembank transfer <amount|all> from <registered alt> Bank liens secure auction bids and some purchases. Player markets let sellers set prices, while global item auctions handle valuable one-off goods. Read help market and help auction before listing or bidding. Darkwind has eleven professions. Herbalism, Mining, Skinning, Fishing, and Forestry gather resources. Alchemy, Leatherworking, Smithing, Tailoring, Cybernetics, and Carpentry turn materials into useful outputs. Refining is a profession service. The profession building is four east and one north of the Center of Town. Buy the right tools there, then use professions guide for a practical first route. Useful commands include: professions Review profession progress professions gathering Review gathering professions crafting Review crafting professions craftable Find things you can make professions check <type> <target> Check a recipe's requirements reagents <type> Review saved materials by type reagents search <item> Find material source hints workorders Review orders at the work-order board guildcraft list Review guild-themed recipes Professions reward patience. Gather, check what you have saved, compare recipe requirements, and use the market to trade with other specialists. Read next: help economy, help bank, help market, help auction, help professions, help workorders, help guildcraft

docs.title: Chapter 11 - Rules and Feedback
docs.text: Chapter 11 - Rules and Feedback ----------------------------------- help rules is the authoritative rules document. Read it in full. The essentials include: * Obey staff requests; raise concerns with a higher staff member after complying. * Report bugs and never exploit one. If something seems too good to be true, stop and ask. * Harassment, slurs, threats, and bypassing another player's ignore are not tolerated. * Use only the main character and additional characters permitted by the registered multichar system, and log in only one registered character at a time. * Unattended botting, automated killing, and automated keepalive activity are forbidden. * Do not steal another player's active kill, equipment, or money. * Player killing has additional rules; read help pk before participating. Use ignore <player> when you need distance. Use virginears on to enable the profanity filter; typing virginears by itself reports its current state. Good reports help improve the game: bug <description> Report a gameplay bug typo <description> Report a typo idea <description> Suggest an improvement clientbug <description> Report a Darkflow/client problem Include what you did, what you expected, what happened, and the room or object involved. Never keep using a suspected exploit while waiting for an answer. Read next: help rules, help bug, help feedback, help ignore, help virginears, help triggers, help multichars, help pk

docs.title: Chapter 12 - Parties and Community
docs.text: Chapter 12 - Parties and Community ----------------------------------- Parties hold two to six players. Members can coordinate on a private channel, share experience from kills, follow a leader, and optionally split gold. Use assist <player> to join the intended fight. Useful party commands: poffer <player> Start a party or invite someone pstatus Review members and status psay <message> Speak privately to the party pemote <message> Emote privately to the party pfollow on / pfollow off psplit <amount> Split coins once pautosplit on / pautosplit off pleader <player> Transfer leadership pname <name> Name the party pboot <player> Remove a member pleave Leave the party Parties are only one part of the community. Channels connect players across the game. Clans are player-run organizations; kingdoms have rulers, nobility, and shared projects. Patrons and deities add another path of alignment and devotion. Darkwind's Discord keeps the conversation going outside the game. Be clear about the destination, loot, quests, and retreats before a dangerous run. Keep quest spoilers off public channels, wait for disconnected members when possible, and ask before joining another player's fight. You have reached the end of the Newbie Tome, not the end of Darkwind. Return to help guide for the current eight-stage path and ask on the newbie channel whenever you need a hand. Read next: help party, help communication, help clans, help kingdoms, help patron, help deities, help discord, help guide

docs.title: Chapter 2 - Getting Started
docs.text: Chapter 2 - Getting Started ----------------------------------- The Center of Town is Darkwind City's main crossroads. If a new character becomes lost, ncot returns there. Pull the dispenser lever at the crossroads whenever you need another Newbie Tome. Erga's newbie store, four west and one south of the Center of Town, gives free equipment to characters through level 5. The donation room, five north and one east, holds equipment donated by veterans. Use get, wear, wield, and equip, then check the result with eq or myeq. The newbie farm is a safe place to practice looking, moving, fighting, and healing. Death has no penalty through level 5. Above level 5 it costs only 10 percent of the experience you currently hold: no stats or levels are lost, and your corpse travels safely with you to the church. Level at the Adventurers' Guild with advance. You can inspect stat costs from anywhere with remcost and buy normal advancement with remadvance <stat> or remadvance level. Guild advancement still follows the rules of the guild you choose. Non-remort characters may use set autolevel on, but leaving it off lets you bank experience for stat raises. Qualifying carried and equipped gear now saves when you leave the game. Donated, broken, unique, consumable, non-droppable, and specially restricted items may not save; items inside containers do not save merely because the container does. Chapter 7 explains equipment in more detail. Read next: help new, help equipment, help death, help leveling

docs.title: Chapter 3 - Combat
docs.text: Chapter 3 - Combat ---------------------------------------- Start a fight with kill <target>. Before attacking, use assess <target> for a rough comparison and read room descriptions for warnings. Some monsters are aggressive and attack as soon as you enter. Every combat round contains one or more independent swings. A swing may critically hit, hit, be dodged, be absorbed, or miss. Weapon size, speed, accuracy, your stats, training, armour, resistances, and guild or class abilities all matter. Watch your resources with monitor bar, mon, or .. Set wimpy <percent> to flee automatically at low health; you can also flee by moving through an exit. Use assist <player> to join a friend's fight without accidentally targeting the friend. New characters can use nheal, nbolt, nkick, npunch, and ncot through level 5. Their adventurer forms aheal, abolt, akick, apunch, and acot remain available from levels 6 through 49. Use combatbrief to control routine combat text. The short, self, hit, and damage options remain independent. combatbrief visual moves routine swings into Darkflow's Combat pane when that pane is ready; important warnings, ability results, fleeing, death, and rewards remain in the terminal. After combat, recover with rest, food, drink, potions, or guild abilities. Do not attack another player's target without permission: kill stealing is against the rules. Read next: help combat, help assess, help wimpy, help combatbrief, help death

docs.title: Chapter 4 - Worlds and Travel
docs.text: Chapter 4 - Worlds and Travel ----------------------------------- Darkwind spans multiple planets, worlds, regions, cities, wildernesses, and hidden places. The old habit of memorizing one fixed list of continents is no longer enough. Use areas to browse every cataloged public area by world and region. Use areas level <number> to find places near a level, areas search <word> to search names and tags, and areas info <number> to inspect a result. where identifies your current location. Wayshards are the main fast-travel network. Find one and touch shard to attune. Touch it again to view reachable destinations, then use travel <id> or travel <area>. Characters through level 10 automatically know the newbie-area shards. Travel is free, but has a 60-second interval, stays on the same planet, and is blocked during or shortly after combat. Moongates connect planets. Ferries, ships, guild travel, and other methods connect particular places. Read the local signs and use help moongates or help ferries before setting out. ncot is the safest return for new characters. Later, recall can return you to the Center of Town when teleportation is allowed, but it has a 15-minute cooldown. Read next: help areas, help wayshards, help moongates, help ferries, help recall

docs.title: Chapter 5 - Areas and Quests
docs.text: Chapter 5 - Areas and Quests ----------------------------------- The areas command replaces old handwritten lists of hunting grounds. It groups cataloged public areas by world and region and shows a rough level range. Try: areas Browse the full catalog areas level <number> Find areas near a level areas search <word> Search names, tags, worlds, and regions areas info <number> Inspect a result from the latest list Level ranges are guidance, not guarantees. An area may contain bosses, puzzles, unusual monsters, or creatures whose levels vary. Explore carefully, especially when the room description warns you. Many areas have a waysteward beside their wayshard or entrance. A bright yellow [?] means work is available. Use engage waysteward to review the suggested level, objectives, prerequisites, and rewards before accepting. You may accept multiple quests and all of them track automatically. myquests lists them; qstatus shows unfinished objectives. When every objective is complete, a bright yellow [!] appears above the waysteward. Engage that area's steward again to turn the quest in. Quest objectives can involve combat, items, rescues, or escorts. Ask friends for help when you need it, but keep quest solutions off public channels so other players can discover them for themselves. Read next: help areas, help quests, help quests commands, help quests objectives, help quests rewards

docs.title: Chapter 6 - Healing, Food and Drink
docs.text: Chapter 6 - Healing, Food and Drink ----------------------------------- Your hit points and spell points recover naturally when you stop fighting. Use sit while you wait in a safe room. Food, drink, potions, guild abilities, and other effects can restore resources faster. Pubs and inns sell healing fare. Read menu, use menu usable when it is available, then buy <number> or order <number>. An item may restore HP, SP, or both, and stronger fare is intended for stronger characters. Carry a few emergency supplies before leaving town, but remember that food and drink do not belong to the saved-gear system. Use buffs to review active buffs and debuffs. Read item descriptions before consuming anything: not every effect is beneficial, and some healing methods belong to a particular guild, class, or location. Corpses can also become a small source of income. An ash processor can provide a corpse burner. Carry it, use burn corpse after a fight, inspect its contents with check burner, and return to a processor to process all ash. set autoburn on automates the burn only after other corpse processing; anything left in the corpse is destroyed. At low health, retreat first and recover second. A meal is not a substitute for wimpy, an escape route, or help from another player. Read next: help effects, help buffs, help potions, help economy, help set, help death

docs.title: Chapter 7 - Equipment
docs.text: Chapter 7 - Equipment ----------------------------------- Characters can wear equipment on the head, body, legs, hands, feet, shield arm, cloak/body, shoulders, aura, two fingers, and two neck slots. Weapons occupy your hands according to their own rules. Race, size, guild, class, strength, curses, and scripted restrictions can all affect what fits. Use: eq or myeq Review equipped items equip <item> Equip an item in an appropriate slot wear <item> Wear armour wield <item> Wield a weapon gearcheck Compare carried and equipped gear gearcheck <item> Inspect one detailed comparison loadout Manage named equipment presets set itemdetail on adds raw weapon and armour ratings to item descriptions. Gearcheck considers protection, weapon class, stats, resistances, durability, known effects, and the slots an item would replace. Its result is advice; sidegrades can still suit a particular build. Equipment may also have an item level. This describes where it belongs in game progression and how ranked weapons and armour interact; it is not by itself a minimum character level. Read separately listed restrictions. Qualifying carried, worn, and wielded gear saves when you leave. Donated, broken, unique, consumable, non-droppable, and specially restricted gear may not save. Items inside containers do not save merely because the container does, and temporary equipment modifications are stripped on return. With a corpse burner carried, set autosell on transmits ordinary sellable NPC loot to Taylor. set autorefine on converts eligible ordinary NPC equipment into profession materials. They are mutually exclusive, and both permanently process items before autoloot, so leave them off while learning what drops. Read next: help equipment, help gearcheck, help loadout, help set, help refining, help professions

docs.title: Chapter 8 - Invasions and Events
docs.text: Chapter 8 - Invasions and Events ----------------------------------- Invasions are announced by Darkwind's Invasion Plan and Protection Siren, usually called DIPPS. Invaders can roam Darkwind City, attack players and residents, and damage shops until defenders win or the invasion succeeds. DIPPS announces the all-clear when it is safe. New and low-level characters should leave the city when an invasion begins. Do not assume the Center of Town, a shop, or an ordinary travel route is safe. Services may remain unavailable while damaged locations are repaired. Bosses are named encounters stronger and more rewarding than ordinary monsters. Many show a tier from T1 through T5; a higher tier usually means more health, pressure, mechanics, and reward expectations. Treat the tier as a clue, not a promise that your build is ready. Other long-term challenges include the Eternal Dungeon, the arena, achievements and achievement titles, daily rewards, and unique equipment. achievements reviews your progress, leaderboard shows the achievement leaders, daily checks the shared daily reward, and uniques explains one-copy items. At level 100, level gives way to renown as HERO, ADV, or VILN according to your deeds. Level 150 earns LEGEND status and another multichar slot. At level 250, remort trades your level for permanent boon points and begins the climb again. Specialization and the metaphysician path add further veteran progression. Events are easier and safer with other players. Read the event's help before joining, watch public announcements, and ask whether a party is forming. Read next: help invasions, help bosses, help eternal, help arena, help achievements, help daily, help uniques, help hero, help legend, help remort, help boons, help specialization, help meta

docs.title: Chapter 9 - Guilds and Classes
docs.text: Chapter 9 - Guilds and Classes ----------------------------------- Guilds are disciplines, organizations, faiths, and traditions your character learns. Classes describe what a character innately is. They are separate choices; use help guilds and help classes for the current rosters. Joining requirements, directions, advancement, equipment rules, and playstyles vary. Many guilds begin around level 5, but that is not a universal rule. Read the guild page, ask current members, and review help archetypes, help roles, and help combos before committing. Current open guilds: checkout bard Bard checkout berserker Berserker checkout cleric Cleric of Mitra checkout fighter Fighter checkout garou Garou checkout mage Mage checkout ninja Ninja checkout paladin Paladin checkout set Priest of Set checkout swashbuckler Swashbuckler checkout thief Thief checkout druid Druid checkout monk Monk checkout necro Necro checkout ranger Ranger checkout street samurai Street Samurai These paths are closed to new applicants, but their pages remain available for existing and returning characters: checkout bastet/gurahl Bastet/Gurahl checkout charlatan Charlatan checkout blood mage Blood Mage checkout deathknights Deathknights Use checkout guilds for this list at any time. At level 50, a character may learn a second compatible guild; the maximum is two. Read help dual guilds and help combos before choosing a pair. Read next: help guilds, help classes, help archetypes, help roles, help combos, help dual guilds

docs.title: Darkwind Newbie Tome
docs.text: Darkwind Newbie Tome Table of Contents ----------------------------------- Introduction Chapter 1 - How do I MUD? Chapter 2 - Getting Started Chapter 3 - Combat Chapter 4 - Worlds and Travel Chapter 5 - Areas and Quests Chapter 6 - Healing, Food and Drink Chapter 7 - Equipment Chapter 8 - Invasions and Events Chapter 9 - Guilds and Classes Chapter 10 - Money and Professions Chapter 11 - Rules and Feedback Chapter 12 - Parties and Community Use read tome for the live table of contents, read chapter <number> to open a chapter, and checkout guilds for the current guild checkout index.

docs.title: On Arms and Armour.
docs.text: On Arms and Armour. ------------------- First weapons. Since combat here is done differently than anywhere else, how weapons work also is done differently. A level 1 player with the most powerful non-magial weapon in the game will not do well here. Each weapon has a range that is most effective for certain levels. Low level player will do much better with lower power weapons than they will with a weapon that was not designed for them. Magical weapons of course can bend this rule, but even then a magic weapon designed for a high level player will not work well in the hands of a lower level player. This isn't to say that low level players only get wimpy weapons, it just means that players can get powerful weapons comparable to their level. If you're looking for a MUD where a new player can get his hands on the best weapon of the game and lay waste to everything, you wont find it here. Armour. Armour here, from a player standpoint, does much the same thing as it does on most other MUD's: It protects you from taking damage. The more and better armour you can find the less damage you will take. Keep in mind though that if your not very strong and you load yourself down with a lot of heavy armour, while you may not take as much damage in combat, you also will not be able to fight very well because of your over encumbrance.

docs.title: I guess we can start this chapter off by saying that wizardhood
docs.text: I guess we can start this chapter off by saying that wizardhood isn't a right, it's a privilege, although it's not a privilege that cannot be attained by anyone who is willing to follow a few simple rules. First-- to become a wizard you must be at a minimum level 20, and, you must have completed all the required quests. From a game mechanics standpoint that is all that is really required. From the people standpoint what we don't want in our wizards are people who: 1.Cheat This could be anything from players who find bugs and don't report them but use them to their advantage; players who are aware of loopholes in the security of the game and use them to either their benefit or the muds detrament. Minor infractions will result in a warning, but major infractions or repeated infractions will make the chances of ever becoming a wizard almost non-existant. 2.Foul-Mouthed *#@&*(^&% People who are unable to speak to others without insulting half the mud in the process or are unable to speak without swearing every other word are not people we want here, and certainly will never be granted the privilege of becoming a wizard. 3.Lazy people. Darkwind currently is a fairly new mud, and we would like to get more areas open. So if you don't plan on doing anything as a wizard we would prefer you stayed a player. And, in actuality, if it appears you are not doing anything on your own, you will most likely be given something to do. What do we want to see in our wizards? 1] basically the opposite of the traits listed above. Darkwind is currently a little on the light side of normal wizards, and if you are a motivated person who is able to do quality work, you will like being here. We are very liberal with our promotions and if you show us you like it here we want to do our best to make you happy here as well.

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS void add_verb(string str) DESCRIPTION This function is connected to the add_action() function. It will set up the command str to trigger a call to the function set up by the previous call to add_action(). This function is now obsolete as the verb can be given directly with add_action(). add_verb() remains for compatibility. [marion Sun Jan 19 1992 Don't use it. This file is retained because of somewhat nostalgic reasons.] HISTORY Removed in LDMud 3.3, obsoleted by add_action(). SEE ALSO add_action(E), query_verb(E), add_xverb(O), remove_action(E)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS void add_xverb(string str) DESCRIPTION This function is connected to the add_action() function. It will set up the command str to trigger a call to the function set up by the previous call to add_action(). add_xverb() differs from add_verb() in that only leading characters of the input line must match with str. It basically is the same as setting flag in add_action(). [marion Sun Jan 19 1992 Don't use it. This file is retained because of somewhat nostalgic reasons.] HISTORY Removed in LDMud 3.3, obsoleted by add_action(). SEE ALSO add_action(E), query_verb(E), add_verb(E)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS mapping allocate_mapping(int size, int width) DESCRIPTION Reserve memory for a mapping. size is the number of entries (i.e. keys) to reserve, width is the number of data items per entry. If the optional width is omitted, 1 is used as default. This is useful only when you are going to construct a mapping whose approximate size you know beforehand, to save on malloc overhead. If you don't fill in data for all the allocated elements, any leftovers will be freed after the current function execution ended. It is also useful if you want the mapping to have a certain width even if you don't provide all the data items for the keys yet. HISTORY Renamed to 'm_allocate()' in LDMud 3.2.6. Since LDMud 3.2.9, not available if driver is compiled without USE_DEPRECATED. Removed in LDMud 3.3. SEE ALSO mappings(LPC), walk_mapping(E), get_type_info(E)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS mapping copy_mapping(mapping) DESCRIPTION This efun is needed to create copies of mappings instead of just passing a reference, like adding/subtraction from a mapping do. HISTORY Superseeded by the copy() efun. Removed in LDMud 3.3. SEE ALSO mappings(LPC), copy(E)

docs.title: REMOVED MASTER APPLY
docs.text: REMOVED MASTER APPLY SYNOPSIS string creator_file(mixed ob) DESCRIPTION Return the name of the creator of a newly created object, i.e. the name of the user that is responsible for the LPC source file the object was loaded from. If the function returns 0, the object can't be loaded and is destructed again immediately. In !compat mode, the returned string serves as the initial uid (``cuid'') of the object. Objects whose cuid is the backbone-id will then get the uid of the currently active user as their userid instead. Under compat mode this function is called as well and provides the information returned by the creator() efun. If this function is not provided by the master object, no other object can be loaded. HISTORY Dropped in 3.2.1, replaced by the _UID driver hooks. SEE ALSO uids(C), creator(E), getuid(E)

docs.title: REMOVED MASTER APPLY
docs.text: REMOVED MASTER APPLY SYNOPSIS string *define_include_dirs(void) DESCRIPTION Return an array of string patterns giving the absolut paths where to search an include file. The patterns have to have a %s at the place where the name given in the #include statement has to be inserted. EXAMPLE define_include_dirs() { return ({ "sys/%s", "lib/%s" }); } HISTORY Dropped in 3.2.1, replaced by H_INCLUDE_DIRS hook. SEE ALSO master(M)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS void efun308(object item, object env) DESCRIPTION The item is moved into its new environment env, which may be 0. This efun is to be used in the move_object() hook, as it does nothing else than moving the item - no calls to init() or such. Don't use it in your own objects! HISTORY Introduced in 3.2.1@1, renamed to 'set_environment()' in LDMud 3.2.6. Since LDMud 3.2.9, not available if driver is compiled without USE_DEPRECATED. Removed in LDMud 3.3 . SEE ALSO remove(A), init(A), move_object(E), transfer(E), hooks(C), native(C)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS string extract(string str, int from, int to) string extract(string str, int from) DESCRIPTION Extract a substring from a string. This is the old notation for str[from..to] and supported only for hysterical raisins. DO NOT USE THIS EFUN ANYMORE. HISTORY Removed in LDMud 3.3. SEE ALSO [](E)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS string file_name() string file_name(object ob) DESCRIPTION Get the name of an object <ob> or, if no argument is given, of the current object. This name is the name under which the object is stored in the muds object table. It is initialised at the creation of the object such that blueprints are named after the file they are compiled from (without the trailing '.c'), and clones receive the name of their blueprint, extended by '#' followed by a unique non-negative number. These rules also apply to virtual objects - the real name/type of virtual objects is ignored. The name of an object can be changed with rename_object(), and object_name() will reflect any of these changes. The returned name always begins with '/' (absolute path), except when the parser runs in COMPAT mode. EXAMPLES find_object(file_name(ob)) == ob This is guaranteed to be true for all objects ob that are not destructed. HISTORY In LDMud 3.2.6 renamed to object_name(), this old name is available as alias. Since LDMud 3.2.9, not available if driver is compiled without USE_DEPRECATED. Removed in LDMud 3.3 . SEE ALSO clone_object(E), load_name(E), load_object(E), find_object(E), program_name(E), rename_object(E), object_name(E)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS mixed *filter_array(mixed *arr, string fun, string|object ob, mixed extra, ...) mixed *filter_array(mixed *arr, closure cl, mixed extra, ...) mixed *filter_array(mixed *arr, mapping map, mixed extra, ...) DESCRIPTION Returns an array holding the items of arr filtered through ob->fun(element, extra, ...), the closure cl, or the mapping map. The function 'fun' in 'ob' resp. the closure 'cl' is called for each element in arr with that element as parameter. The extra and following parameters are in each call if given. The mapping 'map' is likewise indexed by each element. If ob->fun(arr[index], extra) returns != 0 resp. map[arr[index]] exists, the element is included in the returned array. If arr is not an array, an error occurs. The extra argument(s) are optional and must not be protected references like &(i[0]). If <ob> is omitted, or neither a string nor an object, it defaults to this_object(). Since 3.2.1@36, the second arg can also be a mapping. Then only the elements of the array which belong to the map (as keys) will be returned (i.e. map[arr[index]] != 0). EXAMPLE int check_if_idle(object user) { return query_idle(user); } ... object *idle_users; idle_users = filter_array(users(), "check_if_idle"); /* equivalent but smaller and faster */ idle_users = filter_array(users(), #'query_idle ); Now idle_users contains all users that have been idle for more than 1 second. HISTORY Since LDMud 3.2.6 obsoleted by efun filter(). Since LDMud 3.2.9, not available if driver is compiled without USE_DEPRECATED. Removed in LDMud 3.3 . SEE ALSO filter(E), filter_objects(E), map(E), map_objects(E)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS mapping filter_mapping(mapping, string func, string|object ob, ...) mapping filter_mapping(mapping, closure cl, ...) DESCRIPTION ob->func() is called resp. cl applied to every element in the mapping, with first argument being the key of the element, and then the extra args that were given to filter_mapping (these args must not be protected references like &(i[0]). If the function returns true, the element is element, and then the extra args that were given to added to the result mapping. ob can also be a file_name of an object. If <ob> is omitted, or neither a string nor an object, it defaults to this_object(). HISTORY In LDMud 3.2.6 renamed to filter_indices(). Since LDMud 3.2.9, not available if driver is compiled without USE_DEPRECATED. Removed in LDMud 3.3. SEE ALSO filter(E), map(E), map_indices(E), walk_mapping(E), member(E), m_contains(E)

docs.title: REMOVED MASTER APPLY
docs.text: REMOVED MASTER APPLY SYNOPSIS string get_root_uid(void) DESCRIPTION Return the string to be used as root-uid. Under !native, the function is expendable. HISTORY In 3.2.1@40, get_root_uid() was renamed to get_master_uid() and recieved a new semantic. SEE ALSO get_bb_uid(M), get_master_uid(M), uids(C), creator_file(M), creator(E)

docs.title: OBSOLETE
docs.text: OBSOLETE CONCEPT VARIABLE INITIALIZATION DESCRIPTION There are two different flavours of initialisations, selectable in config.h : i) #undef INITIALIZATION_BY___INIT ------------------------------------ Initialisation is done at compile time. This is fast and costs no extra code in the program. Allowed expressions currently include integer literals, string literals, integer operators, string addition, bracketing, array constructors, the empty mapping and structs. When an object with initialised variables is cloned or inherited, all initialised variables are copied from the blueprint. A special application of this feature is to have an initialised non-empty array or a mapping; it will be shared by all clones or inheriting objects unless an assignment to the variable - as opposed to an assignment to an element of the array/mapping - is done in all clones etc. To prevent unauthorised changes in initialised arrays/mappings, you can declare the variables as private or use a nomask reset/create that checks for undesired inheritance. ii) #define INITIALIZATION_BY___INIT ------------------------------------- Creates a function names __INIT() from all variable initialisations and from calls to __INIT() in all inherited objects, and runs this function at object creation time. Any efun can be used in the expressions for variable initialisations, even ones with severe side effects, like destruct() or shutdown(). The code created for __INIT() is a little worse than a medium-skilled lpc-programmer would generate, because it is scattered all over the program. HISTORY Since LDMud 3.3, order_alist() is no longer accepted without INITIALIZATION_BY___INIT. LDMud 3.3.378 replaced this static choice of initialisation methods by compile-time pragmas.

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS int m_sizeof(mapping map) DESCRIPTION Returns the number of indices in mapping 'map'. This function is in fact an alias for sizeof(). HISTORY Since LDMud 3.2.9, not available if driver is compiled without USE_DEPRECATED. Removed in LDMud 3.3. SEE ALSO mappingp(E), mkmapping(E), m_indices(E), m_values(E), m_delete(E), sizeof(E), widthof(E).

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS mixed *map_array(mixed *arr, string fun, string|object ob, mixed extra) mixed *map_array(mixed *arr, closure cl, mixed extra) DESCRIPTION Returns an array holding the items of arr mapped through ob->fun(element, extra) resp. the closure cl. The function fun in ob is called for each element in arr with that element as parameter. A second parameter extra is sent in each call if given. ob can be an object or a string. Principal function: foreach (index) arr[index] = ob->fun(arr[index],extra); The value returned by ob->fun(array[index],extra) replaces the existing element in the array. If arr is not an array, then 0 will be returned. The extra argument is optional and must not be a protected reference like &(i[0]). If <ob> is omitted, or neither a string nor an object, it defaults to this_object(). EXAMPLE string ask_for_uid(object obj) { return getuid(obj); } void func() { string *names; names = map_array(users(), "ask_for_uid", this_object()); /* equivalent but a bit smaller and faster is the following */ names = map_array(users(), #'getuid ); ... } This will create an array holding all uids of the current users. HISTORY Since LDMud 3.2.6 obsoleted by map(). Since LDMud 3.2.9, not available if driver is compiled without USE_DEPRECATED. Removed in LDMud 3.3. SEE ALSO filter(E), filter_objects(E), assoc(E), intersect_alist(E), insert_alist(E), map(E), map_objects(E), member(E), order_alist(E), sort_array(E), unique_array(E)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS mapping map_mapping(mapping m, string func, string|object ob, ...) mapping map_mapping(mapping m, closure cl, ...) DESCRIPTION ob->func() is called resp. cl applied to every element in the mapping, with the key of the element as first argument, and then the extra args that were given to map_mapping (these args must not be protected references like &(i[0])). The data item in the mapping is replaced by the return value of the function. ob can also be a file_name of an object. If <ob> is omitted, or neither a string nor an object, it defaults to this_object(). Note that if mapping m has more than one value per key, these are ignored: the resulting mapping always has one value per key. Also note that the behaviour of this function is different from map_array(). EXAMPLE m = mkmapping(users()); m = map_mapping(m, #'environment); HISTORY In LDMud 3.2.6 renamed to map_indices(). Since LDMud 3.2.9, not available if driver is compiled without USE_DEPRECATED. Removed in LDMud 3.3. SEE ALSO map(E), filter(E), filter_indices(E), walk_mapping(E), member(E), m_contains(E)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS int mapping_contains(mixed &data1, ..., &dataN, map, key) DESCRIPTION If the mapping contains the key map, the corresponding values are assigned to the data arguments, which massed be passed by reference, and 1 is returned. If key is not in map, 0 is returned and the data args are left unchanged. It is possible to use this function for a 0-value mapping, in which case it has the same effect as member(E). HISTORY Renamed to 'm_contains()' in LDMud 3.2.6. Since LDMud 3.2.9, not available if driver is compiled without USE_DEPRECATED. Removed in LDMud 3.3. SEE ALSO mappings(LPC), member(E)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS int member_array(mixed item, mixed *arr) int member_array(mixed item, string arr) DESCRIPTION Returns the index of the first occurence of item in array arr, or occurence of a character in a string. If not found, then -1 is returned. If you want to search through an alist, use assoc() because member_array() is good for unsorted but assoc() is faster for sorted arrays. HISTORY Superseeded by member(). Removed in LDMud 3.3. SEE ALSO member(E), alists(LPC), mappings(LPC), assoc(E), slice_array(E)

docs.title: REMOVED MASTER APPLY
docs.text: REMOVED MASTER APPLY SYNOPSIS string object_name(object ob) DESCRIPTION Return a printable name for an object. This function is called by sprintf() to print a meaningful name in addition to the normal object_name(). HISTORY Renamed in LDMud 3.2.6 from printf_obj_name() due to the introduction of an efun with this name. SEE ALSO sprintf(E), printf_obj_name(M), object_name(E)

docs.title: NAME
docs.text: NAME obsolete DESCRIPTION This directory contains descriptions for features removed from the game driver, since they can come in handy when reworking old LPC code. SEE ALSO applied(A), efun(E), master(M), concepts(C), lpc(LPC), driver(D)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS Compat mode int parse_command (string cmd, object env, string fmt, mixed &var, ...) int parse_command (string cmd, object* arr, string fmt, mixed &var, ...) DESCRIPTION parse_command() is basically a spiffed up sscanf operating on word basis and targeted at recognizing object descriptions from command strings. The efun takes the command string <cmd> and the object(s) <env>/<arr> and tries to match it against the format string <fmt>. Successfully matched elements are assigned to the variables <var>.... The result from the efun is 1 if the command could be fully matched, and 0 otherwise. If the objects are given as a single object <env>, the efun matches against the given object and all objects contained therein. Otherwise, if the objects are given as an array <arr> of objects, the efun matches only against the given objects. If <env> is 0, environment(this_player()) is used as default. The format string <fmt> consists of words, syntactic markers, and %-directives for the values to parse and return in the variables. A typical example is " 'get' / 'take' %i " or " 'spray' / 'paint' [paint] %i ". The elements in detail are: 'word': obligatory text [word]: optional text / : Alternative marker %o : Single item, object %s : Any text %w : Any word %p : One of a list of prepositions. If the variable associated with %p is used to pass a list of words to the efun, the matching will take only against this list. %l : non-compat: Living objects compat: a single living object %i : Any objects %d : Number >= 0, or when given textual: 0-99. A <word> in this context is any sequence of characters not containing a space. 'living objects' are searched by calls to the (simul)efuns find_player() and find_living(): both functions have to accept a name as argument and return the object for this name, or 0 if there is none. The results assigned to the variables by the %-directives are: %o : returns an object %s : returns a string of words %w : returns a string of one word %p : if passed empty: a string if passed as array of words: var[0] is the matched word %i : returns an array with the following content: [0]: int: the count/number recognized in the object spec > 0: a count (e.g. 'three', '4') < 0: an ordinal (e.g. 'second', 'third') = 0: 'all' or a generic plural such as 'apples' [1..]: object: all(!) objects matching the item description. In the <env> form this may be the whole recursive inventory of the <env> object. It is up to the caller to interpret the recognized numeral and to apply it on the list of matched objects. %l : non-compat: as %i, except that only living objects are returned. compat: as %o, except that only a living object is returned. %i (and non-compat-%l) match descriptions like 'three red roses', 'all nasty bugs' or 'second blue sword'. Note: Patterns of type: "%s %w %i" might not work as one would expect. %w will always succeed so the arg corresponding to %s will always be empty. The implementation of parse_command() differs between compat mode and non-compat mode drivers mainly in how the efun retrieves the necessary information from the mudlib objects. DESCRIPTION -- compat mode To make the efun useful it must have a certain support from the mudlib: it calls a set of functions in objects to get the information it needs to parse a string. 1. int id (string txt) txt is an object name of the form "adj1 adj2 ... name". The function has to return non-zero if txt is a valid (singular) name for this particular object. 2. int plural_id (string txt) txt is an object name of the form "adj1 adj2 ... name". The function has to return non-zero if txt is a valid plural name for this particular object. 3. string adjectiv_id() When parsing commands like "get all red ones", the result from this function is used to construct the text passed to id(); in this example "red <adjectiv_id>". If this function doesn't exist, the last word from the result of short() is used instead. EXAMPLE object *items; parse_command( "take apple",environment(this_player()) , " 'get' / 'take' %i ",items); HISTORY LDMud 3.3.258 removed the compat-mode parse_command(). SEE ALSO sscanf(E)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS int query_imp_port(void) DESCRIPTION Returns the port number that is used for the inter mud protocol. HISTORY LDMud 3.2.9 renamed this efun to query_udp_mud(). This version is available if the driver is compiled with USE_DEPRECATED. Removed in LDMud 3.3. SEE ALSO send_udp(E), receive_udp(M)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS void receive_imp(string host, string msg, int hostport) DESCRIPTION Handle a received IMP message. This function is called for every message received on the IMP port. Usually it is passed on to some object that handles inter mud communications. The driver first calls receive_udp(). If that method doesn't exist and if the driver is compiled with USE_DEPRECATED, it will then call receive_imp(). HISTORY The 'hostport' argument was added in 3.2.1. LDMud 3.2.9 renamed this method from receive_imp(); this old version is supported if the driver is compiled with USE_DEPRECATED. Removed in LDMud 3.3. SEE ALSO send_udp(E), query_udp_port(E)

docs.title: OBSOLETE DOCUMENT
docs.text: OBSOLETE DOCUMENT RxCache - Regular Expression Cache ---------------------------------- Written 1998 by Lars Duening. Share and Enjoy!@ The rxcache acts as a wrapper around the regcomp() function in the regexp module. It keeps track of the recently compiled regular expression and stores both the expression string and regexp's internal representation. If an expression is found among the stored ones, the rxcache returns the stored internal representation compiled earlier. The interface is through the function regcomp_cache() which takes the same parameters as regcomp(). However, since the compiled expression is stored and managed by rxcache, the caller of regcomp_cache() must not deallocate the compiled expression after use. The expressions are stored in a fixed size table, with entries indexed by a hash over the pattern string. The table holds RXCACHE_TABLE entries, and every entry can hold RXCACHE_CHAIN expressions. Upon a hash collision, one of the stored expressions is removed (and deallocated) using a round-robin selection. This behaviour may not be optimal, but on the other hand eventually deallocates expressions which are no longer used. The two RXCACHE_ values are defined in config.h. Initial tests showed an acceleration of the regexp _setup_ phase by factor 4. However, since the actual matching is as fast as before, the net savings will be lower. To install the rxcache, apply the diff file (use parameter '-p1' with patch) and reconfigure and recompile the driver. -- Lars Duening; 17. Apr 1998 HISTORY Fully integrated into the driver with the 3.2 line.

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS int send_imp(string host, int port, string message) int send_imp(string host, int port, int * message) DESCRIPTION Sends The message in an UDP packet to the given host and port number. The message can be given either as string, or as array of bytes. The latter variant allows to send binary data as well. The efun causes a privilege violation. If USE_DEPRECATED is in effect, it first tries privilege violation ("send_imp"), and, if this one returns 0, then it tries privilege violation ("send_udp"). If USE_DEPRECATED is not in effect, it just tries privilege violation ("send_udp"). Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure. Note: On some machines a failed send_imp() will not be registered until the next send_imp() - the latter one might return '0' even if itself was successful. HISTORY LDMud 3.2.9 renamed this efun to send_udp(), and also changed the privilege violation string and the apply names. This old version is available if the driver is compiled with USE_DEPRECATED. Removed in LDMud 3.3. SEE ALSO query_udp_port(E), receive_udp(M), receive_imp(M)

docs.title: REMOVED EFUN
docs.text: REMOVED EFUN SYNOPSIS void set_auto_include_string (string arg) DESCRIPTION The arg will be automatically included into every compiled LPC object. This is useful to enforce global definitions, e.g. ``#pragma combine_strings'' or ``#pragma strict_types''. The calling object needs to be privileged by the master object. Note that the auto-include-string is cleared when the master object is reloaded. HISTORY LDMud 3.2.9 replaced this efun with driver hook H_AUTO_INCLUDE. This old version is available if the driver is compiled with USE_DEPRECATED. Removed in LDMud 3.3. SEE ALSO set_driver_hook(E), privilege_violation(M), pragma(LPC), master(M)

The Mud Client Compression Protocol - Specification - Version 2

  • 2000/05/30: Version 2: introduced COMPRESS2 to fix the missing IAC on the option subnegotiation sequence for COMPRESS.

This document describes version 2 of the protocol, using the COMPRESS2 option. An earlier version described a protocol using the COMPRESS option -- this is referred to as the version 1 protocol below.

The protocol used by mcclient is based on 'telnet' option negotiation. See RFCs 854 and 855 for an overview of the mechanism used.

Compression is currently unidirectional - only output from the mud server is compressed. This simplifies the implementation, and also avoids potential problems with hostile clients sending data intended to cause problems (via crashing or excessive memory/cpu use) with the decompressor. The compressor is entirely controlled by the server. While attacks on the client are potentially possible, this seems less of a problem as the client is not a shared resource.

Servers supporting version 2 (this version) of the protocol should indicate they support it by offering the COMPRESS2 option (number 86): IAC WILL COMPRESS2. They may also optionally offer the older version 1 option (number 85) to support older clients: IAC WILL COMPRESS. Servers should offer COMPRESS2 before COMPRESS to allow newer clients to support any extra features added to COMPRESS2 in the future while still supporting COMPRESS.

Clients should respond to the COMPRESS2 option with IAC DO COMPRESS2 if they want the server to enable compression. To support older servers, clients may respond to the COMPRESS option with IAC DO COMPRESS, although it is recommended that the COMPRESS option is refused with IAC DONT COMPRESS if COMPRESS2 has been previously offered by the server.

There is no requirement for either server or client to support the version 1 protocol.

Once either COMPRESS or COMPRESS2 is negotiated, the server may enable compression. Since the start point of the compression stream needs to be known, the server prefixes the start of the stream with a suboption negotiation packet. This is IAC SB COMPRESS WILL SE for the obsolete COMPRESS option (note that this is not a valid suboption negotiation sequence according to RFC854/855 -- the terminating SE isn't correctly escaped), or IAC SB COMPRESS2 IAC SE for the COMPRESS2 option.

Immediately following this, a zlib stream (as defined in RFC 1950 - see also the zlib home page) begins.

In summary, negotiation between server and client takes one of these forms: 

 version 1 server version 1 client IAC WILL COMPRESS IAC DO COMPRESS IAC SB COMPRESS WILL SE (compressed stream) version 2 server (supporting v1) version 1 client IAC WILL COMPRESS2 IAC WILL COMPRESS (nothing) or IAC DONT COMPRESS2 IAC DO COMPRESS IAC SB COMPRESS WILL SE (compressed stream) version 2 server (not supporting v1) version 1 client IAC WILL COMPRESS2 (nothing) or IAC DONT COMPRESS2 (uncompressed connection continues) version 1 server version 2 client (supporting v1) IAC WILL COMPRESS IAC DO COMPRESS IAC SB COMPRESS WILL SE (compressed stream) version 1 server version 2 client (not supporting v1) IAC WILL COMPRESS IAC DONT COMPRESS (uncompressed connection continues) version 2 server version 2 client IAC WILL COMPRESS2 IAC WILL COMPRESS IAC DO COMPRESS2 IAC DONT COMPRESS IAC SB COMPRESS2 IAC SE (compressed stream)

The compressed data should be transmitted unescaped. IAC should be sent as-is. Telnet option negotiation and IAC escaping continues as normal for the uncompressed data stream -- the entire telnet TCP stream is compressed, negotiation and all.

Compression can only be terminated by the server - a normal end to the compression stream is assumed to mean "revert to uncompressed mode". It may be desirable for the server to automatically terminate compression when an IAC DONT COMPRESS sequence is received from the client.

Any decompression errors are unrecoverable, and should result in a disconnection. Given that TCP is a reliable transport mechanism, bug-free implementations should never encounter compression errors, so this should not affect normal operation. When an error is encountered, something has gone badly wrong, and it seems hard to recover. Allowing raw (uncompressed) option negotiation to reset compression is one possibility, but would require that option negotiation take place outside the compressed stream.

 
Oliver Jowett <icecube@ihug.co.nz>, 2000/05/30
