To show that the only MXP tags supported by the client are the <B>, <I>, and <COLOR> tags.

To determine if a specific tag is supported, use it as the argument to the <SUPPORT> tag.  For example, to determine if the client supports the <IMAGE> tag, send <SUPPORT image> and the client will return <SUPPORTS +image> if the image tag is supported, or will return <SUPPORTS -image> if the tag is not supported.

You can query an entire list of tags at once by adding them to the tag.  For example, to query both the IMAGE tag and the FRAME tag, you can send <SUPPORT image frame> and the client would return <SUPPORT +image -frame> if it supported image but did not support frame.

You can also query the arguments of a tag.  For example, to determine the arguments for the <color> tag, use the syntax <SUPPORT "color.*">  The * asks for all arguments, and the client should send back: <SUPPORTS +color.fore +color.back> to indicate that the two arguments supported for the <color> tag are FORE and BACK.  To query a specific argument, replace * with the argument name.  For example: <SUPPORT color.fore> would return <SUPPORTS +color.fore>.

You can mix and match any of these in the list of arguments.  For example:

<SUPPORT "color.*" send.expire image>

might return: <SUPPORTS +color.fore +color.back -send.expire -image>

It is very important to implement the <SUPPORT> tag in your MUD server.  This is the only way to determine what tags are really supported by the client.  The MXP version number isn't enough information to determine this, and using <SUPPORT> is easier and better defined than trying to decide based upon what MUD client is being used.

Optional Tags

The tags given in this section may or may not be implemented by MXP clients.  Use the <SUPPORT> tag to determine if the client implements the tag.  In general, this section provides ideas for client developers interested in extending the MXP concepts, without describing tags that are required to be part of the implementation.

Other HTML tags

The following additional HTML tags might be supported within MXP:

<H1>    Level 1 heading
<H2>    Level 2 heading
<H3>    Level 3 heading
<H4>    Level 4 heading
<H5>    Level 5 heading
<H6>    Level 6 heading
<HR>    Horizontal rule
<SMALL>    Small text
<TT>    Non-proportional font

MSP Compatibility

For MSP Compatibility, the <SOUND> and <MUSIC> tags are available in MXP.   They have the same keyword syntax and the equivalent !!SOUND and !!MUSIC MSP tags.

Using Entities

The MUD can instruct the client to automatically create a graphical Gauge or Status Bar text from MXP entities.

<GAUGE EntityName [Max=EntityName] [Caption=text] [Color=color]>

Creates a graphical gauge.  The value of the first Entity is used as the gauge data.  The Max= argument specifies the name of the entity to use for the maximum value of the gauge.  The Caption= text is optionally displayed on the gauge by the client.  The Color gives the color of the gauge bar.

<STAT EntityName [Max=EntityName] [Caption=text]>

Creates a new Status Bar text on the client.  Text is appended to current status bar.  The value of the entity given by the first EntityName is displayed.  If the Max= argument is given and the entity named by the Max= argument is Published, then the client displays the text as nnn/mmm where nnn is the first entity value, and mmm is the Max entity value.

Frames

HTML allows you to define regions of your browser window called frames and can direct a separate HTML document to each frame.  With MXP, everything needs to be specified from the single MUD text stream, so the normal syntax for frames in HTML does not work for MXP. 

Defining a frame in MXP is similar to HTML, but different enough that you should note the syntax.  First, the <FRAME> and <FRAMESET> tags are effectively combined.  Then, instead of a SRC URL link for the frame, the frame is simply given a name.

The attributes for the <FRAME> tag are:

NAME
The name of the frame to be used to send text to the frame later in the text stream.
ALIGN (LEFT|CENTER|RIGHT)
The alignment of text in the frame.  Default is Left.
PARENT
The name of the parent frame containing this new frame.  If this is omitted, the main MUD window is considered the parent.  If "_new" is used as the parent name, a new floating window is created rather than creating a frame within a window.
LEFT
The coordinate of the left side of the frame.  It can be a percentage (ends in %), a number of character widths (ends in "c") or a number of pixels.  For example, LEFT="50%" starts the frame halfway across the parent window, LEFT="5c" starts the frame 5 character spacings (using the width of the character X if it is a proportional font) from the left side of the parent window.   LEFT=100 starts the frame 100 pixels from the left edge of the parent window.   If a negative number is used, it means the value is relative to the right side of the parent instead of the left.  If the parent was "_new" then the values are relative to the entire screen rather than to a parent window.  Default is 0.
TOP
The coordinate of the top of the frame.  Same syntax as LEFT, but the character spacing using the height of the capital X character instead of the width.  If a negative value is used, it means the frame is relative to the bottom of the parent instead of the top.  Default is 0.
WIDTH
The width of the frame.  Same syntax as LEFT.  Default is 100%.   Percentage refers to the amount of window space remaining to the right of the LEFT position.  If a negative value is used, the frame is created to the left of the LEFT position.
HEIGHT
The height of the frame.  Same syntax as TOP.  Default is 50%.   Percentage refers to the amount of window space remaining below the TOP position.   If a negative value is used, the frame is created above the TOP position.
SCROLLING (yes|no)
Determines whether the frame is allowed to scroll.  The default is yes.
RESIZE
Allows the user to resize the frame.  Normally frames cannot be resized by the user.

The frame borders are controlled by the client rather than the server.  The server should assume that the frames do not have borders.  The user can turn on borders in order to see the frames and resize them if allowed.

Overlapping frames are not supported and can cause undesired results (overlapping text that interferes with the text of the other frame).  So, make sure your frames are properly located.

Some examples:

<FRAME Name="Status" Height="2c">

Creates a two-line high status bar at the top of the current MUD window.

<FRAME Name="Map" Left="-20c" Height="20c">

Creates a frame in the upper-right corner of the MUD window 20 characters wide by 20 characters high.

<FRAME "Chat" Height="10c" RESIZE>

Creates a resizable frame along the top 10 characters of the current MUD window.

To send text to a particular frame, you use the <DESTINATION> tag (or <DEST> for short).  For example, to send a status message to the Status frame, you would use:

<DEST Status>This text is sent to the status window</DEST>

Cursor Control

The <DEST> tag can also be used to position text at a certain position in a frame.  So, instead of using VT100 or ANSI escape codes to move the cursor, you can just use the X and Y attributes of the <DEST> command.  If no frame name is given, the text is sent to the position on the main MUD window.  Note that when text in a frame or window scrolls, the text is no longer at the same X or Y position.  So, for status windows, ensure that you set the frame to be unscrollable.

<DEST Status X=10 Y=2>100</DEST>

Would display the text "100" at the 10 column on the 2nd line of the Status frame.

To erase text already in the frame, you can output spaces, or you can use two of the erase attributes for the <DEST> tag.  The EOL keyword causes the rest of the line to be erased after displaying the text.  The EOF keyword causes the rest of the frame to be erased after displaying the text.  You can erase an entire line using the Y= parameter with no text.  You can erase the entire frame by just omitting any text and other keywords.  So,

<DEST Status Y=2 EOL></DEST>

would erase the 2nd line in the status frame, while

<DEST Status EOF></DEST>

would erase the entire status frame.

Crosslinking multiple MUD servers

Implementation Note (MXP v0.3): The function of the <RELOCATE> command has been changed, and the previous <LOGIN> tag has been replaced by <USER> and <PASSWORD>.

MXP also supports commands that allow multi-server MUD worlds to be built.  The <RELOCATE> tag closes the current MUD connection and causes a new connect to open on a new server.  The attributes for this tag are the hostname and port of the new connection:

<RELOCATE new.server.com 1000>

The optional keyword QUIET can be used to suppress further output from the MUD.  When the closing </RELOCATE> tag is used, MUD output is resumed.  When using the QUIET tag you'll normally put the </RELOCATE> tag after your login sequence to prevent the user from seeing the login text.

To automatically log the user into the other server, use the <USER> tag to cause the client to send the username, and the <PASSWORD> tag to cause the client to send the password.

You can also use <USER> and <PASSWORD> without using the <RELOCATE> command.  Putting these two tags in your login sequence will cause MXP-enabled clients to automatically send the user's name and password, instead of relying on client-side scripting for autologin.

Images

MXP supports an <IMAGE> tag to display inline graphics images.  GIF or BMP images are supported.  Additional image types or encrypted images can be supported with MUD-specific Filters as described in the next section.

This is similar to the <IMG> HTML tag but doesn't implement some of the HTML options.  The <IMAGE> tag is very similar to the <SOUND> tag (or !!SOUND command) in MSP.  The attributes of the <IMAGE> tag are:

FName
The name of the graphics file to display.
URL
The URL of the path for the graphic if it should be downloaded on the fly.  This is not recommended for large graphics but is supported to be compatible with the MSP URL parameter for sounds.  The classname is appended to the URL, along with the name of the graphics file itself.
T (type)
The class for the image.  Same as classes used in MSP.
H (height)
The height of the image (in pixels, character heights, or percentage).  If omitted, the height is computed from the actual image.  If the specified height is different from the image, the image is stretched.
W (width)
The width of the image.  Same syntax as height.
HSPACE
Additional space to add before and after the image
VSPACE
Additional space to add above and below the image.
ALIGN (left|right|top|middle|bottom)
Controls the alignment of the image on the line.  For example, if ALIGN=Bottom is used, the rest of the text on the line will align with the bottom of the image.

Note that when using images, the act as large individual characters as far as the client is concern.  Text cannot wrap on multiple lines next to an image...an image always takes up the entire height of the line.  Text wrapping to the next line will wrap at the normal left margin of the screen until the graphics image.  So, if inline graphics are used, you should make them similar in size to the surrounding text line.   Also remember that the user might be using a different screen font.

The <IMAGE> command is intended to be used with graphic images already loaded to the client's disk.  Using the URL attribute to download graphics on the fly can cause a severe burden to the MUD server.  However, even if the URL attribute is used, the image file is not downloaded if it already exists on the disk.  So, since the image is only downloaded once, the MUD server might be able to handle it.  Also, as with MSP, the downloading will never overwrite an existing file with the same name as a security precaution, or allow any absolute path information.  The file will be stored in a location determined by the client.  To update an image to a new version, you need to specify a new filename.

File Filters

It is likely that the MUD does not want all of the images stored on the clients disk to be viewable until the MUD server requests them.  MXP allows the MUD to define it's own graphics format and to provide a client plugin module that converts the MUD-specific format to a standard GIF or BMP format.  To define a filter, use the <FILTER> tag, with the SRC attribute to specify the file extension of the MUD-specific format, and the DEST attribute to specify the output file extension (default is BMP).  The NAME attribute gives the name of the plugin to be called, and the optional PROC attribute is a numeric parameter that the plugin can use to support multiple conversions as needed.   So, an example would be:

<FILTER SRC='gff' DEST='gif' NAME='MyPlugin'>

This would call the Filter function in the MYPLUGIN plugin module whenever the MUD tries to display a .gff file.  The .gff file is read into memory and passed to the Filter function in the plugin (with PROC=0 in the above example) and expect a .gif format output to be returned by the function.  Simply provide your plugin for users and you can then store proprietary files on the client that are decoded and displayed as needed.  Note that this same Filter function can also be used to process sound files used by MSP.

Outdated Tags

Server-side scripting

The <SCRIPT> tag is no longer supported in version 0.4 MXP.  There were too many client-specific security issues involved in this tag.

Implementation Details

To implement MXP on a MUD server requires some attention.  Most important, you need some way to activate the MXP text output on the MUD.  You don't want to display the MXP tags to a user that doesn't have an MXP MUD client.  One way to activate MXP on your MUD is to simply prompt the user and ask if they want to enable MXP, or provide an MXP command on the MUD that toggles MXP text on and off.

If you want to get more sophisticated, you can use the Telnet Option negotiation to determine if the client supports MXP.  Simple query Telnet option 91 and an MXP client will respond that it will handle MXP.  You can also use the Telnet option to determine if the client supports the MUD Sound Protocol (MXP) or the MUD Compression Protocol (MCP). The following Telnet Option numbers are used:

86    MUD Compression Protocol (see MCP spec for details on the difference between option 85 and option 86)
90    MUD Sound Protocol (MSP)
91    MUD eXtension Protocol (MXP)

Although MXP does not support a separate style sheet, you would be best off in your implementation if you stored all of your !ELEMENT and !ENTITY definitions in a separate file and sent them to the client as part of your welcome message.  This would give you one place to change your tags on the MUD.  The MUD output itself would then use these elements.  You should try to avoid using MXP commands within the specific room output of a MUD and instead encapsulate them into MUD-defined ELEMENTS so that you can easily change how your MUD looks and operates.

A Detailed Example

Want a more complete example of all of this?  I thought so.  Here is a basic MXP package the you can use on your MUD to handle the most common MUD functions.  Go through this example line by line with the documentation above and you should be able to figure it out.  Once you get the hang of it, it is pretty easy.

<!-- Elements to support the Automapper --> <!ELEMENT RName '<FONT COLOR=Red><B>' FLAG="RoomName"> <!ELEMENT RDesc FLAG='RoomDesc'> <!ELEMENT RExits '<FONT COLOR=Blue>' FLAG='RoomExit'> <!-- The next element is used to define a room exit link that sends the exit direction to the MUD if the user clicks on it --> <!ELEMENT Ex '<SEND>'> <!ELEMENT Chat '<FONT COLOR=Gray>' OPEN> <!ELEMENT Gossip '<FONT COLOR=Cyan>' OPEN> <!-- in addition to standard HTML Color specifications, you can use color attribute names such as blink --> <!ELEMENT ImmChan '<FONT COLOR=Red,Blink>'> <!ELEMENT Auction '<FONT COLOR=Purple>' OPEN> <!ELEMENT Group '<FONT COLOR=Blue>' OPEN> <!-- the next elements deal with the MUD prompt --> <!ELEMENT Prompt FLAG="Prompt"> <!ELEMENT Hp FLAG="Set hp"> <!ELEMENT MaxHp FLAG="Set maxhp"> <!ELEMENT Mana FLAG="Set mana"> <!ELEMENT MaxMana FLAG="Set maxmana"> <!-- now the MUD text --> <RName>The Main Temple</RName> <RDesc>This is the main hall of the MUD where everyone starts. Marble arches lead south into the town, and there is a <i>lovely</i> <send "drink &text;">fountain</send> in the center of the temple,</RDesc> <RExits>Exits: <Ex>N</Ex>, <Ex>S</Ex>, <Ex>E</Ex>, <Ex>W</Ex></RExits> <Prompt>[<Hp>100</Hp>/<MaxHp>120</MaxHp>hp <Mana>50</Mana>/<MaxMana>55</MaxMana>mana]</Prompt>

This would display the following:

The Main Temple This is the main hall of the MUD where everyone starts. Marble arches lead south into the town, and there is a lovely fountain in the center of the temple. Exits: N, S, E, W
[100/120hp 50/55mana]

and set the variables @hp, @maxhp, @mana, @maxmana appropriately. Clicking on the exit links would send the proper direction to the MUD to move you in that direction.   It would send the "drink fountain" command if the user clicked on the underlined word "fountain".

Conclusions

Proper use of MXP can radically improve the normal text-only MUD experience.  In addition to embedded graphics, you can now better control the font, color, and size of text.  You can directly control the automapper, allowing it to work perfectly on your MUD without fancy parsing.  You can define links for users that like to point and click with their mouse.  You can add pull-down menus to text displayed by the MUD to give the user a list of possible commands.  The use of MXP will make your MUD stand out among the hundreds of other MUDs on the Internet and help breath new life into MUDs and help them compete against the more graphical RPGs appearing on the Internet.

docs.title: CASTLE CODE
docs.text: -------------------------------------------------------------------------- CASTLE CODE -------------------------------------------------------------------------- This policy is to let any and all that code here know that anything that you code here becomes a part of DarkWind. All code that is generated on DarkWind is considered to be a part of a communal effort to make DarkWind better. What this means is, if you code an area here on DarkWind, first, we want that area to be unique to DarkWind and not running on other muds as well as here, and second, if you decide to leave DarkWind, your castle stays with this mud. If you leave, your code can and will continue to be used here as long as the administration feels that it is a benefit to the mud as a whole. If you choose to leave, we will most likely NOT provide you with a copy of your area unless at least one of the following factors are present: One, your area was never opened here on DarkWind, Two, the administration of DarkWind feels that the loss of your area won't have a detrimental effect on the Mud, or Three, the administration feels confindent that you only want the code for archival reasons and have no intentions of putting the code up on another mud at least for the time it is being used on DarkWind. Even if one or more of the above conditions are met, this does not guarantee you will get a copy, it is still up to the administration to decide this. While this policy may seem a little harsh, it is written this way so that there is no way a person can come back later and state that they didnt understand our policy on this matter. --------------------------------------------------------------------------

docs.title: CODING IN GENERAL
docs.text: -------------------------------------------------------------------------- CODING IN GENERAL -------------------------------------------------------------------------- What you code and how you code here at DarkWind are very important. First and formost is theme, as stated in multiple places, the theme of DarkWind has a fairly serious tone as well as being medieval in nature. With the opening of New Domains, this is changing slightly, but the rule still applies. You are required to code within the the theme of each domain and all domains are to have a fairly serious tone to them. Areas such as Cartoon land, Cybertech, Silly land, Futuristic, etc will 100% not be allowed or tolorated period, so don't even bother to mention or ask about it. Values of objects are also an important topic. As far as weapons and armours go, you should ALWAYS set_value(-1) on these objects and let them be autovalued. If an object has some sort of unique property that doesnt get reflected in the autovalue, you can set_value(-1,<amount>) where amount is the amount to be added to the autovalue. Its always great to make that neat object that is worth a fortune, but as a wizard you must always keep in mind game balance. If too much money is put into the game, the economy of the game will get thrown out of whack. as far as rooms go, we no longer will approve rooms with 1 or 2 line descs, nor will we approve rooms that don't have add_looks for every thing described in the rooms long or in other add_looks. Also, in general, if you feel the need to give a monster something of value, please give them an object of value over straight cash. How often do you think monsters walk around with a fortune in cash on them. It is much more likely that a monster would carry around his favorite sword worth X money while on guard than it is that the guard would be carryig around a backpack full of X coins. Remember this simple rule when coding: "Quality is better than quantity". Anybody can code 200 boring rooms with random monsters or treasure. We want areas that are interesting as well as rewarding. There will also be some policies going into place soon on minimum coding requirements to become or stay a wizard. We do not really want wizards that are not even remotly productive. Part of being a wizard is learning to code and opening up an area. If a person doesn't feel up to this then they would probobly do better as a player. If a person wants to stay a wizard but doesn't feel upto opening and area, we can find you a project to work on in its place (we have plenty). --------------------------------------------------------------------------

docs.title: Desting/forcing others to log off.
docs.text: --------------------------------------------------------------------- Desting/forcing others to log off. --------------------------------------------------------------------- Desting players for any reason except if its your test character or the player is obviouly cheating and you need to dest them to quickly prevent a major problem is strictly forbidden. The command is there for you to get rid of test objects or monsters, not for you to have fun at other players expenses. If you dest another player for any reason except for the above exceptions, you are subject to immediate demotion if the victim wishes it. Demotions will be as follows. 1st offense. 1 level. 2nd offense. 10% reduction in level. 3rd offense. You get to become a player at level 1. 4th offense. Removal and banishment of your character. Wizards and Arches desting other wizards and Arches. Not allowed period, unless the person asks to be dested for some reason. Offenses of the above rule will result in hte same punishement as above. Anyone desting a higher ranked wizard is immediate grounds for demotion. UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES WILL ANYONE DEST A SAGE, DEMI, OR GOD. Infractions to this rule will result in immediate demotion to level 102 for the first offense level 1 for the 2nd offense. SAGE, DEMI, and GOD's are exempt from above rules, unless they prove themselves unable to use common sense. In which case they most likey wouldnt have given the postion in the first place.

docs.title: Unless you are a guild coder or a helper, you may not belong to a guild
docs.text: Unless you are a guild coder or a helper, you may not belong to a guild as a wizard.

docs.title: GUILD RECRUITING
docs.text: -------------------------------------------------------------------------- GUILD RECRUITING -------------------------------------------------------------------------- Wizards or higher will NOT recruit players for any guild. If a player asks a wizards o question on a guild, they should be told that they need to talk to other players to determine that information. It doesn't matter if you coded the guild in question, you will not recruit players for it. Doing so is a breach of the wizard/player non-involvement rule and will be frowned upon. Repeated infractions will be punished.

docs.title: NAME CHANGING
docs.text: -------------------------------------------------------------------------- NAME CHANGING -------------------------------------------------------------------------- The name changing of players or wizards is not allowed. If you do it for one person, you are going to have to do it for everyone who asks, otherwise hard feeling will result. Since no one wants to cater to every name chage whim of the players, name changing in any form except starting a new character under the new name and rm'ing the old charcter will not be allowed.

docs.title: Person to person interactions and the general enviroment of DarkWind
docs.text: --------------------------------------------------------------------- Person to person interactions and the general enviroment of DarkWind --------------------------------------------------------------------- No one be it player, wizard, arch, demi, or god will be allowed to use profanity across ANY channel. If you feel the need to swear to get your point across and cant think of any other way to do it, then go somewhere else. If it makes you feel better to degrade people, at least have the courtesy to do it privately in mudmail. No one is allowed to degrade fellow players via public channels. If you feel that they have done something wrong mail them about it, don't post it in public. If your level 100 or higher this is even more important. You represent what players what to become. If you come across as a less than desirable person, it reflects on every one of us. Infractions to this rule will be as follows. 1st offense. Verbal, documented warning. 2nd offense. Demotion to lowest level in your catagory. 3rd offense. Demotion to level 100 if already a wizard, and demotion to level 1 if a player. 4th offense. Removal and banisment of your character. This is not something to be taken lightly. We want a friendly atmosphere around her for both players and wizards, and if you are unable to abide by this rule, you will not be welcome here.

docs.title: Responsibilities for any Sponsor on DarkWind.
docs.text: Responsibilities for any Sponsor on DarkWind. This file is the official policy on what we expect from sponsors and their sponsorees. From this point on, any person on DarkWind that is a WIZARD or higher is expected to contribute to making this place better. For wizards, this means that you are going to be required to code new areas or continually expand your existing area. Wizards who are unable to achieve this will be demoted back to apprentice until a later time when they feel they are more up to the task. ARCH-WIZARDS and higher are the people in charge of sponsoring new wizards and also to continually check on their sponorees progress to ensure that they are in accordance with DarkWind's rules. Promotions and Demotions can and will result directly from how well you perform this task. If one of your sponsors gets an area open, they will be entitled to a promotion. Also if those in charge of promotions (see below) felt hat you are doing a satisfactory job in your work with your sponsorees, the appropiate sponsor will also be entitled to a promotion. If, on the other hand, the sponsor seems to be incapable of keeping their sponsorees motivated or seems unwilling to help their sponsorees with problems, both the wizard and his sponsor will be subject to demotion. Simply put, if your sponsoree isn't doing their job, it means the sponsor isn't doing their job, and BOTH will be demoted for their failures. This Rule applys to ANY sponsor. You are not exampt from this just becasue you are a DEMI. If you do not do your job, you will be demoted. The amount of demotions will be up to the appropriate individuals (see below). SAGE's are 100 percent in charge of promotions when it comes to this area of sponsor/sponsoree relations. When a wizard opens a new quality area, they will be entitled to a promotion, and it will be up to a SAGE to give that person their promotion. If the SAGE feels that the sponsor also has been doing a good job of keeping their sponsorees motivated and working hard, then they will also be eligible for a promotion. Again the same is true for the opposite. If a SAGE feels you are not doing a satisfactory job of teaching your sponsor and keeping them motivated, then they have the ability and authority to demote you as well. There will be a standard interview that a SAGE will conduct with each perspective sponsoree. The results of this interview will be posted to the AWIZ board, so that everyone can look over the information and make an informed decision before deciding to sponsor an individual. This will ensure that the sponsoree knows whats going to be required of him BEFORE they become a wizard, and will make sure that the sponsor is comfortable with sponsering the individual. More details of this process will be posted at a later time. Under this policy it is very likely that some wizards will end up being demoted back to an apprentice wizard. Such an person is still eligible to become a wizard at a later date, as long as they can find a sponsor that is willing to take the risk with them. It should also be pointed out that if a sponsoree is demoted back to an apprentice, this will look very bad on their sponsor who WILL receive a demotion for their utter failure at their job. Wizards are going to be expected to turn out code on a fairly steady basis. This doesn't mean a wizards has to code fifty rooms a week, but it does mean that if a wizard in on the mud a fair percentage of their time should be devoted to coding most every visit. Being a wizard is a responsibility, not a right. Being a wizard means being willing to take on the responsibilities that are placed on you. If a person feels that they are unable or unwilling to accept those responsibilities then they should not become one in the first place. Sponsors: When you sponsor an APPRENTICE, you are saying that you will be taking responsibility for what that person does. Sponsoring a person and then sending them off to learn on their own with only a 'let me know if you have any questions' is not acceptable. You are expected to keep up with what the person is doing and if needed give them some direction of they have started down the wrong path or some motivation of they have started to stall. Sponsorees: Are expected to learn LPC asap if they are new and begin work on an area immediatily. Their first area should be around 10 to 20 rooms in size with GOOD QUALITY room descriptions, objects should follow all our rules with weapons and armour being auto-valued. and other objects being reasonably priced as well. Once this first area is opened, the wizard should be constantly working to add to and improve their area. NOTHING will be put into the game withput the sponsors approval. If so, both the sponsor and sponsoree will be held accountable for any problems that might arise. Once a sponsoree has asked to have his area checked, the sponsor needs to look at his area within 24 hours of the request or make arrangements for someone else to look it over. If someone else looks the area over and approves it, the actual sponsor will still be accountable for all its contents even though someone else may have approved it. If an Archwizard or above wishes to use a wizard on a special project, it needs to be noted on the Archwizard board, and that note should be left there through the completion of that project so that the Sages are aware of this fact. If for some reason a wizard is going to be forced to leave for an extended period of time, they are REQUIRED to inform their sponsor about this before they leave, so that it can be appropiatily noted. Wizards who leave for extened periods of time with no notice, will be demoted appropiately for failure to fulfill their duties, although under extenuating circumstances a wizard may petition to be reinstated, and if it is decided that the reason was justified, they will be re-instated.

docs.title: WIZARD TOYS (WIZ_TOYS)
docs.text: -------------------------------------------------------------------------- WIZARD TOYS (WIZ_TOYS) -------------------------------------------------------------------------- Plain and simply put, their not allowed at all in wizard directories. We have a directoy of approved commands that you are allowed to use that have been binned. They are available to all wizards at any time. They are all listed on the 'help wizard' screen. If you know of a command or function that you think would be valuable to everyone, let an Ach-Wiz know about it so that they can look into getting it approved to be used and coded up into a bin function.

docs.title: Command: cat
docs.text: Command: cat Argument: file Print the file 'file'. If it is big, characters will be lost because all of the file is written to the socket, without delay. The file will be searched for in the current directory. 'cat castle.c' will print the castle of the wizard. 'cat' isn't really good for lookin at game files, but rather better for reading documentation. Only Arch wizards and higher can read files from other wizards. Files from the basic adventure can be read by all wizards. See also w/ls, w/ed, w/rm

docs.title: Command: cd
docs.text: Command: cd Argument: path Change current directory.

docs.title: Command: clone
docs.text: Command: clone Argument: file Clone a copy of an object. The "bluebrint" must not be used for anything else then cloning. If the object defined in 'file' isn't loaded, it will be. 'reset()' will also be called in the object. When the 'file' is loaded, a new copy of the object will be created, and moved to either the wizard giving the command, or to his room, depending on what 'get()' says in the object. When the object is being copied, it will have a new 'reset()' again. Rooms and castles should never be cloned, because they should always exist singularly, not in several copies. See also w/load.

docs.title: Command: destruct
docs.text: Command: destruct Argument: object If there is an object named "object" in the same room, it can be destroyed with 'destruct object'. If it is a cloned object, the original blue print will still remain loaded. If it is a singular object (not cloned), like a castle, then all data about the object will be discared. An 'update' of a castle will have the same effect. Never 'destruct' a player. See also w/clone, w/update, w/load.

docs.title: Command: echo
docs.text: Command: echo Argument: Any string The string is sent to all players in the same room. This should be used with great care, and is almost already illegal by the RULES.

docs.title: Command: echoall
docs.text: Command: echoall Argument: Any string The string is sent to all players in the game. This should be used with great care, and is almost already illegal by the RULES. See also: w/emote w/echo

docs.title: Command: ed
docs.text: Command: ed Argument: file Edit the file 'file'. For documentations about how to use 'ed', look at /public/docs/build. You can leave 'ed' with the command 'q', or 'Q' if the file has been modified. When in 'ed', the prompr will change to ':'. The file will be searched for in the current directory. 'ed castle.c' will edit the castle of the wizard. A wizard can only edit files in his home directory, /open, /ftp and in /log. If 'ed' is started without argument, it will edit the file where you last had an error message, and print that message. 'ed' without arguments will edit the last file with an error in, either run time error, or compile time error. So, when you log in to the game, start with 'ed' to see if you have had any errors. See also w/ls, w/cat, w/rm

docs.title: Command: emote
docs.text: Command: emote argument: string Give a message 'string' to all in room. Your name willbe prepended to the message.

docs.title: Command: force
docs.text: Command: force Argument: name 'to' cmd Force a player or monster 'name' to execute command 'cmd'. Bugs: Monsters don't have the command 'say' etc.

docs.title: Command: goto
docs.text: Command: goto argument: obj Teleport directly to a room or a player. If 'obj' is a room, the go to that room. If 'obj' is a player, then go to the same room as his. Bugs: If the player isn't in the game, or the name of the room doesn't exist, the teleport will fail, and move you into the void. When teleporting to a player or monster, you will not get a description of the contents of that room. See also: w/trans, w/in

docs.title: Command: heal
docs.text: Command: heal argument: name Heal a player or a monster totally. Spell points are restored. Excessive use of this is considered cheating.

docs.title: Command: in
docs.text: Command: in argument 1: obj argument 2: command Execute a command 'command' in room 'ob'. See also: w/goto

docs.title: Command: load
docs.text: Command: load Argument: file If the object defined in 'file' isn't loaded, it will be. 'reset()' will also be called in the object. If the object was loaded, nothing will happen. This command is implemented by teleporting the wizard to the object, which will force the object to load, and then teleporting the wizard back again. Rooms can also be loaded by just walking to them. That has exactly the same effect. See also w/clone.

docs.title: Command: ls
docs.text: Command: ls optional argument: path Give a list of all files in 'path'. If no argument is given, list the files in current directory, which is the hoe directory of the wizard. 'ls /' will give a list of all files in the game home directory. See also w/cat, w/ed, w/rm

docs.title: Command: mkdir
docs.text: Command: mkdir Argument: file Create the directory 'file' in the current directory. Only arch wizards and higher can remove directories from other wizards. See also w/ls, w/ed, w/cat w/rm

docs.title: Command: more
docs.text: Command: more Argument: file Print the file 'file' 16 lines and wait for input. space: 16 lines more. 'q': Stop printing. 'u': Backup 16 lines. See also w/ls, w/ed, w/rm, w/cat

docs.title: ***  Congratulations!  ***
docs.text: *** Congratulations! *** You have now become a Wizard. Your repertoire of commands have now been extended with some new Wizard commmands. You can get help for those by typing "help lpc", "help build", "help wizhelp" and "help locals". This will list the various wizard help files, which can then be read by typing "help <subject>", just like normal player helps. For subdirectories of these, simple type "help <directory>", and it will list the contents. To read this file again, type "help NEW_WIZ". These new powers MUST be used sensibly! From now on you are bound by the rules that you will find by typing the command "help RULES". Do this as your first action when you stop reading this text. Following these rules is very important. If you fail to do so, you could LOSE YOUR WIZARDHOOD. Remember, the mud IS case sensitive, so "help rules" won't work, but "help RULES" will. Good luck! Now for useful information you may wish to know: Being a Wizard on DarkWind --------------------------- Congratulations. The fact that you are reading this probably means that you have just become a Wizard on DarkWind. First of all, try to remember this at all times ----------------------------------------------- As a wizard, you have immense powers. But, with those powers comes responsibility - so always think before you do anything. For example, it is possible to move a room's exits, to crash the game, and to kill all the players. And it IS possible to do all these things accidentally, so PLEASE be careful! Remember that as far as the game is concerned you are NO LONGER a part of it. Wizards do not play the game, they are above that and participate only by adding new ideas, like plots and rooms. If you don't know what you are doing, then you probably shouldn't do it. If you know what you are doing, but not if you should do it, then you probably shouldn't do that either. The file structure is a tree ---------------------------- DarkWind mimics the file system hierarchy and file handling commands of UNIX. A directory is a set of files, where those "files" can be both normal files and other directories. Everything starts with the so-called root directory, the name of which is "/" (at least from inside DarkWind!). As in UNIX, a file or a directory is referred to by its file name or its path name, i.e. for example "thing.c" and "/players/alarian/thing.c". The rooms in the "basic" DarkWind world are in the directory "/room", and the objects (like the weapon and monster objects) are in "/obj". Each wizard has his/her own home directory, called, for example, "/players/alarian". Some commands for handling files: --------------------------------- ls - list the files in a directory cd - change the current directory pwd - show the present working directory cat - print the contents of a file on the screen more - print the contents of a file, approx. one screenful at a time tail - print the last few lines of a file ed - edit a file using DarkWind's built-in, line-oriented, editor cp - copy a file mv - move a file rm - remove a file Where do I find the documentation? ---------------------------------- The following commands will give you info on the documentation: help wiz - list of Wizard commands help lpc - list of lpc functions help locals - list of major local functions help build - documentation on building things help helpdir - player helps By typing "help <str>", you can get info on subject "<str>", where "<str>" is any item that appears in the above listings. For instance, "help README.3.0-DR" will give you the info in that file. Help scans through all the doc directories and tries to find the subject you want. It can happen that you won't find what you look for in the documentation. In that case, either ask another wizard, read the code (which actually contains some very useful comments sometimes), or find out by testing. One of the first things you should do is to read the entire contents of documentation that "help wiz" makes available. This is not as much work as it seems and it really pays off very soon, since you later will remember where to look for explanations of commands and routines. Remember also that the Arch Wizards and Elders have as part of their duties the obligation to help other wizards with their problems. I especially want to point out that the information on the editor "ed" can be found in "help ed". "ed" is the editor you will be using for most of your work. You can get help from inside of "ed" by typing "h". You can read almost any file with the command "more", as in: "more /obj/object.c" or just "more object.c" if you have changed into "/obj" with "cd /obj". Doing a "?" while in "more" will show you some of its useful sub-fuctions, like numbered backpaging. Object-oriented programming in DarkWind ---------------------------------------- When you play DarkWind, everything you encounter (weapons, monsters, players, rooms etc.) are OBJECTS. Each object is an INSTANCE of a CLASS of objects. One class can INHERIT part of its design from another class. An instance of an object is either created by CLONING or LOADING the object class, and each object is described in a file, written in a C-like language called LPC. These "objects" are the programs that make up the game. All program code that you write as a Wizard or encounter as part of the standard world will be part of a description of an object or a class of objects that can be loaded and cloned. Many of the objects use a feature known as "inheritance", in order to save time and resources. there are many "standard objects" that have special functions that allow you to customize them with a minimum of work. Loading, cloning and updating ----------------------------- "Loading an object" means the process of taking an object file, for example "/obj/object.c", and reading it into the game. This is done as soon as that object is called for any way. For example, if a function in the object is called from another object, or if another object tries to enter it (as when a player walks into a room), then the object is loaded. When the object is loaded, one instance of the object class is created. If there should be only one instance, as for example for (most) rooms, this is enough. If you need to create several instances of a class of objects, you clone it. Objects can be cloned using the wizard command "clone", as in "clone /obj/misc/torch", and with the LPC function clone_object(), as in this_torch = clone_object("obj/misc/torch"); Cloning an object will cause it to be loaded, if it wasn't already. When you have changed the description of an object by editing the file, and want to load the new version of the object, you can use the wizard command "update". Then load (or clone) the new version. If the object in question is a room, a "goto ROOMNAME" will load the room as well. LPC --- LPC is a dialect of C and differs from C mainly in being simplified and in that it allows for handling the objects. It has only four data types (plus arrays of those data types), fewer operators and a simplified control structure. Note that before the contents of a file is read it is run through the standard C pre-processor. This program can be used to insert other files into the file being read, and to define constants and macros. Lines starting with "#", as the lines (no blanks before the #!): #include "config.h" #define INSURANCE_LIMIT 1000 #define CLONE(var, file) var = clone_object(file); are all commands to the p

docs.title: Command: people
docs.text: Command: people List fact of all players: What internet number they call from. The current name. The level of the player. The age of the player (m=minutes, h=hours, D=days). Idle flag 'I' if the player has been idle for more than 5 minutes. Where they are. There is also shown the number of active players, number of commandes per second executed (averaged over the last 15 minutes) and number of lines compiled per second (averaged of the last 15 minutes). This information is only displayed if you are of demigod level or above. You can type people wiz or people players to get just a list of wizards or just a list of players. See also: w/wizlist

docs.title: Command: pwd
docs.text: Command: pwd Argument: none Print current directory.

docs.title: This file documents all standard commands that a wizard have.
docs.text: This file documents all standard commands that a wizard have.

docs.title: Command: review
docs.text: Command: review Show all messages given when you leave or enter a room. See also w/setmin, w/setmout, w/setmmin, w/setmmout

docs.title: Command: rm
docs.text: Command: rm Argument: file Remove the file 'file'. The file will be searched for in the current directory. 'rm castle.c' will remove the castle of the wizard (not to be recommended). Only Arch wizards and higher can remove files from other wizards. See also w/ls, w/ed, w/cat

docs.title: Command: rmdir
docs.text: Command: rmdir Argument: file Remove the directory 'file'. The file will be searched for in the current directory. Only arch wizards and higher can remove directories from other wizards. See also w/ls, w/ed, w/cat w/rm

docs.title: These are the rules for a wizard.
docs.text: These are the rules for a wizard. 1. You should try to avoid giving out free exp,objects, or money, etc... In the event of a crash or ligetimate loss of some sort they have to go to the post office and mail an admin of the game or use bug. 2. Never attack a player or kill him. If a player behaves badly, file the complaint to the Admin. 3. Do not make 'deadly' trapps. A player must never die because he didn't know what happens in the next room. If some room is very dangerous, make some hint (like the giant footprints beside the giant lair). this does not dissalow 'death traps' it just means that through some process of deduction they should be able to figure it will happen... for instance.. if they are storming the villians base... they should expect a surprise attack at any moment, no warnings needed. But if they're walking down market street, they should at least here a milisecond advance warning, if they pass thier perception check :-) 4. Your 'area' should be composed of many entrances an exits, such as building lots of 1-4 room areas, connected by plot line only. Use the city to it's fullest potential, make it your ally in coding, not opponant. look at build castle for help on giving your area multiple entrances... 5. You may not make objects which interfere with the wizard commands. For example, do not make objects which don't allow "destruct." 6. Do not make copies of standard objects like monster.c, weapon.c, and so on without asking a god, as they take immense amounts of memory. If it's something you think should be in that thing, ask. It might already actually be there. If not we might just add it to the standard file. Also remember inherit. 7. You may not build things which do not conform to the rules and guidlines specified in /public/docs/build/RULES, 8. Try to avoid making devices or situations which make players loose experience if they are adventuring or examining objects. Players should be rewarded for adventuring and discovering things. If they get killed... Well, they will then lose some experience, but this is a special case! 9. Use the character 'test' , with the password '123456' for any situations where you need to test something, he should be modifyable by typing ed /players/people/test.o (test is the only character a non-admin can edit). if it says New Character on test.. then make him with this password. 10. Under all circunstances you MUST use the exit defines in room.c to define all obvious exits of ANY room you make. The reason for this is 1) disk space, and 2) room.c has several special functions in it, rooms without which would come accross as 'un-real' to players. For this reason I have designed certain parts of the life routines to be dependant on room.c such that rooms not using it give errors. To use room.c simply inherit it and set the variables. Look at any standard room to see how this is done. 11. WIZARD ITEMS will not be allowed in /player/NAME directory's, all wizard item's must be stored in /open, this rule is here to discourage thier creation, as the only reason people ever make them is to get access to powers they're not suppossed to have (and since -B makes all wiz's get all the powers there is even less point to this). 12. Never generate messages that looks like something it isn't (good and precise rule :-). That is, don't try to fool the player that someone says something when it isn't true etc. More or less... 13. Genre: Industrial fantasy. You must stick to the genre when designing things. If you do not the mud will seem 'inconsistant' and lose it's sense of 'realism', etc...

docs.title: Command: setmin
docs.text: Command: setmin Argument: mess Set the message given when you enter a room. The message will have your name prepended. See also: w/setmout, w/setmmin, w/setmmout

docs.title: Command: setmmin
docs.text: Command: setmmin Argument: mess Set the message given when you teleport to a room. The message will have your name prepended. See also: w/setmout, w/setmin, w/setmmout

docs.title: Command: setmmout
docs.text: Command: setmmout Argument: mess Set the message given when you teleport from a room. The message will have your name prepended. See also: w/setmout, w/setmin, w/setmmin

docs.title: Command: setmout
docs.text: Command: setmout Argument: mess Set the message given when you leave a room. The message will have your name prepended. See also: w/setmin, w/setmmin, w/setmmout

docs.title: Command: shutdown
docs.text: Command: shutdown Shutdown the game immediately. Don't do this if you don't have a very good reason for it. And if possible, give players time to sell their things and save.

docs.title: Command: snoop
docs.text: Command: snoop Argument: a player Listen to everything that player hears or says. You can also listen to wizards if they have a lower level than you do.

docs.title: Command: stat
docs.text: Command: stat argument: name Give status about a player or a monster. See also: w/snoop

docs.title: Command: title
docs.text: Command: title argument: new title Without arguments, print your old title. With arguments, set a new title.

docs.title: Command: trans
docs.text: Command: trans Argument: name Transport a player or monster to you.

docs.title: Command: update
docs.text: Command: update Argument: file Remove the definition of an object. If the object was cloned, all copies of it will remain. Use full path name if the file is not in your home directory. If it is a room, the room will be destroyed. The next refernce of the room will load it again from the file. The 'update' command is implemented as an LPC function that simply calls 'destruct()' on the object. See also w/clone w/destruct w/load efun/destruct

docs.title: ----------	  ed	----------
docs.text: ---------- ed ---------- ed is the editor used by gm's in supermud. the following is a doc file on it, it's rather old, and may or may not make sense... if you have any problems with ed or this doc mail your muds admin When in 'ed', the prompt is ':'. Ed has two modes, command mode and insert mode. The insert mode has no prompt. You exit the insert mode by typing a single '.' on a line. All commands have the following syntax: X,Ycmd or Xcmd For example: 1,10p Will print line 1 to 10. 1,5d Will delete line 1 to 5. 8p Will print line 8. A '.' is the "current line". The current line is the last line referenced. If you want to print last line + 10 more: .,.+10p Commands that use a line range: If no line is given, then curent line is printed. p Print line. d Delete line. l Print line with control characters. r file Read in a file after the line specified. s Substitute patterns. See special documentation. z Print 10 lines. a Start insert mode after specified line. Exit with '.'<return>. i Start insert mode before specified line. Exit with '.'<return>. Commands used without line specification: q Quit. Won't work if file is changed. Q Quit and discard all changes if not saved. w Write the file out. w file Write the file out with name 'file'. x Write and Quit the file. x file Write the file to 'file' and then Quit ed. e file Edit a file. - Go up one line of the file. !cmd Give a game command. For example "say Wait, I am busy". As line numbers '.' is current line, and '$' is last line of file. Thus '1,$p' will always print all of the file. Substitutions are very advanced. First a simple example: s/apa/bepa/ This will substitue the 'apa' in current line to 'bepa'. If an 'p' is appended, you will also immediately see the result. 1,$s/apa/bepa/ Same, but all lines in file. Only first occurence on every line. Any character can used instead of '/': s!apa!bepa!g The 'g' specifies that all occurences of apa on this line are changed to bepa. The pattern that are supposed to be replaced, can be a regular expression. See ed3 about that. Searching is done with: /hello/ Find first line in of after current line. Just // will repeat the search. Theere are special characters that can be used in the pattern: . Match any character. x* Match any numbers of x (0 or more). [abc] Match 'a', 'b' or 'c'. [0-9] Match any digit 0 - 9. [a-z] Match any lowercase letter. \x Match 'x' where 'x' can be any character except '(' and ')'. Example: s/ab.d/ABCD/ Substitute any string 'abXd' against 'ABCD' where X can be any character. this is also the only way to remove a / from a line with s, such as using s/SF.market.300/myroom to change SF/market/300 to myroom How to copy from a standard file. Enter ed. Then do 'r /room/vill_green.c'. Now you have something in the buffer. Change it into what you want it to be. Then 'w /players/peter/hall.c'. Or 'w hall.c'.

docs.title: Command: wizlist (name)
docs.text: Command: wizlist (name) The wizard top score list. This is the purpose of the game: To be on the top of this list. Of course, you have to become wizard first. A wizard get one point for every command he has defined when it is used by a player. It is quite easy to cheat, of course, but cheating wizards are simply removed from the game (and the list). When you use commands defined by your objects, you will also get points, but this is legal for normal use. The score decays with 1 % every reset, and is saved and restored from file when reboot of game. If there are many wizards, not all wizlist data is printed. Give name of wizard as argument if you want to look at a special wizard. Columns: 1: Score of the castle. 2: Score % of total. 3: Rank sorted by column 1. 4: Total number of evaluated nodes. 5: Total number of heart beats. 6: Experience + money given to players by this wizard. 7: Total number of indices used in arrays. See also: w/people

docs.title: Ezekiel Milquetoast needs your help! He has lost a simple trinket
docs.text: Ezekiel Milquetoast needs your help! He has lost a simple trinket that he was going to use to conduct a magical experiment. Some small, annoying goblins jumped him in his courtyard and stole it because - well, goblins like to do that. Seek him out and help him find his lost trinket. Rumor has it, he resides in his home somewhere north of Darkwind City proper. ** This quest must be completed before reaching level 10 **

docs.title: The evil Archwizard Ashkenazy has been scheming up
docs.text: The evil Archwizard Ashkenazy has been scheming up some great plans in his tower... some say he will soon rule all of Darkwind! Reports of massive armies being built and mobilized for the final confrontation with the puny inhabitants of Darkwind. Many foolhardy adventurers have claimed to have defeated Ashkenazy, but as many lickings as he takes, he just keeps on ticking! Find a way to stop Ashkenazy, before it is too late! This is a lower level quest, but requires much exploring.

docs.title: The temple of Athena has been abandoned, left to sink in
docs.text: The temple of Athena has been abandoned, left to sink in the swamps of Araakas, and the symbol of Athena's power has crumbled with time. Find the temple, locate the remains of the statue of Athena and rebuild it, so a force of good may stand against the Arch-lich Araakas. The statue of Athena will not be complete until her eyes are returned and she can see again. This is a medium to high level quest, and requires much exploration.

docs.title: The Cat has claimed another victim! The evil Kitty Cat has seduced its
docs.text: The Cat has claimed another victim! The evil Kitty Cat has seduced its way into another hapless victim's arms, right here in the City. Kill the victim, find the Cat, and redistribute the wealth from the evil Cat to the wholesome needy. You should not have to leave town to complete this low-level quest.

docs.title: The Grand Master of Reality Revisionists, Darvros
docs.text: The Grand Master of Reality Revisionists, Darvros the Magnificent, is having a little trouble finding the time to get away to search for some things he needs for his next grand project. However, he's more than willing to accept help from others, and probably willing to compensate his helpers as well. If you'd like to help, just go mention something to him about the potion he's working on, and he'll give you the details. Darvros, by the way, is the guild master of the Reality Revisionists. He keeps shop just outside the town of Glaverton, far from the depradations of the demons that have invaded Glavia. This is a lower level quest.

docs.title: Rumor has it, that there is a hidden gold mine under the Souvrael
docs.text: Rumor has it, that there is a hidden gold mine under the Souvrael desert. Those mines are known to be ran by an evil Slave Lord! Remember to bring some light. Mines are usually dark. Let it be known, that this quest is not extremely difficult, however it is slightly tricky. This is a medium-low level quest.

docs.title: There have been strange rumblings coming from Volcano Island. Many
docs.text: There have been strange rumblings coming from Volcano Island. Many adventurers have returned with tales of a mysterious Hall, and a newly formed cavern. It is said that a great battle is taking place, but that the help of all races on Darkwind is required to partake in it. The end game of the quest is high level as well, and is a one on one battle to the death. Getting help on the beginning stages is allowed, but not with the final battle. <*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*><*> Warning: The plains of the battlefield are an open pk region. PK players can kill non-pkers, and non-pkers can kill pk'ers. Their PK status will be unchanged when they leave the battlefield. If you were non-PK when you entered, you will be non-PK when you exit. The rewards for the extra challenge might make the risk worthwhile.

docs.title: The tiny Kingdom of Glavia, nestled in the shadow
docs.text: The tiny Kingdom of Glavia, nestled in the shadow of the great mountains of the north between two mighty rivers, has been beset by an invasion of demons. The demons have destroyed everything, and driven off the poor inhabitants. The King of Glavia, distraught with grief, has disappeared into hiding with amnesia. Return his memory and his throne to him. This is a difficult quest, however, there are many items you may find on the way which will help you in more than just the quest. Therefore, it may be worth your while to start now. Note: you *will* need a helping hand during at least one part of the quest. Additionally, look at everything in detail, and use your other senses as well. Treat the area as you would the real world: actions have effects that may range far from your immediate vicinity. Logic should tell you what *should* happen when you try something, and for the most part, it will. This is a mid to high level quest.

docs.title: The tiny Kingdom of Glavia, nestled in the shadow of
docs.text: The tiny Kingdom of Glavia, nestled in the shadow of the great mountains of the north between two mighty rivers, has been beset by an invasion of demons. Once you have restored the King to his throne, help him rid Glavia of the demon menace. Visit him in the throne room for more details. This is a difficult quest, however, there are many items you may find on the way which will help you in more than just the quest. Therefore, it may be worth your while to start now. Note: you *will* need a helping hand during at least one part of the quest. Additionally, look at everything in detail, and use your other senses as well. Treat the area as you would the real world: actions have effects that may range far from your immediate vicinity. Logic should tell you what *should* happen when you try something, and for the most part, it will. You must complete Forgetful King before you may complete this quest.

docs.title: Sometimes the worst foes are within, rather than without. It is said that
docs.text: Sometimes the worst foes are within, rather than without. It is said that in the icy north in a great cathedral one who is consumed by her inner demons lies, waiting for help to conquer them. Those who would gain renown would do well to aid her, for in bringing her back to herself they bring themselves to a higher understanding of their own selves.

docs.title: Find Bueferd and send him out of his pub feet-first!
docs.text: Find Bueferd and send him out of his pub feet-first! Membership in the Dock Workers' club is proven only by possession of a membership card, and you will need one to get into the pub. Search in some low-level places, be clean, and have fun! This is a low-level quest.

docs.title: The king of the trolls has stolen the Minotaur's most prized
docs.text: The king of the trolls has stolen the Minotaur's most prized possession and sent him on a rampage. Return to him his property. This is a mid-level quest involving killing some fairly strong monsters in locations not suited to complete freedom. Some of what was here has had to be recreated, but the feel is hopefully the same. The location of this quest is no longer obvious and will require lots of searching on the part of the questors.

docs.title: A newbie tome can be obtained by pulling the lever in the dispenser
docs.text: A newbie tome can be obtained by pulling the lever in the dispenser at the center of the city of Darkwind. It contains much useful information that you should be aware of. Perhaps there is some small bonus for reading the entire thing? NB This quest is exempt from normal rules regarding quest information.

docs.title: A local wizard has expressed interest in a weapon of great
docs.text: A local wizard has expressed interest in a weapon of great destruction. Seek out Darkwind's resident Archwizard for details (he's a chatty fellow). This is a very high level quest.

docs.title: Rid Egypt of the Curse of the Pharaoh.
docs.text: Rid Egypt of the Curse of the Pharaoh. The lands of Egypt can be found exploring the Segovian Desert out of the eastern gate of Souvrael. A lower level quest.

docs.title: Strange lights and evil auras have been observed near the dark temple of
docs.text: Strange lights and evil auras have been observed near the dark temple of Qazaash and many speak fearfully of the return of that dark god. If this indeed comes to pass, unspeakable disasters will befall Darkwind. One person alone may know the cause, and, more pertinently, the solution to this danger. Seek out the hierophant druid in the refuge he went to after his defeat by the evil followers of Qazaash. With him may lie Darkwind's only chance. This is a hard quest meant for high level players. It requires the killing of several deadly monsters, but also the wisdom to avoid impossible combats. Take care and much grief may be avoided. This quest is only solvable once per reboot.

docs.title: The Curse of the Sword of Sunnah
docs.text: The Curse of the Sword of Sunnah ================================ Legends speak of the great sword of Sunnah. It is said that after a great battle with an enemy force, the great Sunnah was defeated and his sword was stolen. It is said that the sword possesses immense power and it would destroy anyone that tried to wield it. One must be a ninja master in order to handle its power and magic. The enemies who stole the sword knew that they could not use it, so they destroyed it, preventing Sunnah from using it. Its pieces have been scattered around and hidden for centuries. As the legend goes, if anyone can bring the three pieces of the sword together, it is possible to re-unite them. When the sword was destroyed, a dark curse of dishonor was placed upon it. The only way to restore honor to the sword is to sacrifice a piece of your own soul. You must find the pieces of the sword and restore its honor. This quest is for mid to high levels.

docs.title: Adventurers have been disappearing from Kerei at an alarming rate,
docs.text: Adventurers have been disappearing from Kerei at an alarming rate, stem the tide. Begin your quest by searching up the river north of the fortress to where strange sounds have been heard by sailors approaching the area. Get to the bottom of the disappearances and free the tortured souls that inhabit the area.

docs.title: In the past year many adventurers have reported that a town exists in
docs.text: In the past year many adventurers have reported that a town exists in the once declared uninhabitable plains of western Hyperborea. These same adventurers report sightings of supernatural beings. Some say they are ghosts, others say demons, but no one knows for sure. There is a rumor that this hidden town was cursed long ago. Although, this is only a rumor. This quest involves seeking out this supernatural town, discovering the truth behind its existance, and fulfilling the request of its citizens. This quest involves no combat, although it does require careful attention to detail and slight exploration. Feel free to try it at any level.
