docs.title: The Arctic Elves are a subrace of the elves that have adapted to living in
docs.text: The Arctic Elves are a subrace of the elves that have adapted to living in the far north of Hyperborea. Like all elves, they are bright and agile, but suffer from somewhat fragile bodies. Arctic elves are often at odds with the humans of northern Hyperborea, constantly fighting over territory and ancient artifacts of power in order to expand their evil society.

docs.title: The Barbarians are an offshoot of modern human society that settled south
docs.text: The Barbarians are an offshoot of modern human society that settled south of Darkwind City in a settlement known as Canith. Their rugged lifestyle tends towards the development of stronger, healthier bodies than most humans. Canith society values order, and pursuit of the common good. Barbarians are generally friendly to strangers and always eager to learn about exotic people and places.

docs.title: Crannian gnome- A race of small, misshapen, dwarf-like creatures that
docs.text: Crannian gnome- A race of small, misshapen, dwarf-like creatures that dwell in the earth. The name 'gnome' was given to them by the medieval scholar Paracelcus, in an attempt to describe the most important of the earth spirits. Gnomes live under the earth, where they guard treasures. According to Paracelcus they move as easily through the earth as humans walk upon the ground. They cannot stand the light of the sun, for even one ray would turn them to stone. Some sources claim they spend the hours during daylight as a toad. They are in some way related to goblins and dwarfs. They have been known to steal neglected human babies to raise as their own.

docs.title: Dark Elves live deep underground where they worship forgotten gods of
docs.text: Dark Elves live deep underground where they worship forgotten gods of evil and chaos. They are adapted to living in darkness and rarely seeing the light of day. Dark Elves are quite agile and mentally superior to most races, but lack a certain degree of constitution.

docs.title: The humans that live around Darkwind City are collectively known as
docs.text: The humans that live around Darkwind City are collectively known as Darkwinders. Darkwinders are about average among the civilized races in terms of physical and mental powers, but are well accepted by most other cultures due to the importance of the city in world affairs. Darkwinders are outgoing and adventurous, always seeking out new experiences. They are also expert traders and negotiators. Being adventurous in nature, Darkwinder souls are more inclined to take on other forms. Thus they do not suffer from reincarnating into other races.

docs.title: The Desert Dwarves live in a small settlement in the deserts of Souvrael.
docs.text: The Desert Dwarves live in a small settlement in the deserts of Souvrael. The Dwarves live in a peaceful, just society, generally unaffected by outside influences. Physically, they are a short, hardy race. In addition to an innate resistance to magic and psionics, they tend to be quite healthy and strong, but suffer somewhat from a stubbiness in their limbs. Despite their strength, their small size often also creates difficulties in wielding larger weapons.

docs.title: The Desert Nomads are the wanderers of Souvrael. They are a deeply religious
docs.text: The Desert Nomads are the wanderers of Souvrael. They are a deeply religious people who follow the teachings of their prophet. The are quick learners who have adapted to living in the open desert. Desert Nomads are known for their great hospitality, despite the harshness of their habitat.

docs.title: The Duergar are a race of evil subterranean dwarves who have been twisted
docs.text: The Duergar are a race of evil subterranean dwarves who have been twisted by dark forces into hateful caricatures of surface dwarves. They are short, stout and have hardy constitutions, enabling them to hold their liquor and resist small amounts of magic and mental influence. Despite being quite strong, Duergar have problems balancing larger weapons due to their shortness.

docs.title: Glavians are humans that hail from the mountain kingdom of Glavia. Glavians
docs.text: Glavians are humans that hail from the mountain kingdom of Glavia. Glavians are a generally good-aligned people used to opposing demonic forces. Their society is otherwise peaceful and pastoral. Glavians are an inoffensive, likeable lot, with an open mind to new experiences.

docs.title: The Gypsy people are a skilled, artful traveling people.  They are very smart,
docs.text: The Gypsy people are a skilled, artful traveling people. They are very smart, charismatic and light fingered. Singing, dancing, telling stories, fortune telling and lifting money from the rubes are the everyday events in the life of the Gyspy. They prefer to wear bright colors, and usually speak freely, looking to make the next big score.

docs.title: The elven kingdom south of Darkwind City is the home of the High Elves. High
docs.text: The elven kingdom south of Darkwind City is the home of the High Elves. High Elf culture as a whole tends towards goodness and lawfulness in the context of harmony with nature. High Elves have keen senses and are generally superior mentally to most civilized races. Physically however, they can be somewhat fragile and lack the robustness of other races.

docs.title: Hyperborean gnomes are a race of small humanoids that inhabit the more
docs.text: Hyperborean gnomes are a race of small humanoids that inhabit the more habitable rural areas of Hyperborea. They are bright and nimble, with a natural resistance to variations in the environment. They have a slight tendency to work towards the causes of good, if only because they are subject to attack by the forces of evil. Like all gnomes, they are quite small compared to other races, and have difficulty managing larger weapons.

docs.title: Ice Gnolls are an evil warrior race that appears to be a cross of some
docs.text: Ice Gnolls are an evil warrior race that appears to be a cross of some humanoid and a hyena. They are physically powerful but are lacking somewhat in intellect. Ice gnolls live to kill and eat; who their victims are is largely irrelevant.

docs.title: Ice Ogres are large brutish humanoids that live in the cold wastes of
docs.text: Ice Ogres are large brutish humanoids that live in the cold wastes of Hyperborea. Large numbers of them are regularly hired as mercenaries by the giants to wage war against more civilized races. They are immensely strong and rugged, but dimwitted and clumsy as well. They have no real culture to speak of except a penchant for violence. While not quite giant sized, ice ogres are large enough that they can wield large weapons much more easily than most other races.

docs.title: The Kender have always been hidden somewhere around the realms of
docs.text: The Kender have always been hidden somewhere around the realms of Darkwind. They are small jovial creatures with a love of adventure and no fear. They are extremely agile, but are not known for a high level of common sense.

docs.title: Northmen are humans who settled in the frigid north. Northmen are widespread
docs.text: Northmen are humans who settled in the frigid north. Northmen are widespread throughout Hyperborea, although most live in the city of Grimsfjord. Northmen are expert traders and hagglers, due to the need to trade with the southern cities for various goods not produced in Hyperborea.

docs.title: The pixies are a race of small mischievous little fae. These smart
docs.text: The pixies are a race of small mischievous little fae. These smart little critters excel at finding ways to scare and trick their unsuspecting victims. They have beautiful silk-like wings that enable them to explore the skies and are naturally protected from the magical abilities of those who would hunt them. This sadistic little fae folk cares little about goodness.

docs.title: The Rift Duergar are a race of evil subterranean dwarves who have been
docs.text: The Rift Duergar are a race of evil subterranean dwarves who have been twisted by dark forces into hateful caricatures of surface dwarves. They are short, stout and have hardy constitutions, enabling them to hold their liquor and resist small amounts of magic and mental influence. Despite being quite strong, Rift Duergar have problems balancing larger weapons due to their stature.

docs.title: The Scro are an advanced form of orc that is well adapted to the rigors of
docs.text: The Scro are an advanced form of orc that is well adapted to the rigors of travelling in wildspace. While they are not quite as strong nor robust as their more primitive cousins, they make up for this by possessing greater mental faculties and resistances to forces encountered in their more exotic travels.

docs.title: The Shel-zaranites are an ancient offshoot of the elves that live deep
docs.text: The Shel-zaranites are an ancient offshoot of the elves that live deep underground. In their secluded city, they worship forgotten gods of evil and chaos. Dark Elves are quite agile and mentally superior to most races, but are often sickly and lack constitution. Being an underground race however, they are well adapted to lightless conditions.

docs.title: The Sidhe are a race of vile demonic creatures. Originating from the
docs.text: The Sidhe are a race of vile demonic creatures. Originating from the influential fae population of Talamh Darag. These Sidhe were infected by a vampiric condition affecting their society on a large level. The now unseelie Sidhe are known for their evil acts, magical abilities and the moth-like wings that enable them to descend from the ground. The magical nature of the Sidhe fae allows them to regenerate their abilities with greater ease then any other race would be able to. Their weak body is able to purge toxics from their bloodstream at an increased rate, but suffers greatly where raw physical power is concerned.

docs.title: The elven kingdom located on the highway between Darkwind City and the
docs.text: The elven kingdom located on the highway between Darkwind City and the frozen tundra is the home of the Silver Elves. Silver Elves are also known as Moon Elves. Silver Elf culture tends towards goodness and lawfulness so as to please Luna, the moon Goddess. Silver Elves have keen night vision, exude charisma, and are typically more intelligent, though less wise, than other races. Physically they are more nimble than what is typical, though they are rather fragile of constitution.

docs.title: Souvraelis are the native humans of Souvrael who choose to live in cities
docs.text: Souvraelis are the native humans of Souvrael who choose to live in cities instead of leading a nomadic existence. Their culture has evolved over time towards a more cosmopolitan lifestyle based on trade and education. As such, they are cunning negotiators, and have a thirst for knowledge.

docs.title: Stone Dwarves are a society of surface dwarves who long ago dedicated their
docs.text: Stone Dwarves are a society of surface dwarves who long ago dedicated their lives to working in the underworld in the service of Mitra. Like most dwarves, they are short and stout and can hold their liquor, but Stone Dwarves also have a high degree of goodness and lawfulness ingrained into them at an early age. Their small size makes it difficult for them to wield larger weapons, and working in cramped mines have a detrimental effect on their joints, limiting their agility.

docs.title: The sky, mountains, and high places such as the tops of very tall trees
docs.text: The sky, mountains, and high places such as the tops of very tall trees are the favorite home of the Sylphs. Members of the Faerie race, the Sylph are roughly human in appearance with the exception of the fully functional wings on their backs. The Sylph are a culture that tends towards goodness and lawfulness, but also one known for being able to hold their own when it comes to the hearty consumption of the strong libations served at the various festivals they hold. The Sylph are an attractive race with looks to match their mental powers and quickness, though they tend to be weaker and less robust than other races.

docs.title: Thraxian draconians hail from the village of Thrax in eastern Hyperborea.
docs.text: Thraxian draconians hail from the village of Thrax in eastern Hyperborea. While roughly humanoid in shape, they bear a striking similarity to their dragon cousins, including small, vestigial wings and a fiery breath weapon. They maintain some of the dragons' raw physical power and intellect as well. Their alien natures are not well received by other races, and their clawed hands are not well adapted to using most tools.

docs.title: The Uruk are a loose tribe of marauding orcs which live in the Darkwind
docs.text: The Uruk are a loose tribe of marauding orcs which live in the Darkwind area, looting and pillaging small settlements. The Uruk value strength and stamina over useless thought or a pretty face. They are a warlike race that trains for battle from birth to death, acquiring a degree of proficiency in the use of all weapons. They are particularly adapted to living in marginal areas like shallow caves, or fetid swamps.

docs.title: The wayfarians are a race of elves that have been oppressed by forces of evil
docs.text: The wayfarians are a race of elves that have been oppressed by forces of evil for as long as their culture has been around. A powerful Paladin heroine 'Enelya Ar-Feiniel' who is now revered as their patron of adventurers sought out Mitra's blessing to empower and protect her proud folk. This blessing resulted in a holy and virtuous aura surrounding each member of the Wayfarian race. This aura formed a defense against the evil acts of their foes and enabled them to strike out with a holy fury. Finally the Wayfarians were able to beat off their oppressors and build a new city. Their combined auras helped form a powerful holy dome to protect this city against those who would seek to destroy it.

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS object clone_limited_object(string name, int limit) DESCRIPTION Clones a new object much like the clone_object efun would. The difference, however, is that clone_limited_object will register the new object with the unique tracking system and only allow a limited number of instances of the object to be in the game at a given time. Note that the pathname must be complete, which means there are no relative paths allowed. NOTE: clone_limited_object will not check if the object in question has been cloned before using clone_object. Thus, it is entirely possible to clone several instances of an object using clone_object and still get a valid object from clone_limited_object even after there are more objects in the game than desired. However, all calls to clone_limited_object itself fully respect object limitations. EXAMPLE // Clone limited sword object sword, sword2, sword3; sword = clone_limited_object("/obj/sword", 2); sword2 = clone_limited_object("/obj/sword", 2); sword3 = clone_limited_object("/obj/sword", 2); // Sword 3 above will be 0, since only two swords // will be allowed in-game at a time. HISTORY Originally created along with the new additions to UNIQUE_D daemon by James on January 17, 2004. SEE ALSO blueprint(E), clonep(E), destruct(E), clones(E), load_name(E), load_object(E), move_object(E), uids(C), program_name(E), clone_object(E), clone_unique_object(E)

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS object clone_unique_object(string name) DESCRIPTION Clones a new object much like the clone_object efun would. The difference, however, is that clone_unique_object will register the new object with the unique tracking system and only allow a single instance of the unique object to be in the game at a given time. Note that the pathname must be complete, which means there are no relative paths allowed. NOTE: clone_unique_object will not check if the object in question has been cloned before using clone_object. Thus, it is entirely possible to clone several instances of an object using clone_object and still get a valid object from clone_unique_object. However, after a single unique object is created, any additional calls to clone_unique_object will not produce a new object as long as the old object is still in the game. EXAMPLE // Clone unique sword object sword, sword2; sword = clone_unique_object("/obj/sword"); // Following call to clone_unique_object returns 0 sword2 = clone_unique_object("/obj/sword"); if(!sword2) write("The second sword wasn't cloned!\n"); HISTORY Originally created along with the UNIQUE_D daemon by James on January 3, 2004. SEE ALSO blueprint(E), clonep(E), destruct(E), clones(E), load_name(E), load_object(E), move_object(E), uids(C), program_name(E), clone_object(E), clone_limited_object(E)

docs.title: void room_message(object *aoPeople, object oRoom, string sMessage)
docs.text: void room_message(object *aoPeople, object oRoom, string sMessage) Similar to tell_room(), but allows variable text depending on who is receiving the message. The message string is in the same format as general emotes, although this usage cannot handle passing non-living objects, and does not allow special cases separated by ||. The composed message sMessage is spammed to the room oRoom, with the array aoPeople being the array of people involved in the message.

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS int *shuffle(int A, int B) DESCRIPTION Returns an array of integers from 'A' to 'B' in random order. EXAMPLE int *aiNums = shuffle(1, 10); // aiNums will contain the numbers 1-10 in random order within the array // eg. '({ 4, 2, 7, 5, 1, 9, 3, 6, 10, 8 })' SEE ALSO random

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS void tell_visible(object oRoom, string sMsg, mixed xExclude, object oVisCheck) DESCRIPTION Sends the message '<sMsg>' to all living objects in object '<oRoom>' that are visible to object '<oVisCheck>' except for objects '<xExclude>', which can be either an object or an array of objects. If the function 'catch_tell' is defines in the objects this message goes to, then it will be called with '<sMsg>' as the argument. EXAMPLE // This first example will tell all living objects visible to // this_player() in the room the message supplied. tell_visible(environment(this_player()), "I can see you!\n", 0, this_player()); SEE ALSO environment_visible, visible_inventory, visible, visible_to, catch_tell

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS varargs mixed *visible(mixed xItem, object oEnv) DESCRIPTION Checks if an object IDing to string '<xItem>' or object '<xItem>' is visible to the calling_object in optional environment '<oEnv>'. If '<oEnv>' is not supplied it defaults to 'this_object()'. This function first checks if '<xItem>' is present in '<oEnv>' and if so passes it on to the function 'visible_to' and returns an array like '({ <object>, <visibility flags> })'. If an object is found and visible then index [0] will be the object itself and index [1] will be the visibility flags used to see the object. If an object is not found, or is not visible then the result will be a NULL_ARRAY or '({ 0, 0 })' EXAMPLE // This first example will look for an object that id's to the word // 'torch' and if not visible to the player will tell them so. if (!visible("torch", environment(this_player()))[0]) write("You don't see a torch anywhere!\n"); // This second example will take the object the player is currently // attacking and if not present or visible, tell them so. object oTarget; oTarget = this_player()->query_attacking(); if (!visible(oTarget, environment(this_player()))[0]) write("You don't see your target here anywhere!\n"); SEE ALSO visible_to, environment_visible, tell_visible, visible_inventory

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text: SYNOPSIS varargs int visible_to(object oItem, object oObserver, object oEnv) DESCRIPTION Returns 1 if '<oItem>' is visible to '<oObserver>' in optional environment '<oEnv>'. If '<oEnv>' is not suppled, it defaults to the environment of '<oItem>'. This function performs all standard checks including 'query_invis' checks modified by the 'see_invis' attribute, 'query_inventory_hidden' checks, and finally spectrum checks. NOTE: It does not check whether '<oObserver>' and '<oItem>' are actually in the same environment or even have access to each other's environments in any way. EXAMPLE // This first example will take an object 'sword' that is laying on the // ground and if not visible to the player, tell them so. object oObj; oObj = present("sword", environment(this_player())); if (!visible_to(oObj, this_player())) write("You see no sword here!\n"); SEE ALSO environment_visible, tell_visible, visible_inventory, visible, query_invis, query_inventory_hidden, see_invis, present

docs.title: Being A Weapon Specialist - The Inside Story
docs.text: Being A Weapon Specialist - The Inside Story Specializing in a weapon allows you to do exactly that - become a 'specialist' in the use of that weapon type. The most basic advantage of being a specialist is that as you use the weapon, you will find yourself getting better at using it, as well as doing more damage with every hit. However, because of your focus on that particular weapon type, your ability with other weapons will be less than it would if you were not a specialist. There are three categories which describe weapons: First, size. This is the only category which must be specified in order to specialize. Weapons come in four sizes: small, medium, large, and huge. A character may specialize in any of three sizes: small, medium, or large. Each size also grants specialization in the next larger size, so a character who chooses small weapons is specialized in small and medium, while a character who chooses large is specialized in large and huge. Second, damage type. There are four possibilities here: slash, pierce, blunt, and cleave. Choosing a damage type is not required; however, a character who chooses a damage type will benefit more from specialization than one who does not. The character can choose two damage types, in which case he specializes in weapons that do both damage types. If the combination is any except slash/pierce, the damage is even greater than the bonus for specializing in one damage type, but this is not true if the combination is slash/pierce. Third, weapon type. Most weapons are regular melee weapons and require no specification of type. However, there are two special categories that a character can specialize in, and choosing either of these categories adds an extra bonus to the character's damage with the weapon. The categories are missile and polearm. Once you begin your specialization training, you will find yourself getting better with practice. When the time is right, you may return here to train to a higher level of weapon specialization, gaining even more of a benefit with your chosen weapon type. There are ten levels of weapon specialization, each more difficult to attain than the one before. If you should so choose, you may change your weapon specialization choice by retraining here. However, you will lose nearly all benefit from your old specialization. If your newly chosen specialization shares one characteristic with your old, you will retain a third of your training, up to a training level of three. If your newly chosen specialization shares two characteristics with your old, you may retain half of your training, up to a training level of five. If your new specialization is completely unlike your old, you must start completely over. Be sure to keep your guild restrictions in mind when choosing a weapon in which to specialize. Read 'help types' for more information on weapon sizes and damage types.

docs.title: You must pick a size category in which to specialize.  Remember
docs.text: You must pick a size category in which to specialize. Remember that each size also gives specialization in the next larger size; 'small' is really small and medium, 'medium' gives medium and large, and 'large' allows use of large and huge weapons. Small weapons: daggers, saps, small short swords, hand axes, etc. Medium weapons: larger short swords, maces, clubs, longer swords Large weapons: longswords, battleaxes, long maces, shorter staves Huge weapons: awl pikes, two-handed swords, greatbows, long staves You may choose a damage type or combination to specialize in. Damage types are slash, pierce, blunt, and cleave, and you may choose none, one, or two of these types. If you choose two, a weapon must have both types in order to fit into your specialty. Slash: Most sword variants, naginata, some polearms Pierce: daggers, rapiers, spears, bows, wooden stakes Blunt: staves, maces, clubs, hammers, rocks Cleave: axes, halberds, cleavers, some polearms Note that there is some overlap, but not much. Some shortswords are almost equally usable as piercing weapons or slashing weapons. Some polearms are fitted with two different kinds of surfaces for harming a foe, such as a halberd's iron spike for piercing and wide blade for cleaving. But the majority of weapons on Darkwind are one type only. Finally, you may choose to specialize in missile or pole weapons. If you do not specify, then you will train in normal melee (non-pole, non-missile) weapons. Missile: bows, crossbows, slings, throwing daggers, darts Pole: most staves, halberds, spears, tridents, etc.

docs.title: Actions.
docs.text: Actions. Use actions when you want to know what special things you can try in your current room. This is useful for screenreader users because some room details are hidden in descriptions, signs, objects, or local commands. Actions summarizes the most important exploration hooks in one place. Common forms: actions List special actions, things to look at, and things to read in the room. interact roomactions readables Other names for the same command. The output may include lines like: Actions here are "pull", "search", "touch", and "travel". Things to look at here are "altar", "pillar", and "markings". Things to read here are "read sign" and "read inscription". Actions are commands you can type directly. Things to look at are room details you can inspect with look, for example look altar. Things to read are shown as full commands, for example read sign.

docs.title: Exits.
docs.text: Exits. Use exits when you want to know where you can move from the current room. Common forms: exits List visible exits from your current room. look With screenreader support on, look also includes the visible exits in the room summary. Movement commands are usually directions, such as north, south, east, west, up, down, enter, exit, northeast, northwest, southeast, and southwest. Some rooms hide exits until you examine the room or an object in the room. If you feel stuck, try look, then look at anything interesting mentioned by the room.

docs.title: Inventory.
docs.text: Inventory. Use inventory to review what you are carrying and wearing. Common forms: inventory Show your inventory. i Short alias for inventory. look <item> Look more closely at something you are carrying. wear <item> Wear armor or clothing, if the item can be worn. wield <item> Wield a weapon, if the item can be wielded. drop <item> Drop an item, if the item can be dropped. Some special objects cannot be dropped, sold, or put into containers.

docs.title: Items.
docs.text: Items. Use items to list visible non-living objects in your current room. This command is useful when you want to hear only the objects in the room, without NPCs, players, exits, or the room description. Common forms: items List visible items in the room. look <item> Look more closely at one item from the list. get <item> Pick up an item, if it can be taken. put <item> in <container> Put an item into a visible container, if allowed. If several visible items have the same name, the command condenses them and gives a count.

docs.title: Look.
docs.text: Look. The look command describes your current room. When screenreader support is on, look uses a conversational room summary. It tells you where you are, gives the first sentence of the room description, lists the exits, then lists visible NPCs, visible players, and visible items. Common forms: look Describe the room. l Short alias for look. look <thing> Look directly at a named person, creature, item, or room detail. actions List room-specific actions, things to look at, and things to read. exa <thing> examine <thing> Other ways to look closely at something. If the room is dark or you are blind, look may not be able to describe your surroundings.

docs.title: NPCs.
docs.text: NPCs. Use npcs to list visible non-player characters in your current room. This command is useful when look gives too much information or when you want to quickly know what creatures, shopkeepers, guards, quest givers, or monsters are nearby. Common forms: npcs List visible NPCs in the room. look <npc> Look more closely at one NPC from the list. kill <npc> Start combat with an NPC, if combat is allowed. If several visible NPCs have the same name, the command condenses them and gives a count.

docs.title: Players.
docs.text: Players. Use players to list other visible players in your current room. The command does not include you in the list. It only reports other player characters that you can currently see. Common forms: players List other visible players in the room. look <player> Look more closely at a player from the list. say <message> Speak to everyone in the room. tell <player> <message> Send a private message to a player. Invisible players or players hidden from you may not appear.

docs.title: The Darkflow web client.
docs.text: The Darkflow web client. Darkflow is Darkwind's official web client. Open play.darkwind.ai in a web browser and play. There is nothing to install. It is a real terminal with everything telnet offers, plus optional graphical features driven by the game. Panels. Dockable panels show vitals, stats, worth, an XP monitor, your room, a room image, inventory, group, chat, quests, achievements, buffs, the sky, fishing, and more. Panels can be docked to either side or floated, and your layout is remembered between sessions. Live map. A graphical tile map is built from the exploration of all players. Clicking a room on the map walks you there step by step, and the client verifies each step with the game before taking the next. Area maps. The command areas map followed by an area number opens that area's map for browsing in its own Area Map pane, separate from the live map. Sound. Game-driven sound effects and ambient audio, with volume and mute controls. Help. Help topics open in a pop-up window. With screenreader mode on, help is shown as plain text through the pager instead. Automation. Aliases, triggers, highlights, and scripts, plus settings export and import as JSON. Comfort. Dark and light themes, command history, tab completion, and screenreader support, including a setting that sends set screenreader on to the game. Related help: help monitor, help alias, help scripts, help areas, and help interface screenreader.

docs.title: Screenreader support.
docs.text: Screenreader support. Screenreader support changes some command output so it is easier to hear through a screenreader. Common forms: set screenreader on Turn screenreader support on. set screenreader off Turn screenreader support off. Darkflow closes its visual tutorial hover when screenreader support is turned on and repeats the current objective as linear terminal text. Turning screenreader support off restores the hover when the tutorial is still active. Use "tutorial continue", "tutorial hint", "tutorial skip", and "tutorial restart" to control it entirely from the command line. set Show your current settings. When screenreader support is on, some commands use plainer language, fewer visual tables, and less decorative formatting. The help command also checks /public/docs/vihelp first for screenreader-specific help topics, then falls back to the normal help system. Useful screenreader-friendly commands include look, actions, exits, npcs, players, items, inventory, score, and who.

docs.title: Cyberware.
docs.text: Cyberware. Cyberware is machinery grafted into your own body. An installed implant grants its bonuses, such as stats, resistances, or chance-based proc effects, for as long as it stays inside you. Every implant occupies one or more body locations: eyes, ears, brain, skull, jaw, throat, neck, spine, heart, lungs, torso, skin, shoulders, arms, hands, legs, and feet. Only one implant may occupy a location. Implants also strain the body. No implant can cost more than 10 strain, and the 24 cyberware locations create an absolute capacity of 240. Your natural limit starts at 6 and grows with your level: one point per 10 levels, plus larger bonuses at levels 50, 100, 150, 200, and 250. Cyber-touched origins grant 2 extra strain each, to a maximum of 10. Each remort closes part of the distance between your natural limit and 240, reaching full capacity at remort 50. You cannot install an implant that would push your total strain past your limit, and an implant may demand a minimum level or stranger things before your body accepts it. World cyberware comes in standard, refined, military, and artifact qualities. Higher qualities provide more specialized or powerful benefits, but source level still matters. Artifact systems may consume the maximum strain or occupy several locations. Commands: cyberware [player] Show your installed implants, occupied body locations, and strain. Wizards may name a currently connected player to inspect that player's installed cyberware and strain. cyberscan <implant> Inspect an implant's type, grade, body locations, strain, visibility, and proc count before installing it. install <implant> Have a ripperdoc install an implant you are carrying. extract <implant or location> uninstall <implant or location> Have a ripperdoc remove an installed implant, returning it to your inventory. Installation and extraction require a staffed ripperdoc clinic, and the ripperdoc will not operate while you are fighting. The Forbidden Replacement Table in Nethrys Undercity's Ripperdoc Quarter is a formal clinic. Cyberware status and implant scans remain available anywhere. Use "engage ripperdoc" at the clinic to review hardware, see the exact service fee, and confirm the procedure. Installation costs 10,000 coins per point of implant strain, with a 10,000 coin minimum. Extraction costs 5,000 coins per strain, with a 5,000 coin minimum. Installed implants cannot be dropped and stay with you across sessions. They are hidden from normal inventory while installed, but remain visible through cyberware or implants. Grade does not change persistence: standard, refined, military, and artifact chrome all persist normally. Only hardware explicitly created as temporary or nonpersistent is excluded, and normal clinic installation rejects hardware that cannot be preserved. A saved implant can be temporarily unavailable when its blueprint cannot load or a one-of-a-kind implant is active elsewhere; its record remains for a later retry. Only active restored implants consume strain, so missing or inactive hardware releases its strain automatically. Some implants are outwardly visible and anyone who looks at you will see them; hidden ones stay your secret. Procs trigger on their own in combat: on your hits, when you take damage, when you are badly hurt, or when you make a kill, each with its own chance and cooldown. General Tekal forbids cybernetics, so recoverable implants are uncommon and normally expose an illicit source: contraband wetware, augmented criminals, Green Door or Reca operatives, forbidden experiments, or repurposed machinery. Specialists, elites, and named enemies are the usual sources of rarer hardware. Shimmerdeep's Miura do not implant themselves; cyberware found there comes from corrupted external machinery and mechaplants. See also: help effects, help equip.

docs.title: Kingdoms.
docs.text: Kingdoms. Kingdoms are player-ruled realms. Each kingdom has a Ruler, a charter, a roster of citizens, its own nobility titles, and a sigil carried by every citizen. Founding. New kingdoms are chartered and activated with the help of the game administration. If you want a throne, speak with the admins. Joining. Citizenship is by induction, in person. A noble with the power to induct must stand in the same room as you and make the offer. You are then asked whether you wish to become a citizen. Answer yes or no. You must be at least level 5 and cannot already belong to another kingdom. Citizenship. You carry your kingdom's sigil. It cannot be dropped, sold, or stolen, and it marks you as a citizen to anyone who looks at you. You also gain the kingdom channel. Type kchat followed by a message to speak to every citizen. Type ekchat followed by a message to emote to them. Nobility. The Ruler may create custom titles. Each title can grant any mix of four powers: inducting members, removing members, assigning titles, and owning a castle. New citizens start with the title Citizen. The title Ruler is reserved for the kingdom's owner. Management. The Ruler types managekingdom to open the management menu, the Ministry of Administrative Affairs. The Deeds And Titles section sets and views the charter, creates, edits, and removes titles, views citizens, inducts new members, bestows titles, and strips citizenship. The Heraldry And Propaganda section names the sigil, chooses its colors, and writes its descriptions. The Castle Keep And Environs section is the office of the Royal Engineer. The whole kingdom hears arrivals and departures on the kingdom channel. Related help: help clans, help kchat.

docs.title: Your Journey Through Darkwind
docs.text: Your Journey Through Darkwind A stage-by-stage walkthrough from your first steps to seasoned adventurer. Each stage is its own short help page. Read them as your character grows, not all at once. help stage1: your first minutes. The tutorial, useful display settings, and finding your way around town. help stage2: gear up and learn to fight, levels 1 to 5. Safer combat and corpse-loot settings. help stage3: choose your path. Guilds, remote advancement, and leveling. help stage4: see the world, levels 5 to 30. Areas, wayshards, quests, and what death really costs. help stage5: money and craft. Remote banking, the market, and professions. help stage6: find your people. Channels, parties, clans, and kingdoms. help stage7: sharpen the blade, levels 30 to 100. Bosses, dungeons, and uniques. help stage8: renown and rebirth, level 100 and beyond. Hero, legend, and the remort endgame. At every stage: screenreader mode tailors output for you (see help screenreader), "help list" browses every section, and the bug, idea, and typo commands send feedback straight to the builders. See also: help stage1, help basics, help screenreader, help feedback.

docs.title: Stage 1 of 8: Your First Minutes
docs.text: Stage 1 of 8: Your First Minutes A short tutorial starts automatically for new characters and teaches looking, moving, gear, and safe combat. Darkflow shows it in a hover window. Type "tutorial" to see your current step and "tutorial continue" to continue in any client. Learn to look at things with "look <thing>", check your "inventory", and read your "score". If you get lost, "ncot" returns you to the Center of Town, where the Newbie Tome Dispenser (pull lever, read tome) holds the town directions. Screenreader mode intentionally keeps visual-only detail and monitor settings quiet. Use "set list" to review your saved options. If screenreader mode is not already enabled, run "set screenreader on" to enable screenreader-friendly output. Read: help tutorial, help basics, help movement, help new, help set, help screenreader. Next: help stage2. Index: help guide.

docs.title: Stage 2 of 8: Gear Up and Learn to Fight, levels 1 to 5
docs.text: Stage 2 of 8: Gear Up and Learn to Fight, levels 1 to 5 Erga's newbie store (from the Center of Town: four west, one south) hands out free equipment fit for anyone under level 5; the donation room (five north, one east) has castoffs from veterans. Wear and wield everything, then practice on the newbie farm. Death carries no penalty at level 5 and under, so take risks now and learn kill, assess, and wimpy. Ask questions freely on the newbie channel; everyone started here. Choose your corpse automation: "set autogold on" takes coins only, while "set autoloot on" takes coins and every gettable item, making autogold redundant and filling your inventory faster. "set autokill on" does not attack by itself; it only makes a manually entered bare "kill" choose the first visible NPC. Keep naming targets until you are comfortable. "set wimpy 25" retreats below 25 percent HP when an escape is possible. Screenreader mode already condenses combat into short summaries, so the combatbrief display switches are not needed. Read: help kill, help equipment, help wimpy, help combat, help communication, help set. Next: help stage3. Index: help guide.

docs.title: Stage 3 of 8: Choose Your Path
docs.text: Stage 3 of 8: Choose Your Path Once the farm feels easy, pick a guild; it defines your abilities for the climb ahead. Browse the roster, the playstyle archetypes, and which pairings work before committing. Level at the adventurers guild with "advance". Experience costs grow with each level, and your stats shape what your abilities can do. You can handle normal advancement from anywhere. "remcost" is a safe, read-only report of stat costs, available raises, caps, and experience needed. Use "remadvance <stat>" to raise one stat or "remadvance level" to buy every level you can currently afford. Guild advancement still happens at your guild hall with "advance guild". Despite their names, the rem commands work before remort. Non-remort players may use "set autolevel on" to spend experience on levels automatically; leave it off when you want to bank experience for stat raises. Remort souls always level automatically. Read: help guilds, help archetypes, help combos, help roles, help leveling, help costs, help stats, help set. Next: help stage4. Index: help guide.

docs.title: Stage 4 of 8: See the World, levels 5 to 30
docs.text: Stage 4 of 8: See the World, levels 5 to 30 The "areas" command catalogs every region with level ranges. Characters up to level 10 already know the newbie-area wayshards, and touching new shards opens fast travel as you explore. Pick up quests for structured goals and bonus experience. Above level 5 death costs 10 percent of your experience on hand. Your corpse keeps your gear, the church will bring you back, and other players can avenge you to restore what you lost. Read: help areas, help wayshards, help recall, help quests, help death, help avengement. Next: help stage5. Index: help guide.

docs.title: Stage 5 of 8: Money and Craft
docs.text: Stage 5 of 8: Money and Craft Open a bank account early; auction bids and some purchases are backed by bank liens, and your balance is shared across every branch. "rembank" or "rembank balance" opens the account on first use and reports its balance, lien, and spendable amount. From anywhere that is not warded against teleportation, "rembank deposit all" banks every carried coin and "rembank withdraw <amount>" brings coins back. Use "rembank lien" to check reserved funds. The command "rembank transfer <amount|all> from <alt>" pulls funds from one of your registered alts into the current character. Balance and lien checks still work in warded rooms. Learn the player-driven economy: shops, the remote market, and the live auction channel. When you want a break from fighting, professions like fishing, mining, and smithing earn steadily and feed the market. Read: help economy, help bank, help market, help auction, help professions, help fishing. Next: help stage6. Index: help guide.

docs.title: Stage 6 of 8: Find Your People
docs.text: Stage 6 of 8: Find Your People Darkwind is social. Channels connect the whole game; parties share the fight and the spoils; clans are player-run organizations with wars and coffers; kingdoms crown player rulers with their own nobility. Pick a divine patron when the gods start to notice you. Alignment and devotion open their own doors. Read: help communication, help party, help clans, help kingdoms, help patron, help deities, help discord. Next: help stage7. Index: help guide.

docs.title: Stage 7 of 8: Sharpen the Blade, levels 30 to 100
docs.text: Stage 7 of 8: Sharpen the Blade, levels 30 to 100 Mid-game is about power and polish: track your buffs and debuffs, hunt boss monsters and invasions, brave the eternal dungeon, duel in the arena, and chase achievements, daily rewards, and leaderboard rank. Unique weapons and armour, one copy in the whole game, are out there for the claiming. Read: help effects, help buffs, help bosses, help invasions, help eternal, help arena, help achievements, help daily, help uniques. Next: help stage8. Index: help guide.

docs.title: Stage 8 of 8: Renown and Rebirth, level 100 and beyond
docs.text: Stage 8 of 8: Renown and Rebirth, level 100 and beyond At level 100 your level becomes renown: HERO, ADV, or VILN by your deeds. Level 150 makes you a LEGEND and unlocks a free additional multichar slot. New mythic multichar registration is disabled. At 250 the true endgame opens: remort, a rebirth that trades your level for permanent boon points and starts the climb again, stronger each cycle. Specialization and the metaphysician path round out a veteran's power. Read: help hero, help legend, help remort, help boons, help specialization, help meta, help multichars. Index: help guide.

docs.title: Darkwind help for screenreader users.
docs.text: Darkwind help for screenreader users. This help path is shown first because your screenreader setting is on. If a screenreader-specific help topic exists, you will hear that version. If it does not exist yet, Darkwind falls back to the normal help topic. New to Darkwind? Type help guide for a short, stage-by-stage walkthrough from your first steps to the endgame. Good first commands: help basics look How to read your current room. help basics exits How to find where you can move. help basics npcs How to list non-player characters in the room. help basics players How to list other players in the room. help basics items How to list visible items in the room. help basics actions How to find room-specific actions, things to look at, and things to read. help basics inventory How to review what you are carrying. help interface screenreader How to turn screenreader support on or off. Useful commands while exploring: look exits npcs players items actions inventory score who Use help list to hear the available help sections. Use help list basics to hear topics in the basics section.

docs.title: DarkWind
docs.text: # DarkWind DarkWind is a text-based multiplayer RPG set across Blackmar, its continents, its moons, and the strange places between them. The world has been under development since 1992 and continues to grow through player activity, staff building, quests, guilds, professions, events, and long-running story threads. You play by typing commands. Movement, combat, conversation, crafting, travel, shopping, guild abilities, spellcasting, and social systems all happen through the command line. ## Start Here | Page | Use | | --- | --- | | [Getting Started](getting_started.md) | First steps after character creation | | [Basic Commands](basics/commands.md) | Common commands for movement, inventory, help, and character status | | [Account And Session](gameplay/account.md) | Tutorial, saving, quitting, passwords, reboots, and switching characters | | [DarkWind City Services](gameplay/city-services.md) | Shops, bank, church, training, donation room, and city landmarks | | [Communication](gameplay/communication.md) | Channels, tells, mail, emotes, language, and social tools | | [Combat](gameplay/combat.md) | Attacking, assessing, healing, wimpy, and staying alive | | [Death And Recovery](gameplay/death.md) | Ghosts, prayer, resurrection, avengement, and recovery | | [Travel](gameplay/travel.md) | Recall, ferries, ships, domains, hazards, and navigation | | [Guilds](gameplay/guilds.md) | Guild roster, joining, changing guilds, and choosing a play style | | [Economy](gameplay/economy.md) | Gold, banks, shops, auctions, professions, inns, pubs, and markets | ## Useful Commands | Command | Use | | --- | --- | | `help <topic>` | Read in-game help | | `tutorial` | Start or resume the newbie tutorial | | `newbie <message>` | Ask the newbie channel for help | | `look` | Look at your room | | `examine <thing>` | Inspect an object, exit, creature, or feature | | `score` | View your character's current condition | | `inventory` | Check what you are carrying | | `equip` | Wear and wield available equipment | | `where` | See where players are, when visible | | `areas` | Browse areas by level range | | `uptime` | Check reboot timing | ## Connection Come join the friendly player base at DarkWind now. Just click [here](https://play.darkwind.ai/) or telnet to `darkwind.ai` port `4242`. We'll see you soon!

docs.title: Basic Commands
docs.text: # Basic Commands DarkWind is played by typing commands. Most commands are short verb phrases: `look`, `get sword`, `say hello`, `kill rat`, `wear armor`, `wield sword` ## Looking Around | Command | Use | | --- | --- | | `look` or `l` | Look at the room | | `look <thing>` | Look at something in the room or your inventory | | `examine <thing>` or `exa <thing>` | Examine something more closely | | `gl` | Glance at the room | | `inventory` or `i` | Show what you are carrying | | `who` | Show who is online | | `finger <player>` | Show public information about a player | Room descriptions often contain nouns you can inspect. If a room mentions a statue, sign, trail, table, corpse, altar, or doorway, try looking at it. ## Moving Most movement uses compass directions. | Long | Short | | --- | --- | | `north` | `n` | | `south` | `s` | | `east` | `e` | | `west` | `w` | | `northeast` | `ne` | | `northwest` | `nw` | | `southeast` | `se` | | `southwest` | `sw` | | `up` | `u` | | `down` | `d` | Some rooms have special exits such as `enter`, `climb`, `portal`, `knock door`, or `exit`. Room text usually hints at these. ## Items | Command | Use | | --- | --- | | `get <item>` | Pick up an item | | `get all` | Pick up everything you can carry | | `get all from corpse` | Loot a corpse | | `put <item> in <container>` | Put an item into something | | `give <item> to <player>` | Give an item to another character | | `drop <item>` | Drop an item | | `keep <item>` | Mark an item as kept | | `unkeep <item>` | Remove kept status | | `wear <armor>` | Wear armor or clothing | | `wield <weapon>` | Wield a weapon | | `equip` | Wear and wield available equipment | | `weight` | Check carried weight | If there are several similar objects, add a number: `look corpse 2`, `get sword 3`, `sell knife 2` ## Combat | Command | Use | | --- | --- | | `kill <target>` | Start fighting | | `assist <player>` | Help another player fight their target | | `.` | Show a quick HP/SP report | | `monitor` or `mon` | Toggle HP/SP monitoring | | `wimpy <percent>` | Run when your HP drops below that percent | | `wimpycmd <direction>` | Set the direction used by wimpy | | `consider <target>` | Judge a target where available | Levels 1–5 have `nheal`, `nbolt`, `ncot`, `ndomain`, `npunch`, and `nkick`. From levels 6–49, use their adventurer forms: `aheal`, `abolt`, `acot`, `adomain`, `apunch`, and `akick`. ## Help The in-game help system is large and useful. | Command | Use | | --- | --- | | `help` | Show help overview | | `help <topic>` | Read a topic | | `help <section> <topic>` | Read a topic inside a help section | | `help list` | Show help sections | | `help list <section>` | Show topics in a section | | `help all` | Show all help topics | | `commands` | Show general commands | ## Aliases Aliases shorten commands you use often. | Command | Use | | --- | --- | | `alias list` | Show saved aliases | | `alias <name> <command>` | Create an alias | | `alias <name>` | Show an alias | | `alias remove <name>` | Remove an alias | | `talias <short> <player>` | Create a tell alias for a player | | `talias list` | Show tell aliases | Examples: - `alias ga get all` - `alias la look at` - `talias bob bobert` Some commands cannot be aliased, including `get`, `drop`, `equip`, `wear`, `wield`, `take`, and `unwield`.

docs.title: History.Md
docs.text: It was nearly 1800 years ago that the dark wind appeared and ravaged our cities, countries, towns and villages. From where this evil came and what the cause was, I regret to say is not known to us, for most of the immortals were still children at the time. Some say it was an evil birthed of the foul arts of **Alarian**, the great Necromancer, and that he was its first victim, but that is just a legend from the mists of time. Whatever the cause, the effects were obvious. Not even the longest of wars killed as swiftly and effortlessly as that unliving wind of malice. The dark wind has come and gone several times during my life, during the life of the city, and during the rebuilding. Not even **Mitra**, **Gaea** and **Set** fully stopped the destruction. But the first occurrence of the wind was the worst by far. We shall start our history at that time, for history of the time before the coming is lost, just as the lives and cities were lost. The clades of Darkwind were thrown into confusion, and the blancmanges, who had been decimated by the wind, were pushed to the brink of extinction by the resulting wars. The clade wars were bloody affairs. The ogres, orcs and trolls banded together, and with their combined raw strength launched raids and besieged the elves, gnomes and dwarves as they attempted to rebuild. The humans fell victim to massive infighting. The faerie and the halflings managed to escape most of the bloodshed, however they found themselves unable to do much rebuilding of their shattered culture. The death and barrenness caused by the dark wind caught the eye of three gods: **Gaea**, the earth mother; **Mitra**, the goddess of goodness; and **Set**, the god of chaos. Gaea set about to restore the land, the plants, and the animals. Mitra and Set, however, made themselves known to the inhabitants of Darkwind. Gaea worked so very hard at rebuilding life. Mitra and Set, however, attempted to lead the people to a better life. Co- existence between the factions, the clades, and families was not to be at this time. The religious wars that followed were unfortunate, and only served to dilute the population even more. No one but the gods know what happened to change things. 24 years after the cleansing by the dark wind, representatives from the different clades met at the bay where Darkwind City now stands. Many say that Gaea herself came to the representatives and entranced them, giving them power from her own body, as well as power from both Set and Mitra. Thus she bestowed upon them immortality; the ability to command flesh, stone, air, water, and spirit, and the determination to create a better life. With the immortals in place, she forbade Set and Mitra from taking a direct hand in the world, allowing them to only work through the priests and the immortals. The age of immortals had begun. The first act was the creation of a city on the very ground where they were given their power. And the city was called Darkwind, and it was open to one and all. The clades of Darkwind thrived, and explored the surrounding countryside and the oceans. The immortals created many things, guided by Mitra, Set and Gaea.

docs.title: Organizations
docs.text: # Organizations Blackmar is full of groups that shape how players live, travel, fight, trade, and ask for help. ## Adventurers' Guild The Adventurers' Guild is the first practical home for new characters. It gives early guidance, level information, and access to the Newbies' Tome. It is also the place many players use as a common meeting point. ## Guilds [Guilds](../gameplay/guilds.md) are adventuring paths. A guild gives commands, abilities, restrictions, training identity, and a community of players with similar tools. Current guild directions: - Acolyte - Bard - Berserker - Druid - Fighter - Garou - Mage - Monk - Ninja - Ranger - Swashbuckler - Thief ## Clans [Clans](../gameplay/clans.md) are player-created organizations outside the guild system. They provide a clan channel, headquarters, shared coffers, storage, reputation, and optional clan wars. ## Religions Divine systems tie characters to patrons, omens, shrines, tithes, and pilgrimages. This matters most for Acolytes, but any character can encounter divine signs and patron systems. Major patron powers include: - Mitra - Set - Gaea - Luna ## Player-Owned Businesses Player-owned pubs and inns are part of DarkWind's economy. Owners control menus, descriptions, prices, staffing, and business funds. See [Economy](../gameplay/economy.md). ## City Services Darkwind City has public services that matter to nearly every character. - Banks - Shops - Donation rooms - Post office and mail - Adventurers' Guild - Guild halls - Weapons training - Ferry tickets - Ship shop - Chambre of Commerce - Temples ## Staff Wizards and administrators build, maintain, and moderate the game. Players must follow staff instructions in-game. Reports, bugs, typos, and ideas are covered in [Feedback And Reports](../gameplay/feedback.md).

docs.title: World
docs.text: # World Some places described in these pages are known through lore before they can be reached. Use `areas <domain>` in game for available routes and level guidance. Blackmar is the known world of Darkwind: a continent of old roads, rebuilt cities, dangerous wilderness, and domains that feel like their own countries. Most of Blackmar uses medieval fantasy technology. Swords, ships, temples, caravan roads, guildhalls, old keeps, and dangerous ruins form the common shape of daily life. That common shape breaks in a few places. Ashad runs on AshPunk craft, where ash, pressure, brass, glass, and alchemy create machines that look impossible beside a knight's forge. Tekal, the green moon, is stranger still: a technological domain of cybernetics, virtuality, and machine cities. These pages focus on what the places are, what they feel like, and what kinds of stories live there. ## Start Here | Page | Description | | --- | --- | | [Blackmar](world/blackmar.md) | The known world, its domains, and the scars left by the Dark Wind | | [Darkwind](world/darkwind.md) | The rebuilt heartland and starting crossroads of Blackmar | | [Calendar](world/calendar.md) | Days, months, dates, and the three visible moons | | [The Three Moons](world/moons.md) | Dailos, Markas, and Tekal as full domains beyond the sky | ## Domains | Domain | Description | | --- | --- | | [Darkwind](world/darkwind.md) | Rebuilt city, open roads, forests, plains, sewers, keeps, and old scars | | [Ashad](world/ashad.md) | AshPunk desert of pressure engines, soot, brasswork, and furnace cities | | [Souvrael](world/souvrael.md) | Great desert domain of dunes, oases, sultans, pyramids, snake temples, and caravan myth | | [Hyperborea](world/hyperborea.md) | Northern domain of fjords, vikings, giants, dwarves, gnomish wars, and Asgardian legend | | [Kerei](world/kerei.md) | Connected jungle islands of ninja clans, Amazon villages, hidden temples, and faerie courts | | [Lerquird](world/lerquird.md) | Swamp continent of black water, luminous wetlands, and giant mushroom forests | | [Virodia](world/virodia.md) | Tropical coastland of reefs, ports, storms, gardens, and bright sea roads | | [Dramasa](world/dramasa.md) | Barren ice land of white plains, frozen roads, and aurora-lit ruins | | [Iglantu](world/iglantu.md) | Hellish fire continent of lava rivers, basalt, smoke, and elemental heat | | [The Bodachian Fallows](world/bodachian-fallows.md) | Shadowed horror land of haunted forests, old manors, ghosts, and grave roads | | [Islands](world/islands.md) | Sea and sky frontiers that gather stranger pocket-realms around Blackmar | | [Underworld](world/underworld.md) | Deep roads, mines, tunnels, old cities, and hostile realms beneath the surface | ## Moons Blackmar has three moons. Each one is a separate domain with its own landscape, dangers, and powers. | Moon | Description | | --- | --- | | [Dailos](world/dailos.md) | Magenta moon of disease, chaos, plague, and savagery | | [Markas](world/markas.md) | Red moon of strength, stability, healing, and sanctuary | | [Tekal](world/tekal.md) | Green moon of knowledge, balance, Luna, and advanced technology |

docs.title: Ashad
docs.text: # Ashad Ashad lies west and slightly south of the Darkwind mainland, beyond the mountains west of Syldenith and Endrael. Its western Oasis of Life opens onto the Mirage Sea, while the Ocarian Sea curls around the continent's southern approaches. Travelers can come ashore at the Oasis and follow the soot roads into a full continental progression. Ashad is the desert that learned to burn productively. Its cities do not merely survive the heat; they harvest it, refine it, and build with it. Where Souvrael is mythic desert, Ashad is industrial desert: furnace towers, brass pipes, soot-black walls, pressure gauges, glass lenses, ash mills, and caravan engines coughing across the dunes. Ashad's technology is called AshPunk. It uses ash, pressure, alchemy, scavenged bone-white fuel, desert oils, and heat engines to create wonders that look like machines and behave like spells. A knight from Darkwind sees a forge. An Ashadi engineer sees a prayer with valves. Furnace cities anchor the domain with stacks, pressure towers, foundries, water vaults, ash mills, and glasswork. Soot roads carry caravans between refinery houses, engineer-priests, furnace families, machinewright orders, and blackened waystations. Glasswork is everywhere: lenses, warded windows, distillation towers, mirrors, heat traps, and signal lamps. Ashad's beauty is smoky, dangerous, improvised, expensive, and practical. ## Areas | Area | Description | | --- | --- | | Oasis of Life | Protected western port, wayshard hub, market, public mendery, and Lifehouse | | Cinder Flats | Vast soot-road wilderness crossed by pressure lines, mirage engines, predators, and fixed waystations | | Scraplands | Active salvage claims full of old machinery, living rivets, and a self-directing breaker | | Keeo | Pressure observatory whose storm charts, condensers, and signal mirrors watch the continent | | Sandstorm Ridge | Permanent wall of salt and glass crossed by guide ropes, shelters, and storm anchors | | Sunken City | Buried civic roofs, drowned archives, and an impossible engine beneath the wells | | Crystal Caves | Resonant eastern caverns with protected moth nurseries and a sealed crystal heart | | Dunmoss Char Spires | Black northern peaks supporting soot-fed moss, grazers, harriers, and wyverns | | Ashad Ruins | Oldest civic kilns and the dormant Brass Crucible foundation at the southern tip | | Pyre | Vertical plateau city built along Ashfall Road, with working lifts, public refuges, an ash exchange, pub, shop, and inn | | Cinder Watchtowers | Four corner outposts that relay road conditions and keep rescue supplies open to travelers | | Cinder Wells | Deep mineable ash vents whose pressure bells warn of geyser-like eruptions | | Ashcar Outcrop | A minor western rise occupied by one caravan keep, wild rams, and raiders | ## Heat Ashad rewards preparation. Severe and extreme heat ramps up rather than striking immediately. The first sustained exposure leaves a traveler Exposed; remaining outside then applies Burning stacks. Full daylight checks most often and applies the strongest stacks, dawn and twilight are milder, and night is half strength. Type `heat` in an Ashad room to see the local tier, cadence, and the stacks expected for your character. Marked shelters stop new exposure. Resist Heat prevents it, Ranger desert survival reduces Burning stacks, and Souvraeli adaptation helps further. Ordinary fire resistance mitigates the resulting Burning damage. Existing Burning decays normally after reaching safety, and Exposed expires shortly afterward. Heat, scarcity, machines, and human ambition all matter. A player feels the desert pressing in from every direction while civilization hisses, clanks, and refuses to die. Ashad is crossed as one connected desert rather than a collection of detached destinations. Its settled regions meet the Cinder Flats through narrow, defended approaches, while Pyre climbs through terraces above the ash roads. Blank stretches on the map are part of the desert, not missing exits.

docs.title: Blackmar
docs.text: # Blackmar Some places described here are known through lore before they can be reached. Use `areas` in game for available routes and level guidance. Blackmar is the known world of Darkwind. The name covers the great continent, the seas and island frontiers around it, the deep roads beneath it, and the three moons that hang above it as separate domains. The Dark Wind defines the beginning of remembered history. It destroyed cities, scattered clades, broke old nations, and left enough ruin behind that rebuilding became the central story of the age. Darkwind City rose from that rebuilding. Other domains kept their own scars, their own gods, their own styles of magic, and their own answers to survival. Most of Blackmar feels medieval: roads, ships, guilds, temples, castles, caravans, farms, forges, monster-haunted borders, and old ruins. Two places break the pattern openly. Ashad turns ash, brass, pressure, and alchemy into AshPunk machines. Tekal turns the sky itself into a reminder that Blackmar's moons are not just lights overhead. ## Domains | Domain | Description | | --- | --- | | Darkwind | Rebuilt heartland, open city, forests, roads, ruins, and first adventures | | Ashad | AshPunk desert of furnace cities, pressure engines, soot, and brass | | Souvrael | Mythic desert of dunes, oases, pyramids, sultans, snake temples, and caravans | | Hyperborea | Northern fjords, vikings, dwarves, giants, gnomish wars, and Asgardian myth | | Kerei | Jungle island chain of ninjas, Amazons, temples, hidden courts, and faeries | | Lerquird | Swamp continent of luminous wetlands and giant mushroom forests | | Virodia | Tropical coastland of reefs, harbors, orchards, storms, and sea trade | | Dramasa | Barren ice land of frozen roads, white plains, and aurora ruins | | Iglantu | Fire continent of lava rivers, basalt citadels, and elemental heat | | The Bodachian Fallows | Haunted land of shadowed woods, ghost roads, manors, and grave magic | | Islands | Sea and sky frontiers with stranger pocket-realms gathered around Blackmar | | Underworld | Deep roads, mines, tunnels, old cities, and hostile realms beneath the surface | ## The Moons | Moon | Color | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | Dailos | Magenta | Disease, plague, chaos, savagery, and the God of Disease | | Markas | Red | Sanctuary, strength, stability, beauty, and healing | | Tekal | Green | Knowledge, balance, Luna, machines, cybernetics, and impossible science | ## Travel Blackmar is a world of hubs and thresholds. Roads connect the central cities. Ports and wharves open the island routes. Caves, mines, grave roads, and old temple paths lead downward. The moons answer gates and celestial timing. For player use, the `areas` command shows current level guidance. The world docs describe where a place belongs in the setting and what kind of story a player is stepping into.

docs.title: The Bodachian Fallows
docs.text: # The Bodachian Fallows The continental mistlands, Gloamspire, and the outlying Fallows regions are dangerous destinations for levels 200-250. Aerial and magical arrivals begin at the crown of Gloamspire; Fallows Cross remains the village wayshard refuge. The Bodachian Fallows are a continent where the world is slowly forgetting itself. Fields lie under permanent dusk. Roads remain after their destinations vanish from signs and maps. Old houses keep lights in windows no one admits to lighting. Graves are too shallow, bells lose notes, and fog closes around places whose names survive only in somebody's pocket ledger. The Fallows make fear local. They are not a distant underworld or a fire realm. They are villages, orchards, churches, farms, manors, and lanes that look familiar until something moves wrong. Haunted forests, ghost roads, fallow villages, black manors, abandoned chapels, grave fields, and locked family houses give the domain its shape. Spirits, death marks, grave ash, forbidden formulae, and Bodachian study keep the dead involved in daily life. Fear in the Fallows often begins in familiar rooms: a village inn, a family orchard, a chapel lane, a nursery, a cellar, a portrait hall, a road home after sunset. Gloamspire rises near the center of the continent, a giant tower split from crown to foundation by leaking blue-violet energy. Fog has swallowed its lower districts. The inhabited tower, abandoned eastern ascent, drowned civic archive, and dangerous buried engine reveal a city fighting to remember itself. The open crown is the Fallows flight point. The crown waysteward offers **The Ledger of Things That Persist**, a six-part story for levels 200-250. It begins with a loose name-tag at Fallows Cross, then compares testimony and physical records from every named region before returning to the engine beneath Gloamspire. Use `engage <witness>` to hear an account and `give <record> to registrar` when a contract calls for evidence. The chain ends with Blackbriar, Vespercourt, and the thing the split tower was built to contain. ## Areas | Area | Description | | --- | --- | | Gloamspire | Split tower-city, fog-swallowed lower wards, and dangerous buried works | | Duskwood | Haunted forest where the day never feels complete | | The Ghost Roads | Old lanes that move through memory as much as geography | | Fallows Cross | Main village market, gallows square, chapel, and inn | | Blackbriar Manor | Noble estate of locked doors, inheritance, mirrors, and old sin | | The Hollow Chapels | Abandoned holy sites where bells and dead prayers remain active | | Widowmere | Still lake where reflections answer before speakers finish | | The Gravefields | Wide cemetery country with mausoleums, grave ash, and restless ground | | Dawnward Redoubt | Mitran paladin camp holding a line of watchfires and mirrors against the fog | | Moonwold Caverns | Werewolf dens where pack memory is kept in scent, scars, and stone | | Vespercourt | Vampire court preserving bloodlines after every family name has begun to fade | The Bodachian Fallows are about dread, investigation, and consequences. Players are pressed to ask what happened before they arrived, who benefits from silence, and which dead thing is still waiting to be paid. The Fallows also give Mage a natural path into forbidden Bodach and Arcanarton study without making Necromancer a public guild. Travelers can descend from the Aeolus sky to Gloamspire's crown, use `tport fallows` at level 200, or unlock the smoke-dark wayshard in Gallows Square. The eleven named regions are separated by a large fogbound wilderness traversed by mistlings, not joined as one short road. The Shadow Cairn is present in the Gravefields, but its Fallowsworn rite remains dormant. Crooked Market in Gloamspire is a protected working shop. It carries salt-thread travel gear, briarward boots, and Dawnward mirror salvage for the opening progression band. Lord Blackbriar and Lady Vesper retain personal contributor chests with level-250 regional equipment, while Namebearer remains the continent's single scarce artifact. Gloamspire's crown, the settled heart of Fallows Cross, and the defended interior of Dawnward Redoubt are protected refuges. Their outer gates, Dawnward's fogward breach, the continental roads, and hostile interiors are not.

docs.title: Calendar
docs.text: # Calendar DarkWind uses its own calendar, moon cycle, and date commands. ## Commands | Command | Use | | --- | --- | | `time` | Show the current time in DarkWind | | `date` | Show the current date and year | The year is calculated from DarkWind's opening day. ## Time DarkWind's calendar uses: - 300 days in a year - 10 months in a year - 30 days in a month - 3 ten-days in a month - 10 days in a week - About 20 hours in a day ## Days Of The Week | Short Name | Full Name | | --- | --- | | Godsday | Day of the Gods | | Moonday | Day of the Placid Moon | | Seasday | Day of the Open Seas | | Windsday | Day of the Whispering Winds | | Treesday | Day of the Towering Trees | | Hearthday | Day of the Hearth Fire | | Starday | Day of the Blinking Stars | | Sunday | Day of the Living Sun | | Peaksday | Day of the Soaring Peaks | | Marketday | Day of the Golden Harvest | ## Months | Month | Nickname | | --- | --- | | Hammer | Deepwinter | | Alturiak | The Claws of Winter | | Ches | The Claws of Storms | | Tarsakh | The Melting | | Mirtul | Time of Flowers | | Kythorn | Summertide | | Flamerule | Highsun | | Marpenoth | Leafall | | Uktar | The Rotting | | Nighal | The Dawning Down | ## Moons Blackmar has three moons: | Moon | Color | | --- | --- | | [Dailos](dailos.md) | Magenta | | [Markas](markas.md) | Red | | [Tekal](tekal.md) | Green | The moons matter to lore, omens, divine systems, and lunar travel.

docs.title: Dailos
docs.text: # Dailos Some places described here are known through lore before they can be reached. Use `areas dailos` in game for available routes and level guidance. Dailos is the magenta moon of disease, chaos, plague, and savagery. It is the home of the God of Disease and the lunar domain that punishes casual curiosity. The land feels infected rather than merely dangerous: forests sicken, cities rot, foothills corrupt, and ruins curse the memory of whoever built them. Dailos is not only decay. It is also endurance through decay, power taken from sickness, and faith twisted into survival. The God of Disease is the divine presence behind plague, infection, fever, rot, and blighted worship. Magenta moonlight carries chaos, savagery, mutation, and a sense that the land itself has symptoms. Plague cults, desperate healers, heretics, survivors, corrupted forests, sick swamps, altered beasts, and ruined cities all treat disease as more than an illness. On Dailos, disease is law, language, and revelation. ## Areas | Area | Description | | --- | --- | | The Plague-Ridden City | Urban ruin of fever houses, sealed gates, and desperate faith | | The Pestilent Swamp | Wetland of infection, leeches, rot, and poisonous bloom | | The Corruption Foothills | Broken hills where stone, blood, and disease mingle | | The Diseased Forest | Sick woodland of warped roots, fever lights, and hostile growth | | The Cursed Ruins | Old lunar ruin where plague becomes memory and trap | ## What Players Find Here - Diseases, poisons, fevers, and hostile environments - Corrupted beasts and altered survivors - Plague cults and blighted rites - Ruins that remember sickness as history - Tempting power wrapped in obvious danger - Strong hooks for Set, Bodach, Arcanarton, and forbidden magic themes ## Travel Mood Travel on Dailos is stressful because the land feels contagious. Camp, food, water, healing, and status cures matter. Safe rooms feel temporary. Victories often leave players asking what they carried back with them. Dailos is a pressure test. It asks players to manage risk, corruption, disease, and temptation. Victory here feels less like being clean and more like leaving before the moon names a price.

docs.title: Darkwind
docs.text: # Darkwind Use `areas darkwind` in game for available routes and level guidance. Darkwind is the rebuilt heart of Blackmar. The first immortal city rose here after the Dark Wind, on the bay where the surviving clades gathered and began again. Its streets are open to almost everyone, which makes the city less pure kingdom and more living crossroads: merchants, guilds, pilgrims, rogues, adventurers, priests, and old grudges all pass through the same gates. The city is the safest place many players learn to name, but it is not a soft place. The sewers, old roads, nearby forests, and ruined holdings keep the past close. Darkwind is where civilization starts making promises, and where the world immediately tests them. Darkwind City is the social and practical center of the domain, with banks, boards, shops, guild access, public roads, and a constant flow of travelers. Center of Town is the common navigation anchor. The Church of Mitra marks holy influence within the city, while the Lunar Gate answers Dailos, Markas, and Tekal when the moons are right. DarkWood Forest spreads west of the walls, thick with roads, clearings, and stranger paths. The northern roads lead toward mountains and colder frontiers. The southern shore holds abbeys, keeps, pirate paths, and old settlements. ## Areas | Area | Description | | --- | --- | | The Sewers | Low tunnels beneath the city where early danger lives close to home | | The Haunted Keep | A small ruined keep that teaches new adventurers to distrust empty stone | | The Four Dragon Temple | A broad early temple complex tied to dragon lore and old city dangers | | The Four Dragon Shrine | A companion shrine beyond the first city roads | | The Realm of Ashkenazy | A nearby realm of strange rule, old enemies, and early heroic work | | The Faerie Mound | A faerie crossing with gardens, caverns, winter valleys, and hidden country | | Endive's Garden | A deceptively pleasant garden with danger that scales far past its first paths | | The Pirate Ship Albion | A shipboard adventure reachable from the coast | | Pirate Town | A northern port of thieves, sailors, rough alleys, and salt-stained trouble | | The Pirate Cave | A deeper coastal danger hidden past pirate country | | Haxton Province | A large old province with villages, plains, roads, and many levels of trouble | | Glavia | A village, castle, swamp, monastery, river, mountains, and demon-haunted woods | | Beneath the Roots | Deep Glavian danger under the old earth | | Stoker | A town with forest roads, mine paths, and a castle shadowing the region | | Syldenith | An ancient forest and tunnel complex with old elven memory | | Canith | A settlement near holy roads and abbey lands | | The Abbey of Saint Dominic | Religious holdings, farms, precincts, infirmary rooms, and church grounds | | The Convent of St. Lyra | Holy sisterhood grounds near the abbey roads | | The Northwestern Mountains | Mountain paths, elven villages, brutal old woods, and old caves | | The Skeleton Caves | A deep cave network under the mountain roads | | The Forest of Terror | A darker mountain forest where the wilderness becomes openly hostile | | The Ancient City of Sheritym | A high-danger ruin from an older age | | Qazaash | A dangerous realm of outposts, rifts, and enemies that reward careful judgment | | Hades and the Underworld Road | A mythic descent from Darkwind into darker realms below | Darkwind is built for discovery in layers. New players find streets, farms, sewers, and familiar roads first. Returning players learn the same roads hide portals, keys, old factions, and routes to places that felt impossible at level one. The city stays busy and practical. It has taverns, boards, shops, banks, guild access, donation rooms, roads, gates, ferries, and public landmarks. The fantasy comes from walking out of an ordinary street and finding the impossible two rooms later.

docs.title: Dramasa
