docs.text:
-=- /public/docs/wizard/container -=- ----------------------------- The first few lines in any container should be: #include <mudlib.h> inherit NEWCONTAINER; This line sets up the object to be a container object and will allow calls to the container master object as defined below. -------------------- NOTE: The maximum weight allowed in the container should be no more than five (5) times the weight of the filled container itself. Anything more than this qualifies as a special item that must be created UNIQUE! (I.e., a bag of holding or portable hole.) -------------------- set_name("name"); string name. This is the a name for the object. Also sets the name and short description to name and the long description to name + ".
" set_alias("alias"); string alias. This is another name for the object. It doesn't appear anwhere, but it can be used by the player. set_alt_name("alt_name"); string alt_name. This is yet another name for the object. It also doesn't appear anywhere, but it can be used by the player. set_short("short"); string short. This is the description seen in the player's inventory plus a ".
" Sets the short description of the object to short and the long description to short + ".
" set_long("long.
"); string long. Sets the long description of the object to long. I added the ".
" in the LPC line above to remind you that you should add the period and newline in the long description because LPC doesn't add it in for you. This is what the player will see when they look at the object. set_weight(weight); integer weight. This is the empty weight of the container. set_max_weight(max_weight); integer max_weight. This is the maximum weight of all objects inside the container added together. set_weight_ratio(ratio); integer ratio. The number of weight units that must be put inside a container to increase the weight of the container by 1. Note that if this value is larger than the max_weight, the container will never become heavier, regardless of what is put inside it. The default value is 6. set_value(value); integer value. Sets the selling value of the container to value. Buy back value will be twice this amount. set_read("read.
"); string read. This is what the player will see if they read the object. I added the ".
" in the LPC line above to remind you that you should add the period and newline in the long description because LPC doesn't add it in for you. set_no_buy(n); status n. Set this to 0 if you want people to be able to buy and sell this to and from the store. Set to 1 if you don't. If you dont set this command, it will default to buyable. set_steal(n); status n. Set to 1 if you want to make the item unstealable by thieves. Don't abuse this command! It is meant only for things like quest items or objects great importance. If you don't add this command, item defaults to stealable. set_drink_container(n); status n. Set to 1 if you want to make the container able to hold drinks, such as kegs. set_food_container(n); status n. Set to 1 if you want to make the container able to hold food, such as meals. set_container_container(n); status n. Set to 1 if you want to make the container able to hold other containers. If you plan to allow a player to carry a container that can carry other containers, you need to restrict them from putting in containers with items. This function is mainly to be used for guild/ship containers that will hold other containers. -------------------- Some special functions not normally called in reset() update_weight(); This function can be called to make sure the weight of the container is correct. It may become necessary to call this function if objects are moved into or out of the container by means other than the "put" and "get" commands. ie, when a reset clones and moves something into it. status allow_insert(object oWhat) This function can be overriden if you wish to allow only certain kinds of items in your container. Returns 1 to allow the insert, 0 to disallow it. -------------------- Specific functions related to opening, closing, locking, and unlocking containers. The functions can be used to setup an object, set a key object for unlocking/locking the container as well as query the object for specific conditions. If a container should never be closed, opened , locked, unlocked, etc--such as a teacup--then the wizard can use the set_no_X functions. A newly created container will be open and unlocked by default. nomask object query_container_key(); **** This function is currently not used. This function returns either the key that locks the object or null if the object does not have a key. nomask status close_container(); This function returns True/1 if the container is successfully closed, otherwise it returns False/0. nomask status lock_container(); This function returns True/1 if the container is successfully locked, otherwise it returns False/0. nomask status open_container(); This function returns True/1 if the container is successfully opened, otherwise it returns False/0. nomask status query_has_container_key(); This function returns True/1 if the container has an assigned key object, False/0 if it does not. nomask status query_is_closed(); This function returns True/1 if the container is closed, otherwise it returns False/1. nomask status query_is_locked(); This function returns True/1 if the container if the container is locked, otherwise it returns False/1. nomask status query_is_open(); This function returns True/1 if the container is open, otherwise it returns False/0. nomask status query_is_unlocked(); This function returns True/1 if the container is unlocked, otherwise it returns False/0. nomask status unlock_container(); This function returns True/1 if the container is successfully unlocked, otherwise it returns False/0. nomask void set_closed(); This function manually sets the container closed. nomask void set_container_key(string sKeyName, string sFile); This function sets the container's key name and the file. To lock/unlock the container, the player has to have object sFile in their inventory. nomask void set_locked() This function manually sets the container locked. nomask void set_open(); This function manually sets the container to open. nomask void set_unlocked(); This function manually sets the container to unlocked. nomask void set_no_close(); This function sets the NO_CLOSE_FLAG bit which prevents the container from being closed. nomask void set_no_lock(); This function sets the NO_LOCK_FLAG bit which prevents the container from being locked. nomask void set_no_open(); This function sets the NO_OPEN_FLAG bit which prevents the container from being opened. nomask void set_no_unlock(); This function sets the NO_UNLOCK_FLAG which prevents the container from being unlocked. -------------------- Specific functions related to picking the container's lock. int query_container_pick_chance(); This function returns an integer that represents the percentage chance the container can be picked. nomask void set_container_pick_chance(int iChance); This function sets the percentage chance the container has of being picked. To use this functionality, a wizard would set the container's default pick percentage. Then, within the object the wizard has decided to use to pick the lock, they would query the percentage with query_container_pick_chance, roll the success or failure with their own code. If the roll is successful, the wizard would call set_unlocked() on the container. -------------------- Specific functions related to adding guest lists to a container. void set_container_savefile(string sFile); This allows you to create a savefile for the container. The savefile will save the savefile, the owner, and the guest list of the container. This should be set before setting the owner. void set_container_owner(string sOwner); This sets the owner of the container. Only the owner can add and remove people from the guest list. Specific add_action functions dealing with guest lists. add_action("add_container_guest","addguest"); add_action("remove_container_guest","removeguest"); add_action("list_container_guests","listguests"); If the container doesn't have an owner, or the player isn't the owner or on the guest list, the commands will return 0;. -------------------- Here is an example container object for you to look at: #include <mudlib.h> inherit NEWCONTAINER; void reset(int iArg) { if(!is_clone(this_object())) return; ::reset(iArg); if(iArg) return; set_name("grape bowl"); set_alias("bowl"); set_alt_name("fruit bowl"); set_short("Grape bowl"); set_long("This bowl originally contained plump grapes.

"); set_weight(2); set_max_weight(6); set_weight_ratio(6); set_value(30); set_open(); // Set_Open() is called by default in reset(); set_unlocked(); // Set_Unlocked is called by default in reset(); set_read("On the bottom of the bowl reads: Pontius Pilate's

"); set_no_buy(0); set_steal(0); set_drink_container(0); set_food_container(1); set_container_container(0); set_container_pick_chance(10); //Sets the default pick chance to 10%. }

************************************************************************** WEAPON AND ARMOUR CODING GUIDELINES ************************************************************************** Note: A wizard is allowed to have only 1 unique item per 100 rooms, and the number of exceptional items allowed is also restricted. See 'wizhelp 4.14 (uniques)' for details. *************************************************************************** ARMOUR CODING *************************************************************************** Note: For armor coding, there are rules and there are guidelines. You can look at the rules as being related to balance issues and not negotiable. This is because players always gravitate towards the best things. Anything that is overpowered will tend to disrupt overall balance to a disproportionately large extent. Guidelines are more thematic elements that you should try to follow for consistency, but may be violated for other thematic reasons. Don't get carried away making all your items really good since too many good items will make the game too easy for players. *************************************************************************** ARMOUR TYPES/SETTINGS *************************************************************************** When creating your armour, you must make sure you specify its COVERAGE TYPE, COMPOSITION, MATERIAL, QUALITY and SIZE. This is done by using set_new_type(), set_material(), and set_quality(). -----------------------------Coverage Types------------------------------ Valid basic coverage types: TORSO, LEGS, BOOTS, HELMET, AMULET, SHIELD, RING, CLOAK, GLOVES, SHOULDERS, AURA. RING and AMULET each allow two worn items. Ordinary ring and amulet objects will use the first available matching slot. The other basic coverage types normally allow one worn item. Valid composite coverage types: ARMOUR, ARMOR - same as TORSO|LEGS FULL_SUIT - same as TORSO|LEGS|HELMET|GLOVES|BOOTS These are the ONLY allowed armour types. If you set it to something else, the game will reset it to ARMOUR. However, you may OR the types together to create armors with unique coverage. -----------------------------Size---------------------------------------- Size should be specified for all new and recoded armors. However, only SHIELD types are currently affected by size. Valid sizes: SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE, HUGE NOTE: Shield size is *very* important for guild restrictions. ------------------------------Composition-------------------------------- Valid compositions: CLOTHES, PADDED, HIDE, STUDDED, CHAIN, BANDED, SCALE, PLATE. Common armour identities are defined in <basic_armour.h>. New armour should use set_armour_template() when a stock form fits, or use the closest semantic ARMOUR_* identity instead of assembling size, composition, and coverage bits by hand: set_armour_template("breastplate"); or: set_new_type(ARMOUR_BREASTPLATE); Templates provide default material, aliases, weight, value, and generated material/quality prose. Builders may override those defaults after selecting the template. Clonable stock forms live in /objects/standard_equipment/armour/. If a recurring armour form has no suitable identity, extend <basic_armour.h> rather than copying a new bit combination into area code. MAGICAL may be added deliberately to an identity; it is not an armour composition. If the composition you want is NOT in this list, talk to an IMP+ about what category to put it in to. -------------------------------Material---------------------------------- Valid materials are described in 'wizhelp 4.16 (materials)'. Example: set_material(MAT_STEEL); Materials can be mixed. MAT_NATURAL means woven of grass, etc. If you want any materials added to this list, tell us now, as it necessitates rebooting the mud to add new ones. -------------------------------Quality----------------------------------- Quality is a percentage range INCREASE of the armor's quality over the average armor of the appropriate composition. Use a negative value to make armors that are worse than average. Wearing an armor with quality under -100 will result in an overall penalty to the player over not wearing anything at all. Quality can be set using set_quality(); -------------------------------Examples---------------------------------- All of these but size can be mixed. Here are some examples: leather jerkin : set_new_type(ARMOUR_LEATHER_JERKIN); set_material(MAT_LEATHER); set_quality(0); ogre's robe : set_new_type(ARMOUR_SIZED(ARMOUR_ROBE, LARGE)); set_material(MAT_CLOTH); set_quality(-30); leather leggings : set_new_type(ARMOUR_LEATHER_LEGGINGS); set_material(MAT_LEATHER); set_quality(0); small shield : set_new_type(ARMOUR_BUCKLER); set_material(MAT_WOOD|MAT_STEEL); set_quality(-20); plate : set_new_type(ARMOUR_PLATEMAIL); set_material(MAT_STEEL); set_quality(0); full plate : set_new_type(ARMOUR_FULL_PLATE); set_material(MAT_STEEL); set_quality(0); adamantite full : set_new_type(ARMOUR_SIZED(ARMOUR_FULL_PLATE, SMALL)); battle armour set_material(MAT_ADAMANTITE); (dwarf sized) set_quality(30); ************************************************************************* ARMOUR RULES ************************************************************************* Quality ranges normally fall between -100 (for armor that is useless because it's falling apart, to +40 for normal armors of the highest quality workmanship. The quality must roughly reflect the long/short descs of the item. Any armor with a quality above 40 is considered exceptional, and any armor with a quality above 60 must be unique. Under no circumstances should quality be above 100. ************************************************************************* ARMOUR GUIDELINES ************************************************************************* Note: These values are guidelines only, for thematic purposes. Comp. Coverage Weight Quality Warmth ------------------------------------------------------------------------- Gold ring PLATE RING 1 0 0 Gold necklace CHAIN AMULET 1 0 0 Leather necklace HIDE AMULET 1 0 0 Silk cape PADDED CLOAK 1 -50 10 Heavy wool cloak PADDED CLOAK 2 0 25 Sandals HIDE BOOTS 1 -80 3 Fur boots HIDE BOOTS 2 0 9 Knee-high boots HIDE BOOTS 2 20 7 Armor plated boots PLATE BOOTS 3 0 5 Garden gloves PADDED GLOVES 1 -30 3 Fur mittens HIDE GLOVES 1 0 5 Mesh gloves CHAIN GLOVES 2 0 2 Bracers BANDED GLOVES 1 -50 1 Plate gauntlets PLATE GLOVES 3 0 1 Straw hat PADDED HELMET 1 -50 4 Leather cap HIDE HELMET 1 -20 4 Crown BANDED HELMET 1 -90 1 Chain coif CHAIN HELMET 3 0 6 Sallet PLATE HELMET 3 -10 5 Roman helmet PLATE HELMET 4 0 6 Great helm PLATE HELMET 5 20 8 Buckler PLATE SHIELD(SM) 1 0 0 Leather buckler HIDE SHIELD(SM) 1 -30 0 Medium shield PLATE SHIELD(MED) 3 0 0 Kite shield PLATE SHIELD(LG) 5 0 0 Tower shield PLATE SHIELD(HG) 7 0 0 Loincloth HIDE LEGS 1 -90 1 Leather leggings HIDE LEGS 3 0 10 Greaves PLATE LEGS 4 -10 2 Leather jerkin HIDE TORSO 3 0 10 Fur coat HIDE TORSO 3 -20 20 Chain shirt CHAIN TORSO 6 0 8 Breastplate PLATE TORSO 7 -20 6 Robes PADDED ARMOR 2-3 -20 10 Leather armor HIDE ARMOR 4-6 0 20 Heavy leather armor HIDE ARMOR 6-8 25 25 Chainmail CHAIN ARMOR 7-12 0 15 Platemail PLATE ARMOR 10-15 0 15 Full plate PLATE FULL_SUIT 20-25 0 30 --------------------------------------------------------- *************************************************************************** ** *IMPORTANT* ** ** You can only have 1 powerful (unique) item per 100 rooms coded!!!!! ** ** ** *************************************************************************** The weights are a general guideline. If you think something is heavy, make it heavy! Remember that weight here also represents bulk, so a cloak that is light but awkward could still have a high weight. The actual usefulness of a piece of armour is determined internally based on the coverage, composition and quality of the armour, modified by the armour specialization setting of a player. Thus the "armour class" of a particular piece of armor is only so useful in determining how good a piece of armour is. All things being equal, the quality of the armour is a linear modifier over the default (quality 0). Thus an armour with a quality of 50 is 50% better than an armour of quality 0. =========================================================================== ************************************************************************** WEAPON CODING GUIDELINES ************************************************************************** Note: For weapon coding, there are rules and there are guidelines. You can look at the rules as being related to balance issues and not negotiable. This is because players always gravitate towards the best things. Anything that is overpowered will tend to disrupt overall balance to a disproportionately large extent. Guidelines are more thematic elements that you should try to follow for consistency, but may be violated for other thematic reasons. *************************************************************************** WEAPON TYPES/SETTINGS *************************************************************************** Weapon identities are defined in <basic_weap.h>. New weapons should include that header and use the closest semantic WEAPON_* identity instead of assembling size and damage bits by hand: set_new_type(WEAPON_DAGGER); The identity supplies the standard size, damage types, and FINESSE, MARTIAL, FOCUS, POLE, or MISSILE role where appropriate. MAGICAL and a deliberately exceptional TWO_HANDED flag may be added to the identity. If a recurring weapon form has no suitable identity, extend <basic_weap.h> rather than copying a new bit combination into area code. Clonable stock weapons live in /objects/weapons/. They provide sensible material, quality, weight, value, and description defaults. Area weapons with custom behavior should continue to inherit WEAPON and use a WEAPON_* identity. Valid sizes : SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE, HUGE NOTE: Size is *very* important for guild restrictions. The size of the weapon relative to the wielder affects wieldability as well. A weapon that is relatively HUGE compared to a wielder will automatically be used two-handedly. NOTE: A SMALL weapon is something that is about 1.5 feet or so long, and smaller. A MEDIUM weapon falls in the 1.5 to 3 feet or so. LARGE weapons range from about 3 to 5 feet long, and anything bigger is HUGE. This is a rough guideline for most melee weapons (swords, axes, maces etc) and some types of weapons are generally longer for their categories (e.g. bows and polearms). Valid damage types: BLUNT, SLASH, CLEAVE, PIERCE Valid weapon types: POLE, MISSILE, MAGICAL, TWO-HANDED NOTE: You don't have to use a weapon type if it doesn't fit one of the three categories. A weapon which uses the POLE type is automatically considered TWO-HANDED, as is a MEDIUM or larger MISSILE. Use one identity and add only deliberate exceptional flags. Examples: dagger : set_new_type(WEAPON_DAGGER); rapier : set_new_type(WEAPON_RAPIER); short sword : set_new_type(WEAPON_SHORTSWORD); saber : set_new_type(WEAPON_SABER); long sword : set_new_type(WEAPON_LONGSWORD); greatsword : set_new_type(WEAPON_GREATSWORD|TWO_HANDED); sap : set_new_type(WEAPON_SAP); sling : set_new_type(WEAPON_SLING); mace : set_new_type(WEAPON_MACE); short bow : set_new_type(WEAPON_SHORTBOW); war hammer : set_new_type(WEAPON_WARHAMMER); battleaxe : set_new_type(WEAPON_BATTLEAXE); staff : set_new_type(WEAPON_STAFF); halberd : set_new_type(WEAPON_HALBERD); The difference between SLASH and CLEAVE is in the manner of damage; CLEAVE puts a lot of force behind the blow for sheer power in a small hit area, while SLASH tends to be a raking attack, cutting sidewise into the target. Axes, cleavers, halberds, and the like are CLEAVE, while swords, daggers, and claws are SLASH. Weights are set using: set_weight(int iWeight); The usefulness of a weapon is set using: set_quality(int iQuality); Similar to armor settings, set_quality ranges from -100 for a totally worthless weapon to 100 for the maximum allowed class for a high end unique. Any quality setting above 40 is considered exceptional, and any over 60 is unique. *************************************************************************** WEAPON RULES *************************************************************************** The damage type and size of a weapon are limited only to be consistent with the thematic qualities of the weapon. For example, you can't make a normal longsword and call it a CLEAVE|BLUNT. You can make a 'fairy- sized longsword' and make it SMALL though. Weight should be consistent with thematic qualities. When setting weapon weights, try to start with a similar size/type guideline weapon, and adjust it to fit the particular circumstances. ********************************************************************* WEAPON GUIDELINES ********************************************************************* Note: These values are guidelines only, for thematic purposes. TYPE SIZE DAM TYPE WEIGHT ------------------------------------------------------------------ AXE hatchet SMALL CLEAVE 2 battleaxe MEDIUM CLEAVE 3 great axe LARGE CLEAVE 5 ------------------------------------------------------------------ BOW short bow MEDIUM PIERCE 2 long bow LARGE PIERCE 2 crossbow MEDIUM PIERCE 3 great bow HUGE PIERCE 3 ------------------------------------------------------------------ DAGGER butter knife SMALL PIERCE 1 curved dagger SMALL PIERCE/SLASH 1 dirk SMALL PIERCE/SLASH 1 heavy kris SMALL PIERCE 2 ------------------------------------------------------------------ HAMMERS/MACES carpenter's hammer SMALL BLUNT 1 smithing hammer MEDIUM BLUNT 3 warhammer MEDIUM BLUNT 3 mace MEDIUM BLUNT 3 heavy mace LARGE BLUNT 4 maul HUGE BLUNT 6 ------------------------------------------------------------------ POLEARMS spear LARGE PIERCE(POLE) 3 bardiche HUGE CLEAVE(POLE) 7 halberd HUGE CLEAVE(POLE) 6 lance HUGE PIERCE(POLE) 4 naginata HUGE SLASH(POLE) 5 pike HUGE PIERCE(POLE) 4 ------------------------------------------------------------------ STAVES stick SMALL BLUNT 1 cane MEDIUM BLUNT 2 quarterstaff LARGE BLUNT(POLE) 3 ------------------------------------------------------------------ SWORDS shortsword MEDIUM SLASH/PIERCE 2 rapier MEDIUM PIERCE 2 broadsword MEDIUM SLASH 3 scimitar MEDIUM SLASH 3 longsword LARGE SLASH/PIERCE 4 bastard sword LARGE SLASH 5 greatsword HUGE SLASH 6 ----------------------------------------------------------------- "Weapon class" is no longer set explicitly by builders on weapons, except in extremely unusual situations (consult an IMP+ in that case). Instead use set_quality() to set the overall power of the weapon. The quality is a linear modifier over the default usefulness of a weapon. The actual usefulness of a weapon is determined internally based on the material_composition of a weapon, aspects of it's type and quality. ------ Version 1: ? Version 2: Bob - July 17, 2004

docs.title: Rev. 6
docs.text: Rev. 6 UNIQUES ======= Introduction: ------------- The purpose of this document is to define exceptional and unique objects as well as to state regulations governing their implementations into DW. This document is considered law and no exceptions are to be made. Definitions: ------------ Unique - Any weapon, armour, or object that performs some function that cannot logically be explained by normal laws of physics, given the medieval technological level of Darkwind. An item is considered unique if it exceeds the limits contained in ANY document pertaining to that particular item AND exceeds the rules governing exceptional items (see definition below). This can include but is not limited to the object's inherent qualities. All new uniquesmust first be approved for balance before implementation. An item can be made unique without it being required to be unique. Exceptional - Any weapon, armour, or object that performs some function more efficiently or with more positive benefits to the player (or objects that use it) or more severe consequences to whatever is targeted by the item as regulated in documents containing guidelines for standard related objects. The nature of an exceptional can be but is not limited to the craftsmanship or philosphy regarding the object or its use or lack of (if beneficial). Regulations: ----------- Unique - It is the policy of Darkwind that wizards are allowed at most one unique class object per 100 rooms. Such items must be created using make_unique_object(). Exceptional - It is the policy of Darkwind that wizards are allowed at most 15% of their items to be of exceptional quality. This 15% is 15% of all weapons, and armour. If an object is not a weapon or armour but is still considered exceptional, then that item counts as part of the 15% of all weapons and armours. This 15% is also a percentage of the total number in your area at any one time. Weapons, armour, and exceptional objects all contribute to the same 15%. For a 100 room area, this would be a total of 15 items, including a unique. Further Regulations: -------------------- Weapons: The following qualities will make a weapon exceptional: Quality greater than 30. Material composition containing MAT_ADAMANTITE. A dodge bonus of 1. A hit bonus of 1. Gives one level of light/darkness. ^Any stat changes that are not net increases. Allowing use by a normally restricted guilds. ^An extra damage type on hit, ie DAM_GOOD. ^Weapon hits (see below) The following qualities will make a weapon unique: ^Quality greater than 50. ^Any 2 exceptional qualities. ^Any kind of healing. ^Any kind of increase in damage resistance, ie DAM_GOOD or DAM_PIERCE. ^A dodge bonus greater than 1. ^A hit bonus greater than 1. ^Gives more than 1 level of light/darkness. ^Any extra attacks/damage. ^Any net stat increases. ^Armor piercing damage, or 2 or more extra damage types. ^Weapon hits (see below) The following are just not allowed, period: Weapons may not sober a player. Weapons may not make a player unsatiated. Weapons may not lower a player's Soft level. Weapons may not have a quality over 100. **Weapons may not modify combat via the use of tmp_to. Any weapon modification. ie: set_flaming Weapons may not have a hit bonus of greater than 5. Weapons may not have a dodge bonus of greater than 5. * A weapon can contain a weapon_hit function without being considered unique. If the hit_function does no additional damage, then that item is not considered exceptional. It should be noted that the coding wizard should not have an excess amount of weapons yielding hit messages as it defeats the purpose of the message. If the weapon_hit function returns any value other than 0 (thus a bonus on damage), the weapon is considered exceptional. If the weapon_hit is greater than 1, the weapon is considered unique. This applies for the greatest possible bonus, not the average. ** Some items will be able to use the tmp_to modifiers. This is done on a case-by-case basis through a review of the wizards IMP+ and must have valid reason. ie unique rewards on boss mobs. ^ Characterstics denoted with this symbol must be set_no_save(1) in the reset function. As you can see all uniques qualify for this. While the make_unique_object code will handle this, it's just good form to put it into the code to be safe. Armour: The following qualities will make an armor exceptional: Quality greater than 30. A dodge bonus of 1. Any stat bonuses: 1 stat from level 1 to 44. 3 stats from 46 to 64. 5 stats from 65+. Any single damage resistance: 1 resist from level 1 to 44. 3 resist from 46 to 64. 5 resist from 65+. Gives one level of light/darkness. A ring/amulet of AC 1 or 2. Allowing use by normally restricted guilds. The following qualities will make an armor unique: ^Quality greater than 50. ^Any 2 exceptional qualities. ^Any dodge bonus of more than 1. ^Any stat bonus of more than 5. ^Any resistance of more than 5. ^Multiple damage resistances. ^Any resistance to a physical damage type (DAM_SLASH etc.) ^A ring/amulet AC of 3 or more. ^Gives more than 1 level of light/darkness. The following are just not allowed, period: Armour may not sober a player. Armour may not make a player unsatiated. Armour may not lower a player's Soft level. Armour may not have a quality over 100. **Armour may not modify combat via the use of tmp_to. Any permanant armour modification. ie set_thorned(1) ** Some items will be able to use the tmp_to modifiers. This is done on a case-by-case basis through a review of the wizards IMP+ and must have valid reason. ie unique rewards on boss mobs. ^ Characterstics denoted with this symbol must be set_no_save(1) in the reset function. As you can see all uniques qualify for this. While the make_unique_object code will handle this, it's just good form to put it into the code to be safe. Objects: The following qualities will make an object exceptional: Giving two (or more) levels of light/darkness. ^Any stat increases. ^Any kind of added resistance/weakness. Quality greater than 30. ^Any extra damage/attacks. following are just not allowed, period: Objects may not have a quality over 100. Objects may not modify combat via the use of tmp_to. Objects may not have more than 1 qualifying characteristic. ^ Characterstics denoted with this symbol must be set_no_save(1) in the reset function. As you can see all uniques qualify for this. While the make_unique_object code will handle this, it's just good form to put it into the code to be safe. Conclusions: ============ The purpose of this doc is not to target any one person in particular. It is to provide guildelines and regulations regarding objects. This doc can be revised at any time. Such revision will follow with posts to the wizboards. If you are unsure about the classification of an object, please talk to an IMP+. In addition, please provide a variety of strengths in the objects you place in your areas. Not everyone in every situation could possiblyhave the upper limits of all standard weapons and armour. A lot of times, kewl hit messages or even just a kewl looking weapon is enough to make it popular. Also note that there are very few rules concerning how good a unique item can be. This should not be taken to mean that uniques can be infinitely powerful, but rather that the power of uniques is often hard to quantify. Overly powerful uniques may be downgraded/removed at any time. This will be decided by the wizards at IMP+. Revision History: BKB---------------- Rev. 6 - Changed to reflect even newer standards and include objects. Color also added. Rev. 5 - Changed to reflect new weapon/armor standards. Rev. 4 - Added requirements for submitting uniques for review. All changes are marked with a | at the far right side of the doc. Rev. 3 - Fixed some typos, edited a few of the classifications to reflect the way they've been used on the mud; namely, the add_resistance for armour, the set_guild_allow for weapons and armour, and the AC of amulets. Rev. 2 - Added clarifications to the 15% exceptional rule. Also made clarification to the hit_func damage occurance limits for exceptionals. Rev. 1 - Added clarification as to making uniques. Rev. 0 - Initial release

docs.title: TERRAIN
docs.text: TERRAIN ======= Terrain is a REQUIRED setting for all rooms. Every room MUST: #include <terrain.h> and set_terrain(<terrain bit field>); as part of the room settings. Terrain settings MUST be ORed bit field settings defined in terrain.h. For example: set_terrain(TER_OUTSIDE|TER_PATH|TER_FOREST); Don't even THINK about using string values like: set_terrain("path"); Every room MUST set ALL applicable terrain types. That means that for a path in the forest, set_terrain(TER_PATH|TER_FOREST); is WRONG because it doesn't have TER_OUTSIDE. See /open/INCLUDE/terrain.h for currently available terrain settings. ------- Revision: 05/17/96 by Sparhawk Revision: 20/08/98 by Xnedra Revision: 13/05/02 Canopy Terrain added by Acer. Revision: 19/05/02 Doc updated. Revision: 15/05/04 Completely redone by Bob.

docs.title: Rev. 2
docs.text: Rev. 2 MATERIALS ========= Introduction: ------------ This is the Darkwind materials doc, so you know what they are before you start setting them on all your objects. You can set_material on just about any object on the mud; specifically, you can set it on those objects which inherit OBJECT. Additionally, before you are able to use the materials described below, you must first add the following line at the top of the object you're creating: #include <material.h> Syntax: ------- The syntax for specifying the material is: set_material(MATERIAL); You can mix the material types if you wish. For example, a ruby- tipped wand might have this line: set_material(MAT_WOOD|MAT_GEM); Material Types: --------------- MAT_ADAMANTITE - is a near-mythical metal highly prized by dwarves, who are the chief miners of it. It is a ferrous metal that is somewhat lighter than steel, but much sturdier. It is reputed to be nearly unbreakable, in fact. Some people claim it is inherently magical, but this is not the case. MAT_BONE - forms the structural framework of vertebrates. While fairly strong, it is also brittle. Some invertebrates have chitin instead of true bone, but for our purposes they can be considered the same. MAT_BRASS - is an alloy of copper and zinc. It is a shiny yellow-orange color. MAT_BRONZE - is an alloy of copper and tin. It is yellowish-brown in color. It is softer and more malleable than steel, and was once the primary metal used in weapons and armor. MAT_CLOTH - consists of woven fabrics of natural or man-made fibers. On Darkwind, they will be almost exclusively natural. Examples are cotton, wool, flax. MAT_COPPER - is a reddish brown metal. It is fairly common throughout | the land of darkwind and because of this is used in many things from | cookware to inexpensive jewelry. Copper is know to be highly conductive | of heat and electricity. | MAT_CRYSTAL - is the name for a material formed by the regular ordering of molecules into a solid form, such as many of the precious stones that are mined from the earth (diamond, peridot, ruby). Also the name for a very fine, clear glass, typically made with lead. MAT_ELECTRUM - is a naturally occuring alloy of silver and gold. It is | amber in color. It is more valuable than silver alone due to its gold | content but less valuable than gold. It is used in many things from fine | diningware to jewelry to expensive pieces of armour for kings and nobles. | MAT_ENERGY - is used for describing something that is associated with energy | (such as a ball of lightning) and having no real physical form. It can also | be used to describe things such as force barriers and the like. | MAT_GEM - is what we will call the precious stones, regardless what their nature. Certain mineral crystals are highly prized (diamonds, etc), but there are other noncrystalline gems as well (pearls, amber). MAT_GLASS - is formed from molten sand. It is easily worked into a variety of useful and decorative shapes in this state, and cools into a brittle quasi-crystalline form. The addition of various impurities give it color. MAT_GOLD - is a shiny yellow metal that is highly malleable and very soft. It is prized for its beauty and rarity, and is used in coinage and jewelry for this reason. MAT_IRON - The most common and most useful of metals. It is usually found | naturally in the form of an oxide (such as hematite, magnetite, etc.), or | a hydrous oxide (as limonite, turgite, etc.). Iron usually appears dark | brown, from oxidation or impurity, but when pure, is a gray or white metal. | It is easily oxidized (rusted) by moisture, and is attacked by many | corrosive agents. | MAT_LEAD - a heavy, pliable, inelastic metal, having a bright, bluish color, | but easily tarnished. It is both malleable and ductile and has a very low | melting point. It is easily fusible and forms alloys with other metals. | It is commonly used to join different pieces of metal or other materials | together. Because of its nature lead is impractical to use alone in weapons | or armour although some clubs and other bashing type weapons have been know | to employ this metal to make the weapon heavier and provide additional | smashing power. | MAT_LEATHER - is made from the cured hides of animals. When the hide of large animals, which is generally thicker, is boiled in oil, it can become stiff and quite durable. MAT_MAGICAL - this encompasses all other material that may lack a physical | form and are not better described as being MAT_ENERGY. This type may also | be used to describe enchanted materials alon with the normal material type. | | MAT_MITHRIL - is also often called elven steel, or elven silver. It is alleged to be the "true" form of silver by the elves, and attributed nearly magical properties. Whether or not it is truly magic, it is known that it is very light for its strength. A chainmail shirt can be worn under other clothing without being noticed. It is also highly prized by spellcasters, who find that its nature does not prohibit spellcasting like most other metals. MAT_NATURAL - subsumes all other "natural" substances not herein described. A flower would be natural, as would water. MAT_PAPER - any type of material that is basically boiled, bleached and | preseed plants that is allowed to dry and for which is used for writing | or other types of craft. Alchemists use paper in making fireworks and | other incendiary devises. | MAT_PLATINUM - One of the rarest of precious metals, platinum also is one | of the strongest and heaviest. It has a rich silvery-white color, is | corrosion resistant and is malleable. It is much rarer than gold and is | worth approximately twice that of gold. Because of its value and | decorative nature, it is highly prized for use in jewelry. | MAT_ROCK - is any kind of stone. This technically includes many gems, but we generally don't set gems to GEM|ROCK. You might have a stone club set with gems that would fit that description, though. MAT_SILVER - is a shiny white metal that is lighter than gold but nearly as soft. It is usually an order of magnitude less valuable, as well. Highly decorative, it is used for jewelry and ornamentation as well as for coinage. MAT_STEEL - is an alloy of iron with carbon, which yields it more malleable and easier to work as well as less brittle. Once it was discovered, it became the metal of choice for making weapons and armor, replacing bronze. MAT_STONE - for the most part MAT_STONE is the same as MAT_ROCK. One may | use this for things such as stone tablets or bricks that are not truely | rocks. | MAT_TIN - is a soft, faintly bluish white metal. It is quite soft, and is seldom used by itself but often as an alloying agent with other metals to form bronze and pewter, among other things. MAT_WOOD - is a hard, fibrous substance that makes up the greater part of xylemic plants. It is sturdy and is a good structural agent. Weight for weight, it is stronger than steel. However, wood has many undesireable properties that make various metals preferable in many cases. Additional Comments: -------------------- Note that the material types must have the "MAT_" in them now as the bits require it. Revision History: ----------------- Rev. 2 - Revised the doc to contain all current material types. Sections changed have a "|" in the right hand column. Revision made by Olgar - 07-31-04. Rev. 1 - Added the "MAT_" in the material types to reflect changes made to the material bits. Revision made by Olgar - 03-08-96. Rev. 0 - Initial version created by Antcrusher - 12-8-94, 6:42 PM CST.

docs.title: The various types of damage a weapon or monster can do is placed into
docs.text: The various types of damage a weapon or monster can do is placed into a bitfield and as such may be combined and/or masked with the | and & bitwise operators. Please see the armour documentation for specifics about adding weaknesses and resistances to your armour, and the weapon documentation for specifics about adding damage types to your weapons. This file only lists the types of damage and the bitfield names for each type. To use the following types, you must #include <types.h> in your file. ** damage types ** WEAPON_PIERCE Piercing damage (darts, spears, needles) WEAPON_SLASH Slashing damage (razors, swords) WEAPON_BLUNT Blunt damage (clubs, maces, trashcans) WEAPON_CLEAVE Cleaving damage (axes, halberds) WEAPON_DAM_MASK WEAPON_PIERCE|WEAPON_SLASH|WEAPON_BLUNT|WEAPON_CLEAVE DAM_SILVER Silver objects (silver arrows, silver daggers) DAM_MAGIC Generic magic DAM_GOOD "Good" damage (aura bolt, holy fire, holy water, angels) DAM_EVIL "Evil" damage (demons, vampires) DAM_CHAOS Disruptive damage (disintegration, large-scale crushing) DAM_LAW "lawful" damage DAM_ALIGN DAM_GOOD|DAM_EVIL|DAM_LAW|DAM_CHAOS DAM_FIRE Heat and flame damage (fire spells, solar weapons) DAM_COLD Ice and freezing damage (hail, ice spells) DAM_LIGHTNING Electrical damage (lightning, electric eels) ELEMENT_DAM_MASK DAM_LIGHTNING|DAM_COLD|DAM_FIRE|DAM_WATER DAM_POISON Poisonous damage (snakes, poisonous plants, swamps) DAM_DISEASE Health-degrading damage (zombies, mummies) DAM_LIVING DAM_POISON|DAM_DISEASE DAM_SOUND Sound damage (banshee, bards) DAM_ACID Acid damage (black dragons) DAM_ASTRAL Etherial and other-worldly (ghosts, shadows) DAM_PSIONIC Mental damage (mind sting) DAM_WATER Liquid damage (drowning) DAM_AP Armor-piercing damage (ultra-sharp weapons). DAM_LIGHT Light damage (sunray) ALL_DAM_TYPES All of the previous types.

docs.title: There are four classifications of pronouns available for use in
docs.text: There are four classifications of pronouns available for use in coding. pronoun, possessive, objective, absolute possessive Darkwind supports single-player, non-archaic male/female/neuter pronouns. The queries will return as follows: query_pronoun() returns: he, she, it query_possessive() returns: his, her, its query_objective() returns: him, her, it query_abs_possessive() returns: his, hers, its ---Xnedra 08/28/98---

docs.title: --=Coding a Room=--
docs.text:
--=Coding a Room=-- Before I start the actual document, I would first like to make a few comments on rooms. First are the types of rooms we are looking for here at Darkwind. We do NOT want 500 room areas where every room is a description of one line or less. These types of rooms can be coded by anyone and can be found on any mud. We want rooms with good, quality descriptions where everything that is mention in the desc has an associated, add_look, add_read, or an actual object in the room. Rooms that do NOT follow this guideline will NOT be approved. The next point is when objects should be created. There are several different views on this. No one is better than the other, but since I'm writing this doc, I'm going to use the way I do it and give my reasoning for doing it that way. Basically, you can create your objects that are going to go in the room either before the reset function or after it. I feel it is better to do it after mainly for one reason: if an error occurs in the object that is being loaded and it fails to load, the room will still load properly and function normally, but the object causing the problem in it will not be present in the room. If the object being created has a problem when you create your objects before you make the room itself, it will not only not create the object, but the room will also not be created as well. This means that you will be creating a '0' room: A room with no descriptions, exits, etc. If a player stumbles into one of these rooms, they will either have to quit to get out or find a wizard to get them out. It also means that now the room is impassable to what is beyond. Also, in creating a monster that has the ability to move, if you create it before you create the exits of the room it is being moved into, it will never move. If you create the monster after the room is created, then the monster will move about normally. Now on to the creation part of the doc itself. The first part of this file is enough to make a basic room with some interesting features. The second part details more functions that can be called to expand your room. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ The first lines of every room file should always be: #include <mudlib.h> #include <terrain.h> inherit ROOM; void reset(int iArg) { ::reset(iArg); if(iArg) return; Alternately, you may use: void reset(int iArg){ ::reset(iArg); if(!iArg) { The basic difference between these versions is that the "if(iArg) return;" statement is kinder for the game to process. If your room will have wandering monsters, however, you can clone them in your room after the exits are created (so they actually CAN wander) by placing the monster creations after the "if(!iArg){ }" statement. With these lines in place, you are ready to add the actual properties of the room itself to the file. To customize your room, you call the following routines: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ set_light(n); This will set the light level of the room. This line needs to be in every room you code. 0 is dark, 1 is normal light. A number lower than 0 is normally a magically darkend room. And will require either a stronger light source or multiple light sources to illiuminate the room. The same is true with room with high than 1 for a light value. it will take more powerful darkness type magic to get a room like this to go dark. In 99% of most rooms you code up, 0 or 1 should be the light levels of the room. EXAMPLE: set_light(1); ------------------------------------------------------------------------ set_terrain(TER_type); This line sets the terrain type of the room, is this room a inside a structure, underground, a forest, etc. This line is also required in every room you code. For valid terrain types, look at the file 'wizhelp 4.15 (terrain)' to get a listing. One room can be set with multiple types of terrain if necessary, for example an underwater area in the artic would be set as shown below. EXAMPLE: #include <terrain.h> set_terrain(TER_UNDERWATER|TER_ARCTIC); This adds a terrain type after you have already set one with set_terrain. set_terrain(TER_UNDERGROUND); add_terrain(TER_RIVER); add_terrain(TER_INSIDE); This would be identical to initially setting the terrain of the room to: set_terrain(TER_UNDERGROUND|TER_RIVER|TER_INSIDE); Use of add_terrain should be limited to when you are using a customized room inheritable in which all the rooms already have a primary terrain set. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ set_no_clean_up(1); This command is only needed if you have a room that you don't want the driver ever to clean up. By this I mean that periodically the driver will remove all the files that are not being used currently to reduce the memory and cpu usage of the mud. Some rooms NEED to be around at times because they are controlling other functions. You would use this command to ensure that the room wasn't removed from memory during the cleanup phase. This line is only required in the file when you don't want the room cleaned up. If it isn't present it defaults to cleanupable. For example, if you had a room used for storage, you would want it to be no_clean_up so that items stored in it would not be desctucted. Rooms which have the function "make_unique_object" are automatically set to no_clean_up to keep track of the unique, and do not need to be set in addition to that. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ set_short("str"); String str sets the short description of the room to str plus a carriage return. It automatically includes the obvious exits after the description. Please capitalize the beginning of your rooms' short descs. EXAMPLE: set_short("A small demo room."); ------------------------------------------------------------------------ set_long("str"); String str. The format ofsets the long description of the room to str. this line is very important and MUST be done as follows in the example. There are other less efficient ways to do it which will work, but they are not approved for use here. The last line of the long description becomes the obvious exits. The 
 and the 
\ tell the compiler that the line ends there and that any more text needs to be started on a new line. After your description, the compiler will automatically add any obvious exits to the room. EXAMPLE: set_long("\ This is the long description for a
\ test room here in the doc. You should
\ always use this format whenever you
\ set the long description in a room!
"); Using the wrap() function will format your line lengths to 79 characters. EXAMPLE: set_long(wrap("\ This is also a room description. This room description will automatically\ be formatted to the correct size by the game.")); You need not put a 
 at the end of a wrap() statment. Any 
's that are placed within the wrap() will cause a line break if you need it for the effect (i.e., a multiple paragraph description). It should also be noted that we only want good, quality descriptions in all our rooms here on Darkwind. One or two-line descriptions in most cases are not going to be acceptable. When writing your long descriptions, please try to NOT put two spaces after each sentence. Since Darkwind is an on-line text-based service, we have no way to determine what font the text will be read in. So, since different fonts have different effects, text should only have one space between all characters (again, unless having a space is required for some visual effect). NB If you put multi-line text inside a wrap(), you must put a \ at the end of each line. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ set_night("str"); String str. This optional function sets an alternate long description of the room which will appear only at night. This allows you to have "the sun beats down on you," during the day and "the moon casts a peacful glow," during the night. If set_night() is not used, then the description set by set_long is used at night as well as in the daytime. If using this command, your room needs to inherit SEASON_ROOM rather that inheriting ROOM. set_dusk("str"); String str. As set_night(), above, but only appears during the hours of the setting sun. If using this command, your room needs to inherit SEASON_ROOM instead of inheriting ROOM. set_dawn("str"); String str. As set_night(), above, but only appears during the hours of the rising sun. If using this command, your room needs to inherit SEASON_ROOM instead of inheriting ROOM. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ add_exit("dir","/path/file"); This will add 1 exit to the room. If you wish to have more than one exit, you just add an add_exit for each exit in the room. The first variable in the command is the exit direction, and the second variable is the path to the file you wish the the exit to lead to. There is no need to include the ".c" after the filename. EXAMPLE: add_exit("west","/players/alarian/rooms/room2"); add_exit("east","/players/alarian/rooms/room3"); DO not hardcode exits. Use the definition in your header file. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ add_look("what","desc"); This adds something to the room that can be looked at by the player. EVERY object that is mentioned in the room's description MUST have either an object in the room or an associated add_look to go along with it. If an item has both a look and a read, look shows both of them. Multiple items are supported the same way add_exit worked, with a separate add_look for each item. To do a simple one item looks, the following syntax is used: EXAMPLE: add_look("picture","A fancy picture is on the wall."); add_look("cricket","There is a small cricket in the corner chirping"); If you wish to have one description for multiple different looks, you can do them as following: EXAMPLE: add_look(({"wall","walls","floor"}),"It looks to be very smooth."); If your descriptions are more than one 79 characters long, you MUST either wrap() them, or include 
's at the end of each line to add the carrage returns to the description. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ query_look("what"); If there is an add_look for "what" this will return what you would see if you typed "look at what". If "what" is not supplied, it will return the entire add_look array. The array is structured so that the first element is the first item you can look at, the second element is what you see when you look at it, the third element is the second thing you can look at, and the fourth is what you see when you look at the third element, etc. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ add_read("what","desc"); Adds the command/action "read" to the room for the item "what". Read returns the description immediately following the "what". NOTE: This would be a good way to have a sign listed in your long desc, and its description would be entered in this command instead of another object for the sign. Also, an add_read can be seen by "look"ing at the "what". To do a simple one item looks, the following syntax is used: EXAMPLE: add_read("menu","A normal lousy menu.
"); add_read("sign","A fancy sign with swirly things on the corners!
"); If you wish more than one word to be able to call the same description, you can use the following format to achieve this: EXAMPLE: add_read(({"sign","message"}),"It reads: Sell your stuff here.
"); The same rules in add_look are applied to add_read. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ add_trigger("trig","desc"); Adds a command so that when the 'trig' is entered by itself at the prompt it returns the desc. It just writes the string desc to the calling player. EXAMPLE: add_trigger("ithnar", "You say the command word and a bell gongs.
"); prompt>ithnar <----you type prompt>You say the command word and a bell gongs. <----room writes The room writes follow the same rules are add_look and add_read descriptions. Multiple triggers, for example: EXAMPLE: add_trigger(({"sneeze","cough"}),"Yuck, don't do that!
"); is possible, following the same rules as add_look and add_read. remove_trigger("trig"); Removes a trigger that has been added with add_trigger. The argument to remove_trigger must be a string exactly matching the 1st argument given to the add_trigger you wish to remove. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ make_object("name","file_path", howmany); Clones and moves objects or monsters into the room. Name is the name of the object. You must name the object here what it is called in the object itself. If you do not do this, it will not find the object each time it checks for it and will then clone a new one. File_path is the pathname of the object you want to put in the room. Howmany is the number of objects that you want in the room, if howmany isn't set the default is one. EXAMPLE: make_object("orc","/players/alarian/monsters/orc",3); DO not hardcode items. Use the definition in your header file. This will put three orc from the file players/alarian/monsters/orc into the room. It should also be noted that if this function is called from inside the reset function, it will only be called with the room is first created. If you want the object to be recloned each reset, you need to put the make_object function outside the reset. This means, either place it BEFORE the: if(iArg) return; statement or either before or after the: if(!iArg){ ...stuff... } statement. This command will clone "howmany" objects into the room, provided there are _NO_ objects with the same ID as the "name" in the function. If you want the room to clone enough objects each reset, regardless of how many are left over from the previous reset, to equal "howmany", use the add_clone function explained later in this doc. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ make_unique_object("id","file_path"); This function is almost identical to make_object, except it will allow only one of the object in the game at a time. This is used for powerful items, wandering monsters, or just items that you don't want a lot of in the game. EXAMPLE: make_unique_object("widowmaker","/players/alarian/weapons/widowmaker"); DO not hardcode items. Use the definition in your header file. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ make_room_unique("id","file_path"); This function is almost identical to make_unique_object, except it is only to be used for wandering mobs. The information is saved in the room, and does not use the unique daemon. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ add_clone("file_path", num); Once again, this is very similar to make_object except for one main difference. With add_clone, if you have it creating 3 objects and when reset comes around and only one is currenty in the room, it will create to more to bring the total back upto three. EXAMPLE: add_clone("/players/alarian/monsters/orc",3); DO not hardcode items. Use the definition in your header file. This will create three orcs in the room and maintain it at that amount each reset. -------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------- Here ends the basic section of the doc. The functions above are enough to make a decent room with things to look at and monsters and items to find. Next comes some more esoteric functions that can add spice and enjoyment to the rooms. status dir_hook() {what to do} Takes direction "dir" and calls this function anytime somebody tries to use that direction. dir is any of the exits defined in add_exit(). If the function returns 1, the exit fails and the player can't go that way. A return value of 0 allows the player to pass. EXAMPLE: status west_hook() { if(present("my_unique_orc",this_object())){ write("The orc blocks you from going that way.
"); say(this_player()->query_name()+" tried to go west.
"); return 1; /* the player can't go through */ } return 0; /* the player can go through */ } This is a good way to keep wandering NPC's within your own area, or in a certain range within your area. EXAMPLE: status out_hook(){ return this_player()->query_npc(); } Remember, you pretty much never want to block wizards using dir_hooks. The appropriate check to make sure you do not block wizards is to #include <perms.h> at the head of your room, and put the check: if(IS_APPLICANT(this_player())) return 0; at the beginning of your dir_hook(). It should also be noted that this function is placed OUTSIDE the room creation function entirely. It is its own function. See the example that follows for more details. -------------------------------------------------------------------------- set_exit_blocker(sDirection, sName, sFile, sMess); This is a simpler version of the dir_hooks when you have a simple hook. It will check for a sName that matches sFile, and give sMess+"
" if the player can't go that way. This allows you to make sure that the sName present in the room is the actual file you wish to block sDirection, and not any stray object. sMess has a default message if not set of "Something blocks you from going that way." It also innately has the IS_APPLICANT check, so you don't need a seperate check. Unlike dir_hooks, this is in the room code. If you want more than one object to block the same direction, you will need to use a regular dir_hook. If you need more checks or versatility, again you'll need to use a regular dir_hook. Example: set_exit_blocker("north","orc",MYNPC+"orc","You no get by me!"); -------------------------------------------------------------------------- set_property(sAttribute,sXarg); This funtion sets attributes within rooms. Attributes currently used are : no_dirs - hides the visible exits from the players no_castle - deprecated, we no longer drop wizard castles no_teleport - don't allow teleportation skills no_kill - don't allow any combat no_wimpy - dont allow any livings to wimpy from the room no_tell - don't allow tells to be sent from the room no_shout - don't allow shouts to be sent from the room open_pk - combat in the room ignores PK restrictions no_mining - don't allow 'mine ore' no_herbalism - don't allow 'gather herbs' sXarg will be returned when query_property is called using sAttribute. (see below) squeeze_block - "direction" - Block Morpher Squeeze in a single direction - "all" - Block Morpher Squeeze in ALL directions - "monster_id" - Block Morpher Squeeze if monster_id is present query_property(sAttribute); With an arg it returns the property given as arg. Without an arg, it returns all the properties defines by the following functions. For example, set_property("no_tell","cave"), will return "cave" when query_property("no_tell") is called in the environment() of the player. This is used to block tells from certain rooms today. The tell function looks for the "no_tell" property, just as shout looks for "no_shout". -------------------------------------------------------------------------- set_no_show_exit(); Prevents the exits from a room from being included in the long desc. It sets the no_dirs property. EXAMPLE: set_no_show_exit(); set_no_dirs(); This is the same as setno_show_exit(); -------------------------------------------------------------------------- set_no_kill(); Sets the property no_kill. Rooms with this property will not allow combat. EXAMPLE: set_no_kill(); -------------------------------------------------------------------------- set_no_teleport(); Sets the no_teleport flag for querying from outside objects. This adds the no_teleport property. Set this is you have a room that you don't want players to be able to teleport into or out of. EXAMPLE: set_no_teleport(); -------------------------------------------------------------------------- set_no_short(); This command will make the 'exits' or 'autoexit' return the short of "Unknown" instead of the rooms actual short description. This can be used in rooms where you don't want players to know whats in a given room until they have actually entered it. query_no_short(); Returns 1 if set_no_short(); has been set, 0 if not. Currently only used by the 'exits' and 'autoexits' function. -------------------------------------------------------------------------- set_room_open_pk(status tVal); This command will make the room open_pk if tVal is 1, or return the room to normal if tVal is 0. Combat will be allowed as if everyone was PK. All normal checks apply, like no_kill, etc. query_room_open_pk(); Returns 1 if set_room_open_pk(1), 0 otherwise. -------------------------------------------------------------------------- remove_exit("str"); Lets you remove an exit from a room depending on circumstances. EXAMPLE: remove_exit("west"); remove_look("str"); Same usage as remove_trigger and remove_exit. -------------------------------------------------------------------------- query_exit("str"); Str is the exit direction, west, north, etc. With an arg, it returns the file that the exit goes to. Without and arg it returns the whole list of exits defined by add_exit(). EXAMPLE: query_exit("west"); or query_exit(); -------------------------------------------------------------------------- query_triggers(str); Str is the trigger command, ie. foof. With an arg it returns the string that the trigger returns. Without an arg it returns the whole list of triggers defined by add_trigger(); The str can be a variable <sFoof> that ids to a string or it can be the string <"foof"> itself. EXAMPLE: query_triggers(sFoof); query_triggers("foof"); or query_triggers(); -------------------------------------------------------------------------- query_no_kill(); Returns the value of no_kill; EXAMPLE: query_no_kill(); -------------------------------------------------------------------------- query_no_teleport(); Returns the value of no_teleport; EXAMPLE: query_no_teleport(); -------------------------------------------------------------------------- The following functions are for use in setting room chats that are sent like echos to a room. They are nice for adding flavor text to the rooms without having to create invisible mobs doing the chatting. The chats only run when there are players in the room. set_chat_chance(n); This will set the chance of the chat being spammed. If random(100) is less than n, the message is skipped that time. set_chat_delay(int iDelay, int iRandomDelay); This will set the delay between when messages will be spammed to the room. The delay will be iDelay + random(iRandomDelay). The default is 2 seconds if no delay is set, so please set one. EXAMPLE: set_chat_delay(20,30); add_room_chat(string sMsg); This will add a message that will be told to the room. You must include the "
" at the end of the string. You would have to use add_room_chat multiple times to add more than one message, and the messages are a random from the total chats added. EXAMPLE: add_room_chat("The floorboards creak underfoot.
"); remove_room_chat(string sMsg); This will remove sMsg from the possible strings being sent to the room. It must match exactly to the string added with add_room_chat. set_room_chat_check(string sFunc); Allows you to set a function the room will check before spamming the message to the room. If the function returns 0, no message will spam, and all the room chats will stop. The chats will resume if someone enters the room, and the function returns 1. ------------------------------------------------------------------------ If you plan on having a door in your room, you need to be first familiar with this file and how to create rooms, then you need to read through the doc 'wizhelp 4.8 (doors)' and it will go through the step by step process for adding a door to your room. Also, if you are going to be adding additional functions to a room that you wish to define yourself, you need to enable the commands in the following manner. NOTE: This all goes after all the room creation code is completely finished. void init() { ::init(); add_action("yourfunction","name_of_function"); add_action("your2ndfunction","name_of_2nd_function"); etc } More on adding your own functions can be found elsewhere. (or ask an ARCH+ for assistance). -------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------- Following now is an example that uses most of the more commonly used functions of ROOM. #include <mudlib.h> #include <terrain.h> #include <perms.h> inherit ROOM; void reset(int iArg) { ::reset(iArg); make_unique_object("greatsword","/players/alarian/weapons/hellspawn"); add_clone("/players/alarian/monsters/demon",6); if(iArg) return; set_light(0); /* Light level of room (dark here) */ set_terrain(TER_UNDERGROUND|TER_ARCTIC); /* An underground room in the tundra. */ set_short("A frozen cavern"); /* what is seen by players in brief mode. */ set_long("\ This room is deep underground. There are pools of frozen water
\ scattered about in most of the depressions in the floor,
\ and strange writings can be seen on the west wall. There
\ is a small opening leading out of the cavern to the west.
"); add_exit("west","/players/alarian/rooms/cave2"); add_look(({"pool","pools"}),"A thin film of ice covers cold pools of water."); add_look(({"depression","depressions"}),"A low spot in the floor."); add_look("walls","They are stone walls. There is writing on the west wall."); add_look( ({"wall","west wall","western wall"}), "\ There is a small opening in the western wall, and some writing you
\ could read."); add_read("writings","\ It seems to be written in a strange tongue and
\ you can't decipher what is says. Although if you
\ had to make a guess, you would say that whatever
\ is written is written in elvish.
"); set_no_teleport(); } status west_hook() { if(IS_APPLICANT(this_player())) return 0; if(present("demon",this_object())) { write("The demon prevents you from leaving!
"); say(this_player()->query_name()+" was blocked by the demons!
"); return 1; /* the player can't go through */ } return 0; /* the player can go through */ } DO not hardcode items. Use the definition in your header file. The above example created a room with a good description, that has add_looks or add_reads for everything in the description. It also has a unique object and several demons that prevents anyone from leaving once they have entered the room until all the demons are killed. Good luck, if you find any problems or confusing sections in this article use typo/idea/bug to report them. If you have any questions as another BUILDER+, use the Builder line, or post on the Main Wiz board. -------- * Created by Alarian@Darkwind and Hayden@Darkwind. * Last update: 3-28-97 (By Sexy Lexi) * Translated into English: 3/29/97 (Laisha, The Grammarian.) * newroom.c build doc * Added instructions for night/dusk/dawn room descriptions: * 5/9/98 - Hern * Added Hungarian Notation 27/08/98 - Xnedra * Added references to inheriting SEASON_ROOM 7/04/02

docs.title: Magic Resistance and Psionic Resistance.
docs.text: Magic Resistance and Psionic Resistance. Magic and Psionic Resistance are very potent abilities that allow a player or monster to become somewhat immune to the effects of spells and/or certain types of attacks. Because of this, much care must be used when adding an object to the game that has these properties. As a general rule, any object that is not unique, should have at MOST a 1% or 2% magic resistance(MR) OR Psionic resistance(PR), not both. Any object that gives both automatically becomes a unique item. Also, any object that gives more than a one or two percent bonus qualifies as a unique item. There should really be no objects in the game that give over a 15% bonus total. This means that if you have an object that gives both a MR and PR bonus, when you total the bonus's together, they should add up to at most 15%. Also, and object with a bonus higher than 10% should be carried by some sort of legendary creature on the mud (like level 70 to 100 with special abilities). Objects that give bonuses in the 3% to 10% range while unique and hopefully hard to obtain, should be within the grasp of players other than the super high leveled ones. From the perspective of the players, a player that has achieved a MR or PR of 50% should be considered to have an awesome defense. Resistances higher than this should really be unattainable by players. The only real exception to the rule above, would be an object that bestows a higher than normal MR or PR for a short duration. These objects would still be considered unique as far as coding rules go, but would allow for a higher than 15% bonus as long as the duration was short-lived (few minutes or so) or there was some other sort of high cost involved for the user to be able to activate the resistance bonus (like a cost of 5 SP per second or similar). Either way, any object that gives over a 10% or 15% percent bonus can only be temporary items with one or two uses maximum. To use the the above commands, you would need to give the folloing commands: this_player()->add_magic_resistance(1); or this_player()->add_psi_resistance(1); and to remove the bonus: this_player()->add_magic_resistance(-1); or this_player()->add_psi_resistance(-1); *************************IMPORTANT********************************* IF YOU GIVE A BONUS TO A PLAYER FOR SAY "WEARING" AN ITEM, YOU MUST ENSURE THAT WHEN THE ITEM IS REMOVED, THE BONUS IS ALSO REMOVED!!!! *******************************************************************

docs.title: Food and drink contain the standard functions for any object
docs.text: Food and drink contain the standard functions for any object (wizhelp 4.6). Instead of inheriting OBJECT, however, they use the following: DRINK - single serving of alcohol FOOD - single serving of food GEN_KEG - multiple servings of alcohol GEN_MEAL - multiple servings of food They also have additional functions, as follows: Drink: set_soft_strength(int) Determines how filling a drink is. The total of soft plus alco strengths should be proportional to the total of hp plus sp healing. Only single servings currently use this. set_alco_strength(int) set_strength(int) Determines how drunk the drink will make the character. set_hp_healing(int) set_hp_heal(int) Set the amount of hp healed. set_sp_healing(int) set_sp_heal(int) Set the amount of sp healed. set_healing(int) Set both hp and sp healing to int. query_full() Returns 1 if the bottle is full, 0 otherwise. query_drinker_level() Returns the real level necessary to drink the drink. (Remember that bards and halflings will be able to drink it earlier.) set_drinking_message(string) Sets the message others see when the character drinks. Can be left at the default in most cases. Not used for jugs and kegs. set_drinker_message(string) set_drinker_mess(string) Sets the message the character sees when he drinks. set_drinker_message is preferred; set_drinker_mess is preserved for backward compatibility, but works only with drinks, not with kegs/jugs. set_empty_container(string) Determines what the container is. Defaults to "bottle". Does not apply to jugs or kegs. set_stopper(string) Sets the string the character sees if his level is too low to drink. set_drink_name(string) Sets the name of the drink, used in some default messages. Kegs and jugs also use the following: set_kind(<"keg"|"jug">) Determines whether the drink is in a keg or a jug. set_max_drinks(int) Sets the maximum number of drinks that can be held. The default should be used, unless the item is a special case for some reason. set_drinks(int) Sets the number of drinks currently in the container, so you can clone up (for instance) a half-empty keg. Food: set_food_name(string) Sets the name of the food, used in some default messages. reset_short(string) Use this instead of set_short in food, due to a peculiarity of inn food code. set_eater_message(string) set_eater_mess(string) Sets the message the character sees when he eats the food. set_eater_message is preferred; set_eater_mess is preserved for backward compatibility but does not work with snacks and meals. set_hp_heal(int) Sets the amount of hp healed by the food. set_sp_heal(int) Sets the amount of sp healed by the food. set_strength(int) Sets how full the food will make the character. Should normally be about half of the total healing. If hp_heal and/or sp_heal are not set, this also sets them to int. Meals and snacks also use the following: set_kind(<"snack"|"meal">) Set whether the item is a snack or a meal. set_max_uses(int) Sets the maximum number of times the food could be eaten. This should normally default, unless the item is special for some reason. set_uses(int) Sets the number of times the food can be eaten, so you can clone up (for instance) a half-eaten meal.

docs.title: STAT ENHANCEMENT
docs.text: STAT ENHANCEMENT Darkwind has the capability of temporarily increasing a player's abilities without actually changing the character. The functions to do this are add_<stat>(int) where <stat> is the ability you want to increase and int is the amount to boost it. This document contains Darkwind's policy on stat-enhancing items. ALL stat-enhancing items are EXCEPTIONAL. (See wizhelp 4.14 (uniques).) No permanent item may increase a stat more than 4 points. A permanent item that increases a stat more than 2 points must be created unique. Those that increase a stat by 4 are to be considered very powerful, and should only be found guarded by some of the most powerful, legendary creatures of the land. No temporary item may increase a stat more than 8 points. A temporary item that increases a stat more than 5 points must be created unique. (Once it is used up, the item can be created again, but this will prevent guild stockpiles and such.) NOTE: anything with a duration longer than five minutes will not be considered temporary. Multiple stat-enhancing items may be used concurrently, even if they affect the same stat. The old Ogre Gaunlets and Giant Girdle combination is an example. (But see next paragraph.) Players must NOT be able to use multiple copies of an item to stack their bonuses. You cannot have two Amulets Of Beauty worn at the same time to get a larger CHR bonus, for example. If you have a temporary item that enhances a stat, you must put a marker on the player so that they cannot use that item again until it wears off. (There is an example of this type of item in /open/wizards/antcrusher/tome_l_i.c.) Bonus stats may NEVER carry over from one login to the next. Any weapon that enhances stats must be created unique. Period. An armor that enhances stats may not also be exceptional for high armor class or resistance. Enhancing stats is enough. *************************IMPORTANT********************************* IF YOU GIVE A BONUS TO A PLAYER FOR SAY "WEARING" AN ITEM, YOU MUST ENSURE THAT WHEN THE ITEM IS REMOVED, THE BONUS IS ALSO REMOVED!!!! ******************************************************************* Antcrusher - Feb 7, 1996

docs.title: Trap inheritable functions
docs.text: Trap inheritable functions TRAP is the generic trap inheritable. It inherits TREASURE and all of its functions. (Do not use set_short or set_long unless you set a custom search function, however; this is set up with the idea that the typical trap is hidden until triggered.) In addition, TRAP has the following functions: set_trap_message(string) set_trap_mess(string) Sets the custom message a victim sees when he trips the trap. set_trap_message2(string) set_trap_mess2(string) Sets the custom message the rest of the room sees when a victim trips the trap. set_setter(object) Sets the person who set the trap, if any. This person has a 100% chance to find or disarm his trap, and can pass it without setting it off, by default. If the trap does damage, it is also credited to this person. query_setter() Returns the setter, if any. set_damage(int) The amount of damage the trap causes, if any. set_damage_type(int) The type of damage the trap causes. If damage is set but damage type is not, this defaults to WEAPON_DAM_MASK. set_ignore_armor(int) Sets whether or not the trap's damage ignores armor. Set to 1 if it does, 0 otherwise. Defaults to 0. (Useful for poison gas, etc.) set_trigger_action(string) Sets the verb which will trip the trap, ie. 'north', or 'pull', or 'search'. This -must- be set, or the trap will never be tripped! add_trigger_action(string) Performs the same function as set_trigger_action. set_trigger_actions(array of strings) Sets the verbs which will trip the trap.
