docs.text:
Rev. 1 | | Coding Advanced Monsters | ======================== | | Purpose | ======= | | The purpose of this document is to explain some of the more | advanced functions that monsters in Darkwind possess. Basic | functions can be found in the general monster wizhelp file. | Document ======== ************************************************************************* Monster Spells & Specials All monster spells and special attacks use add_combat_mod(). Named presets cover ordinary elemental, magical, physical, and control attacks. A mapping form supports unusual damage, blocks, messages, and named dynamic chance/damage callbacks. ************************************************************************ ------------------------------------------------------------------- A Note on the monster spells: Many, many coders use the monster spells for all manner of special attacks. YOU ARE NOT TO DO THIS. All spells are of type MAGIC automatically and are checked against the target's magic resistance automatically. Therefore, do not set up a monster with a spell attack unless that attack is really a spell! Instead, give the monster an additional add_attack with appropriate settings. The old set_spell functions still work for legacy monsters, but new or edited monsters should register add_combat_mod() entries. ------------------------------------------------------------------- varargs void add_combat_mod(mixed mType, int iChance, string sMessage); mType must be either a bit value or string from the following: SK_MAGIC <-> ( 1 ) <-> "magic" SK_HOLY <-> (1 << 1 ) <-> "holy" SK_UNHOLY <-> (1 << 2 ) <-> "unholy" SK_FIRE <-> (1 << 3 ) <-> "fire" SK_ICE <-> (1 << 4 ) <-> "ice" SK_LIGHTNING <-> (1 << 5 ) <-> "lightning" SK_WATER <-> (1 << 6 ) <-> "water" SK_EARTH <-> (1 << 7 ) <-> "earth" SK_ASTRAL <-> (1 << 8 ) <-> "astral" SK_PSIONIC <-> (1 << 9 ) <-> "psionic" SK_DISEASE <-> (1 << 10) <-> "disease" SK_SOUND <-> (1 << 11) <-> "sound" SK_ACID <-> (1 << 12) <-> "acid" SK_HEAL <-> (1 << 13) <-> "heal" SK_FEAR <-> (1 << 14) <-> "fear" SK_PUNCH <-> (1 << 15) <-> "punch" SK_KICK <-> (1 << 16) <-> "kick" SK_FLURRY <-> (1 << 17) <-> "flurry" SK_DISARM <-> (1 << 18) <-> "disarm" SK_STUN <-> (1 << 19) <-> "stun" SK_SILENCE <-> (1 << 20) <-> "silence" SK_BLIND <-> (1 << 21) <-> "blind" SK_POISON <-> (1 << 22) <-> "poison" SK_BITE <-> (1 << 23) <-> "bite" SK_SLASH <-> (1 << 24) <-> "slash" SK_CLEAVE <-> (1 << 25) <-> "cleave" iChance is an optional value for the percent chance each combat round for the modified combat to happen. Though any integer is accepted, the preset form is capped from 1 to 25. If 0 or no value is supplied, the standard preset chance will be used. Since mods are done per round, this is the chance that a monster mod will proc in a given round. sMessage is an optional value for the message to be supplied to the room. It follows the room_message formatting for a string. If no value is supplied, the standard message will be used. See wizhelp 9.14 for help with string formatting. You can have multiple combat mods with the same type. NOTE: DO NOT include target if using "heal" Examples: add_combat_mod("kick"); add_combat_mod("kick",12); add_combat_mod("kick",15,"$N $vkick $t, HARD!"); add_combat_mod("heal",5,"$N $vcast a spell of healing!"); For a special that does not fit a preset, pass a mapping: add_combat_mod(([ "chance": 30, "message": "$N $vspit a shard through $t!", "damage": 45, "damage_type": WEAPON_PIERCE|DAM_COLD, "blocks": BLK_PARALYZE|BLK_ENTANGLE_ARMS, "effect": "damage" ])); Mapping chance is bounded from 0 to 100 rather than the preset 25 percent safety cap. Use it deliberately. Supported fields are: type optional named or SK_* preset chance fixed percentage chance_func named function returning a percentage message room_message-formatted text other_msg optional literal observer text victim_msg literal victim text paired with other_msg damage fixed damage damage_func named function returning damage damage_type exact damage bitfield blocks blocks which prevent the monster from acting; zero or omitted uses the physical or spell default ignore_blocks explicitly permits the mod to act through control effects effect damage, heal, fear, disarm, stun/paralyze, silence, blind, movement, poison, or callback callback named effect function receiving target, damage, mod duration optional control duration magic_resist whether DAM_MAGIC permits an MR roll (default yes) range_check whether a nonmagical attack requires range Named callbacks receive (object target, mapping combat_mod). If damage and damage_func are omitted, query_mod_combat_damage() provides the normal level-based damage and may still be overridden by the monster. Prefer message and room_message placeholders. Use other_msg/victim_msg only when the two perspectives genuinely need different prose. Boss phases use this same effect executor, but retain their own phase, target, cooldown, and scaling scheduler. Ordinary add_combat_mod() procs are disabled on bosses by default to prevent two independent special-attack schedules from firing together. A reviewed encounter may opt in with set_boss_combat_mods_enabled(1). See wizhelp 4.3c (Boss Monsters) for the full boss contract. A word of caution: Stacking multiple combat mods can be extremely dangerous for players. Since the chances are independent, multiple combat mods can fire each round. Here's a useful formula to see a rough chance of how often a mod will fire: fire_chance = 1; foreach (mod chance) { fire_chance *= (1 - mod chance) } fire_chance = 1 - fire_chance; Here's an example of the above: oMonster->add_combat_mod("kick",10); oMonster->add_combat_mod("disarm",15); oMonster->add_combat_mod("punch",10); oMonster->add_combat_mod("acid",12); fire_chance = 1 - ( (1-.1)*(1-.15)*(1-.1)*(1-.12) ) = = 1 - ( 0.60588) = 39.41% This means that 39.41% of the time, a monster mod will fire. HINT: Using query_avg_mod_chance() on a monster will do the math for you. Each combat mod increase mob xp by 10%. --------------------------------------------------------------------- The following functions are deprecated. Please use the previously described method (add_combat_mod) ** set_chance(c); ** ** int c. Sets the chance that the monster will cast a spell. This is ** checked every round of battle. ** ** set_spell_mess1("m."); ** ** string m. Sets the message written to the room of the monster to ** "m". LPC adds the "
" newline but not punctuation. ** ** set_spell_mess2("m."); ** ** string m. Sets the message written to the victim of the spell to ** "m". LPC adds the "
" newline but not punctuation. ** ** set_spell_dam(d); ** ** int d. Sets the damage done by the spell to d. ** ** set_spell_type(d); ** ** int d. Sets the damage type of the spell to d. The damage type ** will automatically have the type DAM_MAGIC added to it. You can ** set others, such as DAM_FIRE for fireballs, DAM_EVIL for life ** draining, etc. See 'wizhelp 4.17 (damage types)' for a complete ** list. ** ** add_attack(1,2,3,4,5,6,7); | ** ** This function gives the monster an attack. You may call add_attack as ** many times as you want to give your monster several different attacks. ** The elements of an attack are as follows: ** ** 1. Number of swings. Integer representing the potential number of times ** this attack will be executed each round of combat. ** ** 2. Chance to occur. Integer representing the % chance that each of the ** swings will actually happen on any particular round. ** ** 3. Hit bonus. This can be a positive or negative integer and will make ** the attack more or less likely to hit. It is also a percentage. ** ** 4. Damage class. This integer is the amount of damage the attack will ** cause and is analogous to the old 'weapon class'. ** ** 5. Damage type. This is the type of damage done and it set up as a ** bitfield. (See 'wizhelp 4.17 (damage types)' for a list of current types.) ** Attacks can be given multiple types separated by |, so a ** venemous stinger might be WEAPON_PIERCE|DAM_POISON. ** ** 6. This is the attack type of this attack and is also a bitfield of sorts. ** Attack type determines which messages are displayed in combat when this ** attack is used. It has 4 basic settings. It can be BLUNT, SLASH, or ** PIERCE to use the weapon hit strings. It can be 0 to use the default ** "unarmed combat" strings. If you are going to use custom hit strings, ** set this to 0 if you are using a "simple" set of strings, or to some ** nonzero number if you are using a "complex" set. ** ** 7. The last argument is optional. If it is given, it should be either an ** array of string arrays or an array of arrays of string arrays. This ** allows you to customize your own messages to be displayed when an attack ** is used. There are 2 options here. You can use the "simple" method and ** include 1 set of strings, or you can use the "complex" method, in which ** case the string displayed will depend on damage done. This requires ** a full set of 6 arrays, each array having at least one combat message, ** with each combat message itself an array of 4 strings. /* Yes, it's ** complicated. Believe me, I'm not enjoying explaining this any more than ** you are enjoying trying to figure it out. */ ** A single combat message has the format: ** ({"string1","string2","string3","string4"}) ** The game will use this to create messages in the following formats: ** To the attacker: ** You hit target, string4 target string1. ** To the target: ** Attacker hits you, string3 youstring2. <-no space between you & str2 ** Others in the room: ** Attacker hits target, string3 target string1. ** As you can see, string1 and string2 can often be identical, and can be ** thought of as the "adverb" while string3 and string4 can be thought of ** as the 1st person and 3rd person of the "verb". Let's say Hillary ** strikes Bill with the following combat message: ({"in the face"," in ** the face","and slaps","and slap"}). ** Hillary would see : You hit Bill, and slap Bill in the face. ** Bill would see: Hillary hits you, and slaps you in the face. ** Others would see: Hillary hits Bill, and slaps Bill in the face. ** Once you've got one combat message right, make a bunch more and put them ** into an array: ({ ({string1,string2,string3,string4}),({...}),({...}) }) ** and pass the entire array as the 7th argument to add_attack. Make sure ** you have set the attack type (6th argument) to 0. This will cause one ** of your messages to be used at random each hit. If you want the message ** displayed to vary according to damage done, then you need to send an ** entire array of 6 these arrays, going from least powerful to most ** powerful. So, to review: ** ({"string1","string2","string3","string4"}) = one combat message ** ({ message1,message2,message3,... }) = one "simple" array ** ({ simple1,simple2,simple3,simple4,simple5,simple6 }) = one "complex" ** array ** If you pass 1 simple array as an argument, the game will pick one random ** message from it for each hit. If you pass a complex array, the game will ** pick one of the simple arrays based on the damage done, and then display ** a random message from that simple array. --------------------------------------------------------------------- set_viking(); no arg. Gives the monster the viking curse. set_whimpy(); no arg. Will make the monster run away when its hit points get low. set_wimpy_cmd(s); string s. If set, this will cause the monster to always perform the command 's' first when trying to wimpy. You can use this to control which direction a monster attempts to run away. load_chat(chance, strs); int chance, string *strs. Sets the chance that a monster will talk each heartbeat to chance, and sets the things the monster can say to the array passed into load_chat(). load_a_chat(chance, strs); int chance, string *strs. Same as load_chat, but these messages are said only during battle. enable_player_commands(); ***** DEPRECATED: all monsters can use standard commands and emotes. You must #include <daemons.h> to do this. This sets up the monster as able to perform all regular player commands from /cmds/std and /cmds/soul. load_cmd(chance, strs); int chance, string *strs. This works exactly like load_chat, except it is a list of commands the monster will perform. You must first do an enable_player_commands() or else the monster won't have the ability to do much beyond wielding weapons and moving around. It is usually easier to enable the player commands and have an array which includes something like ({"say who are you?","say I'm Bob!","sing"}) rather than having to do ({"Monstername asks: who are you?
","Monstername exclaims: I'm Bob!
", "Monstername sings a song.
"}) for fairly obvious reasons. Anywhere you place a $N, it will be replaced with the name of a random player character in the room, allowing the monster to do directed emotes. "kick $N" would cause the monster to kick a random player, for instance. load_a_cmd(chance, strs); Same as load_cmd, except works in combat. set_random_pick(r); int r. Determines if the monster will randomly pick an object from the room's inventory. If the item it picks up is a weapon which has a better WC than its current wielded weapon, then it wields the weapon. If the item is an armour, and it is not already wearing an armour of that type, it will wear the armour. set_death_clone(string sFilePath, status tCloneToEnv, int iQuantity); At death, the monster will clone sFilePath. If tCloneToEnv is 1 or the monster is SIZ_NONE, the object will clone to the environment. If iQuantity is not set, it will default to 1. To have any other quantity, you must also set tCloneToEnv. If tCloneToEnv and iQuanity are not set, it defaults to loading on the corpse, and 1 item. set_dead_ob(ob); object ob. Usually this_object() is the object passed to set_dead_ob. Use this function in conjunction with monster_died() when you want something done when the monster dies. This function is useful for destructing corpses (Like on Stone Golems...) set_hit_ob(ob); object ob. Usually this_object() is the object passed to set_hit_ob. Use this function in conjunction with monster_hit() when you want the monster to have a special combat ability. The monster_hit() function should be an integer function which returns an amount of extra damage to be done by the monster that attack. The monster will pass its attacker to monster_hit() as and argument. Monster_hit() can be used for many things other than simply doing damage. It can be used to have the monster talk, run away, heal itself, summon more monsters, steal from the player, etc - what's inside monster_hit is up to the coder. set_init_ob(ob); object ob. Usually this_object() is the object passed to set_init_ob. If this is defined, the function monster_init will be called by the monster whenever it has its init called. Essentially, this allows you to write a function that is executed whenever your monster meets another monster or player. Monster_init should return 0 or else it will interrupt the normal init process making aggressive monsters not attack and other things. can_put_and_get(n); optional string n. If n exists, the monster can put and get things. If n does not exist, the monster cannot pick up and drop things. Further examples: can_put_and_get(1); // The monster can pick up and drop things can_put_and_get(yes); // The monster can pick up and drop things can_put_and_get(no); // The monster can pick up and drop things can_put_and_get(); // The monster canNOT pick up and drop things set_keep_alive(keep_alive); int keep_alive. This function should be used VERY INFREQUENTLY on UNIQUE monsters. This will not turn off the heart_beat in monsters. DO NOT use this unless the object you are creating REQUIRES it. If you are not sure of why you would use this, then DON'T USE IT. set_death_messages(i_died,you_killed); When the monster dies it will display the you_killed string to the object which killed it and it will display the i_died message to everyone in the room. If these are not set, the default messages will be used. command("cmd"); string cmd. Forces the monster to perform the command "cmd". The force_us() function isn't always good, because it checks the level of the caller, and this function can be called by a room. set_wander(int chance, int time); This is similar to the move_at_reset function. It gives the monster a percentage chance equal to 'chance' to move. This chance will be checked every 'time' seconds. For example, set_wander(50,20); would cause the monster to have a 50% to make a random move every 20 seconds. This allows greater flexibility than the move_at_reset does. See wizhelp 10.4 for more info. See wizhelp 4.2 for make_room_unique for wandering mobs. --------------------------------------------------------------------- set_match(object,functions,types,matches); You use this to allow your monster to react to what it sees. Object is the object where your functions will be located. Functions, types, and | matches are all string arrays. Each must be exactly the same size as the others, so you should use allocate() and leave the appropriate elements empty. The following example is Fornay's set_match: function = allocate(12); type = allocate(12); match = allocate(12); function[0] = "why_did"; type[0] = "sells"; type[1] = "attack"; type[2] = "left"; match[2] = "the game"; type[3] = "takes"; type[4] = "drops"; function[5] = "must_be_nice"; type[5] = "is now level"; function[6] = "smiles"; type[6] = "smiles"; match[6] = " happily."; function[7] = "say_hello"; type[7] = "arrives"; function[8] = "test_say"; type[8] = "says:"; type[9] = "tells you:"; function[10] = "follow"; type[10] = "leaves"; function[11] = "gives"; type[11] = "gives"; set_match(this_object(),function,type,match); This doesn't make much sense on first glance, but it is fairly clear if a table is made out of it: Array FUNCTION TYPE MATCH position: Execute this function: If monster sees: followed by: 0 why_did sells 1 attack 2 left the game 3 takes 4 drops 5 must_be_nice is now level 6 smiles smiles happily 7 say_hello arrives 8 test_say says: 9 tells you: 10 follow leaves 11 gives gives Anywhere there is a blank spot, the array has a 0 in it, done automatically by allocate(). Every time the monster sees a message it will look through the TYPE array, and scan the message to see if it contains the TYPE. It then sees if the rest of the message contains the MATCH of the same number. If the MATCH string is present in the message, OR if there is no MATCH at all, then the last FUNCTION that it found is executed with the original message as an argument. For example, if Fornay sees the text: "Bill takes our taxes" First, it will find the FUNCTION 'why_did' at position 0 and save it, but won't do anything else because "Bill takes our taxes" does not contain the text "sells". Next, it will go through TYPE until it gets to position 3, where it finds the word "takes". It then looks for a MATCH. Since MATCH position 3 is empty, the MATCH is an "automatic" success. The last function it found was 'why_did' from position 0, so it now does a this_object()->why_did("Bill takes our taxes"; set_friends(names, chance); names can be either a single string or a string array. Each heartbeat an npc has a chance to check whether an npc in its friends list is being attacked and join that combat. The optional chance is a percentage from 1 to 100 and defaults to 10. Use 100 to make friends always join as they did previously. set_friend_join_chance(chance); Changes the percentage chance that the npc will check and join its friends each heartbeat. Values are limited to 0 through 100; 0 disables joining. int query_friend_join_chance(); Returns the npc's current friend join chance. catch_tell(string sStr); | | This function allows you to create responses to your monsters when a specific| string is displayed in the environment that the monster is in. You can hash | up the string anyway you like to check for matches and then call functions as| appropriate. | ** NOTE ** For a way to do easier responses, see wizhelp 5.6 | ***NOTE*** | | It _IS_ possible for a monster's load_chat to get caught and matched in it's | catch_tell. If this happens the mud can crash depending on what you do with | the catch_tell. So unless you specifically desire to simulate NPC's | interacting with each other put an NPC check in the catch_tell before you do | anything with it. | | ***NOTE2*** | | One thing to remember is that a catch_tell is only looking for a string match| in the environment that the monster is in. It _IS_ possible to fool a catch | tell with an emote or something else along that line. So you will have to | put in the appropriate object checks as necessary. | follow(str,i,ob); Using this function allows your monsters to follow other players or monsters around the mud. Str should be the exit message the monster receives. If any positive integer i is passed, then wizards in nohassle mode will be exempted from being followed. Ob is an optional object which, if present, will be the only object the monster will follow. This function is not used in reset, but should instead be called through the use of catch_tell as in the following example: catch_tell(string str) { follow(str,1,this_object()->query_attack()); } In this example, the monster is told to follow its attacker if the attacker leaves the room, but to ignore any other players/npcs or wizards with nohassle mode enabled. DEPRECATED: all monsters should work correctly now. *************************************************************** *Important Note* Additionally, monsters cloned through the reset() of a room will NOT follow properly. To avoid this, if you wish to add following monsters to a room through reset, use a call_out. For example: void reset(int iArg) { ::reset(iArg); call_out("make_monsters",2); etc } void make_monsters() { make_object("monster","/players/johndoe/monster",2); } *************************************************************** varargs void set_monster_destruct_timer(int iTime, mixed xFunc); This function will destruct the monster in iTime seconds. If xFunc is defined and is a closure, it will apply the function before destructing it. If it's a string, it will tell_room or tell_object before destructing it. The monster will be moved to the quitroom before destruction, so anything the monster has will NOT be dropped in the room. If the monster is in combat, the call_out will be called again 30 seconds later.

docs.title: Rev. 0
docs.text:
Rev. 0 Coding Boss Monsters ==================== Purpose ======= This document explains the shared BOSS_NPC inherit: when to use it, how tiers and phases are scaled, how special attacks and personal rewards work, and how a boss room must own respawning. Read wizhelp 4.3 and wizhelp 4.3b first. A boss is still a monster and uses all normal monster descriptions, races, equipment, resistances, and combat functions. The inherit is not a substitute for encounter design. A good boss has a recognizable identity, readable phase changes, attacks which ask different questions of a group, and a room from which players can retreat. More hit points alone make a longer monster, not a better boss. ----------------------------------------------------------------- WHEN TO USE BOSS_NPC ----------------------------------------------------------------- Use BOSS_NPC when the creature needs one or more of the following: - A named encounter with one or more fresh hit-point phases. - Group-aware tier scaling and per-hit damage caps. - A scheduled set of attacks with targets and cooldowns. - Contributor tracking and personal reward chests. - A persistent, blueprint-wide respawn cooldown. - The standard boss event, death, and adaptive-counter lifecycle. Do not use BOSS_NPC merely to mark a captain, shopkeeper, or ordinary rare spawn as important. MONSTER plus normal combat mods is cheaper and clearer when the encounter does not need boss lifecycle behavior. The first lines of a boss should normally be: #include <mudlib.h> #include <types.h> inherit BOSS_NPC; Use <blocks.h> only when the monster directly refers to BLK_* constants. Use a legal race from /open/INCLUDE/monster_race.h. ----------------------------------------------------------------- MINIMUM BOSS SETUP ----------------------------------------------------------------- The normal monster reset contract still applies: void reset(int iArg) { if (!is_clone(this_object())) return; ::reset(iArg); if (iArg) return; set_name("ember warden"); set_level(55); set_boss_name("the Ember Warden"); set_boss_tier(2); /* normal monster setup and set_boss_phases() follow */ } Call the inherited reset exactly once. Set the normal name and level before the phase list. set_level() establishes the base level used by phases which do not provide their own level. set_boss_name(string name); This is the encounter name used in boss information, reward chests, and event announcements. It may be more complete than set_name(). set_boss_tier(int tier); Sets tier 1 through 5. Values below 1 become tier 1; values above 5 use the tier-5 profile. Tier is a mechanical group profile, not a synonym for monster level. set_boss_reset_timeout(int seconds); Sets the time out of combat before an abandoned encounter returns to phase one. The minimum is 10 seconds and the default is 45. Values from 60 to 120 seconds are common when players may need a short retreat. set_boss_respawn_cooldown(int seconds); Overrides the tier default. This is a persistent cooldown for the boss blueprint, not merely a call_out in one loaded room. Use 0 to restore the tier-derived default; 0 does not disable the cooldown. set_boss_overlevel_roasts(status enabled); Overlevel insults in the Events channel are opt-in. Normal boss victory announcements are the default. Enable this only when the public tone is an intentional part of the encounter. ----------------------------------------------------------------- TIERS AND THE NUMBERS YOU ACTUALLY GET ----------------------------------------------------------------- Phase hp, wc, and ac are inputs to the tier profile. They are not final combat values. The core tier values are: Tier Group HP Mult. WC Bonus AC Bonus Reduction Hit Cap Respawn 1 1 x1.60 +2 +4 8% 18% 10 min 2 2 x3.00 +6 +10 18% 12% 15 min 3 3 x5.50 +10 +16 32% 11% 20 min 4 4 x10.00 +14 +24 50% 6% 30 min 5 5 x18.00 +20 +34 68% 3% 40 min The hit cap is a percentage of the smallest scaled phase pool. Higher tiers also add outgoing damage, accuracy, swing rate, regeneration, attack cadence, and group-pressure mechanics. Those bonuses weaken when fewer than the expected number of contributors are present. The framework does not make an undersized group more lethal simply because players are missing. Example: a tier-2 phase with "hp":5000 starts with 15000 HP. Do not first calculate a final 15000-HP phase and then place 15000 in the mapping unless you actually intend a 45000-HP phase. Tier 3 and above also choose adaptive counters from the contributing group's guild composition. These temporarily pressure magic, healing, burst damage, martial attackers, or pets. They are part of the tier profile; do not add a second homemade anti-group system without first reviewing the combined fight. ----------------------------------------------------------------- PHASES ----------------------------------------------------------------- set_boss_phases(mapping *phases); Replaces the phase list. A lethal hit before the final phase is capped, the transition is announced, and the next phase receives a fresh scaled HP pool. The final phase dies normally. add_boss_phase(mapping phase); Appends one phase. Prefer one set_boss_phases() call when the full fight is known in reset; it is easier to read and review. A phase mapping supports: name Player-visible phase name. hp Base HP before the tier multiplier. wc Base weapon class before the tier bonus. ac Base armour class before the tier bonus. level Optional level for this phase. attacks Array of attack mappings. attacks_per_round Maximum successful scheduled attacks each round. transition_msg Room text shown when entering this phase after phase one. enter_func Named function called after phase stats are applied. The enter function receives the phase mapping and the one-based phase number: void awaken_furnace(mapping mPhase, int iPhase) { /* Change room fixtures, summon support, or update encounter state. */ } An enter function also runs when phase one is applied during setup or an encounter reset. Make it idempotent. Validate the room with objectp() before calling it, and clean up anything it creates when the encounter resets. Use a transition message to explain what mechanically changed. Good phase text identifies a new stance, exposed weakness, summoned hazard, or changed arena. Color strings are permitted, but end them with a reset. The framework also repairs legacy newline and white-color tokens in transition text. ----------------------------------------------------------------- PHASE ATTACKS ----------------------------------------------------------------- Each phase attack is a mapping. The scheduler walks the list in order until attacks_per_round attacks have fired. Every attack rolls independently, so putting the strongest attack first gives it first claim on the round's budget. Supported attack fields are: name Required in practice; also identifies its cooldown. chance Percent chance when the attack is off cooldown. Default 20. cooldown Seconds before that named attack may fire again. Default 3. target_mode current, random, lowest_hp, or all. Default current. damage Two-element ({ low, high }) range. Default ({ 40, 80 }). damage_type Exact WEAPON_* and DAM_* bitfield. Default DAM_MAGIC. effect damage, heal, fear, disarm, stun, paralyze, silence, blind, movement, poison, or callback. Default damage. duration Duration used by stun, silence, and movement effects. room_msg One string or an array of room_message-formatted strings. victim_msg One string or an array of messages sent to a single target. callback Named function used when effect is callback. Attack names should be unique within a phase. Cooldowns are keyed by name and are cleared at a phase change. The damage range is rolled first, then tier outgoing-damage scaling and any tier threat floor are applied. Boss phase attacks deliberately do not roll magic resistance and do not perform a weapon-range check. damage_type still matters for resistances, weaknesses, and combat reporting. For current, random, and lowest_hp attacks, room_msg and victim_msg may use the normal room_message placeholders described in wizhelp 9.14. For an all-target attack, write room text which does not depend on one $t target. The room sees one attack announcement and the effect is then applied to every valid target. Custom room_msg and victim_msg values join the framework's built-in variants; they do not replace them. An array can weight the encounter's own voice more heavily. The phase transition remains the clearest guaranteed custom telegraph. Damage, stun, paralyze, silence, and movement apply the rolled attack damage. Heal restores the rolled amount to the boss. Fear, disarm, blind, and poison perform their named effect without applying immediate attack damage. Built-in stun, paralyze, silence, and movement effects participate in the shared boss-control recovery window. Prefer them to callbacks which directly set blocks. This prevents several bosses from chaining control with no chance for the player to recover. ----------------------------------------------------------------- CUSTOM ATTACK CALLBACKS ----------------------------------------------------------------- Use effect "callback" only when the built-in effects cannot express the mechanic. The function signature is: My_callback(object target, int damage, mapping attack); A successful callback owns the whole effect, including applying damage. If the callback is missing or errors, the framework falls back to ordinary damage. Keep callbacks small and defensive: void brand_target(object oTarget, int iDamage, mapping mAttack) { if (!objectp(oTarget) || environment(oTarget) != environment(this_object())) return; oTarget->receive_damage(iDamage, mAttack["damage_type"], 0, this_object()); /* Apply the area's established status-effect contract here. */ } Do not retain a target object in saved state or across delayed work. Capture primitive identity, validate objectp() and environment again in a call_out, and remove callbacks/effects on both normal completion and destruction. ----------------------------------------------------------------- ORDINARY COMBAT MODS ----------------------------------------------------------------- Ordinary add_combat_mod() attacks are disabled on BOSS_NPC by default. This prevents the monster combat-mod scheduler and the boss phase scheduler from both firing specials in the same round. set_boss_combat_mods_enabled(status enabled); Opt in only after reviewing the combined proc rate and attack budget. A normal phase list plus layered combat mods can create unexpected burst damage. Usually the right answer is to move the attack into the phase list. ----------------------------------------------------------------- REWARDS AND CONTRIBUTORS ----------------------------------------------------------------- The framework records players who damage or actively fight the boss. Pet damage resolves to the player owner. At final death, each eligible contributor still in the room may receive a chest bearing that player's name. Chests last five minutes. A player who has left the room or is dead at the delivery boundary is not eligible. With no configuration, tier selects the normal reward-pool rolls and coin range. To override them: set_boss_reward_config(mapping rewards); Supported fields are: enabled 0 disables personal chests; 1 enables them. rolls Number of random tier-pool item rolls. reward_rolls Legacy alias for rolls. items Exact object paths placed in every eligible chest. coins One integer or an inclusive ({ low, high }) range. Examples: set_boss_reward_config(([ "rolls":2, "coins":({15000,30000}) ])); set_boss_reward_config(([ "items":({ CITADEL_EQUIP + "emberglass_cloak" }), "coins":24000 ])); set_boss_reward_config(([ "rolls":0, "coins":0 ])); The items array is not a pool. Every listed item is cloned into every eligible player's chest. An explicit items array also suppresses the generic golden-elixir roll. Do not place a UNIQUE object in personal rewards. Use UNIQUE_D's clone_unique_object() or make_unique_object() contract for a shared unique, and use an area or quest-owned delivery path for personal quest items. set_boss_rewards_enabled(status enabled); Use set_boss_rewards_enabled(0) when an area controller completely owns rewards. Do not let both systems deliver the same encounter reward. If monster_died() is overridden, call the inherited implementation exactly once. It owns the respawn timestamp, room retry, death-watch cleanup, personal chests, Events announcement, and EB_BOSS_DEFEATED event. int monster_died(object oKiller, object *aoAllKillers) { object oRoom; oRoom = environment(this_object()); if (objectp(oRoom) && function_exists("boss_defeated", oRoom)) oRoom->boss_defeated(oKiller, aoAllKillers); return ::monster_died(oKiller, aoAllKillers); } ----------------------------------------------------------------- THE BOSS ROOM OWNS RESPAWNING ----------------------------------------------------------------- A fixed boss should normally be populated with count-aware add_clone(). Put the call before the room's periodic-reset return so the room reasserts its population target: void reset(int iArg) { ::reset(iArg); add_clone(CITADEL_MOBS + "ember_warden", 1); if (iArg) return; /* descriptions, looks, terrain, domain, and exits */ } add_clone() recognizes BOSS_NPC, registers this room as the spawn owner, checks BOSS_RESPAWN_D, and schedules a bounded retry when the cooldown has not expired. Do not clone the boss manually, bypass add_clone() with an area-wide population daemon, or build a second respawn call_out for the same blueprint. The room should have an unconditional retreat route. A dangerous aggressive boss plus a locked only exit is not difficulty; it is a trap. Gates which open after the kill should guard progression beyond the arena, not the route back out. See wizhelp 4.2 for the rest of the room contract. ----------------------------------------------------------------- COMPLETE TWO-PHASE EXAMPLE ----------------------------------------------------------------- #include <mudlib.h> #include <types.h> #include "../citadel.h" inherit BOSS_NPC; void reset(int iArg) { if (!is_clone(this_object())) return; ::reset(iArg); if (iArg) return; set_name("ember warden"); set_aliases(({ "warden", "construct", "boss" })); set_level(55); set_boss_name("the Ember Warden"); set_boss_tier(2); set_boss_reset_timeout(75); set_boss_respawn_cooldown(1800); set_boss_reward_config(([ "rolls":1, "coins":({18000,26000}) ])); set_short("the Ember Warden"); set_long(wrap("Black iron plates overlap around a furnace-bright core. " "Every joint exhales a measured ribbon of sparks, as though the " "construct were counting down to a breach.")); set_race("golem"); set_size(SIZ_LARGE); set_al(-700, 500); set_aggressive(1); set_no_scare(1); add_resistance(DAM_FIRE); add_weakness(DAM_COLD); load_chat(6, ({ "The Ember Warden turns one plated hand toward the nearest doorway.
", "A furnace pulse passes through the Warden's iron ribs.
" })); load_a_chat(10, ({ "The Warden measures the room through a slit of white fire.
" })); set_boss_phases(({ ([ "name":"The Sealed Furnace", "hp":4800, "wc":30, "ac":28, "attacks_per_round":2, "attacks":({ ([ "name":"iron_rebuke", "chance":30, "cooldown":2, "target_mode":"current", "damage":({38,54}), "damage_type":WEAPON_BLUNT ]), ([ "name":"cinder_arc", "chance":24, "cooldown":4, "target_mode":"random", "damage":({32,46}), "damage_type":DAM_FIRE|DAM_MAGIC ]), ([ "name":"locking_grip", "chance":18, "cooldown":5, "target_mode":"current", "damage":({26,38}), "damage_type":WEAPON_BLUNT, "effect":"movement", "duration":2 ]) }) ]), ([ "name":"The Open Furnace", "hp":6200, "wc":34, "ac":30, "attacks_per_round":2, "transition_msg":"The Warden's chest plates peel apart, " "exposing a furnace-white core as heat floods the chamber.
", "attacks":({ ([ "name":"furnace_wave", "chance":26, "cooldown":4, "target_mode":"all", "damage":({28,42}), "damage_type":DAM_FIRE|DAM_MAGIC, "room_msg":"The open furnace releases a flat wave of " "white heat across the chamber!
" ]), ([ "name":"slag_hammer", "chance":32, "cooldown":2, "target_mode":"current", "damage":({48,68}), "damage_type":WEAPON_BLUNT|DAM_FIRE ]), ([ "name":"furnace_draft", "chance":15, "cooldown":6, "target_mode":"current", "damage":({150,210}), "effect":"heal" ]) }) ]) })); } The associated room still needs its full light, domain, terrain, description, looks, and exits. Its population portion is simply: void reset(int iArg) { ::reset(iArg); add_clone(CITADEL_MOBS + "ember_warden", 1); if (iArg) return; /* Set up the room. Keep the retreat exit unconditional. */ } ----------------------------------------------------------------- REVIEW CHECKLIST ----------------------------------------------------------------- Before submitting a boss encounter, verify: - The blueprint uses BOSS_NPC and the clone-only reset guard. - set_name() and set_level() precede set_boss_phases(). - The race exists and size, alignment, descriptions, and aliases are set. - Final phase HP was calculated after applying the tier multiplier. - Attack names, chances, cooldowns, target modes, and types are intentional. - Control is readable and uses built-in recovery-aware effects where possible. - All-target attacks have text which makes sense without a single target. - Phase transitions say what changed instead of only announcing anger. - The room uses add_clone(path, 1) before its periodic-reset return. - The arena has a usable retreat and progression locks do not trap entrants. - Only one system owns rewards and unique items use UNIQUE_D correctly. - Any monster_died() override returns ::monster_died() exactly once. - Room callbacks and delayed work validate objectp() and environment(). - The monster and its owning room compile with lpc-check. *************************************************************************** Making Armours *************************************************************************** Note: All literal code in this help document is separated by a bunch of = signs. The = signs are NOT part of the code. For example: ==================== #include <mudlib.h> #include <types.h> #include <material.h> ==================== refers to the three include lines, literally. *************************************************************************** Basic Armours *************************************************************************** A basic acceptable armour inherits GEN_ARMOUR and sets a few parameters. Your armour file MUST have the following lines of code at the top: ==================== #include <mudlib.h> #include <types.h> #include <material.h> #include <basic_armour.h> inherit GEN_ARMOUR; ==================== If you want to put in comments before these lines, that's fine, but these MUST precede any active code in the file. Your armour MUST haved a reset function, with appropriate checks for clones. That is, it must have the code: ==================== void reset(int iArg) { if (!is_clone(this_object())) return; ::reset(iArg); if (iArg) return; ==================== Even a basic armour has to have a few settings to make it interesting. You should have the following settings for your armour: For a standard armour form, prefer the shared template contract: ==================== set_armour_template("chainmail"); ==================== Templates supply a canonical size, composition, coverage, default material, aliases, weight, value, and material/quality-aware description. The clonable stock forms live under /objects/standard_equipment/armour/. Call template selection before deliberate overrides such as set_material(), set_quality(), set_short(), or set_long(). Use query_armour_templates() to inspect the live template names and query_armour_template_definition(name) to inspect one. Area armour with custom prose can instead include <basic_armour.h> and use the closest semantic ARMOUR_* identity: ==================== set_new_type(ARMOUR_BREASTPLATE); ==================== Do not assemble a recurring standard form from raw size, composition, and coverage bits. Extend <basic_armour.h> when a genuinely recurring form is missing. The individual setters below remain valid for exceptional forms and for overriding template defaults. set_short("short"); Replace "short" with the quoted short description of your armour. The short description is the one a player sees when an object is just lying on the ground, in a shop, in someone's inventory etc. set_long("long.
"); Replace "long" with the quoted long description of your armour. The long description is the one a player sees when he actually does a 'look' or 'examine' on an object. Remember to add both a period and a newline (
) at the end of your description since LPC won't do that for you. set_name("name"); Replace "name" with the quoted name of your armour. This name should be the main name by which your armour is called, since it may show up on occasion in spam to players. It should never be a secret id key used to uniquely identify it for coding purposes. For example, "bobs_magic_plate_key" is a terrible name for an armour. It is often a good idea to use the short description of the armour as its name as well, but always use all lowercase letters and no articles. (e.g. "silver platemail" is good, but "a silver platemail" or "Silver Platemail" are bad). set_alias("alias"); Replace "alias" with the quoted alias of your armour. This alias can be any other way to refer to an armour. For example, if you had a silver platemail with the name "silver platemail" you would also want to have the aliases "silver plate", "platemail" and "mail" as aliases. If you want to use a secret id key to uniquely identify your armour, you can use set it as an alias. You can add multiple aliases by using this setting over and over again. This setting is optional. set_new_type(TYPE1|TYPE2|etc.); Replace TYPE1|TYPE2|etc. with an ORed set of armour type values. That is, something that looks like: MEDIUM|HIDE|TORSO Exactly one of the values must be a size (SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE, or HUGE) and exactly one of the values must be an armor type (e.g. CLOTHES, PADDED, SCALE, CHAINMAIL etc.) Finally, at least one value must be a location (LEGS, TORSO, RING, SHOULDERS, AURA etc). RING and AMULET each allow two worn items. Other locations normally allow one worn item. set_material(TYPE1|TYPE2|etc.); Replace TYPE1|TYPE2|etc. with an ORed set of material values. That is, something that looks like: MAT_STEEL|MAT_WOOD Valid material types are listed in the material documentation, wizhelp 4.16 'materials'. set_quality(quality); Replace quality with an integer quality value from -100 to 100. Quality is how good your armour is, compared to other armours of the given composition. A quality of 0 is average, and a quality of 100 is the best of the best. A -100 quality would be something laughably bad (like old, broken down rusty platemail that impedes more than it protects.) Any armour with a quality of greater than 40 is considered at least exceptional. Any with a quality greater than 60 is unique. (see also wizhelp 4.14 'uniques'). Typical factors that should affect quality are: craftsmanship, wear/damage, rust, poor fit, odd shape, balance, extra thick/thin etc. set_weight(weight); Replace weight with an integer weight value. This is the weight of the object. Weight on Darkwind also represents bulk and awkwardness of carrying. If you want to have the game set a standard weight, you can set_weight(query_equipment_weight()); You need to use that after you have set_new_type() and set_material(). set_warmth(warmth); Replace warmth with an integer warmth value. This is how warm the piece is when worn. Warmth is used in rooms that use the inherit ARCTIC instead of room. Only set this to override the default warmth. set_value(-1); Armour values are automatically determined by the characteristics of the armour. Do not set a value for basic armours. (The -1 means to use the automatically generated value). NB this should be the LAST function called in your reset routine. That's it! An example manually configured armour is given in /open/EXAMPLES/ARMOURS/basic_armour.c. Stock template examples are under /objects/standard_equipment/armour/. If all you want is to make a basic armour, copy that file to directory where your area's armours are, and replace all the content values (e.g. the quoted text used for set_long(), set_short() etc.) with your own stuff. *************************************************************************** Extra Settings *************************************************************************** The following extra settings can be used in your armour as well, but are not required: set_read("text.
"); Replace "text.
" with the quoted string to be seen when the armour is read. It there is writing on a helmet or ring, for example, you may wish to use this. Remember to add both a period and a newline (
) at the end of your description since LPC won't do that for you. set_info("info.
"); Replace "info.
" with the quoted string to be seen when a mage or such identifies the armour. It should NEVER give specific numbers but it should give enough information for a person to get a fair idea of a armours strengths or powers. set_no_buy(); Put this in if this armour cannot be bought from the shop. (After someone has sold it as loot.) set_no_sell(sell_setting); Replace sell_setting with an integer. If sell_setting is 1, the item will be marked as unsellable. If it is 0, it will clear a previously set sell_setting of 1. If you use a sell_setting greater than 1, then it will take that many calls of set_sell(0); to make it sellable again. set_steal(1 or 0); If set_steal(1); is used, the armour is not stealable. If you set_steal(0); the armour will be stealable by thieves. Yes, it seems backwards and very stupid, which it is, but it is correct. set_cursed(curse_chance); Replace curse_chance by an integer percentage indicating the likelihood of any clone of this armour being cursed. If this line is not used, objects will default to a 1% chance of being cursed. set_no_curse(); Put this line in if you want the armour to never be cursed. This should be used very sparingly. It will prevent the 1% chance that any given armour or armour in the game will be cursed. It should be stressed that this should only be set on items that under no circumstances should be cursed. I.e. quest items etc. set_value(-1, ##); Replace ## by an integer value to INCREASE the value of this armour above the default value. Use this instead of the normal call to set_value(-1); if you want your armour to be extra valuable. set_dodge_bonus(bonus) Replace bonus with an integer value. The armour's dodge bonus increases the wielder's dodging stat (average of dex, wis) while using this armour. A negative value will reduce the wielder's dodging stat. This is a very powerful ability and should be used sparingly. (A 6 point increase is roughly equivalent to a level's increase in stats) armours with a dodge_bonus are considered exceptional or unique; see wizhelp 4.14 'uniques' for details. set_arm_light(light); Replace light with an integer value. This setting allows you to make armour that gives off light. The parameter passed is how powerful the light is. 0 = none, 1 is normal day/sun light, and higher would mean very bright light. Setting this to a negative number would make the armour absorb that much light. set_guild_allow(GUILD|GUILD|...); Replace GUILD|GUILD|... with an ORed set of guild defines (from guildd.h) which indicate which guilds are allowed to use this armour, armour restrictions notwithstanding. In order to use this setting, you must include guildd.h at the beginning of your file. set_guild_restrict(GUILD|GUILD|...); This function is the same as set_guild_allow() except it will disallow the use of that particular armour by the guilds you have listed. set_weakness(TYPE|TYPE|..., amount); Replace TYPE|TYPE|... with an ORed set of damage defines (from types.h) which indicate what damage types the wearer of this armour becomes extra weak to. Replace amount with the percentage increase in vulnerability to the given types. set_resistance(TYPE|TYPE|..., amount); Replace TYPE|TYPE|... with an ORed set of damage defines (from types.h) which indicate what damage types the wearer of this armour becomes more resistant to. Replace amount with the percentage increase resistance to the given types. *************************************************************************** Wear/Remove Functions *************************************************************************** Wear/remove functions cause things to happen when the armour is worn or removed. This is useful for example, if you want to give some spam when the item is worn, or give some stat boosts to the player etc. set_wear_func(oFuncObject); Pass the object that defines wear_func() and remove_func() (explained below) as oFuncObject. In most cases, oFuncObject this_object(). Whenever the armour is worn oFuncObject-> wield_func(this_object()) will be called, and whenever removed, oFuncObject->remove_func(this_object()) will be called. int wear_func(oArmour); This function is defined in the oFuncObject passed to set_wear_func(). Usually both functions are in the armour anyway. This function gets called if the set_wear_func() was set, and a player/monster tries to wear this armour. It is the builder's job to fill out the this function with whatever special things that are to happen. If this function returns 0, then the wear will fail. Thus you can use this to block a armour being worn by certain people. int remove_func(oArmour); This function is defined in the oFuncObject passed to set_wear_func(). Usually both functions are in the armour anyway. This function gets called if the set_wear_func() was set, and a player/monster tries to remove this armour. It is the builder's job to fill out the this function with whatever special things that are to happen. If this function returns 0, then the remove will fail. Armour with a scripted wear effect must declare that effect for gearcheck with add_power_feature("scripted_wear", ...). See wizhelp 4.26 for the equipment power API and examples. void add_equipment_stat(string sStat, int iValue, string sStart, string sSto p); This function will handle adding the stat sStat to the player when they wear the item, and remove the stat when the player removes the item. It eliminates the need of creating start_wearing/stop_wearing functions in the item. sStat can be "con","dex","int","wis","str","chr","hp","sp", "tmp_to_hit_stat","tmp_to_dam_stat","tmp_to_dodge_stat", "tmp_to_absorb_stat","tmp_to_crit_stat","tmp_to_swings", "tmp_to_hit","tmp_to_dam","tmp_to_dodge","tmp_to_absorb", "tmp_to_crit","tmp_to_type" tmp_to_* should only be used with permission. sStart is the message when the player wears the armor. sStop is the message when the player stops wearing the armor. The message is in the same format as room_message. The messages should only be used once per item, not stat. Example:add_equipment_stat("con",5,"$N $vseem hardier.", "$N $vseem less robust."); ------ Version 1: ? Version 2: Bob - Jan 25, 2004

"); Replace "text.

"); Replace "info.

If you set_steal(0); the weapon will be stealable by thieves. Yes, it seems backwards and very stupid, which it is, but it is correct. set_cursed(curse_chance); Replace curse_chance by an integer percentage indicating the likelihood of any clone of this weapon being cursed. If this line is not used, objects will default to a 1% chance of being cursed. set_no_curse(); Put this line in if you want the weapon to never be cursed. This should be used very sparingly. It will prevent the 1% chance that any given weapon or armour in the game will be cursed. It should be stressed that this should only be set on items that under no circumstances should be cursed. I.e. quest items, a holy defender unique sword etc. set_value(-1, ##); Replace ## by an integer value to INCREASE the value of this weapon above the default value. Use this instead of the normal call to set_value(-1); if you want your weapon to be extra valuable. set_damage_type(TYPE1|TYPE2|etc..); Replace TYPE1|TYPE2|etc. with an ORed set of damage types. That is, something that looks like: DAM_GOOD|DAM_FIRE Valid damage types are listed in the damage type documentation, wizhelp 4.17 'damage types'. Do not use this to set the standard weapon damage types set by set_new_type(). set_hit_bonus(bonus) Replace bonus with a integer value. The weapon's hit bonus increases the wielder's hitting stat (average of dex, int) while using this weapon. A negative value will reduce the wielder's hitting stat. This is a very powerful ability and should be used sparingly. (A 6 point increase is roughly equivalent to a level's increase in stats) Weapons with a hit_bonus are considered exceptional or unique; see wizhelp 4.14 'uniques' for details. set_guild_allow(GUILD|GUILD|...); Replace GUILD|GUILD|... with an ORed set of guild defines (from guildd.h) which indicate which guilds are allowed to use this weapon, weapon restrictions notwithstanding. In order to use this setting, you must include guildd.h at the beginning of your file. set_guild_restrict(GUILD|GUILD|...); This function is the same as set_guild_allow() except it will disallow the use of that particular weapon by the guilds you have listed. *************************************************************************** Hit/Wield Functions *************************************************************************** Hitting and wielding functions cause things to happen when the weapon hits in combat, or is wielded. This is useful for example, if you want to give some spam in combat, or extra bonuses, or if you want to give the player a stat boost when wielding it. set_hit_func(oFuncObject); Pass the object that defines weapon_hit() (explained below) as oFuncObject. It is the builder's job to fill out this function with whatever special things that are to happen. The returned value is a bonus applied to the wielder's damage stat, for that hit. Use of this function almost always make this weapon a unique-class weapon, so be warned and ask questions before using it. See wizhelp 4.14 'uniques' for guidelines on special hits.) It is the builder's job to fill out the this function with whatever special things that are to happen. If this function returns 0, then the unwield will fail. A weapon with a scripted wield effect must declare that effect for gearcheck with add_power_feature("scripted_wield", ...). See wizhelp 4.26. void add_equipment_stat(string sStat, int iValue, string sStart, string sStop); This function will handle adding the stat sStat to the player when they wield the item, and remove the stat when the player unwields the item. It eliminates the need of creating start_wearing/stop_wearing functions in the item. sStat can be "con","dex","int","wis","str","chr","hp","sp", "tmp_to_hit_stat","tmp_to_dam_stat","tmp_to_dodge_stat", "tmp_to_absorb_stat","tmp_to_crit_stat","tmp_to_swings", "tmp_to_hit","tmp_to_dam","tmp_to_dodge","tmp_to_absorb", "tmp_to_crit","tmp_to_type" tmp_to_* should only be used with permission. sStart is the message when the player wears the armor. sStop is the message when the player stops wearing the armor. The message is in the same format as room_message. The messages should only be used once per item, not stat. Example:add_equipment_stat("con",5,"$N $vseem hardier.", "$N $vseem less robust."); ------ Version 1: ? Version 2: Bob - July 02, 2003

docs.title: // ob doc
docs.text: // ob doc // 970114, Antcrusher This documentation concerns the generic base inheritable ob.c. Every other "object" file inherits it in some fashion. It sets up the basic functions that are common to all of them. Generally you should not inherit this yourself, but inherit the object that is more specific to your application, such as treasure, weapon, etc. void set_id(string sArg); void set_name(string sArg); Both set IDs of the object to sArg, and the cap name to the cap of str. void set_alias(string sArg); void set_alt_name(string sArg); Both of these also set IDs of the object. If you want more than three valid IDs for an object, you will need to write your own id() function, defined below. string query_name(); This returns the string set by set_name and set_id. It is the "primary" name of the object. int id(string sArg); This returns 0 if sArg does not match one of the valid IDs of the object. void set_short(string sArg); Sets the short description to sArg. string short(); string query_short(); Both return the short_desc string. void set_long(string sArg); Sets the long description to sArg. Include your own newline character. string long(); string query_long(); Both return the long description if it was set, else "You see nothing special." varargs void set_value(int iV); Sets the value to iV. Some other inheritables, such as treasure, redefine this with more than one argument, hence varargs. int query_value(); Returns the base value of the object. Buying and selling prices are modified by the shop based on various factors. void set_weight(int iW); Sets the weight of the object to iW. int query_weight(); Returns the weight of the object. void set_info(string iI); Sets an informational string. string query_info(); Returns the information string. void set_read(string sArg); Sets a readable string on the object. The description should make a note that something can be read. int read(string sArg); If sArg corresponds to the item, this writes the string and returns 1. Else it returns 0. void set_new_type(int iT); To set the object as an object type defined in types.h. This is a bitfield. Multiple types can be bitwise-or'd together in the set. int query_new_type(); Returns the number set above. Used as a bitfield. string *query_type_strings(int iNew_type); Returns an array of strings corresponding to which bits are supplied by the argument iNew_type. void set_material(int iM); To set the object as being of a material defined in material.h. This is a bitfield. Multiple materials can be bitwise-or'd together in the set. Ex. set_material(MAT_WOOD|MAT_GOLD); int query_material(); Returns the number set above. Used as a bitfield. string *query_material_strings(int iMaterial_type); Returns an array of strings corresponding to which bits are supplied by the argument material_type. string *query_treasure_strings(int iTreasure_type); Returns an array of strings corresponding to which bits are supplied by the argument iTreasure_type. void set_no_buy(int iI); Set to 1 if it's not buyable. int query_no_buy(); Returns buyable status. void set_no_sell(int iI); Pass a 1 as the parameter to have it be refused in stores. Note that this works a bit differently from no_buy, in that the more times you call set_no_sell(1), the more times you then have to call set_no_sell(0) to get it to a sellable state again. This is done so that the creator can set it no_sell, and if a guild uses no_sell to prohibit players from selling checked-out/borrowed items, when the guild calls set_no_sell(0) when the object is done being borrowed, the item will still not be sellable. int query_no_sell(); Returns sellable status. void set_no_clean_up(int iI); Set this to avoid having this object, or any rooms/containers containing this object, cleaned up. int query_no_clean_up(); Returns the clean up setting. void set_steal(int iI); Set to 1 if it's not stealable. int query_steal(); Returns nonstealability status. (Yes, these should have been called no_steal, but they weren't.) void set_cursed(int iI); Set i from 0-100 as the percent chance the item will be cursed, and be stuck with the player. status query_cursed(); Returns 1 if the item is cursed, else 0. void set_unique(); Marks an item as unique. int query_unique(); Returns 1 if the item is unique, else 0. void set_keep(int iArg); int query_keep(); Returns the value set by the above. varargs void set_object_destruct_timer(int iTime, mixed xFunc); This function will destruct the object in iTime seconds. If xFunc is defined and is a closure, it will apply the function before destructing it. If it's a string, it will tell_room or tell_object of the environment of the object before destructing it.

docs.title: COLOR
docs.text:
COLOR ======= This documentation is meant to teach an easy way to add ansi to your current code on Darkwind. There are a few methods. Adding color to items: You can add color to items very easily. Simple use: set_color(|(colorcode); Example: set_color(|BK0); This would return the set_short in the item as blue Adding color to a write/say: If you are trying to write the color of a certain object (that should already have a color), then you can do something like this: write(this_object()->query_color() + this_object()->short() + "
"); However, if you want to specify a color, you should do this: write("|BK0" + this_object()->short() + "
"); When you use the second method, you must always use the format |XYZ. The color change must also be at the beginning of the string. You may have only 1 color change per write/say/whatever. If you wish to have part of a line a different color than the rest of the line, break up the string into two writes/says without a 
 in the first one (see second Butthead example below). Color changes don't work well with sprintf. Use write("|XYZ" + sprintf(whatever)) instead. Don't attempt to colorize monsters. X == Foreground color. Y == Background color. Valid Colors: Red = R, Green = G, Blue = B, Black = K, Yellow = Y, Cyan = C, White = W, Magenta = M. Z == Effect. (Bold = B, Underscore = U, None = 0) You can see the full list of colors via 'colorlist' Examples: write("|CYBButthead.
"); write("|GBU" + " " + this_object->short() + "
"); write("|CKBButt"); write("|GKBhead.
"); The spaces after the color, before the short, will not be affected by the color.

docs.title: This is the Documentation for creating a door using the newdoor file
docs.text:
This is the Documentation for creating a door using the newdoor file NOTE: Major revisions were made to this code on or about 5/23/97. It should be backwards compatible with the exception that some of the messages were changed and block checks were added. The extra three arguments (mix1, mix2, and str7) are all optional but remember that you'll need place holders for any of them which precede ones you do want to use. So you want to put a door in your castle, eh? Well, this is how you do it. Create a room or edit one already created. Change the inheritance to: inherit DOORROOM; Somewhere in the reset(), (if you want it to reset every time, put it before your if (arg) return; line(s)), you must add the following function: MAKE_DOOR(str1, str2, str3, str4, str5, int1, int2, int3, str6, int4, mix1, mix2, str7); I wrote it like this so you understand what types of values to use: string for str#, integer for int#, mixed for mix#. ******************** str1: This is the door_type to which the door will respond. Usually, a door is a door. In this case, however, a door can be a window, a rockpile, a trapdoor, a casket, a closet, etc. The door_type must be a ONE WORD string. Else, your door may not work. Lets assume you want a "door". The line should look like this now: MAKE_DOOR("door", ******************** str2: This is the direction that the door exits this room in. Let's choose northeast. MAKE_DOOR("door","northeast", ******************** str3: Now this string is required to make sure the door actually goes somewhere. You may have guessed it already. Yes, this is the pathname for the room on the other side of the door. If you have a room in mind, then thats what you should insert here. If you hadn't thought that far ahead, dont worry, just make up a file name for the next room and make a whole new room. You'll have to do the same to that door as you do here, so be forewarned. I call this value the partner_door string. MAKE_DOOR("door","northeast","players/you/room2", ******************** str4: Next comes the door itself. What does it look like? What should players see if they look at it? By the way, you should have mentioned that there is a door here in the room's description (unless you want it to be a secret, of course)! How about a big blue door with a bronze bolt? I always did like aliteration! Oh, if you pass 0 for this argument, you'll get a default description. The default isn't exciting but rather just a basic description. MAKE_DOOR("door","northeast","players/you/room2", "\ This door is big, blue, and on the left, there is a bronze bolt,
\ with a padlock!", *NOTE*: No, you do NOT have to put a carriage return (
) at the end of your door description. You are certainly welcome to, if you so chose. ******************** str5: We said the door had a padlock? then which key will work in it? Here's where you can set that. I call this the key_code string. It can be pretty much any strange code you like, so have fun! I do suggest you stick to one word, and no funny characters. Please remember to use this same code when you make a key! If you dont want to have a door that can be locked, then just set this string to " ". (actually, it still doesn't matter what the code is. More on that later). Code, code,... what should be the code? I know!... MAKE_DOOR("door","northeast","players/you/room2", "\ This door is big, blue and on the left, there is a bronze bolt,
\ with a padlock!", "test1", ******************** int1: Now were're into the integers needed. Those of you familiar with the old door-object might recognize these. The first is the trigger for opening and closing the door. I call it is_closed. If is_closed = 1, then this statement is true, and the door is actually closed. If is_closed = 0, then its a false statement, meaning that the door is open. Make sense? I like starting with a nice, inviting, open door: MAKE_DOOR("door","northeast","players/you/room2", "\ This door is big, blue and on the left, there is a bronze bolt,
\ with a padlock!", "test1", 0, You can use the defined values OPEN and CLOSED here, as well. ******************** int2: Related to the is_closed integer is the is_locked integer. Means about the same thing, except this one controls whether the door is locked or not. Use 1 for true, 0 for false. Oh, btw, These values (int1 and int2) will be true for the door every time there is a reset or shutdown. Thats why this whole thing has to go into the reset function in your room. Why lock the door if its open? (actually i set things so that you can't lock an open door. Please don't be contrary and set it anyway. Unforseen errors will probably occur, erasing all your files and crashing the mud! (Well, they could!) MAKE_DOOR("door","northeast","players/you/room2", "\ This door is big, blue and on the left, there is a bronze bolt,
\ with a padlock!", "test1", 1, 0 You can also use the defined values UNLOCKED and LOCKED here. ******************** int3: What's left? Why, the bit i was talking about earlier, the ability to lock the door! I called it the can_lock integer. Again, 1 is true, the door can be locked and unlocked. 0 means false, not able to lock the door. By setting this variable to 0, the key_code and is_lock items become unnecessary (except it'll mess up if you skip them). I like having a lock... keeps out the unsavory types. :) MAKE_DOOR("door","northeast","players/you/room2", "\ This door is big, blue and on the left, there is a bronze bolt,
\ with a padlock!", "test1", 1, 0, 1, You can also use the defined values NONLOCKABLE and LOCKABLE here. ******************** str6: You will need to also pass the direction of the door from the _other_ room. So in this example, the door in this room went northeast, so the door in the other room will go southwest. Simple eh? Here is what your MAKE_DOOR command will look like: MAKE_DOOR("door","northeast","players/you/room2", "\ This door is big, blue and on the left, there is a bronze bolt,
\ with a padlock!", "test", 1, 0, 1, "southwest", ******************** int4: You should set the percentage on a 1 to 100 scale of how hard it should be to pick this door. If you do not want to worry about that set it to 0 and a default value will be set (currently 40%). MAKE_DOOR("door","northeast","players/you/room2", "\ This door is big, blue and on the left, there is a bronze bolt,
\ with a padlock!", "test", 1, 0, 1, "southwest", 65, ******************** mix1: You can specify either a string or an array of strings which will act as alternate ids for this door. For example, you could refer to the door as the 'northeast door' or as 'glowing portal' or whatever you desire. Whatever you specify will be used to create the add_look() for the door and can be used by a player wishing to open, close, etc. the door. Let's create a couple of alternate names. MAKE_DOOR("door","northeast","players/you/room2", "\ This door is big, blue and on the left, there is a bronze bolt,
\ with a padlock!", "test", 1, 0, 1, "southwest", 65, ({"glowing portal", "shining door"}), ******************** mix2: You can also specify a string or an array of strings from which one will be given when ever someone listens to the door! I'll give a few mysterious noises to be heard by nosy players. Note that you can define your own query_door_sound() function as long as it accepts a string (what you specified for str2) and returns a string representing the sound that is heard. MAKE_DOOR("door","northeast","players/you/room2", "\ This door is big, blue and on the left, there is a bronze bolt,
\ with a padlock!", "test", 1, 0, 1, "southwest", 65, ({"glowing portal", "shining door"}), ({"moaning", "wailing" "screams"}), ******************** str7: Lastly, if you want to be able to do some special processing of your own depending on what is done to the door, you can provide a function name to be called whenever your door is actually touched. The function will be passed whatever you specified as str2 as well as an integer corresponding to what happened to the door as a result of the action: -1 : Nothing done, door not touched. 0 : Nothing done, door was touched. 1 : Door changed state. You can used query_verb() to find out which function was actually called. So, if you wanted to give someone a nasty electric shock when they opened a door, you could specify a function which checks for a positive return from the open() function on your door and let the player have it. MAKE_DOOR("door","northeast","players/you/room2", "\ This door is big, blue and on the left, there is a bronze bolt,
\ with a padlock!", "test", 1, 0, 1, "southwest", 65, ({"glowing portal", "shining door"}), ({"moaning", "wailing" "screams"}), "zap_player"); ******************** That's it for this room. Now go edit the other room: "players/you/room2" and repeat this whole operation. Hey, don't forget to change the partner_door and direction so that the player goes back to the correct room! (you can have wierd jumps where you enter the door by going east, and have to go north to get back or something. Do as Ye Will!). Also, don't forget to change the inherit line to DOORROOM! General Functions: (Not needed if you only want to *create* a door.) status query_door_closed(string direction); Returns a 1 if the door is closed, 0 otherwise. status query_door_locked(string direction); Returns a 1 if the door is locked, 0 otherwise. int query_pick_chance(string direction); Returns the percentage required to pick the lock. void force_unlock(string direction); Call this to force the door to unlock. string query_code(string direction); Returns the key id which will unlock this door. Good Luck!

docs.title: -= Gems =-
docs.text: -= Gems =- Want fast and simple treasure for your mobs? Something that doesn't LOOK like it's the same stuff, over and over again? Have we got the answer for you! The basic gem object would look like this: #include <mudlib.h> inherit STD_GEM; void reset(int iArg) { if(!is_clone(this_object())) return; ::reset(iArg); if (iArg) return; set_gem_type("something"); } Woo! TEN LINES! That's it! If you put that literal code in, you would get one of over fifty random gems (more than 200 counting all the color variations, etc.) every time you cloned it. Let's get into some specifics, now. Listed below are the 6 gem catagories (and average selling prices) and the gem varieties in each. Jewel (1125) ----- diamond emerald ruby star ruby Gemstone (900) -------- fire opal jacinth opal sapphire star sapphire Precious (600) -------- amethyst aquamarine garnet pearl peridont spinel topaz Fancy (300) ----- alexandrite amber beryl cat's eye chrysoberyl coral hawk's eye jade jet tourmaline Semiprecious (120) ------------ bloodstone carnelian carnelian onyx chalcedony chrysoprase citrine hyacinth jasper moonstone onyx sardonyx star rose quartz sunstone zircon Ornamental (40) ---------- azurite banded agate hematite lapis lazuli malachite moss agate obsidian quartz crystal rhodochrosite serpentine tiger eye agate turquoise Each of these also have associated random values: colors, markings, and the like, and will be randomly assigned. So, instead of "something" in the above example, you can put a SPECIFIC stone (IE, "lapis lazuli"), and get a fine specimen of that stone. Or, you can put the catagory (IE, "jewel") and get a random stone from that catagory. Functions for this object: set_gem_type("string"); As listed above, you can put an actual gem name (refer to the lists), or a gem catagory. Anything else will generate a random gem from the entire pool. THIS FUNCTION MUST BE SET FIRST!!!! (otherwise, it will overwrite anything you try to set.) Valid gem types are: "jewel", "gemstone", "precious", "fancy", "semiprecious", "ornamental" or, an individual gem name. Anything else will give you a random gem, rather than returning an error. Nice, huh? This function doesn't recognize multiple arguments. If you want (for example) either a jewel OR a gemstone, use a switch in your code. :) add_value(amt); This will allow you to set an added amount (positive or negative integer value) to the generated value. set_flawless(int); This an integer value; a positive value will guarantee an above average gem, a negative value will guarantee a below average gem, and 0 will restrict the gem to a value in the average range. These are all you need, but if you need to personalize a particular gem, the standard functions as follows are all still available. Defaults are shown below. set_short("Description here"); If you don't set this, it will show as: A <color> <name of gem>. set_long("Set the long description here.\n"); If you don't set this, it will show as: A <description> <gem name> <still more description!>. Basically, you'll have a real description, rather than "you see nothing unusual." set_name("name"); This is set to the name of the gem. set_alt_name("name"); This is set to a single word for the gem, in most cases the name of the gem is used here. In others, such as 'tiger eye agate', part of the name is used, ie: 'agate'. set_alias("name"); This is set to "gem" in all cases. set_weight(int); This is set to 1. set_treasure_type(TYP_GEM); You PROBABLY don't need to change this. If you do want to add another type, be sure to include (TYP_GEM|whatever). set_material(MAT_GEM); Ditto, you PROBABLY don't need to change this. set_value(int); DON'T use this function, except in rare cases; use add_value() or set_flawless() to adjust the value. This is calculated automatically based on the catagory of gem, with a randomly generated modifier for quality (heavily weighted towards the middle, but allowing for WIDE variations). set_info("string.\n") Based on the previously-mentioned quality modifier, this will be set to one of the following strings (from worst to best): This gem is horribly flawed! This gem is somewhat flawed. This gem has no apparent flaws. This gem is flawless. This gem is absolutely flawless! If you have any problems, questions or suggestions refer them to Hern or Tyarra. Last updated: 1/21/96 Updated: 6/8/96 Updated: 27/08/98
