docs.text:
Rev. 1 Tithe/Tax System Description =================================== Introduction: ------------ The tithe/tax (known as the tithe system from now on) is to be used by any guild making compulsary donations to a central coffer or pool for later use. This can easily be adopted for use by a city for a taxation system, by simply adding to the central coffer when a purchase is made. Concepts -------- All functions are held within the TITHE_D system and any command written to utilize the system should also include the <tithe.h> header. Each coffer or pool has an identifier set up by the #define TITHE_ID. This define will be the key for which all transactions are referenced and needs to be defined in a seperate header for that guild/city or within the command itself. Once money is donated into a coffer, requests can be made to withdraw money from the coffer. That request has to be approved by an IMP+ before the permitted offical can then withdraw from the coffers. Basic Functionality ------------------- Adding money: void add_tithe(string TITHE_ID, int AMOUNT) - This puts money into the coffers - Also logs an entry into /log/tithes/TITHE_ID.o Viewing balances: int query_tithe(string TITHE_ID) - Returns the int of the total in TITHE_ID's coffer Withdraw requests: int withdraw_tithe_request(string TITHE_ID, int AMOUNT, string REASON) - Adds a request for withdraw, added to the main array for TITHE_ID int query_withdraw_request(string TITHE_ID) - Will return a formated listing of current tithe withdraws on the books. Approval/Denial/Removal: int approve_withdraw_request(string TITHE_ID, int REQUEST_NUM, (string APPROVAL) - This function allows an IMP+ to approve/deny/remove the request. APPROVAL must equal either "approve", "deny" or "delete". It is up to the coder to decide how to present these options to the user. A log entry is made to /log/tithes/TITHE_ID.approve.o for this transaction. Withdraw: int withdraw_tithe(string TITHE_ID, int REQUEST_NUM) - Providing the request has been approved by an IMP+ the appropriate offical can then finally withdraw the amount from the coffer to his/her pocket. A log entry is made to /log/tithes/TITHE_ID.withdraw.o on the transaction. EXAMPLES ------- These examples will show some basic uses of the above functions. The first example will show how to put money into the account, and the next will show a command to request a withdraw then we show how to list the open withdraw requests and lastly code to show approval. Adding tithes ------------- #include <mudlib.h> #include <tithe.h> #define TITHE_ID "myguild" int do_command(int iAmount) { TITHE_D->add_tithe(TITHE_ID,iAmount); write("Thanks for your donation.
"); return 1; } // End Add Request withdraw ---------------- #include <mudlib.h> #include <tithe.h> #define TITHE_ID "myguild" int do_command(string sRequest){ int iTithes; string sReason; int iAmount, iRequest; if(!sRequest) { notify_fail("Please put the amount then the\ reason in your request.
") return 0; } if(sscanf(sRequest,"%d %s",iAmount, sReason) == 2) { TITHE_D->withdraw_tithe_request(TITHE_ID,iAmount,sReason); return 1; } notify_fail("Please put the amount then the\ reason in your request.
") return 0; } // End Request withdraw Tithe/Tax listing ----------------- #include <mudlib.h> #include <tithe.h> #define TITHE_ID "myguild" int do_command() { int iTithes; write("Pending withdraw requests for "+capitalize(TITHE_ID)+":
"); TITHE_D->query_withdraw_request(TITHE_ID); return 1; } // End Tithe/Tax listing Request approval ---------------- #include <mudlib.h> #include <tithe.h> #define TITHE_ID "myguild" int do_command(string sArg) { string sCommand; int iInt; if(sscanf(sArg,"%d",iInt) != 1) { notify_fail("Try tapp <request number>
"); return 0; } if(!iInt) { notify_fail("Try tapp <request number>
"); return 0; } TITHE_D->approve_withdraw_request(TITHE_ID, iInt, "approve"); return 1; } // End Request approval ----- /secure/daemons/tithe_d.c - The tithe/tax daemon itself, defined as TITHE_D /secure/include/tithe.h - Header file containing various defines. Revision History: ----------------- Rev. 1 - Zureal: First release.

docs.text: Rev. 1 Regression/Unit Testing Framework ===================================== QUICKSTART ---------- If you want to write a test for some new functionality, say in blancmange.c, create a new file, blancmange_test.c. It should inherit TEST_CASE. Now, for each function you wish to test in blancmange.c, create a corresponding void testFunc() function in blancmange_test.c. This test should exercise the functionality of Func() in blancmange.c. Use the assert functions in the TEST_CASE inheritable to test things easily, or you can just use raise_error. The assert functions, however, do lots of nice formatting of the results. Example: #include <mudlib.h> inherit TEST_CASE; object moMyTestObject; void setup() { moMyTestObject = clone_object("/players/malraux/blancmange"); } void teardown() { destruct(moMyTestObject); } void testFoo() { moMyTestObject->foo(); assertTrue("testing query_foo", moMyTestObject->query_foo()); } void testBlah() { moMyTestObject->blah("garble"); assertEquals("testing query_blah", "garble", moMyTestObject->query_blah()); } If you have some state that needs to be set up before each test function is called, like creating an object, or putting a value into a daemon, then put those calls into the void setup() function in blancmange_test.c. Make sure that any objects you create (either in setup() or in a testFunc()) are explicitly destructed in the void teardown() function, which will get run after each test function is called. When you are ready to run your tests, do 'rtest blancmange_test'. The basic call sequence of rtest is: 1) load the blancmange_test object. 2) for each testFoo() function in blancmange_test, do the following: 2a) call setup() 2b) call testFoo() 2c) call teardown() 3) repeat for each testFoo() function. Introduction: ------------ Testing frameworks increase the stability and quality of code by ensuring two things: Unit testing ensures that code performs as intended. Regression testing ensures that code *still* performs as intended after changes are made that could impact the tested code. In order to make testing easy, Kent Beck designed an object oriented testing framework that automated the process of creating and running unit and regression tests. This framework has since been ported to dozens of languages, including (now, that is) LPC. Testing enables us not only to make changes without breaking other pieces of code (provided the tests are run after the changes), but also to develop more quickly. This may seem counter-intuitive at first, but consider that you always (or should always) test what you have coded to make sure it does wha tyou think it does. This usually involves the creation of adhoc test scripts or programs. Now, by using a pre-built testing framework, you can formalize your adhoc testing so that it can easily be rerun later. Concepts -------- #include <mudlib.h> to get the inheritable #defines referenced. A "test case" is an object that contains a series of test functions, each of which tests a limited piece of the code being tested. A "test suite" is a group of test cases. A "test runner" is an object that knows how to run a suite of tests. TEST_RUNNER is our implementation of a test runner, and it is invoked by the "rtest" command. To run a test case file, do 'rtest </path/to/filetest>'. Test cases should inherit TEST_CASE, which includes both the underlying test functionality, as well as a series of assert functions that allow you to make determinations about the results of your tests. A test case can either contain its own test functions, or it can merely be a convenience container for a suite of other test case objects. When a test case is run, each function in the object beginning with the word "test" will be run in order. If any errors are raised, or any of the calls to assert* functions fail, the test function will be considered a failure. Naming consistency: for unit tests that test a paricular .c file, PLEASE name your tests the same name as the object they are testing with '_test' appended. This will allow us to write extra functionality in the update command to automatically run unit tests if they exist. Example: /inherits/events_test.c Basic Functionality ------------------- The test case inheritable defines a reset(int arg) function that must be called with ::reset(arg) if you override it. The reset function sets up a number of internal variables. void setup() -- This function will be called before each test function in the object. Use this to set up data/state in the test that needs to be consistent for each test function. void teardown() -- This function will be called after each test function in the object. Use this to destruct any objects that may have been created during the course of the tests. string *getTests() -- The function should return an array of function names to call to run the tests in this object. It defaults to the list of all non-inherited functions that begin with the word "test". void setTests(string *tests) -- Used to override the default test behavior, in order to use a certain test function order, use functions that do not begin with "test", or use a subset of test functions. object *suite() -- Returns an array of test case objects to call. This defaults to the current object, but this may be overridden to return other cloned test objects in order to collect a number of separate test cases objects into a single convenient test case. mixed run(string test) -- Called by the test runner. Runs a particular test function in the object, and returns either 0 for success, or an error message for failure. void assertTrue(string msg, mixed bool) -- Asserts that the value 'bool' is true. If not, an error is raised, causing the test to fail. The error will contain the text in 'msg'. void assertFalse(string msg, mixed bool) -- Asserts that the value 'bool' is false. If not, an error is raised, causing the test to fail. The error will contain the text in 'msg'. void assertNull(string msg, mixed thing) -- Asserts that the value 'thing' is null. If not, an error is raised, causing the test to fail. The error will contain the text in 'msg'. In LPC, this is the same as assertFalse. void assertEquals(string msg, mixed expecting, mixed actual) -- Asserts that the value 'actual' is the same as 'expecting'. If not, an error is raised, causing the test to fail. The error will contain the text in 'msg'. void assertNonEmpty(string msg, mixed thing) -- Asserts that the value 'thing' is nonempty. For mappings, this means that the mapping is not ([ ]). For arrays, this means that the array is not ({ }). For strings, this means that the string is not "". For any other value (object, numeric) this means that the value is not 0. If not, an error is raised, causing the test to fail. The error will contain the text in 'msg'. void assertNonEmpty(string msg, mixed thing) -- This asserts the opposite of assertNonEmpty; ie. mappings and arrays must have at least one element, strings must be of length >= 1, and objects/numbers must not be 0. void fail(string msg) -- Causes an instant test failure, sending 'msg' in the error message. Examples ------- Please see /inherits/events_test.c You can run the example with "rtest /inherits/events_test". As an example of the use of suite(): object *suite() { object subtest; // This sets up a copy of npcbehavetest that only // runs two test functions subtest = clone_object("/inherits/npcbehavetest"); subtest->setTests( ({ "test1", "test2" }) ); return ({ clone_object("/secure/livingtest"), clone_object("/secure/monstertest"), clone_object("/secure/playertest"), clone_object("/inherits/npctest"), subtest }); } If you were to run 'rtest' on this test object, it would run the livingtest, monstertest, playertest, and subset of npctest. Note that these tests do not exist as of this writing. :-) Files ------- TEST_CASE: /inherits/testcase.c TEST_RUNNER: /objects/testrunner.c Test command: /cmds/builder/_rtest.c Revision History: ----------------- Rev. 1 - 2002-01-27 Malraux: First release.

docs.title: Portal� for Windows MIP v8.0
docs.text: Portal� for Windows MIP v8.0 (Messaging Interface Protocol) ================================================================= Use of this document in any way deems acceptance of the Terms of Use License. This policy can be located at the bottom of this document. If you do not agree to the conditions outlined in the Terms of Use License, you may not use this document, nor the intellectual property contained therein. The term MIP (Messaging Interface Protocol) is used to describe the means of communicating with Portal� through the sending of text strings. Unless otherwise noted, all codes used require the client use of Portal VI - upgrade pack A or higher. That said, let�s get right into the coding specifics. The 3klient Command ================================================================= The security code (SEC_CODE) is a 5-digit number that is generated randomly by Portal�. This code is somewhat like a PIN number. It prevents bogus messages (those that don�t match the code currently held locally by the Portal� user) from being recognized by Portal�. The security code must be sent with any data coming to Portal�. It must be 5 digits in length, so a smaller number would be prefixed with 0s, such as 00051. The security code will be sent to your mud from Portal� through a command, namely �3klient #~<version>� (~ separates the code from the version info) such as �3klient 10401~Portal3.500�, so you need to accept the number and store it as a static variable on the player. The text following the tilde is simply version info. You can either parse it as you desire (for a client-who list for example) or simply ignore it. You create the 3klient command with an add_action() function or however you normally create commands for characters on your MUD. This provides the basis for the Portal� "jumpstart" feature, which sends the 3klient command. The "3klient" command is in all lowercase letters. Remember, the SEC_CODE number you send to Portal@ in any code must be 5 characters in length. That means that if the number a player has attached with is 675, the SEC_CODE you would always send that player is 00675. With the jumpstart the player sends though, the numbers are not prefixed. This means that a jumpstart sent by the player in the example just stated would look like �3klient 675~Portal3.500� The reason for the difference is that it makes it easier for MUDs to grab the SEC_CODE (via a sscanf function for example). Notes: 3Klient? What the hell is that? Well, at one point in time, this MUD client was called 3Klient. That name was purged and replaced by the current name � Portal�. Since the trigger command needs to be something universally unique, we decided to leave 3klient as the trigger, both because of its uniqueness, but also as a reminder of its heritage. The Welcome Trigger ================================================================= Now, the player can do the jumpstart manually, or your MUD can trigger it for them. We have created a resident trigger in Portal� that respond to the word "Welcome" appearing on the screen. When Portal� connects to your MUD, near the end of their normal login spam, put the phrase "Welcome" into a greeting line. Something like "Welcome to SuperMUD!" would work. Once Portal� sees the "Welcome" in a line, it will send the jumpstart "3klient" command automatically. It will also de-activate the trigger until the next, fresh login (to prevent the jumpstart being sent each time the word "Welcome" comes across the screen). Once this is done, the 3klient command, which you setup as described above, will attach your user to your mud accordingly. Notes: v1.4 does not have the Welcome trigger. They must manually jumpstart. v2.0 has the trigger, but requires something on either side of the �Welcome� Any character will do such as: �Hello! Welcome to BlahMUD!� v3.0 actually triggers on text defined by the user in the MUD List screen The default event text is �elcome� but again, is configurable by the user. The default will change if that MUD desires it (and contacts us). How does the extra information get sent without the player seeing it? To send information to Portal� there�s only a few special strings and characters that you need to know, we�ll refer to these as literals. The most important literal is what as known as the ACTIVATE literal. This must precede all information sent to Portal�. Its value is #K%. Following the ACTIVATE literal will be the Security Code (SEC_CODE), the Character Count (CHAR_COUNT), the line code Literal and the Data you wish to send. This will be discussed in more detail below. ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+Literal+Data or #K%+Security Code+Character Count+Literal+Data To recap, when sending information to Portal�, send the ACTIVATE literal first (#K%). Note, do not precede or follow the literal with a line feed. The next piece of information you will send when communicating with Portal� is the SEC_CODE. This is the 5-digit code that hooks up the server (MUD) with the client (the Portal� running on the user's machine). The 3klient command is used to synchronize these values as described above. Also, as described above, it must be 5 digits, so a smaller number would be prefixed with 0s, such as 01459 or 00002. The third piece of information you will send is the CHAR_COUNT. This value will be the total number of characters following it that Portal� needs to intercept and use. It must be 3 digits, so a smaller number would be prefixed with 0s, such as 031 or 009. The next thing on the line is the line code literal. This tells Portal� what data is to follow. A list of the valid line code literals is in the Appendix A. All line code literals are 3 characters, such as FFF or AAB. After the line code literal is the data you wish to send. This, of course, is based on which line code literal you choose. If you use the hit point line literal you will be sending hit point and other related information after it. If it is a mud chat, or an image, appropriate information should be sent as well. Individual fields within the data stream must be separated with the CL_DELIM literal. Its value is ~ (a single tilde), and should be used to separate all types of information for line code literals that accept multiple values (such as FFF). Here are some examples of what gets set to Portal�: #K%00005008AAC12:46 #K%00005008AAF00:50 These two examples break down as follows: #K% The ACTIVATE literal 00005 My security code 008 The number of characters to follow AAC This is the line code literal for displaying when the mud will next reboot AAF This is the line code literal for displaying how long the mud has been up 12:46 This is the data. In this example the mud will reboot in 12 hours and 46 minutes. 00:50 Data as well, indicating that the mud has been up for 50 minutes. Most line code literals will send a single data value similar to the two examples above. However, there are some that expect two or more values on the line. For example, the chat line literal expects 4 values. These 4 values are the line command, line name, sender�s name, and line text, delimited by the CL_DELIM (~). So, if a player�s guild were Mages, an example of the data for a chat would be: magechat~Mage Line~Rastafan~[Mages] Rastafan: Hi guys! So the line would be sent as: #K%00005057CAAmagechat~Mage Line~Rastafan~[Mages] Rastafan: Hi guys! Where #K% is the ACTIVATE literal, 00005 is my security code, 057 is the character count to follow, CAA is the chat line code and the data is described above. Portal�, of course, will display that data in the Chat Monitor when it receives it. The largest of the multiple-data literals is what is called the COMPOSITE literal. This is the one that handles the hit point, spell point, guild points, and related information. This is the only line code literal that can accept a variable number of different data points. Basically just fill it up with however many you want. The data points are identified by the HP_DATA_CODE literal that is part of the data stream. All HP_DATA_CODE literals are a single character. A list of the HP_DATA_CODE literals is in Appendix A. An example of building the line code literal of a COMPOSITE is built as follows: � The ACTIVATE literal � The SEC_CODE variable � The CHAR_COUNT of the data � The COMPOSITE literal (FFF) � The HP_DATA_CODE literal for the first data point � The first data point � The CL_DELIM literal � The HP_DATA_CODE literal for the second data point � The second data point � And so on�(if you wanted to add a 3rd composite or further) The final, formatted COMPOSITE comes out looking like this: #K%00005014FFFA322~B472 #K% The ACTIVATE literal 00005 Again, my security code 014 The number of characters to follow FFF The line code literal for COMPOSITE A The CL_SEND_HP literal indicating current hit points B The CL_SEND_MAXHP literal indicating maximum hit points In this case there are only two data points, and thus two CL_SEND_HP literals A and B. You can send any number of different CL_SEND_MAXHP literals in the COMPOSITE. The first data point is 322 and the second is 472. A is the CL_SEND_HP for current hit points and B is the CL_SEND_MAXHP literal for max hit points. So this example tells the client that the player is currently at 322 hit points out of 472. This is explained better in Appendix A. ================================================================= Appendix A: Line Code Literals ================================================================= Note: For all the below examples, we use 00005 as the SEC_CODE #define CL_SEND_SOUND AAA ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. This literal is used to send the filename of a sound that you wish Portal� to play. All sounds are .WAV files and are stored in the media/sounds/ directory beneath the dir where the Portal� executable resides. Range for this literal is restricted by Windows� file naming conventions. As a general rule, you should not use anything but alphanumeric characters (a, b, c, 1, 2, 3) and the underscore (_). The filename is not case-sensitive. The length of the total filename cannot be longer than 255 characters. Note: This function is only enabled if the user has not disabled system sounds. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_SOUND+filename Example: filename = lock Formatted Example: #K%00005007AAAlock #define CL_SEND_IMAGE AAB ================================================================= This is a dual data point literal. This literal is virtually identical to the CL_SEND_SOUND literal except that it is used to send the filename of the image to be displayed in the Portal� Imagery. All images must be either bitmaps or gifs (.BMP and .GIF extensions respectively). You do not need to include the file extension unless you wish to specify. Portal� will look for a bitmap and then a gif, in that order. All images are stored in the media/images/ directory. The imagelabel (which will appear below the image in the Imagery) is optional, but the CL_DELIM is not. If you don't want a label, simply end the string with CL_DELIM. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_IMAGE+filename+CL_DELIM+imagelabel Example: filename = grey_elf Example: imagelabel = Gray Elf Formatted Example: #K%00005020AABgrey_elf~Gray Elf #define CL_SEND_REBOOT AAC ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. This literal is used to send the amount of time (timestring), in hours and minutes, that are left until the mud has a scheduled reboot. The format should be HH:MM. Note: If the Caption (CAP) literal is used, the Reboot literal is not used. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_REBOOT+timestring Example: timestring = 12:45 Formatted Example: #K%00005008AAC12:45 #define CL_SEND_MUSIC AAD ================================================================= This is a multiple data point literal. This literal is similar to the CL_SEND_SOUND except that it is used to send the filename of the music file to be played. Valid MIDI files formats are supported (*.MID, .RMI, etc.) as well as MP3 files (.MP3) You do not need to include the file extension unless you wish to specify. All music files are stored in the media/sounds/ directory. You can also choose the number of iterations to play of the file. The file will play iterations # of times. If you don�t specify a number of iterations, the file will play only once. Note: This function is only enabled if the user has not disabled remote media support. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_MIDI+filename+CL_DELIM+ iterations (non-repeating music example) Example: filename = canon_in_D Example: iterations = <nothing> Formatted Example: #K%00005013AADcanon_in_D (repeating music example � plays it three times) Example: filename = canon_in_D~1 Example: iterations = 3 Formatted Example: #K%00005015AADcanon_in_D~3 (stops the currently playing music file) Example: filename = <nothing> Example: iterations = <nothing> Formatted Example: #K%00005003AAD #define CL_SEND_UPTIME AAF ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. This literal is identical to the CL_SEND_REBOOT literal except that we�re sending the timestring as the amount of time the mud has been up instead of when it�ll reboot. Note: If the Caption (CAP) literal is used, the Uptime literal is not used. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_UPTIME+timestring Example: timestring = 05:30 Formatted Example: #K%00005008AAF05:30 #define CL_SEND_AVI AAG ================================================================= This is a multiple data point literal. This literal is similar to the CL_SEND_IMAGE except that it is used to send the filename of the AVI movie to be displayed in the Portal� Imagery. Only AVI files are supported. You do not need to include the file extension unless you wish. All AVI�s are stored in the media/images/ directory. The imagelabel (which will appear below the image in the Imagery) is optional. You can specify the height and width of the AVI also. These are optional as well. You can also choose to repeat the MIDI or not. The MIDI will repeat if repeat is anything but an empty string. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_AVI+filename+CL_DELIM+imagelabel+CL_DELIM+height+CL_DELIM+width (non-repeating example) Example: filename = raging_orc.avi Example: imagelabel = Raging Orc Example: height = 300 Example: width = 250 Example: repeat = <nothing> Formatted Example: #K%00005036AAGraging_orc.avi~Raging Orc~300~250 (repeating example) Example: filename = raging_orc.avi Example: imagelabel = Raging Orc Example: height = 300 Example: width = 250 Example: repeat = 1 Formatted Example: #K%00005038AAGraging_orc.avi~Raging Orc~300~250~1 #define CL_DOWNLOAD_MEDIA AAH ================================================================= This is a multiple data point literal. This literal allows you to automatically download media files to the user's media\sounds and media\images directories. The available files for download must be of the kind .WAV, .MID, .RMI, .MP3 (sounds) .BMP, .GIF or .AVI (images). It requires that you specify a filename, which will be the filename that will appear in the user's applicable media directory. You also must supply the URL where the media file resides on the web (usually on your MUD's site somewhere). Notes: � If the filename already exists in the user's applicable media directory, this operation aborts. Basically it's a good idea to keep your files named uniquely, maybe prepended with your MUD's name (e.g. blahmud_bigroar.wav). � The filename cannot contain spaces and is limited to 255 characters in length. � The filename must contain the file type extension (.GIF, .AVI etc.) � The filename is not case sensitive, but the URL is. � The URL is case sensitive, in case you missed it. � This function is only enabled if the user has not disabled auto downloading. � The user will be notified of the filename that was downloaded to their applicable media directory, as well as the URL from which it was downloaded. � Try to keep the files relatively small (under 100K) as downloading them sucks extra bandwidth from the user. Also, spread them out if you can. Having the user download 100 files one right after the other is not always a good idea. A good possible usage would be a command to use on your MUD which would download a list of specific media for the user. This way they could enter the command and come back in a few minutes when it�s downloaded. Portal� won�t attempt to download files they already have, so it�s ok to send files they don�t have. � Unless you KNOW your users have a killer connection, don�t even think about sending them .MP3 files. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_DOWNLOAD_SOUND+filename+CL_DELIM+URL (MIDI example) Example: filename = B5.rmi Example: URL = http://www.gameaxle.com/B5.rmi Formatted Example: #K%00005040AAHB5.rmi~http://www.gameaxle.com/B5.rmi (WAV example) Example: filename = lock.wav Example: URL = http://www.gameaxle.com/lock.wav Formatted Example: #K%00005044AAHlock.wav~http://www.gameaxle.com/lock.wav #define CL_SEND_SPECIAL BAA ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. This literal is used to send a special information textstring to Portal�. Generally this means weapon strikes, special armor messages, or other item/combat related information to send to the client. Guilds should NOT use this code. Instead, they should use the CL_SEND_SPECIAL2 literal as detailed below. Note: The text sent with this literal and with the CL_SEND_SPECIAL2 literal should be 60 characters or less. This is not a hard limit, but it�s the most text that can be displayed in the Portal� field without the user expanding it. (don�t hack lines just to meet this limit, but try.) Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_SPECIAL+textstring Example: textstring = Your sword explodes upon the goblin with a fireball! Formatted Example: #K%00005055BAAYour sword explodes upon the goblin with a fireball! #define CL_SEND_SPECIAL2 BAC ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. This literal is used to send a special guild information textstring to Portal�, such as when a special power has kicked in, or when another has failed, or when somebody advances in guild level etc. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_SPECIAL2+textstring Example: textstring = Your magical barrier of protection has faded! Formatted Example: #K%00005048BACYour magical barrier of protection has faded! #define CL_SEND_TELL BAB ================================================================= This is a multiple data point literal. This literal requires exactly 3 data points. This literal is used to send �tell� information to Portal�. The first argument is a direction indicator if the tell is originating from the player or coming to the player (i.e. �You tell Soandso:� vs �Soandso tells you:�). The indicator is either an �x� (lower case) or an empty string. The second argument is the object of the tell (to or from this person). The third argument is the actual tell text. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_TELL+direction+CL_DELIM+object+ CL_DELIM +text Here are two examples of CL_SEND_TELL lines: x~Fred~Hey fred, how�s it going? ~Fred~I�m doing fine, thanks for asking. The first line indicates that I have sent a tell to Fred from me (the placement of the x tells us this). The second line indicates a tell coming from Fred to me. Both of these would appear on my Tell Monitor. Formatted Example: #K%00005035BABx~Fred~Hey Fred, how�s it going? Formatted Example: #K%00005040BAB~Fred~I�m doing fine, thanks for asking. #define CL_SEND_ROOM BAD ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. This literal is used to send the short description of the room that the player is currently in. This information is displayed at the top of the Portal� screen for quick reference. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_ROOM+description Example: description = You are standing in a dark forest Formatted Example: #K%00005036BADYou are standing in a dark forest #define CL_SEND_MUDLAG BAE ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. If your mud supports any form of meter to display MUD-side lag, you can send it to the client via this literal. This shows in the title bar of Portal� with the uptime and reboot information. Note: If the Caption (CAP) literal is used, the MUDLag literal is not used. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_MUDLAG+meter Example: meter = 0.05 Formatted Example: #K%00005007BAE0.05 #define CL_SEND_EDIT BAF ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. This literal is used to send the current file that is being edited by the user/wizard. When done editing the file, send the CL_SEND_EDIT with an empty string. This will clear the file from the display. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_EDIT+file Example: file = /obj/monster.c Format Example: #K%00005017BAF/obj/monster.c #define CL_GP1_ MASK BBA ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. This literal is used to send the customized mask that will be used on the hints for the Guild Point 1 controls (on the HP bars and Status Monitor, etc.) The default is �Guild Points 1� and most likely will want to be changed by your MUD or guild/class/clan. This will change it automatically. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_GP1_MASK+mask Example: mask = Stamina Format Example: #K%00005010BBAStamina #define CL_GP2_ MASK BBB ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. This literal is used to send the customized mask that will be used on the hints for the Guild Point 2 controls (on the HP bars and Status Monitor, etc.) The default is �Guild Points 2� and most likely will want to be changed by your MUD or guild/class/clan. This will change it automatically. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_GP2_MASK+mask Example: mask = Violet Plasma Format Example: #K%00005016BBBViolet Plasma #define CL_HP_ MASK BBC ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. This literal is used to send the customized mask that will be used on the hints for the Hit Point controls (on the HP bars and Status Monitor, etc.) The default is �Hit Points� and might wish to be changed by your MUD. This will change it automatically. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_HP_MASK+mask Example: mask = Health Status Format Example: #K%00005016BBCHealth Status #define CL_SP_ MASK BBD ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. This literal is used to send the customized mask that will be used on the hints for the Spell Point controls (on the HP bars and Status Monitor, etc.) The default is �Spell Points� and might wish to be changed by your MUD. This will change it automatically. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SP_MASK+mask Example: mask = Mana Format Example: #K%00005007BBDMana #define CL_SEND_CAPTION CAP ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. This literal allows you to set the user�s Portal� window caption (the very top bar of the Main Screen). The string you send will appear after the standard Portal� caption elements: �<MUD> � <Player> (<online time>)� Space is already appended after the (<online time>) element, so prepending your caption with a space is not necessary. Use this literal for whatever kind of string you want to send: news flashes, player status, MUD status, etc. Note: If this literal is used, the Reboot (AAC) Uptime (AAF) and MUDLag (BAE) literals are not used. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_CAPTION+caption Example: caption = Newsbrief: Canada has invaded Michigan! Formatted Example: #K%00005042CAPNewsbrief: Canada has invaded Michigan! #define CL_SEND_BEGIN_FILE CDF ================================================================= This is a multiple data point literal. This literal requires exactly 2 data points. This literal is used to begin a text file �download� from the mud. The two data points are the # of lines being sent and the �tag� to be associated with the download. This could be the file name if it�s a file, or �Who List� for instance if you�re sending a who list as a file. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_BEGIN_FILE+lines+CL_DELIM+file Example: lines = 125 Example: file = /obj/player.c Format Example: #K%00005020CDF125~/obj/player.c #define CL_SEND_CONT_FILE CCF ================================================================= This is a single data point literal. This literal is used to send a line of the file or text that was initialized for download with the CL_SEND_BEGIN_FILE literal. Each line of the file will be sent with this literal. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_CONT_FILE+line Example: line = if (attacker_ob) { attack(); attacked_this_round = 1; } Format Example: #K%00005058CCFif (attacker_ob) { attack(); attacked_this_round = 1; } #define CL_SEND_END_FILE CEF ================================================================= This is a 0 data point literal. No data is sent with this literal. This tells Portal� that a the file being download has completed. It�s a good idea to send this twice, just to ensure that Portal� ends the file transfer just in case one of them gets lost/garbled in line noise. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_END_FILE Format Example: #K%00005003CEF #define CL_SEND_CHAT CAA ================================================================= This is a multiple data point literal. This literal requires exactly 4 data points. This literal is used to send chat line information to Portal�. The 4 data points are line command, line name, source player name, and data. The Line Text should be an unformatted string (no color nor wrapping). Remember, the CL_DELIM literal must separate the data points. Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_CHAT+command+CL_DELIM+line+CL_DELIM+source+CL_DELIM+data Example: command = guildchat Example: line = Guild Example: source = Rastafan Example: data = [GUILD] Rastafan: Hi guys This indicates that Rastafan has sent a chat to his guild using the guildchat command. The Guild title will be the title for this line, and the Data would appear on my Chat Monitor. Formatted Example: #K%00005053CAAguildchat~Guild~Rastafan~[GUILD] Rastafan: Hi guys #define CL_SEND_COMPOSITE FFF ================================================================= This is a multiple data point literal. This literal can have any number of data points. See the examples in the main text on how to create a COMPOSITE data line. The following HP_DATA_CODE literals are valid for the COMPOSITE line code literal: Format: ACTIVATE+SEC_CODE+CHAR_COUNT+CL_SEND_COMPOSITE+composite1+CL_DELIM+composite2+CL_DELIM+composite3+�+CL_DELIM+compositeN #define CL_SEND_HP A ================================================================= This literal is used to send the player�s current hit points. Range for this literal is 0-9999. Example: 312 Formatted Example: #K%00005007FFFA312 #define CL_SEND_MAXHP B ================================================================= This literal is used to send the player�s max hit points. Range for this literal is 0-9999. Example: 410 Formatted Example: #K%00005007FFFB410 #define CL_SEND_SP C ================================================================= This literal is used to send the player�s current spell points. Range for this literal is 0-9999. Example: 300 Formatted Example: #K%00005007FFFC300 #define CL_SEND_MAXSP D ================================================================= This literal is used to send the player�s max spell points. Range for this literal is 0-9999. Example: 425 Formatted Example: #K%00005007FFFD425 #define CL_SEND_GP1 E ================================================================= This literal is used to send the player�s current primary guild points. Range for this literal is 0-9999. Example: 57 Formatted Example: #K%00005006FFFE57 #define CL_SEND_MAXGP1 F ================================================================= This literal is used to send the player�s max primary guild points. Range for this literal is 0-9999. Example: 502 Formatted Example: #K%00005007FFFF502 #define CL_SEND_GP2 G ================================================================= This literal is used to send the player�s current secondary guild points. Range for this literal is 0-9999. Example: 50 Formatted Example: #K%00005006FFFG50 #define CL_SEND_MAXGP2 H ================================================================= This literal is used to send the player�s max secondary guild points. Range for this literal is 0-9999. Example: 100 Formatted Example: #K%00005007FFFH100 #define CL_SEND_GLINE1 I ================================================================= This literal is used to send the player�s primary guild line information. Range for this literal is 0-60 characters. Example: Next Level: 5000gxp Shield Strength: 100% Formatted Example: #K%00005045FFFINext Level: 5000gxp Shield Strength: 100% #define CL_SEND_GLINE2 J ================================================================= This literal is used to send the player�s secondary guild line information. Range for this literal is 0-60 characters. Example: Guild Level: 32 Familiar Health: 75% Formatted Example: #K%00005040FFFJGuild Level: 32 Familiar Health: 75% #define CL_SEND_ATTACKER K ================================================================= This literal is used to send the name of the monster the player is currently fighting. Range for this literal is 0-60 characters. Example: Shamus the Shop Keeper Formatted Example: #K%00005026FFFKShamus the Shop Keeper To set the value to an empty string, send the CL_DELIM (~) after the K code Example: <nothing> (clears the enemy name) Formatted Example: #K%00005025FFFK~ #define CL_SEND_ATTCOND L ================================================================= This literal is used to send the % of max hit points their current enemy has. Range for this literal is 0-9999 (> 100 means above max HP). Again, this is % HP of the enemy, not actual HP. Example: 75 Formatted Example: #K%00005006FFFL75 Note: Sending a 0 will set the enemy name to gray on the Status Monitor and in the Imagery. Setting it to any value above 0 will set it to black. This is supported in Portal� versions 5b and above. #define CL_SEND_ATTIMG M ================================================================= This literal is used to send the image file for the monster they are fighting. Range for this literal is restricted by Windows� file naming conventions. As a general rule, you should not use anything but alphanumeric characters (a, b, c, 1, 2, 3) and the underscore (_). The filename is not case-sensitive. The length of the total filename cannot be longer than 255 characters. Example: townfolk_shamus Formatted Example: #K%00005019FFFMtownfolk_shamus You can send any number of composites from A to M via the CL_SEND_COMPOSITE literal. Here is an example to send HP, SP, GP1 and attacker condition all at once. Example: HP = 312 Example: SP = 300 Example: GP1 = 57 Example: condition = 75 Formatted Example: #K%00005020FFFA312~C300~E57~L75 It is much better to send composite literals in groups this way, compared to sending them individually. You could have accomplished the above by sending four separate CL_SEND_COMPOSITE literals, but that would be a horrible waste of bandwidth. Sending it in a group as shown gains the same results in one efficient sweep. ================================================================= Appendix B: Coding Suggestions & General Hints ================================================================= Here are some tips to help on bandwidth concerns: � For the COMPOSITE literal the best and easiest way to handle sending that information is to track the values from one round to the next and only send the values that have changed. This reduces the overall bandwidth and makes the send a lot smoother. Basically, don�t send two COMPOSITE literals, one sending HP and the other HPMax. Have one COMPOSITE literal send both at once. � Assuming you�re doing the above method of tracking and sending, for your CL_SEND_GLINE1 (and 2) calls, it is best to group values that change frequently into only one of the gline calls, and values that don�t change frequently into the other. This reduces bandwidth by only sending one of the lines frequently and the other seldom. For example, put guild experience (gexp) to next level and guild age into one of them. Put guild level and alignment (or some such) in the other. � Build a client.c router and a few simul_efuns that call it. This will make all your wizards a lot more likely to use it if it is easy to do so. Put the above #define statements into a client.h file so that all the wizards can #include it and just use the defines instead of the key codes. That way if the codes ever change there will only need to be one file changed (though files that #included the old client.h file will need to be updated/loaded). � Create a #define CL_DELIM �~� for that same purpose as above. � This may seem obvious, but get Portal� yourself and make one change at a time and test it, this could save you a lot of trouble in the long run. � Sending images and sounds is very easy, but doesn�t do you any good if the players don�t have them. So post sound and image �packs� on your website somewhere and encourage your players to download and place them into their media/images or media/sounds directories. You can�t really appreciate things like this until you see/hear them. It�s one thing to open a door, but it�s insanely more exciting to hear the sound of a creaking door when you do so. � Don�t forget the �3klient� command, this is what turns it all on! ================================================================= Appendix C: Coloring the Gline1 & Gline2 ================================================================= The gline literals (CL_SEND_GLINE1 & CL_SEND_GLINE2) appear on the HP3 Bar. The text that appears has a black background and the font is colored white by default. While you cannot change the black background, you can change the font color. All you have to do is encapsulate the text you desire to color in the format specified below. You can't use < or > anywhere in the glines as normal text or it'll screw up. If you already use < or > enclosures, you'll have to use something else to encapsulate your data. All text not enclosed in any color activators appear as white. Format: <xword> x color code word text to be colored (any length) Valid Color Codes y yellow r red b blue g green (windows calls it lime) c cyan (windows calls it aqua) v violet (windows calls it fuchsia) s silver (dim white) Example 1: The red <rfox> jumped over the cyan <cdog> Display: The red fox jumped over the cyan dog Example 2: Spells Activated: [<bshield>,<gmagic missile>] Display: Spells Activated: [shield,magic missile] Example 3: Demon Follower's Health: <a95%> Display: Demon Follower's Health: 95% Now, why did it appear all in white? Because "a" was used, which is not a valid code. We suggest you keep the number of uses of the activator to under 10 per gline. That means under 10 usages of the <> pairings. Appendix D:FTP Emulation Upload While the literals CL_SEND_BEGIN_FILE, CL_SEND_CONT_FILE and CL_SEND_END_FILE (defined in Appendix A) take care of the FTP Emulation for download (server to client) transfer, there is also functionality for upload (client to server) transfer. This is done mostly via an added command on the MUD in the format of �3ksendfile filename� which will be used by Portal�. The upstream transfer can only transfer text files. The user can select any number of files to upload via this command, but each one is buffered to be sent every 2 seconds. Lines following the 3ksendfile command are added to the file filename in the order they are received. This is not unlike sending a slew of lines into the standard �ed� editor found on most MUDs. Here the server should build up an array buffer for the lines, which will then be written to the final file filename. When the transfer of lines is complete, Portal� sends the string EOF. When this string comes across, it tells the server that the file transfer is complete and the array buffer can then be dealt with accordingly (dumped into a file, posted to a board, etc.). This is not recommended for use on files more than 300 lines. Standard FTP should be used for such transfers. Windows filenames will have any spaces converted to underscores upon transfer. Again, this will only work with text files. ================================================================= Portal� for Windows MIP Terms of Use License ================================================================= The information contained within this document (hereafter referred to as the MIP) is provided "as is." docs.title: Combat Modification System
docs.text: Combat Modification System ========================== The combat modification system is a system for applying temporary mods to combat. The system is included by all LIVINGs and provides hooks to interact with combat modifying objects. The system requires that an object with functions to set modifications be registered with the living whose combat is to be modified. Registering combat mod objects ------------------------------ void add_combat_adj(object oArg) - This function must be called on the living that will get the mods. The object passed is registered with the living as an object which modifies combat for that living. void remove_combat_adj(object oArg) - This function should be called on the living when a particular modification to combat is unregistered. void add_tmp_to_XXX(int iAdjustment) - XXX to be replaced by a mod type. This function will add a temporary mod of the passed value. void query_tmp_to_XXX() - This function will return a temporary mod of the given type. void reset_tmp_to_XXX() - This function will reset the mod of the given type to 0. The following modifications exist: tmp_to_hit_stat tmp_to_dam_stat tmp_to_dodge_stat tmp_to_absorb_stat tmp_to_crit_stat tmp_to_hit tmp_to_crit tmp_to_dam tmp_to_dodge tmp_to_absorb tmp_to_type tmp_to_swings The crit modifications are critical damage modifiers. They do not alter the chance that an attack becomes a critical hit. Use STATUS_EXPOSED from <status_effects.h> for incoming critical chance. See `wizhelp 9.16` for the living-owned status-effect API. Functions to define in combat mod object ---------------------------------------- int modify_combat(object oTarget) - This is called by the attacking living, at the start of the combat round. The target is the current target being attacked. The return value is currently unused, and not tmp mods are expected to be set. int modify_attack(object oTarget, mixed* axAtt) - This is called by the attacking living, prior to an attack set axAtt being launched at oTarget. The return value is currently unused, and the following tmp mods are cleared prior to this function being called: tmp_to_hit_stat, tmp_to_dam_stat, tmp_to_crit_stat, tmp_to_swings. int modify_swing(object oTarget, mixed* axAtt) - This is called by the attacking living, prior to each swing of an attack set axAtt being launched at oTarget. The return value is currently unused, and the following tmp mods are cleared prior to this function being called: tmp_to_hit, tmp_to_crit. int modify_hit(object oTarget, mixed* axAtt, status tCrit) - This is called by the attacking living, once it has been determined that contact will be made, but before damage is determined. The return value is currently unused, and the following tmp mods are cleared prior to this function being called: tmp_to_dam, tmp_to_type. int modify_get_attacked(object oAttacker, mixed* axAtt) - This is called by the defending living, prior to an attack set axAtt being launched by oAttacker. The return value is currently unused, and the following tmp mods are cleared prior to this function being called: tmp_to_dodge_stat, tmp_to_absorb_stat. int modify_swung_at(object oAttacker, mixed* axAtt) - This is called by the defending living, prior to each swing of an attack set axAtt being made by oAttacker. The return value is currently unused, and the following tmp mods are cleared prior to this function being called: tmp_to_dodge. int modify_get_hit(object oAttacker, int iDam, int iType, status tCrit) - This is called by the defending living, after contact has been made and damage determined, but prior to damage actually being applied. The return value is currently unused, and the following tmp mods are cleared prior to this function being called: tmp_to_absorb. int filter_standard_block(int iBlock, string sEffectId) - This is called by the blocked living when set_standard_block() is about to apply a standard block. The value of iBlock is the current block mask, possibly already modified by earlier combat mod objects. The value of sEffectId is the effect id passed to set_standard_block(). Return the block mask that should continue being applied. Returning 0, or any value less than 1, prevents the block from being applied. Returning iBlock leaves the block unchanged. A filter may also remove individual block bits from iBlock before returning it. The living-side dispatcher for this hook is apply_filter_standard_block(int iBlock, string sEffectId). It calls filter_standard_block() on each registered combat mod object in order before the living's normal noblocks mask is applied. How much of a bonus to give? ---------------------------- The easiest way to give bonuses/penalties is with tmp_to_WHATEVER_stat. This effectively lowers the living's stat in one of the four combat areas as if they had a lower physical stat. The critical variants add to damage before the critical multiplier is applied. Bear in mind that actual combat stats are not as important as their relative ratios, meaning that one point of temporary combat stat is far more valuable to someone with one point of real stat than to someone that already has fifty points. When giving out larger bonuses, it may be useful to scale those bonuses in terms of a living's level or actual stat. tmp_to_WHATEVER will increase the final values in a meaningful way. For example, if one wants to guarantee a hit, an increase to tmp_to_hit of 100 (or more) may be appropriate. In order to increase the actual damage done by a hit, increase the tmp_to_dam by the amount desired. Note that this method is usually much harder to balance.

docs.title: Party System
docs.text: Party System ============= The party system is a means through which players can group together and tackle NPCs as a team, sharing experience and gold between all members of the party. It is assumed that all wizards already know what the party system is and what it does. This document briefly describes the means by which a wizard can create code that will react to party events. The procedure is pretty simple. 1. An object is registered with the player using add_party_listener. [Ex. this_player()->add_party_listener(this_object())] 2. Any time a party event occurs, a specific function is called on the registered object. These functions are described below. void party_add_member(mixed xNewMemberName) : Called when a new member joins the player's party. void party_remove_member(mixed xOldMemberName): Called when a member is removed from the player's party (leave/booted). void party_flag_adjust(mixed xFlag) : Called when the "in party" flag is adjusted on the player, such as when a player joins/leaves a party. 1 = in party, 0 = not in party. In addition to these particular callbacks, the following party related functions exist on all players: string *query_party_members() -- Returns array of party member names int query_in_party() -- Returns 1 if in party, 0 otherwise void end_party() -- Remove the player from his party varargs query_party_members_present(object oMember) -- If you don't supply oMember, it will check all party members and return an object array of party members present (not including the player you're checking from). If none are present it returns 0. If you supply oMember, it will return 1 if oMember is present, or 0 if not.

docs.title: TOWN CRIERS:
docs.text: TOWN CRIERS: Darkwind's town crier system allows the addition of both general and domain-specific messages that can be queried and announced via various means. The messages can be advertisements for areas, quests, specific events, and the like. Relevant commands: Read the help for the following commands: criermsgs, crieradd, crieraddtimed, crierremove Town Crier Inheritable: There is a generic town crier inheritable (TOWN_CRIER) that will automatically shout a variety of messages, preferring general domain messages and messages from its own domain (set with set_domain()). It recognizes souvrael, darkwind, kerei, hyperborea, and underworld as domains. There is an example at /domains/darkwind/roads/obj/crier.c that uses this inheritable. void set_domain(string domain): Sets the message domain that the crier will prefer when shouting messages. void set_all_domains(int flag): If 1, the crier will select messages from all domains. If 0, the crier will shout only messages only from its specified set_domain() domain and from general messages. void set_crier_message(string msg): Sets the message the crier will prepend to its shouts. Defaults to "Hear ye, hear ye!". To add an announcement programmatically: CRIER_D->add_announcment(string key, string msg, string domain, int minutes); Domain is optional, and defaults to "all". The key needs to be unique *across all the announcements*! A good key would be something like "malraux.newbie.ad". A bad key would be something like "message". Do not put newlines or double quotes in your messages. You can add an announcement as many times as you want. Successive additions of the same key merely replace. Announcements are saved, so you only need to add the message once. The announcement will stay until you remove it explicitly. The "minutes" parameter will put a timeout of that many minutes on the announcement, after which it will automatically be removed. To remove an announcement: CRIER_D->remove_announcement(string key); To query a random announcement by domain: CRIER_D->query_random_announcement(string domain); Domain is optional; default is "all". Valid domains are: darkwind, hyperborea, souvrael, kerei, underworld, all Of course, you can create your own domains for internal use, but they announcements will never be queried anywhere else. /inherits/towncrier.c is an example of a way to use the CRIER_D.

docs.title: To use the generic edit object:
docs.text: To use the generic edit object: #include <daemons.h> To start an edit session: EDIT_D->start_edit(string sData, object oCallbackObj, string sCallbackFunc); where sData is a string to pre-stuff the edit buffer with, oCallbackObj is the object which needs to be notified when the edit is done, and sCallbackFunc is a function on that object of prototype: void func(string sData, object oPlayer); The edit daemon will call the callback object's callback function with the data and the player doing the editing. sData will be 0 if the player aborts the edit process. Look in /open/OBJ/newsread.c for an example. -mal

docs.title: from /public/docs/wizard/shop
docs.text:
from /public/docs/wizard/shop ***************************************************************************** This is documentation to explain creating a shop, using the shop inheritable. The new setup of any shop, will remove the backroom of the shop. There is a storing object, that is left in the void. You do not need to do anything for this to occur. In every shop you must: #include <mudlib.h> #include <treasure.h #include <material.h> #include <types.h> inherit SHOP; --> for the shop room. Do not inherit ROOM, SHOP does that already. There are a few functions which you have to define: (preferably in this order) set_shop_ob(this_object()); Setup the shop for this particular object. set_value_info( ({ ({ 200, 20 }), ({ 400, 17 }), ({ 600, 15 }), ({ 800, 13 }), ({ 1000, 11}), ({ 1400, 9 }), ({ 1500, 7 }), ({ 2000, 5 }), ({ 2500, 4 }), ({ 3000, 3 }), ({ 3500, 2 }), ({ 4000, 1 }) }) ); This function is used to set up how many similar items of a certain value the shop will keep. (Although it will still buy more than its max value, it will not keep them, but it will destruct them.) In the above example, the shop will keep 20 items worth less than 200, 17 items less than 400, etc, etc, 3 items less than 3000, 2 items less than 3500 and 1 item less than 4000. Items worth more than 4000 will be destructed. The syntax of the function is as follows, a 2 dimensional array (many arrays, within on large array.) setup(); Setup this object. set_shopkeep(string str, string filename); str = name of the shopkeeper. filename = filename of the shopkeeper. set_shopkeep("shopkeep","players/myname/shopkeep_guy"); NOTE: Do _NOT_ put a '/' up front of the "players" in this string. set_guard(string str, string filename); str = name of the guard. filename = filename of the guard for that shop, that's called if the shop is robbed. set_storeroom("players/myname/guard"); NOTE: Do _NOT_ put a '/' up front of the "players" in this string. set_shop_type(int arg); arg = the bits which you are setting for the type of weapons and armours this shop will buy. You can set ALLTYPES for all armour and weapons. set_shop_type(ALLTYPES); set_shop_type(HELMET|LARGE|BOOTS|SMALL); set_shop_type(~PLATE); // all types except plate set_shop_t_type(int iArg); iArg = the bits which you are setting for the type of treasures this shop will buy. You can set TYP_ALLTREASURES for all of them. set_shop_t_type(TYP_JEWELRY|TYP_FURNITURE); set_shop_material(int iArg); iArg = the bits which you are setting for the material of objects this shop will buy. You can set ALLMATERIALS for all materials. set_shop_material(MAT_GOLD|MAT_SILVER|MAT_COPPER); set_mat_spec(int arg); arg = the bits which you set that the player can sell items of that material for full value, not 1/2. This includes the material of that item. set_mat_spec(MAT_STEEL|MAT_MITHRIL); set_typ_spec(int iArg); iArg = the bits which you set that the player can sell items of that type for full value, not 1/2. set_typ_spec(HELMET|GLOVES); set_t_typ_spec(int iArg); iArg = the bits for the treasure types that the player can sell for full value set_t_type_spec(TYP_BONES|TYP_MAP); set_typ_exclude(int iArg); set_t_typ_exclude(int iArg); set_mat_exclude(int iArg); iArg = a type, treasure type, or material that you want the shop totally barred from buying at all, regardless of anything else that is allowed. For example, a treasure of type TYP_GEM|TYP_BOOK would normally be sellable at a shop that takes TYP_BOOK, but not if you set_t_type_exclude(TYP_GEM); NOTE: You can set all of the bitfield functions again and again. The final value will be the total bitfield you have passed, it 'ors' all the passes together. set_sell(); Call this function to tell the inheritable that your shop will sell items. set_buy(); Call this function to tell the inheritable that your shop will buy items. add_stock(string filename, int number); This is just like add_clone. However, it puts these items in the store object upon updating. You can have multiple add_stock() functions. restock(); This stocks the store. Note: With add_stock and restock, you obviously want to restock the store after your add_stock lines, preferably only once per reboot. There are a few functions already in the init of SHOP. You do not need to add_action these. list: - will list the items in the store. sell: - will allow the player to sell any thing they have, provided the shop buys that type of item. If the it is a specialty item, they will get full price for it. buy: - will alloy the player to buy anything from the shop, provided they have the money, and they can carry it. value: - will value anything on the player, and in the room, telling them what they would get if they sold that item. read: - lets the player read the bounty list. rob: - lets a thief rob the store. loot_me: - will tell you how much cash the shop currently has. ***************************************************************************** Below is an example of a general store that buys and sells anything. It buys all items at half the set value except for MITHRIL items and GLOVES, which it pays full value for. #include <mudlib.h> #include <treasure.h> #include <material.h> #include <types.h> #include "hyper.h" inherit SHOP; void reset(int iArg) { if(iArg) return; ::reset(iArg); set_terrain("city"); add_terrain("inside"); set_domain("hyperborea"); set_light(1); set_short("Ivar's Northern Outfitters"); set_long("\ A large fire burns in a fireplace along the north wall. The windows
\ of this log building are shuttered against the howling wind and
\ freezing temperatures. Tables and shelves are scattered about the
\ store where goods may be found.
\ Commands: <LIST {items}>, <BUY {item}>, <VALUE {item}>, or <SELL {item}>
"); set_shop_ob(this_object()); set_value_info( ({ ({ 200, 20 }), ({ 400, 17 }), ({ 600, 15 }), ({ 800, 13 }), ({ 1000,11 }), ({ 1400, 9 }), ({ 1500, 7 }), ({ 2000, 5 }), ({ 2500, 4 }), ({ 3000, 3 }), ({ 3500, 2 }), ({ 4000, 1 }) }) ); setup(); set_shopkeep("shopkeep",HYPER + "monsters/ivar"); set_guard("guard",HYPER + "monsters/guard"); set_shop_type(ALLTYPES) <-- half price for all items set_shop_t_type(TYP_ALLTREASURES); <-- half price for all items set_shop_material(ALLMATERIALS); <-- half price for all materials set_mat_spec(MITHRIL); <---- full price for mithril items set_typ_spec(GLOVES); <---- full price for gloves /* since they are not set, there are no treasure type specialties, and no type is excluded from being bought/sold here */ set_sell(); <---- you can sell stuff here set_buy(); <---- you can buy stuff here add_stock(HYPER + "obj/torch", 2); add_stock(HYPER + "obj/furmittens", 2); add_stock(HYPER + "obj/furcloak", 2); restock(); add_exit("east", HYPER + "town11"); add_look(({"fire","fireplace","large fire"}),"\ A large fire burns in the fireplace, keeping the store nice and warm.
"); add_look(({"windows","shutters"}),"\ The shutters are closed to keep out the wind and the cold.
"); add_look(({"tables","shelves","store"}),"\ There is a lot of stuff here.
"); } /* EOF - Aeolus - 7/26/95 */

docs.title: The bug reporting system on darkwind is quite featured and unique.  This document
docs.text: The bug reporting system on darkwind is quite featured and unique. This document will attempt to show some of the commands associtated with the bug system. When a player submits a bug|typo|idea|emote, a message is transmitted to the balance line for assignement. Currently, most assignements are executed by Zureal, or other IMP+. To see what bugs are currently not assigned to anyone type: listunassigned bug|typo|idea|emote|all To see which bugs are assigned to you type: listassigned bug|typo|idea|emote|all Before you can close a bug assigned to you, you must first respond to that sumission. To respond, type: respond bug|typo|idea|emote <sub ##> Once you have responded to the submission and it has been fixed|added|rejected|etc you then close the submission by typing: closesub bug|typo|idea|emote <sub ##> If you want to see some general statistics about the overall submission situation type: listtally bug|typo|idea|emote|all listassignments bug|typo|idea|emote|all all|top open|closed|total <name> To see what another wizard has assigned to them type: listassigned bug|typo|idea|emote|all <wizard name> If you want to close a submission that was entered by error or any other reason that the sumission should be closed without response, type: removesub bug|typo|idea|emote <sub ##> To simply display the text of a bug type: lst bug|typo|idea|emote <sub ##> To review all entries that are associated with a specific submission, type: listhistory bug|typo|idea|emote <sub ##> If you are a member of the balance group to assign the initial sub or need to reassign a submission to another wiz, use: assignsub bug|typo|idea|emote <sub ##> <wizard name> reassignsub bug|typo|idea|emote <sub ##> <wizard name> If you need to edit a current submission type: editsub bug|typo|idea|emote (sub ##> This file written by Zureal 10-06-01 12:03a

docs.title: DarkWind Wizard Code of Conduct
docs.text: DarkWind Wizard Code of Conduct Our Pledge In the interest of fostering an open and welcoming environment, we as the Wizards of DarkWind, pledge to making participation in our our MUD a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation. Our Standards Examples of behavior that contributes to creating a positive environment include: * Using welcoming and inclusive language * Being respectful of differing viewpoints and experiences * Gracefully accepting constructive criticism * Focusing on what is best for DarkWind * Showing empathy towards other Wizards Examples of unacceptable behavior by participants include: * The use of sexualized language or imagery and unwelcome sexual attention or advances * Trolling, insulting/derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks * Public or private harassment * Publishing othersâ private information, such as a physical or electronic address, without explicit permission * Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting Our Responsibilities DarkWind Administrators are responsible for clarifying the standards of acceptable behavior and are expected to take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any instances of unacceptable behavior. DarkWind Administrators have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, or to demote, ban temporarily or permanently any Wizard for other behaviors that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful. Scope This Code of Conduct applies within all DarkWind channels (Wizard channels (i.e. BUILD or ARCH), says, tells, etc.) and in public spaces such as email (using an official @darkwind.org account), all DarkWind Discord channels or Twitter. As a Wizard, you represent the DarkWind community and leadership at all times within these communication mediums. Other examples of representation include posting via an official social media account or identifying yourself to be a coder from DarkWind in other Discord channels, MUD's or forums (such as Reddit). Representation of DarkWind may be further defined and clarified by the DarkWind Administration. Enforcement Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported by contacting DarkWind Administration at admins@darkwind.org. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated and will result in a response that is deemed necessary and appropriate to the circumstances. DarkWind Admins are obligated to maintain confidentiality with regard to the reporter of an incident. Further details of specific enforcement policies may be posted separately. DarkWind Administrators who do not follow or enforce the Code of Conduct in good faith may face temporary or permanent repercussions as determined by other members of the DarkWind Administration. Attribution This Code of Conduct is adapted from the Contributor Covenant, version 1.4, available at https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/1/4/code-of-conduct.html For answers to common questions about this code of conduct, see https://www.contributor-covenant.org/faq

docs.title: Basic Invasion Documentation
docs.text: Basic Invasion Documentation by: Malcolm @ Darkwind (updated by Aeolus - 8/10/94) The basics of putting together an invasion are simple. You need two basic things. 1) An event that triggers the invasion. 2) The invaders. Let's start with the trigger. The trigger can be anything important. Let's try to be reasonable here. A large, important event can be the slaying of a level 25 monster, the stealing of dragon eggs, or any other large *rare* event. It should also be somewhat convoluted. Players should not understand under what exact circumstances an invasion will occur. A few tools to help you: Use a random chance. Have 2 or more events trigger an invasion. Make the invasion delayed some time. Or anything else that may somewhat confuse the players as to why the invasion took place. Remember, the goal is to keep players from causing invasions every time they want one, not to make them tear their hair out. Once the event is triggered, you must call the invasion daemon with: #include <daemons.h> ... {triggered event} if(INVA_D -> trigger("invasion name",minimum # people on,approx. average lev) { obj1 = clone_object("invading_monster"); move_object(obj1,"wherever"); INVA_D -> add_invader(obj1) return 1; } INVA_D is the short_hand for the invasion daemon. It simply keeps track the invasion and how long it has been going on. The function <trigger> starts everything off. If the invasion cannot go on for some reason, 0 is returned. If the invasion is actually starting, then 1 is returned. Thus, the if statement. If the invasion goes forward, then we need to clone up the right objects, move them where we want them to start, and tell the invasion daemon to add that object to our list. As soon as the invading object is sent to the INVA_D, then the object begins to follow its invasion orders. This is a good point to start discussing the necessary code in the invading monster. FIRST: PLEASE NOTE: IMPORTANT: You need to inherit both MONSTER and INVASION. So you'll have: #include <mudlib.h> inherit MONSTER; inherit INVASION; The invading monster has 2 basic parts it needs in order to properly work. It needs to call 2 things in reset(). Namely, set_orders(), and set_path(). Set_orders essentially tells the monster what to do. Current possible orders are: MARCH ATTACK DEFEND marching commands FOLLOW secondary marching command WANDER SENTRY GUARD WAIT PATROL general orders ESCORT DESTROY KILL KIDNAP specific orders Orders, like weapon types and materials, are done using bits. set_orders(MARCH|WAIT); <---example Sometimes you need to give another variable. For instance, ESCORT needs to know who you want the invader to escort. In this case, just add another variable: set_orders(MARCH|ESCORT,"leader"); Let's talk about each of these in more detail. MARCH An invader under marching orders will continue to march, regardless of whether anyone is attacking them or not. ATTACK Attack orders make the invader attack others on sight. DEFEND Defend orders make the invader defend himself from enemy attack, even if it means staying put. FOLLOW Follow can only be used with ATTACK or DEFEND. If the invader is in conflict with an enemy, then the invader will follow the hapless victim around. (problem: this causes the invader to lose track of his attack path. We'll fix this soon) WANDER The invader uses the random exit function in monster.c. It ain't great, but it's the best we got for right now. SENTRY Sentry is the order for the invader, once he's reached the room of destination to attack anyone who enters. GUARD Guard tells the invader to prevent others from going a particular direction, Beware, for it stops invaders from going that direction also. WAIT Wait tells the invader simply to stop there and wait for further instructions. It's a lot like Sentry, but the invader won't attack. PATROL Patrol is a touch complicated. But the essence is really simple. The invader keeps going through the invasion path in a loop. Cool, eh? You can get the invader to appear as if it's patrolling certain rooms. ESCORT Escort tells the invader to follow another invader. This only works with other invaders. You can use an object or a string to identify the monster. The advantage of the string, is if you want a grunt to follow a leader, but don't care which one, then just simply have the grunt follow "leader", and when the next leader enters the room that the invader is in, then the grunt will follow. DESTROY Destroy let's the invader loose on a particular area. It takes about 20 seconds, but when it's done, the room will be destroyed. KILL Kill tells the invader, that once it's gotten to the end of its path, to kill a particular npc. String or object may be used to describe the victim. KIDNAP Not implemented yet, but essentially, the invader will carry the victim off. Ok. set_path is the function that gives the individual directions for the monster. Each direction is seperated with a ;(semi-colon). An example would be: set_path("n;n;enter;e"); That causes the monster to go north, north, enter, east. If, at any point, one of these commands is prevented, the monster will continue to attempt to do that direction over and over again. Note that some orders don't mix well with the set_path(). For instance Follow can throw the monster off its path, and random implies that there IS no path. Escort also implies no path. A few last notes: Some of these orders are incompatible. There's nothing to be done about this. Second, you may have noticed that some of the orders need an object or string as a variable for one of the orders. So that set_orders(DEFEND|SENTRY|KILL,"cher") would cause the invader to kill cher, if cher was present at the end of its ride. Do not mix orders that require variables. It's done this way for both simplicity and so that different monsters have different duties. Ok, that's the basics. Read through it a few times, and try to get the swing of it. If you're still having trouble with your area or monsters, don't try an invasion. There's more about invasion in the Intermedate.doc file -Malcolm
