docs.title: This function is messed up enough that it needs its own documentation.
docs.text: This function is messed up enough that it needs its own documentation. nomask varargs void move_player(string sDirDest, string sDest, string sArrive) OK, sDirDest can be one of several things: 1) direction#destinationFileName 2) direction only, if sDest has the filename 3) !msgout#destinationFileName 4) !msgout only, if sDest has the filename But, it gets better. If 1) or 2), then the message printed to the room being left is query_msgout... UNLESS 'direction' is 'X', in which case it uses query_mmsgout. If 3) or 4), the the message is the msgout portion of sDirDest. In any case, if the direction isn't X and doesn't begin with !, it is substituted for $D in the entrance message. Now, on to sArrive. 1) direction 2) !msgin If the direction portion of sDirDest is 'X', then query_mmsgin is used as the entrance message to print to the room the person is arriving in. Otherwise, if sArrive is a direction, then the query_msgin message is used with sArrive being substituted into $D. If sArrive is missing, then the code figures out which exit in the current room leads back to the previous room, and that is substituted for $D. If sArrive begins with !, then all of the above is scrapped and sArrive is used for the incoming message. Does your head hurt now? Good. Just be glad you didn't have to rewrite the damned thing like I did, while still maintaining backwards compatibility. -mal 2002-03-26 The following is an example using messages for leaving and arriving in the new room. The ! strip out all min and mout messages that would have been included, so only the specified strings get sent to the room. this_player()->move_player("!"+this_player()->query_cap_name()+ \ " leaves through the 'Dionysus' door.", AREA_MYTHOS_ROOM_DIR+ \ "temple_1", "!"+this_player()->query_cap_name()+" steps out \ of the shadows.");

docs.title: -=-=-=-=-=-=-=- My Vision Of Castles -=-=-=-=-=-=-=-
docs.text: -=-=-=-=-=-=-=- My Vision Of Castles -=-=-=-=-=-=-=- -or- -=-=-=-=-=-=-= My Kingdom For A Horse =-=-=-=-=-=-=- 1) Environs a) Should be specially prepared sites (ie. this area looks suitable for a castle) b) Various topographies: forested, plains, mountainous, etc. i) terrain governs foodstuffs, wood, mining ii) terrain governs defense c) Should be a 20x20(?) grid around the castle for taxes, food production, wars d) Should include a town and a castle e) Various benefits/detriments based on continent 2) Economy a) Inhabitants are taxed. b) Stores and the like can be located in towns/keeps c) NPC inhabitants slowly accrue over time depending on tax and factors in 1) d) PC inhabitants make their own decisions. :-) e) Kingdom city starts out as a few huts. f) Kingdoms can commission uniques or Wonders. 3) Castle a) Each room must be bought and built (which takes time). b) Rooms include: i) Castle walls, of various materials, size, and strength ii) Specialty defense: barbican, drawbridge, etc. iii) Interior rooms (market place, stables, bunkhouses, etc) iv) Keep rooms (throne rooms, banquet, sleeping, etc) c) The bigger the castle, the better the morale of the kingdom inhabitants d) Castles can also be things like strongholds (think of a thief king stronghold in the forest) e) Materials: wood, stone, steel, "wizard's stone" (requires a Mage to create) f) Castles can be built within a kingdom by allowed nobility of that kingdom, which extends the influence and boundaries of that kingdom. 4) Wars a) Kingdom can hire guards and militia i) Patrols ii) Keep guards iii) Companies of archers iv) Infantry v) Cavalry - uses a modified Paladin warhorse vi) Mountain/forest/desert units b) Militia treated as group NPCs, ie. "a company of archers (5)" c) Siege engines can be employed to damage or defend the castle i) hard to get catapults into the mountains, etc. ii) vehicle based "covered gate ram" iii) oil, fire, etc. d) The Engineer's Guild i) Players can design/create siege weapons ii) Players can "size up" opponent castles (wall height, etc) from afar iii) Players can research technology e) When hiring militia, the kingdom can announce that it is hiring. Militia will then trickle in. This is to avoid a situation where people hire militia just before a war and then dismiss them all immediately afterwards. docs.title: Poison
docs.text: Poison ====== Introduction ------------ Purpose of this document is to explain and document the ongoing additions of various poisons to the game. Definitions ----------- Meal/Keg/Food/Alcohol Poisons - These are what will be referred to as Ingested poisons. These poisons are a one-time damage, with no lingering effect. They can and will kill the victim if they are too low on health. Existing Methods of Delivery ---------------------------- Currently there are the following devices in the game to deliver Poisons: A dull grey jar Can be purchased in the Thief Guild poison hall. Is capable of delivering ingested poisons. One use per keg or meal, 3 uses for drinks or foods. Reverses healing effects of item. Regulations ----------- Poisons are not to affect NPK players. Ingested poisons have been written to support NPK checks, keeping them from ingesting the contaminated substance at all, with no loss to uses. Code Support ------------ The code in the ingested poisons allow for future implementations of purification spells or abilities. The following call applies: void set_purified() When called on the contaminated item, it will be restored to original healing values. *Note* Purification isn't to be easy. The cost for ingested poisons are steep and making purification easy is very counter-productive to mud balance. You can query any ingested poison object with int query_poisoned() and it will return 1 if the item is contaminated, null if not. When actually poisoning an ingested substance, you can use set_poisoned() to throw the query_poisoned() flag and save old healing values which, as mentioned, can be restored via set_purified(). Actual modifying of the healing values of the ingested items are modified using: set_hp_heal(int arg) and set_sp_heal(int arg) Revision History ---------------- 4/20/98 - Original document

docs.title: This is documentation to explain creating a pub or an inn, using the pub
docs.text: This is documentation to explain creating a pub or an inn, using the pub inheritable. Always: #include <mudlib.h> inherit NEWPUB; Do not inherit ROOM. There are a few functions which you have to define: set_type(string sArg); sArg = the type of store this is. This is written to player, for example: "You cannot rob the " + type + ".\n" set_type("inn"); set_save_file(string sArg); sArg = filename of the save file for your pub/inn. (Used with restore and save object.) set_storeroom("/players/myname/save_file"); set_bartender(string sArg, string sFilename); sArg = the name of the bartender, sFilename is the filename of it (with path.) set_bartender("bartender","players/myname/bartender_guy"); set_guard(string sArg); sArg = filename of the guard for that pub, that's called if the pub/inn is robbed. set_guard("/players/myname/guard"); add_item(string sArg, string sFilename, int iLimit); This is just like make_object, however, it accepts no 3rd argument for the number of that object. It will make these drinks available, and they can be bought buy the 1st arguement that you pass. If you pass integer limit, then only that number will be sold, per reset. add_drink("beer","players/myname/neato_beer",10); add_food(string sArg, int iLimit, int iCost, int iStrength); This is similar to add_item. sArg is the name of the food. iLimit is the maximum number to be sold. iCost is how puch to pay for it. iStrength is how many hit_points to heal them, and how satiated they get. add_food("bread",5,25,4); /* 5 breads, cost 25, heals 4 */ add_drink(string sArg, int iLimit, int iCost, int iStrength); This is similar to add_food. All of the arguements are the same. If you want the drink to be unlimied, pass 0 for iLimit. add_drink("beer",0,2,2); /* unlimited beers, cost 2, heal 2 */ set_menu_color(string sArg); str = the color string, that you want the shop menu to display in. If you are unfamiliar with color strings, wizhelp 1.7 (ansi). set_menu_color(""); /* Red on Black, Bold */ Note: At then end of your reset function, add the line restore(); Change your if(iArg) return, to this: if(iArg) { restock(); return; } There are a few functions already in the init of NEWPUB: Buy/Order, Rob, and Read. Read is setup, as you add items, or food to your pub or inn, the menu us modified. Do *not* add_read or menu or sign. You do not need to add_action these. There is an 'exit_hook' function, please dir_hook the exits out of your pub and make them call exit_hook(); If this is a room with no alcohol served, then you do not have to do this. The drinks for your pub, *must* return true for id("alcohol"); IE, set_alt_name or set_alias to alcohol. -Hayden woo woo!

docs.title: I, Antcrusher, worked on converting soft_dri (as it was the only
docs.text: I, Antcrusher, worked on converting soft_dri (as it was the only file I had) into a new inheritable for generic drinks. From what I could tell, alco_dri.c ran instant healing and intoxication off one variable. Likewise, soft_dri.c ran instant healing and soaked off one variable. This object will do all three, and they are driven by different variables so you can set each separately. It can be used to replace alco_dri and soft_dri. Note that the price for the alcoholic healing is less than the instant healing by a factor of 3. You get three points for every point of alco_strength, but since it's on a time delay it seems fair. Thus, to figure your value for an item, it is still 4*x + (x^2)/10. But here, x is the AVERAGE of healing and alco_strength. (Note that the 'standard' pub drinks are far overpriced.) Soft_strength doesn't really do much except keep you from drinking more soft drinks too soon. This value does not contribute to healing at all. The sum of the soft_strength and alco_strength should equal the healing value (or more), in order to keep instant healing from being too easily available. This object now inherits treasure.c, so all the functions from it can be used as well, including treasure and material types. It automatically sets to container and drink when created, and type drink is removed automatically when drunk. This object is a standard drink object and works like /obj/food.c or /obj/armour.c To use this you can do: inherit "obj/gene_dri"; ...... or, object oObj; oObj = clone_object("obj/gene_dri"); oObj->set_name("tequila"); These functions are defined in addition to those on treasure: set_soft_strength(int) To set the soaking power of the item. If you don't wish the item to soak players just set this value to 0. This value has nothing to do with healing...it simply keeps players from drinking more soft drinks too soon. set_alco_strength(int) To set the amount of intoxication. The player will receive three (or whatever it is set to on your MUD) extra hit points for half this number of 'healing rounds', which I believe is every tenth heartbeat, usually. If you don't want it to be intoxicating then (you could have used obj/soft_dri) set this to 0. Does not check for negatives. set_healing(int) To set the amount of instant healing. set_drinker_mess(string) To set the message that is written to the player when he drinks the item. set_drinking_mess(string) To set the message given to the surrounding players when this object is drunk. set_empty_container(string) The container of the liquid inside. For example "bottle" or "jug". This following is an example of a drink. It's the way the beer from the pub looks now. A drink like this was not possible using alco_dri, the pub drinks inherited a special file (because healing and alco level were driven by different variables, and alco_dri couldn't handle it). #include <mudlib.h> inherit DRINK; void reset(int iArg) { ::reset(iArg); if (iArg) return; set_name("beer"); set_alt_name("alcohol"); /* for use in pub */ set_short("a bottle of beer"); set_value(12); set_weight(1); set_drinker_mess("That feels good.\n"); set_healing(0); set_alco_strength(2); set_soft_strength(0); set_empty_container("bottle"); } /* White space and hungarian notation added 20/08/98 References to non-existant files removed 23/08/98 --Xnedra-- */

docs.title: Reputation Hook Notes
docs.text: Reputation Hook Notes ===================== Use SOCIETY_D->record_reputation_event() for new reputation changes. Signature: record_reputation_event(player, heroism_delta, reason, source, hidden_dimensions, metadata) Guidelines: * Guild membership alone should not move reputation. * Use actions: quests, rites, services, crimes, mercy, desecration, public praise, public harm, and other notable deeds. * Keep public heroism simple: positive trends Hero, negative trends Villain, zero stays Adventurer. * Put the "why" in hidden dimensions such as mercy, terror, honor, faith_mitra, faith_gaea, faith_set, nature, crime, secrecy, blood, service, community, and notoriety. * Use metadata["key"] plus metadata["repeat_cap"] for anything that must not be farmed repeatedly. Quest objects may opt in with: mapping query_reputation_event(object player) or: mixed *query_reputation_events(object player) Each returned event mapping can contain: "heroism" signed public heroism delta "reason" short admin-facing reason "dimensions" hidden dimension deltas "metadata" optional event metadata The new quest daemon records quest reputation once per quest event.

docs.title: Submission Documentation for Builders
docs.text: Submission Documentation for Builders The submit code handles submissions for: Bugs Typos Ideas Emotes Areas Unique Objects Mudlib Changes Guild Changes BUG/TYPO/IDEA Bug/Typo/Idea submissions are done via the existing commands. Bugs will no longer report to a log file. They will exist in the submission daemon. To look at the list of bugs, you will have to do the following: listtable <bug|typo|idea> [name] If a bug, typo, or idea has been assigned to you for coding, you may be interested to list all of them assigned to you: listassigned <bug|typo|idea> This will list the bugs, ideas and typos for your area. You can also leave off the name arguement and see a list of these for the entire mud. Optional arguements will be the area subdirectory name: listtable bug darkwind listtable bug necro These will list bugs for the domain of darkwind, and those reported in the necro guild rooms. To list a specific bug, you will have to note the request number of the submission and then do: lst bug <request number> You will notice room for code, content and balance reviews for all submissions. This won't be necessary for normal bug and typo submissions. If they're in your area, you have permission to fix the issue, and then get a balance member to close the submission for you. If you want to implement a new idea for your area, you will have to resubmit the code that has changed. This is discussed in detail, later. The idea submissions are just meant to give you ideas about your area. Lots of times players submit things that are really mudlib issues, and the bug will automatically be reported as a bug in an area. If you notice a submission that isn't meant to be in regards to your area, you should mudmail a balance member, and we'll be happy to change the submission as appropriate. You also have the ability to respond to a bug, typo and idea submission (only these three.) You can enter some information that may help the player understand why something is coded in a particular fashion, or you may ask for more information. respond <bug|typo|idea> <request number> When you do close one of these submissions, a mudmail is sent to the submitter, saying: Thanks for your <bug|typo|idea> submission. The submission has been closed, and the issue has been resolved. -<Name of Person who closed the submission> Note: If you need more information about a submission, you can use the respond command to mail the player. They can then, in turn use the editbug, edittypo, editidea, or editemote commands to add more information. If the submission is assigned to anyone, when the player updates it, then person to whom its assigned, will receive mudmail. How do I submit things for approval? You use the submit command: submit <area|unique|lib|guild|emote> <Subject> Oops! I meant to say something else in my submission. Can I edit it? Sure. Use the command: editsub <area|unique|lib|guild|emote> <Subject> How long does this take? The submission itself is obviously very quick. Depending on the load of the balance team, usually submissions are at least looked at, within a week. By the time the submission is reviewed and the appropriate fixes are made, the entire process can take up to a month, for an area submission. How can I see the status of my submisson? You can see your submission in table format: listtable <area|unique|lib|guild|emote> <your name> If a review has been posted, or if you want to check if there are reviews pending that you haven't read, then notice the status in the output. If the status says "Respond" then your response is more current than the review. If it says "Reviewed" then the review is most current. How do I see the review of my submission? listreview <area|unique|lib|guild|emote> <request number> [review type] To list just a specific review, add the review type to that command. You can also list your responses with the listresponse command. A review has been posted, and I've made the changes. Now what? You should add a response to the review, indicating what changes you have made: respondrev <area|unique|lib|guild|emote> <request number> <code|content|balance> What happens when my submission is approved? An implementor can help you get your submission put into the game, as appropriate.

docs.title: Test Char Armor Help         By: Bullseye a.k.a Scyrus
docs.text: ------------------------------------------------------------------ Test Char Armor Help By: Bullseye a.k.a Scyrus ------------------------------------------------------------------ This help file will tell you about the armor that wizards use for their test char's, how you can create it, and how to transfer it to your test char. First of all I'll tell you the details of the armor, and what you can do with it. ------------------------------------------------------------------ Test Armor Commands: ------------------------------------------------------------------ setaq - Sets the quality of the armor Syntax: setaq <amt> ------------------------------------------------------------------ setac - Sets numerical AC of the armor Syntax: setac <amt> ------------------------------------------------------------------ settype - Sets the type of the armor Syntax: settype <none|padded|hide|studded|chain|banded|scale|plate> ------------------------------------------------------------------ If you need another list of these commands, then just 'look armor'. Now you need to clone the armor using the following string: clone /objects/testchar/test_armor.c The last step is to transfer the object to your test char, you do this by executing a move_object. The syntax is as follows: execute move_object(present("armor", this_player()), find_player("scyrus")); Obviously, all you'll have to do to customize this example is change "scyrus" in the find_player() to "thenameofyourtestchar"

docs.title: Test Char Weapon Help         By: Bullseye a.k.a Scyrus
docs.text: ------------------------------------------------------------------ Test Char Weapon Help By: Bullseye a.k.a Scyrus ------------------------------------------------------------------ Ok, now we're going to cover how to load a weapon for your test char, then transfer it. First let me tell you about the weapon and what you can do with it: ------------------------------------------------------------------ Weapon Commands: ------------------------------------------------------------------ setq - Set the quality of the weapon Syntax: setq <amt> ------------------------------------------------------------------ setwc - Set the class of the weapon Syntax: setwc <amt> ------------------------------------------------------------------ settype - Sets the type of the weapon Syntax: settype <none|slash|pierce|cleave|blunt|pole|missile> ------------------------------------------------------------------ setid - Sets the alias of the weapon Syntax: setid <new alias> ------------------------------------------------------------------ Ok, now to cover how to load the weapon, all you need to do is type the following string: clone /objects/testchar/test_armor.c Simple enough. Now to transfer the object to your test char, to do this just type the following command, changing "scyrus" to "thenameofyourtestchar" execute move_object(present("weapon", this_player()), find_player("scyrus"));

docs.title: Transmogrifier Help         By: Bullseye a.k.a Scyrus
docs.text: ------------------------------------------------------------------ Transmogrifier Help By: Bullseye a.k.a Scyrus ------------------------------------------------------------------ This help file will show you how to create a Transmogrifier and to transfer it from your inventory to your test character, or to any other character for that matter. At this point if you're wondering what the hell a Transmogrifier is, then I'll explain. First of all, a Transmogrifier is more commonly referred to as a mog or moggy. So that's what I'm going to call it for the rest of the doc. Moggy's were made for the purpose of aiding you in modifying your test chars stats, hence the file name test_aid. The following is a list of stats and other things you can do with a Transmogrifier: ------------------------------------------------------------------ Edit your: level Guild Level Wpn Level Str Dex Con Int Wis Chr Money tmpstats Guild Stats Race ------------------------------------------------------------------ Or you can: Consider Targets Heal back to full hps/sps ------------------------------------------------------------------ So now I'll get down to the important stuff. Your first step will be to clone the object. You can do this by typing: clone /objects/testchar/test_aid.c After you've done this you'll want to transfer the object to your test char to do that, you'll have to execute a move_object code. I've put an example below: execute move_object(present("moggy", this_player()), find_player("scyrus")); Obviously, all you'll have to do to customize this example is change "scyrus" in the find_player() to "thenameofyourtestchar" Once you've completed this entire process switch over to your test char and type moghelp for a list of commands.

docs.title: Zork-Only Accounts
docs.text: Zork-Only Accounts In Zork-only mode, new character creation asks only for a name and password. The account is still saved as a Darkwind player so the same authentication system can be used, but normal Darkwind character setup is skipped on the Zork-only listener. Use the regular Darkwind port for full Darkwind gameplay and administration.

docs.title: Zork-Only Commands
docs.text: Zork-Only Commands The Zork-only command path is intentionally small. help [topic] Read help from /public/docs/zork. commands List available Zork-only shell commands. look, l Look at the Zork portal room. gossip <text> Talk on the global gossip channel. egossip <text> Emote on the global gossip channel. gossiphist [n] Review recent gossip. scores List the top 50 Zork scores. quit Save and disconnect. After "enter portal", Zork's own parser handles Zork commands such as look, inventory, take, drop, open, close, read, score, save, restore, and directions.

docs.title: Gossip
docs.text: Gossip The Zork-only listener allows the normal gossip channel. gossip <message> egossip <action> gossiphist [lines] Gossip is shared with the main Darkwind game unless the server is later configured to isolate it.

docs.title: Zork Help
docs.text: Zork Help This is a MUD that only does one thing: play the original Zork game. Use "enter portal" to start or resume your Zork session. Useful topics: help commands help playing help gossip help account help version Inside Zork, use "zork help" or "zork help <topic>" for the same files. Brought to you by Darkwind (https://play.darkwind.ai) - Enjoy!

docs.title: Playing Zork
docs.text: Playing Zork From the Zork portal, type: enter portal Once inside, commands are interpreted by the Zork parser. Common commands include: look inventory take <object> drop <object> open <object> close <object> read <object> score north, south, east, west, up, down Session commands: zork save zork restore zork reset zork exit zork help [topic] Zork inventory is separate from normal Darkwind inventory.

docs.title: ZorkMUD Version
docs.text: ZorkMUD Version This version of Zork is a port of the original source code, preserved by MITDDC at: https://github.com/MITDDC/zork The game has been ported to the LDMud driver, written in LPC, and runs on a slimmed down version of Darkwind. If you like what you see, come visit us at Darkwind: https://play.darkwind.ai
